The 2-azabicyclo[3.1.1]heptane and 2-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane cores were constructed in a single step by a scalable intramolecular carbene N–H insertion, with subsequent functionalization giving α- and β-amino acids and other bifunctional derivatives amenable to two-point diversification. Structural analysis of the disubstituted 2-azabicyclo[3.1.1]heptane derivatives showed that both substitution patterns matched their reference piperidines in all exit vector parameters but one, and in that one occupied a geometry not observed for the parent ring. Virtual decoration of the functional groups on both 2-azabicyclo[3.n.1]alkane cores gave a library whose calculated physicochemical property profile coincided with that of the monocyclic reference, except for a modest increase in molecular weight. To validate the bioisosteric replacement in a biological context, conformationally restricted bupivacaine analogs based on both cores were prepared and evaluated in the mouse tail-flick assay. The 2-azabicyclo[3.1.1]heptane derivative reproduced the antinociceptive effect ofthe reference drug throughout the observation period, whereas the 2-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane-derived counterpart retained only part ofthe reference activity.

papers.title: Partial Pressure Modulation as a Method to Access Non-
papers.abstract: Under steady-state conditions, heterogeneous catalyst surfaces are often represented by thermodynamically favoured surface configurations defined by temperature and pressure. However, catalyst surfaces are inherently dynamic and can populate non-equilibrium states that differ from those expected based on the reaction environment. Herein, we show how partial pressure modulation can be utilised to sustain access to non-equilibrium states. Using CO oxidation over Pd/Al 2 O 3 as a model system, we demonstrate how oscillating the partial pressures of CO and O 2 drives the catalyst surface into a non-equilibrium state, accessing CO* coverages and reactivities unattainable under steady-state conditions. We find that accessing this state enhances catalytic rate up to three times above the steady-state maximum at a given temperature and induces activity under conditions where no steady-state activity can be recorded. Numerical simulations reproduce similar rate enhancements, demonstrating that accessing non-equilibrium states via dynamic operation can enhance activity without invoking catalyst reconstruction or alternative kinetic pathways. We conclude that the rate enhancement is directly related to disrupting the thermodynamically expected relationship between the gas and surface concentrations. More broadly, these findings suggest that dynamic reactor operation provides a powerful strategy for accessing non-equilibrium states and revealing otherwise inaccessible catalytic behaviour.

papers.title: Semicrystalline Polyesters Made by Stereoselective Polymerization of a Biobased Bicyclic Lactone
papers.abstract: Biobased thermoplastics offer sustainable alternatives to petrochemical plastics, but controlling polymer stereochemistry to access biobased materials with desirable thermomechanical properties remains a challenge. Here, we report two new semicrystalline thermoplastics synthesized through the stereoselective ring-opening polymerization of the biobased bicyclic lactone (±)-2-oxo-3,8dioxabicyclo[3.2.1]octane (ODO). Enantiopure bisurea catalysts produced highly syndiotactic poly(ODO) (s-PODO) at low temperatures through an unexpected chain-end control mechanism. Yttrium-catalyzed melt polymerizations afforded high-molecular weight isotactic and syndiotactic PODO. The ductility, strength and modulus of PODO thermoplastics can be tuned through changes in tacticity, processing and crystallinity. By controlling their stereoregularity and processing conditions, we show that semicrystalline PODO films can have exceptional gas barrier properties with enhanced strength and modulus relative to amorphous atactic PODO.

papers.title: Graph Neural Networks for Accelerated Prediction of Excited-State Properties in Transition-Metal Complexes
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) has been increasingly applied to the ground-state properties of transition-metal complexes (TMCs), whereas its use for predicting their stateresolved photophysical properties remains comparatively limited. Here, we evaluate nine ML configurations: a descriptor-based XGBoost model and eight graph neural network (GNN) configurations, using excited-state reference data from tmQMg* together with molecular, structural, and electronic information from the tmQM dataset series. The models were trained to predict the 30 lowest vertical singlet excitations, including excitation energies (∆E), oscillator strengths ( f ), absorption properties, charge-transfer (CT) character, and the metal contributions to the occupied and virtual natural transition orbitals (NTOs). GNNs substantially outperformed XGBoost for ∆E. Among the investigated architectures, the polarizable atom interaction neural network (PaiNN) provided the most favorable balance between accuracy and input requirements, reproducing ∆E with a mean absolute error of 0.124 eV while requiring only an XYZ file and formal molecular charge. Furthermore, PaiNN reliably captured excited-state character, resulting in 87.0% accuracy for CT classification and occupied-and virtual-NTO metal-fraction MAEs of 0.082 and 0.058, respectively, indicating that it generally distinguishes metal-and ligand-centered orbital character well. Individual f values were more difficult to predict accurately; however, combining the predicted ∆E and intensities reproduced the principal features of the broadened absorption spectra. Overall, these results establish PaiNN as a fast and reliable predictor of multiple TMC excited-state properties from minimal molecular input, providing a practical route for large-scale photophysical screening and substantially reducing the need for time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations and subsequent excited-state analysis.

papers.title: ML26: New Ingredients for an Integral-Features Density Functional with Broad Chemical Accuracy
papers.abstract: Integral-features density functional theory (IF-DFT) replaces the conventional integration over local ingredients with a nonlinear mapping from global integral descriptors, enabling machine-learned density functionals with broad transferability. Here we report ML26@MN15, a new IF functional that extends the earlier ML25@MN15 model by incorporating 12 additional correlation features—including overlap-projected rung-3.5 terms, CS1 dynamic-correlation ingredients, and VV10 nonlocal correlation—and by treating Hartree–Fock exchange as an integral feature rather than as a fixed hybrid percentage. ML26@MN15 employs 79 integral features evaluated on MN15 ingredients and a single-hidden-layer neural network with 5000 nodes to produce a size-extensive exchange–correlation energy. Trained on 185 databases comprising 7242 reference data, ML26@MN15 achieves a data-averaged energetic mean unsigned error of 0.89 kcal/mol, improving upon ML25@MN15 by 15% and outperforming a group of previous leading functionals across all eight chemical partitions examined. For the widely used MDB2019S, MGCDB84, and GMTKN55 datasets, ML26@MN15 yields the lowest averaged error among all tested functionals, including the results for GMTKN55 by ML-based Skala-1.1 and DM21 density functional approximations. The new functional also maintains strong performance for systems containing heavy elements and exhibits improved behavior on a challenging self-interaction benchmark. These results show that expanding the integral-feature space with physically motivated nonlocal ingredients yields a density functional with unprecedented accuracy across diverse chemical benchmarks. The broad and consistent accuracy of ML26@MN15 highlights the promise of integral-features density functional approximations as a scalable framework for incorporating additional nonlocal physics into future functional development.

papers.title: Transfer learning guides discovery of NIR-emissive DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters
papers.abstract: Water-soluble near-infrared (NIR) emitters are of interest for imaging in the tissue transparency window. DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters (DNA-AgN) hold promise for this spectral window, but it remains challenging to select oligonucleotides that stabilize NIR-emitting DNA-AgN. We address this challenge using transfer learning (TL), constructing a model that learns from experimental data for DNA-AgN stabilized by short 10-base oligonucleotides to then design longer oligonucleotides for larger, NIR-emitting nanoclusters. Using this model, we experimentally uncover 321 new DNA-AgN with peak emission beyond 800 nm, increasing design success by 710%. DNA-AgN designed using TL exhibit favorable properties including substantial emission above 1,000 nm, high fluorescence quantum yield, upconversion fluorescence, and a 14-electron count - the highest reported for DNA-AgN. These results demonstrate the power of TL for extracting physiochemical information from a limited parameter space and extrapolating these principles for broader design challenges, which is especially important when training data is scarce.

papers.title: Making Analytic Double-Hybrid DFT Gradients Practical: A High-Performance Multi-GPU RI Implementation
papers.abstract: Double-hybrid density functional theory (DHDFT) is the most accurate rung within the density-functional hierarchy, but its use for molecular structure and dynamics remains limited by the high computational cost of analytic nuclear gradients. Here, we present, the first GPU-accelerated implementation of analytic DHDFT gradients. The implementation, developed in the Extreme-scale Electronic Structure System (EXESS), employs resolution-of-the-identity (RI) techniques throughout the calculation and evaluates the complete relaxed gradient on GPUs, including the modified Z-vector response and the explicit nuclear derivative of the exchange–correlation potential. The distributed multi-GPU formulation is performanceportable across NVIDIA and AMD architectures, supports basis functions through g angular momentum, and enables calculations through quadruple-ζ basis quality. The implementation is validated against numerical derivatives and the established CPU implementation in ORCA for B2PLYP and revDSD-PBEP86D4. For sufficiently large calculations, EXESS sustains more than 50% of the theoretical peak double-precision floating-point performance and exhibits efficient strong scaling across multiple NVIDIA H200 GPUs and AMD MI250X GCDs. Compared with ORCA on a modern Sapphire Rapids CPU node, a single H200 GPU provides speedups ranging from approximately 10× to 675×. These results extend high-performance DHDFT from single-point energetics to efficient exploration of molecular potential-energy surfaces at the large basis-set quality required for accurate perturbative correlation.

papers.title: Elucidating Secondary Coordination Sphere Effects on the Electronic Structure and Redox Properties of Biomimetic Iron–Sulfur Cubanes
papers.abstract: Nature readily employs iron–sulfur (Fe–S) clusters to perform a wide range of essential biological processes involving long-range electron transport and catalysis for kinetically challenging redox chemistry. Notably, the structure of Fe–S cubane ([Fe4S4]) metalloclusters that serve as electron transfer mediators are highly conserved, where ligand coordination to four cysteine residues anchors the cofactor within metalloproteins such as ferredoxins (Fds) and high-potential iron-sulfur protein (HiPIPs). Despite sharing the same primary coordination environment, the [Fe4S4] cofactors within Fds and HiPIPs operate with discrete redox couples and potential windows that afford distinct electrochemical properties depending on the Fe–S secondary coordination sphere and protein environment. This enables [Fe4S4] clusters to serve as versatile coupling partners for kinetically challenging redox reactions spanning the full range of biologically accessible reduction potentials. The electrochemical properties of [Fe4S4] clusters are tuned through the cooperative interplay between its strongly-correlated electronic structure and the noncovalent interactions within its secondary-sphere and protein environments. Significant experimental and computational efforts have been made to identify the structure-function relationships driving selective modulation of cluster electrochemical features; however, disentangling this complex interplay remains a significant challenge. Here, we employ a low-scaling, multi-reference computational approach to elucidate how secondary-sphere interactions, namely hydrogen bonding (H-bonding) and solvent electrostatics, tune the electronic structure of biomimetic [Fe4S4] clusters and give rise to the diverging redox properties observed across different protein scaffolds in biological systems.

papers.title: QEpy: Quantum ESPRESSO in Python
papers.abstract: QEpy is a Python electronic-structure software package based on Quantum ESPRESSO (QE). QEpy accomplishes two goals. First, it simplifies running and prototyping calculations with QE. Second, it targets nonstandard workflows where the electronic-structure engine is used in ways for which it was not originally designed. For example, QEpy can instruct QE to run with custom potentials in the Hamiltonian, including external, exchange-correlation, and local pseudopotentials. QEpy also exposes, at any point during an electronic-structure calculation, including between self-consistent-field cycles, quantities that would normally be accessible only through post-processing, such as the electron density and wavefunctions. QEpy’s API to the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE) gives direct access to ASE-based workflows and tools. These capabilities make QEpy a flexible platform for implementing custom workflows, interfacing QE with other simulation tools, and prototyping new electronic-structure methods. This work is written in a hybrid paper/tutorial style. Several example notebooks are presented, together with references to publications in which QEpy has already been employed. Our goal is for QEpy to serve as a versatile platform for research, teaching, and innovation in electronic-structure theory and method development.

papers.title: Microwave electric field-induced dynamic hydration enables selected dehydration of formic acid over a poly(m-phenolsulfonic acid–formaldehyde Catalyst
papers.abstract: Formic acid is a promising renewable C1 feedstock and a safe liquid precursor for on-demand carbon monoxide (CO) production. However, selective dehydration of formic acid to CO remains challenging because solid acid catalysts generally require high temperatures and suffer from competing dehydrogenation and water-induced inhibition of acid sites. Here, we report the selective dehydration of formic acid over a poly(m-phenolsulfonic acid–formaldehyde) (PAFR II) catalyst under microwave irradiation. PAFR II afforded CO in 65% yield at 120 C without detectable formation of hydrogen or carbon dioxide. The catalyst was reused three times while maintaining selective CO formation. PAFR II showed stable catalytic activity during continuousflow dehydration, exhibiting a CO productivity of 31–37 mmol g-1 h-1. This activity was higher than that of previously reported solid acid catalysts operating at or below 150 °C. The resulting CO was directly used for the alkoxycarbonylation of iodobenzene to afford propyl benzoate in 92% yield, demonstrating the practical applicability of this system as an on-demand CO source. Water-addition experiments showed that adsorbed water strongly inhibited dehydration. Microwave electric-field irradiation afforded substantially higher activity than magnetic-field irradiation and conventional heating. Fourier-transform infrared difference spectroscopy and phase-resolved modulation infrared spectroscopy revealed reversible changes in adsorbed water around the sulfonic acid moieties under microwave irradiation. These results suggest that the microwave electric field dynamically modulates the hydration structure around the acid sites, temporarily increasing their accessibility to formic acid.

papers.title: Molecular Origins of Site-Specific CO2 Absorption in Hydrated Deep Eutectic Solvents
papers.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as promising candidates for CO 2 capture because of their highly tunable structures and CO 2 absorption capacities. However, their behavior under practical operating conditions remains poorly understood. In particular, the effect of water on DES structure and their CO 2 absorption capacity remains unclear. In this work, we use free energy perturbation (FEP) and molecular simulations to determine the CO 2 absorption capacities and transport properties of hydrated hydrophilic and hydrophobic DESs. Our results show that increasing water concentration decreases viscosity but also makes CO 2 solvation less favorable in both DESs, revealing a trade-off between transport properties and CO 2 absorption capacity. This trade-off is more favorable for the hydrophobic DES, which shows a substantial reduction in viscosity while maintaining a negative CO 2 solvation free energy. In contrast, the solvation free energy of the hydrophilic DES increases more substantially, becoming positive at 15 wt% H 2 O. Structural analysis reveals that these differences arise from distinct hydration and CO 2 solvation mechanisms in the two DESs. In the hydrophilic DES, CO 2 preferentially localizes around the Br – anion under dry conditions. Upon hydration, water blocks the anionic site, and the preferred CO 2 solvation site shifts to the cation.

papers.title: Tracking Evolution of Reactive Species in Pellets During HyDR through combined X-ray and Neutron Imaging
papers.abstract: Steel production emits 3.6 Gtyr −1 of CO 2 , and the majority of these emissions come from a single step: ironmaking. Hydrogen-based direct reduction (HyDR) offers a lowemission alternative, producing H 2 O instead of CO 2 when operated with green H 2 . Though conceptualized in the 1930s, market adoption of HyDR remains limited due to reactor failures from sticking of iron-ore pellets. The sticking phenomenon is rooted in rate-limiting kinetics, where transport of reactive species competes with surface reaction to become the dominant process. We combine X-ray and neutron imaging to simultaneously resolve microscale pore network evolution and the spatial distribution of reactive species in two iron ore pellets, one non-fractured and one fractured, across three stages of reduction. We detect a consistent accumulation of hydrogenous species on the surface and interior of both pellets across all timepoints. Pellet pores > 10 2 µm, do not contribute to this accumulation, marking regions of efficient mass transport. Within the pellet interior, hydrogenous species are spotted in the pellet matrix and at pore boundaries. Isolated pore boundaries have up to 3× higher enrichment of hydrogenous species than the largest connected pore cluster, marking them as regions of poor mass transport. By quantifying permeability, diffusivity, and tortuosity, we show that improved bulk transport with reduction progress does not mitigate local trapping. Our findings connect hydrogenous species retention to pore network evolution and mass transport behavior. Insights from this study provide a basis for microstructural design strategies that could boost transport of reactive species and improve HyDR reactor performance.

papers.title: Machine-Learned Potentials for Accelerated CCSD(T)-level Evaluations: Applications to OH(H2O)n
papers.abstract: An end-to-end machine learning workflow for the development of potential energy surfaces at the DLPNO-CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ level is described and applied to hydroxide-water complexes with two to five water molecules. This workflow utilizes a two-part machine learning process, achieving both accuracy and efficiency by combining a molecular orbital-based machine learning (MOB-ML) model with a GPU-accelerated equivariant graph neural network (EGNN) model. For both machine learning models trained in this workflow, the training data is obtained through the combination of small diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) simulations initiated at each of the optimized structures of interest for a given system size. A farthest point sampling algorithm based on a principal component analysis is employed to generate a diverse set of geometries that spans configuration space, including transition states. By transforming Cartesian coordinates into a graph-based representation, the EGNN model eliminates additional preprocessing of molecular configurations, provides an unbiased treatment of multiple isomers, and allows for isomerization processes among the isomers. An error analysis is performed on the final EGNN models, comparing the potential energies predicted for optimized structures, transition states, and structures that are obtained from snapshots of the ground state wave function sampled by large-scale DMC simulations to those evaluated at the DLPNO-CCSD(T)/aug-ccpVTZ level of theory and basis. Finally, production-run DMC simulations are performed using the validated potentials for both the OH(H 2 O) 2-5 and OD(D 2 O) 2-5 systems, and an analysis of the relative anharmonic zero-point energies is performed. It is found that deuteration does not change the relative energy ordering of the isomers of the OH(H 2 O) 3-5 complexes. Evidence of proton delocalization is identified in the prism isomer of OH(H 2 O) 5 in which a hydrogen atom in one of the solvating water molecules is found to be, on average, equidistant from the oxygen atoms in the hydroxide ion and the hydrogen-bonded water molecule. This delocalization is found to be retained with full deuteration of this complex.

papers.title: Chiral gold nanofibers as substrates towards SERS-based chiral and flexible sensing
papers.abstract: Chiral plasmonic nanostructures offer unique opportunities for combining surfaceenhanced Raman scattering (SERS) with enantioselective molecular recognition. However, their integration into practical sensing platforms remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate high-aspect-ratio chiral gold nanofibers as versatile substrates for sensitive, chiral, and flexible SERS sensing. Using trans-1,2-bis(4-pyridyl)ethene as a model analyte, the chiral gold nanofibers enable molecular detection down to 1 nM and exhibit higher SERS efficiency (between 2-3× higher) than benchmark nanomaterials such as chiral and achiral gold nanorods. Beyond molecular detection, the chiral gold nanofibers generate distinct SERS responses towards D- and L-cysteine and mixtures with different enantiomeric compositions above analyte concentrations of, at least, 10 mM. Finally, the chiral gold nanofibers retain their SERS activity after integration into low-cost, flexible paper scaffolds, enabling spatial mapping and recovery of characteristic molecular fingerprints across the heterogeneous surface. These results establish chiral gold nanofibers as potential multifunctional plasmonic building blocks that combine molecular sensitivity, enantioselective recognition, and compatibility with flexible surfaces, providing a route towards adaptable platforms for label-free chiral sensing.

papers.title: Transport-guided intensification of plasma activation spray for scalable and tunable water treatment
papers.abstract: Interaction of cold plasma with aqueous media underpins emerging technologies in water treatment, chemical conversion, and biomedicine, yet scalable plasma-liquid activation remains limited by inefficient gas-liquid mass transfer and rapid reactive-species decay. This study reports a droplet-based plasma activation spray (PAS) reactor and establishes transport-guided design principles for intensifying reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) capture. Through systematic variation in spray-nozzle size, chamber geometry, and gas flow, we identify regimes governing the magnitude and composition of plasma activation. Smaller droplets (∼342 µm) favored reactive nitrogen species uptake through increased interfacial area, whereas larger droplets (∼1.3 mm) accumulated hydrogen peroxide through bulk-phase retention. Larger chambers extended droplet flight time and enhanced bulk accumulation, while positioning electrodes near the liquid interface minimized short-lived species transport losses. Spatial repositioning of multiple needles further improved the plasma activation by covering inactive zones. These design principles, validated in scaled PAS systems, achieved peak energy yields (>1.84 mmol/MJ at liter-scale) and enabled rapid antibiotic degradation and superior ≥ 5-log microbial inactivation, bridging the gap between plasma science and large-scale environmental application. The results position PAS as a tunable and scalable platform, providing a robust engineering framework that couples plasma physics with droplet hydrodynamics for high-throughput water activation.

papers.title: Manifestation of van der Waals interactions in the vibrational spectra of alkali metal dimers.
papers.abstract: This article is devoted to the analysis of the vibrational frequencies of alkali metal dimers from Li2 to Cs2 in the ground electronic state X 1Σ+ g, with the aim of identifying manifestation of van der Waals interactions at high vibrational excitation. Based on literature data on the energies of the vibrational levels G(v), vibrational frequency functions have been constructed: the first difference G1(v), representing the sequence of vibrational quanta (G1(v) > 0), and the second difference G2(v), representing the rate of decrease in their energy (G2(v) < 0). For five dimers, these functions have a similar form. The function G1(v) decreases monotonically with acceleration, and concavity appears near the asymptote. The function G2(v) increases in magnitude with acceleration up to an inflection point, where it undergoes a rapid decrease, forming the so-called tail. It is shown that, for the tail levels, the turning points r2 correspond to the van der Waals pair state. Since the excited molecule spends the maximum amount of time in the vicinity of the outer classical inflection point r2, at these energy levels the interatomic distances of ~3.5 Å (Li2)–~3.1 Å (Cs2) exceeds twice the van der Waals radius of the atom. It can be assumed that the valence contribution is small in these states. The main conclusion of this work is that a qualitative change in G2(v) for alkali metal dimers occurs in the same region of the potential well U(r), including the tail. The transition to van der Waals interaction occurs at a constant distance from the asymptote of approximately 120 cm-1, or, possibly, varying from 120 to 90 cm-1 in the studied series of molecules.

papers.title: Magnetic Control of NIR Lanthanide Emission in Molecular Complexes
papers.abstract: Magnetic modulation of luminescence has not been realized in molecular lanthanide complexes, whose spin–orbit coupled 4f excited states are well shielded from external perturbations. Here, we report molecular lanthanide complexes whose photoluminescence is controllably modulated by a magnetic field below 1 T through the spin dynamics of spin-correlated radical pairs (SCRPs). SCRPs, generated by photoexcitation of donor–bridge–acceptor molecules, undergo spin-selective radical pair recombination, thereby gating the energy-transfer pathway to the emissive lanthanide center (Ln 3+ ) through a pendant triplet acceptor in Ln 3+ complexes. Application of an external magnetic field alters the singlet–triplet SCRP interconversion, leading to field-dependent modulation of Ln 3+ emission intensity by up to 50%. This effect is observed at room temperature and is fully reversible. The successful demonstration of SCRP-mediated magnetic control of the Ln 3+ emission establishes a new design paradigm for magneto-responsive lanthanide materials and identifies SCRPs as viable quantum control elements for f-element luminescence.

papers.title: Redox-Metered Paired Electrolysis: A Strategy for Comprehensive Deaminative C(sp3)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: Interfacing transition metal catalysts with radical intermediates is a powerful paradigm for organic synthesis; however, it often requires the precise synchronization of independent catalytic cycles, and this requirement can limit scope and generality. We report a novel electrochemical strategy, which we term “redox-metered paired electrolysis,” in which the formation of a radical precursor in situ gates the rate of activation of its intended partner, thus promoting efficient cross-coupling across diverse substrate classes. We apply this strategy to the deaminative C(sp3)–C(sp2) cross-coupling of primary alkyl amines and aryl electrophiles, facilitated by the design of a bench-stable, dihydropyridine activating group. Notably, our redox-metered approach enables the cross-coupling of four categories of amines with five classes of aryl electrophiles—triflates, chlorides, bromides, iodides, and activated carboxylic acids—all under one unified set of conditions. Nineteen total pairs of amine and aryl electrophile classes are demonstrated to undergo catalytic cross-coupling (>75 examples), including seven that have not been reported previously. These novel pairs include elusive, yet valuable bond formations, such as the deaminative cross-coupling of phenol-derived aryl triflates with amines and the coupling of aryl halides with α-amino acids. Time course analysis supports the proposed mechanism and reveals design principles for future applications of this strategy.

papers.title: The Graph Fourier Transform Recasts Rouse Modes to Encode Polymer Sequence
papers.abstract: Rouse modes diagonalize the polymer connectivity matrix to describe how conformational motion is distributed over structural modes, yet the chemistry distributed along that same chain is traditionally encoded through hand-crafted, system-specific descriptors. Here, we generalize Rouse modes from bead coordinates to bead identity through a Graph Fourier Transform (GFT), which projects a chemically specific sequence signal onto the eigenbasis of the polymer graph Laplacian. The correspondence is exact for the combinatorial Laplacian, and holds by close analogy for its degree-weighted normalized counterpart. GFT descriptors predict the radius of gyration of architecturally diverse coarse-grained copolymers with accuracy comparable to a bespoke graph neural network and, with only the signal redefined, resolve liquid-liquid phase separation propensity in intrinsically disordered proteins. Predictive performance degrades with the degeneracy introduced by symmetric architectures. Generalized Rouse modes thus offer an architecture-adaptive and interpretable alternative to bespoke descriptors for sequence-controlled macromolecules.

papers.title: NanoFTIR spectroscopy probes solvation electrostatics in nanoconfinement
papers.abstract: The structure and electrostatics of liquids change dramatically under nanometric confinement, suggesting that solvent-solute interactions in such environments differ fundamentally from those in the bulk. Here, we combine nanoscale Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (nanoFTIR) with the vibrational Stark effect (VSE) to directly map the local electric field experienced by a molecular probe—the C=O stretching vibration of dimethylformamide (DMF)—within buried nanofluidic channels. To this end, we fabricated hexagonal boron nitride (hBN)-capped trenches with depths ranging from ~100 nm down to 2.6 nm and filled them with a 1:1 (v/v) aqueous DMF solution. Under the strongest confinement (2.6 nm), the DMF C=O stretching mode exhibits a +17 cm -1 blueshift, corresponding to a substantial change in the local solvation electric field strength of 0.39 V Å -1 . Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, combined with MD-derived IR spectra, reproduce the observed spectral shift and the associated change in local solvation electrostatics. The simulations further reveal the emergence of a quasi-phase-separated interfacial layer under finite-size confinement as the origin for the altered electrostatics. Together, these results establish nanoFTIR-based VSE spectroscopy as a direct and quantitative probe of nanosolvation electrostatics in nanoscale fluidic reactors.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Graph Neural Networks for Molecular Lipophilicity Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting molecular properties is a central challenge in cheminformatics and plays a critical role in drug discovery and materials science. Lipophilicity, which describes the partitioning of a molecule between lipid and aqueous environments, is a key physicochemical property influencing drug behavior. Although quantum mechanical methods can provide accurate predictions, they are often computationally demanding. In contrast, large experimental databases can be leveraged to train data-driven models such as graph neural networks (GNNs), which learn molecular representations directly from chemical structures. In this study, we compare four GNN architectures—graph convolutional networks (GCN), graph isomorphism networks (GIN), Graph Sample and AggregatE (GraphSAGE), and Attentive Fingerprint (Attentive FP)—for predicting lipophilicity using both regression and classification approaches. The models are evaluated on a benchmark dataset under consistent preprocessing, optimization, and training conditions. Our results show that the Attentive FP model consistently outperforms the other architectures, yielding improved predictive accuracy across both tasks. We further examine the impact of outlier removal during preprocessing, observing reduced prediction errors and improved robustness. These findings provide insight into the capabilities of representative GNN models for molecular lipophilicity prediction.

papers.title: DEEP LEARNING HELMHOLTZ ENERGIES FOR THERMODYNAMIC PROPERTY PREDICTION
papers.abstract: Based on SAFT equations of state (EoS), we propose a physics informed neural network that learns the residual Helmholtz free energy, yielding pressure, chemical potentials, entropy, and phase equilibria by automatic differentiation. Transport properties are connected through additional relations. The model can be pretrained on synthetic EoS data and fine-tuned with heterogeneous experimental data. The model operates on logarithmic scale and is designed to stabilize learning properties that span several orders of magnitude between phases, state points, and molecules. A differentiable transport model further allows viscosity and self-diffusion data to learn the temperature derivative of the Helmholtz energy during fine-tuning. As a proof of concept, we fine-tune the model to experimental temperature–pressure–density, viscosity, and self-diffusion data for water. Despite using only state point information and transport data for this single, particularly challenging fluid, the model predicts vapor pressure, vaporization enthalpy, density and entropy anomalies, and the critical temperature without direct exposure to these properties during fine-tuning. This demonstrates that jointly learning Helmholtz energies and transport coefficients is viable and beneficial. We argue that such Helmholtz energy centered, data driven deep learning models provide an alternative to the current proliferation of isolated, single property machine learning solutions. Generalization to unseen molecules and a fixed functional mode with optimized molecule representation parameters are also demonstrated.

papers.title: Validated thin-film microextraction-GC-MS reveals volatile metabolite signatures of Acinetobacter baumannii - Candida albicans interactions relevant to polymicrobial infection research
papers.abstract: Background: Microbial volatile organic compounds (VOCs) may provide information on pathogenspecific metabolism and interspecies interactions, but their reliable characterization as potential indicators for diagnosis of emerging infections requires a robust analytical workflow. This study developed an in-house hydrophilic-lipophilic balanced (HLB) thin-film microextraction gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (TFME-GC-MS) workflow for dynamic VOC profiling of Acinetobacter baumannii, Candida albicans, and their mixed culture, to evaluate its applicability to microbial metabolomics in pre-clinical biomarker discovery. Methods: The workflow was optimized and subjected to validation using a panel of 20 VOCs in tryptic soy broth. The method showed compound-dependent analytical performance suitable for comparative microbial volatilomics, with negligible carryover and sufficient sensitivity for profiling dynamic VOC changes. Results: Application to mono- and co-cultures revealed distinct temporal VOC patterns associated with bacterial, fungal, and interaction-dependent metabolism. The multivariate analysis indicated that among the 145 VOCs monitored, 57 showed significant changes in A. baumannii cultures and 60 in C. albicans cultures, while 33 compounds supported differentiation of the investigated culture types based on VIP scores. The co-cultivation produced a VOC profile that could not be accounted for by summing the volatilomes of the individual monocultures, indicating metabolic interactions among the microorganisms. Calibration-based analysis of selected target VOCs further supported the profiling results for representative compounds. Conclusions: The proposed TFME-GC-MS method is a useful pharmaceutical-analysis tool for preclinical prioritization of volatile biomarker candidates relevant to future studies of polymicrobial infections.

papers.title: Cation Coordination as a Molecular Handle to Program Synaptic behavior in OrganicMemristors
Weakening H-bonds facilitate Li+ transport in concentrated aqueous LiTFSI solutions
papers.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of the microscopic processes governing ion transport in concentrated electrolyte solutions is essential for developing efficient, water-based batteries and energy storage devices. LiTFSI has emerged as a model system for Waterin-Salt (WiS) electrolytes because it can be investigated over a wide concentration range. Here, we combine Raman and THz spectroscopy with classical MD simulations to elucidate the reorganization of the water network across concentrations ranging from 1 to 21 mol·kg-1. Isotopic substitution of H2O by D2O allows us to disentangle the distinct spectroscopic contributions of ion rattling modes and H-bond motifs in the THz frequency range. The analysis reveals two solvent-dependent modes in the region of the translational and librational water network modes, rationalized as an overall strengthening of directional H-bonds and a decrease in orientational preference. This picture is consistent with the accompanying molecular dynamics simulations, which predict a continuous shift from solvent-separated to solvent-shared to contact ion pairs, alongside a softening of water-water H-bonds and a broadening in the angular distributions within the water-water H-bond network. A thermodynamic decomposition further reveals correlations among the number of H-bonds, the observed spectroscopic nonlinearities, and the concentration-dependent conductivity. Our findings reveal a gradual, continuous reorganization of the water network as LiTFSI concentration increases: the red-shifted librational mode indicates a lower barrier for the angular part of the intermolecular potential, consistent with the simulated broadening of the angular distributions within the H-bond network. The impact on water dynamics and charge transport is discussed.

papers.title: Development of laser ablation negative-ion ICP-MS for direct fluorine imaging
papers.abstract: The spatial mapping of fluorine in solid samples is heavily hindered by its high ionisation potential in conventional positive-ion ICP-MS. To overcome this limitation without using complex plasma modifiers or mass shift strategies, we introduce laser ablation negative-ion ICP-MS (LA nICP-MS) as a direct approach for fluorine imaging. We systematically optimised the critical instrumental variables governing dry aerosol transport and negative ion extraction, revealing that the 19F signal is strongly driven by the conditions in the extraction interface rather than the core plasma thermodynamics. Operating at a lower RF power (down to 850 W) cools the extraction zone and promotes electron attachment, while a deflector voltage between 10-12 V provides optimal focusing of the negative ion beam under dry plasma conditions. Using matrix-matched gelatine standards, the method demonstrated excellent linearity and a representative limit of detection (LOD) of 10.2 µg g-1. The analytical performance of the method enabled mapping of the fluorine distribution in a cross-section of a honeybee (Apis mellifera) exposed to a perfluorohexanesulfonic acid (PFHxS) diet, revealing clear fluorine localisation within the abdominal gut architecture. Furthermore, simultaneous detection of 35Cl and 32S demonstrates the potential of LA nICP-MS for the multi-element imaging of non-metals in biological tissue. Overall, this study establishes LA nICP-MS as a direct alternative for fluorine imaging and provides basis for extending negative-ion ICP-MS to other challenging non-metals in complex solid samples.

papers.title: ONE-POT SUFEX–HWE REACTION: A THREE-COMPONENT ENTRY TO ALKENYL SULFONAMIDES IN BATCH AND PARALLEL SYNTHESIS
papers.abstract: A robust one-pot sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange – Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons (SuFEx–HWE) reaction was developed as a direct three-component entry to α,β-unsaturated (alkenyl) sulfonamides, an electrophilic warhead class of growing importance in covalent drug discovery. The key reagent, diethyl [(fluorosulfonyl)methyl]phosphonate, was prepared in four steps and obtained on a 70 g scale in a single run. Control experiments established that the amine reacted first at the sulfonyl fluoride (SuFEx), and the resulting α-phosphonyl sulfonamide then underwent condensation with the aldehyde, so that a single operation at rt converted an aldehyde, an amine, and the phosphonate into the alkenyl sulfonamide with complete Eselectivity. Optimization identified DBU (3 equiv.) – LiCl (2 equiv.) in MeCN as the batch conditions (up to 94% yield), whereas iPr2NEt proved to be more general for the compound library synthesis. In a uniform 520reaction parallel set-up, the two protocols gave synthesis success rates of 52% and 65%, respectively. Aliphatic amines and (hetero)aromatic aldehydes were the most productive reaction partners. Heteroaromatic amines demonstrated poor performance that could be somewhat improved by changing the base. In the case of aliphatic aldehydes, the results were also modest, and they could not be altered by the base variation. A homologous reagent bearing an α-methyl group extended the method to trisubstituted alkenyl sulfonamides (88 library members, 79% success rate on the optimal substrate set), albeit with moderate E/Z selectivity.

papers.title: Perovskite Photovoltaics in July 2026: Trap density and ion migration, self-assembled monolayer contacts
papers.abstract: Across 648 indexed publications evaluated this month, with 181 examined in depth, the verified performance ceiling reaches a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 33.1% in monolithic tandems and 27.31% in single-junction inverted devices. Tandem benchmarks rely on current matching across complementary bandgaps, whereas single-junction records depend on multidentate chelating agents and self-assembled monolayer (SAM) contacts that passivate undercoordinated lead cations and align interfacial dipoles. Yet only 22 closely read studies provide independently certified efficiency values, as uncertified reports frequently mask mobile ionic defects and non-radiative recombination under transient voltage sweeps. Scaling introduces severe resistive and geometric transport losses, establishing an area penalty that restricts certified efficiency to 27.31% at the largest reported aperture area of 766 cm2. This scaling deficit arises because molecular passivators that eliminate trap states on microscale cells aggregate during meniscus drying, intensifying non-radiative recombination across laser-scribed module interconnects. Operational durability evidence remains narrow across the literature: only 4 investigations quantify lifetime metrics, with the longest duration reaching 9800 h, while only 6 studies adhere to standardized International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS) protocols. A pronounced reporting disparity persists between claimed and verified performance, with 50.4% of abstracts reporting efficiency but only 8.3% documenting independent certification. Mechanistic evaluation demonstrates that contact stabilization through self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) and multidentate coordination fails to establish resilience against thermo-mechanical fatigue, as thermal expansion mismatches induce cyclic shear stresses that trigger interfacial delamination. Depth-resolved degradation profiles confirm that breakdown initiates at buried selective contacts before penetrating bulk absorbers. Chemical treatments and interlayers also fail to achieve permanent suppression of halide phase segregation in wide-bandgap absorbers, where illumination and thermal cycling drive phase demixing without resolving the boundary between thermodynamic stability and kinetic demixing arrest. Finally, unstandardized aging without continuous tracking leaves the division between reversible ionic polarization and irreversible lattice degradation unquantified.

papers.title: Coordination Alone Does Not Passivate Surface Halide-Vacancy States in Lead Halide Perovskites
papers.abstract: Molecular passivation of halide vacancies at lead-halide perovskite surfaces is conventionally attributed to Lewis-base coordination of undercoordinated Pb2+ sites. Density functional theory with spin–orbit coupling on FA0.75MA0.25PbI3 (001) shows this premise is electronically insufficient. Across ten additives, no coordination metric predicts which additives passivate: molybdic acid coordinates at 2.346 Å (−1.14 e) yet leaves the localized Pb(6p) defect trap intact (p = 0.128; +0.29 eV in HSE06), whereas permanganic acid coordinates at 2.156 Å (−1.06 e) and clears it (p ≤ 0.002). The outcomes exhibit discrete bimodal separation (Ashman’s D = 23.11) governed by specific interfacial chemistry: proton transfer forming a hydridic Pb–H bond (H2SO4, p = 0.008) or charge-transfer depopulation into an accessible acceptor manifold (HMnO4). This mechanism rationalizes the observed processing sensitivity of phosphate additives. Screening additives by coordination geometry cannot identify passivants; targeting proton delivery or redox-accessible acceptor levels can.

papers.title: A benchmark dataset of 86 intermolecular interactions of neutrals, ions, radicals and radical ions with water and hydrogen sulfide
papers.abstract: Guiding the selection of modern density functional approximations (DFAs) for intermolecular interactions requires diverse benchmark assessments. This work reports the development of a new test set of 86 binary complexes formed between either H 2 O or H 2 S and 31 selected partner species, comprising 15 neutral closed-shell molecules, 7 neutral radicals, 4 closed-shell anions, 2 closed-shell cations, and 3 cation radicals. The radical complexes are susceptible to delocalization error, while the interaction strengths span weak to very strong. Benchmark results are obtained at the coupled cluster singles, doubles and perturbative triples, CCSD(T), level, extrapolated towards the complete basis set limit from augmented triple and quadruple zeta basis calculations. This data is used to assess 17 different density functionals, spanning rungs 2 through 5 of Jacob’s Ladder. In common with other benchmarks, we find that the best functional on each higher rung of Jacob’s Ladder improves over the rung below, consistent with the potential to reduce the delocalization error. Only one functional, the ωB97M(2) double hybrid, achieves an RMS error of less than 1 kcal/mol. The best-performing hybrid is the recently introduced COACH functional, which has an RMS error just below 2 kcal/mol, while the best-performing meta-GGA and GGA have RMS errors above 3 and 4 kcal/mol respectively. These errors are dominated by the complexes that involve radical ions or neutral radicals. While the best-performing functionals are useful, these results indicate that further progress is still needed to address the delocalization error in intermolecular interactions.

papers.title: Cooperative Thiol-Amine System Enables Rapid Epoxy Curing with Balanced Thermomechanical Performance
papers.abstract: Epoxy thermosets typically exhibit a fundamental trade-off between curing speed and thermomechanical performance: thiol-cured systems enable rapid gelation but often produce low glass-transition temperature (Tg) networks, whereas amine-cured systems provide high Tg materials at the expense of slow curing kinetics. Here, we report a high-functionality, non-ester polythiol and a cooperative thiol-amine curing strategy that overcomes this limitation. Systematic variation of catalyst loading, epoxy stoichiometry, thiol-amine composition, and amine structure revealed strong structure-property relationships governing cure kinetics, thermal behavior, and adhesive performance. For the pure thiol-epoxy system, increasing catalyst concentration significantly accelerated gelation to minute-scale curing, while epoxy excess enhanced increased Tg without altering gel time. Hybrid thiol-amine formulations achieved substantially higher Tg than thiol-only systems while maintaining rapid cure, and the introduction of a primary amine largely eliminated the need for an external tertiary amine catalyst. Furthermore, the cooperative curing strategy proved effective across structurally different amine curing agents while maintaining rapid curing and balanced thermomechanical properties. This cooperative curing approach provides a simple and versatile platform for rapidly curable epoxy thermosets with balanced thermal and mechanical performance.

papers.title: Perovskite Photovoltaics in August 2026: Non-radiative recombination control and buried-interface treatment
papers.abstract: Across a monthly literature corpus of 531 publications, 144 were examined closely to evaluate defect passivation, contact chemistry, phase stability, and operational durability in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Independent certification establishes the performance frontier for monolithic tandem architectures at a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 33.66%, driven by complementary bandgap absorption that suppresses thermalization losses alongside optimized current matching. Inverted single-junction configurations established a certified PCE ceiling of 27.4%, achieved primarily through tailored self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) and molecular additives that passivate undercoordinated lead defects and suppress interfacial molecular clustering. Scaling these passivated contacts to expanded dimensions incurs an area penalty governed by transparent conducting oxide sheet resistance, interconnect scribe dead area, and spatial film non-uniformity, yielding an accredited PCE of 17.35% at the largest reported aperture area of 61.2 cm2. Operational longevity evidence remains sparse and disconnected from efficiency milestones: only 5 investigations quantified operational lifetime, with a maximum duration of 1400 h, while only 2 studies adhered to standardized International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS) protocols. Degradation pathways identified across this cohort include interfacial redox reactions between acidic phosphonic acid anchoring groups and polar processing solvents, photo-induced halide oxidation and ion migration, and residual lattice microstrain that accelerates phase segregation under continuous operation. Reporting practices reveal a pronounced discrepancy between self-reported claims and certified performance, as 55.5% of abstracts stated an efficiency value, whereas only 9.7% stated independent certification and only 18 articles reported verified values. Although intermediate-phase modulation and seed-layer crystallization mitigate interfacial voids and non-radiative recombination at hole-selective contacts during initial deposition, published evidence fails to confirm that these strategies arrest field-driven halide redistribution or contact degradation during prolonged operation. Resolving these bottlenecks requires operando chemical characterization under bias combined with standardized ISOS testing on scalable apertures.

papers.title: RINSE: A reciprocal-space fingerprint for comparing crystal structures
papers.abstract: Comparing crystal structures, whether to identify polymorphs, follow a phase transition, or search a database for a known motif, requires a descriptor that encodes the chemistry of a crystal while remaining invariant to the arbitrary choices made during structure determination or descriptor construction. RINSE (Reciprocal-space INvariant Spectral Embedding) is such a fingerprint, computed from a crystal’s diffraction pattern. By projecting the intensity-weighted reciprocal lattice onto a combined radial and spherical-harmonic basis, RINSE produces a compact power spectrum that is invariant to crystal orientation and to the choice of unit-cell representation, in tens of milliseconds per structure. The descriptor is inspired by the Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP) kernel but maps the full periodic structure rather than a local atomic neighbourhood. A locality-sensitive hash derived from principal-component analysis of the descriptor space enables rapid approximate retrieval of structurally similar crystals, and provides a convenient pronounceable identifier for a related group of structures. The RINSE code is freely available as an open-source Python package.

papers.title: PolyReader: an agentic LLM pipeline for extracting structured data from unstructured polymer scientific literature
papers.abstract: Machine learning for polymer design requires structured, sample-level records linking polymer identity, synthesis, composition, molecular-weight characteristics, processing conditions, and measured properties. Yet decades of polymer data remain dispersed across the texts, tables, figures, and supporting information of the literature, where individual values are often separated from the samples and experimental context they describe. Here we introduce PolyReader, an LLM agent for provenance-aware extraction of polymer data from scientific papers. Rather than treating a paper as a single block of text, PolyReader represents the manuscript and supporting information as navigable hierarchical section trees. The agent surveys this structure, selectively reads relevant pages, follows cross-references between documents, and integrates dispersed evidence into schema-validated, per-sample records. The resulting extracted fields are thus linked to its source document and page. On a benchmark of 42 polymer papers evaluated by trained annotators, PolyReader achieved F1 scores of 0.92–0.96 across 11 property categories, with comparable performance across three LLM models. Holding the LLM model, parsed document representation, and output schema fixed, PolyReader improved F1 by 13–17 points over single-pass prompting. These results show that reliable polymer-data extraction depends not only on recognizing individual values, but on reconstructing the sample-level relationships distributed throughout a paper. PolyReader produces records that are directly auditable against the primary literature, providing a scalable foundation for constructing traceable polymer datasets for machine learning. The extraction pipeline and benchmark annotations are released for reuse in the community.

papers.title: Broadband Visible Emission from a Rigid Ground State in an Ionic Zn-MOF Single Crystal
Advanced HILIC-MS Analysis of Therapeutic siRNAs with Non-Canonical Backbones and Conjugate Scaffolds
papers.abstract: The evolution of small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics toward increasingly complex chemical architecture has created analytical challenges for structural characterization. Confident sequencing and site-specific localization of modifications by tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) remain difficult due to non-canonical backbone chemistry, diverse chemical modifications and attached conjugates, all contributing to heterogeneous fragmentation. We present an ion-pair-free hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (HILIC–MS/MS) workflow that enables non-denaturing and denaturing analysis of conjugated, heavily modified siRNA constructs through temperature-controlled separation. Under non-denaturing conditions, duplexes can be evaluated to assess therapeutic integrity and stability, whereas elevated temperatures achieve duplex dissociation, permitting chromatographic separation and MS/MS analysis of sense and antisense strands. The method was benchmarked using multiple siRNA therapeutics of increasing structural complexity, including the unconjugated duplex ATU027, patisiran, a Huntingtin (HTT)-targeting siRNA containing an extended nucleic acid (exNA) backbone, and a GalNAc-conjugated siRNA drug, fitusiran. Complementary activation methods, including collision-induced dissociation (CID), higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD), and ultraviolet photodissociation (UVPD), produced extensive backbone fragmentation and high sequence coverage while also revealing conjugate-specific fragmentation pathways for GalNAc siRNA. Customized Nucleo-SAFARI software supported confident localization of chemical modifications, non-canonical backbone chemistries, and conjugation sites. These results establish temperature-controlled HILIC–MS/MS as a versatile analytical framework for robust structural characterization of complex therapeutic siRNAs.

papers.title: An Efficient Temperature-Jump Method for the Calculation of Heat Capacities
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a new method for calculating the heat capacity of molecular systems by means of highly parallel molecular dynamics simulations. In an approach using dynamical non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, a temperature perturbation is applied to the system, enabling enhanced sampling of equilibrium phase space. Calculation of the isochoric heat capacity of TIP3P is used as an example to validate this method.

papers.title: Systematic Bias in TD-DFT Absorption Predictions for Nucleic Acid Fluorophores
papers.abstract: Fluorescent nucleic-acid reporters are central to sequence-specific sensing and imaging, making reliable prediction of the absorption maximum () an important design objective. Due to the potential accelerated design of new reporters using computational methods, the present work benchmarks the performance of time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) against experimental values for a database of 116 chromophores that span literature-validated fluorescent nucleobase analogues and other small molecule probes. Three methodological variables are systematically examined: 1) the relationship between linear-response TD-DFT and the Tamm–Dancoff approximation (TDA), 2) basis-set convergence from double- through quadruple- quality with and without diffuse augmentation for two different families, and 3) the performance of 63 density functionals distributed across Jacob’s ladder. values computed with TDA are found to differ from full TD-DFT results by relatively small, systematic shifts and exhibit a near-linear relationship to the full response treatment, enabling straightforward post hoc calibration while retaining substantial gains in computational efficiency and numerical robustness. Basis-set effects are dominated by the double- to triple- step, and diffuse augmentation is essential, particularly for probes with charge-transfer or diffuse character. aug-cc-pVDZ provides an effective basis set for screening, whereas aug-cc-pVTZ offers a reliable approach for data refinement. Across the methods tested, B2PLYP emerges as the most accurate functional, with mPW2PLYP close behind, and M06 stands out as the best global hybrid. Nevertheless, the optimal method is not universal, being dependent on probe properties. Although lower-cost hybrid functionals such as M06 and B3LYP remain viable for neutral probes and near-UV applications, long-wavelength, cationic/anionic, and cyanine-like (charge-transfer based) chromophores remain the most challenging to describe computationally and are most reliably treated by SOS/SCS double-hybrid functionals, especially the range-separated variants. Overall, the recommended computational workflow offers a productive route for pre-synthetic color tuning of nucleic-acid fluorophores.

papers.title: The Core Matters: Aggregation of Neutral Ligand-Coated Nanoparticles in Membranes
papers.abstract: The aggregation of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) influences their optical properties, including localized surface plasmon resonance, through plasmonic coupling between adjacent particles. For hydrophobic AuNPs embedded in lipid membranes, however, the mechanisms governing aggregation remain poorly understood. Although coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations are well suited to study these processes, commonly used ligand–nanoparticle (NP) models neglect explicit core interactions. Here, we test whether core properties regulate NP aggregation by simulating multiple Martini NP models in a membrane environment. In contrast to the assumption that surface ligands effectively shield the core, we find that interactions with the environment remain sensitive to core parameters even at maximum ligand coverage. Furthermore, core–solvent interactions are consistent with a mechanism that directly drives nanoparticle aggregation. These results suggest that core interactions can contribute to the aggregation of functionalized nanoparticles.

papers.title: Accelerating Proton Affinity Prediction with Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Accurate gas-phase proton affinities (PAs) are essential for designing proton carriers in anhydrous fuel cells, yet high-level quantum-chemical calculations are too expensive for large libraries. We develop a multi-fidelity Δ-learning framework that corrects PM7 semi-empirical estimates toward high-fidelity references using only PM7 electronic properties and cheminformatics descriptors, without DFT-derived features. On a 1,155-molecule NIST WebBook benchmark, an ExtraTrees model correction reduces the PM7 mean absolute error (MAE) from 8.21 to 2.87 ± 0.26 kcal/mol, a 47% reduction over a calibrated PM7 baseline of 5.44 ± 0.39 kcal/mol. A DFT-descriptor-based model trained to the same experimental targets yields 3.17 ± 0.24 kcal/mol, demonstrating that PM7-based features achieve comparable accuracy while avoiding DFT cost at inference. We extend Δ-learning to the harder task of site-specific prediction against a B3LYP/def2-TZVP reference, across 251 diverse molecules and 821 site-matched protonation sites, reducing the raw PM7 error from 10.26 to 7.44 ± 1.00 kcal/mol, versus 8.23 ± 1.02 kcal/mol for calibrated PM7. Functional-group and SHAP analyses identify correction patterns and high-variance cases where direct DFT remains preferable. We then apply the RandomForest model in a seven-stage workflow screening for candidate anhydrous proton carriers, combining similarity retrieval, PM7+Δ-ML prediction, Claude Opus 4.6-assisted preliminary donor–acceptor motif screening, and Pareto selection. From 821,435 filtered ZINC molecules, 30 candidates were DFT-validated, of which 29 fall within the target window (210–235 kcal/mol). Applied prospectively to these 30 molecules, the correction lowers the raw PM7 error from 13.51 to 3.99 kcal/mol. The DFT PA window, motif check, and functional-group exclusion retain 26 candidates, and the five ranked highest by DFT proton affinity span 226.6–234.3 kcal/mol, at or above the 225.3 kcal/mol PA of imidazole. These single-molecule calculations prioritize candidates for experiment but do not by themselves establish condensed-phase proton conductivity.

papers.title: Extending AIMNet2 to Macrocyclic Peptides Through Data-Efficient Continual Training
papers.abstract: Macrocyclic peptides are among the most promising therapeutic modalities, yet no general-purpose machine learned interatomic potential (MLIP) has been validated for their conformational analysis. We show that AIMNet2 matches the accuracy of MACE-OFF23(S) on the MPCONF196 macrocyclic benchmark, despite macrocycles being entirely absent from its training data, at three-to sixfold lower computational cost. To close the remaining accuracy gap, we introduce a continual training protocol that integrates fewer than 25,000 domain-specific conformers (<0.1% of the training corpus) while preserving accuracy on non-macrocyclic molecules, reducing macrocyclic conformational energy RMSE by 25–27%. Applied to cyclosporine A as an independent test case, the continually trained model reproduces DFT conformational energies with sub-kcal mol −1 accuracy (RMSE 0.78 kcal mol −1 ) and correct rank ordering of all metastable conformers, outperforming all other tested MLIPs and semi-empirical methods. This continual training strategy, together with expanded non-covalent interaction coverage, has been adopted in the AIMNet2 (2025) release, which unifies small-molecule, macrocyclic, and intermolecular interaction treatment in a single production potential.

papers.title: Reaction-orthogonal solid-state reference enables potentiometric studies of vapor phase thermochemical catalysis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical mechanisms have been shown to be operative in the catalysis of numerous thermochemical redox reactions. These mechanisms have been elucidated by the measurement of the electrochemical potential of the catalyst during turnover (E cat ). A rich array of electrochemical tools allows for measurement of E cat during liquid-phase catalysis, but these are ill-suited to E cat measurements in higher temperature vapor-phase catalysis. Herein we report a solid electrolyte potentiometry (SEP) methodology that employs a Na β″-alumina solid electrolyte to measure E cat relative to the Na/Na + reference couple. As Na + is not typically a reactant or product in (electro)catalytic reactions, this reference is reaction-orthogonal, providing a common reference value for E cat measurement and analysis across diverse reaction classes and environments. Reaction-orthogonal SEP (RO-SEP) of Pt/C under H 2 enables measurement of the H 2 /H + equilibrium potential in the vapor phase across a wide temperature range from ambient to 325 °C. We find that promoting salts establish vapor phase proton activities comparable to their values in bulk aqueous medium, at ambient temperature. We apply RO-SEP to study the Au/C-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of 2-propanol to acetone and find that the catalyst is spontaneously and differentially polarized as a function of O 2 pressure under vapor phase reaction conditions. Simultaneous measurement of rate and E cat reveals a rate-potential scaling for vapor phase aerobic IPA oxidation that parallels that of liquid phase electrolytic IPA oxidation, suggesting a shared electrochemical mechanism between the two conditions. Lastly, H 2 /H + potentiometry reveals that alkali promoters in this reaction act principally via increasing the pH at the catalyst surface, which in turn enhances the kinetics of both the oxygen reduction and 2-propanol oxidation half-reaction. This reaction-orthogonal methodology for quantifying E cat enables broad-based investigations into the role of charge transfer in vapor phase heterogeneous catalysis.

papers.title: Hyperlocal Sensing and Inverse Modeling Reveal Community Impacts of Urban Air Pollutant Emissions
papers.abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 m × 150 m) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA — an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure — our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ~33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (~10 monitors; ~1 site / km 2 , compared with 6.7 sites/km 2 in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.

papers.title: Acidic local environments inhibit CO2 reduction catalysis on coinage metals
papers.abstract: The carbon-efficient electrochemical reduction of CO 2 (CO 2 RR) requires acidic electrolytes to mitigate irreversible CO 2 capture via non-faradaic CO 2 uptake and (bi)carbonate formation. However, CO 2 RR only takes place in acidic electrolytes upon addition of spectator cations and the mechanistic basis for this requirement remains unclear. Herein, we present scanning voltammetry experiments conducted in bulk acidic electrolytes in conjunction with differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS) analysis of CO 2 consumption and product formation. By quantifying both faradaic CO 2 consumption via CO 2 RR, and non-faradaic CO 2 consumption via the formation of (bi)carbonate in real-time, we deconvolute the direct role of the added electrolyte cations from their indirect role in fostering a transient local pH swing. We find that across coinage metals and electrolyte compositions, CO 2 RR commences only upon substantial depletion of hydronium and coincides with non-faradaic CO 2 uptake. Doping Ag with Pt to promote hydronium consumption via efficient H 2 evolution serves to lower the overpotential for CO 2 RR onset in scanning voltammetry experiments by ~1 V. These findings together indicate that an interfacial pH swing is a pre-requisite for, rather than merely a consequence of CO 2 RR, and that the primary role of the supporting electrolyte cations is to establish a non-equilibrium interfacial ionic environment depleted in hydronium ions. To rationalize these findings, we propose that acidic pH environments foster the formation of *COOH, rather than *COO − , and that this protonated intermediate undergoes unproductive fragmentation to CO 2 and H*, contributing to H 2 evolution, but not CO 2 RR. This work highlights the value of pre-steady state real-time analysis of both faradaic and non-faradaic interfacial reactions and establishes a self-consistent mechanistic picture for CO 2 RR in bulk acidic electrolyte.

papers.title: Hot-pressed, mechanically stable bipolar membranes for water electrolysis and CO2 reduction
papers.abstract: Bipolar membranes (BPM), composed of a cation exchange layer and an anion exchange layer, can enable steady-state operation at different pHs at the cathode and anode in electrolyzers. This enables the independent optimization of the cathode and anode catalysts for acidic and alkaline environments, respectively, which increases the scope for low-cost materials. Commercially available BPMs are operational only in a limited current range, therefore we aimed to develop custom BPMs for higher currents that are easily fabricated, mechanically stable, and suitable for storage in dry form. We used commercial single membranes combined with TiO 2 as the water dissociation catalyst in the junction, and have developed a hot-pressing method to prepare self-standing membranes that are mechanically robust, without a loss in electrochemical performance. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) was used to deconvolute the water dissociation resistance from other processes, leading to better understanding of the parameters that determine BPM performance. We demonstrate that the higher-performance BPMs surpass commercial BPMs for use in water electrolyzers, primarily due to a large decrease in the water dissociation overpotential to < 400 mV at 0.5 A cm -2 at 60 °C compared to ~1.3 V for the benchmark material. We also show how the membranes can be employed for high current density CO 2 electrolysis in a device structure that enable high CO 2 utilization efficiency, with the hot-pressed membranes achieving lower cell voltage and higher CO Faradaic efficiency compared to our previous reports with a custom BPM.

papers.title: Digestion and Orthogonal Click Conjugation Enables Nanopore Reading of Proteins
papers.abstract: Accurate characterization of bioactive peptides and proteins is needed to fully understand the origin of their activity. Nanopore reading enables polypeptide characterization at the single-molecule level. Here we describe a digestion-ligation method based on readily available reagents and benchtop equipment to convert peptides and proteins into DNA-peptide-DNA conjugates that can be analyzed by nanopores. Chymotrypsin digestion yields peptide fragments with C-terminal tyrosine residues suitable for oxidation-induced click chemistry. Subsequent selective installation of an azide on the N terminus enables installation of a template DNA strand needed for nanopore reading. The findings provide a facile approach to prepare DNA-peptide-DNA conjugates that has great potential for applicability to nanopore reading of many proteins.

papers.title: Investigating Segregation Effects in Mixture Adsorption in Mordenite Zeolite Using Monte-Carlo Simulations
papers.abstract: Configurational-Bias Monte Carlo (CBMC) simulations have been used to investigate segregation effects for adsorption of CO2(1)/CH4(2) and CO2(1)/C3H8(2) mixtures in Mordenite (MOR) zeolite. The segregation effects originate from the preferential location of CO2 in the 8-ring side pockets, and C3H8 in the 12-ring 1D channels; the CH4 molecules locate at both these sites. The segregated nature of mixture adsorption causes the quantitative failure of the Ideal Adsorbed Solution Theory (IAST) that mandates a uniform distribution of guest adsorbates in the zeolite framework. For CO2(1)/C3H8(2) mixtures, thermodynamic non-idealities cause selectivity reversals and azeotropic adsorption. Quantitative match with CBMC data is achieved by introduction of activity coefficients and use of the Real Adsorbed Solution Theory (RAST). The experimental data of Talu and Zwiebel (A.I.Ch.E.J. 32, 1263-1276, 1986) for CO2/C3H8 mixture adsorption in H-MOR are in remarkable agreement with the corresponding CBMC simulation data. The phenomenon of azeotropic adsorption occurs at the same composition in both data sets. The PN-DPL model of Ritter (Langmuir 27, 4700-4712, 2011) is able to anticipate the selectivity reversal phenomena. However, the PN-DPL model fails to match CBMC and experimental data at increased pore occupancies because entropy effects that favor CO2 are not properly catered for by the Ritter model.

papers.title: Data-driven strategies for enzyme engineering: From machine learning to protein language models
papers.abstract: Enzymes are key biocatalysts that drive diverse biological processes and industrial applications, offering sustainable alternatives to conventional chemical catalysis. However, the enormous enzyme sequence space and the limited functional annotation have created an urgent demand for computational approaches to accelerate enzyme discovery and engineering. Recent advances in computational methods are accelerating enzyme engineering from empirical trial and error toward predictive design. This review summarizes representative computational tools and predictive models in the enzyme engineering workflow, including (1) enzyme data resources, (2) functional enzyme discovery, (3) enzyme property prediction (e.g., kinetics, optimal temperature and PH, solubility, promiscuity, and specificity), (4) de novo enzyme design, and (5) computationally guided enzyme optimization. We further compare current computational strategies, discuss their strengths and limitations in different engineering scenarios, and highlight emerging trends toward foundation models, generative artificial intelligence, multimodal learning, and closed-loop design–build–test–learn platforms.

papers.title: An Attention-based Architecture to Decode Chemical Transformations from Process Spectroscopic Data
papers.abstract: Spectroscopy is a powerful analytical technique that promises precise characterization of chemical species and their transformations in dynamic chemical processes. Traditionally, spectral signatures are interpreted by calibrating against established spectral libraries. However, for complex molecular systems, mixtures of multiple interacting compounds, or dynamical processes, the resulting spectral signals become highly convoluted. Conventional deconvolution based methods rely on the availability of prior information to effectively decompose the measured data into latent components and infer chemical transformations using plausible reaction templates. However, the dynamics, scale, and dimensionality of process spectroscopic data make such deconvolutions increasingly difficult and often ill-conditioned. These limitations are particularly pronounced in industrial process settings, thus reducing their effectiveness for quality control, impurity detection, and reaction pathway identification. Towards the precise and automated elucidation of chemical transformations, we introduce an attention-based decoder architecture that not only mines the chemical transformations from high-dimensional process spectroscopic data but also facilitates the identification of key participating species without requiring prior knowledge of the reaction template, the number of participating species, or their initial profiles. We employ a spectral-specific learnable embedding that enhances the extraction of informative spectral features, thereby improving inference quality while reducing computational cost. Model inference involves monitoring attention weights through the proposed focal-score metric and identifying the underlying causal template using asymmetry-based directed acyclic graph (DAG) estimation. The correlation of focal scores along the spectral dimension facilitates the identification of participating species, whereas correlation along the transformation coordinate highlights the underlying transformation events. Thus, the proposed framework highlights the underlying chemical transformations encoded in the spectroscopic data while providing interpretability to the proposed decoder model. The efficacy of the developed method is demonstrated on systems comprising multiple chemical compounds undergoing several transformation steps, including the formation of short-lived intermediates and the presence of chemically similar species.
