Particular attention is given to density functional theory (DFT) as a mechanistic tool for resolving heterostructure stability, interfacial charge transfer, electronic structure, and hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔGH*). The review also assesses limitations in current computational descriptions of electrocatalytic interfaces, including solvent and electrolyte effects, potential-dependent surface charging, dynamic surface reconstruction, and the accuracy of commonly used exchange-correlation functionals. By integrating experimental observations with theoretical insights, this review identifies interfacial electronic coupling and local active-site chemistry as central determinants of HER performance, while highlighting oxidation stability, interfacial reproducibility, realistic electrochemical modeling, and scalable fabrication as persistent challenges. Finally, future directions combining controlled interfacial synthesis, operando characterization, and advanced constant-potential and solvent-inclusive simulations are proposed to accelerate the development of efficient and durable MXene/TMD electrocatalysts for green hydrogen production.

papers.title: Microphase Separation and Water Accessibility in Crosslinked Polyurethanes
papers.abstract: Polyurethane materials are among the most widely used synthetic polymers, yet the atomic-scale structural organisation governing their macroscopic properties remains largely elusive. Despite decades of study, the chain organisation of hard and soft domains in polyurethane remains poorly understood because experimental techniques cannot resolve chain packing and intermolecular interactions at atomistic resolution. Here we combine Monte Carlo-based downsampling of chain length distributions fitted to experimental data with an iterative crosslinking protocol coupled to molecular dynamics relaxation to generate fully atomistic models of heterogeneous polymers with varying crosslinking degrees, using toluene diisocyanate (TDI) and propoxylated glycerol-based polyurethane as a model system. The resulting models reproduce available experimental thermodynamic and structural data, and spontaneously develop microphase separated morphologies consistent with experimental observations. The simulations reveal that hard segment aggregation is a major organisational factor driving microphase separation. Within hard domains, interchain NH· · ·O=C hydrogen bonds dominate cohesive interactions, while atomistic resolution reveals aromatic packing motifs consistent with π-π interactions between aromatic rings in both parallel and perpendicular geometries. At the polyurethane-water interface, urea and amine groups are the most solvent-exposed and retain well-defined hydration shells, whereas urethane linkages remain comparatively shielded. Together, these results provide an atomistic account of hard domain formation and microphase separation in polyurethane, and establish how this morphology governs the accessibility of urethane bonds to catalytic cleavage. The approach provides a framework for investigating structure-property relationships in heterogeneous amorphous polymer systems, with potential applications ranging from enzymatic degradation to materials design.

papers.title: Simulation of Ultrafast Fe(II) Photoswitching Dynamics Triggered by Excitation within the Quintet Manifold
papers.abstract: The quintet-to-singlet back-switching process in [Fe(tpy)2]2+(tpy=2,2’:6’,2"-terpyridine), [Fe(dftpy)2]2+ (dftpy=6,6"-difluoro-2,2’:6’,2"-terpyridine) and [Fe(dctpy)2]2+(dctpy=6,6"-dichloro-2,2’:6’,2"-terpyridine), together with the photorelaxation dynamics of the [Fe(dftpy)2]2+ spin-crossover and the [Fe(dctpy)2]2+ high-spin complexes were investigated by full-dimensional trajectory surface hopping (TSH) dynamics. Following photoexcitation, the initial population of the 5Eg (5MC) state decays quickly via a branching mechanism of direct (5Eg → 5T2g) and 3MC-crossed (5Eg → 3MC→5T2g) processes, with the latter dominating the dynamics. The quintet-to-singlet photoconversion, the key step of the back-switching process, remains inefficient (<10%). This low efficiency arises because the singlet–triplet–quintet crossing region is readily accessible only during the initial sub-picosecond dynamics (<500 fs). Shifting the crossing region to improve its accessibility could substantially enhance the quintet-to-singlet conversion efficiency, suggesting that more extensive chemical modification could significantly optimize the back-switching process. Upon excitation to the quintet MLCT manifold, the population decays within <200 fs to the dark 5Eg (5MC) state (followed by the relaxation to the 5T2g (5MC) in less than 1 ps); only 1-2% of the initial population remains in the ligand-centered states in all complexes. In contrast, previous transient absorption spectroscopy experiments identified a long-lived 5/7MLCT state for [Fe(dftpy)2]2+ and [Fe(dctpy)2]2+, potentially because the analysis was restricted to picosecond timescales and probe wavelengths were used at which 5MC states are dark.

papers.title: A Metallic Ground State in a Niobium-Pyrazine Coordination Framework
papers.abstract: Conductive metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) based on low-valent heavy transition metals remain largely unexplored despite the strong metal-ligand covalency and extended orbitals that should favor electronic delocalization. Herein, we report Nb(pyz) 2 Cl 2 (pyz = pyrazine), a layered coordination framework with a metallic electronic ground state. Although charge transport in pressed pellets is limited by thermally activated grain-boundary hopping, the high room-temperature conductivity of 1.2 S cm⁻ 1 , temperature-independent Pauli susceptibility, finite Sommerfeld coefficient (g = 14.0(5) mJ K⁻ 2 mol⁻ 1 ), Wilson ratio close to unity, and periodic density functional theory calculations consistently demonstrate a finite density of states at the Fermi level. X-ray absorption spectroscopy further reveals a strongly delocalized electronic structure involving mixed Nb 4d, Cl 3p, and pyz p* states. These results identify low-valent early-4d ions as promising components for electronically delocalized coordination solids and extend metallic metal-organic frameworks beyond the 3d transition-metal series.

papers.title: The Role of In Situ Crosslinked Polysiloxane/Polylactide Micro-Networks on the PLA Brittle-Ductile Transition
papers.abstract: Polylactide (PLA) has garnered significant attention as a potentially sustainable substitute for conventional petrochemical polymers. This attention is attributed to several factors, including its renewable origin, biodegradability, and its compatibility with conventional polymer processing techniques. However, its inherent fragility restricts its broader utilization as an engineering plastic. In this study, the investigation focused on the thermally activated reactive modification of PLA with two functional polysiloxanes of varying molecular architectures. This modification was explored as a toughening strategy, with the objective of promoting the brittle-to-ductile (BD) transition through the formation of a locally entangled polysiloxane/PLA micro-network within the PLA matrix. Extraction, thermal, spectroscopic, and morphological analyses were conducted to confirm the formation of a crosslinked phase. The micromechanical deformation mechanisms of pristine and toughened PLA under tension, bending, and impact forces are discussed, revealing that the dispersion level, size of dispersed phase, molecular weight, and reactivity of the introduced soft phase strongly influence rheological and mechanical performance, leading to markedly improved mechanical performance. For instance, impact strength reaches ∼37 kJ/m2 at 1 wt% MOD1 and elongation at break increases to 90% at 5 wt% MOD2.

papers.title: Magnetic anisotropy of tellurium(I) and selenium(I)† in a Li3N host crystal
papers.abstract: Magnetic anisotropy in low-coordinate main-group compounds has recently emerged as a promising route toward realizing single-molecule magnet behavior beyond traditional transition-metal and lanthanide systems. In this work, we investigate the electronic structure and magnetic properties of selenium-and tellurium-doped Li3N crystals using a combination of periodic density functional theory and embedded ionic-crystal QM/MM multireference calculations. Substitution of Li(1) sites by Se(I) and Te(I) generates low-coordinate np3 configurations embedded in a highly symmetric crystalline environment. Periodic calculations reveal substantial differences in spin localization and covalency between the two dopants: Te-doping stabilizes a spin-polarized electronic structure with localized magnetic character, whereas stronger Se 4p–N 2p hybridization leads to increased delocalization and a non-magnetic DFT ground state. Multireference SA-CASSCF/NEVPT2 calculations show that both systems possess magnetically isotropic ground states dominated by a singly occupied σ bonding orbital, while the first excited states exhibit pronounced axial magnetic anisotropy arising from nearly degenerate π∗ x and π∗ y orbitals coupled through spin–orbit interaction. For Te-doped clusters, extremely small transverse g-tensor components (gx,gy ≈ 0.002) and large axial components (gz ≈ 3.9) indicate near-ideal magnetic axiality, slightly stronger than in the Se analogues. The larger spin–orbit coupling of tellurium also produces significantly enhanced spin–orbit splitting relative to selenium. These results demonstrate that heavy main-group elements embedded in suitable low-coordinate environments can support highly anisotropic magnetic states and further support theoretical design principles for main-group single-molecule magnets.

papers.title: BigMixSolDB: Extraction of a solubility database in solvent mixtures with an uncertainty-quantified large language model-based pipeline
papers.abstract: The rapidly expanding body of chemical literature contains physical data scattered across unstructured text and complex tables in thousands of publications. Translating this information into machine-readable formats is essential for training data-driven chemical models. The lack of uncertainty quantification in computationally extracted datasets makes manual extraction and curation still necessary. We here address this challenge and present an uncertainty-quantified data extraction pipeline. Our fully automated pipeline utilizes large language models (LLMs) to extract complex tabular and textual chemical data directly from scientific PDFs. We systematically assess several modern LLMs and document-to-text conversion frameworks. We benchmark the uncertainty in extracted data by comparison of our computationally extracted databases with large, existing databases on solubility that are manually curated. Our pipeline achieves between 93 and 79% of the literature contained data, with near-zero median log deviations for structurally matched rows and residual high-magnitude errors concentrated in a small subset of OCR, table-structure, unit-scaling, or reference-dataset discrepancies. We showcase the utility of our pipeline by deploying it to extract data from over 2,000 articles and generate BigMixSolDB, a comprehensive database on solubility in complex mixtures. BigMixSolDB comprises 280,273 solubility entries spanning single, binary, and ternary solvent systems. Our results demonstrate how integrated LLM-based pipelines can be used for literature data extraction that is comparable with manual curation. We envision that these frameworks can be used for large-scale, accurate extraction of literature data into datasets for machine learning applications

papers.title: Bridging MS2 Spectra and Chemical Space: Advances in Spectral Similarity, Molecular Retrieval, and De Novo Structure Discovery
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based metabolomics increasingly relies on computational methods to translate information-rich MS/MS fragmentation patterns into chemical insight, yet assigning chemical identities to spectra ("annotation") remains a major bottleneck because reference libraries cover only a small fraction of plausible compounds. In this review, we frame the field through the lens of two interacting representation spaces: spectral space, where MS/MS data reside, and chemical space, where molecules are represented by fingerprints, descriptors, or learned embeddings. We discuss how different design choices induce different geometries, what it means for spectra or molecules to be "close", and survey methods for representing and comparing spectra, representing molecules, and mapping between both spaces. We highlight emerging deep-learning trends for cross-modal alignment and retrieval, and we outline where the analogy to text-image learning breaks due to peak ambiguity, noise, and the one-to-many nature of spectrum-to-structure relationships.

papers.title: Paving the Way Towards a Compact Complete Chiroptical Toolbox
papers.abstract: Circularly polarised luminescence (CPL) spectroscopy is a technique with applications in materials chemistry, bioimaging, probing fundamental chirality, but conventional photo-elastic modulator CPL instruments remain bulky, expensive and slow. We report a compact single-channel CPL (SC-CPL) spectrometer that alternates left-and righthanded emission through a piezo-actuated pair of orthogonally aligned achromatic quarter-wave plates using a rapid CCD detector. This design minimises moving optics and eliminates the need for detector matching and pre-calibration. It can operate in various acquisition modes such as time gated acquisition mode for long-lived CPL emission and a quasi-continuous mode for short-lived CPL emission. Validation against a benchmark PEM-CPL system using a range of CPL emitters reproduced fine CPL resolution with high sensitivity, orders of magnitude faster. This blueprint SC-CPL reported herein paves the way towards the world's first complete compact chiroptical toolbox. This could lead to significant advancements with pivotal scientific and societal impact.

papers.title: The Gated Quantum Resonator: a reduced-representation Hamiltonian–network framework for gated driven–dissipative quantum systems
papers.abstract: High-dimensional driven–dissipative systems are often described either microscopically or through reduced models whose relation to the underlying dynamics is unclear. Originally motivated by geometrygated catalytic and enzymatic dynamics, the construction is developed here independently of any particular molecular application. We formulate the Gated Quantum Resonator (GQR) as a controlled reducedrepresentation framework in which selected coherent coordinates are modulated by structural or environmental gates. The retained coordinates are supplied by an upstream modelling step; no projection or truncation algorithm is introduced. From a gate-dependent Hamiltonian we develop complementary mode, network and port–Hamiltonian representations, distinguishing exact preservation properties from phenomenological closures requiring independent validation. Open-system dynamics are introduced through a GKSL generator. For the linear lossless sector, the specified mechanical–network map exactly preserves normal-mode frequencies and modal eigenspaces, while matched input–output equality is a consistency property by construction. An exactly solvable lossy three-state bridge then shows that a previously proposed coupling–loss–dephasing coordinate does not select a universal microscopic transport optimum. The framework therefore treats reduced models as generators of explicit mechanistic hypotheses whose spectral, transport and geometric consequences can be tested, narrowed or rejected by independent physical evidence.

papers.title: Machine learning-accelerated evolutionary Monte Carlo for rapid phase exploration of compositionally complex materials in reactive environments
papers.abstract: Compositionally complex materials, e.g. high-entropy alloys/oxides, have long been of research interest for their unique mechanical and functional properties thanks to the synergistic effects between the large number of components. More recently, they have emerged as a promising platform for the development of novel heterogeneous catalysts for thermo- and electro-chemical applications. However, computational investigation of the phase stability of such catalyst materials remains challenging due to the large design space and the complex active site dynamics under reaction conditions. In this paper, we present a novel evolutionary Monte Carlo algorithm which allows fast exploration of stable compositionally-complex catalyst phases in reactive environments and can be generalized for any catalyst materials and any reaction conditions. In detail, we will showcase that this method can be used in combination with finetuned machine learning potentials for predicting bulk and surface mixing/segregating behaviors of compositionally-complex catalysts under various reaction conditions with reasonable computational cost.

papers.title: Development of Improved Liver Steatosis Phantoms for Accurate Histopathologic Representation and Multimodal Imaging
papers.abstract: Despite advances in ultrasound-based noninvasive hepatic steatosis quantification, current methods remain insensitive to the microstructural phenotype of lipid accumulation, which influences outcomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. A methodology is introduced to generate tissue-mimicking phantom models that replicate the lobular liver histologic structure and pathologic patterns of steatosis. Phantoms consist of packed alginate capsules that mimic liver lobules and maintain continuous inter-capsule contact, embedded in agar. Lipid microparticles of controlled size and concentration are encapsulated within these capsules together with perfluorooctyl bromide microparticles serving as background scatterers. This architecture enables control of microscopic features (lipid vacuole size and density) and macroscopic organization (lobular-scale heterogeneity), both of which are expected to influence quantitative acoustic measurements, thereby more closely reproducing the histologic structure and acoustic behavior of healthy and diseased liver tissue. Phantoms with 0% and 20% fat (weight/volume) exhibit liver-like appearance on B-mode ultrasound imaging, with ultrasound-derived fat fraction and acoustic attenuation correlating with fat content. Chosen constituents enable compatibility with MRI and CT. This platform provides a structurally realistic model to refine and develop ultrasound liver fat quantification techniques and to support cross-vendor standardization, as well as cross-modality validation of ultrasound-based liver fat quantification using MRI and CT.

papers.title: A Bipolar Redox Metal-Organic Framework for Metal-Conversion-Free Symmetric Halide-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Rechargeable batteries predominantly rely on cation intercalation or metal conversion reactions, which often suffer from structural degradation, limited reversibility, and safety concerns. We report a symmetric halide-ion battery based on a bipolar redox metal-organic framework (MOF), in which energy storage is governed by reversible intraframework halogenation rather than metal--halide conversion chemistry. The bipolar redox chemistry of the μ 3 -oxo-bridged trinuclear copper centres in the MOF enables reversible halogenation and dehalogenation, allowing identical electrodes consisting of MOF microcrystals embedded within binder-free carbon nanotube (CNT) films to function as either cathode or anode depending on the halide species involved. Operando Raman spectroelectrochemistry reveals the underlying redox mechanism, while density-functional theory (DFT) suggests a thermodynamic preference for bromination over chlorination, rationalising the framework's dual functionality. In a symmetric configuration using a mixture of chloride- and bromide-based neat ionic liquids, the cell reaches a specific capacity of 68.7 mAh g -1 and an energy density of 35.4 Wh kg -1 under extended charging conditions. The cell operates for more than 200 charge--discharge cycles under repeated short-charge cycling. This non-flammable, moisture-resistant system composed entirely of earth-abundant elements highlights the potential of redox-active MOFs for alternative battery chemistries.

papers.title: Molarium: Agent-Generated Adaptive Software for Molecular Design
papers.abstract: Commercial drug discovery software has traditionally bundled three sources of value: the interface, the scientific models, and the specialized expertise required to run the models through the interface, thereby translating outputs into design decisions. Large language models, coding agents, and tool-using agents are beginning to unbundle this paradigm. Interfaces, analyses, workflow logic, and substantial portions of scientific software can increasingly be generated to meet the needs of a particular scientist, project, and question, while agents can automate sophisticated workflows that once required specialist users. This shift repositions where competitive advantage is created in computational drug discovery. More intuitive interfaces and faster execution alone do not fix model inaccuracies or broaden the applicability domain. As the underlying tooling becomes increasingly accessible and fluid, strategic differentiation will shift away from familiarity with a particular software package and toward superior preditive algorithms, more generalizable models, proprietary experimental data, accumulated discovery intelligence, and the human discernment needed to frame the right questions and evaluate the answers. Molarium, available at https://molarium.org , provides a case study of this transition in the context of molecular design software. Created during an intensive weekend effort of a tireless drug-discovery scientist and an AI coding agent, this open-source molecular workbench operates exclusively in a standard web browser. It integrates local molecular graphics, editing, conformer generation, energy minimization, molecular dynamics, machine-learned potentials, and protein-structure prediction workflows. Beneath its rapidly adaptable interface, Molarium maintains a versioned molecular state together with user actions, method specifications, provenance, and validation evidence. Decoupling an adaptable interface from an enduring scientific core points toward a broader architecture for generated adaptive software in drug discovery.

papers.title: Non-Isobaric Is Not Enough: Gap-Merge Safety for Unambiguous Peptide Readout
papers.abstract: Selecting a set of non-isobaric amino acids is the standard way to guarantee unambiguous readout when peptide sequences are used to carry information. We show it is insufficient. Because tandem MS reads residues as differences between consecutive fragment masses, a single missing b/y ion merges two adjacent residues into one observed gap; if that merged gap aliases a single residue mass, the decoder does not register a dropout but emits one confident, wrong residue. Non-isobaricity cannot prevent this, because the colliding quantity is a sum rather than a residue. We formalize the missing condition—gap-merge safety, |m(a) +m(b)−m(c)| > τ for all a, b, c in the alphabet—as a decidable predicate with a machine-checked soundness proof in Lean 4, and characterize the collision structure of the proteinogenic alphabet exhaustively: beyond the Leu/Ile isobar and the Gln/Lys near-isobar, exactly two summed-gap collisions exist, Gly + Gly = Asn and Gly + Ala = Gln, making glycine disproportionately expensive. In simulation, alphabets satisfying gap-merge safety produce zero silent errors at every fragment dropout rate from 0 to 0.4, where alphabets chosen by non-isobaricity alone produce 1.0% to 6.9%; every failure becomes a detectable erasure rather than a silent substitution.

papers.title: Trophic Transfer–Driven Predator Risk from Diatomite Nanoparticles Is Mitigated by a dsRNA Safety Switch
papers.abstract: Diatomaceous earth is widely used in pest management and other industrial applications; however, non-target ecological risks remain poorly resolved. Using a predator–prey microcosm model (Xylocoris flavipes and Tribolium castaneum), we show that diatomite nanoparticles (DNP) impact the predator primarily via trophic transfer after predators consume DNP-exposed prey. Predator mortality increased with prey pretreatment dose and was higher under trophic transfer than co-occurrence exposure, identifying food-web transfer as the dominant pathway driving predator mortality. To mitigate non-target effects while preserving pest control, we developed a double-stranded RNA (dsRNA)-loaded DNP formulation via APTES silanization and electrostatic adsorption (dsRNA@DNP). dsRNA@DNP maintained lethality against T. castaneum while significantly reducing predator mortality during trophic exposure. Release assays showed that dsRNA remained largely associated with DNP across low-ionic-strength and tested pH conditions but was substantially released under high ionic strength, consistent with reversible electrostatic association. Gene-expression analysis showed reduced Chc expression in the predator with no detectable reduction in the prey. These findings identify trophic transfer as an important pathway for non-target effects of diatomite nanoparticles and demonstrate a safety-by-design strategy to reduce predator mortality while maintaining prey suppression.

papers.title: Coupling Insoluble Pteroic Acid Using Quaternary Ammonium Salts: Synthesis of a Peptide Bearing a Folic Acid Moiety
papers.abstract: Herein, I report a unique coupling method for insoluble pteroic acid. Tetraalkylammonium hydroxide effectively enabled solubilization, efficient coupling with an amine, and an easy workup process to produce folate-conjugated peptides. The generality and versatility were confirmed through coupling studies of several amino acids, demonstrating its applicability to the synthesis of various folate and pteroate conjugates.

papers.title: Chainable DataFrame Framework for Interactive Chemical Data Processing with pdChemChain
papers.abstract: Computational chemists frequently build data processing workflows as ad-hoc scripts that are difficult to reuse, share, or deploy. Yet, many of the alternative workflow platforms demand significant complexity overhead or create manual breaks in workflows involving different pieces of software. pdChemChain is an open-source Python framework that bridges interactive use in python with reuse and deployment, by treating chemical data processing chains as composable, self-serializing pandas DataFrame operations. The framework is built around three design principles: (1) every operation takes a DataFrame and returns a DataFrame, (2) operations compose via the + operator into chains that are themselves operations, and (3) all chains are self-configuring, i.e. serializable to YAML for command-line deployment without code changes. Chains are built interactively in notebooks with immediate visual feedback, then deployed as-is via CLI or as scoring components in generative design frameworks. Built on widely used RDKit and pandas, pdChemChain provides links for molecular processing, property calculation, score transformation, and multi-parameter aggregation, while remaining extensible through a minimal dataclass-based API. pdChemChain is available at https://github.com/EBjerrum/pdchemchain under the LGPL-3.0 license.

papers.title: Connected, but for how long? A residual-lifetime criterion for the hydraulic–diffusive boundary in polyamide reverse-osmosis membranes
papers.abstract: The mechanism of water transport through the polyamide active layer of reverse-osmosis membranes is again contested: a 2023 claim that transport is governed by pore flow rather than solution-diffusion reopened a debate many considered settled, and a two-phase treatment has since shown the two descriptions are not mutually exclusive once their coefficients are matched. That reconciliation, however, answers a phenomenological question, not a structural one: whether a genuine, pressure-bearing continuous water phase exists is a separate, testable claim about the material. This Perspective argues that settling it requires two conditions prior work has largely treated as one — an instantaneous through-connected topology, and its survival over the transport timescale — and that the second condition has so far been estimated the wrong way: from the total lifetime of a connectivity interval rather than the residual lifetime seen by a water molecule arriving at a random instant, the same statistical root as the inspection paradox. A dynamic accessibility measure, Adyn = θ·SR(τtr), is proposed to close this gap, built on an intensive areal connectivity measure θ and a residual-lifetime survival function SR rather than an assumed exponential decay. A minimal structural surrogate places the connectivity transition at a model water-accessible volume fraction of 0.14–0.17, close to atomistic estimates for real polyamide, and a comparison of accessible simulation timescales with the residence time implied by realistic operating conditions shows why molecular dynamics alone cannot currently resolve the question. A concrete, falsifiable test agenda is proposed.

papers.title: Hidden Hypoxanthine Neighborhoods in β-Guanine
papers.abstract: Biogenic guanine crystals can incorporate substantial hypoxanthine (Hpx) while retaining the βguanine lattice, but whether the lattice discriminates both dopant identity and local neighborhood remains unresolved. Here, periodic DFT, site-anchored cluster cross-checks, symmetry-complete pair enumeration, and GIPAW 13C calculations connect these two levels of incorporation to experimentally testable observables. In a dry 6.25% fixed-cell model, N7H-Hpx is 21.78 kcal mol ¹ lower in electronic energy than N9H-Hpx; three cluster treatments preserve a 17.40–18.25 ⁻¹ lower in electronic energy than N9H-Hpx; three cluster treatments preserve a 17.40–18.25 kcal mol ¹ preference. A pure-crystal calibration excluding the embedded-Hpx resonance ⁻¹ lower in electronic energy than N9H-Hpx; three cluster treatments preserve a 17.40–18.25 predicts C5 shifts of 115.98 ppm for N7H and 127.94 ppm for N9H, placing N7H-Hpx in the experimentally reported 115–116 ppm region. At 12.5% substitution, 120 site pairs reduce to 13 symmetry-distinct orbits. Fifteen representatives were relaxed, and the corrected orbit means span 2.407 kcal mol ¹, with an adjacent in-plane orbit lowest; independent starts for four low- ⁻¹ lower in electronic energy than N9H-Hpx; three cluster treatments preserve a 17.40–18.25 energy motifs preserve this minimum. Fixed-geometry 700 eV reevaluation in a 4 × 2 × 1 association cycle gives adjacent- and far-pair association energies of −1.2219 and +0.0189 kcal mol ¹. Across four GIPAW pair models, C5 remains comparatively stable, whereas C6/C8 report ⁻¹ lower in electronic energy than N9H-Hpx; three cluster treatments preserve a 17.40–18.25 local arrangement: adjacent and separated motifs yield C8 splittings of 2.854 and 0.037 ppm. Together, the calculations show that the tested β-guanine lattice models discriminate both metabolite identity and relative placement. The resulting ¹³C signatures provide experimentally testable markers of how biologically supplied purine mixtures may become locally organized during biomineralization.

papers.title: Scaffold-Controlled Evaluation of Molecular Representations for Antimalarial Activity Prediction
InGaAs/InAlAs Avalanche Photodiodes: Recent Advances in Growth, Device Structure, Noise Performance, and Emerging Applications
papers.abstract: Inthisstudy,wereviewrecentadvancesin InGaAs/InAlAs avalanche photodiodes (APDs), which remain anestablishedandwidelyusednear-infrareddetection technology for optical-fiber communication, light detection and ranging (lidar), and single-photon quantum applications. This paper reviews recent progress in the epitaxial growth, device structure,andperformanceoptimizationofInGaAs/InAlAs APDs,withemphasisonmetalorganicchemicalvapor deposition(MOCVD)andmolecularbeamepitaxy(MBE) growthconsiderations,separateabsorption,grading,charge, and multiplication (SAGCM) device architectures, doping and gain-stage engineering for excess-noise reduction, and emerging directions including single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) for quantum key distribution, focal-plane array receivers for lidar, andmechanicallyflexibledetectorplatforms.Comparative performance againstalternativemultiplication-layermaterial systems is also discussed. This review highlights the trade-offs between thematurityoftheInGaAs/InAlAs system and the lowerexcessnoisedemonstratedbyantimonide-based alternatives,whileidentifyingopenchallengesinnoise suppression, thermal stability, and large-scale array integration for continued development of this device family.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for a Circular Solvent Economy: An Environmental Decision-Support Architecture for Sustainable Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Industrial decarbonization requires integrated digital strategies that combine artificial intelligence (AI), circular economy principles, and life-cycle thinking to improve the environmental sustainability of manufacturing processes. Pharmaceutical manufacturing is particularly solvent-intensive, with organic solvents contributing substantially to material consumption, energy demand, greenhouse gas emissions, and hazardous waste generation. Although green chemistry, solvent substitution, life-cycle assessment (LCA), and digital manufacturing have advanced sustainable process design, their integration into a unified environmental decision-support architecture remains insufficiently developed. This communication presents an Artificial Intelligence for Circular Solvent Economy (AICSE) framework that connects AI-assisted prediction, digital process simulation, circular solvent management, and life-cycle sustainability assessment within a structured environmental decision-support architecture. The framework retains Process Mass Intensity (PMI), Circular Process Mass Intensity (cPMI), Global Warming Potential (GWP), and Cumulative Energy Demand (CED) as complementary sustainability indicators within an LCA-oriented assessment structure. A literature-based Sertraline active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing process is used as an illustrative application to demonstrate how the proposed architecture can organize solvent evaluation, virtual process assessment, circular solvent recovery, and environmental decision-making. Building upon our previously reported solventcentric sustainability framework, this work extends its scope by explicitly integrating Environmental Artificial Intelligence, life-cycle thinking, Digital Twin, and circular economy principles into a transferable digital sustainability architecture for solvent-intensive manufacturing. In this work, Environmental Artificial Intelligence (Environmental AI) refers to the application of AI and machine-learning methods to environmental prediction, assessment, optimization, monitoring, and decision support within manufacturing systems. The principal contribution is architectural rather than algorithmic: AICSE connects previously independent components into a structured environmental decision-support pathway and introduces implementation-oriented readiness and maturity models. The framework is presented as a conceptual architecture supported by an illustrative literature-based application rather than as an empirical validation study. AICSE provides a practical pathway toward evidence-based sustainability governance, resource-efficient manufacturing, and progressively integrated environmental intelligence.

papers.title: Design and computational evaluation of reversible covalent cathepsin S inhibitors using molecular docking, ADMET, molecular dynamics, MM/PBSA, and density functional theory
papers.abstract: Cathepsin S (CatS) is unique among lysosomal cathepsins in retaining significant proteolytic activity under extracellular conditions. Its extracellular activity has been implicated in tumour progression, chronic inflammation, autoimmune disorders, and cardiovascular diseases, making CatS an attractive target for the development of selective covalent inhibitors . In the present study, a series of 100 α-cyanoacrylamide derivatives was rationally designed and evaluated using computational approaches. The compounds were first assessed by rigid molecular docking. Top candidates were selected for pharmacokinetics study and initial 25 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for further stability evaluation. Based on these results, Compounds F7 and F48 were subjected to density functional theory (DFT) calculations, covalent and non-covalent induced fit docking, followed by 100 ns MD simulations. Complex stability and binding behaviour were further examined using root mean square deviation (RMSD), root mean square fluctuation (RMSF), hydrogen-bond analysis, free-energy landscape analysis, per-residue energy decomposition, and molecular mechanics Poisson-Boltzman surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations. F7 consistently showed more favorable behaviour than F48 throughout the study. It maintained a stable binding mode, persistence interactions with key active site residues, and favorable accommodation of its alkyl substituent within the S2 binding pocket. These observations were supported by lower conformational fluctuations, stronger residue-level energetic contributions, and a more favorable MM/PBSA binding free energy (-33.47 kcal/mol) and than F48 (-27.72 kcal/ mol). The findings provide a molecular basis for the design of extracellularly targeted covalent CatS inhibitors and identify F7 as a suitable scaffold for further experimental investigations.

papers.title: Low-Energy Photocatalysis Platform for Direct Regiospecific α-C(sp3)ꟷH Alkynylation of Tertiary Amines
papers.abstract: Propargylamines constitute a valuable class of α-alkynyl amines that are widely encountered in medicinal chemistry and chemical biology. Herein, we report a regiospecific α-C(sp3)–H alkynylation of tertiary amines that enables the direct synthesis of propargylamines from unactivated tertiary amines and terminal alkynes. The transformation proceeds under mild, base-free conditions using sustainable low-energy photon irradiation and is initiated by single-electron-transfer (SET) activation of the tertiary amine, generating a reactive iminium intermediate that undergoes nucleophilic coupling with a transient Cu(I)–acetylide species. The protocol accommodates a diverse range of tertiary amines and terminal alkynes, including bioactive molecules and pharmaceuticals, providing access to structurally diverse internal alkynes and versatile click-ready terminal alkynes with excellent functional-group tolerance. The synthetic utility of the method is further demonstrated through gramscale reactions, while comprehensive mechanistic investigations provide insights into the photoredox and copper catalytic pathways underlying this transformation.

papers.title: Reversible CO2 Concentration in the Electrical Double Layer in the Absence of (Bi)carbonate
papers.abstract: The behaviour of CO 2 at electrode-electrolyte interfaces is key in the development of climate change mitigation technologies, such as electrochemical CO 2 capture and conversion. In particular, electrochemical CO 2 capture using supercapacitors, an approach known as supercapacitive swing adsorption (SSA), utilises the charging and discharging of supercapacitor devices to reversibly and selectively adsorb CO 2 . As supercapacitive charging incurs low energy losses and can be carried out under ambient conditions, this method has the potential to achieve higher energy efficiencies than other CO 2 capture techniques. However, the design of SSA systems has been hindered by a lack of understanding of the underlying mechanism. In particular, the contributions of different CO 2 -related species—molecular CO 2 , carbonate, and bicarbonate—to SSA remain poorly understood. In this work, the role of molecular CO 2 in SSA using activated carbon electrodes was explored in the absence of carbonate and bicarbonate ions by using an inert organic electrolyte solvent, acetonitrile. Interestingly, this system was capable of reversible electrochemical CO 2 adsorption, which demonstrated definitively that molecular CO 2 is a contributing active species in SSA. It was found that exchanging the gas headspace from N 2 to CO 2 increased the capacitance of both aqueous and acetonitrile-based supercapacitors. This was attributed to the accumulation of CO 2 (in acetonitrile) and/or CO 2 -derived anions (in water) at the electrode-electrolyte interface, modifying the properties of the dielectric and, therefore, influencing charge storage behaviour in the electrical double layer. This reversible concentration of CO 2 in the electrical double layer of supercapacitors presents opportunities for further development in electrochemical CO 2 capture and conversion technologies.

papers.title: High-Throughput Experimentation Enables the C6-Functionalisation of 1H-Indazol-3-Amines as Antitubercular Agents
papers.abstract: The development of novel antitubercular drugs targeting mycobacterial thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) has previously been hampered by the synthetic intractability of promising benzisothiazole-based inhibitors. Here, we identify 6-substituted 1H-indazol-3-amine as a bioisosteric scaffold that offers a comparable binding mode and improved synthetic accessibility. To address the lack of established protocols for the derivatisation of this scaffold at the C6 Position, we carried out a high-throughput experimentation (HTE) campaign with 984 individual reactions. Through parallel screening, the reaction condition space for Suzuki-Miyaura and Buchwald-Hartwig cross-couplings was systematically mapped, identifying a set of generally applicable conditions. Biochemical evaluation of the resulting library validated the bioisosteric design, yielding several derivatives with enhanced inhibitory activity against mycobacterial TrxR, including a micromolar inhibitor. Co-crystal structures of five derivatives could be obtained. This study establishes a synthetic foundation for exploring the 1H-indazol-3-amine scaffold and demonstrates how HTE can successfully address synthetic challenges in fragment-based drug discovery.

papers.title: On Coupled Cluster Theory and Beyond
papers.abstract: Coupled cluster (CC) theory is the “gold standard” of molecular electronic structure theory, yet the full arc of the subject—from its variational origins in Hartree–Fock theory, through the exponential ansatz and its diagrammatic machinery, to its modern reformulation as a system of polynomial equations on an algebraic variety, its multireference generalizations, and its emerging reincarnation as a quantum circuit—is rarely presented as a single connected narrative. This review builds that narrative completely from first principles and carries it through to today’s research frontier. Starting from the electronic Schrödinger equation, we derive Hartree–Fock theory, second quantization, and Wick’s theorem; construct the coupled cluster singles-and-doubles (CCSD) equations via the similarity-transformed Hamiltonian; and show how these same equations reappear, verbatim, as a truncated eigenvalue problem on a projective variety generalizing the Grassmannian, with a computable CC degree controlling the number of solutions. We then develop the perturbative triples correction CCSD(T), the linear-response equationof-motion (EOM-CC) framework for excited, ionized, and electron-attached states, the effective-Hamiltonian formalism underlying multireference coupled cluster theory and its notorious intruder-state problem, and the unitary coupled cluster (UCC) ansatz that restores the variational principle at the cost of an infinite operator expansion—tamed, on a quantum computer, by Trotterization and the variational quantum eigensolver. We close with a synthesis of what is rigorously known about the resulting nonlinear equations, a map of directions deliberately left out of scope, and an assessment of the open question of quantum advantage in this domain. Every claim is stated formally, with a full statement and proof or proof sketch, and cited to its origin; the computational cost of every method is compared explicitly throughout.

papers.title: A glass-box foundation model for density functional theory
papers.abstract: Machine-learned exchange–correlation functionals promise accuracy beyond traditional forms, yet so far they trade interpretability for flexibility. Here we introduce DL-xDH26, a glass-box foundation model for density functional development on the fifth rung of Jacob’s ladder, with separate exchange and correlation expert towers, interpretable enhancement-factor and shift parameters relative to a physical base, and exact degree-one homogeneity. Trained exclusively on relative energies, it recovers atomic exchange and correlation energies and their quantum shell structure, and produces smooth, size-consistent dissociation curves without dispersion corrections, while reaching errors below 1 kcal/mol on the GMTKN55 and MGCDB84 benchmark suites. Lightweight fine-tuning then specializes the same backbone to cyclization reactions, distorted organic geometries, and organometallic reaction energetics while retaining its broad accuracy.

papers.title: Self-Association Propensity of Three Organic Battery Solvents Probed by Infrared Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Cyclic organic carbonates possess high dipole moments, and are extensively used as electrolyte solvents in lithium-ion batteries due to their high dielectric constants, low toxicity, and low flammability. However, intermolecular associations may reduce the availability of solvent molecules for effective coordination with lithium ions, an essential attribute of the battery solvents. Therefore, a preferred carbonate should have lower tendency to undergo selfassociation, where C-H…O-type hydrogen bonding also plays a significant role. In this work, the self-association behavior of propylene carbonate (PC), methoxy propylene carbonate (MPC), and vinyl ethylene carbonate (VEC) was investigated using concentration-dependent Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy in CCl4 solutions at room temperature. Particular attention was given to the νC=O stretching region, where progressive broadening and the emergence of lower-wavenumber bands with increasing concentration indicate the formation of intermolecularly associated species. Experimental band deconvolution, combined with density functional theory calculations at the B3LYP-D3/6-311++G(d,p) level using an IEFPCM CCl4 solvent model, enabled assignments of the observed features to monomeric, dimeric, and trimeric species. The calculated structures reveal antiparallel orientations of the carbonyl groups in the dimers, stabilized by intermolecular C–H… O hydrogen bonding, while the trimers are predominantly stabilized by similar interactions. Among the three carbonates, PC exhibits the strongest tendency toward self-association, followed by MPC and VEC. The comparatively weaker self-association of VEC suggests a greater availability of free solvent molecules for lithium-ion solvation, indicating its potential advantage over PC and MPC as an electrolyte solvent.

papers.title: Superhydrophobic-Like Complete Rebound of Impacting Water Droplets on a Smooth Oleic- Acid-Coated Phenyl-Silica Surface
papers.abstract: We report impact-induced water-droplet rebound on a nanoscopically smooth phenyl-silica surface bearing an oleic-acid liquid layer with a nominal cast-equivalent thickness of ≈1 µm, retained on the substrate through interactions previously attributed to COOH–π association. High-speed imaging (5000 fps) of 10 µL water droplets resolves complete rebound at all sampled conditions from Weber number (𝑊𝑒) = 0.69 to 3.99 and partial rebound with satellite ejection at 𝑊𝑒 = 6.03 and 7.14; a near-zero-impact reference showed no liftoff during the recorded interval. The apex-based rebound proxy (𝑒apex) varied nonmonotonically, reaching 0.72 ± 0.02, whereas the apparent residence time of 16–21 ms showed no systematic dependence on 𝑊𝑒 and remained close to the inertial-capillary timescale. These kinematics are comparable to rebound regimes reported for smooth solids and liquid interfaces. Entrained-gas-film dynamics and the response of the oleic-acid layer are discussed as mechanistic hypotheses, while neither gas-film continuity nor lubricant redistribution was directly resolved. The results establish rapid impact-induced water shedding on a smooth, texture-free oleic-acid-coated interface and motivate future tests of lubricant retention under repeated water impact.

papers.title: Semiclassical initial value representation in curvilinear coordinates
papers.abstract: A semiclassical propagator originally defined on Euclidean space is systematically extended to general curvilinear coordinate systems. This method time-evolves nuclear wave packets on the fly in curvilinear coordinates, without prior construction of global potential energy surfaces or complicated kinetic energy operators, and enables dimensionality reduction by isolating the physically essential degrees of freedom through coordinate constraints. By propagating the dynamics in a redundant coordinate space, the coordinate singularities inherent to curvilinear systems are circumvented in a numerically robust manner. In addition, the topology of each coordinate—such as its periodicity and boundary conditions—is properly taken into account by modifying the coherent state basis of the propagator. We applied this approach to molecular motions that are difficult to describe in conventional normal coordinates—pure rotation of hydrogen and methane, ro-vibrational dynamics of hydrogen, and large-amplitude torsional motion of butane—and reproduced reference eigenenergies and the characteristic features of the corresponding spectra.

papers.title: Clustered Graph Partitions Provide Compact Diabatic Bases for RCI-LC-DFTB Charge-Transfer Calculations
papers.abstract: Restriction-based configuration interaction long-range corrected self-consistent charge density functional tight binding (RCI-LC-DFTB) is an efficient approximate quantum chemical method that uses non-orthogonal diabatic states to describe molecular chargetransfer states. However, its practical performance depends on how the charge-localized diabatic states are selected. Here, we develop and compare two graph-based strategies for automated diabatic-basis construction: a discrete graph Fourier representation and a clustered biconnected-partition representation. Applications to benzene-assembly benchmark systems show that the discrete graph Fourier representation provides a systematic expansion that can require many diabatic states, whereas the clustered biconnected- partition representation gives a more compact and chemically interpretable basis. We further apply the clustered representation to a 16-residue aromatic oligoamide foldamer under an external electric field, demonstrating unit-resolved analysis of field-induced long-range charge localization. These results show that clustered graph partitions

papers.title: A single reference-energy outlier nearly eliminates Co–O chemistry from a generative model's training distribution
papers.abstract: An element-resolved audit of 44,688 oxide structures generated by MatterGen under chemical-system conditioning revealed that the aggregate composition compliance (73.27% exact match) concealed a severe chemistry-specific failure. Cobalt was omitted from 71.27% of the structures requesting it, against 8.12 ± 3.28% for the other 19 requested elements, and 98.17% of the cobalt omissions removed cobalt alone. Cell size, cation substitutability, stability gain and a general training-frequency effect did not account for the anomaly. Tracing the failure upstream showed that only one of the 8,924 cobalt oxides in the public Alex-MP-20 reference set passed the stability filter. The deficit was traced to a single anomalous reference-energy entry distorting the Co–O convex hull; excluding it raises the number of training-eligible cobalt oxides from 1 to 2,499. Four independent DFT calculations and the current Materials Project value agree within 0.024 eV atom-1, whereas the value implied by the released file deviates from them by 6.26 eV atom-1. A pre-registered intervention experiment showed that neither removal of the stability condition nor stronger diffusion guidance normalised the blind spot. These results show how a single high-leverage reference-energy anomaly can be amplified through stability filtering into a training deficit at the scale of a chemical family. Two audits that detect this class of failure without retraining are presented, namely an element-resolved condition-fidelity audit and a reference-hull vertex audit.

papers.title: Unraveling the Infra-Red Plasmons of Ferromagnetic Cobalt Nanorods with EELS
papers.abstract: Localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) in cobalt nanoparticles could offer a cost-effective alternative to noble metals for plasmonic applications, while leveraging their inherent magnetic and catalytic features. Yet the ferromagnetic nature of these objects and their extremely fast oxidation prevent the formation of stable colloidal dispersions, complicating conventional optical characterization in solution or thin films. To address this challenge, we employ electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) in a scanning transmission electron microscope 2 (STEM) to directly probe the plasmonic response of individual ferromagnetic cobalt nanorods. Our experimental findings, supported by numerical simulations, reveal anisotropy-driven optical modes in the infrared region, attributed to dipolar and quadrupolar resonances. This work not only demonstrates the plasmonic potential of cobalt nanostructures but also establishes EELS-STEM as a powerful tool for investigating plasmonic phenomena in magnetically active nanomaterials.

papers.title: Synthesis of 15N-Labelled Complex Saturated N-Heterocycles via Late-Stage Carbonyl-to-Nitrogen Swap
papers.abstract: ‡Process Research and Development, Merck & Co., Rahway, New Jersey 07065, United States ABSTRACT: Efficient construction of 15N-labelled complex saturated N-heterocycles remains a substantial challenge. Here we report a late-stage carbonyl-to-15N skeletal modification strategy that converts complex cyclic ketones directly into 15Nenriched saturated heterocycles. This transformation is enabled by a methylsulfonyl-based 15N-labelled azonation reagent that suppresses unwanted overoxidation without compromising the desired C-C bond cleavage pathway. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope and tolerates a wide range of functional groups, serving as an effective tool for late-stage skeletal modifications of complex natural products and drug-like molecules. Mechanistic insights on the sequential double C–C activation events have been elucidated by preliminary computational studies.

papers.title: TASTET: a Python package for geometry-driven selection of representative atomistic structures from large configurational spaces
papers.abstract: Modern atomistic workflows generate large ensembles of molecular and materials structures, yet only a fraction can be evaluated using first-principles methods. Existing down-selection strategies typically rely on estimated energies, implicitly optimizing for energetic ranking rather than representative coverage of configurational space. Here, we present a geometry-based framework for representative structure selection that maximizes configurational diversity prior to electronic-structure calculations. The framework maps local chemical environments into global measures of structural similarity, which space-filling algorithms use to select diverse subsets with uniform configurational coverage. We demonstrate its performance through two case studies spanning conformational and configurational ensembles. Selecting only 3% of a 949-member Rh-complex conformer ensemble recovered the principal energetic regions of the conformational landscape, and selecting just 0.3% of 10,000 oxide-supported metal nanocluster structures likewise revealed the dominant structure–energy relationships. These results establish representative structure selection as a transferable geometry-driven strategy for maximizing information gained from demanding first-principles calculations.

papers.title: Direct-to-biology approach for the selective identification of ligands for alpha-synuclein aggregates
papers.abstract: The selective targeting of α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregates represents a critical challenge for the diagnosis and treatment of Parkinson’s disease and related synucleinopathies. While several ligands have been developed for amyloid imaging, most of them lack sufficient specificity for α-syn over other amyloid fibrils. We report here a direct-to-biology (D2B) strategy to accelerate the identification of such selective ligands. A library of 384 piperazine-derived compounds was synthesized in a plate-based format and screened to evaluate their affinity for α-syn pathogenic aggregates compared to amyloid-beta 42 (Aβ42) fibrils. Nine compounds were found to bind preferentially to α-syn aggregates, three of which displayed at least a four-fold increased binding compared to Aβ42. Further validation of those molecules using in vitro α-syn fibrils enabled to determine a new potent selective binder of fibrillar α-syn with moderate affinity (181 nM). These findings validate the potential of D2B approaches to accelerate specific ligand development for pathogenic protein aggregates.

papers.title: What actually moves virtual screening performance: two measured resolution limits and a pre-registered decomposition of six interventions
papers.abstract: Reported improvements to structure-based virtual screening are usually differences in AUROC or enrichment between two protocols on one benchmark. We asked what a benchmark of typical size can actually resolve, and then measured six interventions against that limit with the reading rule for each committed to version control before the data existed. Two limits, not one. Scoring the same Vina poses with a second implementation of the same scoring function—agreeing at r = 0.970, no compound differing by more than 2 kcal/mol—moves AUROC by 0.020 [95% CI 0.011, 0.029]. Re-running the whole protocol at a different search effort and scoring it the same way moves AUROC by 0.039 [0.024, 0.056]. The first bounds a comparison of scoring functions on fixed poses; the second bounds a comparison of protocols, which is what most published improvements are. Both fall inside the range in which docking improvements are typically reported. On SARS-CoV-2 Mpro: changing the scoring function on identical poses moved AUROC +0.140, repairing a receptor preparation defect +0.045, scoring the pose ensemble rather than the top pose +0.019, substituting DiffDock-L pose generation +0.017, supplying the correct binding site to a cofoldingmodel −0.013, and eight-fold search effort −0.019. Read against each arm’s own pre-registered bar, one is supported at full strictness, one directionally, and the rest are not. Read against the resolution limits measured here—which were fixed after four of the six bars, and so are reported alongside those readings rather than in place of them—one clears, one is marginal, and four fall inside. The search-effort result is the sharpest either way: its measured effect is smaller than the run-to-run reproducibility of the protocol it was measured in. Docking adds nothing demonstrable over seven free physicochemical descriptors on either panel we assembled: on Mpro it significantly subtracts (−0.002 [−0.004, −0.000]) and on Factor Xa its +0.015 [−0.003, +0.034] crosses zero. Applying the same descriptors to LIT-PCBA gives a median AUROC of 0.7260 across 15 targets against published AutoDock Vina at 0.581 and GNINA at 0.611–0.616. These descriptor baselines are supervised on each benchmark’s own labels while docking is not, so this is a bias control in the sense of Sieg et al., not a claim that descriptors are a deployable substitute. On the AVE-debiased variant the descriptor median falls to 0.6510. One method exceeded the floor. Boltz-2, an open-weights co-folding model scoring compounds from sequence and SMILES alone, does not beat the descriptor baseline on its own (Mpro +0.026, Factor Xa +0.019, both intervals spanning zero) but adds +0.093 [+0.062, +0.125] and +0.075 [+0.051, +0.099] respectively when combined with those descriptors. Its advantage is not that it is less property-driven—descriptors explain 63% of its score and 63% of Vina’s—but that on Mpro its residual, the part orthogonal to those descriptors, ranks actives at 0.642 where five docking scores we measured sat between 0.507 and 0.559.

papers.title: Revealing Elusive Polymorphism in a Highly Luminescent β-Cyano-Substituted Distyrylbenzene Using MicroED
papers.abstract: The elusive dimorphic β-(outer) regioisomer of a cyano-substituted distyrylbenzene derivative (PDN-4) was characterized using MicroED. Despite having identical substituents to α-(inner) regioisomer, β-PDN-4 exhibits an exceptionally rare syn-rotamer alongside an anti-conformation, leading to distinct photophysical properties that are well supported by theoretical calculations.

papers.title: Optical fiber chemistry for catalysis: a programmable optical fiber membrane electrode platform for reaction chemistry and engineering
papers.abstract: Optical fiber chemistry (OFC) is a catalytic platform in which optical fibers actively provide photon transport, interface construction, and process control. This article develops an optical fiber membrane electrode (OFME) framework encompassing architecture, mechanisms, process intensification, and programmable control. Its anode fiber catalytic layer–ion-exchange membrane–cathode fiber catalytic layer sandwich couples internal photon transport, charge transfer, ion conduction, catalytic sites, and fluid-phase mass transport within one membrane-electrode reaction domain. Equation-driven simulations examine model consistency and reactor design trends. A normalized separation of 0.1338 gives a coplanar factor of 0.882; first-order kinetics with a rate constant of 0.0568 min−1 gives 96.69% conversion after 60 min. At a dimensionless axial attenuation of 1, double-ended illumination increases the optical uniformity index from 0.712 to 0.963; at an attenuation of 3, the corresponding values are 0.186 and 0.721. Normalized rate scenarios of 1.00/1.45/2.35 generate distinct kinetic profiles for conventional electrolysis, externally illuminated photo-assisted electrolysis, and embedded OFME architectures. Interfacial chemistry, bubble coverage, membrane transport, energy efficiency, and scale-up are discussed for hydrogen and oxygen evolution, carbon dioxide reduction, and nitrogen reduction. An artificial-intelligence-assisted closed-loop framework treats light intensity, wavelength, potential, current, flow rate, temperature, and pH as executable reaction-engineering variables. OFC thus integrates internal light delivery, membrane-electrode reactions, catalytic process intensification, and digital control in a modularly scalable reaction platform.

papers.title: Reversibility of (De)lithiation of Antiperovskite Li2FeOS through a Paracrystalline, Mixed-Valent Intermediate
papers.abstract: The antiperovskite Li 2 FeOS is simultaneously cation-disordered and heteroanionic, and delivers more than one lithium per formula unit — but the structural and redox pathway behind that capacity, and the origin of its fading, remain unclear. Combining galvanostatic intermittent titration, operando X-ray diffraction and ex situ 57 Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy across the electrochemically accessible compositional range, we separate three processes: a two-phase transformation at a flat equilibrium potential of 1.95 V vs. Li/Li + , a solid solution spanning 2.30–2.55 V, and an irreversible process above 2.6 V. Delithiation proceeds with severe loss of long-range order evident by extreme broadening and attenuation of diffracted intensity. Yet, if limited to the first two processes, accounting for ca. one lithium per formula unit, the pristine crystalline reflections are recovered exactly in position and profile on relithiation, excluding amorphization and particle-size reduction. We propose a description of the intermediate as a paracrystal, retaining the parent antiperovskite topology while losing periodicity through aperiodic displacive relaxation. 57 Fe Mössbauer isomer shifts evolve continuously through intermediate values rather than as coexisting Fe 2+ and Fe 3+ populations, indicating mixed-valent iron, and saturate near Fe 2.8+ placing the onset of anion redox earlier than the prevailing sequential cation-then-anion picture. Cells limited to 2.6 V retain >90 % of capacity over 150 cycles, against <70 % at 3.0 V. Reversible cycling of Li 2 FeOS therefore rests on a mixed-valent, paracrystalline intermediate, and capacity fade follows once sulfur oxidation is driven beyond it.

papers.title: Observation-Guided Computation: Sequential Reobservation for Robust Chromatographic Peak Detection
papers.abstract: Chromatographic peak detection is the bottom-most step of the data-processing chain, yet almost every classical detector defines its decision variables in units of signal amplitude, so those variables co-vary with baseline drift, injection amount, and detector gain, and a single-pass decision is made once against an unchanged trace. We reframe detection not as a better criterion but as a change in the computational organization of observation, and we do so in three ordered layers. Layer 1 — Observation-Guided Computation (OGC) is a sequential computational framework — an analytical data-interpretation principle rather than a new peak detector — built around the Observation Deviation (OD) measure established in our companion work13. OGC does not introduce another peak criterion or redefine OD; it embeds OD as an observation measure into an observe–detect–reconstruct–flatten–reobserve loop, so the observation condition is updated after each detected structure. Within a working window the trace is normalized to a unitless observation space, scored by OD against a single dimensionless threshold, and all final boundaries are re-anchored on the raw signal. OGC is deliberately independent of any particular candidate generator: it can be composed from any apex finder, and six heterogeneous engines all converge to a common performance plateau. Under one frozen configuration OGC reaches interval-coverage F1 = 1.000 on three of four synthetic benchmark sets with zero false positives, converts six heterogeneous apex-finder engines into region locators that all converge to F1 ≈ 1.000 (lifting bare derivative and moving-average detectors, unusable at F1 ≤ 0.090, by up to +0.967), is invariant to four orders of magnitude of dynamic range, and identifies high-confidence observable structures on two real GC–MS chromatograms where no global prominence fraction could serve both. Layer 2 — OGC-Net asks whether the representation of chemical observation can itself be learned: it algorithm-unrolls OGC's recursive loop into a differentiable K = 5-round network of 160,516 parameters. It runs a 150-point segment in 13.9 ms (batch 1) to 0.92 ms (batch 128) on CPU and, evaluated under the identical matching protocol, beats the frozen deterministic OGC by +0.116 peak-level F1 precisely on the harder, deployment-identical windowed distribution (0.6944 vs 0.5782). Layer 3 — OGC-Web delivers OGC-Net as a single offline, zero-backend HTML file whose forward pass is a pure-JavaScript port with base64-embedded weights, reproducing the peak-level agreement with the OGC reference client-side. Our central message is that chromatographic observation can be quantified and computationally organized as a sequential process, and that learning the framework — not fitting output labels — is the stronger objective when a deterministic gold-standard algorithm already exists.

papers.title: PARAM-DOCK: An Integrated Framework for Parallel Multi-Protein–Multi-Ligand Docking and Scoring for Scalable Structure-Based Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is a central component of structure-based drug discovery, but practical docking studies often require several independent programs for receptor and ligand preparation, binding-site definition, docking, visualisation, interaction analysis, and downstream compound assessment. This fragmentation becomes particularly limiting when multiple protein targets and multiple ligands must be evaluated in the same study. Here, we present PARAM-DOCK, an open-source molecular docking engine and integrated web workflow implemented in Python with Numba-compiled numerical kernels. PARAM-DOCK supports parallel multi-protein-multi-ligand docking and automates major pre-processing and post-processing steps within a single platform. The docking engine combines a seven-term empirical scoring function with an iterated local search strategy in which Monte Carlo perturbations are followed by bounded quasi-Newton minimisation using analytical gradients. Final pose selection can additionally incorporate binding-basin population and pocket-complementarity descriptors when they are informative. The web platform integrates molecular preparation, docking setup, pose ranking, 2D and 3D protein-ligand interaction analysis, comparative score and interaction heatmaps, molecular visualisation, and ADMET prediction. PARAM-DOCK was benchmarked against Vina using matched receptor and ligand PDBQT files, identical search boxes, symmetry-corrected RMSD evaluation, and identical hardware. On the 285-complex CASF-2016 core set, PARAM-DOCK achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.631 for scoring power and a mean within-target Spearman correlation of 0.579, compared with 0.604 and 0.528 for Vina. In de novo redocking of 255 complexes, PARAM-DOCK placed the top-ranked pose within 2.0 Å in 68.6% of cases and recovered a near-native pose among nine outputs in 84.3%, compared with 74.1% and 93.7% for Vina. Conditional on generating a near-native pose, PARAM-DOCK ranked it first in 81.4% of complexes versus 79.1% for Vina. These results indicate competitive scoring and ranking performance, while conformational sampling remains the main area for further improvement.

papers.title: Robust Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Improves Joint Predicted-Potency and Drug-Likeness Yield in EGFR Molecule Generation
papers.abstract: Optimizing a molecular generator against a single activity-model estimate can reward structures for which that estimate is unreliable. We extended our published ChemBERTa–reinforcement-learning (RL) workflow for human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) with scaffold-separated activity modeling, empirically calibrated lower scores, bounded chemistry rewards, and matched-seed evaluation. From ChEMBL 37, we curated 6,476 unique structures with Reference/unspecified biochemical EGFR IC50 measurements; 4,491, 680, and 1,305 structures were assigned to scaffold-disjoint training, calibration, and test sets. The random-forest reward model achieved a test mean absolute error of 0.610 pIC50 units and R2 = 0.615. Uniform or potency-enriched masked-language-model continuation was crossed with three RL rewards, with three seeds and 600 generation attempts per combination. The locked LCB-versus-mean-only comparison changed GNN potency-screen yield by +0.28 percentage points (95% descriptive t interval,-1.10 to +1.66) across three seed-cluster means. In the pipeline-level comparison with the published-form baseline, Robust-LCB increased the GNN joint-screen yield in all six matched blocks; averaged across the two MLM arms, the yield rose from 0.72% to 1.22%. Two structures passed the full RF–GNN consensus funnel. These results support a pipeline-level increase in joint predicted-potency and drug-like yield, while the incremental contribution of the lower-score term alone remains uncertain. These comparisons describe computational variability; activity estimates for generated molecules require biochemical testing.

papers.title: Spin-polarized low-density asymptotics of RPA-screened second-order exchange in the uniform electron gas
Operando Cross-Sectional Nanoscale Imaging of Na Anode Formation in Zero-Excess Solid-State Batteries: Coupled Phase–Stress Evolution and X-ray Beam Effects
papers.abstract: Zero-excess solid-state sodium batteries plate Na during charging, which places severe demands on the mechanical stability of the evolving anode and its interfaces. This work resolves the spatiotemporal evolution of phase formation and mechanical stresses across buried interfaces in a Na-Pb model system using a custom-built operando cell for cross-sectional X-ray nanodiffraction with a beam of 150 nm in diameter. The operando phase maps reveal that Na, Pb/NaPb3, and NaPb/Na9Pb4 phases coexist spatially during plating, contradicting the predominantly sequential pathway reported for liquid-electrolyte Na-Pb systems. The temporal evolution of the deviatoric in-plane stress reveals an increasingly compressive state within the solid-state electrolyte, concentrated near the interface and consistent with Na filling residual pores within the ceramic electrolyte, thereby creating local stress concentrations associated with dendritic growth and failure. Unexpectedly, comparison with beam-free reference cells reveals that X-ray exposure measurably suppresses Na plating, evidenced by an altered electrochemical response and substantially reduced Na and alloy formation. Suppressed phase formation at previously unexposed positions further shows that the beam-induced perturbation extends beyond the irradiated region, unlike the predominantly localized effects reported for liquid-electrolyte systems. This non-local response is consistent with radiation-induced charge generation within the ceramic electrolyte and demonstrates that X-ray exposure can directly alter the electrochemical process being probed in solid-state systems under bias.

papers.title: Layered Double Hydroxides with Interlayer Electrons Activate Strong Chemical Bonds
papers.abstract: Layered electrides are an unusual class of materials in which excess electrons occupy interlayer regions and serve as anionic, charge-balancing species. Many prototypical layered electrides are based on subnitrides and subcarbides, motivating the search for new types of host structures. Here, we use density functional theory (DFT) to characterize a class of layered electrides derived from layered double hydroxides (LDHs). Through an anion–electron exchange process, we predict that several LDH compositions can stabilize an electride state wherein significant charge is confined in the interlayer galleries. We evaluate the thermodynamic and finite-temperature stability of the LDH electrides, demonstrating that the balance between stability and interlayer charge can be controlled through partial anion exchange. DFT calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the interlayer electrons impart unique chemical reactivity by facilitating the activation of strong chemical bonds, such as the spontaneous dissociation of Br 2 and the reduction of CO 2 to formate.

papers.title: Fast-Response Operando Mass Spectrometry Demystifies C₂ Product Formation in Cu-Catalyzed CO and CO₂ Reduction: Burst of Ethylene Isotopologues
papers.abstract: It has been a long-standing challenge in electrocatalysis to measure product formation with kinetically relevant time resolution. Here, we couple a real-time gas analyzer mass spectrometer with a modified sampling inlet to a gas diffusion electrode cell, achieving sub-second time resolution for both reactant consumption and product formation. We focus on CO 2 /CO reduction on oxide-derived Cu, motivated by the continuing interest in its reaction mechanism and its high selectivity to ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) formation. Potential step experiments for CO reduction reveal that the initial consumption of CO is fast (< 1 s), but the appearance of C 2 H 4 products can be 10 times slower, which we attribute to the time required for CO storage on the Cu surface and subsequent reconstruction into the active, C 2+ -forming, configuration. Previous studies have reported that the co-feed of 12 CO 2 / 13 CO results in the enhancement of 13 C-containing ethylene isotopologues, but the mechanism causing this remains unknown. Isotopic-labeled gas switching ( 12 CO 2 - 13 CO) experiments yield compelling evidence that 13 C species continue to exist for more than a minute at near proximity to or on the catalyst, even after the supply source has been cut off, evidenced by the significant enhancement of 13 C-containing ethylene isotopologues: pure ( 13 C 2 H 4 ) and mixed ( 13 C 12 CH 4 ), formed through a CO 2 (g)-*CO pathway. Importantly, the size of the C 1 reservoir, the amount of 13 C 12 CH 4 made when CO 2 reacts with it, and the amount of Cu + that is removed are all in the micromole range. Thus, the picture emerges that a monolayer is stripped off from the copper catalyst surface during the CO-CO 2 switch. Tracking of dynamic Cu surface insights (i.e., activation, dissolution and deactivation) provides valuable mechanistic insights for optimizing reaction conditions.

papers.title: Tailoring the Fusogenic Properties of cis-ssPalmO-phe Based Lipid Nanoparticles for mRNA Delivery
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are widely used for mRNA delivery, yet the effects of helper lipids on mixed bilayers containing redox-cleavable, self-degradable ionizable lipids remain unclear. Here, we conducted atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of bilayers formed from self-degradable lipid cis-ssPalmO-phe, examining 20 compositions with variations in helper-lipid headgroup (PC or PE), acyl chain length (C14-C24), and unsaturation, establishing structure-property relationships governing fusogenicity. We found that 40 mol% DOPC is optimal, with bilayer thickness of 4.60 nm and a diffusion rate of 0.37 ×10−7 cm2 s−1, balancing rigidity and dynamics for effective encapsulation and endosomal escape. PC bilayers are thinner (4.50 to 5.39 nm), more fluid, negatively charged (-0.21 to-2.59 V), enhancing stability and circulation. In contrast, PE bilayers are thicker (4.96 to 5.75 nm), denser, positively charged (up to +1.42 V), promoting curvature for endosomal fusion and cargo release. Higher unsaturation increases diffusion but decreases bilayer order, while saturated long-chain lipids maximize packing and binding energy indicating stability (up to-59.37 kcal mol−1). Tilt-angle analysis shows PC and PE adopt similar orientations and radial distribution functions confirm no clustering in saturated systems. These findings connect lipid chemistry to bilayer structure, offering design insights for degradable LNPs for mRNA and oligonucleotide therapies.

papers.title: Facet Selective Adsorption and Mobility of Anthracene Based Nanocars on Gold Surfaces
