papers.abstract: Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of anthracene-based nanocars (ANTH-R; R= H, Me, Cl) on Au(100) and Au(111) facets in explicit water, investigating the combined effects of facet crystallography, substituent chemistry, and solvation previously unexplored. Binding free energies reveal stronger adsorption on Au(111): ANTH-Me > ANTH-Cl > ANTH-H, with diffusion suppressed upto 100 fold on Au(111). Substituent chemistry influences adsorption geometry and create varied transport regimes providing design principles for nanocar motion under realistic conditions.

papers.title: Unit-Cell Molecular Dynamics Framework for Cross-Linked Hydrogels: Linking Cross-Link Density, Hydration Shells, and Swelling
papers.abstract: Rational design of polyacrylamide (PAAm) hydrogels involves linking local amide–water interactions to macroscopic properties. This study combines molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of “unit-cell” PAAm segments with experimental data to explore how the acrylamide (Ac) to N,N′ methylenebisacrylamide (BAc) molar ratio affects network structure and water dynamics. By modeling PAAm chains at ratios from 4:1 to 7:1, we reframe a covalently cross-linked network using a non-covalently self-assembling unitcell analogy, bridging oligomer-proxy and supramolecular modeling paradigms. Validating our findings against gravimetric swelling, FTIR, SEM, and oscillatory rheology data, we identify a two-stage assembly mechanism. Initially, amide groups undergo intrasegment electrostatic pre-organization, followed by inter-segment hydrogen-bonding.

papers.title: Explainable ML force-field for evaluating protein–ligand binding energy using SO3LR
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of protein–ligand binding affinities remains central to structure-based drug design. Classical force fields neglect important quantum-mechanical effects, while quantum mechanical and semi-empirical methods remain impractical for large biomolecular systems. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) offer an alternative, but their performance may be inflated by training on protein–ligand complexes. Here, we introduce SO3LR-SF, a physics-based scoring function built on the pretrained SO3LR MLFF, combining an equivariant message-passing network for semi-local interactions with physically motivated terms for short-range repulsion, electrostatics, and long-range dispersion. Built on an MLFF that was not trained on protein–ligand complexes, SO3LR-SF provides a stringent test of transferability. On PLA15 (15 active-site models), SO3LR-SF attains a relative interaction error of 5.8% against DLPNO-CCSD(T) references, the lowest of all tested methods. On the FEP benchmark (8 targets, 264 ligands), SO3LR-SF achieves an average Spearman correlation of 0.51, on par with the best semi-empirical quantum-mechanical method tested (0.47, GFN-FF) and with MMGBSA (0.44), and surpassing Glide (0.27). On the Wang dataset (8 targets, 199 ligands), it reaches 0.51, approaching the 0.60 average of molecular dynamics-based free-energy methods at a fraction of their cost. Each complex is scored in 1–10 seconds on 12 CPU cores, an 80- to 300-fold speedup over comparable MLFFs. An 8 Å trimming protocol reduces runtime threefold without loss of accuracy, and a restrained geometry optimization recovers ranking accuracy for targets with strained input structures. A multi-level explainability framework adds energy decomposition, per-atom energy contributions reported either for ligand or as 2D protein–ligand interaction maps, and 3D binding site visualization. We identified two pocket descriptors that flag applicability before scoring, e.g. polar solvent accessible surface area (SASA) ratio correlating strongly (r = 0.81) with performance. Together, SO3LR-SF presents a fast, interpretable, and competitive scoring function for drug discovery that requires no domain-specific training data.

papers.title: Physical Metallurgy of Lithium and Sodium and its Role in Electrochemical Stability of Solid-State Battery Anodes
papers.abstract: Alkali metal negative electrodes in solid-state batteries (SSBs) undergo mechanical deformation during cycling, for which an understanding of their physical metallurgy is critical. Here, we study the link between microstructure and plastic deformation in lithium and sodium. Grain size is controlled through deformation processing, and etching methods are developed to reveal grain boundaries, subgrain boundaries, and dislocation structures. Hall-Petch strengthening with decreasing grain size occurs in both metals. Creep rate in lithium is grain-size-independent above the subgrain size, but increases at small grain sizes where diffusional creep dominates. Oxide dispersion-strengthened behavior is observed in Li. At length scales below the subgrain size, strength increases and creep rates decrease due to dislocation starvation. Solid-state electrochemical cell tests in which lithium of differing foil thickness is stripped under pressure validates length-scale effects. Overall, this work provides a physical metallurgy framework for alkali metal deformation and offers design principles for advanced SSBs.

papers.title: Decoding Membrane Biophysics for Nucleic Acid Delivery: Bridging Bilayer Simulations and Lipid Nanoparticle Functionality
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are a proven platform for delivering nucleic acids, evidenced by the approvals of patisiran and COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. However, the molecular mechanisms behind lipid organization, cargo encapsulation, and intracellular release remain partially understood. This review links molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of lipid bilayers to functional LNP systems through a three-level framework. (i) Structural observables: area per lipid, bilayer thickness, intrinsic curvature. (ii) Dynamic and mechanical properties: bending modulus (Kc), deuterium order parameter (SCD), lateral diffusion coefficient (DL), potential of mean force (PMF). (iii) Functional delivery outcomes: endosomal escape efficiency, RNA encapsulation, PEG shedding kinetics, cytosolic cargo release. We assess various MD frameworks, including all-atom, classical coarse-grained, and machine learning-based methods, evaluating their accuracy across the scale frontier. The pH-responsive behavior of ionizable lipids is linked to curvature stress, driving transitions from lamellar to inverted hexagonal (HII) phases, crucial for endosomal escape. We also analyze how cholesterol, helper phospholipids, and PEGylated lipids modify membrane mechanics and aid in cargo release. We highlight current limitations like fixed-protonation force fields and inadequate parameterization for new ionizable lipids. Future directions include constant-pH

papers.title: Multigram Synthesis of Heterabicyclo[4.1.1]octanes: Conformationally Restricted Azepane Analogs for Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: A convenient and scalable synthetic approach enabling multigram access to three heterabicyclo[4.1.1]octane families – 2-azabicyclo[4.1.1]octane, 2,5-diazabicyclo[4.1.1]octane, and 2-oxa-5-azabicyclo[4.1.1]octane – is described. Starting f rom readily available cis -1,3-disubstituted cyclobutanes, the target scaf folds were obtained by the common lactamization – amide reduction strategy, providing access to the (mono)protected (di)amines as ready-to-use building blocks. Representative members were characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies, and basicity (p K a ) and lipophilicity (Log P ) were determined for selected compounds. These rigid f rameworks can be considered as saturated analogs of the azepane, 1,4-diazepane, and 1,4-oxazepane rings.

papers.title: Diffusion-Model-Guided Adaptive Sampling of Rare Conformational States in Adenylate Kinase
papers.abstract: Efficiently exploring the rare conformational states of biomolecules remains a central challenge in molecular dynamics simulation. Here we show, using adenylate kinase as a methodological testbed, that the static structural scores conventionally used to prioritize diffusion-modelgenerated candidates have essentially no power to predict which candidates actually reach a kinetically rare state upon subsequent simulation (AUC = 0.500). Motivated by this finding, we introduce two adaptive strategies — direct PCA-distance targeting and replication of confirmed-hit structures — that achieve significantly higher rare-state hit rates and dwell times than extended conventional molecular dynamics or random-initialization sampling under matched computational budgets, while also enabling, for the first time, statistically stable estimation of rare-macrostate populations. These results show that structural novelty and kinetically meaningful entry into a rare state are not the same property, providing concrete design guidance for generative-model-driven adaptive sampling in other biomolecular systems.

papers.title: A simple demonstration of the importance of purity in nanotechnology with the example of rapid syntheses of gold nanoparticles in water
papers.abstract: A simple and visual demonstration of the importance of purity and the impact of impurities in nanotechnology is described. Stable colloidal gold nanoparticles are simply obtained at room temperature in seconds, adding NaBH4 to HAuCl4 in water without the need for other chemicals. By adjusting the conductivity of the water used, for example by using high purity water, tap water or mixtures of the two in different ratios, the size and stability of the nanoparticles is easily tuned. Size control is easily assessed by the color of the colloids obtained and/or by UV-vis spectroscopy. This undergraduate level demonstration suitable for a wide audience requires only very simple equipment and can be broadly implemented to illustrate the importance of controlled conditions in nanotechnology, raise awareness on the impact of impurities, but also show how to leverage on negative results to turn a drawback into a benefit. Additionally, the concept and the experimental approach proposed integrate well in other pedagogical activities and are a solid foundation to link nanotechnology to other important topics in the education of the chemical sciences.

papers.title: Tandem mass spectrometric analysis of interfacial lipid alkyl chains selectively modified via reactive ion deposition
papers.abstract: The molecular structures of lipids, including branching, double bonds and substitution within the hydrophobic chains, are key aspects in research fields such as biomarkers and signaling, and determine cell membrane properties. Although mass spectrometry has become the dominant method for lipidomics, determining fatty acid chain structures using widely available methods (MSn via CID) remains challenging. In this study, we present reactive ion deposition as a method for chemically modifying interfacial lipids in thin layers. Highly reactive [B12I11]− anions are mass-selected and deposited onto layers containing various fatty acids, phosphatidylserines, phosphatidylcholines and triacylglycerides. Using isotope-labelled compounds, we observed that [B12I11]− selectively binds to the terminal methyl groups of fatty acid hydrophobic n-alkyl chains (≥95%). The molecular structure of the lipid remains intact during covalent binding of the reactive ion on the surface, effectively charge-tagging the lipid at the alkyl chain. Therefore, ESI-MS analysis of the interfacially active layer components is enabled. Collision-induced dissociation of the anionic reaction products reveals structural information about the lipid via MSn spectra regarding both head group and fatty acid chain structure (i.e., branching, double bonds and substituent positions). This method enables not only analysis of lipids molecular structures, but also reveals information about the interfacial composition and molecular orientation of complex samples due to the binding of molecular groups located at the interface of the probed layer.

papers.title: Automated Symbolic Derivation Enables Scalable Ensemble DFT for Strongly Correlated Molecules and Materials
papers.abstract: Strong electron correlation governs the chemistry of bond breaking, polyradicals, and excited states, yet accurately describing it requires computational methods whose cost increases steeply with system size. We present a scalable ensemble density functional theory (eDFT) methodology that extends accurate treatment of strong correlation to molecular systems of realistic size at standard Kohn-Sham DFT cost. Automated derivation of the method’s working equations and a data-driven acceleration scheme enable linear scaling with active-space size while retaining multiconfigurational accuracy. Applied to systems inaccessible to standard Kohn-Sham DFT methods, such as multiple bond dissociation, open-shell polyradicals, and a recently synthesized magnetic quantum material, the framework reproduces experimental magnetic gaps and near-exact wavefunction benchmarks using active spaces up to ten electrons in ten orbitals, thus removing a long-standing barrier to routine simulation of strongly correlated matter.

papers.title: Operando Investigation of the Lithiation Mechanism in CsPbCl3 Perovskite
papers.abstract: Metal halide perovskites offer a structurally responsive platform for lithium-ion battery components, however the interplay between structural transformation and electrochemical functionality remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the lithiation mechanism in all-inorganic CsPbCl3 perovskite as a model system for resolving electrochemically driven phase reconstruction relevant to artificial solid electrolyte interphase concepts. Operando X-ray diffraction combined with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, reveals that lithiation proceeds via a multistep pathway initiated by irreversible perovskite decomposition, resulting in formation of metallic Pb and mixed Cs–Li–Cl phases. Subsequently, reversible alloying reactions during the first cycle leads to the emergence of Li–Pb intermetallic compounds including LiPb and Li8Pb3. The evolution of diffraction features correlates with pronounced changes in the impedance response, revealing a transition from kinetically hindered conversion to more facile charge-transfer and diffusion-associated processes during alloying. Notably, no reconstruction of the perovskite framework is observed upon delithiation, confirming a conversion–alloying mechanism as the dominant charge-storage pathway. The in situ formation of Cs–Li–Cl phases coincides with marked changes in charge-transfer and diffusion-associated resistances, suggesting that the electrochemically generated chloride-rich products may contribute to the interfacial response of the reconstructed electrode. These results elucidate the lithium storage mechanism in halide perovskite-derived materials and highlight the role of decomposition-driven phase evolution in governing electrochemical performance.

papers.title: Strongly bound excitons limit the photocatalytic efficiency of carbon nitride by hindering free charge carrier generation
A simple visual tool to illustrate the relationship between transcript and protein specificity in human organs
papers.abstract: Today a large amount of high depth quantitative proteomic information exists for nearly every human tissue. Despite this wealth of information simple tools for visualizing protein distribution in the human body are somehow lacking. Due to the challenges in accessing protein measurements directly biologists commonly use accessible web portals which provide RNA transcript read counts, which end up being used as a proxy for protein data. This is unfortunate because it is well established that the correlation between transcript counts and protein concentration in mammalian material is low. This is, however, a relatively vague concept that is difficult to both envision and to explain in the context of the central dogma. One way to rectify this problem would be by making protein quantification data as simple and accessible as RNA read count data. To illustrate how a large amount of proteomic data can be easily visualized, I have constructed an example lightweight HTML page that is small enough to be attached to email even when containing deep proteomic analysis of 29 healthy human tissues. The value of simple proteomic data representation is further demonstrated by overlaying proteins predicted to be organ specific from transcriptomic data. Displayed together, it is possible to rapidly determine which transcript measurements can be trusted to be predictive of protein specificity. All data, code and step-by-step analyses are made available in the Supporting Information and a web instance of the resulting tool comparing two gold standard datasets is hosted at: https://www.orsburnlab.org/protein-specificity.

papers.title: Aqueous-rich flow intensification for enzymatic transesterification of rose geranium oil in a coiled flow inverter microreactor
papers.abstract: Enzyme-assisted valorisation of crude floral oils into high-value fragrance esters is constrained by mass-transfer limitations and limited productivity in conventional batch reactors. Rose geranium oil, a naturally complex and terpene-rich multicomponent feedstock containing geraniol, citronellol and numerous other volatile constituents, was selected to investigate continuous enzymatic transesterification directly from a crude floral oil. Using Pseudomonas fluorescens lipase (PFL), geraniol and citronellol were selectively transesterified within the multicomponent oil, without prior isolation of these constituents. A process-intensified strategy was developed using a coiled flow inverter (CFI) microreactor. Aqueous-rich biphasic slug flow at an aqueous-to-organic ratio of 9:1, providing a specific interfacial area of 2319 m 2 m -3 , increased the apparent volumetric mass-transfer coefficient (kLa) by approximately 5-fold for geraniol and 7-fold for citronellol relative to batch operation. At 60 °C and a residence time of 5 min, the CFI achieved 99 % geraniol and 93 % citronellol conversion at 0.2 M rose geranium oil, while maintaining 91 % and 71 % conversion, respectively, at 1.4 M. Increasing the residence time to 7 min increased citronellol conversion at 1.4 M to 95 %. At 1.4 M, the 2 mL CFI provided calculated productivities of approximately 572 g day -1 for geranyl ester and 422 g day -1 for citronellyl ester, assuming continuous operation for 24 h. These results establish aqueous-rich segmented flow as an effective strategy for intensifying selective enzymatic transesterification within a compositionally complex terpene feedstock. The combination of selective conversion, enhanced interphase mass transfer and high calculated productivity provides a basis for the continuous valorisation of rose geranium oil and other complex floral oils into high-value fragrance esters.

papers.title: Electrolyte-Dependent Electrochemical Performance of a Lead-Free Semiconducting Co(II)-Halide Hybrid for Aqueous Supercapacitors
papers.abstract: Developing affordable and stable electrode materials is crucial for advancing sustainable supercapacitor technologies. In this study, a lead-free Co(II)-halide hybrid material (CoTEA) was synthesized via slow evaporation and evaluated as an electrode for aqueous electrochemical energy storage. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction showed a zero-dimensional structure consisting of isolated tetrahedral units separated by tetraethylammonium cations. Morphological and spectroscopic analyses confirmed the crystalline nature and the Co(II) oxidation state of the material. Optical measurements indicated semiconducting behavior with a band gap of 3.64 eV. The electrochemical response of CoTEA was highly dependent on the electrolyte used. At 5 mV s-1, specific capacitances of 5.01, 22.24, and 21.37 F g-1 were recorded in 1 M H2SO4, 0.5 M Na2SO4, and 6 M KOH, respectively. While Na2SO4 yielded the highest capacitance at the lowest scan rate, KOH demonstrated better rate performance and lower charge-transfer resistance, suggesting more efficient interfacial kinetics. In 6 M KOH, CoTEA achieved a GCD-specific capacitance of 21.41 F g-1 at 0.5 A g-1 and maintained about 85% of its initial capacitance after 3000 cycles. These results underscore the significant impact of electrolyte composition on the charge-storage behavior of CoTEA and present it as a promising, tunable material for aqueous supercapacitor applications.strong influence of electrolyte composition on the charge-storage behavior of CoTEA and highlight it as a promising tunable material for aqueous supercapacitor applications.

papers.title: Condition-Aware and Leakage-Resistant Machine Learning of Short-Peptide Self-Assembly Across Bulk State and Supramolecular Morphology
papers.abstract: Short-peptide self-assembly is governed jointly by molecular structure and experimental environment, yet many predictive workflows treat condition-specific observations as independent samples. Here, a source-audited dataset was reconstructed from PeptideMiner and SAPdb to evaluate bulk-state and supramolecular-morphology prediction under leakage-resistant validation. Peptide identity was defined from sequence,terminal modifications,non-terminal modifications,peptide-system annotations,and conjugate partners; experimental descriptors included concentration, pH, temperature, thermal history, incubation, and explicit solvent composition. A conventional random row split was shown to be strongly non-independent: 87.3% of test molecular identities had already appeared in training and 94.2% of test rows came from molecules represented in training.Accordingly,all primary claims were based on molecular-identity-grouped validation and permanently sealed holdouts containing previously unseen molecular systems. For hydrogel versus non-gel prediction, a tuned Random Forest achieved ROCAUC 0.977, PR-AUC 0.882, balanced accuracy 0.945, F1 0.880, and MCC 0.836 on 115 conditions from 20 unseen molecular identities. Solvent identity and composition formed the dominant transferable feature block,but analyses restricted to fully aqueous conditions demonstrated that non-solvent variables,particularly concentration,pH,temperature,and related processing descriptors,retained substantial predictive information. A harder three-class non-gel/hydrogel/organogel task yielded macro ROC-AUC 0.783 and MCC 0.247 on unseen molecules, with organic non-gelling conditions constituting the dominant error mode. For broad morphology, an Extra Trees classifier achieved macro ROC-AUC 0.980, macro PR-AUC 0.925, and MCC 0.665 on 59 conditions from 14 unseen molecular identities, although spherical/particulate morphology remained comparatively difficult.Fine-grained morphology prediction was not forced when independent class support proved insufficient for stable molecule grouped cross-validation. These results establish that reliable learning of short-peptide self-assembly requires explicit representation of experimental environment, source-level curation, and validation at the level of independent molecular systems rather than condition rows.

papers.title: Argon Coordination to the 3d Transition-Metal Monohalides: A Systematic Study of σ-Acceptor Accessibility in Ar–MX (M = Sc–Cu; X = F, Cl, Br)
papers.abstract: Argon is generally regarded as chemically inert, yet direct Ar–metal coordination has been established for several late transition-metal complexes. Here, we systematically investigate Ar coordination across the 3d transition-metal monofluorides, MF (M = Sc–Cu), and subsequently extend the analysis to the corresponding chlorides and bromides. Density functional theory, population analysis, energy decomposition, and multireference calculations reveal a pronounced and nonmonotonic variation in Ar-binding propensity across the MF series. Ar binding is characterized by Ar 3pσ donation into a metal-centered σ-acceptor manifold of mixed 4s and 3dz2 character. In predominantly single-reference systems, the metal 4s population of bare MF provides a simple descriptor of the accessibility of this manifold: low 4s occupation is generally associated with Ar coordination, whereas high 4s occupation is associated with dissociation. Consistent with this picture, single-reference calculations give shortrange Ar-bound minima for MnF and FeF on lower-spin DFT surfaces with reduced 4s occupation, although these solutions are SCF-unstable and require multireference confirmation. The same metaldependent trend is largely retained for the chlorides and bromides, with additional modulation by the M–X framework. Sc halides mark the multireference limit of the simple 4s-based description.

papers.title: Software Tool for Automated Kinetic Tracking in Mass Spectrometry Data
papers.abstract: Time-resolved mass spectrometry produces large datasets that are challenging to organize and screen for kinetic trends. We present an open-source software tool designed for the exploratory screening and visualization of time-dependent variations in extensive series of mzML measurements. Rather than focusing on automated compound identification, the software's main purpose is to highlight and rank the signals that undergo the most significant changes over time. The software streamlines chronological file organization, replicate aggregation, and trend ranking. To demonstrate its utility, the tool was used to monitor the reaction between aniline and 1-iodobutane. Crucially, the software not only correctly identified the expected mono- and dibutyl derivatives of aniline, but it also revealed the unexpected presence of aniline dimers (m/z 183 and 185), and trimer (m/z 274), and their corresponding butylated products. The automated ranking perfectly captured the consecutive reaction profiles, showing the initial accumulation of monobutyl intermediates and their subsequent consumption into dibutyl derivatives. Without this unbiased screening, these dimeric and trimeric pathways could have been easily overlooked. Ultimately, this tool drastically reduces manual data processing while guiding researchers directly to the most chemically interesting variations.

papers.title: Reliable Structure-Processing-Performance Learning in Organic Photovoltaics: Chemical Generalization, Processing-Aware Prediction and Uncertainty under Domain Shift
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models for organic photovoltaics (OPVs) can achieve strong performance under random train-test splits, but such evaluation may overstate prospective generalization when literaturederived datasets contain repeated publications and material systems. Here, two complementary OPV benchmarks were constructed to separate interpolation from chemical extrapolation: a provenanceclean OPV-DB cohort containing 21,590 experimentally reported devices and a processing-rich Wen-Zhang-Ma cohort containing 994 unique physical processing conditions. Random, publication-heldout, donor-acceptor (D:A)-pair-held-out, acceptor-held-out, and donor-held-out validation regimes were compared, together with structure-only, processing-only, and combined structure-processing representations. Extra Trees performance on OPV-DB declined from R2 = 0.813 under random validation to R2 = 0.362 under donor holdout. In the processing-rich benchmark, adding processing information reduced MAE by 19.5% under random validation but by only 1.0-2.4% under chemically grouped validation. This effect was strongly associated with material-system familiarity: processing reduced MAE by 27.1% for test records whose D:A pair was represented in training, compared with 1.8% for completely unseen pairs. Ensemble dispersion was useful for ranking errors under random validation (Spearman rho = 0.462) but lost reliability under donor holdout (rho = 0.047), where the most uncertain 20% of predictions captured only 16.1% of the largest errors. A cross-dataset transfer audit further showed that a common unmodified RDKit representation covered 73.54% of the processing benchmark and only 38.02% of records with PCE >= 15%, creating substantial chemicalselection bias. These results show that validation design is central to claims of OPV model reliability, that processing information primarily refines predictions within familiar chemistry, and that both uncertainty estimation and transfer benchmarking require explicit domain-shift and representation audits.

papers.title: Reliable Structure-Processing-Performance Learning in Organic Photovoltaics: Chemical Generalization, Processing-Aware Prediction and Uncertainty under Domain Shift

papers.title: Empirical Evidence that Dirac–Fock Relativistic and Quantum Corrections are Z-indexing Artifacts
Novel green K-based Metal-Organic Framework with high proton conductivity
papers.abstract: Despite growing interest in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs for protonconductivity applications, monovalent-cation-based MOFs remain comparatively underexplored due to the weaker coordination interactions typically associated with these systems. In this work, we report GR-MOF-28, a novel potassium-based naphthalene tetracarboxylate framework synthesized under mild aqueous conditions at room temperature. Structurally, GR-MOF-28 consists of K2O10 dioctahedra interconnected through tetracarboxylate ligands and coordinated water molecules, generating a confined hydrogen-bond network along the crystallographic channels. The material exhibits proton conductivity values up to 4.3·10-2 S·cm-1 under high relative humidity conditions, placing it among the highest-performing K-based MOFs reported to date. Combined electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and molecular simulations support a water-mediated Grotthusstype proton transport mechanism through the confined hydrogen-bond network. In addition, GR-MOF-28 can be incorporated into a conductive polymer matrix without loss of proton transport properties. These results highlight the potential of underexplored K-based coordination frameworks as proton-conducting materials.

papers.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Disentangles Pore Confinement Across Multiple Zr-MOF CO2 Capture Targets
papers.abstract: Pore confinement in zirconium-based metal–organic frameworks (Zr-MOFs) is often described using the cage–window ratio (ΓCW), the largest cavity diameter divided by the pore-limiting diameter (Df), yet whether this composite coordinate carries information beyond Df alone remains unclear. We modeled CO2 uptake, heat of adsorption (HoA), and CO2/N2 selectivity for 239 Zr-containing MOFs at two pressures relevant to vacuum-swing adsorption using structure-grouped machine learning with SHAP interpretation, reaching test R2 values of 0.77–0.88. Although ΓCW correlated positively with all three targets, controlling for Df weakened these associations and reversed their sign, while the reciprocal analysis left the Df associations largely unchanged and a difference-based formulation produced no significant association. Df played different roles across the three targets, indicating that the apparent confinement effect mainly reflects the limiting aperture rather than relative cage–window architecture.

papers.title: Carbon Nanotube-Induced Magnetic Shielding Effects on 129Xe NMR from Equivariant Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Equivariant graph neural networks (EGNNs) have shown success in building efficient and accurate machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for molecular dynamics (MD) and in enabling the prediction of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) parameters in complex systems. In this work, EGNNs are used to fine-tune an atomistic foundation model, which serves as an MLIP for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of xenon in carbon nanotubes. In addition, EGNNs are employed to develop a machine learning model for the 129 Xe NMR magnetic shielding tensor, σ , enabling its direct prediction from MLMD snapshots. Both models are data-efficient and remain accurate well beyond their training data. Using this dual-model framework, we show that xenon encapsulated in carbon nanotubes experiences a nanotube-induced, negative 129 Xe isotropic chemical shift that varies non-monotonically with nanotube diameter and depends further on temperature and Xe loading, establishing this dual-model approach as an efficient route to interpreting confinement-driven 129 Xe NMR response.

papers.title: From Black Box to Dialogue: An MCP Server for Tanabe–Sugano Diagrams as a Reference Case for Conversational Scientific Tools
papers.abstract: Interpreting the d–d electronic spectra of transition-metal complexes is a routine practice in inorganic chemistry, yet the underlying models behind such interpretations are unexpectedly challenging to operate. Rigorous treatments demand specialized software, expert parameterization, and often high-performance computing, while even the standard textbook tool for first-pass intuition takes practice to read. The Tanabe–Sugano (TS) diagram remains the most efficient method for developing that intuition, and the same ligand-field framework is foundational for more advanced spectroscopic analyses. Here we present TanabeSugano, an open-source Python solver for d2–d8 TS diagrams. It is implemented as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, letting a language-model client act as an interactive front end that operates the solver rather than merely describing it. Through natural-language prompts, users can compute term energies, explore and compare configurations, fit measured absorption bands to extract the crystal-field strength (Dq) and Racah B, and interpret B as an indicator of metal–ligand covalency via the nephelauxetic ratio. The solver runs locally, without compilation or high-performance computing. We outline the tools available within the server and the d-orbital concepts they embody, illustrated by a comparison between d5 and d6 configurations that reveals the high-spin/low-spin crossover and the distinction between spin-allowed and spin-forbidden electronic transitions. TanabeSugano is the proof of concept; the contribution is the pattern it demonstrates, which exposes a validated solver through MCP. More specifically, it offers an accessible route to phenomenological understanding and a transferable model for operating other formal chemical models through dialogue. The proposed MCP implementation does not aim to supplant the rigor inherent in ab initio methods and remains fundamentally distinct from it.

papers.title: A computed thermoelectric feature database for 50,992 GNoME materials
papers.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials now make it feasible to compute rich physical property sets for very large libraries of hypothetical crystals, but such feature sets are rarely released in analysis-ready form, and thermal-transport descriptors — central to thermoelectric performance — are especially scarce. Here we present a computed feature database for 50,992 novel, thermodynamically plausible crystalline materials drawn from Google DeepMind's Graph Networks for Materials Exploration (GNoME) database and filtered for thermoelectric relevance (non-metallic, finite band gap, energy above the Materials Project convex hull ≤ 0.05 eV/atom). For every material we provide composition and crystallographic descriptors; CHGNet universal- potential energetics, per-site magnetic moments, and a 64-dimensional learned crystal embedding; a full harmonic thermal-transport layer (elastic tensor, Debye temperature, sound velocities, and Cahill/Clarke minimum-conductivity bounds); and an anharmonic layer (Grüneisen parameter from a CHGNet equation-of-state, and a Slack-model lattice thermal conductivity). CHGNet formation energies reproduce the underlying DFT values with a mean absolute error of 0.036 eV/atom (Pearson r = 0.999), and two independently computed bulk moduli agree to a 5.3 % median difference (r = 0.992). To our knowledge this is the first release of a complete lattice-thermal-transport feature layer for the GNoME material set, enabling data-driven thermoelectric screening and machine-learning studies at scale.

papers.title: Head-to-tail cyclization of a peptide using a tethered homopolymer as a docking station for ring-closing and its extension to cyclization in the bulk with mm-long tethers
A trace-hierarchy theorem for shared splittings in coupled spin-½ NMR spectra
Solid-State Host–Guest Chemistry of Cyanoborate-Bridged Cubane-Type Tetranuclear Ruthenium Complexes: Solvate Crystal Formation and Reversible Sorption of Volatile Organic Compounds
papers.abstract: Small-molecule sorption by porous metal–organic frameworks has attracted considerable attention but remains largely unexplored in nonporous crystals composed of discrete metal complexes. Here, we report cyanoborate-bridged cubane-type tetranuclear ruthenium complexes, [Ru4(Cp)4{BR(CN)3}4] (R = F (1), Me (2), H (3)), as nonporous adaptive crystalline hosts for volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Recrystallization of 1 from solvents with widely varying polarities, sizes, and shapes afforded solvate crystals containing one to three guest molecules per cubane unit. The guest molecules were accommodated around the shallow concave faces of the cubane units, and the packing structures were classified into three types largely governed by guest size and shape. The desolvated solid of 1 reversibly sorbed various VOC vapors, with the sorption amounts largely consistent with the solvent contents of the corresponding solvate crystals, indicating guest-dependent rearrangement of the intermolecular packing. Complexes 2 and 3 exhibited substituent-dependent CH2Cl2 sorption–desorption behavior. Although 1 showed only very limited N₂ and H₂ uptake at 77 K, it exhibited appreciable low-temperature CO2 uptake. These results expand the scope of nonporous adaptive crystals to discrete metal-complex systems with rigid, three-dimensionally shaped molecular units.

papers.title: Engineering Receptor-Mediated Cell-Surface Mobility with Phage-Inspired DNA Tetrapods
papers.abstract: Viruses have long inspired the development of multiligand display systems that engage cell-surface receptors through strong multivalent interactions. However, considerably less attention has been devoted to recapitulating the early stages of infection, during which weak, reversible interactions promote receptor-mediated mobility across cell membranes. Bacteriophages provide a striking example of this behavior, using transient receptor interactions to move across bacterial surfaces in search of favorable binding sites. Inspired by this mechanism, we developed DNA tetrapods targeting bacterial receptors exploited by phages during adsorption and demonstrate that phage-like lateral mobility on living bacterial cells can be achieved by tuning ligand affinity, valency, and spacer length. Furthermore, this platform can be extended to mammalian systems, where the tetrapod architecture similarly governs lateral motion and cell association, enabling selective cancer-cell recognition and improved antisense oligonucleotide uptake. Together, these findings demonstrate receptor-mediated mobility as a programmable property that could be harnessed to enhance cellular targeting and cargo delivery.

papers.title: Target breadth and mutation resilience in African-natural-product-inspired antimalarial chemotypes: a computational analysis
papers.abstract: Can target breadth and mutation resilience be evaluated as distinct, complementary properties when prioritizing antimalarial chemotypes from African natural-product-inspired chemical space? We addressed this question by linking chemical-space expansion to target-specific docking and a per-target resistance-resilience score (RRS), while keeping computational evidence separate from biological activity. A hybrid library of 65 856 molecules, generated from 396 African natural products and 454 synthetic antimalarial compounds, yielded 19 913 computationally prioritized synthesizable leads. A 17-member polypharmacology-oriented cohort was evaluated by AutoDock Vina against PfDHFR, PfCRT, PfClpP, and PfATP4 using target-specific structural anchors. All 68 candidate–target pairs passed the geometric pose-quality criterion, with scores ranging from −7.91 kcal/mol to −4.63 kcal/mol. Per-target RRS was calculated from separate PfDHFR (N51I, C59R, S108N, I164L) and PfCRT (K76T, K76A) mutant panels, excluding non-binding wild-type targets from the denominator. The cohort comprised six A*, five B, five C, and one D RRS profiles, spanning 68.2 to 111.7. Cross-metric associations were weak or non-significant after multiplicity correction: PNS–RRS ρ = −0.559, ACSI–RRS ρ = −0.132, and RRS–wild-type score ρ = −0.433. The resulting target profiles define testable hypotheses about chemotype breadth and mutation resilience; they do not establish potency, target engagement, or resistance circumvention.

papers.title: Runtime-steered ultrashort molecular dynamics enables million-pose protein–ligand screening
papers.abstract: Applying molecular dynamics (MD) at discovery scale is limited by the cost of evaluating thousands to millions of candidate poses. We present a docking-to-dynamics workflow that makes MD compatible with screening-scale evaluation by applying ensembles of ultrashort trajectories (0.1–5 ns) to each pose. MD-score, a ligand-RMSD stability metric, serves as both a pose-ranking score and, with a threshold, an online stopping criterion. In a conditional six-target benchmark of 88 actives and 702 inactives, MD-score achieved a pose-aware ROC-AUC of 0.868 for the top ten poses, while broad pose and velocity sampling was more effective than extending fewer trajectories. Runtime steering scaled evaluation to 1,234,620 EGFR poses while reducing simulated time to 24% of exhaustive evaluation. A prospective Marburg virus nucleoprotein screen yielded three initial minigenome-active hits among 76 tested compounds. These results position ultrashort MD as a scalable dynamic filter between docking, data-driven prediction and higher-cost validation.

papers.title: MARS-RNA: An Automated Pipeline for Correlating RNA Molecular Dynamics Trajectories with Chemical Probing Data
papers.abstract: Ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules fold into complex, highly dynamic three-dimensional conformational structures that govern their biological activities. Chemical probing methods, such as SHAPE (selective 2’-hydroxyl acylation analyzed by primer extension), provide structural insights in the form of one-dimensional (1D) nucleotide reactivity profiles. However, mapping these one-dimensional profiles back to the underlying dynamic structures remains a key challenge, as traditional analyses rely on a static view based on three-dimensional (3D) high-resolution structures from X-ray crystallography or NMR, rather than accounting for the dynamic nature of the system. In this Application Note, we introduce MARS-RNA (MD Analysis for Reactivity and Structure), an automated pipeline that extracts and integrates multi-scale structural and geometric features from RNA Molecular Dynamics (MD) trajectories, combining them with secondary (2D) and 3D annotations from X3DNA-DSSR to identify features that correlate with experimental reactivity. MARS-RNA processes raw GROMACS trajectories, performs frame-by-frame structural annotation, calculates spatial centroids and physical distance fluctuations, computes Pearson/Spearman correlation coefficients against SHAPE data, and pre-processes results for machine learning pipelines. We show its value on the RNA 3′-UTR (PDB ID: 1AUD, chain A), by highlighting several single correlation with SHAPE reactivity.

papers.title: Dynamic vacancy redistribution shifts Pd nanoparticle coalescence from orientation-gated to defect-enabled on reduced CeO2(110)
papers.abstract: Sintering deactivates supported catalysts, yet how mobile support defects couple to crystallographic transport anisotropy during nanoparticle coalescence remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a ternary Ce–O–Pd machine-learning interatomic potential (Ce–O–Pd MLIP) by fine-tuning a pre-trained large atomic model and validate it against density functional theory (DFT) calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). Large-scale deep potential molecular dynamics (DPMD) simulations resolve early-stage coarsening of Pd 62 /Pd 287 nanoparticle pairs on CeO 2–x (110) and reveal direction-selective coalescence: [11̅0]-aligned pairs exhibit higher probabilities and shorter onset times than [001]-aligned pairs. CI-NEB calculations identify complementary transport anisotropies, with Pd adatom diffusion favored along [11̅0] and oxygen-vacancy migration favored along [001], enabling dynamic defect redistribution within the interparticle region. Statistical trajectory analysis shows that increasing the interparticle oxygen-vacancy fraction from 10% to 30% raises coalescence probability and accelerates bridge and neck nucleation, including along the kinetically less favorable [001] alignment. Time-resolved metrics further show that transient low-coordinated bridge-Pd intermediates precede complete particle merging. Together, these results establish defect–transport coupling as a microscopic mechanism for direction-selective sintering on reduced ceria and suggest that suppressing vacancy enrichment and connectivity in interparticle gaps can improve the stability of oxide-supported metal nanoparticles.

papers.title: The patentability of intermediate chemical compounds
papers.abstract: The present study examines the protection of intermediate chemical compounds and analyses some landmark decisions of the EPO Boards of Appeal. The majority of the decisions under consideration focus on the inventive step requirement (Article 56 EPC). The role of an intermediate product in an innovative production process does not inherently render it inventive. However, it may be eligible for protection if its transformation into the final product requires an original inventive step. It is possible to claim both intermediate and final products in a single patent application, provided there is a strong technical and structural link between them. The rulings highlight the importance of demonstrating an unexpected technical effect—such as a substantial increase in yield—to justify the grant of the patent.

papers.title: Quantifying the Synergistic and Antagonistic Effects of Metal–Organic Complexation on Particulate Matter Oxidative Potential via Redox Kinetics
papers.abstract: Oxidative potential (OP) is an indicator of the ability of redox-active species in particulate matter (PM) to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) via redox chemistry in lung lining fluid. Previous studies have reported synergistic and antagonistic OP effects in mixtures of metals and non-redox-active organics and attributed them to complexation-induced changes in redox potential and kinetics; however, the quantitative validity of this mechanistic hypothesis remains unclear. Here, we evaluated this hypothesis using a newly developed chemical equilibrium–kinetic DTT assay model for Fe–oxalate system. Experiments showed three distinct stages with increasing oxalate-to-Fe ratio: weak interactions at low ratios, strong antagonism at higher ratios, and strong synergy at extremely high ratios. The model successfully reproduced the weak interactions and antagonism. Fe– oxalate complexation enhanced Fe(II)-driven oxidant reduction kinetics but also shifted the Fe(III)/Fe(II) balance toward Fe(III), decreasing Fe(II) concentrations and offsetting much of the kinetic enhancement. Strong antagonism arose from suppression of Fe(III)-driven DTT oxidation by less reactive Fe(III)–oxalate species. Strong synergy was not reproduced by the model, indicating the involvement of additional pathways. These results indicate that the effects of metal–organic interactions on OP are determined by changes in reaction kinetics, chemical speciation, and metal redox balance.

papers.title: ∆-Machine Learning for LC-DFT-level Excitation Energies of Bacteriochlorophyll Molecules in a LH2 Complex
papers.abstract: Bacteriochlorophyll (BChl) molecules are the key pigments in the light-harvesting complex 2 (LH2) of purple bacteria, driving solar energy conversion. During this process, fluctuations in excitation energies of the pigments at ultrafast timescales, modulated by the surrounding protein environment, govern the excitation dynamics within the complex. Because of the relatively large size of these molecules with 85 atoms and their complex electronic structure, these energy fluctuations have so far been estimated using semi-empirical methods or low-level time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT). In this work, we introduce a ∆-machine learning protocol to predict excitation energies at the computationally demanding long-range-corrected (LC) TD-DFT level within a quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) framework, using a semi-empirical tight-binding analogue (TD-LC-DFTB) as a low-cost reference. Excitation energies for 7.2 million BChl geometries from trajectories of the LH2 complex of Rs. molischianum have been determined at the TD-LC-DFT level, both with and without taking the protein environment into account. Unexpectedly, environmental descriptors did not improve performance, so the final model relies solely on molecular descriptors. The resulting LC-DFT and machine-learned excitation energy fluctuations yield reorganization energies closer to experiment than those based on LC-DFTB. The transferability across BChl binding pockets within the protein is, however, limited.

papers.title: Symmetry Breaking Drives Twisted Prismatic Evolution in Atomically Precise Copper Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: The stability of the copper nanocluster has always been a concern owing to its low half-cell reduction potential. It is well documented that anion templates are known to tune the structure and impart stability to the nanocluster. Here, using a simple reduction strategy, we have obtained a dihalide-templated copper nanocluster for the first time. The copper cluster, namely, [Cu23(μ3-Cl)2(SPh-CF3)18(PPh3)6(CF3COO)3], features a unique double triangular prismatic structure. The structure contained a basic unit with the formula of Cu9(μ3-Cl)2 forming an inner triangular prism, which is further wrapped by a second triangular prism with the formula Cu12(SPh-CF3)18(PPh3)6(CF3COO)3, forming a unique twisted triangular double prismatic geometry. Further, we have proposed a plausible growth mechanism that helps us decipher the evolution of the cluster, and here we observed a peculiar “twisted concentric growth” of the two prisms, which occurs due to the radial dimerization of the Cu11 base prism to form the dimeric Cu23 cluster. The unique growth pattern and structure influence the electronic states of the cluster, as evidenced by experimental and theoretical studies, thereby imparting the material with good photoresponse properties. The new insights into this novel dihalogen templated twisted double prismatic copper cluster may pave the way to understanding the unique structural growth and developing photonic materials.

papers.title: Quantitative Cryogenic Orbitrap Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry for structural characterization of lipid nanoparticles
Accelerated characterization of active natural extracts with single-step microfractionation coupled to mass spectrometry and bioassays
papers.abstract: Microfractionation is a prominent alternative for the discovery and characterization of bioactive natural products in complex extracts (e.g., plant, fungal, or microbial); however, the method faces limitations as it requires arduous scale-up for full structural characterization of selected constituents. Furthermore, the integration of microfractionation data with metabolomic data is still a complex and tedious process. To circumvent current limitations, we developed a single-step (i.e., no gram-scale isolation or orthogonal chromatographic steps) microfractionation method that delivers 94 fractions in a 96-deep-well plate, combining biological and computational metabolomic readouts at the milligram scale. Fractionation is coupled to a single-quadrupole mass analyzer, which enables integration with high-resolution metabolomic outputs through an open-source graphical interface we developed. To illustrate the method’s performance, we applied it to characterize extracts from seven plant species — Macleaya microcarpa , Macleaya cordata , Ruta corsica, Thymus camphoratus, Helleborus foetidus, Hypericum hookerianum, and Hypericum olympicum — spanning different extract complexities and biological activities. Across nine independent experiments, totaling 151 sequential injections, we obtained high chromatographic reproducibility. Throughout the study, we injected no more than 10 mg of crude extract per fractionation, and we were able to resolve 17 structures with 1 H NMR dereplication. Furthermore, we associated fraction-level bioactivity with molecular classes and candidate molecules. Our high-throughput, milligram-scale workflow reduces the need for scale-up, making it a practical first step before pursuing gram-scale isolation efforts.

papers.title: A Zero-Shot Single-Point Chemical Language Model Mimics Medicinal Chemist Reasoning for Molecular Optimization and STING Inhibitor Development in Alzheimer’s Disease
papers.abstract: Drug development relies heavily on the ability of medicinal chemists to identify productive, localized structural modifications that improve potency, selectivity, and developability while preserving favorable features of a lead scaffold. Here, we introduce the Single-Point Chemical Language Model (SpCLM), a zero-shot molecular optimization framework designed to computationally emulate this iterative medicinal chemistry paradigm. Built on a Transformer architecture, SpCLM performs controlled single-point molecular modifications encompassing common medicinal chemistry operations and generates focused, chemically interpretable analog spaces rather than large, unconstrained molecular libraries. This strategy enables efficient exploration of structure–activity relationships while maintaining close structural relationships to experimentally tractable lead compounds. Across multiple protein targets and molecular optimization tasks, SpCLM generated compact libraries typically comprising only a few hundred molecules, yet recovered 60%–80% of experimentally validated active compounds from held-out test sets that were not included during model training. Generated molecules showed substantial agreement with experimentally observed structure–activity relationships, including changes in binding affinity and functional activity, demonstrating that the model can reproduce productive chemical transformations without target-specific retraining. These results establish single-point molecular editing as an efficient strategy for translating learned medicinal chemistry knowledge into experimentally relevant molecular optimization. We further applied SpCLM to the development of stimulator of interferon genes (STING) inhibitors as potential therapeutics for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Because aberrant activation of the cGAS–STING innate immune pathway contributes to neuroinflammatory processes associated with AD and related neurodegenerative disorders, pharmacological inhibition of STING represents an emerging therapeutic strategy. Starting from experimentally characterized STING inhibitor chemotypes, SpCLM generated focused analog series through medicinal-chemistry-like single-point modifications. Integration of model-guided generation with structure-based prioritization and experimental evaluation enabled efficient exploration and optimization of STING inhibitor chemical space, identifying analogs with improved activity and providing experimentally supported structure–activity relationships for further lead development. Together, these results demonstrate that SpCLM bridges generative molecular modeling and practical medicinal chemistry by converting broad chemical knowledge into focused, experimentally actionable structural modifications. By recovering a substantial fraction of experimentally active chemical space from only hundreds of generated candidates and enabling the optimization of therapeutically relevant STING inhibitor chemotypes, SpCLM provides a generalizable framework for reducing the experimental search space and accelerating iterative drug discovery.

papers.title: Chemically Fueled Spatiotemporal Patterns from Charge-transfer Supramolecular Assembly
papers.abstract: Creating synthetic systems that autonomously form complex patterns remains a frontier challenge in chemistry and materials science. Here, we present a redox-responsive supramolecular system in which coupled changes in chemical state, assembly, and transport generate spatiotemporal patterns through density-driven chemoconvection. Charge-transfer complexes of pyranine and viologen derivatives undergo reversible redox-controlled assembly–disassembly cycles, producing composition-dependent buoyancy that drive convective flows and feeds back into the evolving assembly distribution. Molecular amphiphilicity and supramolecular assembly morphology tune the resulting pattern type, dot-, stripe-, and flower-like structures without external fields. Finite-element simulations reproduce the observed chemoconvective dynamics, while linear stability analysis predicts the onset conditions and its characteristic wavelength. A weakly nonlinear analysis further identifies reduced translational diffusivity of elongated assemblies as a mechanism that weakens hexagonal mode selection and favors anisotropic near-onset states. These results provide a molecular-to-macroscopic framework for coupling supramolecular organization with chemically driven hydrodynamic pattern formation.

papers.title: Mapping Protein Conformation Ensemble Transitions Using Capillary Vibrating Sharp-edge Spray Ionization and Native Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: Capillary vibrating sharp-edge spray ionization (cVSSI) has been used to examine the effects of applied voltage and ion transfer tube temperature on the mass spectra recorded for ubiquitin ions. For positive polarity experiments, the results duplicate those described previously for one temperature setting where native protein conformer ensembles (N1 and N2) are formed at zero (and low) and high voltage settings and partially unfolded conformer ensembles (P) are formed in the middle voltage range. This work shows that the applied voltage cross over points between production of N1, P, and N2 ensembles shift with ion transfer tube temperature. Similarly, the voltage ranges associated with the presence of these conformer ensembles change with temperature as well. Additionally, the relative abundances of the ions comprising the conformer ensembles respond to ion transfer tube temperatures. Further experiments conducted in negative polarity mode reveal that the P ensemble is accessed for both positively- and negatively-charged ions in the mid voltage regime regardless of solution bias polarity. Taken together, the work supports the prior hypothesis that medium sized, moderately charged, and more slowly moving droplets produced by cVSSI undergo greater heating from the ion transfer tube leading to partial unfolding. The results are discussed with regard to future applications in highthroughput stability screening using “droplet charge tuning” with cVSSI.

papers.title: Beyond Polar Addition: A Radical Alternative for Enantioselective C–C Bond Formation Driven by Alkylzirconocenes Dual Reactivity
papers.abstract: The catalytic asymmetric addition of organometallic reagents to carbonyl compounds represents a fundamental strategy for the synthesis of enantioenriched alcohols. However, conventional carbanionic nucleophiles (e.g., organomagnesium and organolithium) often suffer from competing deprotonation pathways, uncatalyzed background reactions, limited functional-group tolerance, and sensitivity to moisture and air. Alkylzirconocenes, readily generated from abundant alkenes, offer an attractive alternative by virtue of their functional‑group compatibility, photochemical lability, and capacity for remote chain‑walking. Herein, we report a visible-light-enabled, nickel-catalyzed asymmetric radical addition of alkylzirconocenes to aliphatic aldehydes, providing efficient access to enantioenriched secondary alcohols in good yields with high levels of enantioselectivities. This transformation features broad functional-group tolerance, enabling the late-stage enantioselective modification of complex pharmaceutical molecules and natural products. Notably, alkylzirconocenes serve a dual role in this process, acting as both alkyl radical precursors and sources of Zr(III) species for carbonyl activation. Mechanistic investigations, including control experiments, radical‑clock experiments, kinetic analysis, nonlinear effect studies, support a nickel-catalyzed asymmetric radical addition pathway, wherein a Zr(III) species mediates the single-electron reduction of aliphatic aldehydes to generate ketyl radicals. This work establishes a new paradigm for asymmetric carbonyl addition that circumvents the intrinsic limitations of classical polar mechanisms.

papers.title: Empirical Evidence that Dirac–Fock Relativistic and Quantum Corrections are Z-indexing Artifacts
High Temperature Growth and Structural Characterization of ReSe2 Nanotubes
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis and structural characterization of free-standing, highly crystalline ReSe2 nanotubes, the first phase-pure quasi-1D nanostructure to combine a triclinic lattice with wellaligned walls parallel to the tubular axis. The nanotubes were obtained template-free by direct selenidation of ReO3 powder, and characterized by high-resolution imaging, electron di raction, and low-loss electron energy-loss spectroscopy. The 4D-STEM dataset decoded the complex di raction patterns of the triclinic lattice and enabled direct evaluation of the (multi)chirality of individual layers, yielding a workflow transferable to low-symmetry nanotubes. Spectroscopy revealed band edges consistent with bulk ReSe2 and with additional geometry-related subgap features. This preliminary report can open various research avenues e.g., a geometric route to the bulk photovoltaic e ect, or strain-modified optoelectronic properties. Ultrathin nanotubes are expected to enhance symmetry breaking due to curvature strain, resulting in unique band edge properties, while large-diameter nanotubes can support cavity modes, including whispering-gallerytype cavity modes and exciton-polariton phenomena. Additionally, the anisotropic lattice may enable polarization-selective infrared photodetection.

papers.title: New Paradigm in Ligand Coupling: Formation of C(sp2)–C(sp) Bonds by Hypervalent Bismuth
papers.abstract: Ligand coupling is the principal bond-forming reaction of hypervalent main-group compounds, resulting in the formation of diverse carbon–carbon and carbon–heteroatom bonds. Hypervalent organobismuth reagents are known to undergo ligand coupling to form C–O, C–N, C–S, and carbon–halogen bonds, together with carbon–carbon bonds between enolates and aryl groups or alkenes, and phenoxides and aryl groups. Despite four decades of development in organobismuth chemistry, however, coupling between aryl and alkynyl ligands has remained unreported. Here we show that hypervalent organobismuth undergoes aryl–alkynyl coupling through a previously unknown elementary ligand-coupling reaction. A conformationally constrained, recoverable organobismuth scaffold enables selective aryl transfer to terminal alkynes under mild, transition-metal-free conditions. Mechanistic studies support the intermediacy of a pentacoordinate Bi(V) species that is observable by variable-temperature NMR and capable of ligand exchange prior to reductive coupling. These studies establish aryl–alkynyl coupling as a new elementary reaction of hypervalent organobismuth compounds.

papers.title: C-MAGE: Automated Extraction and Organization Engine for Molecular Representations in Chemical Documents
papers.abstract: To exploit the data present in chemical literature for AI applications in chemistry, an expanded and reliable extraction pipeline is needed. AI-ready chemical databases broaden chemical space coverage and provide benchmarking and training sets for machine learning model development to drive innovation within the field. To curate data from chemical documents a multimodal approach is needed. C-MAGE is an open-source molecule extraction engine that processes figures and tables in PDF files to provide machine-readable molecule datasets of the structures as CXS-MILES strings, an encompassing representation which evades heuristic translation of superatoms to SMILES subunits. This led to a 7.1% increase in accurate molecular representations generated. All data extracted undergo confidence-based sorting to ensure high precision (77.6%) in dataset collection, and removes the need for manually sorting datapoint validity. Both the CXSMILES and their confidence values are reproducible and are generated efficiently (1.7 seconds per molecule). C-MAGE’s use is demonstrated by the generation of an annotated dataset containing 1454 CXSMILES strings from 38 chemical documents. C-MAGE thus enables large-scale information extraction of chemical structures in a consistent and reproducible pipeline, complementing the more common text extractions.

papers.title: Developing Efficient and Hyperthermostable Heme Peroxygenase Enzymes as a Biocatalytic Platform for Selective C-H bond Oxidation Reactions
papers.abstract: There is intense interest in using enzyme biocatalysts for chemically challenging oxidation reactions involving the activation of inert carbon-hydrogen bonds in organic molecules. The cytochrome P450 family of heme monooxygenase enzymes can catalyse selective C-H bond hydroxylations and epoxidation reactions. However, the complex and costly nature of these multicomponent systems and the low stability and activity of these systems make larger scale reactions challenging. Thermophilic P450s from bacteria and archaea have been identified but have low activity when reconstituted using electron transfer partner proteins and surrogate oxygen donors. We demonstrate that two cytochrome P450 enzymes (CYP119A1 and CYP119A2) from hyperthermophilic archaea can be engineered to be efficient peroxygenase enzymes requiring only hydrogen peroxide to function. Catalytic oxidation was achieved through modification of three residues in the dioxygen binding groove, including the important addition of a proline residue after the glutamate acid/base residue which significantly enhanced the activity (8-fold over the double mutant and three orders of magnitude over the natural enzyme). These peroxygenases oxidised tridecanoic acid with high activity and enabled further investigation of the substrate range of these enzymes. Both enzymes could oxidise fatty acids and related compounds as well as styrene and the norisoprenoid β-ionone. The oxidation of these substrates occurred with excellent regioselectivity. The CYP119A2-QEP variant was stable to heating at 85-90 °C, had higher activity at 70 °C, could tolerate up to 20 % v/v acetonitrile and was able to catalyse ≥1000 total turnovers across the range of substrates tested. These new peroxygenase biocatalysts, provide hyperthermostable enzyme scaffolds to enable selective and catalytic oxidation of inert C-H bonds using a single enzyme system and cheap cofactors.

papers.title: Acoustic Emission to Provide Early Warning Detection of Lithium-Ion Battery Thermal Runaway
papers.abstract: Understanding lithium-ion battery (LIB) degradation pathways and failure mechanisms is essential given the rare but potentially severe associated hazards. Recent regulations on thermal runaway prevention are driving the need for advanced early detection diagnostic techniques. Acoustic methods, including Acoustic Emission (AE) and Ultrasonic Testing (UT), are promising operando monitoring tools owing to their cost-effectiveness, non-invasive nature, and real-time capability to detect physical and electrochemical changes within cells. This study demonstrates the first use of AE as a diagnostic tool for monitoring stateof-health (SoH), state of safety, and early failure onset. AE measurements were correlated with high-speed synchrotron X-ray radiography, linking acoustic signals to real-time physical changes such as gas formation, cell-volume expansion, and cracking. Experiments across a range of SoC and SoH, covering pristine, aged, and cells cycled below 0 ºC, highlight the robustness of the approach. Machine learning algorithms trained across multiple chemistries and formats enabled real-time signal interpretation. AE reliably identified degradation mechanisms and issued failure alerts across a spectrum of severity, 2 including in lithium-plated cells, with synchrotron imaging confirming the physical origin of key signals. Integrating AE into battery management systems could significantly enhance LIB safety across automotive, grid storage, and manufacturing applications without compromising cost.

papers.title: SugarMALDI: An Application for oligosaccharides’ identification in MALDI-MS data
papers.abstract: Rationale : High-throughput MALDI-MS analyses produce extensive datasets daily. Each spectrum obtained from a complex mixture of oligosaccharides, generated through the enzymatic digestion of polymeric carbohydrates, can contain a vast amount of information requiring processing. Therefore, the availability of specialized informatics tools to facilitate data interpretation is essential. Methods : SugarMALDI is introduced as a cloud-based platform designed to support MALDI-MS interpretation of oligosaccharides. It enables the identification of both labeled and unlabeled oligosaccharides in complex MALDI-MS spectra, facilitates molecular formula assignment, and assesses candidate matches according to mass accuracy. Users can select from nine elemental monosaccharides available in the database, as well as define ionization adducts and chemical modifications, and modify parameters, allowing the software to be flexibly tailored to specific analytical contexts. Results : Designed for high-throughput workflows, the platform accelerates data processing while ensuring reliable interpretation. It was successfully validated using enzymatically digested standard plant gums, including arabinogalactan and galactomannan, as well as authentic watercolor samples, confirming its robustness and practical relevance. The average execution time was approximately two minutes per file, increasing proportionally with the number of selected monosaccharides. These results highlight the software’s efficiency, adaptability, and suitability for diverse analytical applications. Conclusions : SugarMALDI provides assisted data interpretation tailored to the needs of glycobiologists and glycochemists. It supports structural and compositional characterization, enables polysaccharide identification, and delivers clear visual reporting of results, thereby streamlining analysis and enhancing the efficiency and reliability of glycomic investigations.

papers.title: Organometallic chemistry of Pd, Ni, and Au complexes and clusters: the key to high-performance catalysis
papers.abstract: Several liquid-phase organic reactions catalyzed by palladium, nickel, and gold precursors rarely preserve the identity, nuclearity, or electronic state of the added pre-catalyst. Molecular complexes exchange ligands and oxidation states; low-nuclearity aggregates form and fragment; nanoparticles nucleate, leach, ripen, and redeposit. The active catalyst is therefore often a reaction-dependent ensemble rather than a single structure. This Review develops a general, mechanistically explicit framework for these “cocktail” systems. It compares mononuclear complexes, metal clusters and larger nanoparticles of Pd, Ni, and Au; relates their stability to oxidative addition, reductive elimination, ligand exchange, one-electron transfer, and metal–metal bond formation; and distinguishes productive hand-offs from irreversible deactivation. Palladium most readily redistributes population across nuclearity while retaining broad access to Pd(0)/Pd(II) chemistry. Nickel encompasses a wider manifold of oxidation and spin states, but unprotected Ni(0) particles are vulnerable to oxide or hydroxide trapping. Gold is not devoid of redox catalysis: ligand-enabled Au(I)/Au(III) oxidative addition has been demonstrated, while Au(I)-Au(0) exchange can be driven by reduction, deposition, and ligand-mediated particle etching. Its cocktail behavior is therefore more narrowly defined and is largely determined by the ligand architecture and reaction class. We argue that high performance follows from population engineering: controlling the rates of release, interconversion, recapture, and loss of species. Operando population balances, rather than structural snapshots alone, are required to turn this concept into predictive catalyst design.

papers.title: eHydrogenation 2.0: Pd/C-Catalysed Hydrogenation of Alkenes and Alkynes without Externally Supplied H₂
papers.abstract: We report an electrochemically driven Pd/C-catalysed method for the exhaustive hydrogenation of alkenes and alkynes without externally supplied H2. In an undivided cell, commercially available Pd/C in EtOH converts terminal and internal unsaturated substrates under mild constant-current conditions. Standard carbon-electrode/TFA conditions and a complementary Mg-anode/Et4NBF4 protocol furnish saturated products in up to quantitative yield while tolerating alcohols, ethers, esters, amides, sulfonamides, nitriles, phosphates, heterocycles, and carbon–halogen bonds. Most alkenes react at 4 F mol-1, whereas alkynes generally require 6 F mol-1. Coupling heterogeneous catalysis with electrochemical generation of reducing equivalents provides an operationally simple alternative to conventional hydrogenation with externally supplied H2.

papers.title: Regio- and Stereoselective Synthesis and Stereochemical Assignment of Ganaxolone C-3/C-5 Analogues
papers.abstract: Ganaxolone is an FDA-approved steroid for seizures associated with cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 deficiency disorder. Because steroid configuration governs molecular shape and biological activity, unambiguous identification of the C-3/C-5 stereoisomer is essential in steroid medicinal chemistry. However, to our knowledge, comparative synthetic and spectroscopic data for the complete set of four ganaxolone-series C-3/C-5 diastereomers have been lacking. Here, we report their selective synthesis and establish a practical assignment workflow. Conventional MeMgBr addition gave nonselective mixtures that served as reference materials. In contrast, FeCl3/LiCl/MeMgBr afforded the 3α-hydroxy-3β-methyl products 2a and 2b in 91% and 95% yield, respectively, whereas BHT/AlMe3/MeMgBr provided the corresponding C-3 epimers 4a and 4b in 86% and 91% yield. Detailed 1D/2D NMR analysis distinguished the 5α-H and 5β-H series by their C-19 resonances at 11–12 pm and approximately 23 ppm, respectively. Compounds with axial and equatorial C3-Me groups resonated near 26.5 and 31.5 ppm, respectively. VCD spectroscopy, combined with DFT calculations, allowed us to assign spectral markers to specific isomers. The main spectral differences between isomers are localized in two regions of 1250–1150 cm-1, and 1000–900 cm-1. This complete diastereomer set and its authenticated NMR/VCD reference data provide a guide for stereochemical assignment, reaction-selectivity assessment, and impurity control in future C-3-modified neuroactive-steroid research.

papers.title: CampChem: Rubric-Grounded Adaptive Campaigns for Multi-Round Organic Synthesis with Residual Spectral Observation
papers.abstract: Organic synthesis is a multi-round campaign, not a one-shot SMILES completion: a failed solvent, a poisoned catalyst, or leftover starting-material peaks in the 1H NMR force the chemist to revise conditions and try again. Tool-using chemistry agents and condition classifiers still emit a single recipe and then stop. We propose CampChem, an adaptive campaign agent built on a chemistry-instruction LLM. A longitudinal campaign adaptive planner (LCAP) keeps a short memory of failed condition slots and peak signatures and decodes the next catalyst/solvent/reagent tuple under a mask. Chemistry rubric-as-judge reinforcement learning (Chem-RaJ) scores stoichiometry, hazard compatibility, slot completeness, and spectral consistency instead of using a free-form LLM judge. A residual spectral booster (RSB) injects a permutation-invariant peak-set residual when NMR is available and gates to zero otherwise. On SMolInstruct, CampChem reaches 67.1% forward-synthesis and 36.1% retrosynthesis Top-1 exact match with a Mistral-7B LoRA backbone. On USPTO-Condition it attains 0.2940 overall Top-1, and on AutoLabs Experiment 5 it raises protocol F1 from 0.75 to 0.81. Ablations show that Chem-RaJ carries most of the spectrum-free gain, LCAP matters once a prior tuple has been rejected, and RSB contributes mainly on simulated NMR revision.

papers.title: Novel green K-based Metal-Organic Framework with high proton conductivity
papers.abstract: Despite growing interest in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs for protonconductivity applications, monovalent-cation-based MOFs remain comparatively underexplored due to the weaker coordination interactions typically associated with these systems. In this work, we report GR-MOF-28, a novel potassium-based naphthalene tetracarboxylate framework synthesized under mild aqueous conditions at room temperature. Structurally, GR-MOF-28 consists of K2O10 dioctahedra interconnected through tetracarboxylate ligands and coordinated water molecules, generating a confined hydrogen-bond network along the crystallographic channels. The material exhibits proton conductivity values up to 4.3·10-2 S·cm-1 under high relative humidity conditions, placing it among the highest-performing K-based MOFs reported to date. Combined electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and molecular simulations support a water-mediated Grotthusstype proton transport mechanism through the confined hydrogen-bond network. In addition, GR-MOF-28 can be incorporated into a conductive polymer matrix without loss of proton transport properties. These results highlight the potential of underexplored K-based coordination frameworks as proton-conducting materials.

papers.title: Advances in Shear Thickening Fluids: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Shear thickening fluids (STFs) are adaptive materials which exhibit an abrupt increase in the flow resistivity under applied shear stress or shear rate allows the rapid transitions from fluidlike to highly resistant states. This unique response has driven their development for impact protection, vibration damping, soft robotics, biomedical systems and other adaptive technologies. There have been significant advancements in STF research but the links between particle scale interactions, formulation variables, rheological response, processing conditions and application-level performance have not been sufficiently integrated. Reproducibility, long term stability and scalable manufacturing remain limitations to realistic deployment. A critical and integrated evaluation of STFs is presented, relating microstructure, rheological mechanisms, formulation, processing and functional performance into a common framework.
