papers.title: Polarity-resolved imaging reveals active transport in catalytic Janus nanomotors
papers.abstract: Catalytic Janus motors that convert chemical energy into self-propulsion are promising platforms for targeted delivery, sensing, and environmental remediation. Miniaturizing these systems to the nanoscale is challenged by rotational diffusion (𝑫r ∝ 1/𝑹3) increasing faster than translational diffusion (𝑫t ∝ 1/𝑹), which destroys orientational memory. This raises the question of whether catalytic asymmetry can still bias the active displacement direction when orientational memory is short-lived. Answering it requires simultaneous knowledge of particle orientation and translational motion, yet current optical and ensemblebased methods cannot resolve catalytic cap orientation (particle polarity) of Janus nanomotors, leaving its relationship to propulsion direction experimentally inaccessible. Herein, we combine total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy to establish fuel-dependent activity under bulk conditions, with singleparticle visualization by liquid-phase transmission electron microscopy (LPTEM) to characterize active transport of platinum-polystyrene (Pt-PS) Janus nanomotors. TIRF measurements confirm fuel-dependent enhanced diffusion across a range of H2O2 concentrations (0 to 3 wt%). LPTEM analysis reveals superdiffusive transport (𝜶 =1.11) despite the heterogeneous interfacial energy landscape of the liquid-cell and identifies active intervals characterized by a Péclet number (𝑷𝒆) of ∼21. Frame-by-frame extraction of the platinum cap orientation during active displacements reveals a bias towards polystyrene-forward motion, consistent with self-phoretic mechanisms reported for Janus motors at the micron scale, while trajectory analysis yields an orientational persistence length of∼380 nm, corresponding to approximately three particle body lengths. These findings demonstrate that catalytic asymmetry continues to bias displacement direction even when thermal fluctuations limit orientational memory, providing a polarity-resolved mechanistic picture of Pt-PS propulsion at the 100 nm scale.

papers.title: Learning Multiscale Computational Strategies for Supramolecular Recognition
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of host-guest binding affinities with end-point free energy approaches requires a balance between molecular sampling, energetic description, and computational cost, yet the relative importance and interplay of these factors remain poorly understood for chemically diverse supramolecular systems. Here, we establish a systematic benchmark of end-point affinity calculations across more than 300 host-guest pairs involving pillararenes, cucurbiturils, octa acid, and cyclodextrins. We systematically evaluate single-(1T) and three-trajectory (3T) sampling, harmonic entropy corrections, multiple extended tight-binding and DFT levels, and implicit-solvent treatments, and then compare them with established MM/GBSA protocols. We find that different electronic-structure treatments can produce substantially different, host-dependent affinity landscapes, underscoring that the nominal level of theory alone is insufficient to determine predictive reliability. In contrast, the 3T scheme with independent sampling of bound and unbound states consistently improves affinity prediction, whereas MM-based normal-mode entropy provides little systematic benefit. A multi-objective Pareto analysis further reveals a pronounced accuracy-cost trade-off: although selected DFT protocols achieve high predictive accuracy, MM/GBSA 2 / 26 provides a remarkably favorable and broadly transferable balance between accuracy and computational expense. Finally, host-wise analysis and interpretable decision-tree modeling reveal systematic dependence of protocol preference on readily accessible host descriptors, particularly host charge and size. These results establish a practical framework for moving from universal method benchmarking toward host-aware selection of end-point computational protocols, providing a basis for more efficient and adaptive affinity prediction in supramolecular chemistry.

papers.title: From Proteins and Molecules to Cats and Dogs: Visualization as Scalable Minimum Spanning Trees
papers.abstract: Dimensionality reduction and data visualization are essential for analyzing highdimensional datasets, yet traditional projection methods obscure local structural relationships. We present TMAP2, a scalable rewrite of TMAP that maps highdimensional data as a minimum spanning tree. TMAP2 accepts diverse input types, including continuous embeddings, sparse fingerprints, and precomputed graphs, and applies to single-cell, image, chemistry, or protein-language-model data. Every line on the map is therefore a real nearest-neighbor relationship, and exactly one path joins any two points. The number of edges along that path, its hop count, works as a coordinate along a progression: it recovers a pancreatic cell’s developmental age (Spearman 0.90), tracks the collection date of a SARS-CoV-2 spike sequence built from raw sequence alone (Spearman 0.86), and traces a smooth morph from a Persian cat to a Yorkshire terrier that crosses species at a single edge. On 3.6 million CAZyme sequences the same tree separates taxonomic domains and, within the family GH43, sorts sequences by catalytic activity, revealing an anchor enzyme annotated as one activity sitting among a cluster of another. TMAP2 extends the original TMAP from fingerprints to any embedding, at up to one million points with 95–99% recall.

papers.title: Molecular Hydrogen Governs Zinc-Based Battery Failure
papers.abstract: Zinc is among the most promising anode materials for sustainable aqueous batteries, yet its practical deployment is limited by poor interfacial stability and insufficient durability. Because the thermodynamic stability of zinc is incompatible with the water stability window, corrosion and hydrogen evolution inevitably accompany zinc electrochemistry in aqueous electrolytes. Despite being an inherent product of zinc corrosion, molecular hydrogen (H2) has largely been regarded as a passive by-product rather than an active contributor to zinc degradation and dendrite formation. Here, we demonstrate that H2 directly governs zinc deposition and stripping across multiple length scales. By combining operando fibre-optic surface plasmon resonance, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance, X-ray diffraction and operando optical microscopy, we resolve the influence of H2 on the zinc–electrolyte interface from interfacial processes to macroscopic deposit growth. Dissolved H2 destabilizes zinc electrodeposition by increasing the plating overpotential and altering deposition dynamics. It induces a crystallographic texture transition from the basal (002) to the prismatic (101) orientation, producing more porous deposits and modifying the growth kinetics of the zinc deposition front. Quantitative optical-flow analysis further reveals that H2 accelerates local growth dynamics and increases interfacial roughness, thereby compromising deposition uniformity. These effects persist across different electrolyte chemistries and current densities, establishing molecular hydrogen as an active regulator of zinc interfacial stability. Consequently, H2 reduces the cycling lifetime of zinc symmetric cells and promotes premature short circuits in Zn–MnO2 batteries. These findings identify molecular hydrogen as a previously overlooked driver of the morphological and crystallographic evolution of zinc deposits and establish hydrogen management as a design principle for stabilizing the zinc–electrolyte interface. Controlling dissolved H2, including through electrolyte degassing strategies, therefore provides a route towards suppressing dendritic growth, extending battery lifetime and enabling more durable aqueous zinc batteries.

papers.title: Computational shielding of dengue viral prefusion with permeable cyclic-minipeptides
papers.abstract: Permeable cyclic-minipeptide-conformer candidates have been computationally cogenerated to shield the protected prefusionloops (FL) of dengue flavivirus (DENV). The objective was to prevent the pH-dependent dissociation events that trigger flavivirus fusion/ infectivity by exposing the FL highlyconserved sequences to homotrimer fusioncompetent conformations. For that, hundreds of BoltzGen candidates were co-generated targeting a prefusion minimized DENV envelope AB heterodimer (minEAB) model including both EA-protective and EB-FL sequences. The advantages of the newly cogenerated top-affinity nanoMolar candidates include possible bypassing of antibody-related enhancements, low antigenicity, easy chemical synthesis, and strong environmentalphysiological stability. Additionally, top-affinity parents were mutated to derive membranepermeable candidates conserving cyclization, minEAB targets and high-affinities. A few membrane-permeable candidates may serve for in vitro and animal-model experimentallyguided validations of inhibition of DENV fusion and infection.

papers.title: Contrast-Engineered Polymeric Nanoparticles Enable Multicomponent SAXS Imaging in Soft Matter
papers.abstract: Selective visualization of multiple organic components in small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) studies remains a major challenge in complex soft matter systems due to limited electron density contrast. Here, we introduce contrast-engineered polymeric nanoparticles (PNPs) as organic probes for multicomponent SAXS imaging. Well-defined, monomodal cationic PNPs prepared by polymerization-induced self-assembly (PISA) were loaded with the iodine-containing molecule 1,4-diiodobenzene, increasing particle electron density while preserving particle size, morphology, colloidal stability, and surface properties. Incorporation of iodine increased the PNP scattering 2 signal by 57%, improving signal-to-noise ratios and expanding the experimental parameter space for SAXS imaging. To demonstrate the capabilities of the contrast-engineered nanoparticles, they were used to study the flow-induced alignment and spinning of cellulose nanofibril (CNF) filaments. The PNPs were used as spatially resolved tracers to simultaneously visualize and distinguish between sheath flows. The measurements showed that the gelling stream remains confined near the channel walls and does not penetrate the detaching sheath or CNF core, clarifying how the flow architecture supports filament formation. These findings establish contrastengineered polymer nanoparticles as versatile organic probes for SAXS and demonstrate a general strategy for resolving transport, segregation, and spatial organization in multicomponent soft matter systems.

papers.title: Heteroatom-doped fullerene C60 nanoclusters as tunable carriers for a thiazole-sulfonohydrazide lead compound: A DFT study of B, Al, Si, Ga and Ge substitution
papers.abstract: Selective recognition of pharmacologically relevant heteroaromatic lead compounds is important for developing molecular sensing and responsive nanocarrier platforms. C60 fullerene is an attractive nanocluster scaffold because of its stable curved π-conjugated cage and rich electronic structure, but its weakly polarized surface often requires chemical tuning to improve specific host-guest interactions. C60 fullerene and its heteroatom-doped derivatives were investigated as tunable nanocluster platforms for molecular adsorption and electronic sensing using DFT and TD-DFT calculations. The study was aimed at understanding how single-atom substitution in the fullerene cage modified its interaction with a thiazole-sulfonohydrazide lead compound. Pristine C60 had shown only weak molecular adsorption, suggesting that the undoped cage was not active enough for strong host-guest interaction. B and Ge substitution did not significantly improve this limitation. However, doping with Al, Ga, and Si strongly improved the adsorption response of the fullerene surface. Among the studied systems, the Al-doped C60 had the most favourable adsorption profile, while the Ga-doped C60 showed the next strongest interaction. For Si-doped C60, we observed a more balanced behaviour, with stable adsorption and a reliable electronic response. In this study, Frontier orbital, Mulliken charge, DOS, and PDOS analyses were performed. These indicated improved electronic communication upon doping, while QTAIM and NCI results verified stronger non-covalent interfacial contacts. In summary, the results show that the chosen heteroatom dopant can convert C60 from a weak adsorbent into a more responsive nanoplatform. Al-, Ga-, and Si-doped fullerenes were found to be promising candidates for fullerene-based sensing and nanocarrier applications.

papers.title: Identification of Xanthine Oxidase Inhibiting Fractions Containing Low-Molecular-Weight Melanoidins Obtained from Lightly Roasted Barley Products
papers.abstract: Lightly roasted barley flour exhibits xanthine oxidase (XO) inhibitory activity despite containing negligible amounts of pyrogallol, which has been identified as a potent XO inhibitor in highly roasted barley tea. This study aimed to identify the XO-inhibitory compounds responsible for this activity. Assay-guided fractionation of lightly roasted barley extract using octadecyl silica gel (ODS) revealed that the active fractions were not attributable to pyrogallol. Two-dimensional fractionation of the extract from roasted bran part of barley identified fractions II-8-6 and II-8-7 as the principal active fractions under light roasting conditions (180°C). Instrumental analyses (UV-VIS, IR, NMR, and MS) indicated that these fractions contained low-molecular-weight (LMW) melanoidins as active compounds. Supporting this, the thermal reaction products of glucose and glutamine, the most abundant reducing sugar and amino acid in barley bran, respectively, exhibited XO inhibitory activity when heated at 160–180°C. This study is the first to suggest that LMW melanoidins may possess XO-inhibitory activity.

papers.title: A Multi-Coordinate Carbide Ligand as the Anchor for Reactive Transition Metal Clusters: Oxidative Addition, Adduct Formation and Catalytic Hydrosilylation with a Pentanuclear Nickel Carbide Cluster
papers.abstract: The reactivity of a pentanuclear carbide cluster, [( i Pr 3 P)Ni] 5 (µ 5 -C)H 4 ( 1 ), with a variety of reagents was examined. The addition of 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)aniline to 1 resulted in reversible N­­—H bond oxidative addition, forming [( i Pr 3 P)NiH] 5 (µ 4 -C)[N(H)C 6 H 3 ( m -CF 3 ) 2 ] ( 2 ), with a [Ni 5 ] 10+ core. Exposing 1 to neopentyl chloride produced the paramagnetic nickel carbide cluster [( i Pr 3 P)Ni] 5 (µ 5 -C)H 4 (µ 2 -Cl) ( 3 ) from a one-electron oxidation, as well as the homodimerized product 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane. The reaction of 1 with i Pr 3 P=S occurred with a net transfer of the sulfur to give [[( i Pr 3 P)Ni] 5 (µ 5 -C)H 4 (S) ( 4 ). When 1 was exposed to ammonia-borane, BH 3 was incorporated to form [( i Pr 3 P)Ni] 5 (µ 6 -C)H 4 (BH 3 ) ( 5 ) with a short B—C interaction. Carbide complex 1 reacts reversibly with H 2 to give tentatively assigned [( i Pr 3 P)Ni](µ 5 -C)H 6 ( 6 ). Complex 1 catalyzes the hydrosilylation of neohexene by Ph 2 SiH 2 via an intermediate tentatively assigned as the adduct [( i Pr 3 P)Ni](µ 5 -C)H 4 (H 2 SiPh 2 ) ( 7 ). All results demonstrate that despite variable coordination numbers, the carbide ligand can act as an anchoring ancillary ligand that supports geometrical flexible and atypically reactive pentanuclear clusters, even in cases like 5, where the carbide forms bonding interactions with the incoming BH 3 .

papers.title: Stannylene hydrides as key intermediates in redox neutral Sn(II)/Sn(II) catalysis: Hydrodefluorination as a case study
papers.abstract: Low-valent tin hydrides display hydride donor properties that differ markedly from those of conventional organotin(IV) hydrides, yet their catalytic applications have remained largely confined to reactions of polar multiple bonds. Herein, we exploit this distinct reactivity for catalytic C–F bond activation and investigate the mechanism underlying the hydrodefluorination of polyfluoroarenes. An isolable diketiminate-supported Sn(II) fluoride efficiently catalyses the reaction using phenylsilane as terminal hydride source. Stoichiometric and spectroscopic studies establish rapid fluoride–hydride exchange between the stannylene fluoride and phenylsilane, generating a catalytically competent stannylene hydride that directly reacts with polyfluoroarenes to form the hydrodefluorination product and regenerate the Sn(II) fluoride. Density functional theory calculations of its hydricity reveals a substantially greater thermodynamic propensity for hydride transfer than n Bu 3 SnH and further distinguish between two plausible pathways for C–F activation: direct hydride transfer proceeds through concerted nucleophilic aromatic substitution ( c S N Ar) and is favoured over competing oxidative addition to Sn(II). The resulting catalytic cycle therefore operates entirely at Sn(II), combining fluoride–hydride exchange with polar C–F substitution rather than Sn(II)/Sn(IV) redox cycling. These findings establish low-valent tin hydrides as competent intermediates for catalytic C–F bond activation and illustrate how their pronounced hydride donor ability can extend the mechanistic toolbox of stannylene catalysis.

papers.title: PolyGLOT: Graph-Token Language Modeling for Unified Polymer Property Prediction and Programmable Generation
papers.abstract: Polymer design benefits from representations that combine efficient sequence modeling with explicit access to molecular graph structure. String representations provide compact sequences but most remain sensitive to syntax and connectivity errors, whereas sequential graph generation becomes more costly as molecular graphs grow. We introduce PolyGLOT (Polymer Graph Language of Tokens), which represents a linear homopolymer repeat unit as a reconstructable sequence of mostly small molecular subgraphs. A graph encoder embeds each graph token, and a common Transformer backbone is pretrained by masked-token prediction and subsequently fine-tuned for property prediction or causal generation. PolyGLOT achieves competitive property-prediction performance while learning a hierarchy from local graph chemistry to context-dependent token states and property-organized polymer representations. Its attachment-constrained decoder produces valid repeat-unit graphs by construction, and the typically small token size makes local graph operations tractable. Beyond direct generation, the same graph-token interface supports expansion beyond the fixed vocabulary, property-guided local editing, required-substructure control, and small-molecule structural-precedent analysis. These results show that PolyGLOT provides a unified and extensible representation for polymer property prediction, generation, and downstream design.

papers.title: TLQ Method: A Tandem Mixing-Linear Deduction-Quantile Weighted Median Framework for Robust Differential Metabolite Screening in LCMS-Based Untargeted Metabolomics
papers.abstract: Untargeted metabolomics has long been constrained by three interrelated factors: inter-individual variability, difficulty in detecting low-abundance metabolites, and matrix effects. Existing data-processing strategies tend to compensate for systematic variations through algorithmic corrections after data acquisition, but their effectiveness is limited when biological variation is substantial or signals approach detection limits. To address these issues, we propose the TLQ method. Its first module, Tandem Mixing, suppresses matrix effects and enhances signals of low-abundance metabolites through equal‑volume mixing of paired control and treatment samples; its second module, Linear Deduction, strips background through linear subtraction under minimized interference, thereby recovering the true treatment signal; its third module, Quantile Quality‑Weighted Median, performs robust screening on fold‑change data using a chromatographic peak quality-driven weighted median, and further evaluates the reliability of the fold-change direction with Bootstrap confidence intervals. The three modules can be flexibly deployed—the paired mode is optimal when combined, while unpaired scenarios can adopt the A_M mode, and the third module can be independently applied to existing data to improve screening robustness. A validation experiment based on an LPS-induced mouse inflammation model is currently ongoing. Overall, the TLQ method provides an alternative route for differential metabolite screening that compresses inter-individual variability, low-abundance detection difficulty, and matrix effects at the experimental design stage.

papers.title: Facet-Dependent Redox Reversibility Governs the Stability of IrO2 Surfaces under Dynamic Electrochemical Potentials
papers.abstract: Understanding catalyst stability under fluctuating potentials is essential for renewable-powered water electrolysis, yet the surface processes governing degradation remain unclear. Here, we investigate IrO2(110) and IrO2(100) single-crystal thin films under potential cycling relevant to renewable-powered proton-exchange membrane water electrolysis. The activity of IrO2(110) increased after cycling, whereas IrO2(100) deactivated. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated higher Ir valence on both facets, accompanied by a pronounced increase in surface OH species only on (110). O K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy revealed larger oxidation-induced changes on (100), while in situ X-ray absorption fine-structure measurements showed reversible electronic and local structural responses on (110) but irreversible structural evolution on (100). These contrasting responses demonstrate that surface stability under fluctuating potentials cannot be inferred from oxidation state alone. Rather, it depends on whether the facet-specific coordination environment can reversibly accommodate coupled redox and structural perturbations. These results identify redox accommodation as a mechanistic descriptor for oxide electrocatalyst durability under dynamic operation.

papers.title: BiFuN: Machine Learning-Guided Bifunctional Catalysis in Hydrogenation Reactions
papers.abstract: Hydrogen activation and further hydrogenation of substrate cover chemical processes in synthetic and energetic-related technologies. In homogeneous catalysis, transition metal complexes with bifunctional nature offer a platform for the activation and later utilization of the hydrogen-source. However, the development of new catalysts is limited by long-term trial-and-error practices. Screening approaches offer the possibility of relying on key properties to identify promising candidates. Here, we present a data-driven workflow that integrates high-throughput chemical screening, quantum-mechanical (QM) calculations, and machine learning (ML) predictions to accelerate the rational discovery of promising bifunctional catalysts (BFC). Using the Ru-MACHO scaffold as a BFC reference, we systematically explore metal complex variations across four design axes: 11 metal centers, 2,538 pincer ligands, 74 transligands, and 3 axial ligands, generating ca. 1.5M candidate structures. QM-derived data and ML models predict catalyst hydrogenation thermodynamics, enabling rapid identification of top-performing candidates for further mechanistic validation in CO2 hydrogenation. This integrated approach delivers prioritized systems for experimental follow up, demonstrating how curated datasets, targeted QM calculations, and ML together streamline the discovery of next generation homogeneous catalysts for efficient hydrogenation/dehydrogenation reactions.

papers.title: A Solid-Phase Platform for Site-Specific Thiolation and Thioether Functionalization of DNA Oligonucleotides
papers.abstract: Thionucleobases provide distinctive hydrogen-bonding, electronic, and photochemical properties, but their site-specific incorporation into DNA often requires specialized sulfurcontaining phosphoramidites and multistep monomer synthesis. Here, we establish a unified protocol using sodium hydrosulfide (NaSH) and 1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU) for direct on-support conversion of 8-bromo-2′-deoxyadenosine (Br 8 dA) to 8-thio-2′deoxyadenosine (s 8 dA), late-stage C8 thioether diversification, and concurrent conversion of Br 8 dA and 4-triazolylthymidine within a single DNA strand. Electrophilic precursor nucleosides were incorporated by standard solid-phase synthesis and subsequently converted while the oligonucleotide remained support-bound. Conversion of Br 8 dA to s 8 dA was first demonstrated using 2-(trimethylsilyl)ethanethiol and subsequently achieved directly with NaSH·xH2O, eliminating the need for a separate fluoride-mediated deprotection step. Substitution at the C8 was compatible with mixed sequences, multiple modifications, and a range of aliphatic and aromatic thiols, enabling late-stage installation of diverse sulfurcontaining functionalities. Application of the same support-bound protocol to 4-triazolylthymidine afforded DNA containing one or more 4-thiothymidine (s 4 T) residues, and both thionucleobases could be generated within the same strand. Products were characterized by strong-anion-exchange high-performance liquid chromatography and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry. This workflow shifts sulfur installation from specialized monomer synthesis to a simple late-stage conversion and provides practical access to site-specifically thiolated and C8-thioether-functionalized DNA.

papers.title: A General Approach to Highly Substituted 1,2-Azaborines via Borylative Benzannulation of Unsaturated Imines
papers.abstract: Highly substituted, monocyclic 1,2-azaborines could expand the chemical space available for benzene bioisosterism; however, their synthesis remains an unmet challenge. Here we report a general, modular, transition-metal-free strategy that couples unsaturated imines with dihaloboranes to construct diverse 1,2-azaborines through a borylative benzannulation pathway. This method provides efficient access to tetra-, penta-, and hexa-substituted azaborines, including fused, macrocyclic and heteroatom-substituted scaffolds. High chemoselectivity and convenient handling are achieved by developing well-defined quinoline-buffered borylation reagents. Post-functionalization at the boron and nitrogen positions of 1,2-azaborines, synthesis of a BN-isostere of xibornol, and access to isotopically enriched 10B-1,2-azaborines have been demonstrated.

papers.title: Vibrational energy pooling driven by collective light–matter coupling
papers.abstract: Concentrating vibrational energy from multiple molecules onto selected members of an ensemble is central to mode-selective chemistry and molecular energy transport. Yet established mechanisms of vibrational energy pooling (VEP) rely on molecular collisions or strong intermolecular interactions. Here we demonstrate that collective vibrational strong coupling (VSC) provides a distinct route to VEP, with the optical cavity serving as an energetic intermediary. State-resolved cavity quasi-classical trajectory simulations of bend-excited water molecules reveal that the cavity transiently stores and redistributes vibrational energy among spatially separated, noninteracting molecules, producing bend overtones and higher excited states that are absent under otherwise identical free-space conditions. The cavity-mediated energy pooling persists in ensembles containing up to 10,000 molecules, while the pooling yields vary nonmonotonically with both collective coupling strength and cavity detuning. These results show how delocalized vibrational polariton promotes mode-specific vibrational energy localization and identify collective coupling and spectral resonance as joint control parameters for nonequilibrium molecular energy flow.

papers.title: Computational Elucidation of System-Dependent Excited-State Relaxation Mechanisms and Stokes Shifts in Indole-Based Chromophores
papers.abstract: The absorption spectrum of aqueous indole contains contributions from the two lowest-lying excited states, La and lower-energy Lb. The corresponding fluorescence spectrum exhibits a large Stokes shift attributed to solvent-induced inversion of the excited-state ordering followed by emission from the La state. However, modeling excited-state relaxation mechanisms in aqueous indole is challenging because the two excited states are strongly coupled in a condensed-phase environment. Here we employ the thermalized time-evolving density operator with orthogonal polynomials algorithm (T-TEDOPA) to simulate the finite-temperature quantum dynamics of molecular systems with two vibrationally-coupled electronic excited states. We consider indole, 2-cyanoindole (2CNI), and L-tryptophan (Trp) to examine effects of substitution on the optical properties of indole. In all three chromophores, ultrafast population transfer occurs from the brighter La state to the darker Lb state. In indole and Trp, the La state has pronounced charge-transfer character and is stabilized by the polar solvent, leading to its repopulation during solvent relaxation and predominantly La emission. In 2CNI, the reduced charge-transfer character of La weakens its solvent stabilization, suppressing population transfer back to La and resulting in Lb emission. T-TEDOPA reproduces the experimentally supported excited-state relaxation mechanisms and emissive state assignments. The moderate underestimation of the Stokes shifts for systems with strong solute-solvent interactions, such as indole and Trp, is attributed to limitations of the electronic-structure method and the QM/MM solvent treatment. These results further establish T-TEDOPA as a robust framework for simulating photophysical properties in complex condensed-phase systems.

papers.title: A DFT Study of Oxidative Lignin β-O-4 Bond Cleavage by Transition-Metal Catalysis
papers.abstract: Biomass is the only viable source of renewable terrestrial carbon. Lignin, a rigid structure of biomass, has been investigated for its difficulty to depolymerize. β-O-4 linkages, which account for 50-60% of all inter-unit bonds, are the primary targets for breaking down the polymer to derive aromatic compounds. Although transition-metal-assisted oxidative cleavage has been identified as a promising method, the conventionally used 4d and 5d transition metals are scarce and expensive, limiting industrial scalability. This study evaluates the efficiency of cost-effective and earth-abundant transition metals Cu(II), Mn(II), Ti(II), and V(II) for the oxidative cleavage of the β-O-4 bond. Using the hybrid density functional B3LYP and wave function CCSD (T) functionals, geometry optimizations for the adducts, transition states, and intermediate complexes were conducted on methoxyethane as a simplified model dimer. Our results identify vanadium as the most promising catalyst kinetically, with a Boltzmann population of ~100%, and copper as the most promising catalyst thermodynamically, with a Boltzmann population of 99.69%. Additional verification using the actual β-O-4 model compound, guaiacylglycerol-β-guaiacyl ether, showed that both V and Cu stretched the target bond to >2.5 Å, exceeding the C–O bond dissociation threshold (1.7–1.8 Å). Given their strong performance as homogeneous catalysts, vanadium and copper show promise for incorporation into heterogeneous catalyst architectures to enable industrial-scale biomass conversion for applications in sustainable materials and biofuels.

papers.title: GPU-Accelerated Large-Scale Nonadiabatic Excited State Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics is essential for simulating photoinduced processes, but its application to large molecular systems is often limited by the cost of repeatedly evaluating excited-state energies, forces, and nonadiabatic couplings. Here, we present a GPU-accelerated implementation of trajectory surface hopping within PYSEQM (https://github.com/lanl/PYSEQM/), a PyTorch-based semiempirical quantum chemistry framework. The module combines semiempirical model Hamiltonians with configuration-interaction singles excited states and introduces the nonadiabatic coupling vectors and time-derivative couplings required for surface-hopping dynamics. The implementation further includes treatments of trivial crossings and electronic decoherence, providing a complete framework for propagating coupled electronic and nuclear dynamics. To improve GPU utilization, independent trajectories are propagated concurrently in batches. Benchmark calculations show that this strategy substantially increases aggregate simulation throughput as the batch size is increased for small molecules. We demonstrate the applicability of the method to large molecular systems by simulating the excited-state population dynamics of methyl-and tert-butyl substituted molecular nanostar dendrimers, which contain dense manifolds of electronically excited states. These calculations show that semiempirical surface-hopping dynamics can be extended to molecular systems that remain challenging for conventional ab-initio approaches. In addition, the differentiable PyTorch formulation provides a data-science route for optimizing semiempirical Hamiltonian parameters against reference excited-state properties and, ultimately, dynamical observables. PYSEQM therefore provides a platform for high-throughput nonadiabatic molecular dynamics and for the development of data-driven semiempirical models for photophysics and photochemistry.

papers.title: Dramatic acceleration by silica gel under highly concentrated conditions: Aromatic halogenation and nitroaldol (Henry) reactions
papers.abstract: Dramatic acceleration of aromatic halogenation and nitroaldol (Henry) reactions was achieved by the addition of silica gel under highly concentrated conditions. Bromination, chlorination, and iodination of various aromatic substrates were examined in the presence of silica gel under highly concentrated conditions, and significant acceleration was observed for many substrates compared with conventional conditions. The combination of silica gel and highly concentrated conditions also markedly accelerated nitroaldol (Henry) reactions of aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes. Silica gel could be recovered and reused in both halogenation and nitroaldol reactions without significant loss of activity. These results demonstrate a simple, efficient, and more sustainable protocol for promoting important organic transformations.

papers.title: Enantioselective Total Synthesis of (–)-TAN-67
papers.abstract: (–)-TAN-67 is a synthetic opioid alkaloid that acts as a selective δ-opioid receptor (δ-OR) agonist and shares structural similarity to µ-opioid ligands, such as morphine, naltrexone, and many clinically employed derivatives. Previously, the synthesis of (–)-TAN-67 required preparing trans-fused (±)octahydroisoquinoline 1 followed by chiral resolution. The existing routes to access this key intermediate require 7–9 steps, produce 2–20% overall yield, produce racemic material, and have reproducibility issues. Herein, we disclose the first enantioselective synthesis of (–)-TAN-67, which was enabled by the synthesis of a distinct cis-fused (+)-octahydroisoquinoline intermediate, which was synthesized in 10 steps and 15% overall yield. This synthesis features an enantioselective conjugate addition step to establish the all-carbon quaternary stereocenter, a γ-selective Mukaiyama-Mannich reaction to form the isoquinolinone core, a Friedlander’s quinoline synthesis, and a substrate-controlled diastereospecific reduction to establish the tertiary stereocenter delivering (–)-TAN-67 in 13 steps, 8% yield, and 95% ee. This synthesis enables access to (–)-TAN-67 and analogs thereof, which could accelerate medicinal chemistry efforts.

papers.title: 1º Non-Anomeric Glycoboranes: Palladium Catalyzed Synthesis and Functionalization
papers.abstract: The proliferation of methods for transforming the carbon–boron bond has made alkyl organoboranes prized intermediates in organic chemistry. Despite this versatility, the synthesis of borylated carbohydrates (i.e., “glycoboranes”) is largely limited to borylation at the anomeric position or chemistries that leverage glycals to introduce boron at C2 or C3. Herein, we describe a Pd-catalyzed, deiodinative borylation that installs a pinacol boronic ester moiety at the primary position of carbohydrates most distal to the anomeric center to afford 1º non-anomeric glycoboranes. Variously protected glucose, galactose, and mannose scaffolds as well as partially unprotected sugars and di- and trisaccharide substrates readily underwent borylation on millimole scale under these conditions. To demonstrate their utility as functionalizable intermediates, we developed a C( sp 2 )–C( sp 3 ) Suzuki coupling of these 1º non-anomeric glycoboranes. Exploration of the electrophile scope showed generality across a variety of aryl and heteroaryl bromides, including challenging pyridyl and unprotected indole electrophiles as well as four tripeptides containing a (hetero)aryl bromide-functionalized amino acid residue. Taken together, this work illustrates the viability of 1º non-anomeric glycoboranes as intermediates in the synthesis of functionalized glycosides and unnatural glycopeptides.

papers.title: Unveiling Surface Reaction Networks in Biomass-Derived Compound Upgrading
papers.abstract: Biomass-derived platform molecules often undergo complex surface reactions in which productive routes compete with catalyst deactivation, limiting catalyst selectivity and stability. Identifying the molecular origins of these competing processes remains challenging, as conventional computational approaches generally rely on chemical intuition and hypothesis-driven rules, while strongly adsorbed intermediates and poisoning species remain difficult to characterize experimentally. Here, we combine enhanced sampling reaction discovery techniques with machine learning interatomic potentials, experimental catalytic tests, and in situ DRIFTS to unravel the surface reaction network controlling methyl levulinate conversion on zirconia. Our simulations reveal a highly interconnected network of elementary transformations in which surface Lewis acidic Zr sites and basic oxides cooperatively promote carbonyl activation and α-deprotonation, giving rise to competing pathways toward cyclization and catalyst poisoning. This mechanistic picture is supported by experimental evidence, which reveal a progressive decrease in angelica-lactone formation and the accumulation of persistent carboxylate-like surface species. Our results show that the same cooperative acid base surface motif which activates the substrate and promotes productive cyclization, also induces irreversible surface trapping leading to catalyst poisoning. By revealing this intrinsic competition at the molecular level, our work provides a clue on how to steer zirconia reactivity toward selective biomass conversion while suppressing the formation of the persistent surface species responsible for deactivation. More broadly, our work establishes a general strategy to tackle complex reaction networks in heterogeneous catalysis.

papers.title: Probing Factors Important to Bulk Nanobubble Stability: A Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Bulk nanobubbles have attracted considerable attention because of their reported long-term stability. Yet this apparent stability appears inconsistent with classical predictions based on the Young–Laplace equation, and despite extensive theoretical and experimental studies, the underlying molecular mechanisms responsible remain unresolved. In this work, molecular dynamics simulations are used to evaluate the pressure–radius relationship for bulk nanobubbles and to investigate origins for possible deviations from classical Young–Laplace behaviour. Methodological aspects, including appropriate treatment of short-range interactions and determination of bulk liquid pressure in nanobubble systems, are also examined and validated. Comparisons reveal that cutoff-based approaches for short-range interactions introduce significant errors in the system pressure, whereas the Particle–Mesh Ewald method provides an accurate and computationally efficient alternative. We confirm that the system-averaged virial pressure rigorously corresponds to the bulk-liquid pressure for nanobubble systems. Pressure–radius analyses of empty nanobubbles in water and cyclopentane systems using the equimolar radius yield a description consistent with Young–Laplace behaviour when curvature-dependent corrections to the surface tension (i.e. the Tolman length) are accounted for. In water, the pressure contribution due to interfacial dipole polarization was found to be small. Accounting for the pressure (or density) dependence of the surface tension was shown to dramatically impact estimates for the Tolman length in cyclopentane. These results establish a consistent molecular simulation framework for further investigations of nanobubble stability and provide new insights into the roles of curvature, interfacial polarization, and liquid properties in determining mechanical equilibrium in nanobubbles.

papers.title: Zirconium-Mediated C–O Bond Cleavage of Alkenyl Ethers Enables Nickel-Catalyzed C(sp3)–C(sp3) and C(sp3)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: Inert aliphatic C–O bonds are ubiquitous in both natural and synthetic feedstocks, yet their direct functionalization remains a formidable challenge in sustainable synthesis. Here we report a tandem strategy that merges thermal zirconium-mediated deoxygenation of alkenyl ethers with visible-light-induced nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling. Through β-oxygen elimination and chain walking, readily available ethers are transformed into alkylzirconocene nucleophiles, enabling efficient C(sp3)–C(sp3) and C(sp3)–C(sp2) bond formation with alkyl and aryl iodides. The method exhibits broad functional group tolerance, late-stage applicability to pharmaceuticals and natural products, gram-scale scalability, and an enantioselective variant (94% ee). Notably, the oxygen-retentive reaction of dihydropyran and the dual functionalization of PMB-protected ethers highlight the atom-economical potential of this protocol. Mechanistic studies elucidate the preference for β-oxygen elimination over β-hydride elimination and reveal the role of a special Zr (III) species as a single-electron donor in the catalytic cycle. This work provides a direct route from unactivated aliphatic C–O bonds to functionalized alkanes, advancing the sustainable valorization of renewable biomass feedstocks.

papers.title: Site-selective alkali ion alloying in double perovskites via liquid-assisted mechanosynthesis revealed by solid-state NMR
papers.abstract: Lead-free halide double perovskites are promising materials for light-emitting and photovoltaic applications. However, compositional tuning of their structural and optoelectronic properties has largely focused on B-site and halide alloying. In this work, we show that Cs + on the perovskite A-site of Cs 2 AgInCl 6 can be partly substituted with Rb + using simple apolar liquid-assisted mechanochemistry. By comparing Rb + with Na + substitution we show that ion size drives the site-selectivity of alkali ion substitution into double perovskites, with Na + preferentially occupying the perovskite B-site. By combining multinuclear solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy with X-ray diffraction, we show that Rb+ not only enters the double-perovskite site-selectively but also induces local symmetry breaking of the cubic structure, comparable to the effect of B-site Na + /Ag + alloying, with important implications for symmetry-forbidden photoluminescence emissivity. This work extends the tuneable compositional range of lead-free double perovskites to include A-site mixing while also establishing the site-selectivity of alkali ion speciation into the double perovskite structure.

papers.title: Controlled Generation of Unstabilized N-Alkyl Nitrile Imines Enables Regioselective [3+2] Cycloadditions with Diverse Dipolarophiles
papers.abstract: N-Alkyl nitrile imines remain underdeveloped as intermediates for intermolecular cycloaddition. Here, we report their in situ generation and regioselective [3+2] cycloaddition with activated and unactivated alkenes and alkynes, affording N-alkyl pyrazolines and pyrazoles in good to excellent yields. The method accommodates broad variation in both reaction partners and enables gram-scale preparation of a key pyrazole fragment used in the synthesis of lenacapavir in 79% yield over two steps.

papers.title: Population-Specific H-Antigen Chain-Type Variation and Its Potential Impact on Enzymatic Universal-Blood Conversion: A Computational Pilot Study
papers.abstract: Enzymatic conversion of donor blood to universal type O ("ECO blood") is an active area of transfusion medicine research, with recently discovered bacterial enzymes capable of removing canonical and structurally extended ABO blood-group antigens. Whether human genetic variation affecting antigen chaintype distribution influences the efficiency of these conversion enzymes has not previously been examined. Using FucOB, a structurally characterized alpha-1,2-fucosidase, as a test case, we combined published mutagenesis data with molecular docking to compare its interaction with two physiologically dominant chain-type variants of the H blood-group antigen (type I and type II), whose relative abundance on red blood cells is genetically determined by FUT2 secretor status. We find a reproducible docking asymmetry tighter, more consistent binding to H type I than to H type II - that holds under two independent scoring methods. Combining this finding with published Indian FUT2 non-secretor phenotype frequencies (20-33%, varying by region), we estimate that a substantial minority of the Indian population may experience reduced FucOB conversion efficiency due tolacking H type Ichainsentirely.Thisisapreliminary computational finding requiring experimental validation; we report it, together with full methodological transparency and an explicit accounting of AI-assisted contributions, to invite expert scrutiny before further investment.

papers.title: BF2-Boracycles Enabling Selective ortho-Mono Hydrogen Isotope Labelling
papers.abstract: Selective deuteration of pharmaceutical agents and functional materials can enhance their pharmacokinetic, physicochemical, and optoelectronic properties, while selective tritiation is indispensable for the preparation of radiolabeled tracers for highly sensitive studies in chemistry and biology. An efficient and highly coveted approach to selectively incorporate deuterium or tritium at a single position within a chemical structure involves hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE). However, mono selective HIE is highly challenging due to reliance on precious metal catalysts, as well as poor selectivity and limited functional group tolerance within individual protocols. Herein, we report a universal boron-mediated, silver-catalyzed ipso-deuteration methodology applicable to a range of 2-phenylpyridine, phenylamide, and aryl O-carbamate derivatives, employing BBr3 as the borylating agent and D2O as an electrophilic deuterium source. Central to this approach is the initial formation of benchtopstable BF2 complexes, which serve as versatile intermediates and can be converted to the corresponding deuterated analogues in high yield and with high isotopic incorporation, upon demand. This strategy offers both operational simplicity and flexibility. Furthermore, the scope of the method has been successfully extended to several pharmaceutical compounds incorporating these structural motifs, highlighting its utility for the late stage selective deuteration of bioactive molecules.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Electronic Response Modes Govern Catalytic Energetics under Illumination
papers.abstract: While nonequilibrium electronic configurations generated under illumination are widely recognized as central to photocatalysis, how they govern catalytic reaction energetics remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a delta self-consistent field (ΔSCF)-based theoretical framework to investigate catalytic reaction energetics under nonequilibrium electronic conditions and demonstrate it using H2 dissociation, a fundamental hydrogen-activation step, at doped Cu/ZnO photocatalytic interfaces. By constructing and continuously following metastable nonequilibrium electronic configurations along the reaction coordinate, we directly establish their connection with catalytic reaction energetics. We show that illumination-induced catalytic responses are governed not simply by the nonequilibrium electronic configurations accessible under illumination, but by how the resulting electronic perturbations couple to chemically relevant interactions as the reaction proceeds. Depending on catalyst composition, these perturbations give rise to three distinct nonequilibrium response modes, leading to dopant-dependent promotion or inhibition of H2 activation. The present work establishes a mechanistic framework linking evolving nonequilibrium electronic configurations, excitation-induced response modes, and catalytic energetics, providing general design principles for tailoring heterogeneous photocatalysis through nonequilibrium electronic-structure engineering.

papers.title: Runtime-steered ultrashort molecular dynamics enables million-pose protein–ligand screening
papers.abstract: Applying molecular dynamics (MD) at discovery scale is limited by the cost of evaluating thousands to millions of candidate poses. We present a docking-to-dynamics workflow that makes MD compatible with screening-scale evaluation by applying ensembles of ultrashort trajectories (0.1–5 ns) to each pose. MD-score, a ligand-RMSD stability metric, serves as both a pose-ranking score and, with a threshold, an online stopping criterion. In a conditional six-target benchmark of 88 actives and 702 inactives, MD-score achieved a pose-aware ROC-AUC of 0.868 for the top ten poses, while broad pose and velocity sampling was more effective than extending fewer trajectories. Runtime steering scaled evaluation to 1,234,620 EGFR poses while reducing simulated time to 24% of exhaustive evaluation. A prospective Marburg virus nucleoprotein screen yielded three initial minigenome-active hits among 76 tested compounds. These results position ultrashort MD as a scalable dynamic filter between docking, data-driven prediction and higher-cost validation.

papers.title: OptiMatLLM: A Benchmark Suite and a Lightweight Domain-Specific LLM for Optical Materials Research
papers.abstract: The design of optical materials relies on highly specialized knowledge, which creates a major bottleneck for data-driven scientific discovery in the optical material domain. Large language models open new possibilities for scientific research, but general-purpose models struggle with the domainspecific physical logic and terminology. More importantly, no standardized evaluation benchmark exists to systematically assess how well LLMs perform on optical materials tasks. To fill this gap, we first construct two evaluation benchmarks, Optic_Choice and Optic_QA, designed specifically for the optical materials domain. We build a high-quality instruction-tuning dataset of 23,225 question-answer pairs through an automated multi-stage pipeline from a curated corpus of papers and textbook. We then develop OptiMatLLM, a 7-billion-parameter LLM fine-tuned LLM on this corpus. Evaluation results show that OptiMatLLM achieves top performance on our optical benchmarks, reaching 0.79 accuracy on Optic_Choice, while also performing competitively on broader scientific tests such as CMHChem, ChemBench, and MaScQA. The model retains strong general capabilities as well, scoring 0.91 on the GSM8K mathematical reasoning benchmark. We further provide a systematic comparison of multiple leading models on these benchmarks, establishing a reference for future work. All benchmarks, dataset, and model are publicly released to support further research on LLMs for optical and optoelectronic materials design.

papers.title: Quantum Chemical Microsolvation via Free Energy–Based Solvation Site Identification
papers.abstract: In quantum chemical descriptions of solutions, solvents are treated either implicitly, accounting only for bulk properties, or explicitly by including solvent molecules in the calculations. Although explicit treatments are more accurate, they are often computationally prohibitive. As a cost-effective alternative, microsolvation models have emerged that include only a limited number of solvent molecules to capture the most relevant solute–solvent interactions. However, determining their optimal number, positions, and orientations remains a challenge. Existing approaches typically either build up solvent clusters in a stepwise, order-dependent manner or select solvent molecules based on geometric criteria without directly quantifying interaction strength. Here, we introduce the Free Energy Based Identification of Solvation Sites (FEBISS) 2, a revised microsolvation protocol based on Grid Inhomogeneous Solvation Theory (GIST) applied to molecular dynamics trajectories. The method identifies thermodynamically favorable solvation sites from Free Energy contributions. It automatically places, orients, and ranks solvent molecules by interaction strength, using a statistically averaged, order-independent orientation procedure that is applicable to arbitrary rigid solvents rather than water alone. This approach provides a physically grounded criterion for selecting the number of solvent molecules in microsolvated clusters. We demonstrate the applicability of the approach across a range of systems, from small organic molecules to transition-metal catalysts, and for various solvents.{We show that explicit microsolvation affects the electronic structure even in systems traditionally considered weakly solvent-sensitive, highlighting FEBISS 2 as a practical methodology to set-up physically meaningful microsolvation clusters for quantum chemical studies.

papers.title: Model of the Henrys: Eyring, Frank, and the Foundations for Predicting Transport Coefficients
papers.abstract: Henry Eyring’s absolute rate theory provides a microscopic picture of liquid transport based on molecular jumps, while Henry Frank’s free volume theory relates entropy changes to an effective cage volume in condensed phases. In this work, we integrate these two frameworks to obtain the Model of the Henrys (MotH), a unified description of transport phenomena based on the (re)movement of molecules within a system. Starting from Eyring’s viscosity expression, we replace activation energies by residual energies, and express the free volume via Frank’s entropy–free volume relation using residual entropy. The resulting model contains a small set of molecule-specific parameters. We show that viscosity and self-diffusion of alkanes, alcohols, carbon dioxide, and water are described in good agreement with experimental and molecular dynamics data over wide temperature and pressure ranges, including the strongly interacting fluids that approaches such as entropy scaling struggle to capture. Transferring the free volume part of the model to thermal conductivity of alkanes serves as a proof of concept, validating the decomposition on which MotH rests. Analysis of the fitted parameters is consistent with Frank’s original idea that free volume is primarily controlled by molecular size, whereas activation energies are strongly family-dependent. Beyond the model itself, MotH provides a common origin for descriptions of transport that are usually treated as competing: Arrhenius/Andrade correlations and empirical entropy scaling are recovered as limits of the MotH model.

papers.title: Intramolecular oxygen coupling mediates water oxidation on an oxide electrocatalyst
papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanistic pathways of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential for guiding the design of catalytic materials and advancing sustainable energy technologies, as sluggish OER kinetics remain a major limitation. Here, using 18 O isotope labeling experiments, we provide kinetic evidence for oxygen coupling occurring within the lattice of a Bi 0.2 Sr 0.8 CoO 3-δ perovskite catalyst, unveiling an OER pathway distinct from conventional mechanisms and closely analogous to that of Photosystem II. We demonstrate that oxygen-to-metal charge transfer drives the spontaneous formation of oxidized lattice oxygen species, including molecular O 2 -like dimers confined within the crystal lattice, which represent the key catalytic intermediate during oxygen evolution on a highly active cobalt-containing oxide catalyst.

papers.title: A Human Audit of AI-Generated Theoretical Chemistry: Lessons from Ten Chapter-Level Peer Reviews
papers.abstract: AI-assisted study spanning molecular stability, the Born–Oppenheimer approximation, chemical bonding, density functional theory, electron correlation, reaction dynamics, thermodynamics, kinetics, and transport. Across the available referee reports, all ten chapters were recommended for acceptance after minor revision within the assessment rubric used in the review project, and no confirmed substantive error was identified that invalidated a principal scientific conclusion. The main value of the project does not lie in claiming ten new fundamental theorems. Rather, the chapters repeatedly make explicit the mathematical steps separating one level of description from another: stability from binding, exact theory from approximation, finite-system calculation from an asymptotic limit, microscopic dynamics from effective kinetics, and conservation laws from macroscopic transport. The review record therefore suggests that AI can assist in constructing technically sophisticated and auditable theoretical arguments. It also motivates, but does not by itself establish, a broader hypothesis: as scientific generation becomes easier, independent verification may become an increasingly important bottleneck.

papers.title: Observation Deviation as a Quantitative Observability Measure of Weak Chemical Features in Analytical Measurements
papers.abstract: When a chemical signal recedes into noise, deciding whether a weak chemical feature is still worth observing - and where observation should stop - is usually delegated to signal-to-noise conventions, software parameters, or an analyst’s personal judgment. We propose Observation Deviation (τ), a dimensionless measure of chemical-feature observability, that turns this tacit judgment into a quantifiable analytical variable. Within a stated observation protocol, τ quantifies how much an analytical chemical feature deviates from the local profile its observation anticipates. On simulated analytical responses and real GC–MS chromatograms, three independent observer experiments (19 observers in total) order systematically along the τ scale, including the region where observer disagreement is strongest. τ also separates human-judged clear peaks from noise in a case-matched instance where raw signal-to-noise does not. We further develop TauNet - a learned representation of chemical-feature observability - showing that this observability can be learned directly from measured response profiles and, without re-calibration, transfers from controlled simulated responses to previously unseen real chromatographic measurements. The resulting model is independently implemented as a lightweight single-file application. τ thus does not replace analytical judgment, nor does it impose a universal decision threshold; rather, under a declared observation protocol, it renders chemical-feature observability measurable, learnable, and reproducible. This contrasts with existing chemical neural-network work: for peak detection, quantitative regression, or molecular-property prediction, those methods learn to map chemical signals to chemical conclusions - signal → peak/class/property - whereas τ fills an observability layer that none of them occupy, between candidate detection and chemical interpretation.

papers.title: PXRD-Diff: diagnosing the encoder bottleneck in diffusion-based powder-diffraction structure inversion, with classical autoindexing as a drop-in remedy
papers.abstract: Inverting a one-dimensional powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) pattern to a three-dimensional crystal structure remains an open problem, and recent generative approaches report results under mutually incompatible protocols with failure modes seldom catalogued. PXRD-Diff, a 3.7 M-parameter conditional diffusion model trained on the CDVAE MP-20 split, is presented, and DiffractGPT, PXRDnet and deCIFer are reproduced through the same pymatgen StructureMatcher harness. The central, statistically robust finding is mechanistic: the learned PXRD encoder reaches a 0.007 normalised auxiliary lattice-regression loss in isolation, yet substituting that head’s own lattice into the sampler recovers only 1.2 % of structures, because its ~1.1 Å length error shifts every Bragg peak by ~15 %. The limiter is the global pooling that discards absolute peak positions, not the denoiser alone. A perturbation study locates a sharp sensitivity knee at ~0.5 Å cell error, and a true-lattice oracle lifts match to 4.5 % at n = 1000 (three seeds; 95 % Wilson confidence interval [3.8, 5.3]), disjoint from the no-true-lattice indexer’s 1.5 % [1.2, 2.0]. Replacing the learned lattice head with a classical Q-space autoindexer raises no-true-lattice match to 1.5 % from a learned head that recovers essentially nothing; a three-seed paired McNemar test confirms the gain is significant (p < 10−4; 27 fixed, none broken), concentrated in the high-symmetry systems below the sensitivity knee. Reproduced on one harness, deCIFer reaches 73.8 % match, DiffractGPT 18.9 % and PXRDnet 30.0 %, leaving PXRD-Diff 12–46 times behind. The contributions are the encoder-bottleneck diagnosis, the classical-indexer drop-in, a four-item failure catalogue and the shared evaluation harness; code, checkpoints and the differentiable Bragg simulator are released.

papers.title: Reactivity Over Recognition: Covalent Screening of Natural Products against Falcipain-2 and Falcipain-3
papers.abstract: We present a reproducible, reactivity-weighted covalent-screening workflow that separates molecular recognition, intrinsic electrophile reactivity, and matched host-protease covalent capture, and we validate it before applying it. Screening 1,012 South African Natural Compounds Database entries against falcipain-2 and falcipain-3, a warhead/β-accessibility cascade retained 185 compounds, and a consensus of recognition docking, uniform-mode covalent docking, MM-GBSA, DFT reactivity descriptors, and predicted developability prioritized SANC00867. A retrospective benchmark (256 falcipain-2 actives, 5,016 propertymatched decoys) shows recognition docking alone does not enrich covalent falcipain-2 actives (ROC-AUC 0.53), and that the covalent signal is carried by warhead reactivity, not recognition: adding warhead reactivity significantly improves retrieval over docking on both propertymatched and stringent warhead-matched decoy benchmarks (ROC-AUC 0.62 vs 0.56, DeLong p = 0.015 in the stringent test), while docking alone remains near-random throughout; covalent pose recovery is validated against a crystallographic vinyl-sulfone complex, and the dual-target ranking is robust to food-vacuole (pH 5.5) preparation (Spearman ρ = 0.77 and 0.97 for FP-2 and FP-3). Across capped para-substituted cinnamate models, global electrophilicity and the site-local β-carbon Fukui index diverge under strong electron withdrawal (4-NO2 raises global ω yet collapses the β-carbon f+ through LUMO localization), so warhead tuning is governed by local, not global, electrophilicity. A matched host-cathepsin covalent counter-screen shows SANC00867’s apparent selectivity does not survive receptor-normalized analysis, reported as a cross-target scoring result rather than a selectivity claim. The workflow thus delivers a validated, transparent prioritization framework and a chemically interpretable design rule, with all inputs, scripts, and settings deposited for reuse.

papers.title: What an SO(3) orientation flow can and cannot learn in molecular-crystal structure prediction
papers.abstract: Rigid-body factorization is an appealing route to molecular-crystal structure prediction: freezing each molecule’s conformer reduces a crystal to a lattice, a set of fractional centroids on the torus T3, and a per-molecule orientation on SO(3). Whether the orientation field is actually learnable on real molecular crystals has not been examined. We introduce SymMC-Flow, a space-groupconditioned rigid-body flow on lattice×T3×SO(3), used as a diagnostic study on 1,127 crystals from the Cambridge Structural Database. The lattice and centroid flows learn normally, but the absolute per-molecule orientation flow remains at its predict-zero floor. We trace this to a decomposition of the orientation target, Rm = rot(gm) · Rasym, into a space-group-determined relative rotation between symmetry copies and the asymmetric unit’s gauge-arbitrary free orientation, which is not learnable from composition and packing; the relative part is. Re-gauging to cancel the free part lifts held-out non-reference orientation loss by 27% (versus ∼0% for the absolute target) and reconstructs 13.7% (mean over three seeds) of held-out multi-copy packings exactly under StructureMatcher, against 0% for the predict-floor baseline. Conditioning on a discrete space-group coset identity raises the learnable signal to roughly 48% (three-seed mean), showing the residual ceiling is set by the difficulty of inferring the symmetry operation from packing rather than by network capacity. End-to-end joint generation does not yet reconstruct packings exactly, placing this as a characterization rather than a finished generator. The result maps what a rigid-body SO(3) flow can and cannot contribute to molecular-crystal generation, and suggests such generators should condition on crystal symmetry for the relative orientation and sample, rather than regress, the remaining free pose.

papers.title: Coupled-perturbed extended tight-binding for analytic Hessians, infrared and Raman spectra
papers.abstract: We present an analytic response formalism for harmonic vibrational spectroscopy with the extended tight-binding (xTB) family of electronic-structure methods. A fieldspace coupled-perturbed self-consistent-charge treatment delivers molecular polarizabilities and, via the interchange theorem, analytic dipole derivatives (atomic polar tensors). Carrying the same formalism to nuclear perturbations yields closed-form analytic nuclear Hessians, which combine a metric-perturbed coupled-perturbed solve with explicit second-derivative terms built on dedicated integral kernels, and whose response weights carry the occupation and Fermi-level response of a Fermi-smeared reference, so that fractionally occupied and restricted odd-electron systems are treated in the same theory as closed shells. Combining the two first-order response sets in a mixed field–nuclear treatment then gives analytic polarizability derivatives (Raman tensors) without any second-order response solve. The formulation covers the GFN{0/1/2}xTB family, from the non-self-consistent GFN0-xTB to the anisotropic multipole electrostatics and self-consistent dispersion of GFN2-xTB, and is implemented on top of the public interfaces of the tblite library. All properties are validated against finitedifference references at their noise floor, and the response solves add only a small, diagonalization-free overhead to a converged calculation, so all three tensors of the double-harmonic infrared and Raman spectrum become available analytically at tightbinding cost.

papers.title: Extraction Strategies for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS): A Critical Comparative Framework Integrating Sensitivity, Sustainability, and Analytical Trade-offs
papers.abstract: Sample preparation, not instrumental detection, limits PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) quantification to current regulatory thresholds. This review covers 35 PFAS-specific extraction methods, including dispersive solid-phase extraction and solid-phase microextraction (dSPE/SPME, n = 15), liquid-phase microextraction (LPME, n = 7), and magnetic particle-based extraction (MSPE/DSPE, n = 13). We assessed their performance, tested four established green metrics (AGREE, GAPI, Eco-Scale, and AGREEprep) against PFAS workflow demands, examined the role of automation in throughput and contamination control, and compared trade-offs across the three families. MSPE scored highest on reviewer-assigned green metrics (6.6 vs. 5.9 for the other two families), mostly because field separation and sorbent reuse cut solvent and energy use, not because individual methods were better optimized. Only 5 of the 35 methods reported a formal green metric, while the other 30 relied on narrative claims. None of the four major metrics accounts for sorbent synthesis energy, fluorinated internal standard production, or contamination-control infrastructure costs each PFAS method carries. We propose reporting the synthesis energy per extraction cycle as a fix that does not require a new framework. No single method leads to sensitivity, sustainability, scope, matrix tolerance, and throughput simultaneously; these trade-offs are structural. We close with a practical selection framework and case for a PFAS-specific green metric.

papers.title: Reversible Site-Selective Editing of Atomically Precise Au6 Nanoclusters through Controlled Oxidative Addition/Reductive Elimination
papers.abstract: Enacting precise bond formations and dissociations at specific sites is focal to molecular editing of functional materials but remains difficult to achieve on the surfaces of metal nanoparticles. Here, we demonstrate the first site-selective molecular editing of a multidentate ligand-stabilized [Au6(SbP3)2][PF6]2 (Au6) nanocluster (where, SbP3= tris(2-(diphenylphosphino)phenyl)stibine), using iodobenzene dichloride (PhICl2). Treatment of the parent Au6 cluster with PhICl2 leads to selective oxidative chlorination across one Au-Au bond, affording a new [Au6(SbP3)2Cl2][PF6]2 (Au6Cl2) nanocluster. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of Au6Cl2 reveals a rearrangement of the parent Au6 core, with complete detachment of one gold atom from the core. Further, Au6Cl2 crystallizes as a racemic mixture, in contrast to the achiral parent cluster. The electronic structure and optical properties of the Au6Cl2 nanocluster was analyzed experimentally and theoretically, depicting good correlation. The Au6 to Au6Cl2 transformation is readily monitored by UV-visible absorption, NMR spectroscopy, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS). Remarkably, treatment of Au6Cl2 with sodium borohydride (NaBH4) regenerates the original Au6 cluster, establishing a reversible cluster transformation reaction. Taken together, this work illustrates how commonly used oxidizing and reducing reagents can be used to achieve site-specific, reversible structural editing of metal nanoclusters, providing a general strategy for tailoring their structural, optical, and chiroptical properties.

papers.title: Machine Learning for High-Throughput Reaction Yield Prediction in DNA-Encoded Library Synthesis
papers.abstract: DNA-encoded library (DEL) synthesis relies on efficient DNA-compatible reactions to ensure library fidelity and the reliability of downstream affinity selection. However, most existing reaction yield prediction models were developed for general organic synthesis and typically use full-atom representations of complete reactants and products. In DEL single-cycle synthesis validation, an appropriate model reaction is to focus on the exposed reactive handle, its local chemical environment, the incoming building block (BB), and the reaction type, rather than large constant backgrounds such as the DNA tag, linker, and pre-existing scaffold. Here, we propose a functional-group-centric machine learning framework for DEL single-cycle reaction yield prediction. The model uses only the exposed substrate functional group (FG) and its coarse-grained local environment, the incoming BB, and the reaction type as inputs. Benchmarking on a real-world high-throughput DEL single-cycle validation dataset shows that graph neural network (GNN) models based on this localized representation outperform traditional fingerprint-based baselines, with a graph attention network (GAT) achieving the best overall performance and showing strong robustness on highly imbalanced industrial data. These results indicate that foregrounding the local reaction center is not merely a simplification of molecular representation, but a task-aligned strategy that better reflects the chemistry and decision logic of DEL single-cycle transformations. This lightweight framework is readily compatible with practical DEL workflows and provides valuable supports on reagent quality control (QC), building block selection, high-fidelity library design, and retrospective analysis of anomalous results.

papers.title: Chain Cluster Diffusion and Network Relaxation in Poly(vinyl alcohol) and Borax Solutions
papers.abstract: The physical chemistry of poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) and borax solutions reflects the formation of dynamic covalent borate anion cross-links between chains. Due to the reversible linkages, PVA and borax solutions not only exhibit re-entrant phase behavior, but they also display distinct fast and slow relaxations. While the fast regime corresponds to single chain and small cluster diffusion, the slow regime transitions from large cluster diffusion to reversible network relaxation as the borax concentration increases. Because these relaxation processes are highly sensitive to the solution phase behavior, multiple complementary techniques are needed to paint a comprehensive picture of the system dynamics. In this work, we use a combination of 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance diffusion ordered spectroscopy ( 1 H NMR DOSY), dynamic light scattering, and small amplitude oscillatory shear to study the dynamics of PVA and borax solutions across their reentrant phase transitions. In the clear liquid and phase separated windows, increasing borax concentration causes the average size and breadth of the PVA clusters to increase. In the clear gel window, the chains percolate into a dynamic network that becomes invisible to the 1 H NMR DOSY measurements. Increasing temperature alters the mechanism of the slow relaxation process of the clear gel. Through this multi-modal approach, we find that the characteristic sizes, relaxation times, and activation energies of the fast and slow relaxation regimes span several orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Stereoselective Dearomative [2π+2σ] Cycloadditions of Indoles Enabled by Triplet-State Iminium Ion Reactivity
papers.abstract: We report an organocatalytic enantioselective [2π+2σ] cycloaddition mediated by visible-light for the dearomatization of indoles. The transformation provides rapid access to complex and sp3-rich indoline-based polycycles with excellent levels of diastereo- and enantiocontrol (up to >20:1 d.r. and 96% ee), through the tripletstate reactivity of a chiral iminium ion. Central to the development of this process was the identification of a suitable chiral primary amine organocatalyst, together with the generation and spectroscopic characterization of the corresponding triplet excited state by time-resolved EPR spectroscopy. The methodology displays broad substrate scope (31 examples) across diverse indoles, bicyclobutanes, and exocyclic alkenes, providing efficient access to highly functionalized bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes and valuable spirocyclic indoline architectures.

papers.title: Catalyst-Free, Visible-Light-Driven Hydrogenation and Giese Addition of N-Hydroxyphthalimide Ester–Containing Polymers Using Hantzsch Esters
papers.abstract: To address unfavorable monomer reactivity ratios and catalyst deactivation during olefin copolymerization with polar vinyl monomers, alternative synthesis methods, such as the postfunctionalization of N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) ester–containing polymers, have attracted significant attention. Although conventional hydrogenation methods have successfully yielded olefin copolymers, they are limited due to their reliance on toxic, unstable reagents and significant scale-up challenges. Thus, we explored the visible-light-driven reaction of electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes between NHPI esters and safe, inexpensive Hantzsch esters. In this study, we established a catalyst-free, visible-light-driven hydrogenation strategy for NHPI estercontaining polymers via EDA-complex-mediated decarboxylation of side-chain groups. This methodology enabled the synthesis of diverse olefin copolymers, including acrylates, polyacrylonitrile, and polystyrene, and advanced gram-scale reactions under natural sunlight. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the undesired polymer crosslinking commonly observed in acrylonitrile copolymer reactions could be effectively suppressed by adjusting the light intensity. This strategy was applied to Giese addition, achieving a high degree of functionalization of up to 79%. Overall, this strategy represents a milestone toward green, sustainable polymer synthesis.

papers.title: TAME: Element-wise Mixture-of-Experts Fusion for Data-Efficient and Interpretable Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Property prediction for molecules and materials is bottlenecked by label scarcity, and in this regime the operative failure mode is not a low mean but an unpredictable tail: individual training runs collapse. The three dominant molecular representations fail in complementary ways—physicochemical descriptors are exact but fixed, graph neural networks learn topology but degenerate under sparse supervision, and language models supply semantic context but cannot compute exact quantities—yet combining them is itself the learning problem, because modality-level scalar gating commits the whole model to one trust weight per source. We introduce TAME, a tri-modal encoder whose element-wise Mixture-of-Experts router assigns an independent modality mixture to every hidden coordinate, stabilized by a balance–entropy regularizer, a closed-form gate initialization (β = log τ) that removes router burn-in, and two-stage self-supervised graph pretraining. On scaffold-split BACE (≈ 1.5k molecules, 100 seeds), the fusion stage improves level and spread together: median ROC-AUC rises from 0.752 to 0.817 and macro-F1 from 0.634 to 0.703, while seed-to-seed variance falls five-fold and a collapse tail reaching ROC-AUC ≈ 0.45 disappears. Because backbone, checkpoint, split, seeds and optimizer recipe are held fixed, the effect is attributable to the fusion stage alone. The router allocates a distinct mixture to each coordinate, which no scalar gate can represent, and the entropy weight moves that allocation continuously between graded mixing and a near-binary regime in which each coordinate is claimed outright by one modality. Gate mass additionally tracks encoder quality without supervision, shifting from text to topology once pretraining lifts the graph embedding out of rank-1 collapse.
