The same three experts map onto crystal graphs, composition–structure descriptors and literature-mined text, making TAME a transferable template for multimodal representation learning in materials discovery.

papers.title: Harnessing Thiol-Tetrazine Bond Exchange for Engineering Dynamic Covalent Hydrogels for Cell Culture
papers.abstract: Dynamic covalent chemistry (DCvC) provides a versatile toolbox of reactions forming reversible covalent bonds that are strong yet dynamic. Implementing DCvC in hydrogel networks to engineer extracellular matrix (ECM) mimics improves their resemblance to natural tissues, by conferring dynamicity and time-dependent viscoelastic properties. In this work, the nucleophilic aromatic substitution of tetrazines with thiols (thiol-Tz) is proposed as a DCvC strategy to synthesize tunable, dynamic hydrogels under close-to-physiological conditions, which find value as scaffolds for cell encapsulation. The network design consists of a linear poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) macromer end-functionalized with chloro-tetrazine groups (easily synthesized in good yield via a one-step reaction) and a commercially available multiarm PEG precursor terminated with thiols. Derived PEG thiol-Tz hydrogels form rapidly by mixing the two polymeric precursors under physiological conditions (in buffer, pH 7-8, room temperature). NMR spectroscopy analysis provides insight into the thiol-Tz coupling reaction and the subsequent thiol-Tz bond exchange. These results are correlated with macroscopic rheological characterization of derived thiol-Tz hydrogels to elucidate how such dynamic exchange impacts materials properties, including gelation kinetics, mechanical strength, stress relaxation and self-recovery. Thiol-Tz dynamic hydrogels demonstrate good cytocompatibility for encapsulation of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs). These proof-of-concept findings showcase the potential of thiol-Tz DCvC as a novel strategy to manufacture mechanically tunable hydrogels for cell and bioengineering applications.

papers.title: An unlearnable target: diagnosing the orientation gauge in PXRD-conditioned molecular-crystal flow matching
papers.abstract: Rigid-body flow matching reduces a molecular crystal to a lattice, fractional cen-troids and per-molecule orientations on SO(3), and is an attractive route to structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD). We report a negative result and its root cause. Our PXRD-conditioned rigid-body flow recovered 0 of 160 held-out structures, and the failure was neither the lattice nor the sampler: a frame-preserving oracle substitution shows that installing the ground-truth unit cell into the generated packing yields 0/10 matches, while a component decomposition on held-out data puts the lattice head at 91.6% of variance explained and both packing heads at their no-information floors (centroid −0.1%, orientation 3.7%). The orientation loss sat at ∼4.7 against an analytic predict-nothing floor of π2/3+2 = 5.290, because the training target was the absolute molecular pose, which factorises as

papers.title: Irradiation wavelength tuned stepwise [2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives as a platform for light-mechanical energy conversion
papers.abstract: Cyclobutane motifs are widely embedded in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition is a facile method to synthesize four-membered rings. In general, controlling the regioselectivity and stereoselectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. Nevertheless, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules in topo-photochemical reaction can place the atoms in the products at specific positions. In this work, the irradiation wavelength-controlled, stepwise photo-induced [2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives took place in crystals. Under blue light, one kind of monocyclobutane was yielded via the cycloaddition of vinyls, accompanied with single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation. The monocyclobutane product can be converted into bicyclobutane product by the second-step cycloaddition of carbon-carbon double bonds on five-membered heterocyclic ring in indole upon irradiation with 365 nm light. Such catalyst-free dearomatization of indole via [2+2] cycloaddition has not been reported previously. Driven by [2+2] cycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibited obvious photomechanical effects.

papers.title: Force-Dependent Fracture of Dynamic Polymer Networks: Sacrificial Bond Rupture and Dispersion-Induced Physical Crosslinking
papers.abstract: We use coarse-grained molecular dynamics to investigate tensile fracture in dynamically crosslinked polymer networks, where both weak-linker and strong backbone bonds rupture according to Bell-model force-dependent probabilities. Competition between these pathways determines whether preferential weak-linker rupture relieves local stress, redistributes load, and protects the backbone. Lower linker activation energy or stretching stiffness promotes this sacrificial pathway, suppressing backbone rupture and delaying failure. Linker regeneration preserves connectivity but reloads the backbone, weakening sacrificial protection and reducing extensibility. Dispersion interactions between linker beads induce aggregation and physical crosslinking; moderate attraction reinforces the network, whereas stronger attraction suppresses weak-linker rupture, redirects load to the backbone, and causes embrittlement. Varying dynamic crosslinker content further tunes the balance between sacrificial weak-linker rupture and dispersion-induced reinforcement, with an intermediate content providing a favorable combination of stiffness, strength, and extensibility. These results identify force-dependent competition between weak and strong bonds as a unifying mechanism for polymer-network design.

papers.title: Finite-temperature dynamic stability separates foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials that harmonic benchmarks rank equally
papers.abstract: Foundation (universal) machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are now used routinely as cheap stand-ins for DFT in high-throughput stability screening, but they are benchmarked almost exclusively against harmonic (0 K) phonons. Dynamic stability is physically a finite-temperature property, and an important class of materials, including cubic perovskites, bcc refractory metals and cubic fluorites, is harmonically unstable but thermally stabilised by anharmonicity. We test five foundation MLIPs (MACE-MP-0, CHGNet, ORB-v2, SevenNet-0, MatterSim) on this regime using a curated set of references whose finite-temperature behaviour is documented in the experimental and DFT literature, so that no new DFT ground truth is required. We introduce a cheap quantum selfconsistent-harmonic (SCHA) “soft-mode free energy” screen that evaluates every imaginary commensurate mode and calls the high-symmetry phase unstable if any of them condenses, and we cross-validate it against the gold-standard multi-mode stochastic SCHA (SSCHA). We report three findings together with a practical ensemble-disagreement guardrail. (i) At the harmonic level the models divide: MatterSim and SevenNet-0 reproduce every documented soft mode (accuracy 1.00), whereas MACE-MP-0 and CHGNet soften the bcc Zr/Hf instabilities to zero (15% false-stable rate) and ORB-v2 misses the SrTiO3 soft mode (8%). (ii) Harmonic accuracy does not predict finitetemperature accuracy in either direction: CHGNet is the worst model harmonically yet the second best at finite temperature, while MatterSim is harmonically perfect and only midtable, and on the matched set the two are non-significantly concordant at 100 K and significantly anti-associated at 300 K. Screening every imaginary mode rather than the softest one is essential, because the deepest mode need not be the one that condenses: in SrTiO3 the Γ ferroelectric mode is deeper than the R-point tilt yet is quantum-suppressed, and only the tilt drives the 105 K transition. (iii) Multi-mode SSCHA with an MLIP force engine is a clean gold standard for the martensitic bcc metals, but in its default deployment, with the free-energy Hessian truncated at the bubble, it systematically falsestabilises deep displacive (ferroelectric) instabilities and can diverge numerically. Theory predicts this truncation to fail for cubic metal halide perovskites; we measure the failure at benchmark scale and show it extends to oxide perovskites and, free of stochastic blowups, to cubic fluorites. The cheap soft-mode screen is therefore the more reliable finitetemperature indicator for the displacive instabilities that dominate generative crystalstructure-prediction (CSP) screening.

papers.title: Ethanol-Oriented CO2 Hydrogenation for Alcoholto-Jet Sustainable Aviation Fuels: Catalyst Design and Fixed-Bed Performance Benchmarking
papers.abstract: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is expected to play a central role in aviation decarbonization because long-range flights will continue to depend on energy-dense, infrastructure-compatible liquid fuels. Among available SAF pathways, alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) routes connect oxygenated intermediates with established upgrading technologies for jet-range hydrocarbons. In this context, alcohol-oriented thermocatalytic CO 2 hydrogenation could provide an upstream platform for SAF production when coupled with low-carbon H 2 . However, catalytic studies have largely been evaluated using reaction-centered metrics, while the downstream implications of alcohol identity have received less critical attention. This Review positions ethanol synthesis within the broader landscape of methanol and higher alcohol synthesis and examines how alcohol identity affects carbon-chain construction, deoxygenation and hydrogen requirements, separation burden, and pathway compatibility. Ethanol is adopted as the central reference intermediate because it balances upstream synthetic accessibility with downstream ATJ relevance. To establish a data-centered benchmark, ethanol-forming catalyst performance reported over the past two decades under continuous-flow fixed-bed conditions is critically compiled and normalized. Where the source data permit, EtOH selectivity is recalculated on a common total-carbon basis and catalyst-mass-normalized EtOH space-time yield (STY) is derived using a consistent definition. Comparison of noble-metal, Co-based, Cu-based, and Fe/Zn/alkali multielement and tandem catalysts reveals a common design logic in which multifunctional site ensembles, engineered interfaces, and promoter/support effects define the ethanol-forming window. By linking fixed-bed catalytic evidence with downstream ATJ requirements, this Review provides a framework for evaluating CO 2 -to-ethanol catalysts as components of SAF-oriented alcohol platforms.

papers.title: GeoDSSOP: Geometry-aware prediction of protein backbone order parameters from sequence and structure
papers.abstract: Backbone amide order parameters (S2) describe protein motions on the picosecond-to-nanosecond time scale at residue resolution. However, NMR measurement and calculation from atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories are time-consuming. We developed GeoDSSOP (Geometry-aware Deep Sequence–Structure Order-Parameter Predictor) to predict backbone N–H S2 from one amino-acid sequence and one corresponding structure. GeoDSSOP combines frozen ESM-2 residue embeddings with a geometric vector perceptron-style encoder of a residue graph. A gated residual module fuses the sequence and structure representations, and a dilated temporal convolutional network gives a bounded prediction for each residue. We trained these models on 3,490 proteins with MD-iRED labels or S-OPPE pseudo-labels. The two label sources were weighted equally, and homologous proteins were kept in the same data partition. The model gave a protein-macro PCC of 0.8250 on a protected and homology-separated test set of 136 MD-labelled proteins, and 0.8424 on a historical experimental NMR benchmark of ten proteins that was not used to train OPPE, S-OPPE, or GeoDSSOP. In a matched three-run ablation, adding the structure pathway increased the mean protein-macro PCC on MD-iRED validation from 0.7220 to 0.8026. This result shows that one protein structure provides useful information beyond the sequence pathway. Label-source ablations also showed domain-specific performance and asymmetric transfer. Balanced dual-source training gave the best overall performance on the mixed-domain development set. GeoDSSOP can rapidly produce residue-level fast-dynamics profiles from a sequence and one available structure. It does not require a new MD simulation or a multi-conformer structure ensemble, but it remains a statistical predictor and does not replace experiment or trajectory-based analysis.

papers.title: Fast Fourier Transform-Based Approach to Denoise and Enhance GC×GC-TOFMS Data
papers.abstract: Comprehensive two-dimensional (2D) gas chromatography mass spectrometry (GC×GC-MS) provides improved separation quality in comparison to one-dimensional (1D) GC-MS; however, it presents with undesirable noise akin to that of 1D, including background chemical, thermal, and electrical noise. In GC×GC-MS, the narrow peak widths necessitate the use of a fast detector, often a time-of-flight mass spectrometer (TOFMS), acquiring more than 50 spectra per second (Hz). These high detector speeds increase electrical noise. Using a Fast-Fourier Transform (FFT), it is possible to analyze GC×GC-TOFMS data in the frequency domain, which has not yet been explored and addressed in literature. In doing so, we identified intense bands in the frequency domain of both GC-MS and GC×GC-TOFMS data corresponding to common alternating current (AC) frequencies resulting from electrical components in MS detectors operating at sufficiently high acquisition rates. In GC×GC-TOFMS data, we discovered that the periodic resampling of peaks introduces equispaced bands into the frequency domain that are separated by the frequency of the modulation period. To improve data quality, we developed an algorithm operating in the frequency domain to filter unwanted noise while simultaneously preserving and enhancing chemical features. The algorithm uses Butterworth filtering to notch out AC-associated frequencies, reducing the standard deviation of the baseline noise of the total ion chromatogram (TIC) in both GC-TOFMS and GC×GC-TOFMS by 30-50%. Further, all frequencies above a specified threshold can be removed using a Butterworth lowpass filter, providing additional denoising of frequencies unassociated with chemical features. An exponential fit can also be applied to GC×GC-TOFMS data in the frequency domain, intensifying the low, chemical-associated frequencies and damping higher ones. The latter significantly reduced noise in the time domain and decreased baseline standard deviation by over 25%, albeit at the cost of slightly broadened peaks, thus decreasing resolution. Applying all enhancement methods in superposition recovers peaks along the first-dimension baseline of GC×GC-TOFMS data that were previously obscured by noise. The application of this algorithm allows for the denoising of chromatographic data while preserving and optimizing chemical features.

papers.title: Electronic configuration vectors provide transferable elemental representations for machine learning across the periodic table
papers.abstract: Machine learning models typically represent elements as discrete identities, limiting inference for elements absent from training. We introduce the electronic configuration vector (ECV), a physically grounded representation derived from the Aufbau principle that continuously encodes orbital occupancies and energetics across elements. Principal component analysis reveals low-dimensional manifolds that organize elements by atomic number, with extrema corresponding to block transitions. Across adsorption energy, formation energy, and metallicity prediction, ECV yields accurate, lightweight, interpretable models while revealing chemical structure. ECV marginally outperforms the Darwin LLM in metallicity classification on the Matbench benchmark (ROC-AUC 0.9614 vs. 0.9598), despite far lower complexity. It also generalizes to unseen elements, achieving 0.16 eV MAE for perovskite formation energies, compared with 0.39 eV for one-hot encoding and 0.18 eV for elemental property vectors. Unlike one-hot encoding, ECV does not impose elemental orthogonality and, unlike property vectors, is definable for every element. These results establish ECV as a coordinate system for transferable machine learning across the periodic table.

papers.title: Ag13Cu4 Nanocluster-Catalyzed Ambient C-F Bond Activation
papers.abstract: Atomically precise nanoclusters (NC) with discrete electronic states and high surface-to-atom ratios offer unique controllable active sites leading to unique catalytic transformations. Here we demonstrate that an ultrasmall (<3 nm), atomically precise Ag-Cu alloy NC, [Ag13Cu4(o1-CBT)12]3- (o1-CBT = ortho-1-carboranethiol) (Ag13Cu4), leverages these features to accomplish the extremely difficult activation and cleavage of inert C-F bond under ambient conditions. With copper atoms positioned at peripheral sites, Ag13Cu4 catalyzes room-temperature C-N cross-coupling between aryl fluorides and the pharmacologically relevant thioguanine (TG) under aerobic conditions, delivering arylated TG derivatives under operationally simple conditions. Computations revealed the evolution of atomic arrangements, superatom-delocalized electronic states of the bimetallic NC, frontier orbitals of gap-localized Cu and reactants, activation mechanism and a barrier-crossing pathway of the catalyzed reaction, culminating with the uncovering of a concerted SNAr mechanism of the reaction enabling C-F bond-activation and cleavage of benzene fluoride with a cross-coupling transformation forming a C-N bond between the phenyl group and TG molecule. This first demonstration of ambient C-F bond dissociation by an atomically precise cluster highlights a molecular materials-driven frontier in catalysis, opening futuristic pathways for synthesizing fluorinated pharmaceuticals and remediation of fluorinated environmental contaminants.

papers.title: Simulating Chemical Reaction Dynamics Using Sample Based Quantum Diagonalization: A Quantum-Centric Supercomputing Approach
authors: Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala
papers.abstract: Quantum computers offer the potential to simulate chemical systems beyond the capabilities of classical computers. However, current quantum-computing approaches to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and vibrational analysis largely rely on the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), whose circuit depth, iterative optimization, and measurement overhead hinder the practical simulation of molecular systems. Here, we extend Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD), a quantum-sampling-based electronic-structure method, to AIMD and vibrational analysis on noisy quantum hardware. The resulting framework enables nuclear forces and Hessians to be derived from quantum-computed electronic energies, facilitating molecular dynamics and characterization of potential-energy surfaces. We demonstrate the approach using diverse molecular processes, including H2 bond vibration, the proton exchange reaction (H+ + H2), the bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction (Cl− + CH3Cl), and protontransfer dynamics between two water molecules involving transient formation of the Zundel cation (H2O· · ·H+ · · ·OH2). Across these systems, SQD-AIMD trajectories and vibrational frequencies obtained with noisy quantum hardware show excellent agreement with classical reference calculations and substantially improved accuracy relative to previously reported VQE-based simulations. Importantly, the SQD-based approach eliminates costly variational optimization and significantly reduces measurement requirements relative to VQE, enabling AIMD simulations spanning approximately 500 timesteps (∼200 fs), substantially longer than previously reported AIMD simulations on quantum hardware. These results establish SQD-AIMD and SQD-vibrational analysis as practical and scalable frameworks for simulating chemical reaction dynamics and elucidating reaction mechanisms on near-term quantum hardware, extending quantum computing applications beyond static electronic structure calculations.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of LLM-based zero-shot model construction in chemistry and materials science: predictive performance and response reliability
papers.abstract: Purely data-driven materials exploration is often constrained by limited experimental data, motivating exploration strategies that leverage prior knowledge of the target material system encoded in large language models (LLMs). This paper describes an approach that combines LLM-derived pairwise comparisons with preference learning to construct utility-function models that rank experimental conditions with respect to a target property, without directly using measured target-property values for the system of interest either during LLM inference or model fitting. Across nine chemistry and materials science datasets and six LLMs from two providers, we evaluated predictive performance in terms of pairwise-comparison accuracy and rank agreement, and response reliability in terms of position bias, preference consistency, and abstention behavior. Predictive performance depended more strongly on the dataset than on the choice of LLM, and preference learning generally reproduced target-property rankings more accurately than direct property prediction by LLMs. Position bias and preference consistency varied across dataset–LLM combinations. Among 11 abstention configurations, the ensemble performed best overall across the risk–coverage metrics, with consistency-based and LLM-judge-based configurations also performing relatively well. Our systematic examination has characterized the predictive performance of LLM-based zero-shot modeling and the reliability of the underlying LLM output, providing insights into the potential and challenges of this approach.

papers.title: Transport Cross Sections and Collisional Energy Relaxation of Superthermal O(3P) Atoms in N2 for Planetary Aeronomy
papers.abstract: Superthermal (“hot”) oxygen atoms deposit their energy in planetary upper atmospheres and in hypersonic shock layers through collisions with N2, but the rate at which they do so is set not by the magnitude of the collision cross section, which is dominated by forward diffraction, but by transport-weighted moments of the differential cross section (DCS). We derive momentum-transfer and viscosity cross sections, mean collisional deflections, and energy-relaxation rates for O(3P) + N2 from our previously reported quantum coupled-channel DCSs, for 16O, 17O, and 18O over collision energies 0.31−4.0 eV. The momentum-transfer cross section is well represented by σm = 9.90 × 10−16 Ek−0.385 cm2 (Ek in eV), a factor of 28−32 below the collision cross section, with mean deflection ⟨1 − cos θ⟩ = 0.031−0.036. Rotationally inelastic channels supply 72−88% of it, so transport treatments built on elastic angular distributions underestimate the stopping power of N2 several-fold. The heavy-isotope enhancement of the integral elastic cross section (1−5%) does not survive transport weighting. σm is isotope-independent to within 0.4% above 0.6 eV, because the enhancement resides in the transport-inert forward cone, so isotopic effects in thermalization are kinematic (+2.9% recoil per collision for 18O relative to 16O). The mean energy loss per collision rises from 10 to 68 meV, and Monte Carlo slowing down gives ≈120 collisions and a stopping column of 3.7 × 1015 cm−2 to thermalize a nascent 3.48 eV atom in pure N2, some twenty times the isotropic hard-sphere estimate. A loss law that satisfies detailed balance in a 460 K bath raises the number of collisions by 6.5%. Comparing the isotopes at equal velocity instead of equal energy shifts σm by 1.5−2.8%, and this shift is purely kinematic.

papers.title: IQARIS: An Atlas of Interacting Quantum Atoms across Chemical Space
papers.abstract: Chemical machine learning has achieved remarkable predictive performance by leveraging increasingly large quantum-chemical datasets. Yet, the local quantum information underlying molecular behavior remains largely unexplored at scale, limiting the development of models that explain predictions through physically meaningful real-space quantities. In previous work (Nat. Commun. 2024, 15, 4345), we introduced one of the first explainable chemical artificial intelligence (XCAI) models capable of predicting rigorously defined real-space quantum descriptors directly from molecular structure. Extending this approach across chemical space requires comprehensive reference data that have so far been unavailable. Here, we introduce IQARIS, the Interacting Quantum Atoms Reference Information Set, a real-space quantum atlas of CHONSFPCl chemical space built around the atomic, interatomic, and topological building blocks of molecules. IQARIS comprises 268,639 curated neutral closed-shell singlet structures spanning 178,257 unique molecular connectivities and nearly five million atoms, with system sizes ranging from 2 to 266 atoms. Bottom-up enumeration, top-down sampling, and valence-preserving atom replacement provide broad coverage of sulfur-, phosphorus-, fluorine-, and chlorine-rich chemistry. Each structure includes QTAIM analyses of the electron-density topology at the M06-2X and PBE0 levels with the def2-TZVP basis set, a complete IQA energy decomposition at the PBE0 level, and IQA decompositions from five semiempirical Hamiltonians, yielding 182 molecular, atomic, interatomic, and critical-point descriptors. IQARIS provides a consistent real-space quantum reference for developing interpretable and transferable models of local quantum properties. Its DFT, IQA, and semiempirical descriptions of identical structures additionally enable multi-fidelity learning strategies, opening new avenues for XCAI models that learn chemistry directly from real-space quantum building blocks.

papers.title: Understanding Composition-Dependent Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability of (101)-Oriented RuxTi1-xO2
papers.abstract: Rutile RuO 2 is a highly active catalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) but hindered by its high rates of dissolution under reaction conditions. Substitution with elements forming more stable oxides, such as Ti, is an appealing strategy to increase stability. In such solid solutions, the intrinsic activity (and stability) of a given active site is expected to depend on its local environment and the identity of neighboring metal centers. We considered (101)-oriented Ru x Ti 1-x O 2 epitaxial thin films, which enable quantitative consideration of the number and composition of surface coordinatively undersaturated active sites. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed a slight decrease in oxygen binding strength at Ru sites with Ti incorporation, and notable stabilization of oxygen at Ti sites due to charge transfer from Ru. The intrinsic OER activity per Ru site was comparable to that of pure RuO 2 at an intermediate Ru composition (x Ru =0.78), while the stability was significantly higher for all extents of Ti incorporation investigated here. Moderate amounts of Ti doping exhibited reduced Ru dissolution over time, whereas substantial Ti incorporation (x Ru =0.39) lost most surface Ru sites to dissolution with minimal changes to OER activity, supporting calculations that indicate subsurface Ru activates surface Ti sites. Together these findings highlight that the OER activity and stability of Ru sites is dependent on the number of neighboring Ti atoms, but also that Ti sites can contribute appreciably to OER activity depending on their local environment. This work demonstrates that rational design of Ru-Ti coordination is key for durable and active Ru-based oxide catalysts for acidic water electrolysis.

papers.title: Biobased Pressure-Sensitive Adhesives from Tulipalin A and Lauryl Methacrylate Synthesized via PhotoATRP
The origin of red luminescence in o-phenylenediamine-based carbon dots
papers.abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) prepared from o -phenylenediamine (oPD) have attracted significant research interest, because they can exhibit blue, green, or red fluorescence depending on synthetic conditions and dopants. The red- and NIR-emitting oPD-based CDs are of particular interest because of their potential for bioimaging and biomedical applications. Efforts to understand the relationship between their structure and optical properties have led to the proposal of various hypotheses of the red luminescence, which are however difficult to support due to limited knowledge of their precise structural arrangement. Although in some oPD-based CDs, a molecular fluorophore 5,14-dihydroquinoxalino[2,3- b ]phenazine (DHQP) has been identified as a source contributing to the red emission of CDs, the complex synthesis-dependent photophysical properties of oPD-based systems seemingly pointed to more complicated mechanisms. However, here we show that the complex behavior of oPD-based CDs can be in fact almost universally explained solely by the formation of DHQP. Based on the comprehensive data analysis of more than 80 oPD-based red-emissive systems in works published during the past 10 years and a systematic investigation of DHQP emission under various conditions, we demonstrate that the optical properties of more than 95% of such systems can be rationalized by the presence of different protonation forms of DHQP and their solvatochromic behavior.

papers.title: Fluorine-Enabled Photochemical Generation of Carbonyl Ylide 1,3-Dipoles
papers.abstract: The photochemistry of carbonyl compounds underpins a wide range of modern synthetic transformations. However, photoinduced rearrangements, despite their unique potential for skeletal reorganization, remain conspicuously underexplored. Here, we show that fluorine can be used as a design principle to divert these reactions from established photochemical pathways. Mechanistic investigations combining experimental, spectroscopic and computational approaches support an unusual singlet excited state pathway involving initial cyclization followed by skeletal rearrangement. This sequence enables the formation of carbonyl ylide 1,3-dipoles, while exhibiting a pronounced increase in polarization along the reaction path. The high efficiency and selectivity of the process provide an attractive platform for isomerization and photoclick chemistry, while its compatibility with water and oxygen broadens the potential for bioorthogonal applications.

papers.title: New-to-Nature Transformation for the Z-Selective Synthesis of Unsaturated Acids via Acyl Azolium Intermediates
papers.abstract: Organocatalytic methods operating via α,β-unsaturated acyl azolium intermediates are extensively studied in organic chemistry and typically proceed through E-configured intermediates that dictate the stereochemical outcome of the final product. To date, the use of this species within enzymatic systems is restricted to a single natural biosynthetic pathway. Herein, we report an example of a versatile new-to-nature biocatalytic transformation that harnesses an α,β-unsaturated acyl azolium intermediate within the active site of a thiaminedependent enzyme. Remarkably, this enzymatic environment favors the formation of the less accessible Z-acyl azolium, enabling the highly selective synthesis of Z-α,β-unsaturated acids via redox hydrolysis of α-bromoenals. The protocol features a broad substrate scope spanning aromatic and aliphatic substrates, all while maintaining excellent Z/E ratios.

papers.title: Uncovering a Hydrogen-Bond-Enabled Pathway to Dinitrosyl Iron Complexes
papers.abstract: Dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) are prevalent NO-derived iron species; yet the factors that govern their formation at non-heme iron centers remain poorly understood. Here, we show that secondary-sphere hydrogen bonding interaction, together with steric accessibility of the Fe center enables quantitative formation of a {Fe(NO)2}9 (1-DNIC) complex through a previously unrecognized NO-driven redox pathway. Reaction of [Fe(DIG2dien)]2+ (DIG2dien = N-methyl-bis[2-(N,N′-diisopropylguanidino)ethyl]amine) with NO gas affords [Fe(DIG2dien)(NO)2]+ (1-DNIC) as the sole detectable iron-containing product. Spectroscopic and computational characterization by Mössbauer, EPR, SQUID, IR, X-ray absorption spectroscopy and DFT calculation establish an S = 1/2 ground state and a hydrogen-bond-supported {Fe(NO)2}9 unit. Mechanistic studies support a self-sustaining pathway in which NO functions as both a nitrosylating agent and a reductant, thereby circumventing the stoichiometric constraints of the previously reported disproportionation mechanisms. Notably, the sterically hindered analogue [Fe(DIG3tren)]2+ (2, DIG3tren = tris(N’,N”-diisopropylguanidinyl-2-ethyl)amine) reacts with NO gas to form the linear, hydrogen-bonded {FeNO}7 complex [Fe(DIG3tren)(NO)]2+ (2-NO) rather than a DNIC. Furthermore, 1-DNIC transfers NO to the ferrous precursor 2, generating 2-NO with concomitant formation of trace N2O. These findings establish secondary-sphere hydrogen bonding as a key determinant of DNIC assembly and reveal a hydrogen-bond-mediated, NO-driven mechanism for quantitative DNIC formation at a non-heme iron center.

papers.title: Protein and Water Dielectric Response in Confinement
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations are employed to compare the dynamics of the protein in solution, powder and in confinement between two planar slabs mimicking uncharged gold electrodes. The question addressed here is how powder and solution confinement alter the internal dynamics of the protein. We observe a major slowing down of both protein rotations and of internal shape fluctuations both in powders and in water confinement. Changes in protein dynamics are reported in terms of static and dynamic correlation function of the protein and hydration water relevant to measurements done with dielectric spectroscopy. The static dipolar susceptibilities of the protein in confinement become highly anisotropic, caused by anisotropy of the protein-water cross correlations. Anisotropy of protein’s dipolar response, already present in solution, is enhanced in confinement by anisotropy of water’s response.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by the authors because a contributor should not have been listed. An updated version is available at 10.26434/chemrxiv.15007883/v3

papers.title: Predicting CYP450 Induction and PXR Activation with Machine Learning Approaches: Challenges and Opportunities
papers.abstract: Many drugs increase the activity of cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes, an effect known as induction, which is a major cause of harmful drug-drug interactions (DDIs). Predicting induction from chemical structure would help identify DDI risks early in compound development. Yet, unlike many other drug properties, CYP450 induction is rarely modeled, because the data needed to train models is scarce and expensive to produce. Using an industry-scale dataset covering induction of three CYP450 enzymes (CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP1A2) and PXR activation, we benchmark four machine learning models across six molecular representations and compare performance against models trained on a curated public dataset. On the internal data, the best models separated inducers from non-inducers moderately well (MCC 0.35-0.46) but could not predict the magnitude of induction. Almost no model or representation performed significantly better than the others, pointing to the data rather than the method as the limiting factor. The same pattern was observed for public data, where a large public PXR set reached this range, while a small, heterogeneous public CYP3A4 set failed where the data is scarcer and noisier. We then show that the shared biology of these endpoints carries a usable signal. A model trained on one endpoint partly predicted the others, and this transfer followed the known regulatory relationships between PXR and the CYP450 enzymes. Hence, these biological links can serve as useful inductive biases for future models. Finally, we found that the models we trained are already reasonably well calibrated, which, combined with their classification performance, makes them useful for prioritizing compounds that are within the applicability domain of the models.

papers.title: Optimization of pyrazolopyridine derivatives for the treatment of human African trypanosomiasis
papers.abstract: Despite recent advances in the development of therapeutics for human African trypanosomiasis, new treatments are needed to populate the drug pipeline in case of failure and resistance. A previously reported high throughput screen of human kinase inhibitors identified the pyrazolopyridine scaffold as an inhibitor of Trypanosoma brucei ( T.b .), which was subsequently optimized for antiparasitic activity. We report the structure-activity relationships (SAR) of the series, focused on improving antitrypanosomal activity and ADME properties, while using structure-based drug design (SBDD) to introduce parasite selectivity. Through these efforts, we identified analogs up to 11-fold more potent than the initial hits, and with up to 40-fold improvement in aqueous solubility. Selectivity for T. brucei over human kinases remains an area for improvement.

papers.title: Zinc Redox Catalysis in the Photochemical Borylation of Fluorocarbons
papers.abstract: Zinc compounds are ubiquitous in synthesis and materials. They find applications as reagents, catalysts, porous materials and as metalloenzymes — all of which rely on the properties of redox stable and electrophilic zinc(II) centres. In this paper we report the first clear example of redox catalysis involving reversible changes between zinc(I) and zinc(II) oxidation states. Under photochemical conditions a zinc(I) compound was shown to react with fluoroarenes. Turnover was achieved through addition of a diborane reagent, resulting in a catalytic borylation of the C(sp2)–F bonds of fluoroarenes. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a key role of a zinc(II) boryl intermediate in the reductive step from zinc(II) to zinc(I). These findings were further exploited in a small array of photocatalytic approaches to the borylation and reductive coupling of C(sp3)–F, C(sp2)–O and C(sp3)–O bonds.

papers.title: A Generalized Theory for the Structural and Spatial Mapping of Energy, Entropy, and Free Energy
papers.abstract: Systems in which the free energy density is nonuniform in space are familiar; the surface tension of a water droplet and the surface energy of a solid are good examples. Some such cases can be treated with prior theory, notably inhomogeneous solvation theory (IST), but IST is applicable only to liquids. Despite this limitation, IST has proven useful as a guide to the design of ligands to bind a targeted protein, based on the idea that ligands which displace high free energy water will tend to bind more tightly, other things being equal. Here, we present Generalized Thermodynamic Mapping (GTM) theory, a more general theory that is applicable to the entirety of a biomolecular or other chemical system, and which thus may provide additional guidance for molecular design. For example, it might highlight parts of a ligand whose local free energy rises on binding, thus suggesting where modifications could improve affinity. Starting from classical statistical thermodynamics, we derive structural decompositions that assign energy and entropy to individual atoms or to larger chemical components, such as amino acid residues, and spatial decompositions that define continuously varying thermodynamic densities throughout the system. The potential energy is decomposed via the multibody expansion, and the entropy via the mutual information expansion. The resulting thermodynamic densities satisfy key desiderata: their spatial integrals yield the correct total thermodynamic quantities, the densities vanish where the atomic number density is zero, and all entropy terms above first order go to zero in the absence of correlation. The entropy decomposition in GTM theory is closely related to that of IST, but it is simpler, largely because it expresses the entropy in terms of normalized probability density functions instead of non-normalized correlation functions. We show that, while GTM theory is formally exact for any number of particles, $N$, IST is not. The unified framework presented here enables thermodynamic mapping of solute and solvent alike and is expected to support a range of applications, including in structure-based drug design, protein design, the analysis of allostery, and materials science. The use of GTM theory to gain insight into protein-ligand binding is illustrated here with an initial case study.

papers.title: Emzing: A deep learning-enabled software suite for end-to-end analysis of high-resolution LC-MS metabolomics data
papers.abstract: High-resolution LC–MS metabolomics requires transforming noise-dominated raw data into quantitative feature tables and, ultimately, biologically meaningful insights. In practice, this process is fragmented across multiple tools and involves extensive parameter tuning and manual curation. Emzing is a web-based, vendor-agnostic platform that integrates end-to-end analysis, from raw data interrogation to statistical interpretation, within a unified environment. Emzing introduces data-driven, deep learning–based methods for signal extraction and feature quantification, formulating peak detection as a supervised learning problem in both spectral and chromatographic domains. A data-driven noise estimation strategy replaces fixed intensity thresholds, improving sensitivity to low-intensity signals. Feature correspondence across samples is established using robust retention-time alignment and graph-based grouping, while correlation-driven feature tagging assigns isotopes, adducts, and in-source fragments. Metabolite annotation (MSI level 2) combines spectral denoising with composite scoring of MS/MS spectra against reference libraries. Emzing further integrates processing with downstream statistical and machine learning–based analyses to facilitate reliable biological interpretation. Interactive visualization across all stages enables transparent curation and rapid iteration from initial results to publication-quality outputs. The use of pre-trained models in inference mode, together with a reduced parameter space, supports reproducible analysis. Emzing improves true-feature recovery, quantitative accuracy, and reproducibility on benchmark datasets while reducing reliance on manual intervention. Scalability is demonstrated through Emzing Vault, a repository containing over 110 reprocessed public domain datasets.

papers.title: Reconciling visible emission intensity and ON/OFF commutation ratio in photochromic lanthanide complexes of europium(III) and samarium(III).
papers.abstract: Developing highly emissive and photoswitchable lanthanide complexes for advanced anticounterfeiting materials requires overcoming a fundamental photophysical bottleneck: the intrinsic competition between the emission quantum yield (Φ em ) and the isomerization quantum yield (Φ closing ). Traditionally, maximizing photoconversion results in severely quenched, impractical ON-states. Here, we present a counter-intuitive molecular design strategy that deliberately lowers the isomerization quantum yield in favor of increasing the initial lanthanide emission while preserving a high ON-OFF intensity ratio. Using click-chemistry, we synthesized a unique ligand scaffold integrating a dithienylethene (DTE) photochrome with a pyridinebis(oxazoline) (pybox) antenna. Upon coordination, the resulting europium(III) and samarium(III) complexes exhibit a finely tuned moderate isomerization quantum yield (Φ closing = 0.25-0.27). This deliberate moderation preserves a very high emission in the ON-state, reaching a quantum yield of Φ em = 0.22 for the europium(III) complex, alongside a significant Φ em = 0.02 for the rarely investigated samarium(III) analogue. Despite their modest photoconversion, these systems maintain an important ON/OFF contrast with less than 10% residual luminescence at the photostationary state in solution. Finally, incorporating these complexes into PMMA polymer matrices leads to an optical modulation which is easy to detect with the naked eye, even in daylight, thus providing a robust framework for designing practically operative dynamic materials.

papers.title: Graph attention framework for site-selectivity prediction in undirected C(sp3)–H borylation
papers.abstract: C–H borylation has surfaced as a powerful transformation in molecular syntheses, providing direct access to organoboron compounds – highly applicable to pharmaceutical and crop protection industries, as well as materials science. While site-selectivity prediction is established for C(sp 2 )–H borylation, significantly more challenging C(sp 3 )–H borylations remain largely unexplored. In sharp contrast, we have developed a graph-attention deep-learning framework combining molecular representations with quantum-mechanical descriptors to predict relative C(sp 3 )–H borylation site selectivities. Using curated literature reactions and a site labeling algorithm, we evaluated various substrate representations and reaction-condition encodings. Bipartite encoding of reaction conditions outperformed independent component encodings. Validation on previously unreported substrates reproduced experimental selectivity distributions, supporting the framework’s robustness and practical utility.

papers.title: Accelerated Discovery of BPA-Free Dental Resin Candidates through Active Learning of Network-Emergent Properties
papers.abstract: Bisphenol A-glycidyl methacrylate (Bis-GMA) is widely used in dental resins, but its BPA-derived chemistry motivates the search for structurally distinct monomers that retain favorable cured-network properties. Here we introduce EloKriti, an active-learning workflow that links molecular candidate representations to explicit in silico curing and multi-objective optimization of network-emergent properties. We showcase EloKriti by navigating a curated 1000-candidate BPA-free chemical space, filtered from Open Macromolecular Genome for compatibility with vinyl chain-growth polymerization, to simultaneously maximize elastic modulus and minimize volumetric shrinkage and fractional free volume. The retrospectively normalized dominated hypervolume increased from 0.371 to 0.590 by iteration 6, when 57 candidates had been successfully evaluated; although additional candidates were evaluated in the next two rounds, the hypervolume and Pareto-set size did not increase further. From the resulting 13-member Pareto front, three chemically distinct backbones were subsequently incorporated into established, industry-relevant resin building blocks through candidate-specific reactive-site mapping consistent with the growth chemistry of each building block. The resulting synthetically actionable monomers were subjected to five-replica molecular-dynamics virtual-curing validation, and all three networks successfully reached the 95% target degree of conversion. These virtually cured networks exhibited highly specialized property profiles: one optimized the density–shrinkage–free-volume balance, another maximized elastic modulus, and the third achieved the highest glass-transition temperature. These results provide synthetically actionable BPA-free leads for future experimental evaluation and a data-efficient route for prioritizing chemistries on the basis of properties that emerge only after network formation.

papers.title: Harnessing Latent Leaving Groups to Control the Divergent Synthesis of Unsymmetric and Symmetric Dienes
papers.abstract: Conjugated dienes are common feedstocks and motifs in biologically active molecules, dyes, and optoelectronics. However, the synthesis of unsymmetric variants often requires the stepwise functionalization of desymmetrized diene cores or the coupling of two disparately substituted alkenes. Herein we report an alternative approach that enables the synthesis of both unsymmetric and symmetric 1,4-diaryl,-1,3-dienes from a single, unified butadiene surrogate with high stereo-, regio- and chemoselectivity as well as broad tolerance for reactive functional groups. Critical to our approach is the introduction of a latent quaternary ammonium leaving group, which can be used to effectively gate the selectivity-determining elimination step behind judicious choice of reaction conditions.

papers.title: Electrochemical Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer Free Energy Surfaces from Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) is an elementary step in many electrocatalytic reactions, yet molecular-level descriptions of solvent reorganization remain limited. Herein, we describe a first-principles computational platform to calculate free energy surfaces and quantify reorganization energies for interfacial electrochemical PCET. Hydrogen electrosorption at Pt(111)/water interfaces is used as a model reaction to derive PCET free energy surfaces using ab initio molecular dynamics simulations in explicit solvent. The reaction is described as a nonadiabatic transition between reactant and product states defined in terms of localization of electrons and the transferring quantized proton. Free energy surfaces are determined from statistical fluctuation of the vertical energy gap, which directly accounts for explicit solvent reorganization in calculated reorganization energies. The calculated PCET reorganization energy of 3.19 eV compares favorably with previous semi-empirical estimates. This work establishes a robust computational platform to assess the role of interfacial solvent properties on intrinsic electrochemical kinetics.

papers.title: Occupation-Space Variational Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract: Occupation-Space Variational Quantum Optimization (OS-VQO) is introduced as a new framework for quantum electronic structure calculations in which the quantum variational object is an occupation state rather than a many-electron wavefunction. Consequently, the quantum processor operates directly on the occupation numbers, the fundamental variational variables of Natural Orbital Functional Theory (NOFT). The framework is realized through a logarithmically scaling qudit encoding of electron-pair occupation spaces and a hierarchical variational circuit that spans the complete physically admissible occupation manifold while enforcing all N-representability constraints by construction. Noiseless quantum simulations and raw executions on IBM Quantum processors for hydrogen systems up to H216 demonstrate excellent agreement without error mitigation or post-processing, constituting, to the best of our knowledge, the largest raw quantum hardware demonstration reported for a strongly correlated electronic structure calculation. These results demonstrate that quantum variational optimization need not rely on many-electron wavefunctions, opening a new direction for quantum electronic structure calculations based on functional theories.

papers.title: Population-aware Generative Modeling of Lignin Ensemble
papers.abstract: Lignin is a structurally heterogeneous biopolymer whose monomer composition, interunit linkage types, branching, and molecular-weight distribution vary across plant sources and among individual polymer chains. This heterogeneity is essential for understanding lignin self-assembly and morphology, but it is difficult to represent in molecular dynamics simulations because existing rule-based and stochastic generators are generally limited to relatively small structures or populations. Here, we present a machine learning workflow for generating statistically controlled, polydisperse lignin ensembles and converting them into simulation-ready molecular systems. We trained autoregressive molecular language models on 1.16M lignin structures generated with LigninGraphs and represented as canonical SMILES to serve as a generative prior. This generative prior provides a chemically informed distribution for efficient sampling of lignin structures during reinforcement learning. We then introduce a population-aware reinforcement learning scheme that conditions the generative model toward feedstock-specific ensemble properties. Rather than optimizing each generated molecule independently toward the target properties, the generated molecules are evaluated collectively as a population and rewarded according to their contribution to reproducing the target ensemble statistics, including monomer fractions, linkage distributions, branching, number- and weight-average molecular weights, and polydispersity. Molecular-fingerprint and dimensionality-reduction analyses showed that the generated structures remained within the chemical manifold learned from the training data while producing structures not duplicated in the original library. To connect molecular generation directly with simulation, we further extended the structure-construction workflow to automate three-dimensional conversion, residue and linkage-patch assignment, force-field topology generation, and solvent packing. The resulting framework provides an end-to-end route from experimentally informed population statistics to diverse, polydisperse lignin systems suitable for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. By treating the molecular population, rather than an individual molecular structure, as the target of generative modeling, this approach enables molecular heterogeneity to be incorporated explicitly into atomistic simulations and enables systematic investigation of how molecular heterogeneity governs lignin aggregation, morphology, and self-assembly.

papers.title: Biomaterial and bioorthogonal surface engineering of a modular dextran–lipid nanoplatform for tumorresponsive cytokine delivery
papers.abstract: Cytokine-based immunotherapy holds considerable promise for cancer treatment, but its clinical translation is constrained by systemic toxicity, rapid clearance, and limited tumor selectivity. Here, we engineered a modular dextran–lipid nanoplatform that integrates biomaterial design with bioorthogonal surface functionalization for tumor-responsive cytokine delivery (Fig. 1). Azide-functionalized dextran was chemically modified to tune its physicochemical properties and subsequently assembled with an ionizable lipidoid to form hybrid nanoparticles with reactive surface handles. Pro-inflammatory cytokines were covalently displayed on the nanoparticle surface through strain-promoted azide–alkyne cycloaddition, followed by installation of an enzyme-cleavable linker and a PEG-based steric shield. In the tumor microenvironment, tumor-associated proteases cleave the linker, removing the shielding layer and restoring accessibility of the surface-bound cytokine without requiring its complete release from the carrier, as schematically illustrated in Fig. 1. Using IL-18 as a model cytokine, the platform enabled efficient surface conjugation while preserving cytokine bioactivity, and enzyme-triggered de-shielding resulted in time-dependent recovery of biological activity in vitro. The nanoparticles also exhibited good colloidal stability and biocompatibility under the investigated conditions. Overall, this work establishes a modular biomaterial platform in which programmable surface chemistry enables controlled cytokine presentation and tumor-responsive activation, providing a versatile strategy for localized protein-based immunotherapy.

papers.title: Naphthalene-Fused Meta-Dual-Boron Compounds Enable an 80 nm Redshift with Concurrently Narrowed Full Widths at Half Maximum
papers.abstract: Multiple resonance emitters are highly sought after for their intrinsically narrowband emission, yet achieving long-wavelength emission without spectral broadening remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report a naphthalene fused rigid π-extension strategy based on the meta-positioned dual boron framework BBCz-DB by replacing its peripheral carbazole units with naphthalene fragments to develop the yellow MR emitter DB-CzNa. This molecular design leverages the dual aromaticity of naphthalene: while the global π-delocalization effectively narrows the energy gap, the preserved local aromaticity maintains a highly rigid molecular framework, which significantly suppresses excited-state vibronic coupling. This synergistic effect allows the MR emitters to achieve a pronounced emission redshift without sacrificing their narrow emission characteristics. Consequently, DB-CzNa achieves an 80 nm redshift relative to BBCz-DB, delivering yellow emission at 546 nm with an ultra-narrow full width at half maximum of 16 nm (0.07 eV) in toluene. A sensitized fluorescence organic light emitting diode device based on DB-CzNa affords a yellow electroluminescence at 556 nm with a FWHM of 24 nm and a maximum external quantum efficiency of 26.9%. This work demonstrates that judicious naphthalene fusion on meta-dual boron frameworks provides a powerful strategy to overcome the trade-off between spectral redshift and broadening.

papers.title: Valence Delocalization in Trithorium Clusters Identified via Valence-to-Core Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering
papers.abstract: L 3 -edge valence-to-core resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (V2C-RIXS) is applied to thorium for the first time, demonstrating the technique’s sensitivity to actinide 6d-orbital participation in bonding. This sensitivity is exploited to identify states arising from delocalized valence molecular orbitals of predominantly 6d character in two trithorium clusters, [{Th(η 8 -C 8 H 8 )(µ 3 -Cl) 2 } 3 {K(DME) 2 } 2 ] 2b and [K(2.2.2-cryptand)] [{Th(η 8 -C 8 H 8 )(µ 3 -Cl) 2 } 3 ] 3 . Density functional theory based restricted open-shell configuration interaction with singles (DFT/ROCIS) accurately reproduces the V2C-RIXS spectra of 2b and 3 , enabling the quantitative assignment of inelastic intensity to the population of a delocalized three-center 6d z2 σ-bonding molecular orbital. In contrast, L 3 -edge high-energy-resolution fluorescence detection (HERFD) XANES spectra exhibit negligible sensitivity to 6d electron population in these compounds. This study, thus, establishes a clear distinction between the two techniques and identifies V2C-RIXS as a unique probe of 6d orbital contributions to bonding in actinide compounds.

papers.title: How much does the graph help? An information-parity evaluation of graph neural networks for urban air-quality estimation
papers.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly used to estimate air pollution at unmonitored urban locations, but reported gains often conflate what a model is with what it sees. We present a heterogeneous, wind-aware graph attention network that embeds regulatory monitoring stations and traffic counters as distinct node types, and evaluate it under an information-parity protocol: six geostatistical and tabular baselines receive the identical, published information set, within a task taxonomy separating virtual sensing (target history available) from spatial extrapolation (no target-side data at any stage). On five stations and 16 traffic counters in Graz, Austria (2018-2021), neighboring stations’ same-day concentrations account for essentially the entire previously observed GNN advantage: the architecture gap at parity is -0.002 R2. In leakage-free extrapolation the GNN does not outperform task-legal geostatistics (-0.06 R2 versus the strongest baseline), a heterogeneous GNNExplainer analysis routes almost all explanation mass through station-to-station rather than traffic edges, and split-conformal intervals under-cover (0.53 and 0.76 at nominal 0.90), quantifying the cost of crossstation calibration. In dense daily-resolution urban networks, evaluation practice rather than architecture dominates reported GNN advantages; the protocol, code, and data are released so the audit can be repeated on any network.

papers.title: Chain-Growth Synthesis of Sequence-Defined Native Polypeptides via Traceless Cascade Polymerization
papers.abstract: Despite sharing a common macromolecular foundation, synthetic polymers and sequencedefined biomacromolecules have historically evolved along distinct trajectories. Extending the principles of polymerization beyond synthetic materials to nature’s own sequence-defined polymers therefore remains a longstanding challenge. Here we address this challenge by developing a controlled chain-growth polymerization strategy for the synthesis of repetitive sequence-defined native polypeptides. A traceless peri-naphthalene cascade relays the propagating chain end while connecting peptide segments exclusively through native peptide bonds. The resulting synthetic polypeptides reproduce the sequence-dependent biophysical behavior of recombinant analogues while accommodating non-canonical α-, β-, and ᴅ-amino acids. This work fundamentally expands the molecular complexity accessible through controlled polymerization, placing sequence-defined native biomacromolecules within the same chain-growth paradigm as synthetic polymers.

papers.title: Effect of Carboxylate Group Positioning on the Electronic Structure and Sodium-Ion Storage Behavior of Bipyridine Dicarboxylate Anodes
papers.abstract: Understanding how molecular structure influences sodiation thermodynamics and electrochemical properties is important for the rational design of high-performance organic anode materials for sodium-ion batteries. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to establish the structure–performance relationships governing the sodiation thermodynamics and electrochemical properties of three bipyridine-based dicarboxylate isomers: DPC-6,6′, DPC-5,5′, and DPC-4,4′. Although the three systems possess the same N-doped conjugated backbone, differences in carboxylate positioning significantly influence their electronic structure and sodiation behavior. Frontier molecular orbital analysis reveals that carboxylate positioning modulates the LUMO distribution and HOMO–LUMO gap, thereby influencing charge redistribution during the sodiation process. Stepwise sodiation calculations reveal distinct thermodynamic and redox behaviors among the three isomers. DPC-6,6′ exhibits highly favorable initial Na insertion (ΔG = −46.91 kcal mol-1, 1.02 V), whereas DPC-4,4′ shows enhanced stabilization during subsequent Na insertion due to cooperative structural relaxation. DPC-5,5′ displays comparatively balanced thermodynamic stabilization and moderate redox potentials, indicating a more uniform electrochemical response throughout the sodiation process. Comparative analysis with the experimentally reported 2255-Na system further demonstrates that carboxylate positioning and pyridinic nitrogen orientation strongly influence Na coordination, thermodynamic stabilization, and redox behavior during sodiation. These findings provide molecular-level insights into the structure–property relationships governing conjugated organic anode materials for sodium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Tulipalin A-Based Waterborne Acrylic Pressure-Sensitive Adhesives with High Renewable Content
papers.abstract: Waterborne pressure-sensitive adhesives (PSAs) derived from renewable feedstocks offer a route to reduce reliance on fossil resources while retaining the processing advantages of aqueous dispersions. Here, α-methylene-γ-butyrolactone (MBL; tulipalin A) was evaluated as a renewable hard monomer in 2-octyl acrylate (2OA)-rich latexes prepared by seeded semibatch emulsion polymerization. The MBL content, methacrylic acid content, and chaintransfer-agent concentration were varied to balance adhesion and cohesion. Stable latexes with particle diameters of 250–380 nm, glass-transition temperatures from −33 to −28 °C, and theoretical biobased contents of approximately 75–76% were obtained. Reducing the MBL content from 10 to 7 wt% increased the 180° peel resistance from 2.0 to 5.3 N/25 mm, while adding 0.025 wt% chain-transfer agent further increased it to 6.0 N/25 mm. All evaluated formulations sustained a 1 kg static shear load for more than 18,000 min and showed shear adhesion failure temperatures above 215 °C. Rheological measurements confirmed moduli consistent with pressure-sensitive adhesion and predominantly elastic behavior. These results demonstrate that MBL can function as an effective renewable hard monomer in waterborne acrylic PSAs, providing high cohesion and thermal resistance while maintaining useful peel adhesion. Compared with previously reported 2OA/IBOMA waterborne PSAs, the optimized MBL formulation retained comparable peel adhesion while exhibiting markedly enhanced cohesive and thermal resistance, with static shear >18,000 min and SAFT >215 °C.

papers.title: Late-Stage Electrosynthesis of Sulfoxide Metabolites from Phenothiazine-Based Antipsychotic Drugs
papers.abstract: Phenothiazine (PTZ)-based antipsychotic drugs are extensively metabolised in vivo, with S-oxidation representing a major metabolic pathway. Herein, we report the application of an optimised electrosynthetic (ES) S-oxidation strategy to three distinct classes of PTZ-based drug analogues: amino alkyl, piperidine, and piperazine-containing derivatives. The sulfoxide metabolites of the amino alkyl-containing PTZs, including chlorpromazine sulfoxide (1a, 68%), promazine sulfoxide (3a, 34%), triflupromazine sulfoxide (4a, 36%), and promethazine sulfoxide (5a, 11%), were generated under mild, constant-current conditions. For the piperidine-containing PTZs, electrooxidation of thioridazine (6) selectively afforded mesoridazine (7, 15%), while further S-oxidation of 7 at the PTZ ring system yielded the novel bis-sulfoxide 7a (3%). The piperazine-containing PTZs trifluoperazine (8) and fluphenazine (9) provided sulfoxide metabolites 8a (9%) and 9a (5%), alongside unprecedented ring-opened products 8b (1%) and 9b (2%) arising from electrochemical cleavage of the piperazine ring. Two distinct ring-opening mechanisms via decarboxylation (N-demethylation, Shono-type pathway) and via α-cleavage (neighbouring group participation) are proposed. Cyclic voltammetry confirmed successful S-oxidation through the characteristic disappearance of the first oxidation wave in all metabolite products. The methodology was further extended to thioethercontaining active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) extracted from commercial dosage forms.

papers.title: Unveiling Phase Transformation Mechanism in BN from Large-Scale Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: BN-based materials in modern electronics, quantum photonics, and energy devices. Despite their technological importance, the atomistic mechanisms underlying its phase evolution remain poorly understood. Here, we use large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a MACE-based machine-learning interatomic potential to investigate phase-transformation pathways in crystalline BN. Trained on high-fidelity density functional theory (DFT) data and validated against ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, the potential enables simulations of phase evolution across extended length and time scales. We identify a layer-by-layer transformation mechanism that initiates at interfaces, where lattice mismatch and local structural disorder promote reconstructive transformations. We further show that transformation propensity depends non-monotonically on interfacial energy and is enhanced by compressive stresses generated during thermal treatment. These results provide atomistic insight into BN phase transformations under diverse thermodynamic conditions, while the associated MACE training workflow offers a generalizable framework for studying phase-transformation mechanisms in other complex materials.

papers.title: A tetrahedral four-center–one-electron lanthanide–lanthanide bond
papers.abstract: Direct lanthanide–lanthanide bonding has been so far established only in two- and threecenter systems. Here we report lanthanide complexes containing a tetrahedral Ln4 core featuring a four-center–one-electron (4c–1e) lanthanide–lanthanide bond. In a two-step reductive assembly, six-electron reduction of hexaphenylbenzene (HPB) generates a geometrically reorganized HPB6– framework that provides a multimetal-binding environment for assembly of a core comprising four LnII centers and one additional electron. Structural, spectroscopic, magnetic, and computational analyses show that this electron occupies a diffuse cluster orbital of mixed Ln 6s/6p/5d character and is delocalized over the four central metal centers. These results establish a three-dimensional regime of single-electron Ln–Ln bonding and demonstrate how deeply reduced molecular carbon frameworks can access unconventional f-element electronic structures.

papers.title: Uncovering the high efficiency of aromatic aldehydes as energy transfer photocatalysts
papers.abstract: The diverse synthetic applications offered by the — so far not widely explored — excited-state catalysis has intensified the need for development of new EnT catalysts. Herein, we uncover the high efficiency of an unrecognized class, aromatic aldehydes, as EnT photocatalysts. Structure-catalytic efficiency relationship studies on a wide range of common, commercially available and cheap aromatic aldehydes led to the discovery that several aldehydes, for example biphenyl-4-carboxaldehyde, 1-naphthaldehyde and 2-methoxy-1-naphthaldehyde, are highly efficient catalysts for [2+2] cycloadditions and isomerizations under UVA irradiation. To explore the theoretical underpinnings of this catalysis, computational studies combined with principal component analysis suggested that both energy factors and aromaticity/antiaromaticity of ground and excited states contribute to the overall outcome. A wide substrate scope for cyclobutanes/cyclobutenes construction by the addition of alkenes/alkynes to N -arylmaleimides along with dimethyl fumarate isomerization and the dimerization of cinnamates to truxinates demonstrated the wide potential of aromatic aldehydes, expanding the EnT photocatalyst-space.

papers.title: Aromaticity in Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs): A Comparative Analysis Using Magnetic, Geometric, and Electronic Criteria
papers.abstract: An extensive computational investigation has been carried out to determine aromaticity properties in 12 representative polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) compounds of various structural types: reference benzene; linear acenes (naphthalene, anthracene, tetracene); angular (phenanthrene); peri-condensed (pyrene, coronene, perylene, fluoranthene); curved (corannulene); doped by a heteroatom (quinoline, dibenzothiophene). The global and local aromaticity properties of these PAH compounds have been investigated using both local and global aromaticity descriptors calculated at two different theoretical levels, namely B3LYP/def2-SVP and B3LYP/def2-TZVP: geometric (HOMA, mean bond length); magnetic (NICS(0), NICS(1), NICS(1)zz); and electronic (PDI, MCI, FLU) as well as HOMO-LUMO gap and energy. A cross-correlation analysis between all these properties shows that the correlations between geometric and electronic properties are very good (r ≈ 0.8), while there exists an inverse correlation between HOMA and NICS(1)zz values and, finally, that there exist topology-dependent relationships between HOMA and energy gap. As expected, linear acenes present a decrease in HOMA and energy gap values as the number of units of their chains increase. On the other hand, peri-condensed and angular compounds preserve their high local aromaticity because they stabilize through Clar’s sextets. Finally, the analysis of PDI, MCI, and FLU values shows that, in contrast to what occurs in non-fused systems, the local delocalization in fused systems differs from one ring to another depending on whether they belong to the central or to the peripheral region of the compound. This investigation demonstrates that aromaticity in PAHs are a multidimensional property in which geometric and electronic properties show similar behavior while magnetic

papers.title: Inert Low-Spin Rhenium(I) Tricarbonyl Complexes of Phosphine-Based Schiff Bases: Integrating Synthesis, Luminescence, Structural Elucidation, and Biological Activity
papers.abstract: Rhenium(I) tricarbonyl complexes in their monometallic forms have been extensively studied, mainly for their potent inhibitory activity against cancer cells. In this study, we report the synthesis, photoluminescence, crystal structure, and in vitro biological screening of five (5) ligands and their corresponding metal complexes. Of the five ligands, three crystal structures were analysed (with one being an oxidized ligand), while four metal complexes were studied. All crystallized in the monoclinic crystal system. The ligands and complexes, under the Beer-Lambert concentration range, displayed tuneable luminescent properties, with emission energies influenced by the electronic nature of the substituents on the backbone of the Schiff Base ligands. The in vitro cytotoxicity of selected compounds was tested against a panel of human cancer cell lines, including pancreatic (PANC-1, CFPAC-1), breast (MCF7, MDA-MB-231), and cervical (CaSki, HeLa) cancers. While most compounds showed moderate activity, complexes Re-2 and Re-3 exhibited interesting cytotoxicity against MCF7 and MDA-MB-231 cells, with IC50 values of 11.42 and 12.07 μM, respectively.

papers.title: Zirconium-Mediated C–O Bond Cleavage of Alkenyl Ethers Enables Nickel-Catalyzed C(sp3)–C(sp3) and C(sp3)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: Inert aliphatic C–O bonds are ubiquitous in both natural and synthetic feedstocks, yet their direct functionalization remains a formidable challenge in sustainable synthesis. Here we report a tandem strategy that merges thermal zirconium-mediated deoxygenation of alkenyl ethers with visible-light-induced nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling. Through β-oxygen elimination and chain walking, readily available ethers are transformed into alkylzirconocene nucleophiles, enabling efficient C(sp3)–C(sp3) and C(sp3)–C(sp2) bond formation with alkyl and aryl iodides. The method exhibits broad functional group tolerance, late-stage applicability to pharmaceuticals and natural products, gram-scale scalability, and an enantioselective variant (94% ee). Notably, the oxygen-retentive reaction of dihydropyran and the dual functionalization of PMB-protected ethers highlight the atom-economical potential of this protocol. Mechanistic studies elucidate the preference for β-oxygen elimination over β-hydride elimination and reveal the role of a special Zr (III) species as a single-electron donor in the catalytic cycle. This work provides a direct route from unactivated aliphatic C–O bonds to functionalized alkanes, advancing the sustainable valorization of renewable biomass feedstocks.

papers.title: Reproducibility Limits of Public MS/MS Spectral Libraries: Irreproducibility, Outlier Spectra, and Indistinguishable Compounds Across One Million Reference Spectra
papers.abstract: Compound annotation in untargeted metabolomics relies on matching an experimental MS/MS spectrum against a reference library, and the quality of such libraries is routinely summarized by the proportion of spectrum pairs exceeding a similarity threshold. We show that this class of metric is structurally invalid. Analyzing 1,022,449 spectra covering 66,843 compounds from GNPS, MS-DIAL, and MassBank of North America, we compute all within- and between-compound pairwise similarities and demonstrate that proportion-based consistency estimates are confounded by sampling depth as a matter of construction: the apparent high-consistency rate falls from 91% for compound groups supported by a single comparison to 5% for groups supported by more than one hundred. Consequently, any comparison of libraries, instrument platforms, or acquisition conditions that does not control depth measures coverage rather than quality — an apparent advantage of one instrument platform over another narrows substantially once depth is matched. We further identify a resolution floor that no improvement in library curation can remove: 31.7% of compounds share near-identical spectra (cosine ≥ 0.9) with at least one structurally distinct compound, so for these the identification is underdetermined by spectral matching alone. Against this corrected framework, 49.6% of 12,613,259 same-compound comparisons fall below the conventional 0.7 threshold and 6.4% of spectra behave as outliers within their own compound group. We release the collection annotated with spectrum-, group-, and compound-level metrics, each reported alongside the evidence supporting it rather than as a bare proportion, together with the pipeline as an open-source R package.

papers.title: Nitrogen-Centric Optimization of Polyamide Chemical Recycling: A Reaction Network Flux Analysis with New Metrics for Nitrogen Atom Economy and Nitrogen Footprint
papers.abstract: Polyamide 6 and 66 (PA6/PA66) are the only commodity plastics with structural nitrogen (12.4 wt%), yet chemical recycling frameworks treat nitrogen fate as an uncontrolled byproduct. We extend Reaction Network Flux Analysis (RNFA) to a full C-H-O-N mass balance and introduce two new metrics—Nitrogen Atom Economy (NAE) and Nitrogen Footprint (NF)—enabling the first systematic nitrogen-centric optimisation of PA6/PA66 depolymerization. Across 795 NLP solves (GAMS/BARON) spanning six products, five depolymerization route families, and five objective weight scenarios, three findings emerge. First, nitrogen-centric optimisation achieves NAE = 87–100% across all products, compared with the conventional unoptimised baseline of ∼60%. Second, carbon-only objective functions generate NF 6–62× higher than nitrogen-inclusive weighting; for caprolactam and 6-ACA, two economically identical routes differ by up to 62× in nitrogen footprint. Any objective weight w2 ≥ 0.3 on the nitrogen term recovers >90% of the achievable NF reduction. Third, for five of six products, the nitrogen-optimal configuration is simultane- ously the economic optimum—no cost penalty is incurred. These results support a seventh guiding principle for nitrogen-containing polymer upcycling: maximise nitrogen circularity, extending the six-principle framework of Jehanno et al. beyond carbon-centric assessment to address the planetary nitrogen boundary, currently transgressed by a factor of ∼2.4.

papers.title: DEL-GPT: learning the language of DNA-encoded libraries to design focused screening collections
papers.abstract: Focused DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) yield higher hit rates and cleaner selection data than billioncompound collections, and are affordable enough to build for a single target. Designing one means choosing a few hundred synthons from a much larger pool, and in the split-and-pool format that choice is collective and irreversible: the library is the full combinatorial product, so each synthon's value depends on every other one chosen alongside it. Brute force is out of reach – there are on the order of 10189 ways to draw 100 synthons from 3,000. We therefore recast the problem as sequence modeling.
