Treating a synthon as a token and an efficiency-ordered synthon set as a sentence, a generative pretrained transformer trained by next-token prediction learns context-dependent synthon value and composes new sets one synthon at a time. DEL-GPT was trained on one million ranked synthon sets drawn from NADEL, a validated 58,302-member library, with one model per target for five NAD+-dependent enzymes (PARP1, PARP2, PARP10, PARP12, PARP15). Across all five, DEL-GPT libraries outperformed those built from randomly drawn synthons – a demanding baseline, since every NADEL synthon is an expert-selected NAD+ mimetic – and contained two to three times more compounds that experimental affinity selection retained. Quality falls off once generated sets exceed the size range seen in training, but a model trained on longer sequences generated correspondingly larger high-quality sets – a validated recipe for scaling. The method is chemistryagnostic and applies to any combinatorial library over a shared building-block set.

papers.title: Sustainable recycling of end-of-life Nd-Fe-B permanent magnets through hydrogen based plasma reduction
papers.abstract: Nd–Fe–B permanent magnets are essential for multiple energy, mobility, safety, and decarbonization-related technologies, yet rising demand, environmental impacts, and limited sustainable recycling options increase their material criticality. Herein, we propose Hydrogen Plasma Smelting Reduction (HPSR) as a novel composition-independent recycling strategy, applied for the first time to end-of-life (EoL) Nd–Fe–B magnets, enabling the universal treatment of mixed-quality magnetic scrap. The maximum oxygen content reduction of 66% is realized within tHPSR = 2.5 min of processing, reaching ~810 ppm while preserving the overall alloy stoichiometry, including critical rare-earth elements (REEs = Nd, Pr, and Dy). HPSRrecycled powders present higher remanent polarization (Jr = 0.54 – 0.66 T), intrinsic coercivity (Hcj = 1.02 – 1.45 T), maximum energy product (BH)max = 53.5 – 72.4 kJ m-3) and improved thermal stability, surpassing the magnetic properties of the starting scrap material without the addition of primary elements (Jr = 0.56; Hcj = 0.93 T, (BH)max = 46.5 kJ m-3). Under intentional contamination from the coating material (Ni), the reduction in the overall extrinsic magnetic properties is observed, as expected. These findings establish a foundation for the first fully sustainable and composition-independent so-called intermediate recycling loop for mixedquality REE-based magnet waste.

papers.title: From Surface to Bulk and Back: Dynamic Redistribution of Iron in CeO2(111) Model Catalysts under Reducing and Oxidizing Conditions
papers.abstract: Transition-metal modification of cerium dioxide (CeO2) is widely employed to enhance catalytic performance through the creation of active sites, promotion of oxygen-vacancy formation, and improved oxygen mobility. All of these effects can be strongly influenced by the dynamic redistribution of dopant species under reaction conditions, a phenomenon that remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the redox-dependent redistributing of Fe in a well-defined FeOx/CeO2(111) model systems using scanning tunneling microscopy, near-ambient pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, low-energy electron diffraction, and ion sputtering depth profiling by introducing ultra-high vacuum conditions and reducing (H2) or oxidizing (O2) environments at temperatures up to 850 K. Under reducing conditions, the FeOx overlayer becomes unstable above 600–750 K and undergoes extensive disintegration accompanied by Fe diffusion into the CeO2 bulk. Depth profiling reveals a non-uniform Fe distribution with preferential accumulation in deeper regions of the ceria film, eventually approaching the CeO2(111)/ Pt(111) interface. In contrast, oxidizing conditions stabilize Fe at the CeO2(111) surface over the entire investigated temperature range accompanied by substantial restructuring of FeOx species on the surface. Fe incorporation is shown to be reversible, as oxygen annealing of samples with Fe-depleted surfaces restores Fe to the surface. These results demonstrate that FeOx/CeO2(111) systems exhibit fundamentally different structural and chemical behavior under reducing and oxidizing environments, enabling a dynamic redistribution of Fe. The observed activation temperatures for Fe redistribution closely coincide with those reported for Fe–CeO2 catalyst activation in hydrogen temperature-programmed reduction experiments, suggesting that redox-controlled Fe redistribution represent a key structural process governing the performance of Fe-containing ceria catalysts.

papers.title: AMIDR Validation with PyBaMM
papers.abstract: The accuracy of the Atlung Method for Intercalant Diffusion and Resistance (AMIDR) for determining solid-state lithium diffusion was evaluated using synthetic data generated with the Single Particle Model (SPM) and Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) models implemented in PyBaMM. Under SPM conditions, the AMIDR model achieved single-digit errors across a wide range of parameters but exhibited significant fitting errors at extreme parameter values. DFN simulations revealed an additional systematic underestimation of diffusion at high DNMC due to electrolyte transport, with errors approaching two orders of magnitude despite optimized cell design.

papers.title: Silver Nanoparticle Synthesis in a Plant-Derived Gel and Exploration of its Redox and Catalytic Properties
papers.abstract: On the basis of interest and speculation in the field of nanoscience and nanotechnology, curiosity towards innovating different method of synthesis grabs attention. In this regard, the green synthesis method has distinct advantages because it utilizes natural products and abundant substances from nature. Synthesizing metallic nanoparticles using plant-based products is generally cost-effective, non-toxic, and environmentally friendly. Based on this premise, a new and innovative method of silver nanoparticle (Ag NP) synthesis has been reported herein. Precisely, AgNPs have been synthesised in Aloe vera (AV) gel by chemical reduction method, when a thin film of AV containing Ag NPs resulted, hereinafter referred to as AVAg film. The AVAg film has been characterised by different analytical techniques, such as UV-Vis spectroscopy, FTIR spectroscopy, and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Further, the utility of the synthesized Ag NPs was demonstrated by spectrophotometric studies, involving redox reaction considering the decomposition of permanganate ion (MnO4 -), on one hand, and as a reusable catalyst for the reduction of p-nitrophenol (p-NP), on the other.

papers.title: A Novel Biocompatible Magnetic Nickel Nanoparticle-Based Nanocarrier for Potential Application in Promoting Plant Growth
papers.abstract: Herein, we report the synthesis of BSA coated Ni-NPs. The protein-coated NPs were employed as a nanocarrier (delivering magic shots of nutrients) where loading of metal ions (Fe2+, Cu2+, Mn2+, Mg2+, K+, Ca2+) and their subsequent release is established, as illustrated in Scheme 1. UV-Vis spectrophotometric and ICP-OES investigation revealed the effectiveness of the nanocarrier in not just loading but release of the metal ions. Further, we emphasize loading of metal ions as well as release of the metal ions equally and that’s where our vision lies to load the metal ions to the carrier and thereby, releasing them to the deserving site; choosing a biofriendly carrier. Our results have shown the potential of the nanocarrier towards soil fortification by typically monitoring the growth patterns of different plant species. The day-to-day observation of plant growth in the presence of nanocarrier revealed the effectiveness of the nanocarrier towards

papers.title: Synthesis of Dual Opto-Magnetic Property Bearing Nanocomposite and its Utility in the Detection of Cu2+ Ions
papers.abstract: In the present work, mercaptopropionic acid (MPA) stabilized silver nanoparticles (Ag@MPA) and Ag/Fe@MPA opto-magnetic nanocomposites were successfully synthesized through a facile and efficient chemical approach for potential applications in heavy metal ion sensing and remediation. FTIR studies confirmed the covalent binding of MPA onto the Ag nanoparticle surface through Ag–S linkage, while the terminal carboxylic acid groups remained available for surface interactions and colloidal stabilization. TEM analysis revealed the formation of predominantly spherical nanoparticles with an average particle size of 20 ± 3 nm and good dispersibility. The Ag@MPA nanoparticles exhibited pronounced pH-responsive behavior in aqueous medium, where reversible aggregation and redispersion occurred due to protonation and deprotonation of the surface carboxylic groups. The sensing performance of the Ag/Fe3O4 nanocomposite toward different heavy metal ions was investigated using a colorimetric approach. Among the tested ions, Cu2+ ions produced a distinct color change in the nanoparticle dispersion, whereas Hg2+, Pb2+, and Cd2+ ions showed negligible response, demonstrating the selective detection capability of the nanocomposite toward Cu2+, with LOD value of 0.1 mM. Furthermore, the magnetic Fe3O4@MPA component enabled rapid magnetic separation of the Cu2+-bound nanoparticle assemblies from the aqueous medium using an external magnetic field, thereby facilitating simultaneous detection and removal of Cu2+ ions. The combined plasmonic sensing and magnetic separability of the Ag/Fe@MPA nanocomposite make it a promising multifunctional platform for environmental monitoring, selective heavy metal ion detection, and wastewater remediation applications.

papers.title: Automated Multimodal Mapping of Optical and Relative Surface-Potential Responses in a FAPbI3–BDAPbI4–PEA2PbI4 Halide Perovskite Library
papers.abstract: High-throughput (HT) characterization has accelerated materials screening, however most workflows for functional characterization rely on a single measurement modality. This approach leaves the relationship between different aspects of materials response, such as optical emission and local electronic behavior, largely unassessed within the same campaign. Multimodal characterization, particularly pairing probe-based electronic measurements with optical screening, remained comparatively underdeveloped. Here we address this gap by combining automated Kelvin probe force microscopy under illumination (photoKPFM) with HT photoluminescence (PL) peak-intensity mapping to screen a formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3), 1,4-butanediammonium lead iodide (BDAPbI4), and phenethylammonium lead iodide (PEA2PbI4) combinatorial halide perovskite library. A Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization with pure exploration workflow selects photoKPFM measurements to reconstruct the composition-dependent surface potential response, benchmarked on a binary FAPbI3–PEA2PbI4 line before extension to the ternary system. Comparing photoKPFM against PL peak intensity across 13 unique nominal ternary compositions, measured on independently prepared replicate libraries, shows that both descriptors broadly prioritize PEA2PbI4-rich compositions, but individual composition rankings frequently disagree, and exploratory correlation analysis finds no statistically significant global association between the two measurements after multiple-comparison correction. Rather than indicating redundancy, this divergence shows that photoKPFM and PL provide complementary, non-interchangeable candidate-selection information, jointly identifying compositions that rank consistently strong by both descriptors and compositions whose priority depends on which functional descriptor is used. This work demonstrates how pairing automated probe-based and optical HT methods surfaces candidates that single-modality screening would rank differently, motivating multimodal characterization as a general, extensible strategy for combinatorial materials discovery beyond this specific material system.

papers.title: Technical and Engineering Challenges in Scaling Up Microwave-Assisted Pyrolysis of Waste Plastics
papers.abstract: Microwave‑assisted pyrolysis (MAP) has emerged as a promising thermochemical route for converting waste plastics into fuels, chemicals, and carbon materials, offering fast volumetric heating, lower apparent reaction temperatures, and distinctive product selectivity compared with conventional pyrolysis. At present, however, MAP of plastics is still largely confined to laboratory and bench‑scale batch reactors, corresponding mainly to laboratory and pilot technology readiness levels, and the engineering barriers to continuous, large‑scale operation remain poorly understood. This review critically examines the technical and engineering challenges that hinder the scale‑up of MAP for plastic waste valorisation, complementing existing chemistry‑focused reviews that emphasize process parameters and product yields. The key scale‑up barriers discussed include: (i) electromagnetic field non‑uniformity and limited microwave penetration depth in larger cavities, leading to hot spots, thermal runaway, and variable product quality; (ii) design and operation of continuous feeding systems for thermoplastic melts and mixed solid feeds, including mechanical integration of screw feeders, conveyors, and augers in high‑temperature microwave environments; (iii) susceptor selection, durability, and in‑process management (SiC, activated carbon, in‑situ char); (iv) real‑time temperature measurement and process control under microwave irradiation; (v) feedstock variability and the heterogeneous dielectric behaviour of post‑consumer plastic streams; (vi) downstream product quality requirements and constraints for refinery and steam‑cracker integration; and (vii) the current status of coupled multiphysics modelling (electromagnetic–thermal–CFD–reaction) and emerging digital‑twin approaches for reactor and process scale‑up. Reported techno‑economic analyses and life‑cycle assessments suggest that MAP can reduce energy use and greenhouse‑gas emissions relative to conventional plastic pyrolysis under favorable conditions, but robust pilot‑scale datasets and validated process models remain limited. By systematically mapping these unresolved engineering challenges onto recent advances in reactor design, susceptor engineering, process monitoring, Multiphysics simulation, and industrial pilot lines, this review proposes a lab‑to‑pilot‑to‑industrial roadmap for plastic MAP. It identifies priority research directions to advance MAP toward commercial deployment and clarifies its potential role within a broader circular economy framework for plastic waste.

papers.title: What Cycle Closure Can and Cannot See in a Relative Binding Free Energy Network
papers.abstract: Cycle closure is the standard consistency check on a perturbation network, and what such a check can see is fixed by the gradient–cycle decomposition of edge flows (HodgeRank): the cycle part of a network’s error is auditable and biases nothing, while the gradient part biases the affinities and is invisible to any statistic computed from the network’s own values, at any magnitude. Both parts are measured here on 1145 real binding edges. The auditable subspace spans a third of the error space and, in the variance-weighted metric the closure statistic uses, carries under one per cent of the error against experiment. Experimental and annotation error is per-ligand, so it falls in the invisible part by construction and can only have made that share smaller: the measurement is a floor, and it survives correction: in the metric the closure statistic uses on every system measured, at one cell as a tie, and in an isotropic reading on every system of the wider grounded set, failing only on the two weakest of the four the test itself selected. The test built on it behaves as the bound predicts, and its flag set is not stable: the per-edge residuals and the ranking of systems reproduce across independent repeats, and the list of flagged systems does not. Fitting closure against the precisions the estimator already reports gives that test its stated null; it ties the standard fixed 1.0 kcal/mol cutoff, and on every replicate the set of systems it flags lies inside the set that cutoff flags. It flags nothing once the reported errors are widened by half, enough to cover the pose and preparation variance the protocol repeats hold fixed, and it names no removal that recovers accuracy against experiment. Resolving the gradient part needs measurements from outside the network, at worst one per unresolved dimension.

papers.title: Rescuable Stagnation: A Diagnostic for Benchmark Suitability in LLM-Guided Materials Optimization
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly incorporated into closed-loop materials optimization, yet existing benchmarks provide little controlled evidence of what they contribute once Bayesian optimization stalls. We introduce a benchmark qualification criterion for rescue experiments—which we term rescuable stagnation—for determining, before the optimization comparison is run, whether a benchmark stalls while meaningful improvement remains available. Benchmarks that fail this test make it difficult to distinguish ineffective rescue strategies from saturated or non-stalling optimization. Qualifying a benchmark in advance therefore reduces the risk that null results reflect benchmark design rather than the method under evaluation. We demonstrate the approach on a benchmark constructed from Materials Project shear-modulus data, on which LLM-guided rescue gives no statistically significant improvement over heuristic injection—including a heuristic control provided with the same search information. The LLM nonetheless steers the search toward chemically distinct, high-modulus regions that conventional heuristics do not reach. This exploration behavior reproduces across two model capability levels and does not depend on the coherence of the model’s rationales, though it carries a substantially higher per-proposal cost. The LLM’s distinctive contribution on this benchmark is therefore in where it places exploration rather than in the optimization outcome it achieves, though this distinctiveness did not translate into a measurable advantage under the budget tested. More broadly, conclusions about LLM-guided discovery hinge on benchmark suitability—which qualifying the benchmark makes testable before experiments begin.

papers.title: Interface-Engineered MXene/TMD Heterostructures for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution: Progress, DFT-Guided Mechanisms, and Perspectives
papers.abstract: The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) requires efficient, durable, and earth-abundant electrocatalysts to reduce reliance on platinum-group metals. MXene/transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures offer a promising platform by combining the abundant, tunable catalytic sites of TMDs with the high electrical conductivity, hydrophilicity, and versatile surface chemistry of MXenes. This review critically examines recent advances in the synthesis, interfacial engineering, and HER performance of MXene/TMD heterostructures, with particular emphasis on how interfacial interactions govern catalytic behavior. The roles of phase engineering, defect and heteroatom incorporation, surface terminations, and heterointerface construction are discussed in relation to interfacial charge redistribution, electronic-structure modulation, hydrogen adsorption energetics, active-site accessibility, and reaction kinetics. Experimental HER performance across representative MXene/TMD systems is compared to establish structure-interface-performance relationships and identify the origins of enhanced activity and stability. Particular attention is given to density functional theory (DFT) as a mechanistic tool for resolving heterostructure stability, interfacial charge transfer, electronic structure, and hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔGH*). The review also assesses limitations in current computational descriptions of electrocatalytic interfaces, including solvent and electrolyte effects, potential-dependent surface charging, dynamic surface reconstruction, and the accuracy of commonly used exchange-correlation functionals. By integrating experimental observations with theoretical insights, this review identifies interfacial electronic coupling and local active-site chemistry as central determinants of HER performance, while highlighting oxidation stability, interfacial reproducibility, realistic electrochemical modeling, and scalable fabrication as persistent challenges. Finally, future directions combining controlled interfacial synthesis, operando characterization, and advanced constant-potential and solvent-inclusive simulations are proposed to accelerate the development of efficient and durable MXene/TMD electrocatalysts for green hydrogen production.

papers.title: Tackling antibiotic resistance: a dual-criterion computational filter for selective MexAB-OprM efflux pump inhibitors
papers.abstract: Drug repositioning against bacterial efflux pumps has classically relied on a single criterion: the predicted binding affinity for the target transporter. This approach overlooks a distinct failure modetranscriptional derepression of the pump's own expression, through inhibition of the associated transcriptional regulator. Here we propose a dual-criterion screening protocol, combining (i) a relative selectivity index between affinity for the MexB pump and affinity for its repressor MexR, and (ii) an absolute risk threshold calibrated on a documented derepression inducer (pyocyanin). The method was tested by molecular docking (AutoDock Vina) on 139 compounds spanning four independent chemical families (antidepressants, antipsychotics, H1 antihistamines, phytomolecules), against the MexB (PDB 3W9J) and MexR structures. The ΔG(MexB)–ΔG(MexR) correlation proved robust and generalizable across the four families (r = 0.834–0.924, all p < 10-7 after FDR correction), validated by bootstrap, permutation testing, and leave-one-out analysis. Controlling for molecular weight and LogP across the full dataset (n = 135) confirms a partial but non-exclusive contribution of molecular size to this correlation (partial r = 0.805 vs. raw r = 0.880). The dual-criterion filter revealed that 43.1% of the tested compounds, despite showing a good relative selectivity index, exceed the absolute risk thresholdamong them the historical reference compound PAβN and the previously proposed candidate vilazodone. Ensemble docking on three MexR structures (1LNW, 3ECH, 3MEX), performed on a subset of 14 priority compounds, quantified the associated structural uncertainty (mean standard deviation 0.512 kcal/mol): this test confirms the robustness of vilazodone's at-risk status, but reveals that a candidate initially classified as favorable (mianserin) becomes at-risk once this uncertainty is taken into account. These results indicate that filtering by relative index alone is insufficient to rule out derepression risk, and propose a reproducible methodological framework, including an uncertainty estimate, for drug repositioning in the context of combination therapy.

papers.title: Sn Speciation and Spectroscopic Signatures of Sn(II) Sites in Alumina-Supported PtSn Propane Dehydrogenation Catalysts
papers.abstract: The increasing propylene demand-and-supply gap accelerates the development of on-purpose propane dehydrogenation (PDH) technologies. In industrial PDH processes, Pt-Sn based catalysts have had a major impact due to their specific catalytic performances, despite few shortcomings and need for further optimization. Thus, large research efforts have been centered on identifying the roles of the Sn-promoter, including the use of surface organometallic chemistry (SOMC). While so far, SOMC has been mostly used to identify the role of Pt-Sn alloying, the focus here is to explore the speciation of the surface and interfacial Sn sites across synthetic steps. A Pt-Sn catalyst supported on alumina is thus prepared via SOMC, and the detailed spectroscopic and microscopy characterization allows monitoring the evolution of Sn sites, evolving from SnIV sites after grafting to SnII sites, best described as SnII single atoms, upon thermal-treatment. Subsequent grafting of Pt and H2-treatment yield small and narrowly distributed Pt-Sn nanoparticles, which are active, selective and stable for PDH, while residual well-defined SnII sites remains. Notably, while SnII single atoms co-exist with PtSn alloy, this study pinpoints that these SnII single atoms dispersed on alumina display specific 119Sn NMR signatures, that is difficult to distinguish SnII from Sn0 sites solely based on their XAS signatures.

papers.title: Unified Mesoscale Framework Bridging Equilibrium Thermodynamics and Transport Properties of Ionic Liquids and Their Mixtures
papers.abstract: Ionic liquids (ILs) have emerged as sustainable alternatives to molecular solvents due to their unique physicochemical properties. Although quantum chemical simulations provide fundamental insights into their intermolecular interactions, conventional all-atom and coarse-grained frameworks can hardly predict equilibrium thermodynamics and transport properties at the same time. This simulation challenge comes primarily from the high viscosity and low diffusivity of ILs due to strong ion-pairing, resulting in Schmidt numbers (Sc) that span multiple orders of magnitude. In this work, we present a unified mesoscale simulation framework that preserves thermodynamic consistency while quantitatively reproducing the transport properties of pure ILs and their mixtures. This framework integrates a bottom-up approach and an extended dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) formulation: equilibrium thermodynamics are derived from COSMO-RS analysis and fragment molecular orbital (FMO) calculations while DPD resolves coarse-grained dissipative forces into parallel and perpendicular components. A important contribution from this study is a novel algorithm grounded in micromechanical theory that systematically determines friction coefficients and cutoff radii. By incorporating the pair correlation function of the equilibrium structure, the algorithm establishes a functional dependency for the simulated viscosity and diffusivity and ensures they match experimental values across varying solvent compositions. We validate this framework using an imidazolium-based IL system, which demonstrates quantitative agreement with experimental transport properties and captures negative viscosity deviations from ideal mixing. Our framework bridges molecular chemistry and macroscopic rheology and will facilitate the screening, design, and implementation of IL-based processes for energy and separation systems.

papers.title: Ordered interfacial assembly of rough microellipsoids
papers.abstract: Dense, orientationally and translationally ordered, two-dimensional (2D) monolayers of colloidal ellipsoids are fabricated at air-water interfaces. Kinetic arrest and disordered structures from long-range quadrupolar capillary attraction are overcome by synthesizing polystyrene microellipsoids with surface roughness, specifically nanoscale concavities, which attenuate capillary attraction. With increasing area fraction, the particle assembly shows a disorder-order transition from isotropic to plastic crystal at low ellipsoid aspect ratio (AR) and an isotropic to nematic transition at high AR, agreeing qualitatively with simulated hard ellipse close-packing in 2D. The ordered particle assembly is successfully transferred to solid substrates via Langmuir-Blodgett deposition, demonstrating the potential of surface roughness to create anisotropically ordered 2D patterns via interfacial templating.

papers.title: Catch-and-Release of Molybdate [MoO4] 2– by a Synthetic “Molybdophore” Host.
papers.abstract: The neutral 7,7’-diamino-2,2′-diindolylmethane-derived ligands L1 and L2 are shown to selectively recognize the d-block oxyanion of Mo over V and Re (supplied as the tetrabutylammonium salts of [MoO 4 ] 2– , [VO 3 ] – , [ReO 4 ] – ) in CD 3 CN. Incremental additions of [ n Bu 4 N] 2 [MoO 4 ] to CD 3 CN solutions of L1 monitored by 1 H NMR are consistent with the overall 2:1 host-guest equilibria (2 L1 + [MoO 4 ] 2– ⇌ L1 + [ L1 •MoO 4 ] 2– ⇌ [2 L1 •MoO 4 ] 2– ); K11 ≈ 1.6 × 10⁵ M⁻¹ and K 21 ≈ 3 × 10³ M⁻¹. Corresponding additions with vanadate result in K 11 as 46 M -1 , and no interaction could be detected with perrhenate. The (at least) four orders of magnitude selectivity for [MoO 4 ] 2– reflect that the two “protic pockets” of these hosts – comprised of vicinal N–H indole / N–H amide groups – are better matched for the oxy-di-anion [MoO 4 ] 2– . Further structural information can be suggested via the isolation and x-ray crystallographic characterization of the 1:1 host-guest adduct [ L2 ·MoO₄]²⁻ (bis-tetrabutylammonium salt). The encapsulated Mo guest could be released by the incremental addition of acids HBF 4 •Et 2 O or HNTf 2 , resulting in the precipitation of polyoxomolybdates (“molybdenum blues”). X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy suggests that the ratio of Mo(VI)/Mo(V) changes with the receptor/acid identity. Our work illustrates that flexible polyprotic hosts, if designed appropriately, can be selective for specific d-block metallates, manifesting in “molybdophoric” characteristics (at least within the scope of this investigation). .

papers.title: Artificially intelligent modeling of macromolecular assemblies
papers.abstract: The study of macromolecular assembly formation is one of the most challenging tasks in computational modeling, as it requires extensive exploration of conformational and configurational space, especially when driven by conformational transitions or folding instabilities, which are typically associated with high energy barriers. While this type of study has traditionally been addressed in silico by using techniques that reduce the computational cost of simulations, such as coarse-grained models, artificial intelligence (AI) has recently entered the field at multiple levels, aiding in parameter optimization or trajectory analysis, and even replacing potentials or force calculations. Recently developed algorithms such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold enable the direct prediction of final structures with high efficiency and confidence, an achievement that earned them the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In this work, we review and analyze the different AI-based strategies used to model proteins structure and dynamics and simulate macromolecular assemblies, comparing them with traditional methods, to highlight their respective advantages and limitations. By placing these approaches along an ideal continuum in which accuracy increases as interpretability decreases, we show that hybrid solutions and combinations of methods can be devised to maximize their strengths. Finally, we perspectively outline practical strategies for implementing such integrated approaches in a coherent manner, preserving accuracy and feasibility while maintaining insight into aggregation pathways, intermediate structures, and the molecular mechanisms underlying the phenomenon.

papers.title: Ion–polymer affinities of PEDOT:PSS from open-circuit titrations in a multi-cation background
papers.abstract: Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) is a widely used solid contact in solid-state ion-selective electrodes. In an electrolyte, the fixed charge of the PSS − backbone can exchange cations in a manner that depends on the electrolyte composition. Whether the sulfonate group has an intrinsic affinity for particular cations remains open. We estimate the fixed PSS charge density (c f = 1.18 M) from an open-circuit potential (OCP) calibration in pure NaCl, then independently dose NaCl, KCl, CaCl2 and MgCl2 into a 0.1× HEPES-buffered saline baseline containing the four cations at extracellular proportions and record the OCP of a PEDOT:PSS film after each addition. By inverting the titrations through a Donnan partition model, we numerically calculate the ion–polymer affinities k i . Taking Na + as reference, we find k K = 1.05, k Ca = 0.65 and k Mg = 0.44: the polyelectrolyte phase shows no measurable preference between monovalent cations Na + and K + , while showing less affinity with the divalent cations Ca 2+ and Mg 2+ . However, the divalent uptake remains substantial, since the affinity enters the partition linearly while the valence of the ion sits in the exponential of the Donnan potential. Therefore, the ionic composition of the film depends strongly on the ionic strength: at the used baseline Ca 2+ and Mg 2+ together compensate about half of the fixed charge while carrying under 5% of the cation charge in the electrolyte, a phenomenon known as electroselectivity. At 10× our baseline (physiological ionic strength) Na + dominates the PSS compensation and the divalent compensating fraction amounts to 10%.

papers.title: A quantum eigensolver framework for assessing solvent effects of an SN2 reaction
papers.abstract: We present a hybrid quantum-classical framework for molecular simulations that combines the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) with projection-based embedding (PBE) and an implicit solvation treatment. Solvent effects are incorporated through the solvation model based on density (SMD), enabling the investigation of chemically relevant processes in condensed phase environments within a quantum computing workflow. The embedding strategy partitions the molecular system into active and environment subsystems, allowing correlated quantum simulations of the chemically important subsystem while retaining an efficient classical description of the surroundings. As a representative application, we compute the potential energy surface of a bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction between the chloride ion and chloromethane in multiple solvents, demonstrating that quantum eigensolver methods can be extended beyond gas-phase models to include solvent effects relevant for reaction energetics.

papers.title: Next-Generation Enzyme-Responsive "Covalent-Assembly" Fluorescent Probes Based on Dendritic Self-Immolative Molecular Amplification
papers.abstract: Activity-based fluorogenic sensing is now regarded as a powerful approach for the accurate and sensitive detection of a myriad of important analytes, in aqueous matrices of varying complexity. Among the different molecular strategies recently proposed to devise high-performance detection schemes based on the chemical reactivity of species to be detected, the "covalent-assembly" principle is particularly promising. In order to further improve detection performances of the probes designed using this approach, we have explored their combined use with a signal amplification strategy based on the integration of a dendritic self-immolative core whose degradation should lead to in situ synthesis of several fluorophore molecules. To establish and validate this sensing system, penicillin G acylase (PGA) from E. coli was chosen as model enzyme and Pinner cyclization for in situ formation of fluorescent 2-iminocoumarin was selected as an effective biocompatible reaction. Fluorogenic AB 2 and AB 3 dendritic self-immolative molecules have been successfully synthesized. The excellent performances of PGA-responsive AB 2 dendron in terms of signal amplification and aqueous stability have been highlighted through analytical validations involving fluorescence-based enzyme assays completed with RP-HPLC-fluorescence/MS investigations. This study is a further step towards even greater popularization of the "covalent-assembly" approach in the fields of fluorogenic sensing, and bioimaging.

papers.title: In Silico Repurposing of Nilotinib as a Type II Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor to Overcome C797S-Mediated Resistance in EGFR-Mutant Non-small cell lung cancer
papers.abstract: Drug resistance due to mutations in the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) remains a major, well-characterized bottleneck in the targeted therapy of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Among these mutations, C797S, emerging after treatment with third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) such as Osimertinib — prevents covalent drug binding to EGFR protein and results in current therapies ineffective. This study aims to identify and repurpose (Originally used to treat other conditions) potential FDA-approved TKIs capable of overcoming a particular C797S mutation through in silico molecular docking of 52 inhibitors (Type I–VI) against the EGFR T790M/C797S double mutant (PDB: 5ZWJ). AutoDock Vina was used to evaluate binding affinities to EGFR, with EAI045 serving as the reference fourth-generation inhibitor for validation because it shows promising allosteric inhibition but remains limited by its inability to prevent receptor dimerization. Results compared and confirmed the simulation of our docking model with a self-docking baseline of –10.46 kcal/mol for EAI045. Generally, screening revealed that Type II inhibitors exhibited the strongest binding affinity to the EGFR, with Nilotinib and Altiratinib (Note that Altiratinib is not an FDA-approved drug) outperforming EAI045. Nilotinib, an FDA-approved Type II Bcr-Abl inhibitor originally used in chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), displays hydrogen-bonding with the EGFR, sustaining the kinase in its inactive DFG-out conformation when it’s binding. This mechanism prevents ATP binding and stops auto phosphorylation, allowing inhibitory effects even in environments with high ATP concentration by inhibiting the EGFR protein orthosterically. Results show that Nilotinib is a promising candidate to be repurposed into a 4th generation (Post-Osimertinib) TKI for EGFR with C797S mutation NSCLCs. As repurposing drugs have a quicker and cheaper administrative+pre-clinical testing process compared to de novo drug discoveries, by aiming to repurpose drugs we can accelerate clinical translation. While further in vitro and in vivo validation is necessary, this study provides a foundation for developing targeted therapies against the C797S-mediated resistance in advanced NSCLC.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Electronic Response Modes Link Excitation Energy to Catalytic Reactivity
papers.abstract: Illumination can promote or inhibit catalytic reactions, yet the origin of their excitation-energy dependence remains unclear. Here, constrained ΔSCF calculations and spin- and k-resolved wavefunction-overlap tracking are used to follow nonequilibrium electronic configurations across four excitation-energy intervals along H2-dissociation pathways at doped Cu/ZnO interfaces. The preferred pathway switches from final-state-referenced configurations at low excitation energies to initial-state-referenced configurations at higher energies, with dopant-dependent crossover energies and nonmonotonic barrier responses. Metal-site dopants regulate reactivity primarily through excitation-induced reconstruction of collective metal-H bonding, whereas support-site dopants act through pathway-dependent interfacial spin redistribution. Neither excitation energy nor the magnitude of charge, bonding, or spin redistribution alone universally predicts catalytic promotion; the response depends on its direction, localization, and differential coupling to the initial and transition states. Application to Ag-mediated O2 dissociation further demonstrates that population-dependent interfacial reorganization, rather than net adsorbate charge alone, controls bond activation.

papers.title: Two-State RNA Recognition of the FUS RRM Characterized by RNA Sugar Puckering Dynamics
papers.abstract: The RNA recognition motif (RRM) of Fused in Sarcoma (FUS) targets four nucleotides in the hairpin loop of spliceosomal RNA in a sequence-nonspecific manner. To elucidate the mechanism underlying recognition of RNA hairpin loops by the FUS RRM, we performed molecular dynamics simulations of the FUS RRM–RNA hairpin loop complex. Markov state modeling and free energy landscape analyses revealed two distinct conformational states of RNA within the FUS RRM–RNA complex, governed by microscopic ribose puckering equilibria and base-flipping dynamics. Switching between the two states allows the RNA to adopt multiple binding modes, enabling recognition without reliance on any interactions between specific atom pairs. Consequently, RNA sequence variations that weaken specific interactions can be tolerated through alternative interaction networks. Further systematic base-substitution analysis suggests that the FUS RRM potentially recognizes an NHBN-like sequence motif (N = any, H = A/C/U, and B = U/C/G), broadening the previously proposed NYNY paradigm (Y = C/U). The dynamic and multistate nature of RNA recognition observed here provides a mechanistic basis for the ability of the FUS RRM to interact with diverse RNA targets, including exposed hairpin loops in the spliceosome.

papers.title: Ionic and Electronic Mobility in Organic Mixed Conductors
papers.abstract: Charge transport in organic mixed ionic and electronic conductors (OMIECs) is the most basic phenomenon that governs device performance. Due to the material complexity, decoupling ionic from electronic transport is challenging: both measurements and models remain unsatisfactory. Here, we demonstrate that transport of both species in specially designed structures can be described using a unified drift-diffusion model and equivalent circuit. Under these transport-limited conditions, we leverage distinct diffusion features emerging in electrochemical impedance spectra to extract both cation and hole mobilities in PEDOT:PSS on a microfabricated chip. Ultimately, this framework provides a fundamental theoretical model and a robust, single-chip platform to decouple and quantify the transport properties of both ionic and electronic species. This platform offers an immediate opportunity to study structure-property relationships in the context of ionic and electronic transport, guiding the rational synthetic design and predictive discovery of next-generation OMIEC materials and devices.

papers.title: Surfactant-free alcohol-mediated colloidal syntheses of gold nanoparticles beyond aqueous media
papers.abstract: The synthesis of nanomaterials by simple processes is a key towards the full exploitation of their unique properties. Recently, a range of surfactant-free alcohol-mediated colloidal syntheses in alkaline water-alcohol mixtures have been reported. It is shown that the knowledge gained from studying those syntheses can be transferred to other solvents and solvent mixtures with the example of mixtures of dimethyl sulfoxide and ethylene glycol. The results open up new opportunities for the controlled synthesis of surfactant-free nanomaterials and to broaden the scope of their applications.

papers.title: Studying Biologically Important Monovalent Cation Diffusion across Lipids Using Molecular Fe Redox Reporters in Hybrid Bilayer Membranes
papers.abstract: We developed a new hybrid bilayer membrane (HBM) platform, Fe(TPY)(CN)3 HBM, incorporating mononuclear Fe complexes chelated by tridentate 2,2':6',2''-terpyridine-4'-oxy-hexane-1-thiol (TPY) ligands and cyanide (CN–) ligands on an Au electrode, forming a stable and robust octahedral complex, covered by a monolayer of 1,2-dimyristoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DMPC) lipids, to study the transmembrane diffusion behaviours of monovalent cations, Li+, Na+, K+ and NH4+. The most positive shift in the half-wave potential (E1/2) of Fe3+/2+ redox occurred in presence of Li+, following the descending trend of Li+ > NH4+ > Na+ > K+. On the other hand, the Fe3+/2+ redox exhibited the largest peak separation (ΔE) in presence of Li+, which follows the same descending order. These trends highlight that the transmembrane diffusion mechanism for the monovalent cations studied is governed by interplay of charge density, intermolecular interactions, dehydration energy, and interfacial steric hindrance.

papers.title: Controlling Interfacial Cation Interdiffusion to Unlock the Intrinsic Performance of Pr-Based PCFC Cathodes
papers.abstract: Bridging the gap between the intrinsic electrocatalytic activity of cathode materials and their practical performance in proton-conducting fuel cells (PCFCs) requires a fundamental understanding of cation interdiffusion at the electrode-electrolyte interface. In this study, we investigate the cation diffusion and adhesion ability for Pr-based perovskite cathodes of Pr 0.5 Sr 0.5 Co 0.75 Fe 0.25 O 3−δ (PSCF), PrBaCo 1.5 Fe 0.5 O 5+δ (PBCF), and Ba/Sr co-doped PrBa 0.5 Sr 0.5 Co 1.5 Fe 0.5 O 5+δ (PBSCF) on a BaZr 0.1 Ce 0.7 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 3−δ (BZCYYb) electrolyte. X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that conventional 1000 °C adhesion process triggers irreversible cation interdiffusion across the interface, resulting in a severe lattice expansion in PSCF and PBCF of +0.5 % and +1.3 %, respectively, leading to the delamination of the cathode from the electrolyte. To eliminate these interfacial penalties and evaluate the intrinsic electrocatalytic activity, a 750 °C bonding process was employed. By suppressing this cation interdiffusion, the irreversible volume variations were constrained to approximately ±0.1%, achieving crack-free interfaces for all compositions. Evaluated under these ideal conditions, the Sr-substituted simple perovskite PSCF demonstrated the highest peak power density, exceeding the benchmark PBSCF. This performance fundamentally originates from its disordered framework (Pnma), which provides enhanced electron-donating capability, an enriched concentration of surface-active oxygen intermediates, and superior electrical conductivity for rapid bulk charge transfer during the oxygen reduction reaction. Our thermomechanical analysis also reveals that the Ba/Sr co-doped PBSCF uniquely utilizes interfacial cation interdiffusion to counterbalance contact-induced expansion, maintaining a continuous interface even at 1000 °C. This study establishes a dual strategy for advancing PCFCs: unlocking the intrinsic electrocatalytic potential of active cathodes by either suppressing interfacial cation mixing via low-temperature processing or utilizing it through interface-tailored A-site engineering for spontaneous strain neutralization.

papers.title: Guidelines to Evaluate Structure-based Methods for Protein-Ligand Binding Prediction
papers.abstract: Scoring functions built with advanced deep learning algorithms have recently gained prominence in protein-ligand pose generation and binding affinity prediction for computational drug design. However, a number of shortcomings make it increasingly difficult to evaluate scoring functions for a specific task across studies. Transparent disclosure of training data, code and procedures is essential to permit reproducibility, reuse and independent scrutiny. Guarding against leakage, sampling bias and flawed design is equally important. Furthermore, meaningful comparisons require common data splits, checks for run-to-run variability and performance baselines. Here we propose a set of guidelines to help the community identify the most promising methods for these important problems.

papers.title: Construction of Chiral Piperidine Scaffold through an Enantioselective (8+3)-Cycloaddition of Donor-Acceptor Cyclopropanes with Azaheptafulvenes
papers.abstract: An efficient synthesis of chiral piperidine derivatives via an enantioselective Brønsted base-catalyzed (8+3)-cycloaddition is reported. This strategy employs azaheptafulvenes, which undergo cycloaddition with donor-acceptor cyclopropanes serving as three-carbon building blocks, providing efficient access to a new class of chiral piperidine frameworks. The developed method enables the synthesis of a broad range of chiral piperidine derivatives fused to a seven-membered cycloheptatriene ring with high stereoselectivity, broad substrate scope, and excellent functional group tolerance. Furthermore, transformations of the obtained products were demonstrated, providing access to new chiral piperidine-based frameworks.

papers.title: Machine-Learned Short-Range Repulsive Hamiltonians for Electrostatic QM/MM Embedding
papers.abstract: Accurate description of short-range quantum effects between a quantum-mechanical (QM) region and its molecular-mechanical (MM) environment remains a central challenge in electrostatic embedding QM/MM methods. In conventional point-charge embedding, MM atoms polarize the QM wave function through electrostatics but lack an explicit electron density, resulting in an incomplete description of short-range Pauli repulsion and, in unfavorable configurations, electron spill-out and excessive QM-MM attraction. Here we develop EmbR, a physically constrained machine-learning framework that restores this missing short-range quantum response while retaining the simplicity of point-charge embedding. Rather than learning an energy correction alone, EmbR predicts environmentdependent MM-site contributions constrained by the spatial overlap between QM electron density and MM-centered density-like functions. These site contributions are then transformed into explicit atom-centered exponential repulsive potentials and incorporated directly into the QM Hamiltonian. A self-consistent energy-matching procedure further accounts for the density relaxation induced by the added repulsive operator without altering the learned spatial distribution. Across amino-acid–water and amino-acid–water/NaCl model systems, EmbR reduces the interaction-energy errors of conventional electrostatic embedding from 20.21–59.18 kcal/mol to 1.23–2.58 kcal/mol relative to counterpoisecorrected full-QM references, while maintaining strong agreement with the reference interaction energies (𝑅2 = 0.9798–0.9912). Beyond energetic accuracy, EmbR suppresses electron spill-out near positively charged MM sites and reproduces the dominant electrondepletion features associated with interfacial Pauli repulsion. These results demonstrate that physically constrained machine learning can provide an efficient intermediate strategy between conventional point-charge embedding and fully electronic embedding approaches by introducing an environment-dependent short-range quantum operator into QM/MM Hamiltonians.

papers.title: Human–Robot Collaborative Reaction Development with a Self-Driving Laboratory
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) can accelerate chemical optimisation, yet their application has largely focused on established reaction classes rather than the uncertain and iterative process of developing new reactivity. Here we introduce human-robot collaborative reaction development, in which researchers drive ideation, interpretation and scientific decisionmaking, while an SDL performs the systematic experimentation required to rapidly evaluate emerging reaction concepts. We demonstrate this approach through the development of a photochemical α-(fluoro)alkylation of cyclic secondary amines via in situ imine formation. Starting from an initial human-discovered reactivity hit, RoboChem-Flex was repeatedly deployed as new questions emerged: to establish whether the reaction warranted further development, adapt conditions to di erent substrate classes, rapidly assess coupling partners, and optimise promising but underperforming reactivity. Transfer of knowledge between campaigns further enabled an initially low-yielding α-methylation to be developed in only 11 additional experiments. The resulting methodology accommodates diverse cyclic amines and alkyl iodides and enables downstream derivatisation. More broadly, this work demonstrates how autonomous experimentation can augment human scientific reasoning, accelerating the transition from initial reactivity to synthetic methodology while keeping scientific judgement at the centre of the discovery process.

papers.title: DFT/XCIS: A Kohn-Sham Approach to Extended Configuration-Interaction Singles, for Valence- and Core-Level Spectroscopy of Open-Shell Systems
papers.abstract: Core-to-valence transitions are sensitive probes of unoccupied valence orbitals and are especially informative for open-shell molecules and materials, where frontier molecular orbitals are often degenerate or nearly so. Accurate simulation of core-level spectra for open-shell molecules is challenging because methods such as time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) typically rely on a spin-unrestricted reference determinant, leading to spin contamination. A restricted open-shell reference state eliminates spin contamination in the ground state but excited states computed using the configuration-interaction singles (CIS) approach may yet exhibit significant spin contamination. This can be eliminated by extending the CIS excitation space to include a small number of doubly substituted determinants, in what has been called “extended” (X)CIS, and this approach affords a variational and size-consistent wave function for each excited state, free of spin contamination but also free of dynamical correlation. Here, we introduce the latter via density functional theory (DFT), using Kohn-Sham orbitals within the XCIS formalism and scaling the electron repulsion integrals to reduce double-counting of correlation effects. Reasonable valence excitation energies are obtained with the new DFT/XCIS approach, and combing it with core/valence separation (DFT/ XCIS-CVS) extends the method to core-level spectroscopy. Absolute excitation energies for K-edge transitions are improved, relative to conventional TDDFT, by means of an empirical shift in the 1s eigenvalues. Incorporation of dynamical correlation improves the accuracy of spectral splittings for open-shell systems, relative to the recently reported XCIS-CVS approach.

papers.title: Transfer Protocol Matters More Than Source-Task Selection in Low-Data Molecular Property Prediction: An Audit of QM9 Pretraining on Computed Oxidation Potentials and Redox Reaction Energies
papers.abstract: Pretraining a network on QM9 quantum-chemical labels and transferring it to a data-scarce molecular endpoint is a common strategy in chemical machine learning, and a growing literature proposes tasksimilarity descriptors for deciding which source task to transfer from. We audit both decisions on two non-synthetic computational chemistry datasets — DFT-derived oxidation potentials (OxPot, 15,238 molecules) and redox reaction energies (RedDB, 15,551 molecules) — using 24 independently initialised QM9 source models spanning eight quantum-chemical tasks. We first establish, in a controlled synthetic benchmark with known informative coordinates, that magnitude-pruning masks can be aggregated into interpretable task-level feature-usage signatures that recover ground-truth feature overlap (pooled mean Spearman 0.2749, versus 0.1755 for unpruned first-layer weights and 0.0614 for a random control). Eleven signature series were compared; their relative ordering proved sensitive to pooling, with gradient saliency ahead in the unmatched pooled summary (0.2855) and behind by 0.211 in a paired same-setting audit. This mechanism did not translate into deployable source selection: on the two molecular datasets every selector produced negative mean transfer gain under full-weight transfer (feature-similarity top-1: −0.124, negative-transfer rate 95.8%; pseudo-label top-1: −0.177, 100%), and an agreement gate limited harm mainly by abstaining in 87.5% of cases. We then evaluated 144 matched case–source pairs under four transfer protocols (576 transfer runs). At the target-case level, resetting the output head improved relative gain by 0.087 (case-bootstrap 95% CI 0.070–0.106; 18/18 cases positive), and restricting transfer to the first layer added 0.044 (95% CI 0.034–0.055; 18/18 positive). Protocol changes produced the largest and most consistent shifts in realised gain. Only under the most conservative protocol did any dataset reach non-negative mean transfer (OxPot, +0.003; RedDB remained negative). For this setting, transfer protocol and an explicit abstention option deserve priority over increasingly elaborate sourcesimilarity descriptors.

papers.title: From Computational Chemistry to Generative Models: A Survey of AI-Driven Small-Molecule Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery requires navigating enormous chemical space to identify candidates that are simultaneously potent, selective, synthetically accessible, and acceptable across pharmacokinetic and safety profiles; modern generative AI extends a long computational medicinal chemistry lineage that began with QSAR, pharmacophore modeling, and early structure-based de novo design. This survey focuses primarily on developments from 2017 to 2025, with the literature updated through 31 January 2026. Using a medicinal-chemistry lens, it first establishes the shared machinery of the field: molecular representations such as SMILES, SELFIES, graphs, fingerprints, three-dimensional coordinates, voxels, and latent vectors; commonly used datasets and benchmarks; and graph neural network encoders, including message-passing, directional, and equivariant architectures. We compare five principal generative mechanisms—autoregressive models, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, normalizing flows, and diffusion models—together with reinforcement learning as a major goal-directed optimization framework. Across these approaches, we show that current methods offer complementary rather than interchangeable trade-offs, and we highlight recurring challenges, including validity versus synthesizability, limited prospective experimental validation, mode collapse and diversity loss, stereochemical and physical realism in three-dimensional design, computational cost, data scarcity, and the emerging convergence toward scaffold-conditioned generation, hybrid architectures, developability-aware optimization, and molecular foundation models.

papers.title: Water-Stable Superferromagnetic Nanoparticle Chains Break the Langevin Resolution Limit in Magnetic Particle Imaging
papers.abstract: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) localizes superparamagnetic iron oxide tracers through their nonlinear magnetization response, but its spatial resolution is bounded by the Langevin behavior of independent magnetic moments, confining clinical tracers to point spread functions (PSFs) near 10 mT and limiting clinical tracer resolution to the centimetre scale in humans. Superferromagnetic iron oxide (SFMIO) tracers — linear chains of dipole-coupled cores that reverse cooperatively — surpass this limit, yet have remained confined to organic solvents, because the charged corona required for aqueous colloidal stability generates an electrostatic repulsion opposing the dipolar attraction that drives chain assembly. Here, a water-stable SFMIO tracer is reported. Monodisperse ~26 nm cores are grown by thermal decomposition, magnetophoretically enriched, encapsulated in poly(maleic anhydride-alt-1-octadecene) to a ~2 nm shell, and assembled into chains under a uniform field at 1.5× phosphate-buffered saline, where screening balances dipolar attraction. The tracer exhibits a mean PSF full-width at half-maximum of 4.3 ± 0.3 mT at 20 mT and 20 kHz across three independent syntheses — 2.6-fold narrower than the preclinical reference tracer VivoTrax, and equivalent to 0.67 mm at a 6.4 T m−1 gradient. The measured coercivity, 12.1 mT, matches the 12.0 mT predicted by a positive-feedback dipolar model parameterized by TEM-measured geometry and a literature-bounded saturation magnetization, confirming cooperative avalanche reversal within structurally static chains.

papers.title: Practical Aspects of GC-MS Towards Enhanced Understanding of Lignin Decomposition products
PFAS Uptake from Regulatory-Compliant Irrigation Water Exceeds Dietary Limits in Radish and Lettuce: Dose-Response and Activated Carbon Mitigation
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are regulated primarily in drinking water and soil, yet neither matrix is what consumers ingest. We tested whether irrigation water meeting regulatory thresholds can still produce unsafe PFAS burdens in edible crops. Radish (Raphanus sativus) and lettuce (Lactuca sativa) were irrigated across five arms (0, 16, 152 and 301 ng L −1 total PFAS from five long-chain compounds, plus a 152 ng L −1 activated carbon (AC)-filtered arm); plant and soil PFAS were quantified by liquid chromatography- mass spectrometry. Tissue PFAS accumulated dose-dependently, exceeding the European Food Safety Authority tolerable weekly intake by 2–39×. Critically, at 16 ng L −1 , below the Massachusetts drinking-water maximum contaminant level, tissue exceeded dietary limits by 2–4× while soil PFAS remained below international agricultural screening values, revealing a soil–plant regulatory disconnect. The contamination was undetectable by inspection: growth metrics did not differ across treatments and 67 blinded observers classified contamination at chance. Gravity-column AC pre-filtration reduced tissue PFAS by 84–91% without growth penalty. Compliance in the two monitored matrices does not predict crop burden, supporting direct crop-tissue monitoring and accessible pre-harvest filtration.

papers.title: An experiment-calibrated in-silico AI co-scientist discovers chemoselective silicon-nitride passivation for area-selective SiO2 atomic layer deposition
papers.abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) of SiO 2 -on-SiO 2 requires passivating adjacent SiN to isolate charge-trap nitride in 3D-NAND. We hypothesize that a smallmolecule electrophilic inhibitor chemoselectively acylates SiN surface amines (–NH 2 /–NH) over SiO 2 silanols (–OH), capping SiN against oxide nucleation. We build an in-silico AI co-scientist that (i) constructs amorphous a-SiO 2 /aSiN surfaces validated against diffraction and calibrates their reactive-site density to experiment, (ii) benchmarks its own methods, (iii) agentically screens inhibitors, and (iv) validates against a published positive control. The core selectivity is kinetic: reaction thermodynamics are near-degenerate, but acylation strongly favors the SiN amine over the SiO 2 silanol (gas-phase barrier difference ∼0.9 eV, a stepwise addition; xTB and DFT concur on the direction), reproducing textbook amine≫silanol chemose-lectivity. With a first-principles cap oxidative-initiation barrier (Ea≈0.68 eV ⇒ kdeg≈2.9× 10 −2 /cycle), a mechanistic multi-cycle model then demonstrates the target rather than assuming it: a re-passivation supercycle (redose every 3 cycles) reaches S = 0.91 at 10 nm. Run as a genuine closed loop, the agent autonomously proposes and screens candidates, inventing a novel lead that beats a naive electrophilicity-only baseline by 2.5 eV of selectivity. Our pipeline independently reproduces the published aminosilane oxide-preference (BDIPADS), anchoring the method. The pipeline is built entirely on open-source software.

papers.title: Commentary on the use of Virial fits for calculation of the isosteric heats of adsorption
papers.abstract: For analytic determination of the isosteric heats of adsorption, Qst, in microporous crystalline materials such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and zeolites, it is common practice to fit experimental data of unary isotherms at different temperatures using Virial fits, with a total of 12 parameters. The Virial fits of unary isotherms, however, do not allow calculations of adsorption selectivities using the Ideal Adsorbed Solution Theory (IAST). The main objective of this article is to demonstrate that a better approach is to fit the unary isotherms at different temperatures using the Dual-Site Langmuir-Freundlich (DSLF) model in which the saturation capacities and Freundlich exponents are constrained to be T-independent, and requiring a total of 8 parameters. The DSLF fits allow analytic determination of Qst, and may also be used in IAST calculations. Examination of published experimental data on unary isotherms for several guest/host combinations shows that the Virial and DSLF fits are of comparable accuracy, despite the fact that significantly fewer parameters are required for DSLF fits. Also, the Qst vs loading characteristics of the Virial and DSLF fits are distinctively different. The overall conclusion to be drawn is that DSLF fits with T-independent saturation capacities, and Freundlich exponents are generally to be preferred to Virial fits.

papers.title: Stabilization and Functionalization of an Enzyme Complex via Modular In Situ Conjugation
papers.abstract: Enzymes are unparalleled catalysts that combine high activity and selectivity with operation under mild conditions. Despite these advantages, their broader use as industrial biocatalysts is limited by insufficient stability under process-relevant conditions and by the difficulty of achieving site-specific chemical functionalization. Simultaneously enhancing protein stability and enabling site-specific functionalization through a single chemical strategy remains a central challenge, particularly, when addressing multimeric enzymes. Here, we show that a four-armed crosslinker with tetrahedral symmetry enables simultaneous stabilization and programmable functionalization of the tetrameric enzyme borneol dehydrogenase. A twostep crosslinking–modification reaction yields a well-defined and stable protein quaternary architecture with an incorporated reactive handle, enabling the installation of diverse functionalities, including bioorthogonal tags and functional groups for immobilization. The chemically engineered bicyclic enzyme exhibits remarkably enhanced thermal stability and resistance to organic cosolvents, which results in exceptional longevity supporting ten weeks of continuous flow operation. Unlike previous methods that decouple stabilization from modification, this strategy unites structural reinforcement and functionalization, thereby expanding the scope of chemical protein engineering.

papers.title: Capping-Agent Regulation of Exciton Transport in Organic Nanoparticles Enables Ultrabright Flow Cytometry Probes
papers.abstract: Fluorescent dye-loaded nanoparticles (NPs) offer powerful platforms for bioimaging, biosensing, and flow cytometry, but their performance is often compromised by aggregation-caused quenching and exciton trapping. Although molecular isolation can suppress aggregation, controlling exciton transport within fluorescent NPs remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the capping agent provides a powerful means to regulate exciton dynamics in small-molecule ionic isolation lattice (SMILES) NPs. Replacing the conventional phospholipid capping agent DSPE-PEG with poly(styrene-co-maleic anhydride) (PSMA) increases the fluorescence quantum yield more than threefold, reaching 61%. Polarization-resolved femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals markedly slower exciton depolarization with PSMA, with the anisotropy remaining at ~0.1 at long delay times, indicating restricted exciton migration and reduced trapping at nonradiative defects. This exciton confinement enhances fluorescence efficiency and substantially increases NP brightness. The capping-agent-dependent regulation of exciton transport is applicable to structurally diverse fluorophores, enabling SMILES NPs with distinct emission colors spanning the visible to near-infrared spectral range. Following antibody functionalization, these ultrabright NPs produce fluorescence signals up to 17-fold higher than commercial phycoerythrin-conjugated antibodies in flow cytometry of human peripheral blood. These findings establish capping-agent regulation of exciton transport as a general approach to enhancing the brightness and analytical performance of fluorescent nanoprobes.

papers.title: Nanostructured Semiconductor Helices with Circularly Polarized Light Emission in Near Infrared Telecommunication Wavelengths
papers.abstract: Materials with circularly polarized luminescence have recently gained increasing interest due to their potential applications in three-dimensional displays, optoelectronic devices, optical sensors, and optical information storage.1,2 Emitters with circular polarization in the near infrared (NIR) part of the spectrum have been found to have advantages over visible light for the areas of bioimaging and telecommunications. This is due to low absorption of NIR light in biological samples, which allows for high-quality imaging and minimal sample damage, and low attenuation of NIR light in optical fibers, which is ideal for long-distance communication.3,4,5 Only a few NIR active chiral emitters have been reported and characterization equipment for circularly polarized light detection in the NIR is limited; this has made the development of materials with optical activity in this optical range challenging. This work seeks to expand this material library through simple compositional tuning of established chiral semiconductor morphologies that exhibit strong circularly polarized light emission in the visible region.

papers.title: Exploring the Potential of on-DNA Phthalimide Deprotection for DNA-encoded Libraries
papers.abstract: DNA-encoded library (DEL) synthesis currently relies on a limited set of DNA-compatible protecting group strategies, highlighting the need for orthogonal methods to expand accessible chemical space. Herein, we report a synthetic strategy for the conjugation of phthalimide-protected amino acids to DNA and their subsequent deprotection on-DNA. Optimization studies established mild coupling and deprotection conditions that minimized competing phthalimide hydrolysis, with ethylene-1,2-diamine in aqueous MOPS buffer/acetonitrile affording moderate to good deprotection yields across a range of DNA-conjugated phthalimide-protected amino acids. More sterically demanding substrates required elevated temperatures but remained amenable to deprotection. The utility of the developed protocol was further demonstrated through a subsequent on-DNA amide coupling following phthalimide deprotection. Collectively, this methodology expands the repertoire of DNA-compatible protecting group strategies and provides an orthogonal approach for sequential functionalization in DEL synthesis.

papers.title: Understanding male urethral mechanics: from ex vivo testing to mathematical modelling and in situ assessment, a review.
papers.abstract: Male urethral disorders, in particular hypospadias and urethral stricture, frequently require reconstructive surgery. However, current autologous grafts fail to replicate the supportive bed provided by the corpus spongiosum, contributing to high recurrence rates. Developing functional, off-the-shelf tissue-engineered replacements requires a comprehensive understanding of urethral mechanics, which remains fragmented in the literature. Here, we review and integrate diverse methodologies—including ex vivo mechanical testing, mathematical modelling, and in situ clinical assessments—to elucidate the complex, anisotropic, and viscoelastic properties of the male urethra. This multidimensional approach highlights physiological pressure ranges, tissue compliance, and biomechanical behaviour under dynamic conditions, stressing urethral mechanics' location- and orientation-dependency. We provide standardised mechanical guidelines and modelling frameworks that can guide the design of biomimetic urethral grafts. Ultimately, this work advances the understanding of urethral mechanics, informing regenerative medicine strategies aimed at improving long-term outcomes for patients with urethral disorders.

papers.title: An Amdahl Framework for Agentic Computational Science
papers.abstract: AI agents increasingly compress human-mediated parts of computational research, shifting bottlenecks toward whatever remains slow. Amdahl-like models capture this serial-bottleneck logic but usually take the non-compressible block as fixed. Here I ask what that block contains in computational science. I start from a fixed-workflow baseline separating numerical execution and resource waiting from active human work and synchronization delay, then relax the assumption that nominal simulation time is irreducible. Human researchers already provide semantic oversight intermittently; persistent agents can apply the same scrutiny earlier and more consistently. This motivates a counterfactual split between core and avoidable computation, and a closed-loop ceiling in which only minimum necessary critical-path computation remains irreducible after accounting for validation cost. As human-mediated delays shrink, bottlenecks migrate toward numerical kernels and resource constraints, making faster solvers, surrogate models and high-performance computing more valuable.

papers.title: Interfacial Microenvironment on Pt(100) Controls Electrochemical Methane Activation
papers.abstract: Electrochemical conversion of methane into liquid oxygenates has attracted significant attention as a sustainable process for the valorization of natural gas. Platinum single crystals provide well-defined model surfaces for mechanistic studies of methane oxidation via direct activation, with Pt(100) being the only facet capable of catalyzing this reaction. Here, we combine electrochemical measurements and theoretical calculations to investigate how the microenvironment at the Pt(100) electrode interface influences methane activation. We first confirm the crucial role of (100) terraces as the main active sites by using electrodes with different degrees of surface order, obtained by cooling them under different atmospheres. Cyclic voltammetry further reveals that methane dissolved in the electrolyte can be activated only at potentials between 0.30–0.60 V vs RHE, a window in which OH species are co-adsorbed on the electrode surface in acidic media. In contrast, more alkaline electrolytes inhibit the overall reaction. Density functional theory calculations show that interfacial OH directs methane activation toward either OH-mediated or surface-mediated C–H abstraction, with activation barriers of 1.0 and 0.6 eV, respectively. By accounting for the co-presence of adsorbed OH during methane activation, our results provide a more realistic description of the electrochemical interface and rationalize the pronounced structure sensitivity of methane activation on platinum surfaces.

papers.title: Atomistic Mechanism of the Spontaneous Formation of Ferroelectric Nematic Order from an Isotropic Liquid
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric nematic (N F ) liquid crystals have fluidity with macroscopic polar order, yet the transition pathway at the molecular scale by which an isotropic liquid spontaneously develops long-range ferroelectric order remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that microsecond-scale, unbiased all-atom molecular dynamics simulations can reproduce the spontaneous development of strong, system-wide polar order from an initially isotropic state. For DIO, highly polar local domains emerged upon cooling but remained nanoscopic because slow molecular diffusion kinetically suppressed their further growth. In contrast, UUZU-2N, which exhibits an enantiotropic N F phase at relatively high temperatures, underwent progressive polardomain growth and coalescence, ultimately reaching a nearly monodomain state with a polar order parameter of 𝑃 1 ≈ 0.9. The calculated spontaneous polarization reached 6.7 μC/cm 2 , in reasonable agreement with experiment. Notably, nematic orientational order developed rapidly, whereas long-range polar order emerged over several microseconds through much slower domain coarsening. The spontaneous development of strong polar order was also reproduced for C2-BOE. Further structural analyses revealed characteristic offset configurations and head-to-tail correlations between neighboring molecules. In comparison with molecular electrostatic distributions, it is suggested that longitudinally asymmetric and modulated charge distributions contribute to the stabilization of these polar arrangements. These results provide an atomistic mechanism connecting molecular electrostatics, local packing, domain coarsening, and macroscopic polarization in the N F liquid crystals.

papers.title: Custom-designed carbosilane-based reactive surfactants for surface hydrophobization – AFM, Raman microscopy, and XPS investigations
SYNTHESIS OF AZOPYRIDINES BASED PHOTOSWITCHES VIA ZINCKE IMINE INTERMEDIATES
papers.abstract: Azopyridines are an underexplored subclass of heteroaryl azo photoswitches whose pyridine nitrogen confers pH- and metal-responsiveness in addition to reversible E/Z-photoisomerization, yet no general method exists for their regioselective synthesis. Here we report that aryl diazonium salts undergo direct electrophilic azo coupling to Zincke imine intermediates, providing a mild, two-step route to substituted azopyridines that operate exclusively on the dearomatized pyridine core, leaving electron-rich aryl substituents untouched. Reaction conditions were optimized using a Design of Experiments/Response Surface Methodology approach. The method tolerates a broad range of diazonium and Zincke imine substituents including halogens, methoxy, nitro, cyano, extended aromatic and heteroaromatic systems, furnishing the first complete set of positional isomers bearing a substituent at C2, C3, C4, and C5 of the 3-azopyridine ring, and enabling 15N labelling in the parent pyridine ring. UV-Vis and DFT/TD-DFT studies reveal red-shifted, structurally tuneable π→π* absorption relative to azobenzene, while photoisomerization experiments show fatigue-resistant bidirectional switching up to >80% conversion in both directions with thermal Z-isomer half-lives spanning hours to weeks. This work establishes Zincke imine chemistry as a general platform for azopyridine synthesis and provides a structurally diverse toolkit for structure–property evaluation.

papers.title: Sequential Chiral-Layer Processing for Large Chiroptical Responses in Polymer Films and CP-LEDs
papers.abstract: Chiral small molecules can induce chiroptical responses in otherwise achiral fluorescent polymers, making these materials relevant to circularly polarized lightemitting materials and devices. Sequential deposition offers a route to chiroptical polymer films when a fluorescent polymer and a chiral small molecule cannot be readily co-processed from the same solvent. Here, poly(9,9-dioctylfluorene-altbithiophene) (F8T2) and a chiral inducer are deposited as initially separate layers from orthogonal solvents. A chiroptical response develops after thermal annealing, after which the excess inducer is reduced by selective ethanol treatment. With R-DbHP, the apparent peak absorption dissymmetry factor (|gabs|) increases from 0.09 for an optimized blend film to 0.35 for the sequentially processed film. With R-5011, the apparent film value reaches 1.06, and CP-LEDs show |gEL| up to 1.02. Across two independently fabricated devices per condition, the external quantum efficiency was 0.16–0.17% without EtOH treatment and 0.20–0.27% with treatment, and the corresponding turn-on voltages were 9V and 7V; the peak gEL remains similar, whereas the maximum luminance is lower in the treated devices. These device comparisons are exploratory and no statistical inference is made. The CD-derived values are also treated as apparent because complete polarization-artifact controls and independent validation of the largest raw ellipticities were not available.
