Within these limitations, the results identify sequential chiral-layer processing as a potential alternative to bulk co-doping in polymer CP-LEDs.

papers.title: High precision, fast computation and high accuracy? Linear scaling double hybrid DFT calculations with spin-polarization
papers.abstract: Double-hybrid density functional theory (DH-DFT) has emerged as the most accurate DFT for molecular thermochemistry and kinetics, yet its widespread adoption for molecules with many atoms, A, is restricted by the steep O(A5) computational scaling and large O(A3) memory footprint of conventional canonical basis second-order Møller–Plesset (MP2) perturbation theory. Our previously reported spin-restricted local MP2 framework based on numerical sparsity successfully eliminated the O(A5) scaling bottleneck of MP2 for closed-shell systems. In this work, we address the challenge of generalizing it to achieve a linear-scaling, spin-unrestricted local MP2 algorithm, which enables asymptotically linear scaling evaluation of double hybrids for open shell and reactive molecules. The O(A1) linear scaling wall time of our implementation is validated on model radical-cation chains. Shared-memory (OpenMP) and distributed-memory (MPI) parallel implementations are benchmarked on open-shell transition metal configurations from the ROST61, MME55 and 16OSTM10 datasets. Governed by a single, user-defined precision threshold (ϵ), the numerical sparsity algorithm recovers over 99.99% of the canonical correlation energy using ϵ = 10−6 (a reasonable choice for production calculations), and yields relative energies with root-mean-square errors well below the threshold of chemical accuracy. As a larger example, a 181-atom transition metal complex is evaluated in the large def2-QZVPP basis set (8, 792 basis functions) with ϵ = 10−6 within one day utilizing 128 MPI ranks. Finally, integration with different double hybrid functionals, including ωB97M(2), PBE-QIDH and revDSD-PBEP86-D4, is demonstrated.

papers.title: Ligand Curvature Controls the Size of Self-Assembled Twisted Metallacycles
papers.abstract: Coordination-driven self-assembly often yields dynamic libraries of macrocycles whose size distribution is difficult to control, and ligand-design strategies for directing such equilibria have so far been limited to discrete changes in coordination angles. Here we introduce the first twisted metallacycles, in which ligand curvature is tuned through the tether-to-twist approach. Two twistacene dipyridyl ligands with only a 6° difference in the overall bend: the nearly planar Pl (14° twist) and the twisted Tw (34° twist), assemble with (dppp)Pd(II) and (dppp)Pt(II) corners, {M}, into dynamic equilibria between rhomboidal {M} 2 L 2 and hexagonal {M} 3 L 3 metallacycles. NMR, nanoESI-MS and X-ray crystallography show that racemic ligands self-sort with high fidelity: socially, into heterochiral meso {M} 2 L 2 rhomboids, and narcissistically, into homochiral {M} 3 L 3 hexagons. Van 't Hoff analysis shows ring expansion to be endothermic and entropy-driven throughout, with an enthalpic cost rising from 6–10 kJ mol-1 for Pl to 17–18 kJ mol-1 for Tw . This is explained by increased strain energy for mismatched planar ligands in {M} 2 L 2 assemblies. A few degrees of backbone curvature therefore reshape the free-energy landscape of coordination-driven self-assembly.

papers.title: Sequential Direct Electrodegradation of Polyurethane
papers.abstract: Polyurethane (PU) is a structurally complex polymer whose hard aromatic and soft aliphatic segments define its materials properties. The urethane linkers connecting these segments provide stability and hydrolysis resistance but make end-of-life chemical processing challenging. Electrodegradation provides a mild, scalable, and efficient approach to polymer degradation that has been used to oxidatively or reductively cleave specific linkers or functional groups. Here, we report the sequential direct electrodegradation of the multiple segments within polyurethane. We chose a commercial polyurethane with a diaromatic methylene-bridged hard segment and ether and polyester soft segments, and characterized its dissolution and electrochemical properties. We then measured polymer degradation via size exclusion chromatography for different reaction conditions and determined that only an oligomeric polyester product remained. We characterized reaction intermediates of the polymer and representative model compounds to determine that oxidation begins at the electron-rich hard segment methylene bridge, followed by the electron-rich ether soft segment, and finally resulted in the release of the electron-poor polyester soft segment as the final product. This work establishes that a complex polymer can be sequentially electrodegraded based on electrochemical properties of the individual segments.

papers.title: Synthesis, structure and time-resolved studies of the stability of multimetallic LaBO3 perovskites in acid
papers.abstract: Lanthanum-based perovskite oxides with formula LaBO3 are promising functional materials. Interestingly, their physicochemical properties can be tuned through compositional engineering of the B-site in the structure. While extensive research has focused on tailoring these materials for applications such as catalysis and energy conversion, the influence of the composition on phase formation and chemical stability remains poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate the synthesis, crystal structure, and acid stability of a series of La-based perovskites containing one, two, three, or five transition metals on the B-site, including Fe, Co, Ni, Cr, and Mn. Pure Fe-containing perovskite takes an orthorhombic structure, whereas all other single-phase perovskites adopt a rhombohedral phase, including the high-entropy La(CrMnFeCoNi)O3 composition. Co-containing samples exhibited larger crystallite sizes than Nicontaining analogues. The chemical stability of the perovskites was investigated by exposing the materials to an acidic solution and monitoring the degradation process using time-resolved X-ray total scattering and pair distribution function analysis. The results reveal that acid stability is primarily governed by the Fe content on the B-site. Compositions containing more than 50% Fe remained resistant to dissolution under the investigated conditions, whereas lower Fe contents led to progressive structural degradation. For compositions that dissolved completely, distinct crystallite sizes resulted in different dissolution behaviours, highlighting the additional role of microstructure in controlling chemical durability. No intermediate crystalline or amorphous phases were detected, indicating a direct dissolution pathway. PDF analysis further revealed the progressive leaching of La and transition metal cations into solution during degradation. These findings establish composition–structure–stability relationships in La-based perovskites and provide design principles for improving the chemical durability of compositionally complex oxide materials under acidic conditions.

papers.title: Low-Threshold Red Lasing in Diketopyrrolopyrrole-based Organic Semiconductor Films
papers.abstract: Achieving low-lasing threshold organic semiconductor lasers (OSLs) in the red to deep-red region remains challenging due to the intrinsic trade-off between long-wavelength emission and high optical gain. Extended π-conjugation required for red-shifted emission typically enhances non-radiative decay and aggregation-induced quenching, resulting in reduced radiative rate constants (kr) and increased lasing thresholds (Eth). Here, we report molecular design strategies based on a diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) scaffold that independently address high radiative decay and advanced molecular orientation control aimed at low-threshold red OSLs. For solution-processed architectures, donor rigidification using hexamethylazatriangulene (HMAT) combined with DPP cores enables precise modulation of excited-state dynamics, suppressing non-radiative pathways while maintaining high oscillator strength. This strategy affords efficient deep-red emission and reduced lasing thresholds in distributed feedback (DFB) structures. Further, a miniaturized DPP framework with improved thermal evaporation compatibility enables stable vacuum deposition and promotes preferential horizontal molecular orientation, leading to efficient red DFB lasing with low thresholds. These results establish complementary molecular design strategies for controlling the photophysical properties and molecular orientation of DPP-based gain media, providing a versatile platform for low-threshold red OSLs across both solution-processed and vacuum-deposited architectures.

papers.title: Can continuum-solvated DFT resolve the bisulfite protonation-isomer equilibrium? A quantitative benchmark of S- and O-protonated HSO3
papers.abstract: The aqueous bisulfite anion supports experimentally established S- and O-protonated isomers whose relative populations vary with temperature, making the pair a compact test of solution-phase electronic-structure methods. We carried out 46 independent Q-Chem 6.2 calculations spanning conformer generation, B3LYP, PBE0 and ωB97X-D, diffuse double-, triple- and quadruple-ζ basis sets, SMD and PCM water, gas-phase controls, frequency calculations and temperature-dependent thermochemistry. Four S-protonated starts collapsed to one minimum within 0.035 kcal mol-1, whereas four O-protonated starts formed a 0.412 kcal mol-1 manifold. At B3LYP/def2-SVPD/SMD, the O-protonated minimum was 12.11 kcal mol-1 lower in electronic energy, but a def2-TZVPD single-point comparison on the selected minima inverted the ordering to +0.641 kcal mol-1, favoring the S-protonated isomer. Energy decomposition localized the 12.75 kcal mol-1 basis shift almost entirely to the intrinsic electronic term; the differential SMD polarization remained near −5.46 kcal mol-1. def2-QZVPD changed the O−S gap by only 0.008 kcal mol-1 for B3LYP, 0.016 for PBE0 and −0.073 for ωB97X-D, establishing triple-ζ convergence. Combining the basis-converged B3LYP electronic energy with validated qRRHO corrections gave ΔG298 = −0.473 kcal mol-1 and Qi = 2.22, close to the experimental Qi = 2.67. However, experiment decreases from Qi = 3.31 at 278 K to 1.63 at 358 K, whereas the calculation increases from 2.03 to 2.54. The associated effective enthalpy changes sign, from −1.746 kcal mol-1 experimentally to +0.550 kcal mol-1 computationally. Continuum-solvated DFT can therefore reproduce the room-temperature equilibrium fortuitously while failing the more stringent temperature-dependent benchmark.

papers.title: VisXAI: Structure-Mapped Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Molecular Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Background. Molecular machine-learning models use representations such as fingerprints, tokenized simplified molecular input line entry system (SMILES) strings, and molecular graphs. Explanation methods then return importance values for fingerprint bits, sequence tokens, graph nodes, or graph edges. These values must then be mapped to atoms and bonds. This mapping depends on the representation and is often implemented separately for each model. Results. We present VisXAI, a modular Python framework for molecular featurization, trainedmodel interfaces, attribution, structural mapping, and visualization. It supports TreeSHAP for Morgan and MACCS fingerprints. For tokenized SMILES models, it supports attention, Integrated Gradients, and Grad-CAM. For PyTorch Geometric graph neural networks, it supports Integrated Gradients and Grad-CAM. Pretrained Hugging Face sequence checkpoints are supported through a tokenizer adapter and model loader. Every pathway produces the same explanation object containing atom and optional bond scores in RDKit index space. Explanations can be rendered as static two-dimensional scalable vector graphics (SVG), compared in a notebook dashboard with shared or per-panel color scales, or explored using a linked molecule/SMILES widget inspired by XSMILES. Six executable notebooks cover the three representation families, pretrained sequence models, interactive comparison, and a logP case study with an exact Crippen reference decomposition. The current source tree defines 619 Python test cases and 44 JavaScript tests, with separate continuous-integration jobs for the Python and widget front ends. Conclusions. VisXAI does not introduce a predictive architecture or attribution algorithm. It provides a tested integration and mapping layer for expressing different types of molecular explanations in the same chemical coordinates. The framework supports model analysis, method comparison, and reproducible molecular-XAI workflows without requiring separate mapping and visualization code for each representation.

papers.title: Laser-engineered Crystalline Rutile-Type Iridium-Tantalum Oxide with Enhanced OER Activity and Stability
papers.abstract: Ir-M mixed-metal oxides with M = Ti, Nb, and Ta offer a route to reduce the use of scarce Ir while balancing activity and stability for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). However, conventional preparation routes yield either poorly controlled, unstable amorphous materials or highly crystalline, phase-separated oxides with low activity. Here, we report sub-3-nm crystalline nanoparticles of rutile-type IrTaOx. Ir selectively absorbs laser light, promoting rapid crystallization and atomic mixing with Ta under non-equilibrium conditions. With only 35 wt% Ir, the catalyst exhibits a mass activity of 449 mA mgIr-1 at 300 mV overpotential and a stability matching that of the most stable commercial IrO2 catalyst. Simulations attributed the stability to stronger Ta–O bonding at the IrO2(110) surface, reinforcing the oxide lattice and raising the energy required to form oxygen vacancies associated with Ir dissolution. This work demonstrates that laser-induced nanoengineering enables otherwise challenging crystalline, phase-homogeneous mixed oxides with improved noble-metal utilization.

papers.title: Mineralogical diversity and internal mixing of dust with carbonaceous particles in wintertime Indo-Gangetic Plain haze
papers.abstract: Wintertime haze in the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP) is driven by biomass burning, fossil fuel combustion, industrial emissions, and resuspended dust, yet the mineralogical diversity of individual dust particles and the physical properties of co-occurring carbonaceous aerosol remain poorly constrained. We characterize the elemental composition of mineral dust particles across seven size-resolved aerosol samples collected in January 2018 in the eastern IGP and investigate the thermal volatility of morphologically distinct carbonaceous particle types and the phase states based on the composition of co-occurring organic aerosol. Single-particle micro-spectroscopy analysis revealed predominantly Si-rich aluminosilicate dust substantially internally mixed with carbonaceous material, alongside an episodic enhancement of low-Si, low-Ca Fe-rich particles inconsistent with fly ash and suggestive of local Fe-oxide mineral sources. Microscopic imaging with in-situ heating showed that highly viscous tar balls were the least volatile, while low-viscosity particles with crystalline K-sulfate inclusions showed intermediate volatility, reflecting the thermal lability of inorganic sulfate phases. Furthermore, glass transition temperature estimates from high-resolution mass spectrometry analysis indicated that morning organic aerosol existed predominantly in semi-solid to solid phase states, shifting to semi-solid to liquid in the afternoon as relative humidity increased from 43% to 78%. These results highlight the mineralogical heterogeneity of IGP dust, the role of internal mixing in governing particle volatility, and the strong sensitivity of organic aerosol phase state to ambient humidity in this heavily polluted wintertime environment.

papers.title: Fragment-Grounded Neural Simulation of Electron Ionization Mass Spectra at Library Scale
papers.abstract: Electron ionization mass spectrometry (EI-MS) is a sensitive, reproducible analytical technique, yet compound identification conventionally relies on reference databases that capture only a fraction of accessible chemical space. In silico prediction of EI-MS spectra can extend these libraries, but existing data-driven models generalize poorly beyond their training distribution, and physics-based simulations are too costly for library-scale use. Here, we present a fragment-grounded neural workflow that predicts an EI-MS spectrum by exhaustively enumerating the fragmentation graph of a molecule and then assigning intensities to the resulting substructures. By relating every predicted peak back to a candidate substructure, our model generalizes more reliably to unseen scaffolds and out-of-distribution chemistry than prior fingerprint-and black-box transformer-based predictors. On a scaffold split, it improves top-1 retrieval accuracy from formula-matched compounds by 32% relative to the strongest baseline, and it matches the accuracy of quantum-chemical simulation while being roughly seven orders of magnitude faster. To test the model’s capabilities under a harder, formula-agnostic setting, we further evaluate retrieval against a library of 87.3 million compounds from

papers.title: Peptide-Based Coacervates for Stimuli-Responsive Drug Delivery: Design, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers.abstract: Peptide-based coacervates have emerged as a versatile platform for stimuli-responsive drug delivery, leveraging their unique physicochemical properties and dynamic phase behaviour. These coacervates, formed through liquid-liquid phase separation of peptide sequences, offer tunable encapsulation and release, making them promising candidates for biomedical applications. This review explores the fundamental principles governing peptide coacervation, emphasizing the impact of both endogenous and exogenous stimulus such as pH, temperature, redox conditions, metal ions, magnetic fields, enzymes and light on the coacervation process and how this can be harnessed for drug delivery applications. Special attention is given to the molecular design strategies that enhance the responsiveness of peptide-based coacervates, including sequence modifications, incorporation of non-canonical amino acids, and conjugation with functional moieties. Additionally, we discuss recent advancements in the synthesis and characterization of these materials, highlighting their potential in gene therapy, cancer treatment, and regenerative medicine. Finally we give an outlook to future-possibilities and remaining challenges for the use of this promising platform for next-generation therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Site-Resolved Prediction of Mayr Nucleophilicity with Reactivity-Pretrained Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Nucleophilicity is a key kinetic descriptor for understanding organic reaction mechanisms and guiding reaction design. However, existing machine-learning models typically predict Mayr nucleophilicity at the whole-molecule level without identifying the experimentally relevant reaction site. Herein, we develop a P retrained and P hysicochemical feature-augmented G raph neural network model for joint N ucleophilicity and S ite prediction (PPGNS) for site-resolved Mayr N prediction. PPGNS integrates curated experimental reaction-site annotations, explicit-H molecular graphs, lightweight GFN1-xTB electronic descriptors, and reactivity-oriented pretraining incorporating methyl cation affinity. In connectivity-disjoint five-fold out-of-fold evaluation, PPGNS achieved R 2 of 0.937 and 0.950 and MAEs of 1.22 and 1.15 N units for automatic- and known-site prediction, respectively, together with 93% Top-1 and 98% Top-3 site recovery. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified local electronic descriptors as the dominant model attributions. PPGNS therefore enables simultaneous prediction of where nucleophilic reactivity resides and how strong it is.

papers.title: ALIGNing Learned Representations: Domain-General Models Triangulate Physicochemical Interactions in Analytical Separations
papers.abstract: Despite rapid progress, foundation models for chemistry have yet to consistently deliver broadly transferable, experiment-grounded representations for structure-to-measurement tasks in practice. This reflects both the scarcity and fragmentation of experimental datasets and the weak alignment between common molecular representations (e.g., SMILES and graphs) and measured chemical behaviour. Here, we formalize domain-general models: pretrained models constrained across multiple measurement contexts within a physically coherent domain to learn transferable chemical representations that capture how molecular structure gives rise to experimental observables. Using liquid chromatography as a testbed, we develop ALIGN and show that it outperforms conventional baselines, including foundation models and transfer learning approaches, across diverse chromatographic contexts while retaining performance in data-limited and chemically out-of-distribution settings. By training across multiple chromatographic methods, ALIGN triangulates an underlying physicochemical interaction space, with each method providing a complementary projection that constrains the learned representation. We show that ALIGN learns embeddings consistent with physicochemical properties and chromatographic principles and provide evidence for a mechanism underlying improved method-specific adaptation. These representations transfer to related analytical modalities, including GC, CCS, and DMS, suggesting that these measurements encode overlapping physicochemical relationships. Together, these results demonstrate the value of physically grounded representation learning and suggest that domain-general approaches may extend to other fragmented scientific domains.

papers.title: Geometry-Dependent Redistribution of Exocytotic Spike-Shape Populations Revealed by Ultrafast Disk and Nanotip Acetylcholine Biosensors
papers.abstract: Measurements of sub-millisecond acetylcholine (ACh) exocytosis have only recently become possible through the development of ultrafast electrochemical ACh biosensors. These biosensors convert transient presynaptic ACh release events into sub-millisecond amperometric spikes that can be analyzed at the single-event level. Although both disk and nanotip electrode geometries have been incorporated into ultrafast ACh biosensors, it remains unclear whether sensor geometry influences quantal measurements and the observed distribution of exocytotic spike shapes. Amperometric recordings were obtained from single cholinergic cells and analyzed using a spike-shape classification system consisting of eight distinct event categories, including low sharp, high sharp, increasing, decreasing, plateau, high spike, overlap, and funky events. Although disk and nanotip biosensors produced comparable estimates of vesicular release content and global spike kinetics, detailed spike-shape classification revealed a geometry-dependent redistribution of the detected exocytotic event populations. Nanotip biosensors detected a significantly higher proportion of high sharp events and lower proportions of morphologically more complex full-release events and overlap events than disk biosensors. The reduction in complex full-release events was not driven by a single subtype but instead reflected distributed changes across multiple event categories. These findings demonstrate that electrode geometry can influence the apparent composition of the detected exocytotic spike populations without substantially altering estimates of vesicular release content or global spike kinetics. The results provide new insights into how nanoscale sensor geometry shapes electrochemical observations of neurotransmitter release and highlights the importance of considering biosensor geometry when interpreting single-cell exocytosis measurements.

papers.title: From Signals to Measurands: A Measurement-Science Roadmap for Reproducible Analytical Biochemistry
papers.abstract: Analytical biochemistry often reports kinetic or binding constants as though they were observed directly. Each result is instead inferred from an instrumental signal. Calibration establishes the scale, biochemical and observation models connect the signal to a target, and statistical analysis produces the estimate and its uncertainty. This Perspective treats reproducibility as the recovery of a specified measurand, with an uncertainty statement, through an auditable measurement chain. A Michaelis-Menten substrate-depletion example provides the organizing case. Two progress-curve experiments generated with the same parameters and noise model both fit well, yet only the design that samples substrate concentrations around the Michaelis constant yields a bounded interval for, K M . In that design, uncertainty in active-site concentration dominates the uncertainty of, k cat , even though the curve fit is precise. Ligand--receptor binding shows parallel effects of depletion, signal modeling, and parameter confounding. The framework connects established metrological and chemical-measurement concepts with enzymology reporting standards, machine-readable data formats, and modern identifiability analysis. It distinguishes repeatability, transfer to another laboratory, and agreement across independent measurement routes (or techniques), and explains what interlaboratory studies can reveal. The recommendations are prioritized as minimum practice, stronger support for parameter estimation, and reference-grade validation. The same logic applies whenever a biochemical quantity is inferred from a measured signal.

papers.title: Seamless QM/MM simulations via a GROMACS–CP2K interface
papers.abstract: Understanding and controlling chemical reactivity in biological systems requires atomic-level insight into processes that are often inaccessible to experiments. Hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations provide a powerful framework to describe chemical reactions in complex environments, but their practical application remains limited by fragmented software ecosystems, restricted accessibility, and methodological approximations that can compromise accuracy and reproducibility. In particular, many existing QM/MM implementations rely on ad hoc couplings, proprietary software, or truncated treatments of long-range electrostatic interactions. Here, we present a robust and fully periodic QM/MM interface between the open-source molecular dynamics engine GROMACS and the electronic structure theory code CP2K. The implementation enables efficient and reproducible QM/MM molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling simulations with a consistent treatment of long-range electrostatics under periodic boundary conditions. By combining the strengths of two widely used community codes, this interface provides a general and scalable platform for studying

papers.title: Proton-Donor Identity Shapes Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Nitrite on Silver
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction is a key reaction in sustainable nitrogen cycling and water remediation, yet the mechanistic interpretation of its voltammetric response remains poorly understood. On silver electrodes, cyclic voltammograms often display multiple cathodic features assigned to different reaction steps, although a consistent mechanistic interpretation remains elusive. Here, we combine cyclic voltammetry analysis with in-situ product detection using scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM), and hydrodynamic analysis using rotating disk electrode (RDE), to investigate nitrate-to-nitrite electroreduction on silver. We show that the cathodic response changes from a single peak to two distinct features with increasing nitrate concentration when using phosphate buffer as supporting electrolyte. Analysis of concentration, scan rate, and pH dependencies, together with systematic variation of phosphate electrolyte composition, indicates that these features arise from distinct interfacial proton-transfer regimes associated with the availability of H 2 PO 4- as a proton donor. In addition, SECM enables the assignment of each feature to local nitrite formation, ruling out changes in product identity as the origin of each feature. These findings show that phosphate electrolyte modulates proton-donor availability, and, consequently, the voltammetric response of nitrate reduction on silver, providing a framework for interpreting the complex electrocatalytic behavior observed in this system.

papers.title: Competition-Derived Relative Reactivity and 3D Electronic-State Analysis of Site- and Facial Selectivity in NaBH4/MeOH Ketone Reductions
papers.abstract: Yield-based measures of reactivity can be distorted by side reactions and reaction conditions and therefore may not accurately reflect intrinsic reaction rates. In this study, competition experiments, in which two substrates react simultaneously with the same reagent, were used to build a unified kinetic scale for the reduction of ketones by sodium borohydride (NaBH 4 ) in methanol, expressed as activation free energy differences (ΔΔ G‡ ). Kinetic data for 89 structurally diverse ketone reaction faces tracked substituent electronic effects and steric congestion, and transition-state calculations identified methanolysis as the step that determines the identity of the active reductant. A Lasso model trained on 83 of these reaction faces with three-dimensional electron-density, electrostatic-potential, and carbonyl-centered projected C=O π * descriptors achieved R 2 = 0.804 under strict nested outer leave-one-out cross-validation. The monoketone-derived model recovers the dominant site and face for every diketone examined, with 85.5% of the cross-validation models reproducing all assignments; however, the predicted product distributions are indicative rather than quantitative. The workflow integrates a yield-independent kinetic scale with experimental measurements, theoretical calculations, and data-driven analyses within the evaluated NaBH 4 /MeOH domain and provides a basis for testing broader applicability through reaction-specific data, retraining, and validation.

papers.title: Numerical simulation-guided development of dynamic kinetic resolution reactions
papers.abstract: Dynamic kinetic resolution is attractive for efficiently converting racemic substrates into enantioenriched products; however, its development remains challenging because product optical purity depends on both catalyst stereoselectivity and reaction conditions, often giving rise to pseudo-selectivity that confounds stereoselectivity assessment and complicates condition optimization. Based on numerical simulations, we show that the stereochemical outcome of DKR reactions can be described by four physically meaningful dimensionless composite parameters, which clarify how catalyst properties and reaction conditions jointly determine reaction behavior. This analysis further reveals that eeinit (initial ee measured within a low-conversion window) is governed primarily by catalyst stereoselectivity and is largely insensitive to reaction conditions, enabling more reliable characterization of a catalyst’s intrinsic stereoselectivity. After catalyst selection, the findings also guide reaction optimization by matching the catalyst with appropriate reaction conditions to maximize overall reaction performance. The practical utility of this approach is demonstrated through two preparative-scale syntheses.

papers.title: When Do Models Win? A Learning Curve Benchmark for Molecular Property Prediction in Low-Data Regimes
papers.abstract: In molecular property prediction, labeled data are often limited to tens to thousands of samples, yet it remains unclear which model classes are most effective in these low-data regimes and how their ranking evolves with data size. We present a learning-curve benchmark spanning traditional machine learning, graph neural networks, transformer-based molecular language models, rotationally equivariant and SE(3)-invariant 3D networks, descriptor-based hybrids, multi-task learning variants, and graph–sequence fusion baselines. Training size is varied from 50 to 3,000 samples, with dataset-dependent maxima, on QM9, ESOL, Lipophilicity, and BACE under scaffold splits with repeated trials. Four patterns emerge. (1) Model optimality is regime-dependent: deep learning leads continuous physicochemical properties (ESOL, Lipophilicity) while Gaussian Process Regression leads bioactivity (BACE) across most of the range, with clear traditional-versus-deep-learning crossovers. (2) The benefit of 3D inductive bias is target-dependent: on QM9 an equivariant 3D network trained on DFT geometries is strong on LUMO and the HOMO–LUMO gap but weak on HOMO, although all three targets use the same DFT-optimized geometries; single-conformer ETKDG inputs instead give near-flat curves on Lipophilicity and BACE. (3) Pretraining chiefly raises the low-data floor rather than the mean. Its advantage concentrates where no single model dominates, typically at intermediate sizes, and its clearest effect is on worst-case accuracy: in a matched Uni-Mol pair, pretraining lifts the minimum QM9 R² at N≤200 by approximately 0.6 on every target. Neither parameter count nor pretraining-corpus size predicts the ranking — the compact ChemBERTa-2 (3.4M parameters) outperforms the far larger MoLFormer (44.5M) and SELFormer (86.8M) on ESOL, yet the ordering reverses on the other datasets. (4) Under data scarcity, model selection beats averaging: even oracle ensembles barely improve on the best single model at the smallest sizes (at most +1.2% in RMSE at N=50, and negative on ESOL). Together these results give data-scale-aware guidelines for model selection and establish learning-curve analysis as a principled tool for characterizing model behavior across the property–scale plane. Scientific Contribution: This study establishes a comprehensive learning-curve benchmark for molecular property prediction in low-data regimes, comparing a broad suite of model families across four datasets spanning physicochemical, quantum-mechanical, and bioactivity properties. It shows that the best-performing model family is jointly determined by data scale and target type — including reproducible crossovers between traditional machine learning and deep learning — and converts these findings into actionable, data-scale-aware model-selection guidelines.

papers.title: Substrate-adaptive reaction development enables modular access to functionalized activated olefins
papers.abstract: The decarboxylative olefination of aldehydes with malonic acid derivatives offers a mild and modular route to activated olefins, allowing the β-substituent, α-substituent and carbonyl-derived activating group to be varied independently. However, this modularity has not been realized within a unified framework: Existing methods remain fragmented across individual carbonyl classes and are dominated by αunsubstituted products, while access to α-heteroatom-substituted olefins, particularly α-halo derivatives, remains poorly developed. Moreover, these methods provide little guidance for adapting the reaction to new or challenging substrates. Consequently, despite its attractive features, decarboxylative olefination remains underutilized relative to established methods such as the Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons reaction. Here, we develop a unified, substrate-adaptive platform for the synthesis of functionalized activated olefins. Rather than optimizing a single model reaction and applying the resulting conditions across a fixed substrate scope, we used Bayesian optimization across representative substrate pairs to generate a compact, information-rich reaction-development dataset. This dataset was then used directly as prior knowledge for active transfer learning, enabling the identification of tailored, high-yielding conditions for new substrate combinations and complex targets with minimal additional experimentation. The resulting workflow provides access to α,β-unsaturated thioesters, esters and amides, substantially expands the scope of α-functionalized olefins and identifies effective conditions for substrates that were limitations of previous fixed-condition substrate scopes. More broadly, this study demonstrates that reactiondevelopment datasets can serve as transferable reaction knowledge, enabling efficient substrate-adaptive optimization and accelerating the maturation of emerging synthetic methods into practically general transformations.

papers.title: DeepHeal: An Interpretable Framework for Phenotype-Based Antineoplastic Drug Discovery Using Drug-Perturbation Proteomics
papers.abstract: Drug-perturbation proteomics provides a direct molecular readout of compound-induced cellular states, but its high dimensionality and limited interpretability hinder its use for mechanism-oriented drug discovery. Here, we present DeepHeal, an interpretable consensus representation framework that transforms drug-induced proteomic responses into biologically readable and experimentally actionable antineoplastic response programs. Using an HCT116 perturbation atlas comprising 875 compounds and 9,960 protein features, DeepHeal integrates ensemble variational autoencoders, supervised contrastive learning, consensus latent-variable aggregation, and protein-level attribution. A label-independent Average branch captures recurrent proteomic variation, whereas a complementary label-aware SupCon branch concentrates known antineoplastic structure. The resulting latent programs are mapped back to proteins, pathways, and interaction networks, revealing shared cell-cycle, DNA-replication, stress-response, metabolic, proteostasis, apoptosis-related programs, together with mechanism-dependent response heterogeneity. DeepHeal prioritized 19 initially unlabeled compounds for experimental follow-up, of which seven inhibited HCT116 cells with IC₅₀ values below 10 μM, including two compounds with nanomolar activity. Without retraining, DeepHeal representations further recovered antineoplastic response states across 566 external proteomic perturbation profiles spanning multiple cellular contexts. Together, these findings establish DeepHeal as, to our knowledge, the first proteomics-first interpretable consensus representation framework that transforms large-scale drug-perturbation proteomes into protein- and pathway-resolved response programs for cross-context anticancer candidate prioritization and experimental validation.

papers.title: Probing VOC Capture and Sensing in BN-Engineered Quasi-2D FullereneMonolayers: First-Principles Insights
papers.abstract: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to investigate the adsorption behaviour of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) on pristine and BN-doped quasi-two-dimensional C60 fullerene sheets. Three systems-pure C60 , single BN-pair doped (C58 B1 N1 ), and multi-pair doped (C50 B5 N5 )-were examined to evaluate structural stability, electronic modulation, adsorption energetics, sensitivity, work-function variation, and recovery time. Results show that single BN-pair substitution significantly enhances adsorption and sensing performance compared to pristine C60 . Among the studied VOCs, formaldehyde (HCHO) exhibits the strongest interaction with C58 B1 N1 , with an adsorption energy of -0.47 eV, accompanied by a substantial band gap reduction (1.08 →0.20 eV) and enhanced electrical conductivity at 300 K. Sensitivity is markedly improved upon single BN doping, reaching 7.51 for CH3 OH and 4.41 for HCHO, whereas pristine C60 shows comparatively lower responses (maximum S ∼ 1.88). Work-function modulation (4.42-4.99 eV) further indicates strong surface electronic perturbation, supporting its suitability for chemiresistive and work-function-based sensing mechanisms. Recovery-time analysis reveals fast desorption for pristine C60 (0.05-3.36 s), while stronger chemisorption on C58 B1 N1 results in longer recovery times for highly polar molecules. In contrast, excessive BN incorporation (C50 B5 N5 ) leads to unfavourable adsorption and poor sensitivity. Overall, controlled single BN-pair doping effectively optimizes selectivity and sensitivity toward polar VOCs, establishing BN-engineered fullerene monolayers as promising platforms for environmental monitoring applications.

papers.title: Simulating Catalytic Resonance with Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Static heterogeneous catalysts are constrained by the Sabatier principle, where their overall turnover is limited by balancing the kinetics of reactant binding, surface reaction, and product unbinding. Modulating the surface binding energies between a strong binding state and a weak binding state can overcome this limit. For such a dynamic catalyst, a maximum turnover is achieved at a catalytic resonance modulating frequency. Here we demonstrate that classical molecular simulation approaches can be used to study this phenomena. Our method introduces a generic classical model for a surface reaction with time-dependent surface binding energy. Using a non-equilibrium molecular simulation in which reactants tend to be added to the system and products tend to be removed, we can simulate many catalyst cycles. Our approach reproduces catalytic resonance, with the dynamic catalyst providing up to a three-order-of-magnitude boost in turnover compared to the static catalyst. We further demonstrate the presence of a second resonant frequency in the gas phase, associated with resonance of the reacting bond. The general approach outlined here can be extended to more detailed models and used to study the molecular-scale effects of surface modulation and to computationally test input frequency, amplitude, and waveform for programmable catalysts.

papers.title: Aqueous Phase Reforming of Model HTL Wastewater with Pt/C and Ru/C Catalysts
papers.abstract: Aqueous Phase Reforming (APR) was conducted at a temperature of 225 °C, a pressure of 450 psi, and with two catalysts: 5 wt.% platinum and 5 wt.% ruthenium supported on active carbon. Single- and multi-component surrogate feedstocks consisting of acetic acid, acetone, ethanol, glycerol, succinic acid, and N-methylacetamide were tested to compare the two catalysts. Among the catalysts, the ruthenium catalyst consistently outperformed the platinum catalyst, achieving hydrogen yields of 77-100% compared to 44-54% with platinum for multi-component feedstocks. The wastewater resulting from the Hydrothermal Liquefaction (HTL) of Municipal Sewage Sludge (MSS) was tested at 225 and 250 °C, and at 450 and 650 psi. Results demonstrated that while hydrogen can be produced from MSS-HTL wastewater using a ruthenium catalyst supported on carbon, catalyst deactivation was severe. Future work is suggested to investigate methods to prevent catalyst deactivation due to carbonaceous solid deposition.

papers.title: Regiodivergent Biocatalytic Rearrangement of Indoles: Enantioselective Access to 2- and 3-Oxindoles Bearing Quaternary Stereocenters
papers.abstract: Chiral oxindoles bearing a quaternary stereocenter are prevalent scaffolds across a wide range of biologically active natural products and pharmaceutical agents, yet their enantioselective synthesis via oxidative 1,2-shift reactions remains largely underdeveloped, particularly within the realm of biocatalysis. Herein, we report the first biocatalytic asymmetric semipinacol-type rearrangement of indoles with C–C bond migration, mediated by engineered flavin-dependent styrene monooxygenases (StyAs), enabling the enantioselective synthesis of both 3,3-dialkyl-substituted 2-oxindoles and 2,2-dialkyl-substituted 3-oxindoles. Screening of an extensive library of flavin-dependent monooxygenases, comprising wild-type StyAs, Pseudomonas StyA variants and Baeyer-Villiger monooxygenases, against a pyrano-[2,3]-fused indole model substrate identified the double mutant PsStyA-Q4 (V48N/Y73V) as the optimal biocatalyst, delivering the (R)-configured spiro-2-oxindole with up to full conversion and excellent enantioselectivity (>99% ee) under mild aqueous conditions. Substrate scope evaluation confirmed broad generality across methyl- and halogen-substituted indoles, while a set of 3-allyl- and 3-benzyl-substituted indoles, converted by PsStyA-Q4 or wild-type SwStyA, gave access to the complementary 2,2-dialkyl-3-oxindole scaffold with equally excellent enantiocontrol. Quantum chemical calculations suggest that both substrate classes share the same intrinsic migratory preference, so that the exclusive formation of spiro-2oxindoles from the pyrano-fused indoles cannot be traced back to substrate control alone. These observations indicate that the styrene monooxygenases exert control not merely over the initial oxygen transfer, but throughout the rearrangement itself.

papers.title: Humidity-Controlled Inverse Gas Chromatography for Preserving the Adsorption-Relevant Surface State of Dehydration-Sensitive Pharmaceutical Hydrates
papers.abstract: p. 2 Abstract Preservation of the adsorption-relevant surface state is critical for meaningful surface characterization of dehydration-sensitive pharmaceutical hydrates, because changes in hydration and surface structure may occur during sample preparation and measurement. Previous studies have demonstrated that humidity-controlled inverse gas chromatography (IGC) can prevent bulk hydrate-to-anhydrate phase transformation during specific surface area measurement. However, preservation of the bulk crystalline phase does not necessarily ensure preservation of the adsorption-relevant surface state. In this study, humidity-controlled IGC was investigated as a means of maintaining the hydration environment during surface characterization of three pharmaceutical hydrate systems: sodium saccharin dihydrate, L-cysteine hydrochloride monohydrate, and citric acid monohydrate. Hydration behavior was characterized by dynamic vapor sorption, and changes in particle morphology were examined by optical microscopy. IGC measurements were performed under controlled relative humidity using n-nonane as an adsorption probe, and BET analysis was used to estimate the probe-accessible surface area under the specified measurement conditions. The applicability of the IGC-based approach was supported by measurements of the reference material BCR-170, for which the obtained surface area was consistent with the certified value. Importantly, the adsorption-derived surface area was found to depend on sample history and elapsed time even under humidity conditions selected to maintain the hydrate state. In L-cysteine hydrochloride monohydrate, the apparent surface area decreased from 0.43 to 0.30 m2 g-1 after storage following sieving, accompanied by a substantial decrease in column pressure drop. These findings suggest that preservation of the hydrate phase alone does not ensure preservation of the adsorption-relevant surface state. Humidity-controlled IGC provides a useful approach for evaluating probe-accessible surface behavior of dehydration-sensitive pharmaceutical hydrates while minimizing perturbation of their hydration environment.

papers.title: Comparative assessment of Au- and Ag-based SERS substrates for cancer and disease diagnosis: A review on analytical performance, reproducibility, and practical challenges
papers.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), which provides ultrasensitive and molecular fingerprint analysis, has emerged as a potent analytical method for biological applications. SERS achieves signal enhancements on the order of 106 to 1015 by utilizing localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) in noble metal nanoparticles, primarily gold (Au) and silver (Ag), and exhibits a femtomolar or attomolar detection limit. Developments in surface chemistry and fabrication techniques have made it easier to create a variety of plasmonic substrates, such as core-shell nanoparticles, nanowires, nanostars, and bimetallic alloys, all of which are optimized for chemical and electromagnetic enhancement. The development of Au and Ag nanoparticle-based SERS platforms and their uses in biological sensing are evaluated critically in this review, with an emphasis on development in diabetes monitoring, pathogen identification, cancer diagnostics, and biomarker detection. Reproducibility, substrate stability, and in vivo translation still present difficulties despite these developments. New strategies for overcoming these obstacles include biocompatible coatings, microfluidic integration, and spectral analysis aided by machine learning. We describe the potential uses of SERS in point-of-care and clinical diagnostics in the future, highlighting the necessity of quantitative, scalable, and repeatable sensing platforms.

papers.title: Ab Initio Potential Energy Surface, Quantum Close-Coupling Scattering, and Transport Properties of the Au–N2 van der Waals Complex
papers.abstract: We present a first-principles characterization of the neutral Au–N 2 van der Waals complex, connecting ab initio electronic structure through quantum close-coupling scattering to macroscopic transport properties, bound rovibrational states, and the second virial coefficient. The two-dimensional rigid-rotor potential energy surface, computed at the UCCSD(T) level with a 60-electron effective core potential for Au, was obtained from a dense (R,θ) ab initio grid subjected to systematic outlier removal: a short-range (R ≲ 3–5 Å, angledependent) discontinuous branch, roughly two orders of magnitude deeper than the surrounding physical surface, was identified and excluded following diagnosis as a likely single-reference electronic-structure artifact, together with a smaller population of isolated numerical outliers. The resulting physical surface has a global well depth of −104.9 cm −1 , 1.5–3 times deeper than the isoelectronic neutral Ag–N 2 complex depending on orientation, consistent with gold’s larger polarizability and stronger relativistic effects. Full close-coupling scattering calculations show that Au–N 2 requires roughly twice the partial waves of Ag–N 2 to converge at equal collision energy, a direct, quantified consequence of the deeper well. Generalized Senftleben–Beenakker cross sections, computed at six collision energies spanning 20–500 cm −1 using a corrected channel-filtering procedure for energies at which some rotational levels are energetically closed, were thermally averaged via calibrated Chapman–Enskog theory to yield diffusion coefficients and viscosity for Au dilute in N 2 buffer gas. Twenty five converged bound rovibrational levels were located across three (J tot , parity) blocks, a richer progression than Ag–N 2 consistent with the deeper well, though the deepest few levels per block did not converge, a documented numerical limitation attributed to short-range potential extrapolation rather than a physical finding. The second virial coefficient remains negative throughout the tested range up to 1000 K, indicating a substantially higher Boyle temperature than neutral Ag–N 2 (370 K). Comparison with the isoelectronic Ag–N 2 system, and with prior close-coupling studies of the related Na–N 2 and Ag–N 2 systems, provides both physical-consistency checks and a quantitative picture of how relativistic and polarizability effects scale across this coinage-metal pair. To our knowledge, these constitute the first reported potential energy surface, scattering calculations, and transport properties for the Au–N 2 complex.

papers.title: Diiron Complexes Display Potent Antiproliferative Activity and Synergize with Lenalidomide in Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma
papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common subtype of aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) and remains a clinical challenge in patients with relapsed/refractory disease, despite treatment with lenalidomide- or oxaliplatin-based regimens. Herein, we report on the development of new tailored organometallic complexes evaluated against DLBCL cells as single agents and in combination with lenalidomide. The tailored diiron(I) complexes [Fe2Cp2(CO)(µ-CO){µ-η1:η3-C(R’)CHC=NMe(Ind)}]CF3SO3 [R’ = n-pentyl, 2a; R’ = SiMe3, 2b; Cp = h5-C5H5, Ind = 5-(1H-indolyl)] were synthesized in 69-88% yields, and fully characterized by elemental analysis, IR and NMR spectroscopy and, for 2a, by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The complexes showed adequate aqueous solubility (≈ 10-4 M), balanced hydrophilic/lipophilic character (Log Pow = 0.73 and 0.31) and significant stability in aqueous media, with 90–93% and 73–81% of 2a and 2b, respectively, remaining intact after 72 h in D2O/DMSO-d6 and DMEM-d/DMSO-d6 mixtures at 37 °C. Complexes 2a-b strongly inhibited cell proliferation in SU-DHL10, OCI-LY3 and Toledo DLBCL cell lines after 72 h of exposure; 2a and 2b were substantially more potent than oxaliplatin and lenalidomide, particularly in SU-DHL10 and OCI-LY3 cells, with IC50 values up to 22-fold lower than those of oxaliplatin. Combined treatment with lenalidomide and the diiron complexes, particularly 2a, resulted in strong synergism across almost the entire range of affected fractions (combination index < 1) and dose reduction indices as high as 347 in OCI-LY3 cells. Overall, these findings identify an emerging class of organo-diiron complexes as promising candidates for combination-based therapeutic strategies against DLBCL, warranting further preclinical investigation.

papers.title: Avidity by Design: Scalable Programmed Synthesis of Bivalent DNA-Encoded Libraries for Enhanced Selection Sensitivity
papers.abstract: DNA Encoded Libraries (DELs) are used for finding small molecule binders to proteins and other targets of pharmaceutical interest. DELs tether small molecules made by combinatorial chemistry to DNA oligos whose sequences identify the molecules to which they are tethered. DEL selections, or screens, typically separate binders from non-binders and use sequencing to discern binder structures. Typically, selection methods more efficiently capture tighter binders than weaker ones. There are two key reasons why DEL selections may return very few, or no binders. One is the presence of only a few binders in the library (or none); less appreciated is the case where there are true binders, but the selection protocol lacks the sensitivity to capture them. We report in our “Theoretical Analysis of Bivalent Binding Avidity and Kinetics: Implications for DNA-Encoded Libraries” that through an avidity effect bivalent DELs increase the sensitivity of selections and capture more and weaker binders than their cognate monovalent counterparts. Here, we present our development of the means to efficiently build bivalent DELs.

papers.title: Structure–Performance Relationships in Newly Designed Linear Polyamines for Advanced CO2 Sorption
papers.abstract: Establishing structure–performance relationships is key to designing next‑generation CO2 sorbents with high efficiency and durability. This study investigates two newly designed linear polyamines, poly(hexyleneimine) (PHI) and poly(undecyleneimine) (PUI), obtained from polyamide feedstocks and developed as innovative polymer‑based materials for advanced CO2 capture. Their sorption capacity, desorption kinetics and thermal stability were evaluated in unsupported and fumed‑silica‑supported forms to elucidate how backbone architecture and amine spacing govern performance. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed that unsupported PHI and PUI effectively sorb and desorb CO2 at 110°C and 50°C, respectively. Cryo-milling selectively enhanced PUI performance, highlighting the critical influence of molecular architecture on amine site accessibility. Support impregnation significantly improved low-temperature performance: supported PHI achieved a maximum uptake of 1.67 mmol·g-1 at 70°C with an amine efficiency of 0.34, comparable to commercial linear poly(ethyleneimine) (L-PEI), while supported-PUI reached 0.85 mmol·g-1 at 50°C. Both polyamines demonstrated superior resistance to oxidative degradation compared to L-PEI, attributed to their higher density of amine spacers. Overall, PHI and PUI demonstrate how molecular design directly translates/impacts CO2 sorption performance, positioning these linear polyamines as robust, thermally reversible sorbents for advanced carbon‑capture applications.

papers.title: What makes a good photoactive monomer: Insights from excited state analysis
papers.abstract: Ground and excited-state properties of a large number of possible donor-acceptor (D-A) monomer units with applications as photoactive polymers in organic photovoltaics (OPVs) were computed at the density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) levels. The D-A monomers were constructed from a set of building blocks with donor and acceptor character. Their optoelectronic properties were compared with those of the DA monomer unit of the D18 photoactive polymer to assess their potential performance in OPVs. Based on a set of computed excited-state descriptors, we identify D-A combinations that are expected to have a narrow optical gap, strong absorption, and delocalized excitons favorable to charge separation and hole mobility.

papers.title: Green and efficient organocatalytic delignification of woody biomass
papers.abstract: To realize a sustainable society with circular flows of energy and materials, it is crucial to develop eco-friendly methods to isolate valuable chemical components, such as cellulose, from wood, thereby utilizing woody biomass as a renewable resource. We have devised a one-step delignification process using hydrogen peroxide as a green oxidant. This method selectively breaks down and removes lignin while preserving polysaccharides, especially cellulose, at relatively low temperatures (around 60 ̊C). By evaluating various solvents and catalysts, we demonstrate that a biphasic reaction system comprising aqueous hydrogen peroxide and a hydrophobic solvent enables smooth delignification with organosulfonic acid catalysts bearing a hydrophobic substructure, and reduces the use of hydrogen peroxide and acid catalysts compared to conventional approaches.

papers.title: Targeted mitigation strategies for critically polluted PM2.5 regions in India using spatially constrained airsheds
papers.abstract: Air pollution in India is a regional problem, yet the current air quality management policy is largely city-centric. Here, we developed an airshed management framework that emphasizes cooperative action for PM2.5 pollution mitigation. This framework identifies air pollution control areas (APCAs) for targeted emissions control across four critically polluted regions in the Indo-Gangetic Plain by mapping sectoral emissions from administrative units to pollution levels to meet specified air quality targets. We find that the dominant emission sectors differ across APCAs, such as agriculture, transport, and domestic to micro, small and medium-scale industry, highlighting the inadequacy of broad regional airshed management and the need for tailored air quality management plans. This framework yields differentiated policy guidance at the airshed and sub-airshed scales for the districts that constitute an APCA, leading to a spatially fine-tuned and implicitly minimal-effort mitigation plan. The developed framework is generalizable worldwide to polluted regions at any PM2.5 level.

papers.title: Bulk hexagonal diamond remains elusive
papers.abstract: Hexagonal diamond (HD) is an enigmatic polymorph of diamond whose crystal structure, diffraction properties, spectroscopic features and hardness remain controversial. [1–2] This carbon allotrope contains only hexagonal (h) stacking of puckered layers of carbon atoms and displays a complete absence of cubic (c) stacking that is found in the ‘ordinary’ cubic diamond. The use of the mineral name lonsdaleite as a synonym for HD complicates the situation further, despite several studies showing that the type material originally described as lonsdaleite does not represent a discrete phase. Obtaining pure HD would be a step change in diamond research that would resolve many long-standing controversies. A recent study claimed the bulk synthesis of 100-μm to millimeter-sized HD crystals by compressing and heating single-crystal hexagonal graphite. The authors based their identification and structural characterization on in-situ and ex-situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and Raman spectroscopy. They interpreted their data in terms of ~100 nm triple-twinned HD domains. We identified problems with this interpretation and demonstrate that the material is not a highly ordered, pure HD phase, but instead stacking-disordered diamond (SDD) containing both hexagonal and cubic stacking. Our analysis also reveals a new type of intergrowth structure which provides fresh insight into the graphite – HD transition, and may help guide the future synthesis of pure HD.

papers.title: Error Models for Uncertainty Quantification in Molecular Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Molecular property optimization is essential in drug discovery and medicinal chemistry. Machine learning (ML) models have demonstrated successful predictive ability and a certain degree of generalization capabilities to predict several molecular properties, including absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) endpoints. However, quantifying the uncertainty of individual predictions remains a critical challenge. Assessing whether a given prediction is likely to be correct has the potential to fundamentally change how ML-based predictions are used in molecular design. In this work, error models (EMs), which are ML systems trained to predict the error of the primary property models, were systematically developed and analyzed to assess the reliability of property predictions. EMs were shown to discriminate between predictions of varying error levels, highlighting their utility for uncertainty quantification (UQ) and decision-making. Using both proprietary and public datasets covering diverse ADME and physicochemical endpoints, EM-derived uncertainty estimates outperformed standard UQ metrics, such as the distance to the training set or ensemble variance. Overall, random forest-based EMs built with the distance to the training set, ensemble variance, and predicted property values provided a robust and interpretable default configuration. While alternative feature sets, algorithms, and data configurations occasionally improved performance for specific ADME datasets, these gains were generally modest compared with the improvements achieved over standard UQ metrics. Feature importance and explainability of EMs were analyzed to better understand sources of uncertainty. Such explainability analyses further showed that the three EM input features provide complementary information for reliability assessment and enable compound-level interpretation of uncertainty estimates. Taken together, EMs are presented as a tool that bridges prospective uncertainty estimation and error analyses, supporting the identification of model failures and enabling more informed decision-making in molecular ML.

papers.title: caMPO: Correlation-aware multiparameter optimization for data-driven compound prioritization in drug design
papers.abstract: Drug design is inherently a multiparameter optimization (MPO) problem, where several properties need to be simultaneously improved. Beyond activity against the therapeutic target, other relevant properties related to pharmacokinetics and safety are considered during lead optimization. A common MPO approach for compound ranking and prioritization is to identify a set of property objectives and desired ranges (target property profile) and aggregate them into a single MPO score. Sometimes a relative importance or weight is assigned to each property objective. However, this MPO approach suffers from a few drawbacks. For instance, positively correlated objectives may be inadvertently overemphasized while independent objectives may be masked, resulting in a biased approach. In this work, the correlation‑aware MPO (caMPO) framework is introduced to automatically derive weights that account for correlations in the data. This method down‑weights property objectives that are largely predictable from others and up‑weights those that contribute unique information. caMPO was first validated in a controlled setting with synthetic data to assess how predefined correlation patterns affect the derived weights. Moreover, analyses on real drug discovery projects showed that the approach enabled the identification of development candidates (DCs), with an enrichment in compound ranking. For most projects (13/15), DCs were ranked within the top 25% of project compounds, and in approximately half of the projects (7/15) DCs were within the top 10% of the ranking. caMPO consistently matched or exceeded the performance of other standard MPO approaches. Importantly, caMPO can be adapted to project-specific target property profiles, helps to define complex MPO scores while reducing redundancy among property objectives, and gives insights into optimization trade-offs. Taken together, caMPO provides a flexible and data-driven MPO framework for compound prioritization and property optimization.

papers.title: Redox-State-Selective Hydrogen Bonding Enables High Seebeck Coefficient and High Durability of Ruthenium Thermocells
papers.abstract: Thermocells generate electrical voltage from a temperature difference through the temperature dependence of redox potentials. One method for improvement is to make electron transfer trigger a substantial rearrangement of surrounding solvent molecules. Here, we realize this concept by designing hydrogen-bonding interactions that depend strongly on the oxidation state of a ruthenium complex. Tris(4,4′-dioxido-2,2′-bipyridine)ruthenium ([RuII/III(bpy(O)2)3]4−/3−) forms hydrogen bonds with alcohol added in organic solvents, with substantially stronger interactions in the Ru(II) state. This redox-state selectivity was evidenced by a larger blue shift of the MLCT absorption peak for Ru(II) than for Ru(III). Their hydrogen bond interaction can be also controlled by the concentration of alcohol in mixed solvent, evidenced by the systematic redox potential shift with log[CH3OH]. The hydrogen bond affinity was thus dependent strongly on temperature change, and as a result, enhancement of Seebeck coefficient in both DMSO/CH3OH and CH3CN/CH3OH mixed solvents, reaching −2.95 mV K-1 in the CH3CN-based electrolyte. The Ru(II)/(III) couple further sustained power generation for over 50 h under a continuous temperature gradient. These results show that redox-state-selective intermolecular interactions can couple electron transfer to solvent reorganization, providing a molecular strategy for achieving both high Seebeck coefficients and durable thermocell operation.

papers.title: Quantitative structure and energetics of pyrophosphate protonation microstates in implicit water
papers.abstract: Pyrophosphate is a minimal phosphoanhydride whose protonation microstates can reorganize local electrostatics and bridge geometry. We optimized 24 structures spanning five protonation states at B3LYP/ def2-SVPD with SMD water and quantified within-charge energy landscapes, structural asymmetry, Mulliken populations and orbital gaps. Most states were shallow, whereas H2P2O72- spanned 13.37 kcal mol-1. Its lowest sampled structure redistributed the two protons, contracted the P–O–P angle to 120.29°, formed two 1.89 Å intramolecular hydrogen-bond contacts and nearly equalized the phosphorus charges. Persistent asymmetric minima were 13.23–14.81 kcal mol-1 higher across B3LYP, PBE0 and ωB97X-D/ def2-TZVPD calculations; quasi-RRHO thermochemistry retained an 11.10 kcal mol-1 preference. These results identify proton placement as a major determinant of the static aqueous pyrophosphate landscape and motivate microstate screening before more expensive explicit-solvent simulations.

papers.title: Revealing the H2O/Na environments in Hydrated Manganese Iron Prussian White: a D/H exchange and machine-learning-assisted MD simulation study
papers.abstract: Manganese-iron Prussian blue analogs (MnFePBA) are promising sodium-ion battery positive electrodes, offering capacities comparable to LiFePO4 while avoiding critical metals such as cobalt and nickel. Despite their promise, the role of water in the PBA framework remains a central point of contention: some studies report severe first-cycle capacity loss and electrolyte decomposition driven by water co-extraction during cycling, while others show that hydration stabilizes a monoclinic phase capable of smooth, solid-solution sodiation which delivers superior long-term cycling stability. This disagreement is compounded by unresolved structural ambiguity of hydrated PBAs—conventional XRD cannot reliably distinguish sodium from water due to their similar electron densities, and existing neutron diffraction and computational studies disagree on where each species resides within the framework. Here, we address this gap by characterizing deuterated/hydrated (D/H) samples with neutron powder diffraction (NPD) and solid-state 2H/1H NMR to achieve improved contrast and spectral resolution between sodium and water environments, alongside machine-learned interatomic potential molecular dynamics (MLIP-MD) simulations that capture finite-temperature dynamics and configurational sampling beyond the reach of static DFT. NMR confirms consistent local environments across isotopically exchanged samples and resolves distinct signals for interstitial and coordinated water. Contrary to the prevailing XRD-based consensus, our combined NPD and MLIP-MD analysis reveals that water occupies body-center sites while sodium resides at face-center and off-face-center positions—the reverse of the commonly accepted structural model. These findings offer a revised atomic-scale picture of hydrated MnFePBA and establish a methodology for systematically probing hydration effects across the broader PBA family.

papers.title: Excited-State Dynamics in 4-Dimethylamino-4’-Nitrostilbene in Solution: The Role of Solvent Relaxation and Reabsorption Effects
papers.abstract: Push-pull donor-acceptor stilbenes are model systems for probing solvation dynamics and intramolecular processes. However, the precise nature of the excited-state evolution remains debated. To obtain a comprehensive picture of the processes involved, we combine broadband ultrafast spectroscopies, fluorescence up-conversion and transient absorption, to study the excited-state evolution of 4-dimethylamino-4’-nitrostilbene (DANS) in solvents of increasing polarity (from cyclohexane to acetonitrile). We demonstrate that the evolution is fully described by solvent relaxation only, perturbed by reabsorption effects due to transient overlap between the fluorescence and excited-state absorption bands. No intramolecular charge-transfer is involved in the observed dynamics. We extract the solvation correlation function C(t) in dibutyl ether, diethyl ether, tetrahydrofuran and acetonitrile. This work highlights the strength of combining broadband femtosecond absorption/fluorescence to disentangle the solvation dynamics from intramolecular contributions.

papers.title: Water-Soluble Diiron Bis-Aminocarbyne Complexes: Photoinduced CO Substitution, Generation of Diiron(I) Aqua-Carbonyl Complexes, and Biological Evaluation
papers.abstract: The diiron bis-aminocarbyne complexes [Fe2Cp2(CO)2{μ-CNMe2}{μ-CNMe(R)}][CF3SO3]2 (R = Me, 4a; Cy, 4b; CH2Ph, 4c; Cp = η5-C5H5, Cy = cyclohexyl) were synthesized in 64 – 87% yields from the corresponding isocyanide precursors [Fe2Cp2(CO)2(CNR){μ-CNMe2}][CF3SO3], 2a-c. The acetonitrile derivatives [Fe2Cp2(CO)(NCMe){μ-CNMe2}{μ-CNMe(R)}][CF3SO3]2, 5a-c, and the chloride derivatives [Fe2Cp2(Cl)(CO){μ-CNMe2}{μ-CNMe(R)}][CF3SO3], 7a-c, were obtained from 4a-c in 55 – 65% and 50 – 96% yields, respectively, via photoinduced CO substitution using a mercury blended UV lamp. Complexes 4a-c, 5a-c and 7a-c were characterized by IR, UV-Vis and multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, while the structures of 4c, 5c and 7a were determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Compounds 4a-c display aqueous solubilities of approximately 10–60 mM and stability of the Fe2Cp2(CO){μ-CNMe2}{μ-CNMe(R)} scaffold in water and DMEM cell culture medium. Upon irradiation with sunlight or a mercury blended UV lamp, 4a-c undergo photoinduced CO release in aqueous solutions, leading to almost complete conversion into [Fe2Cp2(CO)(water){μ-CNMe2}{μ-CNMe(R)}][CF3SO3]2, 6a-c. These unprecedented diiron(I) aqua-carbonyl complexes were identified by NMR and UV-Vis spectroscopy, and by HR-ESI-MS analysis for the representative compound 6b. Cytotoxicity in the dark and phototoxicity under 415 nm illumination were assessed in 4T1 mammary carcinoma cells for 4a-c, 7b, and the benchmark mono-aminocarbyne complex [Fe2Cp2(CO)3{CNMe2}][CF3SO3], 1. Illumination did not enhance the cytotoxicity of 4a-c and 7b over the 3 – 200 µM concentration range, whereas 1 showed increased phototoxicity at 100 µM.

papers.title: Quantifying Multi-Objective Optimization in Generative Chemistry for Molecule Design
papers.abstract: Multi objective optimization (MOO) is central to molecular design, yet its impact on generative chemistry outcomes remains poorly quantified. Consequently, it is unclear how different MOO strategies influence chemical space exploration and property optimization in generative methods. Here, we introduce a benchmarking framework for evaluating MOO strategies in generative chemistry. Six MOO approaches are highlighted including arithmetic and geometric means, non dominated sorting, Chebyshev scalarization, generational distance, and binary thresholding within a lead optimization setting. Across 60 scaffolds derived from six potency datasets, we explore a many-objective task for the simultaneous optimization of various compound properties, including potency, solubility and lipophilicity. We evaluate methods using metrics aligned to recurring medicinal chemistry use cases or decision scenarios and assess differences across datasets and scaffolds. We find that the MOO choice substantially changes both optimization outcomes and explored chemical space across datasets, scaffold and intended use cases. Overall, our results provide practical, use case driven guidance for selecting and comparing MOO strategies in generative chemistry workflows.

papers.title: CatWalk: Reaction Pathway Generation and Transition State Sampling via Score-based Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Computing transition states for heterogeneous catalyst surface reactions is computationally demanding due to the relatively high cost in precisely locating a saddle point using ab initio electronic structure calculations. In this work, we present a new generative score-based diffusion model—CatWalk—that predicts the initial structures for reaction pathways of heterogeneous catalysts with surface adsorbates. Given only the desired reaction type and reactant structure, CatWalk produces nine pathway structures by iteratively perturbing the coordinates of the previous output. CatWalk was trained on 731 nudged elastic band (NEB) calculations from the CatTSunami dataset, which contains diverse substrate elements with adsorbates undergoing three types of chemical reactions: desorption, dissociation, and atom transfer. The model can be directed to target one of these three reaction types during generation, and due to its stochastic nature can generate various products via multiple pathways from the same initial state. Optimizing CatWalkgenerated pathways using a pretrained foundation machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) with the nudged elastic band (NEB) method leads to several lower-energy pathways compared to what is obtained by the traditional linear interpolation initialization method for NEBs. Additionally, repeated intermediate structure generations using CatWalk enabled sampling of different pathways and final states which can lead to multiple saddle points with variation in energy by up to 0.2 eV. Overall, CatWalk provides a general and scalable framework for accelerating reaction-pathway discovery, enabling broader exploration of catalytic mechanisms at significantly reduced computational cost.

papers.title: Anchor-Oracle Fourier Neural Operator Framework for 3D Membrane Field Prediction in PEM Fuel Cells: From Steady-State Operation to Transient Degradation
papers.abstract: Membrane durability limits the service life of proton exchange membrane fuel cells, but the average degradation rate does not capture the degradation spatial heterogeneities. Existing approaches either resolve these spatial features at high computational cost (three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics modeling) or replace it with a scalar or curve-level surrogate; neither is fast enough to be queried across a wide spectrum of cell operation conditions. We develop an Anchor-Oracle Fourier Neural Operator, a three-stage neural operator that predicts the complete three-dimensional fields of membrane ionic conductivity and ionic current density from operating conditions and degradation time, achieving steady-state accuracy within one percent at four orders of magnitude lower cost than the reference solver. Using the surrogate as a full-field probe, we show that operating conditions reorganize the two fields' spatial heterogeneity along different axes, and that degradation rate and spatial heterogeneity vary non-monotonically with each other. We further find that current is progressively redistributed away from degraded regions over space and time. This redistribution is invisible to a single pooled correlation, and it advances together with the degradation front. We then use the surrogate to construct an inverse-design operating map, showing influences of different boundary conditions on power and durability.

papers.title: Time- and Synthesis-Solvent-Dependent Luminescence of Citric Acid–Urea Carbon Dots and Their Alkylamine-Tunable Interfacial Activity
papers.abstract: Citric acid–urea carbon dots are widely used fluorophores, but the influence of reaction duration and solvent on their structural and optical evolution remains underexplored. Here, citric acidurea carbon dots were prepared in water and N,N-dimethylformamide at 200 °C with reaction times ranging from 10 min to 72 h, and selected samples were subsequently functionalized with butylamine, hexylamine, or octylamine via carbodiimide-mediated amide coupling. Structural analysis showed that DMF-derived particles were nitrogen-rich and amide-dominated, whereas water-derived particles were more hydrophilic and carboxyl/hydroxyl-rich, with nonmonotonic compositional changes over time. These differences were mirrored in the photoluminescence behavior: DMF-based synthesis produced gradually red-shifted emission, while aqueous synthesis favored blue-shifted emission and higher quantum yields at specific excitation windows. Alkylamine grafting converted surface carboxyl groups into amides, reduced ζ-potential magnitude, and produced chain-length-dependent interfacial activity, lowering the air–water surface tension from about 70 mN·m −1 to approximately 34 mN·m −1 .
