The results show that solvent choice and reaction time provide a practical route to tune the core composition, surface chemistry, emission properties, and interfacial behavior of citric acid–urea carbon dots.

papers.title: Streamlined Ultrafast Chromatography for High-Throughput Discovery and Development Chemistry via Predictive Analytical Modeling
papers.abstract: Modern high-throughput experimentation can generate complex chemical data at an unprecedented pace taxing existing analytical capabilities. Although recent advances in ultrafast liquid chromatography (LC) enable rapid analysis of reaction profiles, enantiopurity, and multicomponent mixtures, the experimental effort required to identify suitable chromatographic resolution often limits streamlined implementation. Herein, a predictive in silico framework that transforms ultrafast LC assay development from empirical screening into a model-driven design workflow is introduced. Experimental retention data are used to model chromatographic selectivity across temperature, gradient slope, flow rate, and column geometry, enabling rapid identification of the fastest separation conditions that preserve decision-critical information. The approach is demonstrated across closely related isomers, chiral analyses, and high-throughput reaction screening, where model-predicted separations translated directly to reliable experimentation while reducing analysis cycle times substantially with minimal manual intervention. Retention modeling is further combined with fit-for-purpose resolution criteria and in silico peak clustering to selectively resolve critical components while intentionally grouping analytes to maximize throughput. Together, this framework establishes a general strategy for the systematic deployment of reliable ultrafast chromatographic assays, reducing method-development burden and accelerating analytical decision-making across applications in biocatalysis, natural products, metabolomics, high-throughput experimentation, and modern synthesis.

papers.title: Chroma-Agent-Alpha: An Open-Source Framework for Automated Chromatography Preprocessing, GNN-Based Peak Deconvolution, and FAIR Data Lineage
papers.abstract: Gas and liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (GC-MS/LC-MS) are foundational to analytical chemistry, quality control, and metabolomics. However, manual baseline removal, dynamic peak integration, and retention time alignment across multiple sample runs remain persistent bottlenecks. Commercial chromatography data systems depend on locked binary formats, manual integration tweaks, and inflexible rules. We introduce Chroma-Agent-Alpha, an open-source software framework that automates raw chromatography processing. The system implements native binary parsers for Agilent .ch and Varian .xms formats, Whittaker-Eilers Asymmetric Least Squares (ALS) baseline correction, Sakoe-Chiba constrained Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), and a two-layer Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) paired with Exponentially Modified Gaussian (EMG) non-linear fitting to deconvolve co-eluting analyte signals. Output matrices are formatted into Zarr v3 coordinate arrays and indexed in a local SQLite LaminDB database for FAIR data lineage tracking. We benchmarked the GNN model against the 2023 PeakDetective baseline. On ambiguous co-eluting peaks, the curation F1-score rose from 0.2222 to 0.9787, while peak integration error dropped by 48.8% in under 12 seconds on standard CPU hardware.

papers.title: Static correlation, a coupled-cluster diagnostic blind spot, and its quantum-computing resolution in silver–dinitrogen clusters
papers.abstract: The size-dependent adsorption of molecular nitrogen on small silver clusters, Ag n N 2 (n = 1–6), is investigated by density functional theory, and an adsorption energy of −0.44 eV, two-to seven fold stronger than for any neighboring cluster size, is identified for n = 3, accompanied by the only appreciable N–N bond elongation in the series. Complete active space self-consistent field calculations reveal that this coincides with static correlation that grows substantially along the N–N stretching coordinate, a correlation index rising from 1.14 to 4.15 between equilibrium and 2.40 Å. Over the same range, the Lee–Taylor T 1 diagnostic from coupled-cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations is found to plateau between 0.03 and 0.05, and, for a second cluster, to fall from a maximum of 0.042 to 0.030 as the bond is stretched further. This diagnostic blind spot is confirmed, in a markedly amplified form, for the dissociation of free dinitrogen, where explicit wavefunction-stability analysis establishes that the coupled-cluster reference becomes variationally unstable precisely where the diagnostic offers no warning. Motivated by this finding, a sixteen-qubit unitary coupled-cluster variational quantum eigensolver calculation, comprising approximately 5,700 Pauli terms, is benchmarked against the multireference reference across the identical coordinate, reproducing the reference energy to within 0.29–0.39 mE h at equilibrium and 6.0 mEh at the most strongly correlated geometry examined. These results establish a concrete, cross-validated case study of a practically consequential coupled-cluster diagnostic limitation, together with a physically motivated demonstration that a variational quantum algorithm reproduces the correct multireference physics in a regime where the conventional single-reference benchmark cannot be trusted.

papers.title: Spatially Patterned Laser Irradiation Synergistically Enhances Crystal Nucleation
papers.abstract: Use of lasers has increasingly been recognized as a promising tool for the spatiotemporal control of crystallization, which is required in various scientific and industrial fields. This work reports synergistic enhancement of crystal nucleation by spatially patterned multi-spot laser irradiation, which drastically improves crystallization efficiency from melt and solutions. We found that pulsed laser irradiation at two different spots with a certain separation distance could significantly enhance ice crystal nucleation in supercooled water, where no nucleation could be induced by single-spot irradiation with the doubled pulse energy. Furthermore, we revealed that not only the inter-spot distance but also the spatial geometry of laser-induced stimuli is critical for the enhancement of ice crystal nucleation, suggesting that multi-spot irradiation enhances nucleation by the synergistic interplay of multiple cavitation bubbles and/or pressure waves that were generated from different laser spots. Such crystal nucleation enhancement by multi-spot laser irradiation was also confirmed in a solution system. These results clearly indicate that crystallization probability is governed not simply by the total laser energy delivered to the solution but by its spatial distribution, which provides a practical design guideline for efficient spatially patterned laser-induced nucleation and mechanistic insight into precise crystallization control.

papers.title: Ethenolysis as an on-purpose linker cleavage strategy for delamination of metal-organic frameworks
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are a unique class of hybrid organic-inorganic materials that distinguish themselves with their highly porous crystalline structures, making them desirable for a variety of applications. The successful implementation of MOFs in various industries relies on the ability to precisely tailor their structures in a post-synthetic fashion. On-purpose cleavage of organic linkers has recently gained traction as one of the strategies for morphological tuning of MOFs due to its ability to deliver a range of desirable outcomes, such as their dimensional reduction or porosity enhancement. Although several classes of chemical transformations have been leveraged to date for that purpose, they all require harsh and/or aqueous reaction conditions that may be unsuitable for tuning of less stable MOFs. Herein, we establish ethenolysis reaction, a variant of iconic olefin metathesis, as a new tool for on-purpose cleavage of MOF linkers. In our prototypical study, we demonstrate that the ethenolysis of the three-dimensional pillared MOF, UofT-2, causes delamination of the material with decrease of the bulk crystallite thickness and evidence for formation of MOF nanosheets. Crucially, ethenolysis-driven linker cleavage proceeds under anhydrous/anoxic conditions and without the need of applying harsh reaction conditions.

papers.title: Automated Multimodal Mapping of Optical and Relative Surface-Potential Responses in a FAPbI3–BDAPbI4–PEA2PbI4 Halide Perovskite Library
papers.abstract: High-throughput (HT) characterization has accelerated materials screening, however most workflows for functional characterization rely on a single measurement modality. This approach leaves the relationship between different aspects of materials response, such as optical emission and local electronic behavior, largely unassessed within the same campaign. Multimodal characterization, particularly pairing probe-based electronic measurements with optical screening, remained comparatively underdeveloped. Here we address this gap by combining automated Kelvin probe force microscopy under illumination (photoKPFM) with HT photoluminescence (PL) peak-intensity mapping to screen a formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3), 1,4-butanediammonium lead iodide (BDAPbI4), and phenethylammonium lead iodide (PEA2PbI4) combinatorial halide perovskite library. A Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization with pure exploration workflow selects photoKPFM measurements to reconstruct the composition-dependent surface potential response, benchmarked on a binary FAPbI3–PEA2PbI4 line before extension to the ternary system. Comparing photoKPFM against PL peak intensity across 13 unique nominal ternary compositions, measured on independently prepared replicate libraries, shows that both descriptors broadly prioritize PEA2PbI4-rich compositions, but individual composition rankings frequently disagree, and exploratory correlation analysis finds no statistically significant global association between the two measurements after multiple-comparison correction. Rather than indicating redundancy, this divergence shows that photoKPFM and PL provide complementary, non-interchangeable candidate-selection information, jointly identifying compositions that rank consistently strong by both descriptors and compositions whose priority depends on which functional descriptor is used. This work demonstrates how pairing automated probe-based and optical HT methods surfaces candidates that single-modality screening would rank differently, motivating multimodal characterization as a general, extensible strategy for combinatorial materials discovery beyond this specific material system.

papers.title: Single Crystal Vibronic Spectroscopy of [Yb(trensal)]
papers.abstract: Understanding vibronic coupling in molecular materials is crucial in the development of high performance molecule-based optical and quantum technologies. Vibronic coupling governs spin state lifetimes in these systems, and is additionally a source of decoherence. Hence, gaining detailed understanding of vibronic coupling will enable improvement of candidate materials. In this regard, magneto-spectroscopic techniques provide a direct probe of the vibronic coupling, which can be performed on polycrystalline and more recently single crystal samples. Single crystal magneto-spectroscopy offers a clear advantage due to its improved resolution and its ability to probe magnetic anisotropy, however, simulating the resulting spectra has proven difficult due to the simultaneous requirements of solid-state phonon calculations, embedded correlated electronic structure theory methods, and inclusion of large numbers of vibrational modes in the Hamiltonian to recreate experimental spectra. In this work we present single crystal far-infrared magneto-spectroscopy (FIRMS) and photo-luminescence magneto-spectroscopy (PLUMS) measurements on [Yb(trensal)] . We can experimentally verify previous assertions that most of the vibronic transitions in the FIRMS map are intra-Kramers doublet transitions and additionally elucidate the origin of the transitions observed in the PLUMS map. Crucially, to achieve this we have developed a new computational framework to perform robust and efficient simulations of magneto-spectroscopy incorporating hundreds of vibrational modes based on ab initio simulations in the solid state.

papers.title: Crystal structure of ITQ-1p, the pure-silica precursor to the zeolite ITQ-1 (MWW framework type)
papers.abstract: The synergy between solid-state NMR, a probe of local structure, and X-ray powder diffraction, a probe of long-range order, has been exploited to untangle the details of the structure of ITQ-1p, the layered precursor to the pure silica zeolite ITQ-1 (MWW framework type). Rietveld refinement of the structure using synchrotron powder diffraction data was guided by the results from a variety of solid-state NMR techniques, including two-dimensional (2D) 29 Si– 29 Si correlation spectra that resolve all eight Si sites, 2D 29 Si{ 1 H} and 13 C{ 1 H} correlation spectra that show a complicated distribution of hydrogen-bonded environments in the interlayer space, and a 1D 23 Na spectrum that indicates a nearly symmetrical environment around the Na + ions. The main features of the resulting structure are: MWW silicate layers with silanol nests at the interlayer surface, hexamethyleneimine (HMI) molecules in the intralayer channel and in the interlayer space, trimethylaminoadamantane ions (TMAda + ) in the "pockets" at the surface of the layer with the trimethylamino group pointing towards the interlayer space, and a Na + ion surrounded by a puckered ring of 3 water molecules and 3 OH – groups at the origin between the two TMAda+ ions in adjacent layers. This well-defined TMAda + -Na + (OH – ) 3 (H 2 O) 3 -TMAda + complex may well be the key to the unusually high crystallinity of ITQ-1p. Indeed, these structural details give considerable insight into the synthetic process, and provide a foundation for tailoring interlayer chemistry to realize specific catalytic features.

papers.title: Turning Air Exposure into an Advantage for Lithium Metal Anodes
papers.abstract: Lithium metal anodes (LMAs) are central to next-generation high-energy batteries, but extreme air sensitivity hinders their commercialization. Expanding the allowable air-exposure window would let LMAs use existing Li-ion battery manufacturing infrastructure. Here we show that a two-step protocol of prolonged dry pretreatment followed by brief controlled air exposure engineers a mechanically robust surface reaction layer (SRL) on Li metal. Insufficient pretreatment yields a poorly adherent SRL that delaminates on air exposure, whereas optimal pretreatment yields a composite oxide/hydroxide/carbonate SRL that accommodates growth-induced compressive stress (20–290 MPa) by wrinkling rather than delaminating. This wrinkled, adherent SRL promotes uniform Li deposition and improved electrochemical stability: full cells built with the optimally processed anode maintain stable cycling performance up to 1,300 cycles with higher sustained capacity than cells using as-received Li. These findings establish the chemo-mechanical principles governing SRL evolution during air exposure and provide practical guidelines for handling LMAs under realistic atmospheric conditions.

papers.title: Protecting Groups as Catalysts: Direct Synthesis of Primary Amines from Ammonia under Carbonyl Catalysis
papers.abstract: Primary amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, yet their direct, modular synthesis from ammonia remains challenging. Here we report a carbonyl catalysis strategy that enables the direct synthesis of structurally complex primary amines from ammonia by integrating the conventional multistep sequence of protection, N–H functionalization, and deprotection into a single catalytic cycle. As a proof of concept, amino-trifluoromethylation of alkenes using ammonium salts and Togni reagent afforded a wide range of β-trifluoromethylated primary amines, including derivatives of complex natural products. 1,8-Diazafluorenone was uniquely competent as a carbonyl catalyst, highlighting the critical role of catalyst design in ammonia transformation. Mechanistic studies revealed that its distinctive electronic structure promotes efficient ammonia activation through N–H ketimine intermediates, thereby enabling catalytic turnover. These findings establish carbonyl catalysis as a platform for the direct ammonia transformation and demonstrate how protecting groups can function as catalysts.

papers.title: Sustainable photocatalytic borylation: updated review
papers.abstract: Organoboron compounds are suitable precursors for a wide verity of organic transformation (Suzuki and Chan-Lam reactions), and have got significant applications in catalysis, drug discovery, diagnostics, and materials science. Photocatalysis falls under the twelve principles of Green Chemistry, and United Nations (UN) sustainable development goals (SDG) 9 and 12. Though recent review articles have been published on metal-free or photochemical C-H borylation reactions, this review article covers photoinduced C-H, decarboxylative, carbon-halogen, C-N, C-O, and C-S borylation reactions (from year 2018 to 2025) catalysed by metals, organocatalysts, including catalyst-free reactions. The varieties of catalysts, and their applications for the synthesis of diverse boron substrates have been discussed in this article.

papers.title: Mixed-Mode On-Line SPE-LC Broadens Analytical Coverage for Non-Target Discovery of Mobile Chemicals in Water
papers.abstract: Discovery and quantification of hazardous mobile substances in environmental waters are challenged by their poor retention in solid-phase extraction (SPE) or reversed-phase (RP) liquid chromatography (LC). Here we employed a test-mixture of 218 diverse analytes (log P -4.8 to 7.9) and tested 13 columns to optimize and validate two complementary on-line SPE-LC workflows to maximize analytical coverage for a range of hydrophobic and hydrophilic analytes in target and non-target analysis. When combining the on-line SPE-RPLC and -mixed-mode (MM)LC methods developed here, each consuming only 1-2 mL sample per injection, we detected 206 of 218 analytes with median absolute recovery of 96% and median method detection limit of 1 ng/L. The SPE MMLC method enabled expanded chemical-space coverage for smaller, more polar and ionic analytes. When applied to 21 urban stormwater samples, 46 target analytes were quantified, including 1,3-diphenylguanidine (42-5200 ng/L), diphenyl phosphate (5.6-550 ng/L) and perfluorohexanoic acid (5.0-11 ng/L) in all samples. Many of the non-target annotations (level 2a) were unique to the RPLC (N=100) or MMLC methods (N=95), demonstrating broader analytical coverage by their complementarity application. Annotations included many known anthropogenic chemicals from traffic and urban activity, as well as novel discoveries such as the tire-wear compound isomer N-(4-methylpentan-2-yl)-N-phenylbenzene-1,4-diamine.

papers.title: HIV-1 Nef Rewires Beclin 1 Conformational Allostery to Suppress Autophagy
papers.abstract: Understanding the relationship between protein flexibility, conformational-and dynamical-allostery drive the biological function is essential as these interconnected features orchestrate biochemical processes required for biological activity. Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are central to cellular signalling and attractive therapeutic targets, yet their modulation remains challenging to elucidate using conventional approaches as it is highly govern via conformational transitions and allostery, yet how allosteric mechanisms diversify at PPI level to provide functional output is poorly understood. Here, we focus on Beclin 1, a key autophagy regulator that functions in a PPI-dependent manner. Autophagy is a critical cellular degradation and recycling pathway implicated in numerous human diseases including viral infection. Viruses like HIV exploit this process, where the viral protein Nef interacts with Beclin 1 to suppress autophagy and enhance viral survival. However, the structural basis of this inhibition remains unclear, likely due to the complex nature of PPI. To investigate as how Nef binding impair beclin 1 association with membrane, an integrative approach combining conventional and advanced molecular dynamics simulations was employed to capture conformational transitions and determinants which alter Beclin 1 during Nef binding from active-to-inactive state. Our results reveal that three dynamic loops of Beclin 1 undergo significant rearrangements, forming an aromatic cage that drives, a shift from active to inactive states, thereby impairing membrane binding and autophagy regulation. All together these analysis not only elucidating the critical mechanistic determinants responsible from activeto-inactive tansition, moreover, can be utilize for therapeutic intervention harnessing the typical PPIs.

papers.title: Alginate Ionic Hydrogels as Hierarchical Supramolecular Materials
papers.abstract: Alginate ionic hydrogels (AIGs) are widely used for cell and drug encapsulation, as well as across the food and pharmaceutical industries. However, unexplained phenomena—such as initial burst drug release, anomalous pH shifts, and the presence of counter-anions in the gel—are inadequately addressed by the scientific community and the conventional "egg-box" gelation model. In this work, we apply supramolecular theory to explain these stochastic behaviors, via evaluating AIGs under four core postulates for the theory: constitutional diversity and dynamics, spontaneous hierarchical assembly, and guest molecule accommodation. Using rheological, drug release, and spectroscopic (FTIR, XRD, EDX) analyses, we demonstrate that AIGs display all essential attributes of supramolecular materials. Results reveal that traditional calcium-alginate "egg-boxes" serve merely as primary structural units, whereas anion-driven secondary organization produces the material's hierarchical architecture. Consequently, altering the counter-anion of crosslinking calcium salts introduces constitutional diversity to tune various hydrogel 2 properties. The unexplained acidity in standard AIGs stems from spontaneous dissolution of environmental carbon dioxide during gelation, aligning with guest accommodation postulate of the theory. Replacing chloride anions with acetate or lactate promotes the conversion of dissolved carbon dioxide into insoluble mineral phases, neutralizing the gel's pH significantly. Similarly, switching from chloride to acetate mitigates initial burst drug release anomaly. Overall, this supramolecular framework provides deeper fundamental insights into alginate ionic gelation and opens new pathways for designing functional hydrogels.

papers.title: Prediction of Singlet-Triplet Gaps Using Self-Attention–Based Regression with Model Integration into a Molecular Editor
papers.abstract: The singlet–triplet gap (STG) is an important property of photofunctional materials, but obtaining reliable values can be challenging. Experimentally, its determination often requires a combination of advanced spectroscopic techniques, while computational approaches can be time-consuming and demand specialized expertise. Therefore, a low-cost and user-friendly approach for obtaining reasonable STG estimates could make this property more accessible to non-experts. In this work, we evaluate regression models based on different molecular representations using the INVEST dataset from the Aspuru-Guzik group that contains ADC(2) energy gaps for ~70K molecules. We compare transformer models operating on SMILES representations, graph-based models (AttentiveFP), and fingerprint-based models. While AttentiveFP performs best for molecules similar to those in the training set, pre-trained transformers generalize better to unseen chemical space after fine-tuning. Motivated by these complementary strengths, we integrate our best-performing models into an online 2D chemical structure editor, enabling users to obtain STG estimates directly from drawn molecular structures. The editor can be accessed at http://ketcher-predict.ttk.hu/.

papers.title: Temporal Control of Chiral Selection in Non-Covalent Systems through Kinetically Programmed Threading
papers.abstract: While challenging, current methods for achieving stereoselectivity in non-covalent systems are dominated by thermodynamic strategies, leaving the dynamic expression of chiral biases under kinetic control almost unchartered. In this work, a programmable, reversible (pseudo)[2]rotaxane assembly is introduced to realize stereoselectivity under kinetic control. By leveraging the well-defined interlocked structures and threading pathways, not only the structures of the interlocked components can be precisely engineered to create a substantial difference in the activation barriers for kinetic stereoselectivity, but also the exchange rate, and hence lifetime of the kinetically generated chiral bias can be modulated via the thermodynamic stability of the (pseudo)[2]rotaxanes. Furthermore, the mechanically interlocked platform is integrated with the supramolecular encapsulation of a chromophoric guest, and the evolution and decay of the kinetic chiral bias is successfully translated into a readable, time-dependent optical signal. Due to the dynamic nature of the non-covalent and reversible threading, this transient kinetic bias and output can be erased on demand by thermal acceleration of the noncovalent exchange. Ultimately, this strategy introduces a general design paradigm for using mechanical interlocking to achieve precise temporal control over chirality transmission in nonequilibrium supramolecular systems.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by agreement with the authors because it contained figures reproduced without appropriate permission. An updated version is available at 10.26434/chemrxiv.15008082/v2.

papers.title: A Fluorescent Pillarplex Rotaxane as a Modular Supramolecular Organometallic Platform for Nanoassemblies
papers.abstract: Mechanically interlocked molecules (MIMs) offer attractive opportunities to modularly integrate bioactivity, molecular recognition, and optical readout within a single supramolecular architecture. Here, we report a fluorescent [2]rotaxane platform based on a cationic organometallic pillarplex ring and fluorescein stoppers as intrinsic imaging labels. The pillarplex ring promotes interactions with biorelevant polyanions such as nucleic acids, while the fluorescein stoppers ensure optical traceability by confocal microscopy. Cellular uptake by A549 cancer cells is demonstrated, showing that the fluorescent rotaxane remains predominantly localized in the cytoplasm. The rotaxane can furthermore be integrated into multicomponent nanoassemblies, such as coacervates and biopharmaceutical-relevant polyplexes. For the latter, in the presence of siRNA and cationic polymers, the rotaxane forms assemblies that even enhance cellular uptake and imaging. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that dye incorporation provides a powerful strategy for modulating pillarplex rotaxanes, thereby enabling controlled uptake, localization within the cell by fluorescence labeling and co-assembly.

papers.title: AutomaticMolCraft: A Web Interface for 3D Molecular Generation, Dataset Curation, and Structure–Property Analysis
papers.abstract: Here, we present AutomaticMolCraft, a locally deployed browser platform for running and organising 3D molecular discovery campaigns. It is designed to complement MolCraftDiffusion, a 3D molecular-generation platform that provides the computational layer for model training, 3D molecular generation, and analysis, while AutomaticMolCraft serves as the interactive interface for visualising molecular data and generated results. It also supports molecular data management while keeping data, computations, and results connected and traceable. The three applications are selected to showcase distinct capabilities of the interface across data-driven molecular discovery tasks. First, we demonstrate the data management and visualisation components by curating three organocatalyst datasets and comparing their molecular structures and properties to support the selection. Second, we show how these data components connect with the computational layer of MolCraftDiffusion by running and comparing property-directed generation workflows for producing 3D molecules with specified scalar properties. Third, we extend this integration to steric-property-directed generation, where AutomaticMolCraft is used to identify underrepresented regions of property space, generate molecules toward those regions, and incorporate the resulting candidates back into the molecular data for subsequent analysis. The codebases are available at: https://github.com/lcmd-epfl/MolCraftDiffusion and https://github.com/lcmd-epfl/AutomaticMolCraft.

papers.title: Demonstration of Ultraviolet Photodissociation Induced by Light-Emitting Diodes Externally Interfaced to a Linear Ion-Trap Mass Spectrometer
papers.abstract: We report the first demonstration of ultraviolet photodissociation (UVPD) mass spectrometry achieved with Light-Emitting Diodes externally interfaced to a linear ion-trap mass spectrometer. LEDs provide a low-cost, compact photon source that is technically simpler to operate than the high-powered pulsed laser systems that are currently used in UVPD instruments. Mounting the LEDs external to the mass spectrometer provides advanced flexibility for interchanging LEDs with different wavelengths. Here, we demonstrate 365 and 280 nm LED-UVPD on flavin mononucleotide, tryptophan and the pentapeptide, Leu-Enk. The UVPD fragments observed are in full agreement with fragments observed using pulsedlasers as the photon source.

papers.title: AlCl3-Mediated Arylation of Dimethyl 2-Arylcyclopropane-1,1dicarboxylates with Benzene: A Facile Approach to Dimethyl 2-(2-Aryl-2-phenylethyl)malonates
papers.abstract: It was found that the reaction of dimethyl 2-arylcyclopropane-1,1-dicarboxylates with benzene in the presence of two equivalents of AlCl3 at room temperature (23 o C) for 1 h leads to the selective opening of the three-membered ring with the formation of dimethyl 2-(2-aryl-2-phenylethyl)malonates in high yields (89-94%). The developed method demonstrates high tolerance toward both electron-donating (4-Me) and electron-withdrawing (4-Cl) substituents on the aryl ring of the starting cyclopropane, providing a simple and effective route to the synthesis of substituted malonates.

papers.title: Hydrophobic Interaction as the Result of Interfacial Frustration
papers.abstract: The hydrophobic effect is one of the most consequential organizing principles in molecular biology, laying the foundation for explanation of concepts like protein folding, molecular recognition, membrane self-assembly and allosteric communication. Its conceptual description remains dependent primarily on a framework established in the mid-twentieth century, as per which, hydrophobic association is driven primarily by the entropic release of water molecules ordered around non-polar surfaces. The framework, while thermodynamically correct, is incomplete in some ways that have become increasingly consequential as structural, dynamic and calorimetric data have been accumulated over the years. In this paper, I propose a reframing of the hydrophobic effect in terms of interfacial frustration- a continuous, geometry sensitive incompatibility between the hydrogen bond requirements of liquid water and non-polar surfaces it is forced to accommodate. This paper argues that hydrophobic association represents the resolution of this frustration, rather than the mere expulsion of constrained solvent. This reframing provides a unified mechanistic account of phenomena that the classical picture cannot explain alone, or treats as separate problems: the geometry dependence of hydrophobic association strength, the qualitative distinction between small-solute and extended-surface hydrophobicity, the thermodynamic crossover with temperature and the propagation of allosteric signals through hydrophobic protein cores. This paper also proposes that hydrophobic cores in proteins are not passive burial sites, but active and dynamic modulators of a distributed frustration landscape. Allosteric communication through these cores operates through cooperative frustration redistribution, a mechanism distinct from classical strain propagation, but consistent with the growing body of evidence that allostery frequently proceeds through changes in protein dynamics rather than average structure. This framework generates specific, experimentally testable predictions that distinguish it from both the classical entropic model and existing density functional theories of hydrophobicity

papers.title: Workflow design as a research variable in computational materials discovery
papers.abstract: For decades, much of computational materials discovery has relied on campaign architectures whose high-level decision policies were written in advance by human researchers. Agentic AI changes this arrangement because choices of method, system, and next step can increasingly be made at runtime. The workflow can therefore become a deliberative trajectory rather than only a pre-authored graph. I argue that this shift creates a new layer of research design. The central questions are no longer only how capable scientific agents are, but which decision rights should be delegated, how frequently humans should intervene, how agents should be distributed within a laboratory, and how stochastic research trajectories should be audited and reproduced. I develop the engagement-cadence trade-off, laboratory organization as an experimental variable, and a distinction between trajectory and conclusion reproducibility. I also address the strongest practical objection, namely that reliability degrades with task horizon and verification may erase throughput gains. I close with a measurement agenda for studying human-agent research systems empirically.

papers.title: Zero-Waste Upcycling of Potato Peels via Direct PLA Grafting for Rapidly Biodegradable Bioplastics
papers.abstract: The escalating global demand for petrochemical plastic packaging has driven a severe environmental crisis due to its inherent resistance to degradation and challenging recycling processes. While upcycling agro-industrial side streams into bioplastics offers an attractive solution, traditional physical blending fails to meet practical packaging requirements due to severe interfacial incompatibility and phase separation. Here we report a scalable, solvent-free surface-initiated ring-opening polymerization (SI-ROP) strategy that directly bridges sustainable agriculture with high-performance degradable packaging. By utilizing minimally treated macroscopic biomass, ubiquitous potato peel waste, and chemically consuming lignocellulosic surface hydroxyls to form permanent ester linkages, we construct a entangled topological network that fundamentally overcomes interfacial limitations. This highly integrated architecture delivers the exceptional mechanical robustness, near-complete UVA/UVB shielding, and competitive gas impermeability required for demanding packaging applications. Furthermore, metagenomic and enzymatic profiling reveals that these packaging materials undergo accelerated, microbially driven mineralization in soil via a synergistic dual-degradation mechanism involving secreted carbohydrate esterases and glycoside hydrolases. By seamlessly transforming agricultural waste into materials designed for complete mineralization, this solvent-free engineering paradigm provides a promising route to unite sustainable agriculture with next-generation packaging in a closed-loop bioeconomy.

papers.title: Non-Orthogonal Exciton Theory Including Charge Transfer Effects for Strongly Coupled Chromophores
papers.abstract: Frenkel exciton models are popular ways to describing non-covalently bound multichromophore systems in large molecules and molecular aggregates, where system size poses a challenge for mainstream quantum-chemical methods. While fragments can conveniently be described with embedding methods at the desired level of sophistication, the proper description of the interaction of the chromophores requires accurate coupling between them. At large distances it is dominated by the Coulomb-type term, but at short separations, the exchange contribution, the overlap of the wave functions, and the charge transfer (CT) effects also play an important role. In this work a strategy for evaluating the latter terms, by exploiting second-quantized formalism with non-orthogonal orbitals, is presented. The derived formulae use quantities from the monomer calculations, such as transition densities for local excitations and Dyson orbitals of ionized species for CT states. This ensures that the framework can be used with a wide spectrum of electronic structure methods, including high-level EOM-CC variants. The importance of the different contributions as functions of the intermolecular separation is tested on the formaldehyde dimer. While all terms become important with decreasing distance, their actual magnitude cannot be predicted without calculations. The robust accuracy of the proposed exciton model down to the 2 Å intermonomer separation is shown for the eight lowest lying excited states of the formaldehyde dimer, by comparing the potential curves obtained from dimer calculations and those from the presented model involving ten electronic states.

papers.title: From Memorisation to Mechanistic Reasoning in Biochemistry with METAL: An Integrated Framework for Course Design
papers.abstract: Content-heavy biochemistry courses can reward memorisation without supporting students in constructing chemical explanations of biomolecular phenomena. This Perspective presents METAL (Mechanistic Explanation and Transfer through Aligned Learning), an integrated framework for redesigning content-heavy courses around explanation and transfer. We illustrate the framework through a fourth-semester biochemistry course organised around three recurring explanatory resources: intermolecular interactions and bonding, thermodynamic driving forces, and electron density. Examples from enzyme kinetics, structural modelling, weekly tasks, and an oral examination show how these resources were reused across increasingly demanding contexts. METAL offers instructors a practical route from topic coverage to courses in which students repeatedly build, test, and transfer mechanistic chemical explanations.

papers.title: Solvent-directed Cathodic Deoxygenation of Carbonyl Compounds and Alcohols
papers.abstract: The deoxygenation of carbonyl compounds and alcohols is an important transformation in organic chemistry but remains challenging with respect to selectivity and resource efficiency. Herein, we present a metal-free electroreductive method for deoxygenation of both compound classes, which involves simple means (undivided cell, galvanostatic conditions) and covers a broad range of substrates in which the carbonyl/hydroxyl groups are each located in benzylic position. Key to success is the use of dimethyl carbonate (DMC) as a solvent, which promotes the formation of readily reducible methyl carbonate intermediates from the respective electrochemically inert alcohols. The in situ-formed methyl carbonate group thus plays a dual role, first as an electro-auxiliary supporting the accommodation of negative charge upon cathodic reduction, and then as efficient leaving group to facilitate formation of carbon-centered radical intermediates. In addition to a comprehensive investigation of the scope of alcohol and carbonyl substrates, including scale-up to the gram level, our work also includes a detailed mechanistic analysis based on cyclic voltammetry, control experiments, and quantum chemical calculations. The study illustrates how electrolyte engineering can be effectively used for steering the selectivity in electro-organic synthesis.

papers.title: On the role of surface oxidation for the nucleation delay in ALD of AlN
papers.abstract: The early stages of thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) of aluminium nitride (AlN) using trimethylaluminium (TMA) and ammonia (NH3) on Si (100) with a natural oxide was investigated using operando ambient pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS). Real-time monitoring of the O 1s, N 1s, C 1s, Si 2p, and Al 2p core levels reveal that TMA pulses consistently generate strong Al–O signals and surface-bound methyl ligands, but no evidence of nitrogen incorporation even after several ALD cycles. Subsequent NH3 exposures result only in weak, transient N 1s features assignable to adsorbed NH3 and –Al(CH3)2:NH3 surface species, with no signs of Al–N bonding. The surface remains dominated by Al–O bonding even after repeated ALD cycles at 250 °C, with nitrogen incorporation below the detection limit. This persistent absence of nitrogen uptake across multiple cycles identifies an extended nucleation delay as the dominant feature of the early growth regime, rather than a steady-state surface chemistry that simply favours one reaction pathway over another. These results demonstrate that TMA reacts readily with oxygen-containing surface groups, while NH3 is hindered from dissociating on methyl-terminated surfaces and is unfavourable relative to Al–O bond formation. The outcome is oxygen-driven growth, yielding Al–O rich material rather than AlN. Rather than a conventional picture of

papers.title: Direct synthesis of high aspect ratio chiral gold nanofibers
papers.abstract: Chirality, a fundamental characteristic of nature, plays a decisive role in molecular recognition, catalysis, and cellular organization. Translating this asymmetry into synthetic systems has the potential to unlock new functionalities at the interface of nanoscience and biology. Here, we report the first synthesis of high aspect ratio chiral gold nanofibers, a class of one-dimensional chiral plasmonic materials, fabricated via a seedless, soft-templated, ligandassisted growth method. Using D- and L-cysteine as chiral inducers, we direct the anisotropic reduction of gold ions to produce left- and right-handed nanofibers with tunable surface topologies. The resulting chiral gold nanofibers exhibit pronounced, mirror-symmetric circular dichroism signals and characteristic plasmonic resonances, confirming their intrinsic structural chirality. 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy analysis demonstrates that the atoms arrange in a chiral fashion, governing the final chirality of the gold nanofibers. Beyond their optical properties, these gold nanofibers provide topographical cues that promote directed neuron cell alignment when integrated into paper-based chips, offering a simple platform to model neuronal organization. Altogether, this effort establishes a scalable route to chiral gold architectures and demonstrates their capacity to couple plasmonic chirality with biological function, opening a new pathway for nanomaterials-based neuroregeneration.

papers.title: EZGA transition kernels bridge structure discovery and thermodynamic sampling in one engine
papers.abstract: We introduce a transition-kernel layer for EZGA, a modular evolutionary framework for atomistic structure exploration. The layer extends EZGA’s population-based optimization machinery into a statistically controlled sampling engine. Moves generate trial structures, while the selected kernel accepts, rejects, or reweights them. Different statistical methods are obtained by combining the required transition kernel and moves. The engine, archive, move pool, data model, and energy backend remain common across compatible methods. For methods with a stationary target distribution, the central abstraction is a move-level detailedbalance contract. Each move reports the logarithms of the probabilities or probability densities for proposing the forward and reverse transitions. The kernel combines their difference with the ensemble-specific target weight. This treatment supports asymmetric and particle-numberchanging moves without embedding ensemble corrections in individual moves. We implement and validate fifteen statistical methods spanning equilibrium sampling, density-of-states and partitionfunction reconstruction, generalized ensembles, and free-energy calculations. Each implementation is compared with reference solutions obtained by quadrature for a non-interacting gas and/or by exact enumeration for an interacting lattice gas. By placing structure exploration and thermodynamic sampling in the same engine, EZGA can follow candidate structures from discovery to statistical characterization. The same infrastructure can quantify their equilibrium populations, reconstruct free-energy landscapes, and compare competing states. Structure discovery thus becomes the starting point for thermodynamic characterization rather than the endpoint of a calculation.

papers.title: Measurement-Informed Methane Inventories for Colorado’s Upstream Oil and Gas Sector: Two Independent Modeling Approaches
papers.abstract: The state of Colorado is recognized as a leader in regulating oil and gas methane emissions, with Colorado requirements often influencing subsequent federal policy. Building on existing efforts, Colorado published a greenhouse gas intensity verification rule in 2023, requiring upstream operators to either create their own measurement-informed emissions inventory or multiply their bottom-up inventory by a state-developed default factor. This factor is intended to address known deficiencies in bottom-up emissions reporting by increasing the bottom-up inventory to match measured emissions. In this paper, we describe the aerial measurement campaign and subsequent modeling approaches used to create the 2026 default factor. Three aerial technology vendors (Bridger Photonics, GHGSat, and Insight M) performed over 30,000 scans of production facilities across Colorado, covering roughly 94% of the state’s oil and gas production facilities that were operating or partially operating. Using these aerial measurements as inputs, two independent models were developed to estimate state-wide annual methane emissions. One model uses a discrete event simulation tool, Mechanistic Air Emissions Simulator (MAES), to estimate total emissions, while the other model, referred to as the statistical model, is purely data-driven and estimates a facility-level emission rate distribution from the measurement data. MAES and the statistical model estimate upstream oil and gas emissions of 38.7 (35.3, 44.6) and 97.7 (84.4, 114.7) Gg/y, respectively, which are 1.47 (1.34, 1.69) and 3.70 (3.19, 4.34) times higher than the state’s bottom-up inventory.

papers.title: Treatment Pluralism in Full-Scale UV LED Wastewater Disinfection Showcasing Flexible Flow and Energy Control with Predictable Performance
papers.abstract: Wastewater treatment facilities (WWTFs) are currently facing multitudes of challenges including incline in population, climate change driven challenges and stringent regulation limits. Ultraviolet light emitting diodes (UV LEDs) are becoming an attractive disinfection system that has demonstrated powerful inactivation capabilities with modular system design, becoming a useful alternative treatment to conventional UV systems. A UVLED full-scale reactor was assessed for real municipal wastewater at the highest reported flow rates with a max flowrate of 2,725 m3 day-1. The reactor showed results ranging between 0.68 and 3 log reduction values for E. coli inactivation across the various high flowrates tested. The results accumulated throughout the study periods was further used to characterize the true capacity of the full-scale UV LED flow through reactor and demonstrated prediction capabilities through a sampling methodology. Furthermore, statistical analysis conducted between the two full-scale systems at the study site predicted probabilities of 66.5 and 25.6% of the UV LED system and conventional UV system for achieving 3 LRVs based on the data available throughout the study. Overall, the results provided by this study and the previous study by MacIsaac et al. (2024) demonstrated the performance and pluralist treatment variability of UV LED systems for wastewater treatment.

papers.title: An activity‑based high‑throughput screening platform for identifying functional modulators of OFF‑type riboswitches
papers.abstract: Structured regulatory RNAs, such as riboswitches, represent attractive yet challenging targets for small‑molecule discovery. Many existing screening approaches prioritize ligand binding over their function, such as controlling gene expression. Here, we describe an activity‑based high‑throughput screening platform designed to identify effector compounds of off‑type riboswitches by directly reporting transcriptional readthrough. The assay combines a miniaturized in vitro transcription system with a dual molecular beacon readout to enable discrimination between ligand‑induced riboswitch control and non‑specific effects such as transcriptional inhibition or fluorescence interference. Using a previously uncharacterized Staphylococcus aureus thiD thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) riboswitch as a model, we validate the platform against a radiolabelled in vitro transcription readthrough assay and demonstrate robust performance in a miniaturized 1536-well format. Screening of several diverse compound libraries did not yield validated non‑native modulators under the assay conditions and the chemical space explored, consistent with previous predictions of low druggability for the TPP riboswitch. Importantly, these results highlight the utility of the platform as a stringent functional filter that enables the identification of riboswitches that operate at the transcriptional level, the identification of effector ligands of bacterial RNA targets, and the assessment of the functional ligandability of RNA targets, thereby aiding in target prioritization.

papers.title: In situ Ni(II) to Ni(0) Reduction Enables Catalytic H2 Generation from Fe(II)-bearing Minerals
papers.abstract: Hydrogen is industrially produced at a scale of 70 million tons annually, with the majority of it derived from steam-methane reforming, an intensely emissions-heavy process. Vast reservoirs of mineralogical Fe(II) in the Earth’s subsurface and anthropogenic Fe(II) from steel slags represent an opportunity to stimulate mineralogical hydrogen by the reaction of hypoxic water with Fe(II)-rich phases, potentially allowing for both emissions-free and economically scalable hydrogen production. For select minerals, H 2 production from the coupled oxidation of Fe(II)-bearing solids is dramatically enhanced upon addition of Ni(II) ions, and mechanistic models posit that H 2 forms at co-precipitated Ni(II) sites bound to the ferrous substrate. Herein, we test this model by examining the temporal progression of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) driven by Fe(OH) 2 oxidation in presence of exogenous Ni(II). We find that Ni(II) is not the active catalyst, but instead serves as a pre-catalyst that is reduced in situ to metallic Ni(0) particles that then catalyze H 2 generation. This Ni(II) to Ni(0) conversion mechanism is also operative for hydrogen evolution from the mineral siderite (FeCO 3 ), suggesting that it may be a general mechanistic motif across ferrous minerals, which accelerates H 2 generation where HER is rate-limiting. These studies offer mechanistic insight into the in situ speciation of a catalyst commonly used for stimulated mineralogical hydrogen production, laying the foundation for further catalytic studies in the pursuit of evaluating and maximizing the potential of stimulated mineralogical hydrogen production.

papers.title: Molecular Origins of Lithium-Ion Transport in the Anionic Metal–Organic Framework SU-102
papers.abstract: Metal–organic framework (MOF) quasi-solid electrolytes offer chemically tunable environments for ion transport, but the molecular roles of framework coordination and confined solvent remain unclear. Here, we combined solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) measurements with molecular dynamics simulations to determine the Li+ transport mechanism in propylene carbonate-filled SU-102. Variable-temperature direct-and cross-polarization 7Li ssNMR reveal two distinct Li+ populations with different local tumbling dynamics. Our simulations identified Zr-associated, linkerassociated, and fully PC-solvated Li+ coordination environments. We found that Zrassociated sites provide the strongest thermodynamic stabilization, whereas the sitepersistence function decays more rapidly for linker-associated Li+ over the simulated interval. The linker-associated state exhibits the largest trial-weighted displacement, and linker-to-linker hopping is the most frequent classified event under the sampled fields, followed by Zr-to-Zr hopping. Chemical color-diffusion nonequilibrium molecular dynamics yielded an ionic conductivity of 1.34 ± 0.48 mS cm−1, the same order of magnitude as the experimental value of 0.52 mS cm−1. Together, our results support a picture in which PC-assisted hopping between linker sites contributes more strongly than vehicular diffusion of fully solvated ions under the simulated conditions. These findings identify the balance between ion–framework stabilization and facile site-to-site exchange as a key design principle for reticular quasi-solid electrolytes.

papers.title: Fully integrated, finite-volume-based, time-dependent multi-scale modeling of electrochemical CO2 reduction
papers.abstract: Electrochemical systems couple reaction kinetics and mass transport across multiple temporal and spatial scales. To address this multiscale coupling, we present an integrated Julia-based simulation framework for defining and solving complex kinetic–transport models. Specifically, CatmapInterface.jl enables the construction of mean-field reaction networks with adsorbate–adsorbate interactions and EDL chargingcorrected electrochemical kinetics, while LiquidElectrolytes.jl enables detailed EDL and mass-transport models. The resulting equations are solved monolithically using the finite-volume package VoronoiFVM.jl, yielding mass-conservative and numerically robust solutions under strong transport–kinetics coupling. As an example, we study CO2 reduction on gold, for which steady-state simulations show consistent results with a previous finite-element-based implementation but improved numerical stability. Timedependent cyclic-voltammetry simulations further provide an explanation for the experimentally observed double peak in CO re-oxidation during the anodic sweep as arising from hydroxide depletion and delayed buffer equilibration. The framework thus provides a powerful tool for nonequilibrium multiscale simulations of complex electrochemical systems.

papers.title: Testing Small Parameterized Quantum Circuits for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) are widely proposed as feature transformations in quantum machine learning (QML) pipelines. However, few molecular-QML studies combine strong classical baselines, repeated training runs, and controls that separate a quantum branch from its trainable anglegenerating encoder. We benchmark three-qubit PQCs combined with two pretrained molecular embeddings, MiniMol and CheMeleon, for lipophilicity and solubility prediction. Five model variants, including a classical baseline, two hybrid quantum-classical architectures, a quantum-only model, and a frozen-branch control, were evaluated on two datasets, two embeddings, and five random seeds, giving 100 runs. No tested quantum variant showed a statistically detectable improvement over the classical baseline after falsediscovery-rate correction across all 16 paired comparisons. The frozen-branch control also showed no detectable advantage over the classical baseline. This control freezes the full angle-generating quantum branch, not an independent set of variational circuit weights. A separate one-qubit depolarizing-noise sweep showed no detectable change in accuracy over the tested error range. Quantum variants required 18–37 times longer training time than the classical baseline on the same platform. These results set a benchmark for small parameterized QML layers applied to the pretrained molecular representations and ADME tasks examined here.

papers.title: Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal
papers.abstract: Thermally induced solid-state polymorphic transitions in an n-hexyl-functionalized naphthalenediimide organic semiconductor (NDI-C6) are investigated using atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. NDI-C6 exhibits two stable polymorphs: the α phase at room temperature and the γ phase at higher temperatures. The MD simulations reproduce the structural stability of both phases and provide a refined description of their unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations, which have been only partially resolved experimentally. The α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, non-concerted two-step mechanism. An initial fast (sub-nanosecond) process involves the collective rearrangement of the NDI cores, followed by a slow process (>100 ns) characterized by side-chain extension. These results provide an atomistic picture of polymorphism in NDI-C6 and establish a robust computational protocol for investigating labile phase transitions in the broader class of NDIbased n-type soft organic semiconductors.

papers.title: Synergistic Energetic Realignment and Interfacial Passivation via Perovskite Nanocrystal-Doped Spiro-OMeTAD for Efficient Planar Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Non-radiative recombination at the perovskite/hole transport layer (HTL) interface fundamentally constrains the open-circuit voltage (Voc) and charge-collection efficiency of planar perovskite solar cells. In this work, we report an effective interface engineering strategy of incorporating MAPb (IxBr1-x)3 nanocrystals (NC) into a Spiro-OMeTAD matrix which is used as HTL. Consequently, planar n-i-p devices incorporating the composite HTL deliver an enhanced power conversion efficiency of 20.31 %, highlighted by a surge in 𝑉𝑜𝑐 (up to 1.1 V) alongside stable photocurrent density of 24.62 mA cm −2 . Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) reveals that NC incorporation results in reduced bulk resistance of the Spiro-OMeTAD layer. Furthermore, systematic analysis of the characteristic time constant extracted from EIS measurements provides evidence of halide-ion redistribution which modulate the interfacial energetics and enhance the built-in electric field, thereby contributing to the observed improvement in PCE. This work highlights the potential of nanocrystal-engineered HTLs as an effective approach for potential suppression of interfacial recombination and developing defectpassivated, high-voltage perovskite solar cells.

papers.title: Redox Chemistry of the Cyclononatetraenyl Ligand: A Tale of Radical Coupling, Homo – and Möbius Aromaticity, and Comproportionation
Kinetic Criteria for Finite CSTR Staging toward Plug-Flow Performance
papers.abstract: Finite CSTR cascades converge hydrodynamically toward plug flow as the number of stages increases, but the number of stages required to preserve reaction performance cannot be determined from residence-time variance alone. This work derives a dimensionless kinetic staging coefficient for equal-volume CSTR cascades by combining the composition dependence of the reaction-rate vector with the sensitivity of a selected outlet objective. The coefficient is invariant to uniform acceleration of all reaction rates, is exactly zero for common-factor parallel selectivity, and reaches its consecutive-reaction maximum when formation and consumption time scales are matched. In a nonlinear xylose-dehydration network, the coefficient passes through an interior maximum as concentration-dependent and direct furfural-loss rates become comparable. The leading coefficient sets the stage-count scale required to retain a specified fraction of optimized PFR performance, while higher-order terms account for finite-stage corrections. Published kinetic systems show that reaction time, attainable yield, and staging requirement can vary independently. The resulting criterion links reaction kinetics directly to the finite number of mixed stages required to approximate a specified PFR objective.

papers.title: What Cycle Closure Can and Cannot See in a Relative Binding Free Energy Network
papers.abstract: Cycle closure is the standard consistency check on a perturbation network, and what such a check can see is fixed by the gradient–cycle decomposition of edge flows (HodgeRank): the cycle part of a network’s error is auditable and biases nothing, while the gradient part biases the affinities and is invisible to any statistic computed from the network’s own values, at any magnitude. Both parts are measured here on 1145 real binding edges. The auditable subspace spans a third of the error space and, in the variance-weighted metric the closure statistic uses, carries under one per cent of the error against experiment. Experimental and annotation error is per-ligand, so it falls in the invisible part by construction and can only have made that share smaller: the measurement is a floor, and it survives correction: in the metric the closure statistic uses on every system measured, at one cell as a tie, and in an isotropic reading on every system of the wider grounded set, failing only on the two weakest of the four the test itself selected. The test built on it behaves as the bound predicts, and its flag set is not stable: the per-edge residuals and the ranking of systems reproduce across independent repeats, and the list of flagged systems does not. Fitting closure against the precisions the estimator already reports gives that test its stated null; it ties the standard fixed 1.0 kcal/mol cutoff, and on every replicate the set of systems it flags lies inside the set that cutoff flags. It flags nothing once the reported errors are widened by half, enough to cover the pose and preparation variance the protocol repeats hold fixed, and it names no removal that recovers accuracy against experiment. Resolving the gradient part needs measurements from outside the network, at worst one per unresolved dimension.

papers.title: Realistic Simulations of Energy Materials Using Foundation Models and Electrode-Potential Learning
papers.abstract: Here, we evaluate SevenNet-Omni [Kim et al., Nat. Commun. 2026, 17, 3432], a universal machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP), in realistic energy-material systems whose long timescale simulations are beyond the practical reach of density-functional theory (DFT). Tests span explicit solvation, metal-support interfaces, and reactive battery surfaces and interfaces, all of which involve realistic cross-domain interactions between inorganic materials and organic species. Without system-specific fine-tuning, SevenNet-Omni achieves sufficient accuracy for these out-of-domain systems, demonstrating strong transferability. To extend MLIPs to electrochemical systems, we also develop a model that predicts work-function changes across surface configurations. The model achieves errors of approximately 0.1 V, suggesting the usefulness of the approach for simulating energy systems under applied electrode bias potentials. Together, these results highlight the potential of foundation MLIPs for simulating next-generation energy systems.

papers.title: DNA Directed Chemistry: Scalable Programmed DNA-Encoded Library Synthesis for More Chemically Diverse and Drug-Like Libraries
papers.abstract: DNA-Encoded Libraries (DELs) are indispensable high-throughput platforms in drug discovery, but the widely adopted split-and-pool synthesis method is fundamentally limited: the DNA merely records, rather than directs, the steps of chemistry. This lack of programmatic control imposes mandatory downstream chemistry congruency, restricts structural diversity, and inevitably generates a combinatorial explosion of un-drug-like molecules, hindering both hit-finding and the acquisition of structurally informative data required for machine learning (ML) models. To resolve these core constraints, we developed Programmed DEL Synthesis (PDS), a robust, industrially applicable platform for non-combinatorial DEL construction in which the DNA actively directs the synthesis. PDS is built upon a sort-and-pool mechanism expanded by three key innovations: sequence-specific installation of first building blocks using charged carrier codons, a multinomial encoding strategy that enables libraries exceeding 20 billion unique encodings in three chemical steps, and non-combinatorial germline assembly that allows for the programmatic omission of undesirable building block combinations. We demonstrate the platform with Library i01, a three-step, threepathway library employing 137 trifunctional scaffolds. The design successfully programmed the systematic merging and un-merging of three mutually incompatible reaction pathways: Acid→Aldehyde→Amine, Amine→Aldehyde→Acid, and Aldehyde→Acid→Amine within a single synthesis. Pilot affinity selections against Carbonic Anhydrase (BCA-II) validated the high fidelity of DNA encoding and efficient building block installation across all steps and pathways, confirming the platform's robust utility for selection. PDS transforms chemical congruency and drug-likeness into programmable properties, offering a precise, efficient solution that improves library quality without sacrificing chemical space. Crucially, PDS enables the construction of structurally tailored 2nd Generation DELs needed to provide the high-resolution data required for productive ML-driven active learning cycles, establishing a critical operational link for modern drug development.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by the authors because a contributor should not have been listed. An updated version is available at 10.26434/chemrxiv.15007800/v3.

papers.title: Scale-Invariant Work and State Functions: Connecting Kullback-Leibler and Bregman Divergences to Chemical Conversions and Fundamental Equations of State
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic work function vectors formalize the energetic principles governing scale-invariant process trajectories and equilibria via relative entropy representations along a directional path trajectory e p . While macroscopic processes are inherently irreversible, chemical transformations originate from microscopic reversibility along a positive time coordinate, where the non-dimensionalized work function vector maps directly to the statistical Kullback-Leibler divergence D KL. This divergence determines chemical conversion and equilibrium, altering the intensive properties that drive macroscopic boundary gradients. By transforming this statistical description into a geometric representation over Hessian manifolds, the formulation systematically maps non-ideal fluid phases and localized structural configurations, extending explicitly to long-range gravitational fields. This mapping establishes that the non-dimensionalized thermodynamic state space of the non-flat system is directly corrected by the asymmetric Bregman divergence D Ψ formulated with respect to a physically fixed ideal reference baseline. The resulting fundamental equation of state resolves fluid phase coexistence directly via the global convex envelope of the work function landscape. Through this formulation, the developed work and state functions unify the microscopic phase space and the macroscopic state space into a single, consistent conceptual framework mediated by the non-dimensionalized entropy vector s . To track non-equilibrium trajectories within long-range gradients, a secondary geometrical operator acts as a kinetic functional, yielding a dual-metric framework. This structure defines a total time-dependent state transformation vector l state(τ ) that isolates path-dependent transport kinetics from the static landscape. The transport dynamics enforce a monotonic reduction in the transient distance metric until the trajectory collapses onto the stationary identity defined via the Bregman divergence, validating the work function vector as a scale-invariant process property anchored across all spatial magnitudes. Consequently, an energy-time duality is established, reconciling microscopic reversibility along the forward trajectory with macroscopic thermodynamic irreversibility.

papers.title: Predicting CYP450 Induction and PXR Activation with Machine Learning Approaches: Challenges and Opportunities
papers.abstract: Many drugs increase the activity of cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes, an effect known as induction, which is a major cause of harmful drug-drug interactions (DDIs). Predicting induction from chemical structure would help identify DDI risks early in compound development. Yet, unlike many other drug properties, CYP450 induction is rarely modeled, because the data needed to train models is scarce and expensive to produce. Using an industry-scale dataset covering induction of three CYP450 enzymes (CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP1A2) and PXR activation, we benchmark four machine learning models across six molecular representations and compare performance against models trained on a curated public dataset. On the internal data, the best models separate inducers from non-inducers moderately well (MCC ~0.5) but cannot predict the magnitude of induction, and no model or representation does meaningfully better, pointing to the data rather than the method as the limit. The same pattern holds in public data, where a large public PXR set reaches this range, while a small, heterogeneous public CYP3A4 set fails where the data is scarcer and noisier. We then show that the shared biology of these endpoints carries a usable signal. A model trained on one endpoint partly predicts the others, and this transfer follows the known regulatory relationships between PXR and the CYP450 enzymes, so these biological links can serve as useful inductive biases for future models. Finally, we found that the models we trained are already reasonably well calibrated, which, combined with their classification performance, makes them useful for prioritizing compounds today.

papers.title: Fluorescent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Chemical Sensing: Design Strategies, Mechanisms, and Analytical Applications
papers.abstract: Fluorescent metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as transformative platforms for chemical sensing, combining ultrahigh porosity, tunable optical properties, and versatile host-guest chemistry to achieve exceptional sensitivity and selectivity. This review synthesizes recent advances (2018-2025, with emphasis on 2021-2025) in the design, synthesis, and application of luminescent MOF sensors for environmental monitoring, biomedical diagnostics, and food safety. Three interconnected themes are examined: (1) design principles governing fluorescence tuning through ligand engineering, metal node selection, and pore architecture optimization; (2) synthesis strategies and composite architectures enhancing stability and sensitivity, including post-synthetic modification, lanthanide functionalization, and MOF-dye hybrids; and (3) sensing mechanisms (photoinduced electron transfer [PET], Forster resonance energy transfer [FRET], and inner filter effects [IFE]) and their translation into analytical applications achieving sub-parts-per-billion detection limits and rapid response times. Representative systems demonstrate exceptional performance: Ag12bpy-NH2 achieves 0.1 ppm oxygen detection in 0.3 s, LCU-109 detects Fe3+ and Cu2+ at 0.0043 and 0.0028 ppm in river 2 water, and Zr-CAU-24 enables 5-min aflatoxin B1 screening in beverages. Despite these advances, persistent challenges, including water stability, photostability quantification, mechanistic standardization, and scalable manufacturing, limit widespread deployment. Critical research gaps are identified, including the need for quantitative structure-property models, long-term operational stability data, and techno-economic analyses. Coordinated interdisciplinary efforts in materials innovation, standardized validation protocols, and device integration are proposed as enabling pathways for MOF sensor translation from laboratory demonstrations to validated analytical tools within 3-5 years.

papers.title: Quantifying Fragment Ambiguity inLC-ESI-HRMS-MS2 Spectral Databases
papers.abstract: LC–MS/HRMS-based non-target analysis relies heavily on MS2 spectral matching for compound annotation. However, not all fragments contribute equally to identification confidence, and quantitative measures of fragment ambiguity remain lacking. In this study, we developed a data-driven probabilistic framework to assess fragment level diagnostic power through the Fragment Ambiguity Score (FAS), which combines fragment stability and specificity within precursor-mass-defined candidate spaces. FAS was evaluated using five experimental spectral databases (MassBank, MoNA, GNPS, NIST20, and MSnLib), comprising together of 1,026,855 spectra and an in silico spectral library containing 256,865 spectra. The results showed that MS2 spectra contain fragments with substantially different levels of ambiguity. Using FAS ≤ 0.5 as 12 the threshold for diagnostic fragments, only 14.1% of fragments in the experimental databases and 10.7% in the in silico library were classified as diagnostic. Fragments appearing highly diagnostic in smaller databases often become substantially more ambiguous when evaluated against larger and more diverse spectral collections. Comparison of experimental and in silico spectral databases further illustrated that fragment ambiguity estimates depend on database origin and composition. Application of FAS to suspect screening and spectral library matching demonstrated that fragment level ambiguity provides complementary evidence to spectral similarity. These findings demonstrate that the number of matched fragments alone is insufficient for confidence assessment and highlight the importance of complementary sources of evidence. The proposed framework provides a quantitative basis for assessing fragment ambiguity in spectral databases.

papers.title: Cross-exposure transferability and failure boundaries of self-supervised DNN denoising for AR-HAXPES depth profiling
papers.abstract: Laboratory-source angle-resolved hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (AR-HAXPES) is photon-starved at the spatial resolution required for mapping, where the frame averaging needed to recover a clean depth profile at every position drives total acquisition time into a prohibitive regime. Self-supervised deep-neural-network (DNN) denoising offers an alternative to acquisition-time scaling, and a recent companion study has systematically benchmarked its performance against alternative strategies; however, its operational envelope across exposures, its cross-exposure transferability, and its failure modes in the photon-starved regime remain uncharacterized. Here we evaluate self-supervised denoising at the smallest possible target window across three exposures spanning a 25-fold range of per-frame photon flux on a model C / Al₂O₃ / TiO₂ / Si multilayer. We find cross-exposure denoiser deployment to agree with an empirical directional rule — train signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) ≥ inference S/N — characterize the failure boundary in the photon-starved regime where upstream denoiser collapse propagates into constraint-saturated inversion solutions, and locate the asymptotic reach of all tested denoising strategies (frame averaging, Self-DNN, Cross-DNN) relative to a methodological floor set by the reproducibility of the reference. Within the success region of this rule, cross-exposure transfer enables up to a 48-fold equivalent acquisition-time reduction on the depth root-mean-square error (RMSE) axis (14-fold on the Wasserstein-1 interface-localization axis) at the most photon-starved 4.8 s/frame condition. These results frame self-supervised AR-HAXPES denoising as a characterizable engineering operation with quantifiable failure boundaries and recovery routes, rather than as an empirical post-processing recipe.

papers.title: Nanomechanical Insights into Curing-Driven Morphological Evolution in Crumpled Polyamide Nanofiltration Membranes
papers.abstract: Crumpled polyamide thin films are widely used as selective layers in nanofiltration membranes, where morphology strongly influences water transport and solute separation. Although crumpled morphology is commonly discussed in terms of reaction-diffusion processes during interfacial polymerization (IP), increasing evidence suggests an important yet less understood role of thermal curing as an active morphology-evolution step. Here, we combine amplitude-modulation frequency-modulation (AM-FM) atomic force microscopy, in situ heating measurements, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), finite element analysis (FEA), and nanofiltration testing to examine how thermal curing reshapes crumpled polyamide nanofiltration membranes. Thermal curing simultaneously increases surface roughness and XPS-estimated crosslinking while decreasing Young’s modulus, indicating that the nanomechanical softening occurs concurrently with curing-associated chemical evolution. In situ AFM measurements and FEA reveal that pre-existing nanomechanical heterogeneity generates spatially heterogeneous thermal stress that may promote ridge amplification and growth during thermal curing. Membranes with amplified crumpled morphology exhibit enhanced water permeance while maintaining high salt rejection. Together, these results support a working framework in which reaction-diffusion processes establish a heterogeneous precursor film, while thermal curing promotes coupled morphological, nanomechanical, and chemical evolution. This study highlights thermal curing as an active materials-processing parameter for controlling polyamide thin-film morphology and nanofiltration function.

papers.title: Pathway-Resolved Observable Memory Reveals Hidden Mediation from Sparse Conformational Measurements
papers.abstract: Biomolecular conformational transitions are often characterized through measuring a small number of observables, leading to memory functions due to the fact the underlying dynamics involve many coupled and hidden degrees of freedom. Here we discuss extraction of effective memory from molecular simulation data with a transfer tensor approach. We then use a hierarchy of models to examine what mechanistic information can be gleaned from such extracted memory. An analytically solvable model that involves coupled harmonic oscillators shows how memory modes encode local and shared hidden-bath couplings in an ideal limit. A nonlinear double-well potential coupled bilinearly to a harmonic bath provides an analytical Zwanzig memory kernel, which we compare with transfer tensors extracted from trajectory data to distinguish physical bath friction from effective observable memory.
