In vivo PET-CT imaging in healthy mice revealed the biodistribution of SDends to be typical of long circulating nanoparticles, with a significant portion of particles remaining in circulation 96 h post-injection (p.i.), alongside a positive trend between pSar chain length and blood circulation time, with 56 repeat units of pSar required to prolong the blood circulation time. Moreover, a greater percentage of particles remained in circulation 96 h p.i. than were sequestered by the liver for SD56 and SD100, highlighting the stealth impact of pSar. Notable uptake in the bone marrow was also observed alongside variable uptake in the female reproductive system. SDends overall possess a favourable biodistribution pattern with minimal immune sequestration, holding great potential for tumour targeting applications.

papers.title: Site-Resolved Prediction of Mayr Nucleophilicity with Reactivity-Pretrained Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: The magnitude of a compound’s nucleophilicity is pivotal to mechanistic studies and rational catalyst design. Over the past decades, Mayr and co-workers developed an invaluable framework for quantifying nucleophilicity, comprising N parameters. Nevertheless, achieving accurate nucleophilic site prediction and low-cost quantification remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we construct a nucleophilicity prediction model, termed PPGNS (Pretrained and Physicochemical feature–augmented Graph neural network model for joint Nucleophilicity and Site prediction). By integrating carefully designed physicochemical and physical organic descriptors and extended tight-binding (xTB) calculations, graph neural networks (GNN) are employed to predict the N parameters, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) adopted for mechanistic interpretation. The PPGNS model achieves a higher accuracy and efficiency performance for N prediction relative to previous benchmark studies, with R 2 of 0.94 and 0.95 for automatic-site and known-site evaluations, both from pooled (out of fold) OOF predictions across five outer folds. Most notably, PPGNS enables site-resolved nucleophilicity prediction, achieving 93% Top-1 and 98% Top-3 recovery of nucleophilic reaction sites, a capability not reported in previous studies.

papers.title: The Teaching Effects of a Chemistry-Specific AI Assistant: An Empirical Study Using Difference-in-Differences
papers.abstract: To examine the core value of introducing domain-specific artificial intelligence (AI) teaching assistants in higher education, this study takes the “Organic Chemistry A” course in the Department of Chemistry at Tsinghua University as a case. Adopting a difference-in-differences (DID) approach, the pilot class equipped with an AI teaching assistant (e.g. ChemBot) was set as the treatment group, while a parallel class in the same period served as the control group. Focusing on two core indicatorslearning engagement and higher-order thinking skills—and accounting for heterogeneity based on students’ backgrounds in high school chemistry competitions, this study systematically evaluates the net effect of AI-enabled teaching. The findings indicate that the introduction of the AI teaching assistant increased students’ learning engagement by 13% (with most of the increase attributable to interactions with the AI assistant) and enhanced higher-order thinking skills by 32%. For students without competition awards, the improvement in learning engagement was more pronounced (25%), while for awardwinning students, the enhancement in higher-order thinking skills was more substantial (41%). Mechanism analysis reveals that AI facilitates a chain pathway of “pre-class motivation–self-directed inquiry–interdisciplinary practice,” leading to a dual improvement in students’ learning initiative and cognitive depth, while significantly reducing the teaching burden on instructors. This research provides empirical evidence for the integration of “AI + education” focused on core educational objectives.

papers.title: Mapping Structured Absences in Scientific Papers: An Auditable LLM-Assisted Workflow Demonstrated on Cross-Coupling Chemistry
papers.abstract: Scientific papers record what was discovered and communicated, but the resolution at which evidence relations are made explicit—a paper’s documentary resolution—often falls short of what later computational reuse, benchmarking, or data-driven synthesis requires. We present UQS (Unasked Question Structuring), an auditable LLM-assisted pipeline that takes scientific papers as input and produces structured absence records with evidence chains, an Evidence Pack (EP) dictionary specifying the evidence needed to reach the next evidential level, a bounded filling-status map across later literature under pre-locked criteria, and cross-paper research-question briefs. Applied to Kumada’s 1972 Ni-catalysed cross-coupling communication over a 54-year record window (1972–2026), UQS derives ten EPs and reveals a VQ-hierarchy inversion: methodology-level documentation is addressed early, whereas system-matched mechanistic documentation (VQ-3) appears only after 49 years (Mazet 2021), and quantitative-reliability documentation (VQ-4) remains a bounded non-detection—a pattern consistent with publication-incentive structure. The paper claims auditability, configuration-pinned rerun consistency, and internal robustness (four-model cross-comparison, N=6 multi-run aggregation); external expert validation is registered as future work.

papers.title: Label-Free mapping of nanoscale polarization heterogeneity in supramolecular fibers
papers.abstract: Supramolecular fibers often contain hidden nanoscale structural heterogeneity that influences their functional properties. Resolving this local molecular organization typically requires extrinsic fluorophores, which can perturb the native assembly. Here, we introduce sequential polarization-dependent STORM (SPD-STORM), a label-free super-resolution approach to map nanoscale polarization heterogeneity in intrinsically blinking SachCHO supramolecular fibers. By sequentially imaging under orthogonal excitation polarizations, SPD-STORM reveals that individual fibers contain alternating polarization-preferential and mixed domains along their length. Furthermore, bundled thick fibers exhibit transverse polarization heterogeneity, supporting a hierarchical assembly of distinct thin fibrils. We demonstrate that assembly temperature modulates this nanoscale architecture; lower temperatures favor longer polarization-preferential domains, whereas higher temperatures produce greater polarization mixing and closer blinking hotspots. Ultimately, SPD-STORM uncovers local molecular organization invisible to bulk morphological analysis.

papers.title: Soft and Hard X-ray 1s and 2p Photoelectron Spectroscopy of La(TM)O3 (TM = Cr, Fe, Co)
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive soft X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (HAXPES) investigation of LaCrO 3 , LaFeO 3 , and LaCoO 3 perovskite oxide thin films. Measurements at excitation energies of 1.8 keV (XPS), as well as 5.9 keV and 11.8 keV (HAXPES), yield consistent elemental compositions and chemical states, with differences in relative intensities reflecting variations in photoionization cross-sections and probing depth. The analysis of La 3 d and 4 d core levels highlights strong final-state hybridization effects and characteristic satellite structures associated with ligand-to-La charge transfer. Transition-metal (TM) 1 s and 2 p spectra reveal element-specific chemical shifts, spin–orbit splittings, and charge-transfer satellites, enabling quantitative comparison across the three perovskites. Valence-band spectra exhibit clear separation between the TM 3 d and oxygen 2 p states, consistent with previous reports. The valence-band and TM 1 s and 2 p core-level spectra are simulated within the dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) framework combined with the Anderson impurity model.

papers.title: Merging CO2 reduction and carbonylation into a single catalytic platform
papers.abstract: Conversion of carbon dioxide into value-added molecules remains a central scientific challenge with major environmental and societal implications. A compelling strategy is combining CO 2 reduction to CO with catalytic carbonylation. However, until now this approach has been limited to systems operating under demanding or specialised conditions. A truly simplified strategy enabling seamless integration of both transformations still remains elusive. Here we demonstrate how deliberate parameter overlap allows for a merged reductive photocatalytic platform to be used for direct coupling of CO 2 reduction with carbonylation protocols for the first time in a single vessel. Shared use of phenol as proton source and nucleophile and phosphine as oxygen acceptor and electron-donor for EDA activation enables direct coupling of CO 2 -derived-CO with alkyl iodides towards esters and amides. Most importantly, by focusing on reaction compatibility, rather than compartmentalization, we provide a general blueprint for designing integrated and efficient catalytic platforms that couple CO 2 activation with downstream bond-forming reactions for sustainable synthesis.

papers.title: Controlled Generation of Unstabilized N-Alkyl Nitrile Imines Enables Regioselective [3+2] Cycloadditions with Diverse Dipolarophiles
papers.abstract: N-Alkyl nitrile imines remain underdeveloped as intermediates for intermolecular cycloaddition. Here, we report their in situ generation and regioselective [3+2] cycloaddition with activated and unactivated alkenes and alkynes, affording N-alkyl pyrazolines and pyrazoles in good to excellent yields. The method accommodates broad variation in both reaction partners and enables gram-scale preparation of a key pyrazole fragment used in the synthesis of lenacapavir in 79% yield over two steps.

papers.title: Visible Light-Driven Hydrogen Production with Hydrated Electrons in Neat Water Using a Single-Molecule Catalyst
papers.abstract: The generation of molecular hydrogen with visible light typically relies on multi-component systems requiring two photons per catalytic turnover. Single-molecule photocatalysts combining light-harvesting and electron-accumulation are attractive alternatives, but reported systems suffer from expensive donors, organic co-solvents or moderate activity. We introduce a two-photon mechanism in neat water that releases hydrated electrons for proton reduction, generating hydrogen atoms as key intermediates. A bench-stable iridium complex, accessible in two synthetic steps, serves as the single-molecule photocatalyst and enables a competitive initial turnover frequency exceeding 20 h -1 under blue-light irradiation. The process requires only sodium sulfite as an unusually inexpensive sacrificial donor. The combination of laboratory-scale irradiation and detailed spectroscopic studies provides deep mechanistic insight into this previously unexplored pathway. We identify a pH of ~5 as ideal to achieve proton reduction while maintaining sufficient activity of the sacrificial donor in its dual role as electron source and hydrogen atom donor. Our results demonstrate that a photon accumulation approach is a viable alternative to conventional electron accumulation. Beyond hydrogen generation, our platform is highly promising for further reaction classes, such as homogeneous radical hydrogenations, owing to the catalytic generation of free hydrogen atoms.

papers.title: Synthesis, physical, chemical and biological properties of a M(CO)3 (M = Cr, Mo, W, Mn, Re) matched quintet
papers.abstract: A matched quintet bis-quinoline tricarbonyl complex was synthesized across Group 6/7 transition metals (M = Cr, Mo, W, Mn, Re). The complexes display trends in structure and bonding, observed by X-ray crystallography, NMR, Infrared, UV-Vis and fluorescence. Biological testing reveals high activity for Group 7 complexes against Gram-positive bacteria. Post-synthetic functionalisation with Click chemistry was explored.

papers.title: SmartReact: An Open-Source Python Package for Scalable Forward Synthesis Enumeration Built on Interpretable SMARTS Templates
papers.abstract: Predicting which products can be made from a set of building blocks underpins library design, analogue generation, and synthesis-constrained generative modelling. Reaction templates encoded as SMARTS patterns are the standard tool for this forward synthesis enumeration task. However, existing approaches force a trade-off between chemical coverage, specificity, and the computational cost of applying large template sets at scale. We present SmartReact, an open-source Python library whose template set inverts that trade-off, because the construction that produces the specificity is the same construction that makes the templates cheap to eliminate. Its templates are combinatorial expansions over SMARTS-RX, a fixed hierarchical functional group ontology of 406 patterns, so the library exposes only a few hundred distinct reactant-side patterns no matter how many templates it holds, and one classification per molecule resolves thousands of templates at once. Every prediction of SmartReact is traceable to a named reaction and an explicit set of functional group requirements, making results directly interpretable by chemists and straightforward to audit. New reaction types can be incorporated by specifying a SMARTS pattern and its functional group requirements, making the library easy to extend. A case study enumerating 536,171 unique products from 1,000 building blocks in 15.7 s demonstrates real-world utility at scale. Scientific Contribution: SmartReact contributes a large, expert-refined SMARTS reaction template library together with an open-source Python package designed to use it efficiently. The library's 9,770 templates spanning 37 medicinal chemistry reaction types are generated by combinatorial expansion over the SMARTS-RX functional group ontology, which gives them a chemical specificity and non-redundancy that auto-extracted libraries lack and, at the same time, a bounded reactant-side pattern space that makes them cheap to pre-filter.

papers.title: A Novel Operando Tool for Mechanochemistry: NQR spectroscopy
papers.abstract: In this contribution we present for the first time an operando study of mechanochemical syntheses relying on Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance spectroscopy (NQR). This method represents, to date, the best functional alternative to NMR spectroscopy for the real-time monitoring of ball-milling (BM) syntheses. Two mechanochemical syntheses were followed in operando mode by NQR, namely the formation of a halogen-bonded cocrystal and the preparation of a hybrid perovskite, demonstrating potential applications of this novel technique, as well as its complementarity to more conventional operando methods used in mechanochemistry. Lastly, we show that our BM-NQR set-up can also be used in real-time to follow the temperature evolution directly inside the milling jar.

papers.title: Neutral Ligands, Distinct Zeta Potentials: Consequences for Hafnium Oxide Nanoparticles Biodistribution
papers.abstract: Nanoparticles are extensively explored in biological contexts, and while their core composition determines their specific functionality, surface chemistry governs their interactions with the biological environment. In this work, we used ultrasmall (d < 5 nm) hafnium oxide nanoparticles as a model system, given their biocompatibility and established use in contrast-enhanced X-ray computed tomography and external-beam radiotherapy. We systematically compared three surface ligands featuring the samehigh-affinity nitrocatechol anchoring group but different terminal moieties: a short ethylene glycol (EG) oligomer, a 2 kDa polyethylene glycol (PEG) polymer, and a short zwitterionic (ZW) chain. Despite the neutral character of all ligand tails, only the long PEG chains yielded nanoparticles with a near-neutral zeta potential. The short ligands produced nanoparticles with significantly negative zeta potentials (-30mV), which was found to be an essential component of their colloidal stability. NPs stabilized with short EG or ZW ligands exhibited enhanced uptake by THP-1 macrophages in vitro and short circulation times in vivo in zebrafish larvae, despite low in vitro protein corona formation on ZW nanoparticles. In contrast, nanoparticles stabilized with long PEG chains largely escaped detection by the phagocyte system. They exhibited prolonged circulation and extravasation in the zebrafish larva model, highlighting their promise for future targeted nanomedicine delivery. Zeta potential showed the strongest correlation with macrophage uptake and biodistribution. It reflects the combined effect of different physicochemical parameters (e.g. surface charge and steric shielding) and proved to be more predictive than the ligand architecture alone.

papers.title: Acrylate-Scavenging Beads Enable High-Throughput Purification of Copolymer Libraries
papers.abstract: High-throughput polymer science provides new opportunities to accelerate materials discovery. Acrylate copolymerization provides rapid access to diverse polymer libraries but requires equally rapid, parallel purification to remove unreacted monomers. Here, we report low-cost thiol-functionalized acrylatescavenging beads (Beads–SH), prepared in two steps from a commercial ion-exchange resin, that efficiently remove residual acrylates through thiol–Michael addition. The beads achieved nearquantitative removal of diverse small-molecule acrylates within 12 h and remained effective in both organic solvents and water. Sizerestricted access to the reactive sites within the beads minimized polymer adsorption and side reactions, with no measurable changes in polymer composition, molar mass, or dispersity. As a proof of concept, Beads–SH were used in a microplate format to purify a 72-member library of amphiphilic acrylate copolymers and evaluate polymer-mediated modulation of enzyme activity. This inexpensive, practical, and accessible strategy enables rapid purification of polyacrylate libraries for high-throughput materials discovery.

papers.title: Vacancy Ordering Mediated Symmetry Breaking in a Twinned Lacunar CsCl-Related Phase: Cr1−𝛿Ni2Ga4 (𝛿 ≈ 0.2)
papers.abstract: This investigation focuses on the high temperature synthesis and characterization using the single crystal and powder X-ray diffraction analysis of a partly disordered ternary intermetallic phase Cr 1−𝛿 Ni 2 Ga 4 , 𝛿 ≈0.2 within the CsCl-related 𝑇 3 Ga 4 family. With increase in annealing time during synthesis, the vacancy-disordered cubic (𝐹𝑚3̅𝑚, 𝑎 = 5.77 Å) phase transforms into a vacancy-ordered tetragonal phase (𝐼4 1 /𝑎𝑚𝑑, 𝑎 = 5.77 Å, 𝑐 = 11.54 Å) with three perpendicular twin domains. The superstructure reflections corresponding to vacancy ordering can be observed with both the single crystal and powder X-ray diffraction. Although the phase could not be separated in its pure form, the DFT simulations on the tetragonal model suggest the phase is suspectable to antiferromagnetic ordering. The partial occupancy of the Cr is rationalized by the antibonding populations near the fermi level. Furthermore, the variations in atomic sizes and electronegativities among the first-row transition metals provide additional insight to rationalize the structural distinctions of Co, and Fe containing analogues with the Cr-containing phase in the broader CsCl type/related 𝑇 3 Ga 4 family and providing a rational pathway to discover novel intermetallic phases.

papers.title: Microscopy Paired Fluorophores for Live Cell FLIM and STED Imaging of Intracellular Lipids Structures
papers.abstract: A novel approach is described in which a microscopy pairing of two fluorophores is used to image intracellular lipid structures in living cells using FLIM and STED. The fluorophore pair employed have similar absorption and emission wavelengths but differing lifetimes. The intracellular lifetimes being measured as 2.9 and 5.7 ns were both insensitive to microenvironmental changes such as viscosity and polarity. Their structural design was relatively uncomplicated, avoiding the use of substituents to induce TICT or PeT photophysical processes, with one containing alcohol substituents and the other not. When administrated to cells simultaneously both fluorophores responded in unison to the STED depletion laser allowing excellent super-resolution images to be obtained of the nuclear membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria and lipid droplets. The minor structural difference between the fluorophores resulted in their cellular distribution being heterogeneous across different lipid compartments resulting in distinct phase lifetimes for mitochondria, nuclear membrane / endoplasmic reticulum and lipid droplets. Using phasor plot lifetime segmentation, three separate images of the nuclear membrane with endoplasmic reticulum, the mitochondria, and the lipid droplets were readily obtainable. As the principles established for microscopy fluorophore pairing could be applied to other combinations of intracellular structures this approach offers broad potential for chemical-biology investigations utilising FLIM and STED.

papers.title: Proof of Concept Demonstration of Exsolution as a Method for Preparing Nanoparticle Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Catalysts
papers.abstract: Developing efficient, durable, and cost-effective hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalysts is critical for proton exchange membrane electrolyzer cells (PEMECs). This study explores exsolution as a route to embedded nanoparticle catalysts by exsolving Ru-containing nanoparticles from Sr 0.95 Ti 0.3 Fe 0.63 Ru 0.07 O 3-δ (STFR) under H 2 /H 2 O at 500-800°C. Electron microscopy showed nanoparticle size and density increased with reduction temperature and time. In 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 , exsolution significantly enhanced HER activity, generally correlating with increases in electrochemical surface area. However, particle coarsening likely reduced accessible active surface area. While STFR showed lower catalytic activity than RuO 2 , exsolution is a promising approach for the synthesis of nanoscale HER electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Cross-Scale Assessment of MACE Foundation Models and from Scratch Trained Potentials for Bi-Pt Systems
papers.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer a computationally efficient alternative to first-principles methods for atomistic simulations, but their performance beyond the configurations represented in their training data remains difficult to assess. Here, we benchmark four pretrained MACE foundation models (MP-0b3, MPA, OMAT, and MATPES) against two MACE potentials trained specifically on Bi-Pt configurations . The models are first evaluated for structural relaxation and vibrational properties of a Bi18Pt24 nanocage using DFT as a reference. The best-performing foundation model, OMAT, is then assessed at the bulk scale for the equilibrium structure, phonon dispersion, and melting behaviour of NiAs-type BiPt. All four pretrained models reproduce the DFT nanocage structure with sub-Å RMSD values of 0.059–0.089 Å, whereas the models trained from scratch give substantially larger deviations of 0.289 Å and 0.463 Å for the 1000 and 6000 models, respectively. The pretrained models also reproduce the main features of the DFT vibrational spectral distribution, with OMAT showing the closest quantitative agreement. In contrast, increasing the scratch-training set from 1000 to 6000 substantially reduces energy and force errors but does not improve structural accuracy for the nanocage. For bulk BiPt, OMAT predicts lattice parameters within 1.15% of experiment and reproduces the DFT phonon dispersion with an overall frequency RMSE of 11.62 cm−1. Two-phase coexistence simulations give a melting temperature of 1083±38 K, compared with the experimental value of 1038 K. These results show that pretrained MACE models can provide accurate structural and dynamical predictions for the Bi-Pt systems examined here despite the limited representation of Bi-Pt in the Materials Project and OMat24 datasets. The comparison also shows that conventional energy and force errors alone do not necessarily predict performance outside the systemspecific training domain. Structural, vibrational, and finite-temperature benchmarks therefore provide complementary measures for assessing the generalization of MLIPs across chemical environments and length scales.

papers.title: Deterministic optical redox (bio)sensing with molecular switch quantum defects
papers.abstract: Fluorescent sensors are powerful tools in the life sciences, but they lack the discrete relation between analyte concentration and signal intensity known from electrochemical sensors. Here, we present a fluorescent material equipped with a molecular redox switch that enables quantitative optical redox sensing. We incorporate ferrocene (Fc) quantum defects into the lattice of fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs). Switching the Fc2+/Fc3+ redox states either with analytes or electrochemically modulates the defect-specific near infrared emission at 1130 nm by up to 300%. These sensors directly detect redox-active molecules such as nitric oxide (NO) and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) in the µM range. Coupling enzymatic oxidases further enables optical detection of non-redox active biomolecules. Finally, we deploy these sensors in vivo to reveal dynamic (NO) stress signalling in living plants. This architecture provides a generalizable framework for quantitative optical redox sensing.

papers.title: Overview of the Consumer products, Lights, Environmental Air cleaning in Normal conditions (CLEAN) Home Indoor Field Study
papers.abstract: The Consumer products, Lights, Environmental Air cleaning in Normal conditions (CLEAN) study was an experimental field campaign in a residence in Boulder, Colorado USA focused on indoor air quality and chemistry. This study investigated the interactions between common indoor air pollution sources and a suite of indoor oxidant scenarios. Indoor pollution sources included cooking and gas stove operation, surface cleaning, smoke injections, and outdoor air infiltration, and indoor oxidants investigated included ozone injections, germicidal ultraviolet lamp operation (222 nm and 254 nm), cleaning surfaces with chlorine bleach, and operating a photoelectrochemical oxidation air cleaner. A suite of instruments was deployed to measure gas- and particle-phase species in indoor and outdoor air to study the effects of air pollutant and oxidant interactions in a real kitchen environment. This work presents an overview of the study site, experimental design, and measurement approach, along with initial observations from the campaign. Select findings showed that the kitchen air contained a complex mixture of air pollutants resulting from surface emissions and indoor everyday activities. The indoor air showed a high background secondary organic aerosol formation potential compared to typical outdoor levels, which increased significantly during some indoor activities like cooking and the use of terpene-based cleaning products.

papers.title: PERCEPTION-DRIVEN EXPERIMENTAL WORKFLOWS FOR SELF-DRIVING POLYMER LABS WITH MOBILE ROBOTS AND COBOT WORKCELLS
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) promise faster materials discovery, yet most current implementations are confined to single devices or to workcells within the reach of one robotic arm. Thermoplastic polymer research, however, often requires handling large material samples as well as spatially distributed, human-scale equipment (extruders, injection molders, mechanical testers). Herein, we present a perception-driven architecture that scales SDLs across rooms by combining mobile robots for long-range transport with cobot workcells for precise local specimen manipulation. Our approach fuses fiducial-marker augmented reality (ArUco) with learning-based perception (YOLOv11) to localize trays and specimens, estimate pose, and plan manipulation under uncertainty. A ROS 2 navigation stack on a mobile base (demonstrated on TurtleBot4 with LiDAR SLAM) identifies stations via tags and performs reliable pick–transport–place between devices. Standardized, camera-readable trays enable seamless handoffs to cobots equipped with wrist cameras for fine positioning. This perception stack reduces the need for rigid jigs and accommodates variable part poses common in polymer processing. We validate the system in an SDL focused on thermoplastic materials, integrating extrusion, injection molding, weighing, and mechanical testing. Notably, we tackle challenging tasks such as post-mold sprue detection and cutting, where parts fall unpredictably into receptacles and require precise trimming to avoid specimen damage. With modest training data, the vision models support fast, robust detection and closed-loop correction, enabling dependable end-to-end workflows across heterogeneous instruments. By unifying AR fiducials, machine learning, and ROS 2 navigation, this work turns dispersed polymer facilities into reconfigurable, perception-led SDLs. The methods generalize to higher-end mobile robots and other materials domains, lowering integration overhead and expanding the spatial and functional scope of self-driving materials research.

papers.title: Overcoming Homodimerization: Visible-Light Induced Energy-Transfer Catalyzed Crossed [2+2] Cycloaddition of Aryl Terminal Olefins
papers.abstract: This work describes a visible-light-assisted methodology for the crossed [2+2] cycloaddition of aryl terminal olefins utilizing an iridium-based photocatalyst. This transformation presents a broad scope of cyclobutanes by employing chemically distinct styrene derivatives via diradical formation under triplet-triplet energy-transfer photocatalysis. By overcoming the thermodynamic and kinetic barriers that typically favour homodimerization, this approach enables the efficient synthesis of diverse, di-substituted cyclobutanes from readily available aryl terminal alkene precursors.

papers.title: Bifunctional, Steroidal Photoaffinity Probes Enable Targeting of Sterol Transport Proteins
papers.abstract: Intracellular cholesterol transport plays a key role in maintaining cholesterol homeostasis, which is essential for human health. To map the cholesterol interactome, bifunctional steroidal photoaffinity probes were introduced, containing a diazirine for light-dependent covalent binding to target proteins and an alkyne for the introduction of a reporter tag through click chemistry. However, sterol transport proteins (STPs) are underrepresented in the cholesterol binding proteins identified using these probes. Here, we report the synthesis of a library of 14 bifunctional steroidal photoaffinity probes, designed to target STPs. Our affinity probes vary in placement of the two key functional groups and their connection between a sterol framework and an aliphatic side chain. We assessed the potency of our library against nine recombinant STPs through fluorescence polarization and differential scanning fluorometry assays and identified both selective and promiscuous binding profiles, which could be rationalized using molecular docking. These profiles could be recapitulated in fluorescent labeling experiments of sterol binding proteins in HeLa cells. Finally, we established a competitive pull-down assay to specifically enrich selected STPs and confirm their inhibition in live cells. This work provides a benchmark against which future bifunctional lipid probes should be measured and lays the foundation for applying bifunctional SPAPs in a range of downstream applications.

papers.title: Li@Au6H6+: A Preorganized Gold-Hydrogen Scaffold Unlocks Planar Hexacoordinate Lithium
papers.abstract: Achieving planar hexacoordination represents a longstanding challenge in chemical bonding. Although representative planar hexacoordinate species have been established for nearly every main-group group, a Group 1 member has remained elusive because alkali metals are intrinsically poor participants in delocalized multicenter bonding. Herein, systematic screening of 1,920 star-like E@X6L6 candidates, combined with global potential-energy-surface searches, identifies Li@Au6H6+ as the global-minimum cluster featuring a planar hexacoordinate lithium center. The cluster adopts idealized D6h symmetry, with Li embedded in a rigid hydrogen-bridged Au6H6 framework, and lies at least 24 kcal/mol below the next-lowest-energy isomer. Strikingly, unlike previously reported planar hexacoordinate systems, the stability of Li@Au6H6+ originates from the combination of an intrinsically stable Au6H6 scaffold, which itself corresponds to a global-minimum structure, and cooperative σ-dative donation from the framework into the vacant Li 2s/2p acceptor orbitals, while electrostatic interactions make only a negligible contribution.

papers.title: Carbon Nanotube-Induced Magnetic Shielding Effects on 129Xe NMR from Equivariant Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Equivariant graph neural networks (EGNNs) have shown success in building efficient and accurate machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for molecular dynamics (MD) and in enabling the prediction of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) parameters in complex systems. In this work, we use EGNNs to fine-tune an atomistic foundation model (AFM) and to build an NMR machine learning model. The former is used to build an MLIP for large-scale MD simulations of xenon in carbon nanotubes, while the latter is used to predict the 129 Xe NMR magnetic shielding tensor, σ , directly from the MD snapshots. Both models are data-efficient and remain accurate well beyond their training data. Using this dual-model framework, we show that xenon encapsulated in carbon nanotubes experiences a nanotube-induced, negative 129 Xe isotropic chemical shift that varies non-monotonically with tube diameter and depends further on temperature and Xe loading, establishing this dual-model approach as an efficient route to interpreting confinement-driven 129 Xe NMR response.

papers.title: Estimation of the Pre-Exponential Factor and Conversion Function of Solid-State Reactions Using the Incremental Integral Isoconversional Methods
papers.abstract: The incremental integral isoconversional methods provide a useful model-free framework for investigating the kinetics of solid-state reactions, but their conventional implementation is mainly focused on estimating activation energy. However, determination of the pre-exponential factor and conversion function generally requires additional assumptions concerning the kinetic model. In this study, a new methodology is introduced by combining the modified Ortega isoconversional method with the discrete cosine transform (DCT) reaction model and, where necessary, the compensation effect relationship. This framework enables estimation of the pre-exponential factor and conversion function for both simple and complex reaction systems using isothermal or nonisothermal kinetic data. The methodology can also accommodate reactions characterized by single or multiple reaction-rate peaks and allows the conversion function to be evaluated for processes exhibiting non-Arrhenian temperature dependence. The approach was first validated using simulated kinetic datasets under isothermal and nonisothermal conditions and was subsequently applied to experimental systems, including the thermal degradation of poly(methyl methacrylate) and its blend with cyclic olefin copolymer, and the melt crystallization of poly(butylene 2,5-furandicarboxylate), demonstrating the applicability of the proposed framework to a range of kinetic systems. GNU Octave/MATLAB codes were provided to facilitate implementation of the methodology with experimental kinetic data.

papers.title: Atmosphere-Dependent Chemical Stability of BZCYYb–YSZ Interfaces: A Kinetic Origin for BaZrO3 Suppression Under Reducing Conditions
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle infiltration of proton-conducting BaZr0.1Ce0.7Y0.1Yb0.1O3−δ (BZCYYb) into Ni-YSZ fuel electrodes offers a route to intermediate-temperature solid oxide cell operation, but its viability depends on chemical compatibility between the infiltrate and the YSZ scaffold. We aged a milled BZCYYb–YSZ powder mixture at 900 °C to test this compatibility. In air, degradation is severe: BaZrO3 and doped ceria form within 24 h, consuming the parent phase from ∼48 to ∼15 wt% over 144 h. We quantified phase fractions using a joint neighbor-pair adaptation of the direct derivation method with Lorentzian peak profiles, validated against a stoichiometric mass balance (mean absolute deviation 0.65 wt%). Johnson–Mehl–Avrami–Kolmogorov analysis (n < 1) indicates a diffusion-limited transformation initiating at BZCYYb–YSZ contact points. Under forming gas, BaZrO3 formation is substantially suppressed, reaching 2.5 wt% after 4 h against ∼11 wt% predicted from the air-aging kinetics. Machine-learned interatomic potential (CHGNet) calculations indicate the local thermodynamic landscape for Ba vacancies is flat and largely unchanged between atmospheres, while BaZrO3 formation remains strongly exothermic (−136.6 kJ/mol) in both. Nudged elastic band calculations instead show oxygen vacancies contracting the window that coordinates Ba2+ migration and raising the computed hop barrier by ∼0.5–0.6 eV, a kinetic penalty whose estimated magnitude exceeds

papers.title: Population-Specific H-Antigen Chain-Type Variation and Its Potential Impact on Enzymatic Universal-Blood Conversion: A Computational Pilot Study
papers.abstract: Enzymatic conversion of donor blood to universal type O ("ECO blood") is an active area of transfusion medicine research, with recently discovered bacterial enzymes capable of removing canonical and structurally extended ABO blood-group antigens. Whether human genetic variation affecting antigen chaintype distribution influences the efficiency of these conversion enzymes has not previously been examined. Using FucOB, a structurally characterized alpha-1,2-fucosidase, as a test case, we combined published mutagenesis data with molecular docking to compare its interaction with two physiologically dominant chain-type variants of the H blood-group antigen (type I and type II), whose relative abundance on red blood cells is genetically determined by FUT2 secretor status. We find a reproducible docking asymmetry tighter, more consistent binding to H type I than to H type II - that holds under two independent scoring methods. Combining this finding with published Indian FUT2 non-secretor phenotype frequencies (20-33%, varying by region), we estimate that a substantial minority of the Indian population may experience reduced FucOB conversion efficiency due tolacking H type Ichainsentirely.Thisisapreliminary computational finding requiring experimental validation; we report it, together with full methodological transparency and an explicit accounting of AI-assisted contributions, to invite expert scrutiny before further investment.

papers.title: Elemental Structural Looseness Parameter System: 63-Element Quick Reference Table with Quantitative Isotope Effect Correction
papers.abstract: This paper provides a directly consultable quick reference table for isotope effect corrections, covering 63 elements (including 5 rare earth elements), detailed in Appendix A. Quantitative validation of isotope effects was completed on diamond-group elements (C/Si/Ge). The geometric basis of the looseness parameter is independently authenticated by crystallographic data from 6 classes of molecular crystals and high-coordination bond length corrections (Appendix B); other elements are semi-quantitative estimates. The model introduces a universal baseline looseness constant epsilon_0 = 0.045, calibrated via C-13 diamond lattice data, and cross-validated on two independent systems (Si-28/Si-30 and Ge-70/Ge-76). The three-point back-calculation averages 0.0454, with an equivalent deviation of 0.8%. The correction formula contains only one element-sensitive coefficient k_A: delta_total(isotope) = (epsilon_0 + delta_element) * (1 - k_A * Delta_m / m_0). The looseness parameter can be directly used for bond length prediction, reaction activity ranking, and catalytic material screening.

papers.title: Transition-Metal Modified Zinc Oxide (ZnO) Nanostructures for Photocatalysis Application — A Comparative Review of Metal Doping and Metal-oxide Conjugation
papers.abstract: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is a benchmark wide-band-gap semiconductor for photocatalytic environmental remediation, yet its performance is limited by a large ~3.2 eV band gap that confines absorption to the ultraviolet range and by rapid electron–hole recombination. Two dominant strategies to overcome these limitations using inexpensive first-row transition metals: substitutional doping, in which Mn+ ions replace Zn2+ within the wurtzite lattice; and metal-oxide conjugation, in which a discrete MxOy phase is coupled to ZnO to form a heterojunction. This review compares the two paradigms across synthesis, structural characterization, and photocatalytic activity for seven metals—Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co and Ni. For each metal, the contrast between the doped and conjugated forms in terms of how they are made, the diagnostic signatures that distinguish them, and their reactive-species-level degradation mechanisms and kinetics are elaborated. A consistent picture emerges: isovalent, radius-matched dopants (Mn, Co, Ni) give the largest single-phase band-gap narrowing effect, whereas well-aligned heterojunctions (TiO2–ZnO, Fe2O3–ZnO, Co3O4–ZnO, NiO–ZnO) deliver the most durable charge separation and, frequently, the highest efficiencies, sometimes with magnetic recoverability. An in-depth, mechanismanchored, metal-by-metal treatment drawn from primary research of the last five years are provided with addressing stability, recyclability, cost and toxicity of the conjugates. Finally, an assessment of these nanoconjugates to implemented in the semiconductor industry and future directions of research are outlined.

papers.title: Microkinetic Equation for the Electrochemical Impedance of the Heyrovsky-Volmer Mechanism
papers.abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is a powerful technique to study the kinetics of electrochemical reactions. The conventional way to analyze EIS spectra is to fit experimental data with equivalent circuits. This approach yields the charge transfer resistance as the main parameter explaining electrode kinetics. However, converting the charge transfer resistance to individual rate constants is not straightforward, because the number of observed charge transfer resistances do not always match the number of rate constants. The difficulty of mechanistic interpretation is further amplified considering the values of charge transfer resistance changes upon the choice of the equivalent circuit model. Here, we report an analytical formula which expresses the impedance of the hydrogen evolution and oxidation reactions using kinetic parameters. Namely, we have focused on the Heyrovsky-Volmer mechanism and expressed its impedance using parameters contained within the Butler-Volmer equation such as standard heterogeneous rate constants, electron transfer coefficients, and equilibrium potentials. Numerical simulations show that a 0.05 V shift of the equilibrium potential of the Heyrovsky step is visible in the EIS spectra. As binding free energies are directly related to equilibrium potentials, our simulations suggest that EIS may be sensitive enough to determine binding free energies experimentally. Furthermore, we show how conventional equivalent circuit analyses fail to reproduce the true rate constants used during simulations, highlighting the importance of using microkinetic equations to analyze EIS spectra. We expect our work will promote the usage of EIS towards the kinetic understanding of electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Explain and Go Beyond with Surfacia: A Surface-Descriptor based Workflow for Interpretable Molecular Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models are widely used in chemistry, yet black-box predictions are often difficult to translate into chemically actionable descriptor-response rules or candidate-prioritization decisions. We present Surfacia, an automated workflow that transforms molecular structures and target values into wavefunction-derived surface descriptors, compact interpretable models, SHAP-based chemical interpretation, and visualization. The Surfacia descriptor system contains two complementary components: whole-molecule physical descriptors, which summarize geometry, orbital properties, and statistics of real-space molecular-surface functions, including electrostatic potential (ESP), average local ionization energy (ALIE), and local electron attachment energy (LEAE); and multi-scale quantitative surface analysis (MQSA) descriptors, which reorganize these surface properties around chemically meaningful units. We evaluated Surfacia on three case studies: sulfur-containing modifiers in carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR), a homologous organocatalyst series, and the Estimated SOLubility (ESOL) benchmark. The Results and Discussion are organized in two layers. First, compact selected Surfacia models are interpreted as chemically readable regression models. Second, a separate frontier-conditioned acquisition analysis asks whether the same sparse descriptor-SHAP landscape can support high-value candidate prioritization under a limited experimental budget. This second layer formalizes the chemist's go-beyond question as a sequential discovery problem: given only the current labeled set and a hidden frontier candidate pool, which acquisition rule can reach the true top-1 candidate with the lowest experimental cost? The comparison shows that descriptor-space novelty is the most stable region-entry signal, while SHAP-derived landscape information provides an interpretable way to order candidates within or around those novel regions. Thus, Surfacia connects mechanistically legible descriptor-response interpretation with a practical framework for discovery-oriented candidate selection, without requiring the SHAP-cliff variant to be universally superior to all novelty or diversity baselines.

papers.title: Discriminating Cardiovascular Risk-Related Lipoproteins at the Single-Particle Level with Solid-State Nanopore Technology and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Lipoproteins, macromolecular assemblies of lipids and apolipoproteins, play a central role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). While the ratio of ApoB-100bearing atherogenic particles to ApoA-I-bearing HDL provides critical risk assessment, standard lipid panels rely on static cholesterol mass (LDL-C), which often fails to capture true risk. Patients with healthy LDL-C levels can still develop ASCVD because the same amount of cholesterol can be contained in fewer large particles or many smaller ones. These smaller particles can circulate more easily in arteries and are more prone to penetrate the arterial lining, resulting in deposition and oxidation. This process contributes to plaque formation in the arterial walls and raises the risk of ASCVD. This discordance between cholesterol mass (LDL-C) and particle number (LDL-P) is commonly associated with conditions like dyslipidemia, metabolic syndrome, and diabetes, highlighting the need for accessible, accurate methods to assess lipoprotein levels and particle count. To address the need for accessible, single-particle subfractionation estimates, we present a nanopipette-based sensing platform integrated with machine learning to discriminate the three major plasma lipoproteins—HDL, LDL, and VLDL. This methodology enables direct estimation of the atherogenic (non-HDL)/non-atherogenic (HDL) lipoprotein ratio, providing an accessible framework for refined cardiovascular risk stratification.

papers.title: From Promotion to Poisoning: Temperature- and Coverage-Dependent Effects of Trace Fe on the Hydrogen Evolution Activity of Pt
papers.abstract: Trace iron impurities can strongly alter the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet how temperature governs their surface accumulation and kinetic consequences remains poorly understood. Here, the influence of 0–60 ppb Fe impurities on polycrystalline Pt was systematically examined in 0.1 M KOH over 280–336 K. Fe addition progressively suppressed the hydrogen underpotential-deposition (Hupd) charge, indicating blockage of Pt sites by Fe-derived surface species, while this suppression was substantially mitigated at elevated temperature. Despite this site blocking, 10–20 ppb Fe enhanced the HER current, whereas further Fe addition caused pronounced deactivation, particularly at 280–298 K. Wide-potential-range voltammetry revealed electrochemical responses consistent with hydroxide-like Fe species undergoing an Fe(II)/Fe(III)-type redox transition, with the Fe-associated anodic charge decreasing markedly at 336 K. Apparent thermodynamic analyses further indicated that Fe-induced site blocking cannot be described by adsorption on a single population of independent, equivalent sites. Most importantly, correlation of the Hupd-derived blocked-site fraction with the Tafel slope revealed three coverage-dependent regimes: kinetic promotion at low Fe coverage, predominantly site-number-limited deactivation at intermediate coverage, and severe kinetic inhibition at high coverage. These results demonstrate that trace Fe does not behave as a simple inert poison but dynamically modifies the Pt/Fe-derived interface in a coverage- and temperature-dependent manner. The findings establish electrolyte temperature and trace-impurity coverage as coupled parameters controlling alkaline HER kinetics on Pt.

papers.title: FOLDTRACE finds and maps active-site states across AI-predicted protein structures
papers.abstract: Proteins can retain their fold after active-site chemistry changes. FOLDTRACE is an open-source workflow that searches AI-predicted protein structures by fold and then determines whether chemistry-defining sites are retained, altered, lost or unresolved. In proteins with known biology, FOLDTRACE correctly read all 37 tested site states and exposed failures of sequence-based mapping. Across unrelated folds, it recovered remote families, probable annotation errors and testable functional hypotheses.

papers.title: Synthesis and Optimization of a Nanoparticle Vaccine to Deliver Tumor-Associated Glycopeptide Immunogens Against Pancreatic Cancer
papers.abstract: β-glucans are polymers of glucose, primarily with a 1,3- “beta” linkage at the anomeric center connection points. They are found in various forms in fungi, bacteria and cereals, and are known for their immune stimulant activity as well as being a source of essential fiber in the human diet. These polysaccharides have been employed in many experimental immunotherapeutic modalities as targeting agents to the protein Dectin-1 on Antigen Presenting Cells (APCs). We have previously synthesized gold nanoparticle coated with yeast β-glucans and functionalized with glycopeptide antigens from tumor-associated Mucin-4, a potential biomarker for pancreatic cancer, as a possible vaccine candidate against Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinomas (PDACs). In this report, we have refined this design to include β-glucans from different sources, designed a novel attachment point to covalently link antigen to the polysaccharide backbone and evaluated the cytokine response to treatment of RAW264.7 tumor macrophages with these new nanoparticles and found them to elicit an inflammatory antitumor response through the gene expression of TNF-a and IL-6. We also included a built-in cleavage site for protease release of antigen after endocytosis of these particles into an APCs. Future administration of these constructs into animals should provide a new and selective way of delivering tumor neoantigens to the immune system as a therapeutic vaccine against not only PDACs, but any cancer where glycopeptides from highly overexpressed tumor-associated surface proteins can be processed by adaptive immune surveillance.

papers.title: How do Alkali Cations Affect Alkaline HER Activity of Nickel and Platinum?
papers.abstract: Alkali cations substantially affect the kinetics of electrocatalytic reactions like CO2 reduction and the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). In this work, we investigate the effect of the electrolyte through grand-canonical Density Functional Theory (DFT) in conjunction with Quantum Mechanics/ Molecular Mechanics (QM/MM) simulations, and validate these results with electrochemical experiments of alkaline HER on commercially relevant and benchmark electrocatalysts, Ni and Pt, respectively. Our results show that the cation trend of alkaline hydrogen evolution depends on the electrocatalyst and is reflected in the activation barrier for water dissociation, studied as a proxy for the Volmer step. Meanwhile, the stability of *H and *OH does not depend significantly on the electrolyte cation.

papers.title: HófvarpnirHCON: An Interpretable Composition-Derived Volume and Bond-Overlap Dictionary Model for Fast Crystal Density Prediction from SMILES
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of crystal density from molecular structure remains challenging because it depends on the complex relationship between molecular composition, intermolecular interactions, and three-dimensional crystal packing. Current approaches often require explicit crystal structure prediction, computationally expensive simulations, or large machine-learning models that provide limited insight into the physical factors governing density. Here, we show that a substantial fraction of crystal volume can be predicted directly from molecular composition and connectivity without reconstructing the crystal lattice. We introduce HófvarpnirHCON, an interpretable framework based on a composition-derived reference volume, termed Leonardus Volume (derived from a cubic-root transformation of atomic masses), combined with effective bond-level packing correction terms. The framework represents crystal volume as a composition-derived baseline adjusted by a transferable bondcorrection dictionary optimized using non-negative least squares. The method was evaluated across six published crystal-density datasets comprising both experimentally measured and computationally derived structures, totaling more than 235,000 molecular structures. Across these independent evaluations, HófvarpnirHCON demonstrates that molecular composition captures a significant component of crystal-density variation, while bond-connectivity corrections account for systematic deviations from the compositionderived baseline. The model achieves a pooled molecule-weighted mean absolute error of 0.035 g cm−3 across the combined benchmark population, with individual dataset MAEs ranging from approximately 0.01 to 0.04 g cm−3 while maintaining full interpretability of the learned correction terms. Large-scale convergence analysis further demonstrates that the correction dictionary stabilizes as training data increases, supporting the emergence of stable transferable chemical patterns, consistent with the performance reported for the corresponding datasets in their original publications.

papers.title: Divergent CRAM formation and persistence across freshwater and marine environments revealed by AI-expanded MS/MS libraries
papers.abstract: Carboxyl-rich alicyclic molecules (CRAM) are a major refractory component of marine dissolved organic matter (DOM), yet their isomeric structures and formation chemistry remain sparsely represented in public MS/MS libraries. We trained a Property Conditioned Transformer Variant Autoencoder (VAE) —Enhanced Hierarchical GAT with Ring Chain Encoder, 64-dimensional 40 latent code, 17D property head on z, and a six-layer Transformer SELFIES decoder—on a curated CRAM-focused set (n = 5,842) and compiled an environmentally screened in silico library of 5.04 million structures. On a 10,000-molecule audit sample, 57.6% of generated molecules satisfied all four strict CRAM criteria, corresponding to enrichment ratio = 210.3 [128.9, 343.2], 95% CI, relative to training occupancy (16/5,842). Evaluated on 476,647 spectra from 98 sources spanning open-ocean, deep-sea, coastal, coral-reef, and riverine DOM, the library expanded CRAM-region formula coverage from 4,296 to 7,069 unique formulas and isomer candidates from 5,401 to 13,519. Within TRFU CRAM-compositional features (O/C 0.3–0.6, H/C 0.7–1.5; n = 18,513), explained peak ratio (EPR) rose from 31.8% under PubChem-only top hits to 38.0% under max-over-union retrieval across libraries (+6.2 percentage points), with CRAM-library hits alone reaching 40.4%. Mass-difference networks from the same 98 sources were oxidation-rich across environments, with riverine networks showing elevated alkylation and a stronger alkylation-to-hydrolysis Markov contribution. NPClassifier pathway mixes place alkaloid-associated labels among the largest marine CRAM-node classes alongside terpenoids and shikimates, with riverine polyketide-associated labels elevated; pooled non-CRAM to CRAM formation edges further show alkaloid-like labels declining and terpenoid-like labels rising. Microbial-molecular docking confirmed that network CRAM ligands are sterically compatible with diverse bacterial enzymes (global mean ΔG = −6.45 kcal mol-1; 1,324 ligands / 846 pairs). Together, property-conditioned generative expansion measurably strengthens environmental MS/MS annotation and enables source-resolved, annotation-supported pathway 59 comparisons beyond formula-level description.

papers.title: From Black Box to Dialogue: An MCP Server for Tanabe–Sugano Diagrams as a Reference Case for Conversational Scientific Tools
papers.abstract: Interpreting the d–d electronic spectra of transition-metal complexes is a routine practice in inorganic chemistry, yet the underlying models behind such interpretations are unexpectedly challenging to operate. Rigorous treatments demand specialized software, expert parameterization, and often high-performance computing, while even the standard textbook tool for first-pass intuition takes practice to read. The Tanabe–Sugano (TS) diagram remains the most efficient method for developing that intuition, and the same ligand-field framework is foundational for more advanced spectroscopic analyses. Here we present TanabeSugano, an open-source Python solver for d2–d8 TS diagrams. It is implemented as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, letting a language-model client act as an interactive front end that operates the solver rather than merely describing it. Through natural-language prompts, users can compute term energies, explore and compare configurations, fit measured absorption bands to extract the crystal-field strength (Dq) and Racah B, and interpret B as an indicator of metal–ligand covalency via the nephelauxetic ratio. The solver runs locally, without compilation or high-performance computing. We outline the tools available within the server and the d-orbital concepts they embody, illustrated by a comparison between d5 and d6 configurations that reveals the high-spin/low-spin crossover and the distinction between spin-allowed and spin-forbidden electronic transitions. TanabeSugano is the proof of concept; the contribution is the pattern it demonstrates, which exposes a validated solver through MCP. More specifically, it offers an accessible route to phenomenological understanding and a transferable model for operating other formal chemical models through dialogue. The proposed MCP implementation does not aim to supplant the rigor inherent in ab initio methods and remains fundamentally distinct from it.

papers.title: Total Synthesis: Backbone of Organic Chemistry, a Discipline in Decline?
papers.abstract: Total synthesis has long been regarded as the intellectual backbone of organic chemistry, driving reaction discovery, stereoselective methodology, and molecular design. Yet its place within the contemporary discipline is actively debated, largely on the basis of editorial opinion rather than evidence. In this Perspective we bring quantitative data to that debate. We examined the annual share of articles carrying the phrase “total synthesis” in their titles across four leading journals—Angewandte Chemie International Edition, Journal of Organic Chemistry, Organic Letters, and Tetrahedron Letters—from 1959 to 2025. The share rose through the late twentieth century to a peak of about 4.79% in 2009, then fell to 1.85% by 2025, a relative decline of roughly 61%. Structural-break analysis places a consistent inflection near 2020, and an AIC-selected ARIMA(0,1,0) model with drift projects continued decline to about 1.40% by 2030. Crucially, the fall is relative rather than absolute: the annual number of total syntheses has held broadly steady while overall journal output has expanded dramatically. We argue that total synthesis is not disappearing but being diluted and redefined, and we outline how researchers, editors, and funding agencies might sustain it as a driver of innovation.

papers.title: Bridging Food Chemistry and Computational Approaches with Agentic AI: Plant Protein Solubility and Bioactive-Enzyme Interactions
papers.abstract: Computational approaches can provide valuable molecular-level and data-driven insights for food chemistry research, but their broader use remains limited by the need for specialized computational and programming expertise. In this study, we propose a human–AI collaborative framework that bridges food chemistry and computational approaches through simple, visible, step-by-step agentic AI workflow design. The framework enables food scientists to translate domain-specific hypotheses into computational workflows that can be planned, implemented, tested, refined, and reused with AI assistance. Two practical applications are presented. The first uses surface-based structural descriptors to investigate plant protein water solubility. Principal component analysis explained 94.19% of the total variance in the first two components and distinguished proteins with greater surface exposure of charged residues from those enriched in surface-exposed Asn/Gln or nonpolar residues, which may favor protein–protein interactions and lower water solubility. The second integrates AlphaFold 3-based structural prediction and MM/GBSA binding affinity estimation to investigate interactions between food-derived polyphenols and pancreatic lipase. The predicted binding-affinity ranking of quercetin > curcumin > resveratrol was consistent with reported enzymatic inhibition trends, while residue-level analysis suggested that hydrophobic contacts and interactions with catalytic residues, particularly Ser153, contribute to ligand stabilization near the catalytic region. Together, these examples demonstrate how food chemistry hypotheses can be translated into clear, traceable, and reusable agentic AI workflows, lowering technical barriers to computational food chemistry while supporting both task execution and computational learning.

papers.title: Sulfated Prism[6]arene Binds One Guest Internally and One Guest Externally
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of sulfated prism[6]arene (Pr[6]AS) by reaction of (HO)12Pr[6] with SO3•pyridine in 35% yield. Pr[6]AS has very good solubility in water (>30 mM) and does not undergo self-association according to 1H NMR dilution experiments. Qualitative 1H NMR investigations show that guest resonances shift dramatically upfield and become significantly broadened upon complexation with Pr[6]AS. Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments show that Pr[6]AS forms ternary complexes (Pr[6]AS•guest2) with hydrophobic ammonium ions in phosphate buffered saline with b-values (Ka1 x Ka2) values up to 6.84 x 1013 M-2. Molecular dynamics simulations show that Pr[6]AS firmly binds one Me4Bipip guest within its cavity and a second Me4Bipip guest on the convex region of Pr[6]AS in close proximity to the externally directed sulfate substituents. Uncomplexed Pr[6]AS holds 7.6 ± 1.9 H2O and one Na+ ion within its cavity. Formation of the 1:1 and 1:2 Pr[6]AS-Me4Bipip complexes results in expulsion of the Na+ ion and approximately five of the solvating H2O molecules. Intriguingly, the combination of larger naphthalene walls and sulfate ionic groups that are conformationally restricted creates a secondary guest binding site on the exterior of Pr[6]AS which suggests a route toward design of high molecularity complexes.

papers.title: Robust Optical Coherence in a Chemically Tunable Eu(III) Molecular Crystal
papers.abstract: Chemical substitution o!ers a powerful route to tune molecular quantum materials, but its e!ects on optical decoherence extend beyond the simple dilution of interacting emitters; here, we investigate these e!ects in the molecular crystal [Eu(III)(TMHD)3(phen)], its dilution series in the isostructural host [Y(TMHD)3(phen)], and a partially deuterated analogue. The optical inhomogeneous linewidth of the 7F0 ↔ 5D0 transition near 580.4 nm exhibits a pronounced concentration dependence, ranging from 6 to 20 GHz, while the transition frequency shifts by up to ↗25 GHz across the dilution series. In contrast, the homogeneous linewidth measured by two-pulse photon echoes remains in the 50–130 kHz regime at 1.4 K, and shows a non-monotonic dependence on Eu(III) content. Partial phenanthroline deuteration also leaves the homogeneous linewidth essentially unchanged. Spectral-di!usion and temperature-dependent photon-echo measurements identify non-magnetic fluctuations of the molecular environment as the dominant residual dephasing channel. In contrast to rigid inorganic rare-earth hosts, the molecular crystal lattice supports low-frequency lattice modes that can dynamically modulate the anisotropic Eu(III) crystal field, while the extrapolated zero-temperature linewidth is most likely limited by electric-field perturbations. These results establish Eu(III) molecular crystals as chemically tunable materials with robust optical coherence and show that chemical dilution simultaneously reshapes static disorder, lattice dynamics, and decoherence, identifying molecular-lattice rigidity and electrostatic stability as central design parame-

papers.title: Inducing Surface Symmetry Breaking via Organic Molecule Templating for Phase-Stable Halide Perovskites
papers.abstract: Local symmetry breaking in soft ionic semiconductors can control functional properties, yet deliberate spatial confinement of structural desymmetrisation via chemical programming remains unexplored. Here we present a mechanism to induce surface-localised symmetry breaking via tilting of [PbX6] octahedra using tailored organic zwitterions and thereby stabilise formamidinium- and iodide-rich halide perovskites. L-arginine and related molecules react in situ in perovskite inks to produce distinct additive-perovskite coordination modes whose nature and strength depend on additive chemistry. Solid-state NMR and infrared nanospectroscopy show that these atomic-level interactions persist into perovskite thin films, inducing pronounced tilting of [PbI6] octahedra at the perovskite surface. Local nanostructure characterisation by scanning electron diffraction, supported by density functional theory calculations, indicates that additive-induced surface tilting both templates photoactive perovskite phase formation during crystallisation and subsequently forms a protective surface layer that resists self-propagative growth of photoinactive non-perovskites. These findings unveil new, directed pathways to chemically induced, spatially confined local symmetry breaking in soft ionic materials, and thus to new avenues for atomic-level manipulation of macroscopic functional properties.

papers.title: Kinetic Criteria for Finite CSTR Staging toward Plug-Flow Performance
papers.abstract: Finite CSTR cascades converge hydrodynamically toward plug flow as the number of stages increases, but the number of stages required to preserve reaction performance cannot be determined from residence-time variance alone. This work derives a dimensionless kinetic staging coefficient for equal-volume CSTR cascades by combining the composition dependence of the reaction-rate vector with the sensitivity of a selected outlet objective. The coefficient is invariant to uniform acceleration of all reaction rates, is exactly zero for common-factor parallel selectivity, and reaches its consecutive-reaction maximum when formation and consumption time scales are matched. In a nonlinear xylose-dehydration network, the coefficient passes through an interior maximum as concentration-dependent and direct furfural-loss rates become comparable. The leading coefficient sets the stage-count scale required to retain a specified fraction of optimized PFR performance, while higher-order terms account for finite-stage corrections. Published kinetic systems show that reaction time, attainable yield, and staging requirement can vary independently. The resulting criterion links reaction kinetics directly to the finite number of mixed stages required to approximate a specified PFR objective.

papers.title: Shear viscosity of liquid Sb and Bi from pseudopotential theory: the temperature-insensitive soft-tail component
papers.abstract: Liquid Sb and Bi are two pnictogens whose structure factors show the Friedel shoulder characteristic of nonsimple liquid metals. We compute their shear viscosity with a static, pairwise pipeline, a Bretonnet–Silbert (BS) pseudopotential with Rice–Allnatt transport theory. The main result is component resolved: the soft-tail contribution accounts for 54–59% of the viscosity yet supplies little of its measured temperature dependence. The calculation runs from each melting point to at least 500 K above it, uses five local-field corrections and the Zahid parameters, and resolves the temperature gradient |dη/dT| into kinetic, hard-core, and soft-tail components. The calculated gradient is systematically too weak: η is underestimated at the melting point (−16% for Sb, −32% for Bi) and overestimated at high temperature. Because η_s is an integral over g(r), replacing the hard-sphere form g^HS(r) with a modified hypernetted-chain (MHNC) one changes η_s by −2 to +21%, but does not recover the gradient; nor does varying the pseudopotential parameters across the BS physical window, so no single tested ingredient accounts for it. The local-field correction changes η by only 3–4%, an order of magnitude less than the spread from the non-unique BS parameters; the ab initio molecular-dynamics data are too sparse to test the gradient. These results delimit the static, pairwise framework for Sb and Bi and identify the component that such dynamic, many-body, or screening extensions need to address.

papers.title: The Role of Electrochemically Reduced Tungsten in Deoxygenative Reactions
papers.abstract: Direct functionalization of carbonyl moieties in a deoxygenative fashion is emerging as a valuable synthetic tool in the preparation of organic compounds. Among the possible strategies, the use of transition metals provides access to formal carbonyl metathesis in a selective and efficient way. In this context, the use of tungsten has been underdeveloped despite its peculiar reactivity with oxygenated compounds. Herein, the systematic investigation of cathodically reduced tungsten in deoxygenation reactions is presented. A continuous flow recirculation setup was developed to harness the reduced tungsten reactivity and circumvent technical limitations, streamlining the preparation protocol. The transformation was explored on different activated aldehydes, ketones, and diols (27 examples). Mechanistic investigation demonstrated the necessity of a thermal step to perform the C–O cleavage, as well as unprecedented evidence of an electron shuttling effect of W(IV) for the formation of ketyl radicals. The understanding of this fundamental reactivity then led to the discovery of a Giese-like reaction with readily available cinnamaldehydes, revealing an innovative method to access p -terphenyl scaffolds (14 examples).

papers.title: Drug classification with IR spectra: Evaluating the effect of analyst decisions in the context of simpler and harder classification challenges
papers.abstract: We studied the effect of three specific analyst decisions when computationally classifying single component drug samples by their infrared (IR) spectra: (i) how spectra are encoded as vectors, (ii) whether dimensionality is reduced, and (iii) what classification algorithm is used. We evaluated these decisions in the context of two classification tasks representing different levels of challenge: (i) the easier distinct-class challenge, and (ii) the appreciably more difficult fuzzy-class challenge. All spectra used to evaluate these challenges were sourced from the most recent version of the SWGDRUG IR library (Version 3.1). Eight models (combinations of analyst decision variables) were created for each task, and 10000 trials were completed using each model. All eight models performed well for the distinct-class challenge, with one model configuration having a median accuracy of 100%. The most important driver for accuracy with the distinct-class challenge was choice of classification algorithm. The models did not perform as well with the fuzzy-class challenge, with median classification accuracies ranging between 50% and 75%. However, we found that all three choices affected classification accuracy, with a strong interaction between choice of encoding and whether to employ dimensionality reduction. We posit that developing robust methods for feature selection will be important when trying to classify more closely related drugs. We also suggest that deeper exploration of how we label drugs (i.e., define classification labels) is necessary to meaningfully evaluate classification procedures. All data and source code used to prepare this article are freely available at https://github.com/Brandon12G/GiotisNumericalTreatments.

papers.title: Decoding Resonance and Nonresonance Raman Spectra of Biological Systems using Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Raman spectroscopy has been widely employed for advancing our understanding of biological systems, such as determining protein secondary structures, tracing chemical reactions, and studying therapeutically relevant biological species. To decode the complicated and convoluted Raman spectra into meaningful atomistic level information, peak assignment is indispensable. Herein, we proposed a unique method that computes the Raman spectra and assigns the complex spectra to Raman fingerprints based on the bond polarizability model. Using this method, we computed the resonance and nonresonance Raman spectra of real biological systems, such as protein and B-DNA, and successfully assigned each peak to atomic groups.

papers.title: pH-Gated Two-Channel Histidine Nanochelant for Electrostatic Interception of Furin-Processed Polycationic Species and Soft Heavy Metals
papers.abstract: Furin (PCSK3) is a pH- and Ca²⁺-gated proprotein convertase that cleaves polybasic motifs in the trans-Golgi network and endosomes (pH 5.5–6.5). The resulting linear polycationic fragments and metal-coordinating species contribute to pathogenesis across metabolic, inflammatory, neurodegenerative and infectious pathways. We describe 5H-EAF, an erythritol-capped linear penta-histidine peptide (MW ≈ 868 Da) whose activity is controlled by the titration of its five imidazole side chains (pKa ≈ 6.0–6.1). At endosomal pH the molecule carries a net charge of +4 to +5 (Channel E dominant) and engages two related electrostatic mechanisms: (i) competitive occupancy of acidic sites on target proteins and (ii) local neutralization of the negative potential lining the PA63 pore lumen. At neutral pH the charge collapses (Channel C dominant), enabling preferential coordination of soft heavy-metal ions (Hg(II), Pb(II)) while Zn(II) and Cu(I) remain weakly bound. Density-functional and multi-replica molecular-dynamics calculations show pH-gated binding free energies that reverse upon return to neutrality. In a 34-node directed network the same protonation state suppresses a subset of pathophysiological edges at pH 5.5 and leaves the GLP1R safety node unperturbed at both pH values. The functional cycle is therefore a single, reversible electrostatic switch rather than a permanent steric block.

papers.title: Capturing live cell dynamics at the nanoscale by sweeping laterally at a fixed standoff
papers.abstract: Scanning ion conductance microscopy (SICM) offers non-contact, label-free imaging of live cells with nanometer-scale resolution. However, its conventional imaging mode is inherently slow due to repeated vertical scanning, limiting temporal resolution and causing inertial issues. Here, we present Scanning Counter Ion Conductance Microscopy (SCICM), which enables a new mode, Sweep mode, by simply introducing a polyelectrolyte gel-filled (PGF) nanopipette into the SICM. This modification allows continuous lateral scanning without vertical feedback, improving imaging speed and pixel density with simplifying operation. The high conductivity of the polyelectrolyte gel, combined with ion concentration polarization (ICP) near the tip, enhances distance sensitivity, yielding a gradual approach curve essential for Sweep mode operation. SCICM enables high signal-to-noise imaging at a pixel rate of 8,000 Hz, beyond the temporal limitation of SICM, allowing visualization of dynamic morphological changes in live hippocampal neurons and establishing SCICM as a practical platform for high-fidelity, label-free imaging.

papers.title: Docking-Score Landscapes Shape Active-Learning Performance across Vina, Glide, and SILCS
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of large chemical libraries has created a need for virtual screening workflows that are both efficient and accurate. Active learning (AL) offers a scalable strategy by iteratively training surrogate models to prioritize promising compounds and reduce the number of required docking calculations. However, direct benchmarking of active-learning protocols across docking engines remains limited. In this study, we ask whether docking scores generated by different docking engines affect AL performance and what factors underlie these differences. To do so, we compare four active-learning virtual screening workflows, Vina-MolPAL, Glide-MolPAL, SILCS-MolPAL, and Schrödinger’s active-learning Glide, across multiple protein targets and library sizes. Performance was assessed by recovery of top-scoring molecules according to each workflow’s respective docking engine, score-prediction accuracy, chemical diversity, and computational cost. Vina-MolPAL achieved the highest top-1% recovery at a 1% batch size, whereas SILCS-MolPAL achieved comparable recovery at a larger batch size. Latent-embedding analyses suggest that the docking-score landscape strongly influences active-learning performance. In addition, combining active learning with SILCS provides a computationally efficient, membrane-aware approach for screening compounds at transmembrane binding sites.

papers.title: Hit-Triage Pretrained Transformer (Hit-TPT), an Interaction-Agnostic Graph-Transformer for Post-docking Enrichment
papers.abstract: Computational docking-based virtual screening is widely used to identify hit compounds in earlystage drug discovery.
