However, current docking methods still suffer from high false-positive rates, often resulting in no hits identified in campaigns against novel targets. For instance, in the first several CACHE challenges, the hit rate was consistently below 1%. This underscores the need for more selective and reliable triage methods. Here we present the Hit-Triage Pretrained Transformer (Hit-TPT), a graph neural network operating on protein-ligand interaction graphs to recognize true protein binders from decoys. Rooted in molecular recognition, Hit-TPT treats molecular complexes as 3D physical entities. It utilizes an interaction-agnostic graph transformer architecture combined with physics-informed atom features to reflect underlying chemical relationships while employing a novel 3D-positional encodings to represents the geometric context of each atom. The model was developed and evaluated using the DUD-E dataset, which comprises 102 targets with known actives and property matched decoys. To ensure rigorous validation, the model was trained on 77 targets and evaluated on a strictly held out test set of the remaining 25 targets. Hit-TPT achieved a mean Enrichment Factor in the top 1% of best-ranked ligands (EF1%) of 42 across these 25 test targets, substantially outperforming benchmarked conventional and ML-based methods. Crucially, we demonstrated that this high performance is not a dataset related artifact. Many previous machine learning models inadvertently function as ligand-only classifiers because training datasets rarely feature the same ligand across multiple targets with varying affinities. To prove Hit-TPT overcomes this limitation and learns genuine intermolecular interaction patterns rather than memorizing ligand scaffolds, we conducted a cross-target prediction analysis. This showed that Hit-TPT assigns high binding-probability scores to an active ligand exclusively when evaluated against its native target, confirming that the network successfully avoids ligand bias. Our results demonstrate that this physics-oriented architecture can markedly reduce false positives in virtual screening, offering a practical and generalizable approach to improve hit-finding efficiency by prioritizing compounds with genuine, target specific activity.

papers.title: What Cycle Closure Can and Cannot See in a Relative Binding Free Energy Network
papers.abstract: Cycle closure is the standard consistency check on a perturbation network, and what such a check can see is fixed by the gradient–cycle decomposition of edge flows (HodgeRank): the cycle part of a network’s error is auditable and biases nothing, while the gradient part biases the affinities and is invisible to any statistic computed from the network’s own values, at any magnitude. Both parts are measured here on 1145 real binding edges. The auditable subspace spans a third of the error space and, in the variance-weighted metric the closure statistic uses, carries under one per cent of the error against experiment. Experimental and annotation error is per-ligand, so it falls in the invisible part by construction and can only have made that share smaller: the measurement is a floor, and it survives correction: in the metric the closure statistic uses on every system measured, at one cell as a tie, and in an isotropic reading on every system of the wider grounded set, failing only on the two weakest of the four the test itself selected. The test built on it behaves as the bound predicts, and its flag set is not stable: the per-edge residuals and the ranking of systems reproduce across independent repeats, and the list of flagged systems does not. Fitting closure against the precisions the estimator already reports gives that test its stated null; it ties the standard fixed 1.0 kcal/mol cutoff, and on every replicate the set of systems it flags lies inside the set that cutoff flags. It flags nothing once the reported errors are widened by half, enough to cover the pose and preparation variance the protocol repeats hold fixed, and it names no removal that recovers accuracy against experiment. Resolving the gradient part needs measurements from outside the network, at worst one per unresolved dimension.

papers.title: Correlating Multiscale Morphologies with Function via Selective Deuteration in Non-Fullerene Organic Photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Whilst the versatile chemical tunability of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) has driven organic photovoltaic efficiencies beyond 20%, a deep understanding of the relationship between chemical structure, multi-scale morphology, and device performance has yet to be established. Here, we investigate three closely related indacenodithiophene-based NFAs (EH-IDTBR, OIDTBR, and O-IDTBCN) blended with the conjugated polymer PTB7-Th. Partial deuteration of the NFAs provides high compositional contrast enabling small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) and neutron reflectometry (NR) measurements, which are combined with complementary X-ray scattering and microscopy. We find that subtle variations in NFA sidechain and terminal-group chemistry strongly influence the size, crystallinity, intermixing, and vertical distribution of donor–acceptor domains. Higher device efficiencies are achieved for EH-IDTBR- and O-IDTBCN-based systems, which are characterized by small domain sizes and a high degree of donor–acceptor intermixing. In comparison, O-IDTBR-based systems form larger and less intermixed domains, which limit exciton dissociation and charge transport, and consequently device performance. These results demonstrate that targeted chemical modifications provide a direct means to control hierarchical morphology and establish molecular design rules for optimizing OPV efficiency.

papers.title: Design and Optimization of Guanidinium Bis(borane)amide Derivatives for Thermoneutral, Non-Volatile Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carrier (LOHC) Systems with Earth-Abundant Catalyst Compatibility
papers.abstract: The widespread deployment of Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carrier (LOHC) systems is currently limited by the high dehydrogenation temperatures (> 300 ◦C) of conventional hydrocarbon carriers (e.g., methylcyclohexane) and volatile emissions that contaminate fuel cells. To address these thermodynamic and operational limitations, this study presents a systematic computational design and screening of a novel ionic liquid LOHC system based on Guanidinium Bis(borane)amide (GBBA) derivatives. Using the dispersion-corrected composite density functional theory method PBEh- 3c and semi-empirical GFN2-xTB calculations, we evaluate the thermodynamic and kinetic profiles of the carrier loop. The theoretical maximum active hydrogen capacity of monomeric GBBA is estimated at 11.7 wt% (outperforming methylcyclohexane at 6.2 wt% and N-ethylcarbazole at 5.8 wt%), while the sterically shielded Monomethylguanidinium derivative (MMG-GBBA) preserves a high active density of 10.3 wt%. While the intrinsic dehydrogenation of monomeric GBBA is slightly endothermic (∆Hdehyd, monomer = +4.66 kcal/mol H2, ∆E = +10.10 kcal/mol H2), we computationally demonstrate that the net reaction enthalpy is shifted to a nearthermoneutral regime (∆Hnet ≈ +0.87 kcal/mol H2, +3.6 kJ/mol H2) in the liquid state by coupling the dehydrogenation step with the highly exothermic cyclic dimerization (∆Hdimerization ≈ −15.13 kcal/mol dimer) of the spent monomers. Furthermore, we address a common challenge in amine-borane chemistry: predicted catalyst poisoning caused by competitive coordination of the carrier’s cation to active metal sites. To mitigate this, we propose a steric shielding strategy. Structural screening of methyl-substituted cations identifies Monomethylguanidinium Bis(borane)amide (MMG-GBBA) as the optimal candidate. MMG-GBBA is predicted to preserve a high theoretical hydrogen storage density (10.3 wt%) while providing steric hindrance that computationally redirects bimetallic catalyst coordination to the active bis(borane)amide anion. Finally, we outline a conceptual laboratory synthesis pathway and key thermo-dynamic limits to guide future experimental validation of this thermoneutral carrier system.

papers.title: InP Quantum Dots, from Atomistic Reconstruction to Opto-Electronic Properties
papers.abstract: The molecular orbitals of semiconductor nanocrystals or quantum dots (QDs) strongly depend on the size, shape and surface termination of the crystallite. However, directly relating the energy level structure to an atomically precise QD geometry has remained an outstanding challenge. Here, we reconstruct the geometry of InP QDs from quantitative scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) images by means of atom counting and molecular dynamics simulations. We identify six structural features, which include In-terminated (111) and (100) facets, a stacking fault, and P-terminated (−111) facets. According to density functional theory (DFT) calculations, this surface termination gives rise to delocalized conduction-band orbitals, and a broad band of occupied surface-localized orbitals above the InP bulk valence-band edge. While showing no measurable photoluminescence, femtosecond pulsed excitation leads to a welldefined band-edge bleach, even when using below-band gap pump light, that persists for several nanoseconds. We argue that this observation agrees with the computational prediction of well-defined conduction-band orbitals and occupied, surface-localized orbitals. This demonstrated interplay between the experimentally verified geometry and energy level structure creates a new paradigm for analyzing surface geometry / electronic structure relations in QDs.

papers.title: On-site Trace Heavy-Metal Detection at Surfaces by Handheld X-ray Fluorescence
papers.abstract: Trace heavy metals at surfaces can control catalyst performance, maintenance safety and the interpretation or conservation of valuable objects, yet representative sampling may be difficult or prohibited. We show that a handheld energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (XRF) instrument operated in air at room temperature and pressure can enter a trace-surface regime well beyond that suggested by routine “point-and-shoot” analysis. The method combines raw-spectrum access, a matrix-matched blank, interleaved specimen and reference acquisitions, normalisation to a strong matrix line, spectrum subtraction, replicate summation and confirmation from independent analyte lines. It is intended for a narrowly specified analyte–matrix pair, not unrestricted material identification. As a demanding case study, mercury was measured on a nineteenth-century platinum mass standard. Although the instrument’s built-in software did not report mercury, the differential spectra resolved its Lα1 and Lβ1 lines and gave an areal density of 0.96 ± 0.19 µg cm−2. XRF samples deeply enough to include mercury transported into polishing damage and grain-boundary defects; the result is equivalent to about 70 µg over the surface area of a Pt–10%Ir prototype kilogram and confirms substantial subsurface ingress. The wider opportunity is on-site screening of mercury poisoning on platinum-group-metal catalysts, mercury deposits on oil and gas equipment, and Hg, Pb, As and other high-atomic-number constituents in pigments, corrosion products, gilding and historical pesticide residues. Portable XRF can survey an object or component rapidly and nondestructively before selective XPS, SIMS or destructive analysis. Quantification remains conditional on matrix, geometry, layering, spectral overlap, heterogeneity and the availability of appropriate reference materials; XRF identifies elements rather than chemical state.

papers.title: Perbutyrylated alkyl-glycosides as templates in carbohydrate chemistry: In search of a fast and green method of synthesis.
papers.abstract: Perbutyrylated carbohydrates are useful precursors for chemoenzymatic transformations but can be difficult to access; we demonstrate a microwave-assisted methodology for their preparation. Using imidazole as base under microwave heating, O-perbutyrylated-β-phenyl-galactose was obtained in 1 h in 50% yield, and these conditions were shown to be generalizable to O-perbutyrylated-β-phenyl-glucose, O-perbutyrylated-α/β-galactose, O-perbutyrylated-α/β-glucose, O-perbutyrylated-α/β-fucose, and O-perbutyrylated-α/β-lactose. This improved synthesis is as high yielding as reported protocols but uses a less toxic base and reduces reaction time by 6-8-fold. This is the first time that microwave heating has been employed for the perbutyrylation of sugars and suggests that it might be amenable for peracylation syntheses more generally.

papers.title: SERS
papers.abstract: Plasmonic nanoparticles possess a strong optical absorption but suffer from low catalytic activity and limited sustainability. Here, we demonstrate that earth-abundant chalcopyrite CuFeS2 nanocrystals (NCs) can serve as a dual-functional platform benefitting from a strong polaritonic absorption enabling surfaceenhanced Raman scattering (SERS), and providing at the same time high activity for light-induced electrontransfer catalysis. The nanocrystals exhibit a prominent optical resonance at 500 nm, originating from interband transitions into a Fe 3d derived intermediate band that drives the dielectric function toward the Fröhlich condition. This localized resonance yields a SERS analytical enhancement factor of ~ 3×103 for 1,2-bis(4-pyridyl)ethylene (BPE), validated by Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain (DGTD) electrodynamic simulations and Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations that motivates synergistic near-field and charge transfer contributions. In addition, the CuFeS2 NCs efficiently drive the selective photoconversion of p-nitrothiophenol (NTP) to 4,4′-dimercaptoazobenzene (DMAB). Crucially, wavelength-dependent SERS and kinetic measurements prove that both Raman amplification and surface reactivity follow the optical resonance profile. Power-dependent and substrate-heating controls further confirm that this reactivity is mediated by photoexcited electron transfer into adsorbate orbitals rather than photothermal heating. By integrating a polaritonic optical enhancement with long excited state lifetimes provided by the intermediate band electronic structure in a single earth-abundant material, this work establishes CuFeS2 nanocrystals as a versatile architecture for SERS diagnostics and non-thermal photochemistry.

papers.title: Support Engineering with Phosphorus: Tuning the Palladium-Catalyzed Selective Hydrogenation of α,β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
papers.abstract: Support engineering of oxide materials offers a powerful yet underexplored strategy for controlling the performance of supported metal catalysts. Here, phosphorus functionalization (1 – 5 wt% P) of alumina and silica provides a simple and modular strategy to tune the Pd-catalyzed selective hydrogenation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes. Phosphorus incorporation enhances catalytic activity on both supports while inducing pronounced support- and substrate-dependent selectivity patterns. Using cinnamaldehyde and citral as model substrates, a design-of-experiments approach reveals that catalytic performance is governed primarily by support chemistry and reaction conditions, whereas phosphorus loading exhibits threshold-type behavior, consistent with discrete restructuring of Pd surface ensembles rather than gradual electronic perturbation. Diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) demonstrate that phosphorus suppresses extended Pd ensembles and stabilizes highly dispersed, low-coordinated Pd sites. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) further reveals a shift of the Pd toward more positively charged surface species upon phosphorus modification. These findings establish phosphorus-based support engineering as a simple, transferable strategy to control metal dispersion, active-site accessibility, and catalytic selectivity without the need for complex alloying or bulk phase formation.

papers.title: Interaction Potentials, Quantum Scattering, and Transport Properties of Neutral and Cationic Ag–N2: From Buffer-Gas Cooling to Ion Mobility
papers.abstract: A comprehensive, first-principles characterization of the neutral Ag· · ·N 2 and cationic Ag + · · ·N 2 van der Waals complexes is presented, spanning the interaction potential, quantum close-coupling scattering dynamics, generalized transport cross sections, bound rovibrational states, and macroscopic transport properties, including the first predicted ion mobility for Ag + in N2 buffer gas. The neutral two-dimensional (rigid-rotor) potential energy surface was computed at the UCCSD(T) level with a 28-electron effective core potential for Ag, yielding a global well depth of 67.26 cm −1 at R = 4.40 Å, θ = 50◦. A three-dimensional vibrational coupling correction was found to affect scattering observables by less than 1%, validating the rigid-rotor treatment. Full close-coupling calculations were used to derive state-to-state cross sections, and the exact close-coupling formula for generalized Senftleben–Beenakker cross sections was independently transcribed and validated against its analytic isotropic limit before being converted, via calibrated Chapman–Enskog theory, into diffusion coefficients, viscosity, and thermal conductivity. The methodology was externally validated through independent reproduction of published He–CO 2 interaction energies (85–89% agreement). For the cationic complex, a separately computed, counterpoise-corrected potential energy surface was found to have a well approximately 58 times deeper than the neutral system (−3877 cm −1 at R = 3.44 Å, end-on), consistent with charge-induced-dipole binding. Full close-coupling calculations, requiring roughly six times more partial waves to converge, were used to obtain momentum-transfer cross sections, from which a reduced ion mobility of K0 = 1.35 cm2 V −1 s −1 was predicted at 300 K via the Mason–Schamp equation—within the typical range for comparable ions. A custom molecular-dynamics implementation was also developed, and several methodological findings are reported, including a quantified coupled-states/full-close-coupling discrepancy and two corrected force-discontinuity errors in the potential representation.

papers.title: Effect of UV and Visible LED Light on the Translocation Behavior of DNA through Quartz Nanopipettes
authors: Y. M. Nuwan D. Y. Bandara
papers.abstract: DNA translocation through solid-state nanopores has been investigated extensively as a powerful platform for label-free and single-molecule sensing. The molecular-level sensing resolution of these sensors can be leveraged to further our understanding of the interactions between environmental factors and biomolecules. Biomolecules are known to have wavelength-dependent structural and functional susceptibilities, and here we sought to primarily investigate the effect of visible and UV light on the canonical DNA molecule. In this study, we investigate the effects of visible light on DNA molecules using quartz nanopipettes—low-noise solid-state nanopores with a tapered geometry. We systematically exposed DNA to various controlled wavelengths of light and characterized the induced structural changes. We monitored waveform features such as ionic current blockades, rectangularity, and aspect ratio (among others) as indicators of photon-induced damage or conformational changes and compared them with the control parameters. Waveform patterns arising from DNA translocation showed both wavelength- and exposure-time dependence. These variations were attributed to photoproduct formation or local strand instabilities, which alter DNA conformation and influence dynamics through the nanopore. These findings position nanopore-based analysis as a promising platform for studying light-illuminated structural changes in biomolecules.

papers.title: IR Light Induces a Switch of Protein Translocation Direction from Electroosmotic to Electrophoretic in Quartz Nanopore Sensing
authors: Y. M. Nuwan D. Y. Bandara
papers.abstract: Single-molecule nanopore sensing provides a high-resolution, label-free platform to probe biomolecular dynamics and transport phenomena. Here, we investigate the biophysical response of proteins to low-powered (~160 mW) near-infrared (NIR) radiation (1050 nm) — a spectral region traditionally considered silent due to minimal absorption by water and biomolecules. Using nanopore sensors, we record single-molecule translocation events under varying electrolyte conditions. In control conditions with 2 M LiCl as the electrolyte, proteins translocate in the electroosmotic flow (EOF) direction. However, after 1050 nm NIR exposure, single-molecule recordings reveal a distinct switch in the transport mechanism, marked by the emergence of events in the electrophoretic (EPF) direction. This behavioral shift is observed across five distinct proteins, demonstrating a generalized phenomenon. Furthermore, in EPF-favoring electrolytes (KCl, NaCl, and CsCl), NIR illumination leads to a clear increase in current blockade depth (). Together, these direct single-molecule observations suggest that 1050 nm NIR radiation can potentially induce non-covalent protein aggregation, fundamentally altering transport behavior despite operating within an optically silent window.

papers.title: Synthesis of [carbonyl-11C]biaryl lactones and lactams via Palladium-Mediated Carbonylation with [11C]CO
papers.abstract: Carbonylation with [ 11 C]CO is a powerful strategy for the direct incorporation of carbon-11 into carbonyl-containing molecules, yet its application to cyclic structures remains underexplored. Here, we report two complementary palladium-mediated carbonylative cyclisation methods for the rapid synthesis of six-membered [ carbonyl - 11 C]biaryl lactones and lactams from readily accessible aryl bromide precursors. Biaryl lactones were efficiently accessed using Pd(PPh 3 ) 4 /Na 2 CO 3 , whereas formation of the corresponding lactams was enabled by a Pd(dba) 2 /P( t -Bu) 3 /Bu 4 NCl system. Both reactions proceeded in DMF at 120°C within 5 min and displayed broad functional-group tolerance across structurally and electronically diverse substrates, affording the desired products in predominantly good to excellent radiochemical conversions. The synthetic applicability of the methodology was demonstrated through late-stage carbon-11 labelling of the biologically active compounds Palomid 529 and PJ34, obtained in excellent conversion. This work expands the scope of [ 11 C]CO carbonylation to six-membered cyclic carbonyl compounds and establishes carbonylative cyclisation as a practical strategy for accessing [ carbonyl - 11 C]heterocycles.

papers.title: Progress towards Biomimetic Supramolecular Hydrogels Capable of Dual Covalent/Dynamic Covalent Stabilization
papers.abstract: Reproducing the hierarchical organization and dynamic interaction networks of native extracellular matrices, where supramolecular and covalent interactions are combined to provide both dynamic behavior and mechanical stability, remains a major challenge in the design of synthetic hydrogels. Here, we report the synthesis of an aldehyde-functionalized benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxamide hydrogelator designed to combine supramolecular selfassembly with two covalent reinforcement modes. The hydrogelator first self-assembled in aqueous media into fibrous structures forming hydrogels, which underwent an irreversible increase in stiffness upon heating. We have attributed this behavior to proximity-assisted aldehyde self-condensation crosslinking within the preorganized supramolecular network, supported by rheological measurements, control experiments, and the resistance of the heated hydrogels to dissolution. This stabilization preserved the shear-thinning behavior, viscoelastic relaxation, elasticity, and self-healing capacity of the material. The aldehyde groups were able to be exploited to introduce dynamic covalent crosslinks using bifunctional hydrazide or hydroxylamine crosslinkers, which strongly reinforced the hydrogels while also maintaining processability and dynamic behavior. Interestingly, all hydrogels converged toward similar stiffnesses after heating, suggesting that the final reinforcement may be constrained by the underlying supramolecular architecture. Preliminary culture experiments with human mesenchymal stromal cells (seeded on top of the hydrogels) demonstrated preliminary cytocompatibility of the aldehyde-functionalized hydrogels. Overall, this work highlights both the challenges and the potential of imine-type reinforcement in supramolecular hydrogels, which represent promising and versatile platforms for dynamic, self-healing, and mechanically tunable ECM-mimicking materials.

papers.title: Electrostatic attraction unlocks rapid tetrazine– trans-cyclooctene click chemistry in organic solvents
papers.abstract: The inverse electron-demand Diels–Alder (IEDDA) reaction between tetrazines (Tz) and trans -cyclooctenes (TCO) is among the fastest click reactions known. Although extensively optimized for aqueous environments, its reactivity in organic solvents remains strongly constrained, limiting applications under non-aqueous conditions. Here we report a charge-mediated strategy that enables rapid tetrazine– trans -cyclooctene ligation in organic media through electrostatic attraction. Reversible association between complementary charged Tz and TCO affords apparent second-order rate values of up to 10 7 M -1 s -1 in organic solvents, exceeding typical non-aqueous IEDDA rates by several orders of magnitude and approaching the fastest tetrazine ligations reported in water. Mechanistic studies support a reversible ion-pairing model, in which electrostatic pre-association generates unusual concentration-dependent kinetics, while preserving high reactivity even at nanomolar levels. We demonstrate the practical utility of this rate enhancement through selective peptide ligation and rapid tetrazine ligation of water-insoluble substrates. These findings establish intermolecular electrostatic attraction as an orthogonal framework for controlling IEDDA kinetics beyond conventional reagent-centered optimization.

papers.title: A hybrid stochastic-deterministic kinetic model for cellulose pyrolysis
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of cellulose pyrolysis requires resolving how molecular structure and reaction kinetics evolve during thermal decomposition. However, existing kinetic models commonly describe polymer evolution in an averaged or lumped manner, with the effects of degree of polymerization (DP), chain-end chemistry, and phase behavior often treated implicitly. In this study, a mechanistically grounded population balance model is developed to explicitly track DP and chain-end chemistry during cellulose pyrolysis. Density functional theory (DFT) derived kinetic parameters are used in a hybrid stochastic–deterministic framework, in which kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) method is used to describe stochastic depolymerization, deterministic rate equations represent chain-end and monomeric reactions, and a simplified vapor-liquid partitioning accounts for volatile product removal. Numerical convergence analyses establish suitable time stepping and Monte Carlo sampling conditions, with increasing Monte Carlo chain number primarily reducing stochastic variability. Validation against experimental literature data shows that primary depolymerization reactions govern overall mass-loss behavior, whereas secondary reactions are essential for predicting product distributions. The model reproduces the major experimental trends with temperature and heating rate, including a shift from levoglucosan (LG) formation toward lighter oxygenates and permanent gases as secondary reactions become increasingly important at elevated temperatures. Increasing initial chain length favors LG formation and suppresses fragmentation products, while pathway analysis identifies concerted depolymerization as the dominant route to LG, with fragmentation becoming more important at higher temperatures. Although the model captures the principal trends, it delays mass loss to higher temperature, overpredicts LG yield, and underpredicts secondary products and char yields, highlighting the need for improved fragmentation and char-forming pathways. Overall, the proposed framework provides a mechanistic link between cellulose molecular structure, reaction kinetics, operating conditions, and product distribution, while retaining the computational tractability required for population-level pyrolysis simulations.

papers.title: 3-Dimensional Mass Spectral Libraries for Improved Metabolites Identification using Collision Energy Profiles of Protonated and Radical Cation Precursors
papers.abstract: Electron impact ionization (EI) is routinely applied in industrial and national laboratories for structural identification using standardized libraries but is restricted to volatile and thermostable analytes separated by gas chromatography. In contrast, collision-induced dissociation (CID) of radical cations generated by atmospheric pressure photoionization (APPI) makes EI-library searches applicable to liquid chromatography and supercritical fluid chromatography, enabling analysis of thermolabile and involatile analytes. Within this study, we extend the utility of radical cation CID beyond EI-Library searches, by systematically investigating collision energy profiles of radical cations and protonated precursors from 40 low-molecular-weight compounds. Across collision energies from 10-115 eV, 79% of the 10 most abundant elemental formula losses differ between radical cation and protonated precursor CID. Most frequent elemental formula losses for radical cations are methyl and hydrogen radical losses, and for protonated precursors water and carboxyl group losses. Common fragment ions from radical cation and protonated precursor CID often show distinct collision energy profiles with shifted intensity maxima. While most fragments from radical cation CID resemble those produced by EI, additional structurally informative fragments become accessible at lower collision energies and are likely missed under 70 eV EI conditions due to excessive internal energy deposition. Collectively, these results establish collision-energy-resolved fragmentation as a basis for structurally informative 3-dimensional spectral libraries incorporating collision energy, fragment intensity, and m/z values for compound identification. The applicability of this approach is demonstrated for 9 exogenous substances spiked into human plasma using SWATH data acquisition and collision-energy profile matching with an emphasis on radical cations.

papers.title: Enantiomeric enrichment at a microcavity embedded in a modified clay: In-column reactions of a coordinatively unsaturated racemic iridium(III) complex
papers.abstract: A chiral nanoconfined reaction field was constructed by modifying the interlayer space of a smectite clay mineral with enantiopure tris(1,10-phenanthroline)ruthenium(II) complexes), Δ- or Λ-[Ru(phen)3]2+. A racemic coordinatively unsaturated cyclometalated iridium(III) complex, rac-[Ir(nBuBQ)2Cl] (nBuBQH = 2butylbenzo[h]quinoline), was introduced into a short chromatographic column (1 cm × 0.4 cm (i.d.)) packed with a synthetic hectorite/Δ-[Ru(phen)3]2+ ion-exchange adduct. The adsorbed iridium complex was quantitatively retained within the clay interlayer and could not be eluted with methanol. Subsequent injection of the chelating ligand, disodium 4,7-diphenyl-1,10-phenanthrolinedisulfonate (Na2BPS), triggered coordination-sphere expansion, affording the anionic six-coordinate complex, [Ir(nBuBQ)2(BPS)]-, with a recovery yield of 88%. In contrast, the isolated Δ- and Λ-enantiomers of [Ir(nBuBQ)2Cl] exhibited substantially lower recovery yields of only 10% and 15%, respectively, indicating a pronounced chirality-dependent reaction pathway within the chiral clay environments.

papers.title: N-Phosphinyl Imines Enable Intermolecular Aza Paternò–Büchi Reactions with Unactivated Alkenes
papers.abstract: Intermolecular aza Paternò–Büchi (aPB) reactions provide a direct and convergent approach to azetidines through the photocycloaddition of imines and alkenes. However, reactions involving unactivated alkenes remain challenging, particularly with acyclic imines, whose excited states are susceptible to rapid nonradiative relaxation and competing photochemical pathways. Here, we report N-phosphinyl imines as readily accessible and stable photoreactive partners for visiblelight-mediated intermolecular aPB reactions with unactivated alkenes. Triplet sensitization using thioxanthone as an inexpensive organic photocatalyst enables productive [2+2]-cycloaddition across a range of alkenes, establishing a new reagent platform for intermolecular aPB chemistry to expand the accessible reactivity of acyclic imines with unactivated alkenes.

papers.title: Dynamic Reactant Forcing Circumvents CO Poisoning in Catalytic CO Oxidation
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysts are usually optimized under static feed conditions, forcing a compromise between reactant adsorption, surface reaction, and site regeneration. For CO oxidation on Pt, this compromise is especially severe because CO binds strongly and suppresses O2 activation. Here we show that externally imposed square-wave modulation of the CO pressure can break this static limitation on Pt(111). Using synchronized infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy and mass spectrometry under constant O2 background, we directly resolve the coupled evolution of CO∗ coverage and CO2 production during each forcing cycle. CO introduction produces an initial CO2 burst followed by CO poisoning, whereas CO removal generates a second CO2 burst as vacant sites reopen O2 dissociation pathways. A Langmuir–Hinshelwood microkinetic model reproduces these transients and identifies the optimum forcing window as a balance between CO replenishment, CO desorption, and O2 activation on regenerated sites. Model-guided experimentation indicates the most favorable regimes of forcing frequency and duty cycle. At 475 K and PO2 = 5 × 10−5 mbar, the strongest tested protocol (approximately 0.3 s CO-on and 0.7 s CO-off) gives an approximately threefold larger time-averaged normalized m/z = 44 signal than continuous CO exposure at the same temperature, O2 pressure, and peak CO pressure. These results provide direct experimental evidence that reactant forcing can access productive non-steady-state surface coverages unavailable under static operation, establishing a mechanistic framework for programmable catalytic rate enhancement.

papers.title: Exploring the Energy Landscape of Hydroxide-Water Complexes
papers.abstract: The structures and energies of complexes of hydroxide ions with two to five water molecules are explored at the DLPNO-CCSD(T)(-F12) levels of theory. For complexes with two or three water molecules, the most stable structures have all of the water molecules forming hydrogen bonds to the hydroxide ion, oriented so as to form weak water-water hydrogen bonds. For the complex with four water molecules, the lowest energy structures with three and four water molecules bound to the hydroxide ion are nearly isoenergetic, with the complex with three water molecules bound to the hydroxide ion roughly 10 cm -1 lower in energy. This result is consistent with photoelectron and infrared spectroscopy for this ion. For the larger complexes, the structures with four water molecules in the first solvation shell are the lowest in energy, while structures with three water molecules bound to the hydroxide ion and two in the second solvation shell resemble low-energy isomers of (H 2 O) 6 . The effect of the introduction of harmonic zero-point energy on the relative energies of these isomers is explored, and the sizes of the shifts in the relative energies with the addition of zero-point energy are attributed to a balance between increases in the frequencies of the intermolecular vibrations and decreases in the frequencies of the OH stretching vibrations with increased hydrogen-bond strength. Finally, we find that DLPNO-CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ calculations are shown to reproduce the relative energies of the isomers of these hydroxide-water complexes evaluated at the complete basis set limit.

papers.title: Ribosomal Synthesis of Noncanonical Cyclic Peptides via DNA-Templated, PNA-Mediated tRNA Aminoacylation
papers.abstract: An efficient peptide nucleic acid (PNA)-based tRNA aminoacylation system was established for ribosomal synthesis of noncanonical cyclic peptides. This system allows the preparation of aminoacyl-tRNAs containing various noncanonical amino acids, including D-amino acids, N-methylated amino acids, and sterically hindered amino acids which are poorly compatible with aminoacyltRNA synthetase-based method. This system was employed for the ribosomal synthesis of noncanonical cyclic peptides bearing a head-to-side-chain cross-linking topology. A comprehensive study reveals that the acyl transfer reaction occurs most efficiently when the donor PNA and acceptor RNA hybridize seamlessly, with no gap or overlap at the hybridization site. To avoid hydrolysis of the aminoacyl-tRNA products, we developed a low-temperature PNA-based RNA aminoacylation approach to maintain the integrity of the labile ester bond during tRNA aminoacylation. Remarkably, the DNA-templated acylation proceeds even at –78°C, showing the unique advantage of the DNA-templated strategy over conventional enzymatic approaches, which usually become ineffective at a low temperature. This platform is independent of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases and flexizyme, and has the potential to overcome the substrate limitations of the existing methods. We expect that the efficient DNA-templated PNA-based system will be a promising methodology for the ribosomal synthesis of noncanonical peptides.

papers.title: A single-reagent vibrational tag (VibeTag) for peptide sequencing via iterative N-terminal amino-acid identification
papers.abstract: Reading a molecule’s identity from its vibrational spectrum is a long-standing goal of chemical sensing. Vibrational reporters have largely been built to show where a moiety sits rather than to tell one chemical environment from another. We introduce VibeTags, isothiocyanate chromophores that couple to a peptide N-terminus through the same reaction as the classical Edman reagent, so one molecule both reports the adjacent side chain through its Raman fingerprint and remains competent for Edman cleavage. Identity is encoded by simultaneous modulation of peak intensity, frequency and lineshape across many modes rather than by a shift in one band. A molecular-dynamics/DFT screen selects the azobenzene DABITC over the xanthene TRITC-5iso and phenyl isothiocyanate. On bulk surface-tethered peptides, DABITC resolves all 20 canonical amino acids at 96% classmean recall, separates leucine from isoleucine, resolves phosphorylation, methylation, acylation, and citrullination without modification-specific reagents, and supports a cleave-and-retag cycle advancing the read by one residue.

papers.title: Electrocarboxylation of 1,3-butadiene with CO2 to 3-hexenedioic acid: effect of operating parameters on product selectivity
papers.abstract: The electrochemical carboxylation of alkenes using CO2 is a sustainable and promising approach for synthesizing a variety of organic compounds, especially carboxylic acid derivatives. These processes are of high scientific and commercial interest as only one or two electrons are required per CO2 molecule to produce value-added products. Here, we report on the electrochemical dicarboxylation of 1,3-butadiene with CO2 to obtain 3-hexenedioic acid, a key intermediate to produce adipic acid. The electrocarboxylation was performed in acetonitrile using a nickel cathode, an aluminium anode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode in an undivided cell. We systematically explore how different operating conditions including the applied voltage, water content, and temperature affect the reaction performance and the product distribution. Importantly, we find that the water content significantly influences product formation, highlighting its critical role in optimizing the reaction conditions. Temperature was found to play a key role as a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 36% toward electrocarboxylation products was achieved under ambient conditions, which increased to 59% at 40 °C but decreased to 49% at 60 °C.

papers.title: Iodocyclization as a Hub Reaction for Lead- and Diversity-Oriented Synthesis of sp3-Enriched Six-Membered O- and N-Heterocycles
papers.abstract: Iodocyclization was applied as a single hub reaction to a uniformly prepared set of 50 precursors, providing the monocyclic, spirocyclic, and fused versions of four saturated six-membered heterocycles: 1,4-dioxanes, tetrahydropyrans, morpholines, and piperidines. Under mild conditions (I 2 , NaHCO 3 , MeCN), the reaction worked well for 1,4-dioxanes and tetrahydropyrans, but became substrate-specific once the ring contained nitrogen. In particular, the alkenylamine-derived precursors provided morpholines, whereas their alkenol-derived counterparts did not, and the free alkenylamines polymerized instead of giving piperidines. The limitations were defined by the nature of nucleophile rather than by the ring itself – replacing the amine with carbamate enabled the cyclization, and ring closure of 1,2-amino alcohols with epichlorohydrin provided the morpholine-derived cores, so that the scaffold collection remained complete across all four classes. Further transformations of the iodide handle did not depend on the scaffold, delivering amines, alcohols, carboxylic acids, esters, sulfonyl chlorides, sulfonamides, and amino acid derivatives (95% of the transformations attempted) on up to 50 g scale. The resulting 44 distinct heterocyclic scaffolds and 252 building blocks occupied lead-like chemical space (median MW 186 Da, median F sp 3 0.92). The matched molecular pair analysis showed that replacing a ring oxygen atom with CH 2 increased the mean cLog P value by ca. one unit, equally in the 1,4-dioxane/tetrahydropyran and the morpholine/piperidine pairs. One-point virtual decoration provided a compound library that fitted well the lead-likeness criteria, whereas the two-point decoration left the resulting library members drug-like but no longer lead-like.

papers.title: Accelerating the Optimization of Tandem CO2 Hydrogenation Catalysts via Bayesian Experimentation in a High-Dimensional Design Space
Counteranion-directed polar packing in organic cage piezoelectrics
papers.abstract: Organic piezoelectrics are fundamentally limited by the tendency of molecular crystals toward centrosymmetric packing, which forbids a macroscopic piezoelectric response. Here we establish organic cage salts as a programmable platform for overcoming this limitation, in which counteranions direct local cage–anion electrostatic asymmetry, while crystal packing determines whether the resulting polar-shell dipoles cancel or are retained in the solid state. Multiscale dipole analysis reveals that high piezoelectric performance requires both large local cage-anion shell dipoles, arising from anisotropic cage-anion interactions, and their cooperative alignment within the crystal lattice. Across the RCC cage-salt series, RCC3-CF3SO3 gives the largest uncompensated cell dipole and the strongest measured response because its local dipoles are constructively aligned along the polar axis. Flexible RCC3-CF3SO3/PDMS composites (d33,eff = 54.1 pC N-1) generate open-circuit voltages up to 13.5 V, operate stably over 30,000 cycles, and enable self-powered wearable sensing and underwater ultrasonic detection with voltage sensitivities exceeding commercial polymer transducers while preserving frequency fidelity. Because the anion is introduced simply through the choice of acid, this counteranion-directed polar-packing strategy is synthetically modular and potentially transferable to other charged molecular scaffolds.

papers.title: DeepField: Condensed-Phase Quantum Learning for All-Atom Protein Dynamics in Explicit Water
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are beginning to make quantum-derived biomolecular dynamics practical, but a central mismatch remains between the scale of quantum reference data and the scale of the target simulation: reference calculations are commonly performed on isolated molecules or local fragments, whereas protein function emerges in a heterogeneous condensed-phase protein-water environment. Here we present DeepField, an environment-matched MLIP that uses energies and atomic forces reconstructed for complete hydrated biomolecular configurations as the supervised learning targets. The labels are generated at the CF22D/aug-cc-pVDZ level using electrostatically embedded generalized molecular fractionation with conjugate caps (EE-GMFCC), enabling system-level quantum supervision for configurations beyond the practical reach of conventional full-system electronic-structure calculations. The resulting data set contains 64,605 configurations spanning bulk water, hydrated amino acids, solvated peptides, proteins, ions, and protein-water interfaces, with system sizes up to 2,423 atoms. DeepField combines an equivariant manybody representation with latent Ewald summation so that protein, water, ions, and their mutual interactions are described by one potential. In a controlled comparison using identical training data, the long-range model narrows energy and force residuals for unseen solvated proteins and preserves the distance dependence of polar interactions beyond the local cutoff, while retaining computational throughput comparable to MACELES-OFF. DeepField reproduces key structural and vibrational features of liquid water and supports all-atom trajectories of explicitly solvated proteins containing up to approximately 36,000 atoms. For ubiquitin, the simulated ensemble reproduces experimental backbone scalar couplings and residue-dependent N-H orientational fluctuations within the sampled window. Together, these results establish quantum fragmentation as a route to system-level training targets for condensed-phase biomolecular MLIPs and enable unified quantum-derived dynamics of proteins in explicit water.

papers.title: Realistic Simulations of Energy Materials Using Foundation Models and Electrode-Potential Learning
papers.abstract: Here, we evaluate SevenNet-Omni [Kim et al., Nat. Commun. 2026, 17, 3432], a universal machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP), in realistic energy-material systems whose long timescale simulations are beyond the practical reach of density-functional theory (DFT). Tests span explicit solvation, metal-support interfaces, and reactive battery surfaces and interfaces, all of which involve realistic cross-domain interactions between inorganic materials and organic species. Without system-specific fine-tuning, SevenNet-Omni achieves sufficient accuracy for these out-of-domain systems, demonstrating strong transferability. To extend MLIPs to electrochemical systems, we also develop a model that predicts work-function changes across surface configurations. The model achieves errors of approximately 0.1 V, suggesting the usefulness of the approach for simulating energy systems under applied electrode bias potentials. Together, these results highlight the potential of foundation MLIPs for simulating next-generation energy systems.

papers.title: FragFlow: depth-resolved cosolvent mapping recovers cryptic and allosteric sites inside lipid bilayers
papers.abstract: Cosolvent molecular dynamics maps druggable hotspots by seeding small organic probes into a simulation, accumulating their density, and converting density to free energy against a single scalar bulk reference. That reference is what has kept the method from scoring a site inside the membrane: probes have been mapped there, but against a background that does not know how deep it is. A hydrophobic probe partitions into the acyl core, so referenced to bulk water the bilayer itself is a hotspot: benzene’s transfer free energy into a protein-free POPC core is −3.34 kcal mol−1, and the core sits at 48-146× bulk-water probe density (Table S1) before any protein is present. We replace the scalar reference with a depth-resolved one. Reduced membrane depth ζ = 2·d/⟨DPP⟩ is measured per frame, and every voxel is scored against the far-field probe density at its own depth (Algorithm S1), taken from the same simulation box. On three proteins spanning three architectures (a mitochondrial carrier, a class-A G-protein-coupled receptor, and a twopore-domain potassium channel) the false-positive rate of a frozen detection rule in non-site acyl-core voxels falls from 43.5-63.6 % to 0.03-0.44 % (Table S2), measured out-of-sample on identical voxels with only the reference term exchanged. The gain is in specificity and it is a deliberate trade, quantified on both sides: discrimination between the scored site and non-site core voxels rises from 1.72×, 1.74× and 0.65× to 1843×, 104× and 15.7×, the first of these measured against a predicted candidate and the other two against experimentally validated sites, and a scalar value below unity means that reference fires more often on non-sites than on sites. The price is that firing at the validated sites falls from 75.0 %, 85.7 % and 41.4 % to 50.0 %, 7.1 % and 6.9 % at the same fixed threshold. We regard that as the correct trade: a method that fires on the whole bilayer has no use for the sensitivity it appears to retain: the first of these against a predicted candidate rather than a validated site, the other two against experimentally validated ones; the scalar value below unity means that reference fires more often on non-sites than on sites. FragFlow localizes a co-crystallized antagonist site without being given its position (98 % of the detected region lies within 5 Å of the ligand) and declines the same receptor’s orthosteric pocket; we show that this recovery rests on the geometry, hydration, lining and occupancy channels and not on the fragment score, which ranks a neighboring non-site lobe above the true site. It also identifies a transient hydrophobic cavity on the carrier at ζ = −0.77. We further show that the reference’s shape is reproducible to 0.039 kcal mol−1 between replicates while its level scatters by 0.411, that binding-site residence resolves into components spanning two orders of magnitude that no mean describes, and that a probe cannot report on a site it does not enter.

papers.title: Resolving isomeric barriers of phosphatidylcholine in mixture by LC-MS/MS using copper(II) stabilization in the gas phase.
RETRACTED: Molecular Immobilization of Tetranuclear Nickel Complex for Electrocatalytic Overall Water Splitting Reaction.
papers.abstract: Retracted at the authors' request because the work requires further development. Molecular immobilization has emerged as an effective strategy to get an advantage of structural information of homogenous catalysts with the operational stability of heterogeneous catalysts for electrochemical water splitting. A few molecularly immobilized catalysts have been reported for water splitting, however, they typically suffer from short‑term durability and their true catalytic active phase under operating conditions has rarely been thoroughly investigated. In this regard, a tetranuclear nickel cluster (Ni4) was synthesized and investigated its electrocatalytic performance for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER), and for overall water splitting (OWS) in two electrode configurations. Under heterogeneous conditions, Ni4/CNT@CP (Ni4 complex immobilized on multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) and coated on carbon paper) demonstrated a long-term stability for 50 hours for OER and OWS at 10 mAcm-2 in 0.5 M KOH solution. The chronopotentiometry experiments reveal that Ni4/CNT@CP requires 330 mV overpotential and 1.9 V cell potential to maintain a current density of 10 mAcm-2. Moreover, the overpotential requirement for HER was found to decrease from 430 mV to 250 mV over long term chronopotentiometry experiment, highlighting the catalyst transformation under reductive conditions. Collectively, the present results expand the scope of immobilized nickel complex by combining durable performance along with catalytic phase analysis and mechanistic analysis.

papers.title: VENTUS - An obstacle-aware backward Lagrangian model for emission estimation in complex aerodynamic environments
papers.abstract: Atmospheric dispersion models are widely used to estimate methane emissions from concentration measurements, yet existing approaches remain limited in aerodynamically complex environments such as oil and gas facilities. Gaussian plume (GP) models rely on idealised assumptions of homogeneous terrain and steady-state flow, while backward Lagrangian stochastic (bLs) approaches provide improved physical realism but typically neglect terrain and obstruction effects or represent them only implicitly. This study introduces VENTUS, a computationally tractable bLs inversion framework that explicitly incorporates terrain variation and aerodynamic obstructions within the particle transport formulation. The model combines stochastic particle tracking with terrain-following dynamics and a detectability framework that identifies conditions where source–receptor connectivity is insufficient for reliable emission inversion. Model performance was evaluated using a three-phase testing framework comprising atmospheric stability sensitivity, environmental complexity sensitivity, and validation against controlled methane release experiments from the Methane Emissions Technology Evaluation Center (METEC). Validation was performed using the same input data previously applied to GP and WindTrax bLs modelling studies, enabling direct comparison under identical conditions. VENTUS reproduced expected stability-dependent dispersion behaviour and demonstrated strong sensitivity to footprint magnitude and source–receptor connectivity. Against the METEC dataset, 84% of detectable emission estimates fell within a factor of two of known release rates. A moderate underestimation bias was observed (slope = 0.64; mean fractional bias = −0.14), while approximately 28% of cases were identified as non-detectable. The results demonstrate that VENTUS provides a practical framework for near-field emission estimation while explicitly identifying conditions under which inversion results are unreliable. Although validation was limited to a single experimental regime, the framework offers a transparent and extensible alternative to existing dispersion-based inversion approaches.

papers.title: Rescuable Stagnation: A Diagnostic for Benchmark Suitability in LLM-Guided Materials Optimization
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly incorporated into closed-loop materials optimization, yet existing benchmarks provide little controlled evidence of what they contribute once Bayesian optimization stalls. We introduce a benchmark qualification criterion for rescue experiments—which we term rescuable stagnation—for determining, before the optimization comparison is run, whether a benchmark stalls while meaningful improvement remains available. Benchmarks that fail this test make it difficult to distinguish ineffective rescue strategies from saturated or non-stalling optimization. Qualifying a benchmark in advance therefore reduces the risk that null results reflect benchmark design rather than the method under evaluation. We demonstrate the approach on a benchmark constructed from Materials Project shear-modulus data, on which LLM-guided rescue gives no statistically significant improvement over heuristic injection—including a heuristic control provided with the same search information. The LLM nonetheless steers the search toward chemically distinct, high-modulus regions that conventional heuristics do not reach. This exploration behavior reproduces across two model capability levels and does not depend on the coherence of the model’s rationales, though it carries a substantially higher per-proposal cost. The LLM’s distinctive contribution on this benchmark is therefore in where it places exploration rather than in the optimization outcome it achieves, though this distinctiveness did not translate into a measurable advantage under the budget tested. More broadly, conclusions about LLM-guided discovery hinge on benchmark suitability—which qualifying the benchmark makes testable before experiments begin.

papers.title: Quantitative SPME-LC-MS profiling reveals metabolite signatures associated with molecular alterations in human gliomas
papers.abstract: Gliomas are the most common primary brain tumors and remain among the most challenging to diagnose and treat. Prognosis depends largely on tumor grade and molecular characteristics, with low-grade gliomas associated with a median survival of approximately 7 years, compared with only 12–18 months for grade 4 gliomas. These differences highlight the need for rapid and reliable diagnostic methods for glial tumors. In this work, the optimization and validation of a quantitative SPME-LC-MS method for selected metabolites were performed. Validation was performed according to the FDA-specified criteria. Subsequently, the method was applied in an experiment involving 31 patients with glial tumors, and the results were compared with the genotype profiles. The strongest univariate association was observed between PTEN deletion and α-aminoadipic acid. Higher α-aminoadipic acid concentrations were also observed in EGFR-amplified tumors, whereas the associations involving acetylcarnitine did not reach statistical significance. Additionally, it was noted that EGFR and PTEN alterations often co-occurred within the same cohort. These results should not be interpreted as evidence of two independent, mutation-specific metabolic effects but may reflect a common molecular context involving dysregulation of the EGFR–PI3K–AKT pathway. The results confirmed that the presented SPME-LC-MS method enables the quantitative analysis of amino acids and acylcarnitines. Moreover, genetic alterations revealed that metabolomic alterations in gliomas are linked to their molecular background rather than occurring randomly.

papers.title: Synthesis of 5-Aminoisoxazolidines from Azetidine Nitrones via Formal Ring Expansion
papers.abstract: A formal ring-expansion reaction of azetidine nitrones has been developed for the synthesis of 5-aminoisoxazolidines. Nucleophilic addition of an amine, alcohol or water to an azetidine nitrone is proposed to initiate azetidine nitrone ring-opening followed by cyclization to the corresponding 5-membered ring. A variety of examples are presented highlighting the scope of the method as well as the differences in stereochemical preference between primary aniline and secondary amine nucleophiles. A two-step, one-pot process is also described for the direct conversion of N-alkenylnitrones to 5-aminoisoxazolidines.

papers.title: Surface Flaw Controlled Li Dendrite Initiation in Garnet Solid Electrolyte
papers.abstract: Li dendrite initiation in solid electrolytes, followed by dendrite propagation that eventually causes cell shorting, remains a major obstacle to the practical realization of all-solid-state lithium metal batteries. Although surface flaws (e.g. grain boundaries, voids, scratches, etc., intersecting the surface) are widely considered potential initiation sites, their quantitative role in controlling dendrite initiation remains unclear. Here we directly monitor Li dendrite initiation in garnet solid electrolytes using an in-plane cell geometry. We show that single-crystal garnet electrolytes sustain a dendrite initiation current nearly 10 times higher than polycrystalline counterparts containing grain boundaries and voids. Introducing surface scratches into the single-crystal electrolytes decreases the dendrite initiation current by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the finely polished sample. Weibull statistical analysis of the dendrite initiation current distributions reveals a strong dependence of dendrite initiation on surface flaws and surface roughness. In addition, nanoindentation experiments reveal that single-crystal garnet electrolytes possess substantially greater resistance to crack initiation than polycrystalline electrolytes. Multiphysics simulations further show that larger surface flaw sizes (a proxy of larger surface roughness) intensify current focusing and stress concentration, thereby promoting dendrite initiation at lower current densities compared with smaller flaws. Overall, these findings establish surface flaws and their sizes as the key parameter controlling Li dendrite initiation and provide a mechanistic basis for enabling high-current operation in solid-state batteries.

papers.title: The Enthalpy–Entropy Tug-of-War in Pt-Hydrogen Adsorption: Reconciling Bond Strength and Interfacial Order
papers.abstract: In electrochemical systems, the thermodynamics of hydrogen underpotential deposition (HUPD) on platinum are traditionally explained solely by the strength of the metal-adsorbate bond. Here, we demonstrate that the structural reorganization of the electrical double layer plays an equally vital role. Using temperaturedependent adsorption experiments in diverse acidic and alkaline electrolytes, we systematically isolate the Gibbs free energy (ΔG°), entropy (ΔS°), and enthalpy (ΔH°) of adsorption. Our findings reveal an enthalpyentropy tug-of-war, where the interfacial entropic term (TΔS°) constitutes a substantial 40% to 60% of the total enthalpic contribution. Highly solvated, structure-making ions (such as SO4 2- and Na+) enthalpically stabilize adsorbed hydrogen but impose a severe entropic penalty by strongly ordering interfacial water molecules. Adsorption spontaneity (ΔG°) emerges as a delicate balance of these competing thermodynamic forces. These insights provide an actionable framework for rational electrolyte design in electrocatalysis.

papers.title: The Design and Application of Diureido Functionalized Spiroligomers as Diphosphate Receptors
papers.abstract: Spiroligomers are rigid, stereochemically defined scaffolds that can be programmed to display functional groups in precise three-dimensional constellations. We utilize this scaffold to position two urea groups in a preorganized geometry for anion binding. Among the receptors synthesized, the spiroligomer with RRRR-configuration displayed the strongest affinity for hydrogen pyrophosphate H2PPi (H2P2O7

papers.title: Versatile Zinc Catalyst for Solvent-free Selective Polyester Mixture Depolymerization
papers.abstract: Catalytic depolymerization of waste polyesters and admixtures with other polymers remains challenging, reflecting limitations in selectivity, solvent use, and product separation. Here we report an earth-abundant Zn(OTf)2-catalyzed (OTf = trifluoromethanesulfonate) solvent-free, sorting-free process that converts polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and related polyesters into the corresponding monomer diacids and acetaldehyde under aerobic conditions, even with commodity polymers containing pigments, additives, and other polymers. This process operates across diverse polyester classes, maintaining chemoselectivity in postconsumer plastics mixtures, blended textiles, and real-world feedstocks including colored bottles, carpet fibers, and fabrics. Coupling depolymerization to volatile product separation enables direct recovery of high-purity diacids and acetaldehyde, leaving non-volatile catalyst and other contaminants behind. Kinetic analysis, control experiments, acetaldehyde trapping, and DFT computation identify a non-classical Zn+2-mediated β-H-assisted fragmentation via a vinyl ester intermediate, distinct from conventional hydrolytic pathways. Sequential-addition and multi-gram continuous-process simulation experiments confirm catalyst recyclability and integrated monomer recovery, establishing a scalable reaction–separation platform for closed-loop polyester recycling.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by the authors because a contributor should not have been listed. An updated version is available at 10.26434/chemrxiv.15007883/v3

papers.title: Photoredox/Cobalt-catalyzed Cascade Rearrangement-Cyclization of Alkene
papers.abstract: A photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed sequential rearrangement-cyclization of unactivated alkenes is reported. 1,1diarylalkenes bearing tethered nucleophiles undergo a selective 1,2-aryl migration, initiated by metal-hydride hydrogen atom transfer and radical-polar crossover, and followed by intramolecular cyclization. Evaluating the catalytic reaction manifolds suggested that this system offers high reactivity and migratory selectivity. The preference for the 1,2-aryl shift over direct cyclization was rationalized by DFT calculations. This catalytic protocol enables accessing diverse spirocyclic and heterocyclic architectures.

papers.title: Tuning covalence for phosphorus-mediated C-C coupling in carbon monoxide electroreduction to multicarbon oxygenates
papers.abstract: Electrochemical carbon monoxide reduction (COR) is a promising route for sustainable production of multicarbon chemicals from CO2, as it bypasses the large carbon losses of direct CO2 electroreduction. In most electrocatalysts currently explored to tune COR selectivity towards highadded value multicarbon oxygenated molecules, like acetate and ethanol, copper is the catalytic site of C-C bond formation. Herein, we show that by designing nanoparticles of a strongly covalent copper compound, CuSi2P3, we retain isolated copper atoms during COR and trigger the intervention of phosphorus atoms as C-C coupling sites, without directly involving copper atoms. This profound change in COR mechanism results in a high selectivity towards C2 molecules (80 % Faradaic efficiency), especially oxygenates (73%), at a current density of -150 mA cm-2. This work reveals the importance of tailoring, via the crystal structure, the local environment of metal atoms, to achieve original selectivity in COR with new families of electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification Reveals the Limits of Lattice Thermal Conductivity Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (κ L ) drives thermoelectric materials discovery, yet existing machine learning models rarely quantify the reliability of their predictions. Here, we use evidential neural networks to quantify predictive uncertainty and split it into aleatoric uncertainty (data noise) and epistemic uncertainty (model ignorance). Our analysis reveals that predictions of very low lattice thermal conductivity are inherently unreliable as aleatoric noise dominates the uncertainty, and this noise can rival or even exceed the predicted value itself. High-κ L materials, by contrast, carry higher epistemic uncertainty, indicating room for improvement by additional training data. Consistent with this observation, adding out-of-distribution samples improves model accuracy by reducing model uncertainty. We further develope an uncertainty-aware screening method that prioritizes predictions with low total uncertainty rather than relying solely on the absolute value of κ L . This approach recovers a wide range of compositional classes with low κL from the Starrydata experimental repository at nearly twice the rate of random selection, thereby narrowing the search space needed to identify promising materials. These results establish evidential neural networks as a practical uncertainty-aware tool for κ L prediction, enabling reliable candidate screening and guiding data-collection to accelerate materials discovery.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Molecular Science: A Survey on Representation and Cognition
papers.abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into the natural sciences marks a shift from specialized discriminative models to generalist generative agents. However, adapting LLMs to chemistry presents a core challenge: the mismatch between the linear, ambiguous nature of natural language and the discrete, topological, and physical nature of molecules. This review provides a systematic framework for bridging this gap, organizing recent advances through the dual lenses of representation alignment and cognitive mechanism. First, we examine how molecular modalities are adapted to the transformer architecture, progressing from Linguistic Linearization, which optimizes symbolic grammars such as SMILES and SELFIES, to Topological Perception, which injects graph inductive biases through adapters and projectors, and finally to Geometric Grounding, which encodes 3D physical reality and equivariance. Second, we analyze how LLMs acquire and deploy chemical knowledge through three complementary pathways: Internalization, which cultivates parametric intuition through pre-training and alignment; Externalization, which anchors generation to physical reality via retrieval and tool orchestration; and Reasoning, which we further decompose into four strategies spanning contextual analogy, sequential deduction, strategic planning, and introspective refinement. Building on this dual-lens framework, we map downstream capabilities onto a four-level task hierarchy spanning Semantic Translation, Predictive Inference, Constrained Generation, and Autonomous Discovery, and we identify three coupled challenges at the representation-cognition interface, outlining a research roadmap toward chemically grounded AI systems.

papers.title: Visualizing Electron Flow at Transition States by Natural Reaction Orbitals
papers.abstract: Transition-state analysis in quantum chemistry provides structural and energetic information but does not directly reveal how electron density is redistributed at the onset of bond reorganization. Although frontier-orbital theory is highly effective for predicting reactivity from reactant molecules, it is less suited to transition states, where bond-breaking and bond- forming processes are already underway. Here, we show that natural reaction orbital (NRO) analysis provides a response-based framework for directly visualizing electron flow at transition states. By extracting the dominant occupied-virtual mixing induced by nuclear displacement along the imaginary vibrational mode, NRO analysis reveals the electronic response that drives bond reorganization. Applications to representative pericyclic reactions show that the essential electron-density redistribution is captured by only a few dominant NRO pairs and closely reproduces conventional curved-arrow descriptions. In a more 2 complex system, NRO analysis automatically extracts localized, reaction-relevant orbital response even when canonical frontier orbitals are extensively delocalized. NRO analysis thus provides a compact and chemically intuitive framework for transition-state electronflow analysis.

papers.title: Synergistic living lubrication by microalgal suspensions
papers.abstract: Hypothesis: Friction limits the efficiency of both large-scale engines and miniature devices. While current reliance on petroleum-based lubricants raises sustainability concerns, microalgal suspensions could be an eco-friendly alternative. Microalgae cells remain surrounded by a slippery extracellular matrix called mucilage; these cells also carry a negative charge, so that, electrostatic repulsion against a similarly charged confining surface is expected to reduce the solid-solid contact thereby reducing friction. Furthermore, intracellular components from ruptured cells too are expected to yield lubricating effect. Experiment: Friction experiments were conducted with microalgal layer deposited on glass plate as a lubricant and a deformable hemispherical lens of poly(dimethylsiloxane) as indenter. Five different green microalgae strains: Scenedesmus species, Scenedesmus Obliquus, Desmodesmus species, Chlorella species, Chlorella Vulgaris were used. Control experiments were done on wet glass plate and on lipid layer extracted from enzymatically ruptured microalgae cells. The surface chemical character of the substrate too was systematically varied. Finding: The algae suspension was found to reduce friction by an order of magnitude compared to a bare glass. Extent of lubrication increased progressively with growth of microalgae. The total lipid released upon cell rupture, together with the microalgae suspension, reduced the friction coefficient by approximately two orders of magnitude. A reduction in friction was observed also on plasma oxidized surfaces carrying surface charges. Furthermore, 2 a spent microalgal suspension could be regenerated and recycled, highlighting its potential as a green, sustainable and cost-effective lubricant.

papers.title: NO-Driven Radical Propagation Enables Accretion-product Formation in Cis-Decalin Oxidation
papers.abstract: Molecular-level understanding of secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation from anthropogenic volatile organic compounds (AVOCs), including polycyclic hydrocarbons such as decalin (C10H18), remains limited. Here, we investigate the OH-initiated oxidation of cisdecalin in quartz flow-tube reactors at short residence-times using chemical ionization orbitrap mass spectrometry employing a multi-scheme chemical ionization (MION) inlet. Bromide (Br-) and nitrate (NO3-) ionization methods were applied at 0.9 and 2.9 s reaction-times, respectively, to characterize oxidation-products. Under NO-free conditions, oxidation propagation remained inefficient at short reaction-timescales. Upon NO addition, highly oxygenated molecules (HOMs) and accretion-products formed rapidly, a finding that contrasts

papers.title: The chemomechanics of paracetamol polymorphs studied using density functional theory
papers.abstract: The mechanical properties of pharmaceutical crystal polymorphs are of great importance in tablet manufacturing, reducing the overall production cost. In this study, computational work was performed via density functional theory (DFT) calculations on three paracetamol crystal polymorphs: Forms I, II, and III. Form I is of monoclinic structure while forms II and III are orthorhombic. Linking types of chemical bonding to elastic properties, we discovered that for both forms II and III, the direction governed by the intermolecular hydrogen bond OH-O possesses the stiffest Young’s modulus and the lowest Poisson ratio. Meanwhile the least stiffness and largest Poisson ratio were found to be along the directions bonded by van der Waals (vdW). Lastly NH-O bond governed directions showed intermediate stiffness and Poisson ratios. For form I, no specific bond controls the axes directions; therefore, no similar chemomechanical trends can be elucidated. Moving to compressibility, there is a contradiction in literature regarding whether Form I or II is more compressible. This is due to their nearly equal bulk modulus values. Lastly, we compared the evaluation of the elastic properties of the three forms using two computational approaches: brute-force calculations and second-order elastic constants. Both agree well in terms of magnitudes and chemomechanical trends. Furthermore, the elastic constants approach revealed that Form III is mechanically unstable along certain crystallographic directions other than the principal axes, and this would be difficult in brute-force due to the higher computational cost.

papers.title: Shape-Aware Gaussian Process Kernels for Closed-Loop Bayesian Optimization of Gradients in Automated LC Method Development
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a promising strategy for accelerating gradient-elution liquid chromatography (LC) method development, but its practical success depends on several tightly coupled components. Here we report two main advances. First, for the Gaussian process (GP) surrogate models used within BO, we introduce a shape-aware gradient representation that compares gradient profiles directly through a Wasserstein-distance kernel, rather than through the pump-timetable coordinates used by standard representations. Second, we establish a robust automated acquisition and analysis workflow based on a trap phase that isolates gradient-driven elution and makes reliable closed-loop measurement possible. These are supported by three refinements: a flexible gradient domain with variable method duration and user-defined composition bounds, a window-relative sampler for monotonic gradient programs, and an adaptive reference point for multi-objective optimization. Across in silico and experimental datasets, Wasserstein-based representations generally predict separation quality more accurately than timetable-based approaches, especially when only a few training samples are available. This improved accuracy translates into more data-efficient singleand multi-objective optimization campaigns. Finally, we demonstrate the closed-loop framework in experimental case studies, where both single-and multi-objective campaigns improve upon a custom baseline method for a polymer-additive sample. Together, these results show that shape-aware gradient representations improve both GP predictive accuracy and BO sample efficiency, and that a flexible gradient domain, robust automated acquisition and analysis, and compatible sampling and optimization strategies enable effective closed-loop LC method development

papers.title: Anisotropic Nanochitin Hydrogels as Biomimetic Scaffolds Supporting Directed Osteoblast Adhesion and Alignment
papers.abstract: Developing biomimetic scaffolds that replicate the complex anisotropic structure of natural bone remains a persistent challenge in tissue engineering. Here we report an anisotropic hydrogel based on chitin nanofibrils, engineered through a combination of unidirectional freezing and amine-phosphate crosslinking. These hydrogels feature highly ordered, macroscale pore channels where the individual fibrillar building blocks are co-aligned along the freezing front, exhibiting a hierarchical structure with alignment from nanoscale to macroscale. The hydrogels showcase remarkable mechanical properties in aqueous environments exhibiting nonlinear strain-stiffening, exceptional fatigue resistance enabled by dynamic realignment of their oriented pore walls under compression load. The anisotropic matrix environment directed the growth of MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblast cultures. The in vitro cell adhesion and growth experiments performed on 2D substrate quantitively revealed a crosslinker dependent cell attachment and viability. Together, these findings establish an anisotropic hydrogel platform that combines mechanical robustness, efficient mass transport and cellular growth, offering potential for applications in tissue repair and regenerative medicine where structurally guided biomaterials are desirable.

papers.title: Chemical Descriptors as Bases and Metrics across Interpolation and Unseen-Element Transfer
papers.abstract: Chemical descriptors determine both the effect functions a model can express and the chemical levels across which it shares information. On complete perovskite and protein grids, we separate these roles as the rank and geometry of a common kernel: free categorical effects with a descriptor metric remove basis error, while the ratio of observed compositions to identified parameters, n/p, predicts where regularisation is most valuable.
