Holding an element out entirely exposes a second information limit: semiparametric transfer succeeds for smooth formation-energy and volume fields, whereas magnetic error concentrates in context-dependent A × X state variation. Target-free electronic probes reduce error from 0.7095 to 0.6523, and their per-element gain tracks the increase in outer-training state support (ρ = 0.475). These results define a two-axis design rule: use n/p to choose regularisation for represented levels and context-conditioned state support to evaluate representations for unseen-level transfer.

papers.title: A trace-hierarchy theorem for shared splittings in coupled spin-½ NMR spectra
A Flexible Framework for Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experiences in Advanced Chemistry Laboratory Courses
papers.abstract: Course-based undergraduate research experiences (CUREs) broaden access to the high-impact practice of undergraduate research, but even faculty experienced in mentoring undergraduate researchers may lack a clear roadmap for translating that research into a course format, creating a barrier to adoption of the CURE pedagogy. To address this barrier, we present a flexible framework (Flexi-Framework) for integrating faculty research into upper-level laboratory coursework using a series of activities that guide students through four phases of scientific research: (I) Obtaining, Evaluating, and Organizing Information, (II) Asking Questions and Planning Investigations; (III) Investigation, Data Analysis, and Iteration; and (IV) Justification and Communication through a written report and/or oral presentation. The framework consists of assessable, workshop-style activities that can be adapted to different research topics while maintaining the CURE-defining elements of collaboration, discovery and relevance, and iteration. Over the past decade, the Flexi-Framework has been implemented in multiple upper-division chemistry CUREs across three institutions and several subdisciplines of chemistry. Assessment using the Classroom Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE) survey and the Laboratory Course Assessment Survey (LCAS) demonstrates student-reported gains and course elements consistent with national CURE benchmarks. The CURE Flexi-Framework thus provides a model for integrating faculty research into coursework, with the goal of lowering barriers to CURE development and adoption across institutional and disciplinary contexts.

papers.title: First-Principles Design of a Quantum-Selective Solid-State Hydrogen-to-Electricity Conversion Cell with Catalyst-Free Anode Dissociation (H2DE)
papers.abstract: Traditional Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) fuel cells are limited by the high cost of Platinum catalysts, polymer degradation, and parasitic pumping losses. In this work, we present the first-principles design of a quantum-selective, air-breathing solid-state hydrogen-to-electricity conversion cell (H2DE) utilizing a catalyst-free anode. By sandwiching a monolayer Hexagonal Boron Nitride (h-BN) membrane between a Magnesium (Mg) anode and a Nickel Oxide (NiO) cathode, we establish a permanent contact potential of Vbi = 1.64 V, yielding an intrinsic field of 0.492 V/ Å. To split hydrogen without a precious metal catalyst at the anode, we design tapered Magnesium nanotips on the anode face. These tips concentrate electrostatic lines, amplifying the local field to Eapex = 2.77 V/ Å at the apex, which exceeds the 2.0 V/ Å polarization threshold to dissociate H2 spontaneously. WKB quantum calculations show 100.0% proton transmission with electron leakage suppressed to 0.21%. 3D finite element (CalculiX) and finite volume (OpenFOAM) modeling verify nanoscale structural safety (SF = 2.11) and negligible parasitic pumping power (7.23 μW). This solid-state design provides a durable, high-efficiency pathway for clean hydrogen-to-electricity conversion utilizing earth-abundant materials. Highlights A catalyst-free, Platinum-free anode design for hydrogen-to-electricity conversion is proposed. A built-in Mg–NiO Schottky field (0.492 V/Å) drives spontaneous H2 dissociation at Mg nanotips. WKB tunneling calculations show 475× proton-over-electron selectivity through monolayer h-BN. DFT, FEA, and CFD modeling jointly verify electronic, mechanical, and fluidic feasibility. Key limitations — periodic-boundary effects, ZPE corrections, and H2 embrittlement risk — are identified for future experimental validation.

papers.title: Lifecycle and technoeconomic assessment of Donnan dialysis for lithium brine concentration in direct lithium extraction
papers.abstract: Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from brines could help meet the growing demand for lithium needed for the global energy transition. Of the proposed DLE processes, unit operations required for lithium purification and concentration are often the most energy- and emission-intensive stages of DLE. In this work, we develop steadystate simulations of a commercial-scale DLE treatment train alongside a framework for lifecycle and technoeconomic assessment. We also simulate a novel DLE treatment train using a low energy-intensity Donnan dialysis (DD) process for lithium purification and concentration, and we compare the lifecycle impacts (specific energy consumption, embodied energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, and water use) and economics (levelized cost of product, net present value, and internal rate of return) of the conventional and novel process on a kg -1 Li 2 CO 3 product basis under six base case scenarios. We observe a clear trade-off between energy- and emission-reduction benefits of the novel process versus water use and cost. Monte Carlo simulation confirms the robustness of analysis to changes in process parameters. Simulation of a best-case scenario (optimal membrane properties and membrane cost reduction guided by federal targets) projects that the novel process could become energy-, emission-, and costcompetitive against the conventional process, though it would remain inferior in terms of water use. Ultimately, this simulation framework provides a means for DLE researchers spanning material innovation, technology development, and process design to benchmark and quantify process-level impacts of their work.

papers.title: Beyond Multiscale: A Neural Network-Unified Molecular Model for Asymmetry-Free Dynamics Simulation
papers.abstract: Adaptive multiscale simulations, such as adaptive QM/MM, are indispensable for investigating complex solution dynamics but historically suffer from a fundamental dilemma: the dynamic exchange of identical solvent molecules across different model resolutions introduces an energetic asymmetry under solvent exchange (specifically, a permutation asymmetry where physically identical molecules are treated indistinguishably yet subjected to different force fields depending on their instantaneous positions). This asymmetry forces a prohibitive trade-off between severe structural distortions and the violation of Hamiltonian conservation (continuous energy drift). To resolve this issue, we propose the ”Integrated Molecular Model,” a paradigm-shifting framework that unifies multiple resolutions into a single, dynamically consistent potential. By employing a neural network that takes only the multiscale weight functions as input descriptors, our model learns to systematically cancel the non-physical transition forces originating from spatial discontinuities. As a proof-of-concept, we validated this unified framework on bulk water, aqueous ionic solutions, and reactive hydronium ions. Our approach not only faithfully restores artifact-free solvation structures but also strictly conserves the Hamiltonian, enabling unprecedentedly stable, long-term simulations under the microcanonical (NVE) ensemble. Consequently, the model successfully eliminates artificial thermostat-induced breathing modes, allowing for the rigorous evaluation of intrinsic dynamical properties such as diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, owing to its physically informed network design, the correction potential introduces less than 2% additional computational overhead and demonstrates remarkable zero-shot transferability across chemically similar ionic species. By eradicating the inherent asymmetry of adaptive multiscale modeling, this highly scalable framework establishes a robust foundation for high-fidelity simulations of complex condensed-phase phenomena, including reactive dynamics at solid-liquid interfaces and ion transport in battery electrolytes.

papers.title: Sanity and Decomposition Pipeline for Metal-Organic Frameworks in Generative AI
papers.abstract: Generative models for metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) demand automated validation and decomposition tools that scale to large datasets while preserving chemical realism. Here we present a unified sanity and decomposition framework built around two newly developed tools – LibCif, an ultrafast C++ library for MOF decomposition and structural validation, and OxiChecker, an oxidation-state anomaly detector – complemented by external geometry-based sanity filters (PLATON, MOFChecker). We benchmark OxiChecker against MOSAEC across major MOF databases (ARCMOF, BWDB, CoRE-MOF, QMOF), compare the full Sanity Pipeline against standalone methods on CoRE-MOF, QMOF, and approximately 25,000 structures from an in-house LLaMA-3-based generative model (1B parameters), and summarize PLATON alerts over the 300k-scale BWDB collection. The Sanity Pipeline is shown to effectively subsume the charge-balance diagnostics of MOSAEC while providing complementary geometric checks. LibCif achieves sub-second per-structure runtimes, up to three orders of magnitude faster than competing tools, making it uniquely suited as a real-time reward signal in reinforcement-learning generative pipelines, while the full validation cascade serves as an offline post-filter. LibCif further provides O(N) supercell-aware decomposition into chemically meaningful nodes and linkers. Applying it to several million structures pooled from 26 public datasets, we extract ∼7 million linker occurrences and deduplicate them into ∼1.05 million unique organic linkers (∼0.84 million after chemical curation), organized into scaffold families. A six-tier similarity search system, deployable as a local web platform, was also created, turning the decomposition output into a practical resource for building-block extraction and generative design.

papers.title: Redox Properties of Structural Fe in Clay Minerals: 5. The Role of Fe in the Tetrahedral Sheet of Synthetic Smectites
papers.abstract: Iron-bearing smectite clay minerals are important redox-active phases in soils and sediments. Yet, the influence of iron substitution in the tetrahedral sheets ( Tet Fe) of smectites on their redox properties remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the repeated reduction and re-oxidation of synthetic Fe-rich smectites, known as synthetic nontronites (SyN), with constant content of Fe in the octahedral sheet, Oct Fe, but variable initial content of Tet Fe. The redox properties of redox-cycled smectites were characterized using mediated electrochemical analysis. The resulting Fe 2+ /Fe Total ratios determined over a wide range of reduction potentials were analyzed using a process-based model to extract thermodynamic and kinetic descriptors of the interfacial electron transfer and subsequent charge redistribution processes that occur during the redox reaction. The fitted standard reduction potentials and apparent diffusion coefficients for charge redistribution were insensitive to Tet Fe content, indicating that thermodynamics and bulk charge transport within the smectite crystal are predominantly governed by the Fe–O–Fe networks in the octahedral sheet. Conversely, samples containing Tet Fe exhibited fitted interfacial electron-transfer rate constants approximately an order of magnitude higher than the Tet Fe-free sample. Tet Fe accelerated the rate constant of smectite redox reactions by approximately an order of magnitude. Comparison of these thermodynamic and kinetic descriptors between synthetic nontronites and natural reference smectites showed that parameter values converge within a narrow range across iron-rich dioctahedral smectites. These model-based results highlight the distinct roles of Oct Fe and Tet Fe in controlling smectite redox reactivity in subsurface environments, with Oct Fe governing the thermodynamics and Tet Fe primarily influencing interfacial electron transfer kinetics.

papers.title: Iso 9-HODE and iso 13-HODE: Novel markers of thermal processing in vegetable oils
Gateway to Data Visualization and Analysis in Solid-State Nanopores
authors: Y. M. Nuwan. D. Y. Bandara
papers.abstract: Solid-state nanopores are a class of single-molecule sensors with a growing footprint in molecular fingerprinting. Given the unique nature of experiments, data extraction, visualization, and interpretation are often carried out using customized software: an unacknowledged legacy barrier that stifles overall productivity and hinders entry for early-career researchers. With concerted efforts to democratize the solid-state nanopore technology and make it more accessible to a broader audience, there is a need to create a roadmap for data handling and processing associated with solid-state nanopores. In this work, we present a suite of apps and methods engineered to transition from raw ionic current traces to actionable data metrics. Our platform provides an integrated framework for the rigorous characterization of translocation events through the HyperXtract 2.0 app (HX2.0), which extracts over 50 distinct waveform features per event. To ensure data integrity, the quality of the nanopore is quantified using a suite of health parameters that underpin the biophysical reliability of the resulting waveforms. To facilitate multi-dimensional analysis, the software integrates specialized visualization modules for scatter plots, histograms, and non-linear curve fitting. It also includes high-density contour and heat maps (with clustering and denoising options), which are essential for resolving overlapping molecular populations that standard 1D plots might obscure. Collectively, bivariate contouring of waveform features from HX introduces a new path for the construction of QR-like molecular fingerprinting architecture. These apps considerably accelerate the data treatment step, empowering rapid and confident post-experiment decision-making.

papers.title: A framework for accessing elusive intermediate-sized PdnL2n (n = 8, 9) metal-organic cages
papers.abstract: Within the extensive family of Pd n L 2n metal-organic cages (MOCs), some structures are much easier to access than others. Small structures (Pd 2 L 4 to Pd 6 L 12 ) and large pseudospherical structures (≥Pd 12 L 24 ) can be readily obtained from flat aryl-based ligands. Intermediate-sized, lower-symmetry Pd n L 2n MOCs have remained challenging to access as thermodynamic products, limiting structural diversity. We present a general design strategy exploiting dihedral twisting and donor group offset in bisimidazole-naphthalene and bisimidazole-pyrene ligands to achieve the required coordination angles for Pd 8 L 16 (~105.1°) and Pd 9 L 18 (~109.5°) assemblies. This approach delivers the first thermodynamically stable Pd 9 L 18 tricapped trigonal prisms alongside multiple rare Pd 8 L 16 square antiprisms, expanding the accessible range of Pd n L 2n geometries. Crystallographic analysis, supported by a newly developed three-angle mathematical framework, rationalises these assemblies and provides predictive guidelines for future cage design. Our findings establish a generalisable route to intermediate-sized MOCs, bridging the gap between small and large structures and enabling systematic control over symmetry and topology.

papers.title: A computed thermoelectric feature database for 50,992 GNoME materials
papers.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials now make it feasible to compute rich physical property sets for very large libraries of hypothetical crystals, but such feature sets are rarely released in analysis-ready form, and thermal-transport descriptors — central to thermoelectric performance — are especially scarce. Here we present a computed feature database for 50,992 novel, thermodynamically plausible crystalline materials drawn from Google DeepMind's Graph Networks for Materials Exploration (GNoME) database and filtered for thermoelectric relevance (non-metallic, finite band gap, energy above the Materials Project convex hull ≤ 0.05 eV/atom). For every material we provide composition and crystallographic descriptors; CHGNet universal- potential energetics, per-site magnetic moments, and a 64-dimensional learned crystal embedding; a full harmonic thermal-transport layer (elastic tensor, Debye temperature, sound velocities, and Cahill/Clarke minimum-conductivity bounds); and an anharmonic layer (Grüneisen parameter from a CHGNet equation-of-state, and a Slack-model lattice thermal conductivity). CHGNet formation energies reproduce the underlying DFT values with a mean absolute error of 0.036 eV/atom (Pearson r = 0.999), and two independently computed bulk moduli agree to a 5.3 % median difference (r = 0.992). To our knowledge this is the first release of a complete lattice-thermal-transport feature layer for the GNoME material set, enabling data-driven thermoelectric screening and machine-learning studies at scale.

papers.title: Reaction-induced selection of phase-separated RNA protocells
papers.abstract: The earliest Darwinian entities likely coupled self-reproducing molecules to protocell survival. However, such coupling has not been demonstrated for RNA-based protocells. Here, we show that ribozyme-catalyzed RNA reactions drive the differential survival of coacervate droplets. Sequence-dependent reactions generate distinct RNA length distributions, which shift coacervate phase boundaries. Consequently, a salinity increase induced during partial drying selectively dissolves less stable droplets, whereas droplets enriched in longer RNA products persist. Upon rehydration, surviving droplets regrow while retaining part of their previous RNA composition, alongside the formation of new droplets. These results establish a direct link between RNA sequence, catalytic activity and compartment survival, and show that selection can be combined with compositional inheritance in RNA-based coacervates. They provide a minimal physicochemical route by which RNA reactions could generate protocell-level Darwinian properties.

papers.title: Quintet Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip TDDFT with a Dressed Kernel for Four-Orbital Strong Correlation
Multimodal thermodynamic dataset for polymer solution model training
papers.abstract: Polymer solutions are thermodynamically complex mixtures owing to local correlations from chain connectivity and size asymmetry between polymer and solvent. A consequence of polymer solution complexity is a richness in solution phase behavior which gives rise to industrially and scientifically relevant material properties, the prediction of which is a long-standing goal of polymer science. The Flory-Huggins \chi -parameter remains the most widely-used method for quantifying such interactions despite being a fitted parameter specific to the Flory-Huggins solution model. This approach contrasts with small molecule thermodynamics which generally use model-free thermodynamic interaction data such as the activity coefficients. The lack of an accessible database of model-free thermodynamic interaction properties for polymer solutions is one obstacle hindering the development of more advanced thermodynamic models for polymer solutions. In this work, a database of over 7,000 model-free thermodynamic properties obtained across the composition range with a variety of experimental techniques was compiled. These points represent over 1,000 unique polymer-solvent combinations of over 50 polymers and 170 solvents. An additional ≈10,000 points of liquid-liquid equilibrium (LLE) data was compiled for over 180 unique polymer-solvent pairs. To make the dataset widely available to the community and to encourage community contributions, all data was uploaded into the CRIPT data ecosystem.

papers.title: Dynamic Covalent Hydrogels as Fluorescent Sensors for Pseudomonas aeruginosa Lectins and Biofilms
papers.abstract: A smart hydrogel incorporating LecA-targeting galactose residues, in combination with a boronic acid fluorescent reporter, gives rise to a material capable of discerning P. aeruginosa biomarkers through modulation in its fluorescence. The principle has been demonstrated in solution and solid phase experiments, as well as with isolated lectin biomarkers and in the presence of live, whole cell bacteria. This strategy offers a means of indicating P. aeruginosa biofilms on surfaces, with potential applications in identifying healthcare-associated contamination on medical devices, including catheters and tracheal tubes.

papers.title: Fragment-Based Virtual Screening and Experimental Validation of MMP-9 Hemopexinlike Domain Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) is a key mediator of extracellular matrix remodeling and cancer metastasis, yet the development of selective inhibitors remains challenging due to high conservation of its catalytic domain. Targeting the less conserved hemopexin-like (PEX) domain offers a promising strategy for isoform-selective inhibition. Here, we report an integrated fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) approach combining pharmacophore modelling, structure-based virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and extensive biological validation to identify novel MMP-9 PEX domain inhibitors. Fragment screening and structure-guided optimization led to a focused series of indole-based derivatives, which exhibited favourable binding energies and stable interactions within the PEX domain, confirmed through MD simulations (n=3). The top candidates were synthesized and subjected to comprehensive biological evaluation, including cytotoxicity profiling across multiple cancer cell lines, colony formation, cell migration, apoptosis induction, mitochondrial membrane depolarization and flow-cytometric analysis. Among them, IN-06 demonstrated potent and selective antiproliferative activity against HCT-116 colon cancer cells while sparing noncancerous cells. Target-specific studies using immunofluorescence, gelatin zymography and enzyme-based fluorometric assays established that IN-06 effectively suppresses MMP-9 expression and enzymatic activity in a concentration-dependent manner. Overall, this work highlights the effectiveness of integrated computational modelling, synthesis and experimental validation for the discovery of novel MMP-9 PEX domain inhibitors and provides a promising chemical scaffold for further preclinical development.

papers.title: External Evaluation of Multi-Agent AI Systems in Drug Discovery: A PRISMA-Informed Scoping Review of the External-Evaluation Gap
papers.abstract: Multi-agent large-language-model (LLM) systems are increasingly proposed for tasks across drug discovery and development. This PRISMA-informed scoping review examines a narrower question than capability surveys: whether reported system performance has been evaluated by investigators independent of the original developers. The review applies an explicit operational definition of multi-agent architecture and maps included systems to one of six stages: target identification, molecular screening, molecular design, lead optimization, delivery formulation, or clinical-trial workflows. Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity (ADMET) properties appear as an optimization objective within molecular design rather than as a separate stage, because no system in the corpus treats ADMET evaluation as its primary reported task. The curated primary corpus contains 13 unique systems satisfying the strict multi-agent definition. One system (STELLA) has an independent external evaluation, reported by an unaffiliated group through BioML-bench. Three systems (Robin, OriGene, LipoAgent) report author-run empirical validation in biological systems. One system (MT-Mol) reports author-run evaluation on third-party benchmarks. The remaining eight report author-curated computational evaluation only. Six benchmark resources are inventoried separately; four have no located deployment against any system in the corpus, and of the two that do, only one was run by an unaffiliated group. A pre-specified sensitivity analysis shows that the two additional systems with documented independent external evaluation — TrialGPT and Biomni — both fall outside the strict multi-agent boundary, indicating that independent evaluation currently concentrates in single-agent, modular, and general-purpose systems rather than in strict multiagent architectures. The review provides a transparent taxonomy, an explicit classification protocol with a stated precedence rule, and a versioned evidence ledger.

papers.title: Text Embedding-Assisted Prediction of Corrosion Inhibition Efficiency Using Machine Learning under Small-Sample Conditions
papers.abstract: Machine learning has been increasingly applied to corrosion prediction, but limited experimental data remain a challenge for small-sample prediction. This study investigates how text embedding can be used as a molecular representation for predicting the corrosion inhibition efficiency of organic inhibitors for ZE41 magnesium alloy. An experimental dataset containing 75 inhibitors was used, with 60 samples for training and 15 samples for testing. Conventional molecular descriptors were combined with text embeddings generated using ChemBERTa and Qwen-text-embedding-v4, and five feature construction strategies were compared to examine the effects of embedding dimensionality and feature integration. Direct incorporation of high-dimensional ChemBERTa embeddings provided limited improvement, whereas dimensionality reduction improved the prediction performance. A selective hybrid strategy was further investigated, in which selected descriptors were incorporated into the text embedding while other descriptors were retained in their original numerical form. This strategy achieved a coefficient of determination of 0.61 and a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.79, compared to those of 0.12 and 0.43, respectively, for the conventional descriptor-based representation. The results suggest that text embedding may be more useful as a complementary representation to conventional molecular descriptors than as a direct replacement, when experimental data are limited.

papers.title: Development of the 12-6-4-3B Model: Incorporating Nonadditive Three-Body Interactions into Metal Ion Simulations
papers.abstract: Metal ions play fundamental roles in diverse biological and materials systems, yet accurately simulating them with force field models remains challenging due to pronounced polarization and charge transfer effects, which are intrinsically many-body in character. For example, Zn2+ serves as an essential co-factor in many important proteins. It can adopt coordination numbers of 4, 5, and 6 in aqueous phase and metalloenzymes, and capturing both the equilibrium among these states and the kinetic barriers connecting them remains difficult. Energy decomposition analysis (EDA) offers a lens into distinct energy components, providing deeper insight into contributions of different physical origin. By combining SobEDA with many-body expansion (MBE) framework, we systematically investigated the many-body EDA components for the [Zn(H2O)n]2+ (n = 2 − 6) clusters. Our results show the orbital term—representing polarization and charge transfer—dominates the three-body and higher-order contributions. Furthermore, many-body interactions in metal ion complexes converge considerably more slowly than in pure water: the many-body expansion for Zn2+ in aqueous solution is oscillatory, with successive terms alternating in sign and decaying slowly, such that four-body and higher-order contributions remain non-negligible. To examine how the water–ion–water three-body term depends on molecular geometry, we systematically scanned this trimer system by varying the ion–water distance and the water–ion–water angle. Using EDA throughout the scan and reasoning from the physical origins of each term, we proposed and parameterized three-body terms, yielding the 12-6-4-3B model, which explicitly incorporates three-body effects into a classical force field. Conventional 12-6 and 12-6-4 potentials, though widely used for metal ions in molecular dynamics simulations, are effectively pairwise and capture many-body effects only implicitly, which cannot simultaneously reproduce the water exchange mechanism and energetics of Zn2+. By contrast, after adjusting the C4 term, the 12-6-4-3B model correctly reproduces both the water exchange mechanism and the associated free energy barrier, demonstrating the benefit of explicitly incorporating three-body terms in metal ion force fields.

papers.title: Insights into Lithium Diffusion in Crystalline and Amorphous Solid Electrolytes with Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Amorphization is a widely used approach to tune the ionic conductivity in solid electrolytes, but its effect in different anion chemistries remains poorly understood. In this work, we employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) to quantify the effects of amorphization on Li-ion transport in lithium solid electrolytes from three anion chemistries: Li3YCl6 (LYC), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7P3S11 (LPS). With amorphization, it is observed that the ionic conductivity increases for LYC, decreases for LLTO and remains relatively unchanged for LPS, in agreement with previous experiments. Coordination analysis at 300K reveals that these ionic conductivity changes can be correlated with amorphization-induced changes in Li-anion coordination environments; decreases in coordination increase ionic conductivity and vice versa. These different responses show that the effect of amorphization on Li-ion diffusion behavior is not universal and is governed by specific anion coordination motifs.

papers.title: Shape-aware Gaussian process kernels for Closed-loop Bayesian Optimization of Gradients in Automated LC Method Developement
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a promising strategy for accelerating gradient-elution liquid chromatography (LC) method development, but its practical success depends on several tightly coupled components. Here we report two main advances. First, for the Gaussian process (GP) surrogate models used within BO, we introduce a shape-aware gradient representation that compares gradient profiles directly through a Wasserstein-distance kernel, rather than through the pump-timetable coordinates used by standard representations. Second, we establish a robust automated acquisition and analysis workflow based on a trap phase that isolates gradient-driven elution and makes reliable closed-loop measurement possible. These are supported by three refinements: a flexible gradient domain with variable method duration and user-defined composition bounds, a window-relative sampler for monotonic gradient programs, and an adaptive reference point for multi-objective optimization. Across in silico and experimental datasets, Wasserstein-based representations generally predict separation quality more accurately than timetable-based approaches, especially when only a few training samples are available. This improved accuracy translates into more data-efficient singleand multi-objective optimization campaigns. Finally, we demonstrate the closed-loop framework in experimental case studies, where both single-and multi-objective campaigns improve upon a custom baseline method for a polymer-additive sample. Together, these results show that shape-aware gradient representations improve both GP predictive accuracy and BO sample efficiency, and that a flexible gradient domain, robust automated acquisition and analysis, and compatible sampling and optimization strategies enable effective closed-loop LC method development

papers.title: Enantioselective endo-[2 + 2] Cycloaddition Catalyzed by Rhodium
papers.abstract: Transition metal-catalyzed enantioselective intramolecular [2 + 2] cycloadditions are less explored and have long failed to access 5/4-fused rings with bridgehead quaternary stereocenters—ubiquitous in complex natural products and pharmaceuticals—because the dominant exo-oxidative cyclometalation (exo-OCM) pathway is geometrically incompatible with these strained frameworks. We show that endo-OCM of type II diene-allene substrates circumvents this fundamental limitation. This strategy enables the first endo-[2 + 2] cycloaddition, providing asymmetric access to 5/4-fused skeletons bearing a bridgehead quaternary stereocenter using a rhodium/chiral phosphine catalyst. This work establishes a general platform for synthesizing previously inaccessible strained bicyclic motifs via enantioselective transition metal catalysis.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Antifungal Drug Discovery Against WHO Critical-Priority Pathogens: Toward a WHO-Aligned, Selectivity-Integrated Discovery Pipeline
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has demonstrated real power in medicinal chemistry generally, yet it remains almost entirely absent from actual antifungal drug development, a gap made more urgent by rising antifungal resistance and a drug pipeline that has produced almost no genuinely new chemical classes in two decades. Invasive fungal infections, rising antifungal resistance, and a critically depleted drug pipeline together constitute a public health emergency that recent burden estimates suggest rivals tuberculosis in annual mortality. Since 2022, the WHO Fungal Priority Pathogen List has offered a strategic plan for prioritizing resources; however, the use of artificial intelligence in the discovery of antifungals is still scattered, and even the most recent and extensive scoping review of the literature (106 primary studies) outlined existing applications but did not suggest how to unify them. This review concludes that the gap must be addressed by shifting the focus of antifungal AI research from two concepts to two principles: pathogen prioritization that is directly taken from the WHO list, and therapeutic selectivity that is considered a scored, quantitative constraint that is applied at every pipeline stage instead of as an afterthought when potential compounds are already identified. We are proposing a conceptual pipeline with 6 steps: pathogen stratification, AI-enabled target validation, generative molecular design, multi-objective optimization, forward ADMET and resistance predictions, and experimental prioritization. We operationalize this with two tools: a scored Priority-Selectivity Matrix, demonstrated here with a worked numerical example across five real antifungal targets, and a Stage-Specific AI Toolkit. We further provide a critical appraisal of the specific published tools that already exist in this space, HitList, Fung-AI, FungAMR, and a 2026 pooled CRISPRi screen, showing precisely where each stops short of an integrated, selectivity-first system, and we identify a structural blind spot largely absent from prior antifungal AI literature: the highest-value antifungal targets are integral membrane proteins, the exact protein class that current structure-prediction and docking models handle least reliably. Finally, we remark that all the antifungal agents developed in the last five years have been developed by traditional medicinal chemistry, not AI, so the regulatory process for an AI-generated antifungal has never been tested. This synthesis is designed to translate the scene of a series of disconnected computational demonstrations to a prioritized, discovery-focused, quantitatively assessed effort in the realm of antifungals.

papers.title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Enantioselective Intermolecular C-H Carbo-amination with Racemic Allenes
papers.abstract: Enantioselective carboamination of allenes especially in conjunction with 3d-metal catalysis remains a significant challenge. We report chiral cyclopentadienyl cobalt(III)-catalyzed regio-, chemo-, and enantioselective intermolecular C-H carboamination of racemic allenyl esters with N-phenoxyisobutyramides. The protocol offers an efficient approach for highly selective carboamination of allenes and affords synthetically valuable chiral γ-substituted-β-enamido esters with exceptional selectivities (up to 88% yield, >99:1 er, and >20:1 E/Z). Operating by a kinetic resolution pathway, the transformation was additionally optimized for recovery of enantioenriched allenes with high selectivity factors of up to 138. The utility was showcased by the resolution of methyl-(R,E)-(−)-tetradeca-2,4,5-trienoate, the male bean weevil pheromone.

papers.title: Evolutionary Approach for Construction of Miniproteins Incorporating Constrained β-Amino Acid Residues
papers.abstract: Although the progress of computer-aided design of proteins has been significant over recent years, de novo design of miniproteins remains challenging. In particular, structures with noncanonical secondary structures induced by β-amino acids, which exhibit exceptional properties, could not be readily obtained. Here, we develop a new approach to constructing a miniprotein based on evolution. The application of computer-assisted methods and the experimental validation of each step proved to be very effective. Several structural changes can be applied, including the addition of the β-amino acid-containing helical fragment, modifications of connectivity between secondary structures, changes in sequence length, and loop structure. The final set of highly conformationally stable miniproteins has been characterized by measuring thermodynamic parameters of folding using CD spectroscopy. The most stable miniprotein was analyzed in detail using NMR spectroscopy.

papers.title: Development of Hydrogen Valleys: Defining a Merit-order of End-uses
papers.abstract: Hydrogen valleys, which integrate renewable energy sources, hydrogen infrastructure, and end-use applications, play a crucial role in decarbonizing industrial energy hubs. However, the large-scale deployment of hydrogen is constrained by limited renewable electricity availability and high technology costs. To address these challenges, we develop a framework for optimally allocating renewable hydrogen across end-use sectors to maximize social welfare. A key insight from our analysis is that the merit order of hydrogen end-uses is dynamic, evolving with an increasing Social Cost of Carbon (SCC). When the SCC surpasses a threshold defined by the Social Opportunity Cost of Abatement (SOCA), allocating hydrogen to the most emissions-intensive sector becomes socially optimal, even if that sector has a higher sectoral abatement cost. Additionally, we demonstrate that minimizing welfare losses requires prioritizing sectors with limited viable low-carbon alternatives, ensuring that hydrogen is deployed where it delivers the greatest marginal benefit. A two-period dynamic model further illustrates how investment decisions should prioritize applications with higher learning potential in the initial period to accelerate cost reductions and long-term efficiency gains. We also evaluate second-best policy instruments in scenarios where carbon taxation alone fails to fully internalize externalities. Our findings indicate that demand-side subsidies, which directly support hydrogen adoption in end-use sectors, are more effective than production subsidies in ensuring a better alignment of hydrogen allocation with the social welfare optimum. We calibrate the model to the Industrial-Port-Zone of Marseille-Fos, revealing that sectors with limited low-carbon alternatives, such as chemicals and sectors with high learning potential such as steel industry, rank highest in the merit order for hydrogen deployment.

papers.title: Vector-Guided Drug Action via Active-Site Electric Fields: A Theoretical Framework Combining Quantum-Mechanical/Molecular-Mechanical Modeling and Vibrational Stark Tuning Principles
papers.abstract: Traditional rational drug design paradigms rely primarily on spatial complementary interactionssteric fit, localized hydrogen-bonding topologies, and static lipophilicity profiles—within macromolecular binding pockets. These models largely omit the catalytic and kinetic contributions of the large-scale, oriented endogenous electrostatic fields generated within structured enzymatic and receptor microenvironments. Building on experimentally established vibrational Stark effect (VSE) spectroscopy of enzyme active sites, we present a theoretical framework for Vector-Guided Pharmacology, in which the directional alignment between a pharmacophore’s transition dipole moment (∆µ ‡) or ground-state dipole (µ g) and the intrinsic active-site electric field vector (Epocket) is proposed as a determinant of binding affinity and the activation free-energy barrier (∆G‡) for covalent and non-covalent ligand stabilization. We formulate an electrostatic-embedding QM/MM Hamiltonian, consistent with polarizablemultipole (AMOEBA-type) force-field architectures, and derive the linear and quadratic Stark perturbation terms that couple a ligand’s dipole and polarizability to Epocket. Using representative, literature-consistent parameter values (field magnitudes of 10–50 MV/cm, as established by VSE spectroscopy, and transition dipole differences of several debye, typical of polarizable electrophilic warheads), we present illustrative worked evaluations of the model showing that parallel vector alignment can, in principle, lower the activation free energy by several kcal/mol relative to the antialigned configuration. These worked examples are direct, reproducible evaluations of the derived equations for assumed input parameters; they are not the output of new density-functional-theory (DFT) or molecular-dynamics (MD) calculations performed for this study, and no such calculations are claimed. The framework is offered as a conceptual and mathematical foundation, together with a proposed computational validation protocol, for treating electrostatic vector alignment as an orthogonal, testable parameter in rational drug design.

papers.title: A comparison of bottom-up, measurement-based and EPA inventory methane emission estimates for non–oil and gas sources in the Denver–Julesburg basin, Colorado
papers.abstract: While oil and gas emissions have historically received the most attention from regulators, industry stakeholders, and researchers due to regulatory and economic drivers, non-oil and gas sources can also contribute substantially to basin- and regional-scale methane (CH 4 ) fluxes and represent important mitigation opportunities. As part of a broader effort to quantify CH 4 from all sources within the Denver-Julesburg (DJ) basin, this study develops a measurement-based inventory of major non-oil and gas CH4 sources and reconciles measurement-based and bottom-up US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) estimates. Specifically, a facility-level bottom-up inventory generated using measurements from vehicle-mounted instruments coupled with backward Lagrangian stochastic modelling (WindTrax) was compared to a bottom-up inventory based on EPA emission factors (EFs) and emissions reported by landfill operators to the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP). We focus on emissions from concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs), municipal solid waste landfills, wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), and surface waterbodies (lakes and reservoirs). The utility of monthly mobile surveys to construct a measurement-based inventory in the DJ basin (39.9–40.7°N, 105.3–104.2°W) is evaluated. Seasonal variability in CH 4 emissions differed across sources, with CAFOs and WWTPs showing no consistent seasonal pattern, landfills exhibiting higher winter emissions, and lakes and reservoirs displaying higher emissions in warmer seasons. Total non-oil and gas annual emissions are estimated at 125 ± 22 Gg y -1 , compared to the EPA bottom-up estimate of 121 ± 31 Gg y -1 . These non-oil and gas emissions are higher than the measurement-based estimate of oil and gas emissions, 57 Gg y -1 , for the same DJ Basin boundary based on a previous study. Aggregated CH4 emissions indicated that CAFOs were the dominant source in the DJ region, contributing 53% of the total inventory in this study compared to 58% in the EPA inventory. Oil and gas sources were the second largest contributor, accounting for 31.4% and 32.1% of total emissions in this study and the EPA inventory, respectively, followed by municipal solid waste landfills (7.6% and 8.4%, respectively). Lakes and reservoirs contributed 7% in this study compared to 0.8% in the EPA inventory, while WWTPs were the smallest source category, contributing approximately 0.7% and 0.9%, respectively. Most previous studies compare short-term snapshot measurements with annual inventories, often leading to discrepancies because temporal variability is not adequately captured. In contrast, this study provides one of the most comprehensive year-long datasets currently available for non-oil and gas CH 4 sources in the DJ Basin and demonstrates that deriving and extrapolating EFs from repeated measurements across a spatially distributed set of facilities can produce annual estimates consistent with EPA inventories and GHGRP self-reported emissions. These results strongly suggest that agreement with inventories improves when measurements capture seasonal variability representative of annual operating conditions.

papers.title: Simultaneous Two-Directional Catalytic Radical Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: Two-directional synthesis is a powerful strategy for rapidly increasing molecular complexity, yet its tactical implementation with radical cross-coupling remains underdeveloped. Here, we report simultaneous two-directional radical cross-coupling of bifunctional radical precursors. Diacidderived bis-redox-active esters undergo Ag–Ni electrocatalytic decarboxylative arylation to access functionalized dibenzyl amines and related linkers, while diamine-derived bis-sulfonyl hydrazides participate in redox-neutral deaminative RCC. This strategy enables chemoselective, scalable access to valuable products from readily available starting materials.

papers.title: Strain Anisotropy as a Design Principle for High-Entropy Intermetallic Oxygen Reduction Catalysts
papers.abstract: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a major bottleneck for the efficiency of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. While alloying Pt with 3d transition metals can reduce Pt loading and improve catalytic activity of ORR catalysts, Pt-based solid solutions suffer from reduced activity and stability at Pt fractions below 75-80 at. %. Here, we investigate the role of atomic ordering in multimetallic Pt catalysts by comparing high-entropy solid solutions (HESOSO) and high-entropy intermetallics (HEI) with identical nominal composition, Pt5MnFeCoNiCu. Gas diffusion electrode (GDE) setup measurements at industrially relevant current densities (>1 A cm-2 geo) show that catalysts containing the intermetallic phase outperform solid solution counterparts in both specific and mass activity despite their larger particle sizes. Density functional theory calculations attribute this improvement to anisotropic strain arising from the tetragonal intermetallic lattice, which generates distinct adsorption environments with near-optimal *OH binding energies. These results identify strain anisotropy in ordered multimetallic intermetallics as a promising catalyst design principle for independently tuning adsorption energetics and Pt loading. On-line inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) measurements reveal reduced 3d-metal dissolution in the HEI sample compared to HESOSO sample and binary PtNi reference. Operando X-ray total scattering and pair distribution function analysis further demonstrate that both crystallographic structure and local atomic arrangement are retained during accelerated stress testing, indicating that nanoparticle structural collapse is not the dominant degradation pathway. Instead, the observed activity losses are primarily associated with catalyst-layer degradation and mass transport limitations. Overall, the results identify atomic ordering and strain anisotropy as key parameters for designing low-Pt ORR catalysts with enhanced activity and structural stability under operating conditions.

papers.title: Geometric Locking in B–O–B Bridged Helicenes: Simultaneous Enhancement of Emission Efficiency and Configurational Stability
papers.abstract: Helicene-type emitters are an attractive platform for optoelectronic materials because of their distinctive chiroptical properties arising from their inherent helical chirality and extended aromaticity. We developed novel B–O–B bridged helicene-type complexes to investigate how annulation and substituent variation affect their structures and photophysical properties. The combination of a phenanthroline-based annulated framework and B–OB bridged moiety afforded a rigid yet modular molecular architecture that enables the synthesis of configurationally stable chiral emitters using a concise synthetic route. The six newly synthesized emitters exhibited cyan-to-yellow luminescence modulated by differences in the torsion angle and substituents. Structural analysis, density functional theory calculations, and transient absorption measurements indicated that the rigidified framework suppressed excited-state structural relaxation. Meanwhile, altering the substituents further modulated the emission color and excited-state deactivation pathways. The chiroptical properties of the optically resolved enantiomers, including circular dichroism and circularly polarized luminescence, were fully investigated. Thermal stability experiments of the separated enantiomers combined with computational analysis using an advanced reaction path search method identified a minimum-racemization pathway involving bond cleavage, with a calculated activation free energy of 51.77 kcal mol−1. Our findings provide valuable insights into the molecular design of helicene-type emitters to promote their broader applications ranging from fundamental material science to chiral optoelectronic devices.

papers.title: Divergent Multigram Access to sp3-Rich Spirocyclic Building Blocks via Iodocyclization of β,γ-Unsaturated Carboxylic Acids
papers.abstract: A divergent and scalable approach to three families of spirocyclic sp 3 -rich building blocks was disclosed, based on iodocyclization of common β,γ-unsaturated carboxylic acids bearing a quaternary center. These intermediates were obtained from commercially available ketones through a three-step reaction sequence including Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons olefination, ester reduction with DIBAL, and Johnson-Claisen rearrangement on up to a 100 g scale in a single run without chromatographic purification. The choice of the iodocyclization substrate affected the product type: classical iodolactonization gave γ-lactones, reduction to the alkenol followed by iodoetherification provided tetrahydrofurans, and amidation led to γ-lactams (65–82% yields). O-Cyclizations were promoted by NaHCO3 in THF–H2O, which worked for both substrate types but resulted in different reaction rates, whereas less nucleophilic amides required activation via N,O-bis(silylation). Further modification at the iodomethyl group provided a series of building blocks including primary amines and sulfonyl chlorides; in the lactone series, recyclization to spirocyclic 5-hydroxypiperidin-2-ones was also achieved.

papers.title: Coupled Electronic and Structural Regulation Enables Stable Lattice-Oxygen Evolution in Hexagonal YMnO3
papers.abstract: The lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) frees oxygen evolution catalysts from the scaling relations that limit the conventional adsorbate pathway, but the same oxygen redox chemistry also degrades the host lattice, so stable LOM operation has largely been restricted to structurally flexible materials. Here we show that a single substituent, Cr3+, equips the rigid hexagonal oxide YMnO3 with both the electronic and structural prerequisites for stable lattice-oxygen-mediated oxygen evolution. Density functional theory reveals that Cr upshifts the O 2p band center by 0.50 eV toward the Fermi level and weakens Mn–O bonding, activating oxygen redox; X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows that the vacancy concentration concurrently falls to a moderate level, stabilizing the lattice; and 18O isotope-labeling TOF-SIMS depth profiling shows that the enhanced oxygen exchange remains confined to the near-surface region, leaving the rigid hexagonal framework intact during turnover. Cr-substituted YMnO3 delivers an overpotential of 248 mV at 10 mA cm-2 (336 mV for pristine YMnO3), a Tafel slope of 103 mV dec-1, a 16-fold increase in mass activity, and stable operation over 16 h of multistep cycling in 1.0 M KOH. Coupling electronic activation with structural regulation through a single dopant thus extends stable lattice-oxygen catalysis to rigid oxides.

papers.title: The Ethanol Illusion: Hidden Peroxides as a Source of Radical Artifacts
papers.abstract: Ethanol is widely used as a solvent, cleaning agent, and sacrificial hole scavenger. Traditionally, researchers rarely question influence of its purity on the reactions under investigation.However, we demonstrate that even commercial analytical-grade ethanol inherently harbors trace peroxide impurities—ranging from submicromolar to hundreds of micromolar levels. Orthogonal peroxide assays, together with catalase treatment, indicate that these impurities are mainly composed of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) and organic hydroperoxides (ROOH). These solvent-borne peroxides are not chemically silent: they can become enriched during ethanol evaporation, generate radical adducts upon mild heating, water dilution, or Fe 2+ addition, and produce electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) signals that may be mistaken for radicals generated by the target reaction. These hidden peroxides act as an unrecognized source of reactive oxygen species (ROS), with the radical distribution shifting from alkoxyl (·OR) and alkyl (·R) toward hydroxyl radicals (·OH) dominated chemistry as water increases. Such artifacts systematically mislead the interpretation of reaction pathways in radical-mediated systems. These peroxide-derived species also accelerate dopamine oxidation and polymerization, and surface residues left after ethanol cleaning generate fluorescence artifacts. These results establish that commercial ethanol hidden peroxide impurities can redirect oxidative pathways and bias mechanistic assignments across solution and surface experiments.

papers.title: Spin–orbit-coupling-guided state selection for complete active space second-order perturbation theory calculations of Eu3+ energy levels
papers.abstract: The accurate and efficient ab initio computation of energy levels of lanthanide ions like Eu3+ is very challenging due to strong electronic correlation and spin–orbit coupling effects. We present an in-depth investigation of how com-plete active space second-order perturbation the-ory (CASPT2) and spin–orbit restricted state interaction (SO-RASSI) calculations might be carried out to obtain a favorable balance between computational efficiency and the accuracy of the obtained energy levels. First, we benchmark the effect of the basis set, shifting techniques, the frozen core approximation, and different multi-state treatments. We find that a state-averaged Fock operator is necessary to obtain reasonably degenerate terms and that ap-proximations in basis set and correlation treat-ment might be reasonable only for the low-lying much better accuracy–cost trade-offs than hand-picking states. The scheme is designed to be generally applicable to other systems, including atoms and ions as well as molecular and materials applications. Third, we analyzed the individual CASPT2 correlation energy contributions between all orbital shells, to identify which orbital shells are most relevant for an accurate description of correlation. Here, we find that the 4d shell is of highest relevance; it’s inclusion in the active space significantly improves the balanced description of correlation energy of states of different multiplicity and angular momentum.

papers.title: Current Progress on Semi-Supervised Learning for Data-Limited Chemistry and Material Discovery
papers.abstract: Machine Learning (ML) has become one of the most important tools in science and industry, yet chemistry and materials science have not benefited from it to the same extent as many other fields, because ML models depend on clean, large labeled datasets that are inherently difficult to obtain in these domains. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising route, by leveraging small labeled sets alongside abundant unlabeled data, but the central question is not which SSL method to use; it is when unlabeled data can be trusted. Unlabeled data can just as easily hurt a model as help it when pseudo-labels are wrong or the data shifts, and this risk is not uniform. Reviewing work across molecular property prediction, synthesis, text mining, diffraction, microscopy, and materials screening, we find a consistent divide: SSL is reliably effective in classification and segmentation tasks where errors are bounded but remains structurally fragile in the continuous regression problems (yields, lifetimes, molecular activity) that dominate this field, where a single bad pseudo-label can propagate unchecked. We use this divide as a diagnostic lens throughout the review, and close by outlining what reliable SSL requires (uncertainty pseudo-labeling, principled evaluation, and a minimum reporting standard) and where the open challenges lie.

papers.title: Single and Multiexciton Dynamics in Porphyrin Nanorings
papers.abstract: Exciton transport in molecular assemblies is typically studied in linear chains and polydisperse aggregates, where chain ends perturb the electronic structure and structural inhomogeneity can obscure size-dependent trends. Molecular nanorings overcome both limitations: they are end-group-free macrocycles with well-defined sizes, while their dimensions can be synthetically tuned from a few to several tens of porphyrin units. Here, we use intensity-cycled femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy to disentangle single- and multiexciton dynamics in a series of fully conjugated molecular nanorings containing 6–40 Zn-porphyrin units. By isolating the third-, fifth-, and seventh-order nonlinear responses, we independently track single-, two-, and three-exciton dynamics, enabling the ring-size dependence of exciton–exciton annihilation (EEA) to be determined without relying on a priori kinetic assumptions. The EEA rate decreases systematically with increasing ring size, accompanied by a crossover from annihilation-limited to diffusion-limited EEA between 20 and 30 porphyrin units. The smallest nanoring exhibits no resolvable multiexciton dynamics, consistent with exciton delocalisation across the entire ring, whereas larger rings exhibit increasingly diffusive exciton motion as static disorder limits delocalisation. The retrieved exciton diffusion coefficients are approximately three times higher than those we previously reported, indicating that the assumptions inherent to conventional intensity-dependent fitting can substantially underestimate exciton mobility.

papers.title: Virtual screening of approved drugs nominates tofogliflozin for the SHP2 allosteric pocket
papers.abstract: SHP2 supports oncogenic RAS–MAPK signaling, and ligands in its regulatory allosteric pocket can stabilize the autoinhibited state. Approved drugs were screened for an accessible probe of this pocket. A combined ranking of docking scores and interaction fidelity to the crystallographic SHP099 contact pattern prioritized compounds for simulation. In a matched benchmark of target-level SHP2 actives and property-matched decoys, the ranking achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.892 and 21.42-fold enrichment in the top 2% of the list. Short molecular dynamics simulations and comparative MM/GBSA narrowed the candidates, and successive 100 ns simulations reduced them to tofogliflozin. Across three independently seeded trajectories, mean ligand center-of-mass drift was 1.407–2.091 Å. Reference-matched hydrophobic contacts occurred in 97.3–100.0% of frames, and hydrogen bonds matching the reference pattern occurred in 34.0–86.2%. Three absolute binding free-energy protocol repeats from one shared coordinate model gave ∆G = −10.33 kcal mol −1 with a reported uncertainty of 0.53 kcal mol −1 , supporting numerical repeatability within that model. Experimental measurements of binding and pocket dependence, followed by SHP2 activity assays, are needed to confirm the proposed interaction and determine whether it produces inhibition.

papers.title: Why Diamondoid Nanodiamond Precursors Lose Their Defect Blueprint under HPHT Conditions: A Graphitic Conversion Pathway
papers.abstract: Nanodiamonds hosting nitrogen-vacancy centres have emerged as promising quantum sensors, motivating bottom-up strategies that encode particle size and defect architecture through molecular precursor design. Nitrogen-substituted diamondoids have been proposed as atomically defined seeds for nanodiamond growth under high-pressure, high-temperature conditions, but the transformation pathway and its impact on defect formation remain unclear. Here we investigate adamantane and five nitrogen-substituted derivatives as molecular nanodiamond precursors. We show that precursor chemistry controls nucleation density, growth kinetics and nitrogen retention, producing nanodiamonds from a few to several hundred nanometres and substitutional nitrogen concentrations up to ~450 ppm, yet only scarce nitrogen-vacancy centres. Using 2-adamantanamine as a model precursor, in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction reveals a graphitic intermediate before diamond formation. This reconstructive pathway erases the molecular defect blueprint during carbon-skeleton rearrangement, precluding the direct inheritance of atomically encoded nitrogen-vacancy configurations and defining a mechanistic limit for bottom-up colour-centre engineering.

papers.title: σ-hat: A physics-informed model for accurate prediction of halogen, chalcogen, pnictogen and tetrel bond energies
papers.abstract: Directional and tuneable σ-hole interactions, encompassing halogen, chalcogen, pnictogen and tetrel bonds, drive supramolecular assembly and materials design. Although computational chemistry is essential for exploring and rationalising these processes, high-level coupled-cluster calculations are computationally prohibitive for large-scale screening. Conversely, standard density functional theory (DFT) struggles to compute accurate interaction energies for heavy main-group elements in complex, multivalent environments. Here, we introduce the σ-hole approximation tool (σ-hat), a lightweight, physics-informed machine learning model that predicts high-level interaction energies near-instantaneously from low-cost geometric and atomic properties. On the SHEF1552 dataset, σ-hat outperforms the widely used M06-2X-D3(0) density functional, achieving an overall RMSE of 0.85 kcal mol−1 and hence meeting the benchmark of “chemical accuracy”. The model also excels in modelling the pnictogen and tetrel bonds where DFT errors are most pronounced. Further validation on the SH250×10 dataset demonstrates robust transferability (MAE = 0.80 kcal mol−1) and a capacity for extrapolation to non-equilibrium geometries. The speed and accuracy of σ-hat enable high-throughput screening of pairwise motifs and supramolecular synthons across large structural databases, unlocking new computational pathways as a platform for materials and catalyst discovery.

papers.title: Catalytic S-to-CC Transmutation of Benzothiazoles into Quinolines
papers.abstract: Skeletal editing enables the remodeling of intact rings one atom at a time. Still, it has primarily been applied to refine individual complex targets rather than to diversify structures from a common precursor. Catalytic approaches for editing fused sulfur heteroarenes remain limited, and general methods for sulfur excision coupled with ring expansion in a single operation are lacking. This study presents a nickel-catalyzed method that transforms benzothiazoles directly into polysubstituted quinolines via a one-step, sulfur-extruding, ring-expanding transmutation with an external alkyne. Mechanistic investigations indicate a pathway involving oxidative cyclization to an aza-nickelacycle, followed by β-sulfide elimination and sulfur extrusion. A single, readily available benzothiazole can serve as a branching hub for assembling structurally diverse quinolines by varying the alkyne, establishing a modular platform for scaffold diversification.

papers.title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Enantio- and Diastereoselective Synthesis of Indane-Fused Succinimides through Multiple Chiral Induction: Access to Central and Axial Chirality
papers.abstract: The enantio- and diastereoselective construction of molecular architectures bearing multiple chiral elements remains a formidable challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Herein, we report a cobalt/salox-catalyzed enantio- and diastereoselective [3+2] annulation of aryl hydrazones with maleimides, for the rapid assembly of chiral indane-fused succinimide frameworks through sequential C–C bond formation. The protocol exhibits broad substrate scope, providing the corresponding annulation products as single diastereomers in yields of up to 99% with enantiomeric ratios of up to >99:1. Furthermore, the methodology enables the simultaneous construction of axial and central chirality through the use of ortho-substituted N-aryl maleimides, affording a single enantiomer bearing one C–N chiral axis and three chiral centers, out of 16 stereoisomers. The practicality of the transformation is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis, late-stage diversification of biologically relevant molecules, and postsynthetic derivatizations. Mechanistic insights from control experiments provided compelling support for a plausible catalytic pathway for the current transformation.

papers.title: ROSE: a Foundation Model for Reusable One-dimensional Spectrum Embeddings in 1H NMR
papers.abstract: Most deep learning models for 1H NMR are trained for a single endpoint and do not provide representations that can be reused across analytical tasks. We introduce ROSE (Reusable One-dimensional Spectrum Embeddings), a 7.8-million-parameter spectrum-side foundation model pretrained on 3.2 million experimental and simulated spectra using an InChIKey-14 identity holdout that excludes all molecules appearing in the external benchmark test sets. Its shared spectral encoder supports denoising, peak detection, classification, cross-field alignment, molecular retrieval and structure-tospectrum prediction. Beyond internal evaluation on identity-disjoint holdouts, ROSE was assessed on external benchmarks excluded from pretraining, matching the published QIB PLS-DA result for 60-MHz edible-oil classification (98.8% balanced accuracy vs 98.9% accuracy), reducing NMRNet structure-to-spectrum Chamfer loss by 39% over Morgan+Ridge (0.79 vs 1.29), achieving 69% peak-detection F1 on NMRformer, and, after short domain adaptation, reaching 37.1% Top-1 and 67.7% Top-10 retrieval on NMR-Solver. ROSE represents a first step toward a general-purpose NMR foundation model for scalable industrial analytical applications.

papers.title: Ethylene to Medium-Chain Linear Alpha Olefins: Alkali Cation Modulation of Nickel Oligomerization Selectivity
papers.abstract: To enable high-yield production of medium-chain linear alpha olefins (LAOs) from ethylene, we developed a cation-based strategy that allows modulation of metal-catalyzed ethylene oligomerization beyond the classical Schulz-Flory distribution. After screening a series of metal catalysts (Ni1–Ni8), nickel phosphine‑sulfonate (Ni8) emerged as the most promising system, enabling external alkali ion coordination and producing primarily LAOs over branched and internal olefins. Activation of Ni8 with Ni(COD)2 (COD = 1,5-cyclooctadiene) under a continuous ethylene feed afforded 50 wt% C8–C14 products (82% 1-Cn), along with 6 wt% polyethylene. In contrast, treatment of Ni8 with Li+ salt and 15-crown-5 prior to being subjected to the standard reaction conditions increased C8–C14 selectivity to 82 wt% and LAO purity to 90%, with negligible polymer formation. Using B(C6F5)3 instead of Li+/15-crown-5 also enhanced LAO purity (90%) but the fractional weight of C8–C14 (41 wt%) was reduced relative to that in the Ni8 only reaction. Density functional theory calculations of Ni8, both alone and in the presence of either [Li(15-crown-5)]+ (Ni8-Li15C5) or B(C6F5)3 (Ni8-BAr3), reveal that coordination of a Lewis acid has minimal impact on the nickel–ligand bond lengths and the atomic charge at nickel. However, Ni8-Li15C5 exhibits a predominantly positive surface in its molecular electrostatic potential map, a feature not observed in Ni8 or Ni8-BAr3. This work establishes that cation tuning is an operationally simple and effective means of controlling ethylene oligomerization selectivity, enabling access to medium-chain LAOs with significantly greater efficiency than is achievable using conventional wide-range processes.

papers.title: Activity-Guided Identification of Pro-Inflammatory Neutrophils with Dual Enzyme and Metabolite-Activatable Fluorescent Probes
papers.abstract: Neutrophils are the most abundant circulating leukocytes in the innate immune system. Primary neutrophils comprise multiple distinct subtypes that regulate antimicrobial defense and inflammatory diseases. Current fluorescent probes for imaging neutrophils cannot distinguish between activation mechanisms. In this work, we present dual enzyme and metabolite-activatable fluorogenic probes that are selective for activated neutrophils prone to inflammatory responses. Our probes integrate, within a single scaffold, two neutrophil-associated activation mechanisms, that is, cathepsin G-mediated cleavage of FRET substrates and fluorophore oxidation by hypochlorous acid. This chemical design allows the selective identification of pro-inflammatory activated neutrophils over other immune cells from peripheral blood of human donors. This strategy provides a unique approach for in situ analysis of neutrophil heterogeneity in multiple pathologies, including different inflammatory diseases.

papers.title: Transforming the Greenhouse Gas Fluoroform into a Bench-Stable Reagent for Trifluoromethylation Using an Aluminum-Based Metal-Organic Framework
papers.abstract: Fluorochemicals are central to the modern medicinal, agrochemical, and polymer industries, yet the sustainability of fluorochemical synthesis is challenged by an over-reliance on non-renewable fluorine sources such as fluorospar (CaF2). Recycling fluorinated waste represents a promising solution to this challenge, but to date there are limited platforms that enable both the capture of fluorinated waste products and their subsequent conversion into value-added products. Herein, we demonstrate that the robust and inexpensive Al-based metal-organic framework (MOF) MIL-160 (MIL = Matériaux de l′Institut Lavoisier) enables the capture of the waste greenhouse gas fluoroform (CHF3), a byproduct of semiconductor and fluoropolymer manufacturing, from mixtures of other fluorinated gases and from dilute emission streams. MIL-160 exhibits record-setting adsorption of CHF3 at low pressures (3.88 mmol g−1 at 0.1 bar and 298 K) and selectivity over N2 (10:90 CHF3/N2 IAST selectivity of S = 1504) owing to its unique crown ether-like binding pocket for CHF3. CHF3-loaded MIL-160 can be stored long-term and employed directly in a range of nucleophilic and metal-mediated trifluoromethylation reactions. Thus, our findings establish the first integrated strategy for the separation, storage, and utilization of CHF3, providing a pathway for transforming an environmentally problematic waste gas into a synthetically valuable reagent.

papers.title: Anisotropic Nanochitin Hydrogels Promoting Guided Cellular Growth for Bone Defect Repair
papers.abstract: Developing biomimetic scaffolds that replicate the complex anisotropic structure of natural bone remains a persistent challenge in tissue engineering. Here we report an anisotropic hydrogel based on chitin nanofibrils, engineered through a combination of unidirectional freezing and amine-phosphate crosslinking. These hydrogels feature highly ordered, macroscale pore channels where the individual fibrillar building blocks are co-aligned along the freezing front, exhibiting a hierarchical structure with alignment from nanoscale to macroscale. The hydrogels showcase remarkable mechanical properties in aqueous environments exhibiting nonlinear strain-stiffening, exceptional fatigue resistance enabled by dynamic realignment of their oriented pore walls under compression load. The anisotropic matrix environment directed the growth of MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblast cultures. The in vitro cell adhesion and growth experiments performed on 2D substrate quantitively revealed a crosslinker dependent cell attachment and viability. Together, these findings establish an anisotropic hydrogel platform that combines mechanical robustness, efficient mass transport and cellular growth, offering potential for applications in tissue repair and regenerative medicine where structurally guided biomaterials are desirable.

papers.title: A modular and low-cost self-driving lab platform for battery electrolyte optimization
papers.abstract: Electrolytes critically influence the performance, safety, and operational window of zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs). Here, we report a modular, low-cost (EUR4,000) self-driving laboratory (SDL) platform designed for the autonomous, high-throughput screening and optimization of multi-component aqueous zinc electrolytes (ZnSO 4 , ethylene glycol, DMSO, and H 2 O). Integrated with Atinary’s cloud-based SDLabs™ platform and driven by its Falcon Bayesian Optimization (BO) algorithm, the closed-loop workflow navigates a high-dimensional design space without manual intervention. The system targets multi-objectives simultaneously: maximizing ionic conductivity across subzero to elevated temperatures (−20 ◦ C to 40 ◦ C) while maximizing the room-temperature electrochemical stability window (ESW). Within 48 autonomous iterations, the platform revealed fundamental design trade-offs: DMSO expands the ESW at the expense of ionic conductivity, whereas ZnSO 4 drives ion transport while narrowing the stability window. Operating under complete software-hardware orchestration, this accessible platform demonstrates how SDL enables rapid, reproducible discovery of advanced energy materials.

papers.title: Binding mechanism of the DOPA-deficient mussel foot protein dbfp7 on rutile TiO2(110): an all-atom molecular dynamics study.
papers.abstract: Protein adhesion to titanium dioxide surface underlies both biological implants and mussel based wet adhesives and is commonly attributed to the post translationally modified catechol bearing wild amino acid 2,3-dihydroxyphenylalanine. However, how the DOPA deficient protein dbfp7 adheres to the surface remains unclear. Using all atom molecular dynamics and umbrella sampling, we studied the mussel foot protein dbfp7, both short sequence-motif peptides and the intact N-terminal fragment across multiple conformers and orientations using rutile titanium oxide surface (110). Individual residues bind only weakly (at or below thermal energy) to the surface and binding did not strengthen with peptide length. Nonetheless, the intact protein fragment adheres irreversibly to the surface, engaging with multiple different interfaces rather than a single binding site. Aromatic residues were enriched at the interface when exposed to the surface but were not required, as an aromatic-poor face also binds equally well. These findings suggest that dbfp7 adheres to the surface through the collective action of many weak, non-specific contacts, providing a mechanism for robust adhesion in the absence of catechol chemistry.

papers.title: Versatile Bimolecular Mechanochemistry via Heterobicyclic Mechanophores
papers.abstract: Mechanophores utilizes mechanical force for productive chemical transformations, yet the mechanochemical reactions accessible from a single mechanophore adheres largely to the unimolecular scheme. Here, we report a heterobicyclic design of mechanophores that enables efficient bimolecular mechanochemistry via a persistent force-generated intermediate. The 5oxabicyclo[2.1.0]pentane (oBCP) scaffold exhibits high mechanical reactivity and undergoes efficient formal [3+2] cycloaddition reactions with added small-molecule reagents. Mechanistic studies reveal that the bimolecular reaction proceeds via a force-generated carbonyl ylide with significant diradical character. The persistence of the ylide intermediate is manifested by its ability to crosslink polymer chains with either intrachain or interchain dimerization. The effective generation of the long-lived intermediate accommodates installation of a diverse range of functional motifs into polymer backbones, opening doors to facile mechanochemical tuning of polymer properties and architectures.

papers.title: An in-situ Electrophotochemical Generated Hydrogen-Bonded Complex drives the Catalytic Activation of Carbon-Halogen Bonds
papers.abstract: We find that under electrophotochemical conditions, the radical anion of 9,10-dicyanoanthracene (DCA•‾) – a widely used organic electrophotocatalyt - undergoes a cascade of transformations leading to an unconventional dimeric intermediate that acts as the effective photocatalyst in the reaction. Using operando UV-Vis spectroelectrochemistry, we track the real-time evolution of DCA through its radical anion to the formation of 9,10-anthraquinone, which then evolves toward the catalytically active hydrogen-bonded dimeric complex in presence of water and oxygen traces. Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations not only support the occurrence of the dimeric structure and predict its facile photoexcited reactivity within the synthetic framework. This work also demonstrates how the presence of residual moisture in commonly employed solvents is sufficient to drastically impact on the behaviors of electrophotocatalytic processes.

papers.title: Halide Exchange via Perovskite Nanocrystals for Interfacial Defect Passivation in Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Metal halide perovskites have emerged as leading candidates for next-generation optoelectronics, with perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieving power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) exceeding 26%. However, solution-processed hybrid perovskite films typically suffer from non-radiative recombination and ion migration driven by surface and interfacial defects, limiting device performance, fill factor, and long-term stability. To address these bottlenecks, we report a novel, scalable interface engineering strategy utilizing bromide-rich perovskite nanocrystals to modify 3D perovskite film surfaces via self-driven solid-state halide exchange.
