The resulting surface-graded heterojunction passivates key iodide vacancies, suppresses ion migration, and optimizes charge extraction. Consequently, modified PSCs demonstrate a ~5% boost in short-circuit current density () and an improved fill factor of 75.3%, driving a ~10% relative increase in PCE from 20.13% (control) to 22.19%. This simple, single-step nanocrystal treatment provides a promising pathway toward robust, scalable, and high-efficiency optoelectronic architectures.

papers.title: Graph-Theoretical Analysis of Electrochemical Swelling in Conducting Polymers
papers.abstract: Understanding how electrochemical swelling reorganizes the morphology of conducting polymers is one of the central challenges in organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors because this process ultimately governs charge transport and device performance. Although molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed structural information, they do not directly quantify how swelling modifies the connectivity and topology of transport networks. Graph theory offers a natural framework for this purpose, yet a fundamental methodological question has remained unanswered: how should polymer morphology be represented as a graph so that graph-theoretical (GT) descriptors faithfully capture the underlying physics? Here, we address this question by performing a systematic GT analysis of an n-type conducting polymer poly(benzimidazobenzophenanthroline) (BBL) during electrochemical reduction. Physics-informed graphs are constructed from atomistic MD simulations at four levels of coarse-graining: atoms, aromatic rings, naphthalenic transport units (A-site), and entire polymer chains. The resulting graphs are analyzed using six representative GT metrics comprising three local (Average Degree, Degree Assortativity, Average Clustering Coefficient) and three global (Average Closeness Centrality, Average Betweenness Centrality, and Global Efficiency) descriptors. We show that electrochemical swelling transforms BBL from a compact transport network into a swollen porous heterogeneous gel with reduced long-range connectivity and increasingly important transport bottlenecks. More importantly, we demonstrate that the same GT metrics can describe fundamentally different structural features depending on the level of coarse-graining. The atomistic, ring, and A-site representations respectively probe swelling and pore formation, π–π contact organization, and mesoscale aromatic linkages. These findings establish graph theory as a powerful complement to conventional MD analysis and provide a general methodological framework for interpreting transport-relevant morphology in conducting polymers and other disordered soft materials.

papers.title: DNA Directed Chemistry: Scalable Programmed DNA-Encoded Library Synthesis for More Chemically Diverse and Drug-Like Libraries
papers.abstract: DNA-Encoded Libraries (DELs) are indispensable high-throughput platforms in drug discovery, but the widely adopted split-and-pool synthesis method is fundamentally limited: the DNA merely records, rather than directs, the steps of chemistry. This lack of programmatic control imposes mandatory downstream chemistry congruency, restricts structural diversity, and inevitably generates a combinatorial explosion of un-drug-like molecules, hindering both hit-finding and the acquisition of structurally informative data required for machine learning (ML) models. To resolve these core constraints, we developed Programmed DEL Synthesis (PDS), a robust, industrially applicable platform for non-combinatorial DEL construction in which the DNA actively directs the synthesis. PDS is built upon a sort-and-pool mechanism expanded by three key innovations: sequence-specific installation of first building blocks using charged carrier codons, a multinomial encoding strategy that enables libraries exceeding 20 billion unique encodings in three chemical steps, and non-combinatorial germline assembly that allows for the programmatic omission of undesirable building block combinations. We demonstrate the platform with Library i01, a three-step, threepathway library employing 137 trifunctional scaffolds. The design successfully programmed the systematic merging and un-merging of three mutually incompatible reaction pathways: Acid→Aldehyde→Amine, Amine→Aldehyde→Acid, and Aldehyde→Acid→Amine within a single synthesis. Pilot affinity selections against Carbonic Anhydrase (BCA-II) validated the high fidelity of DNA encoding and efficient building block installation across all steps and pathways, confirming the platform's robust utility for selection. PDS transforms chemical congruency and drug-likeness into programmable properties, offering a precise, efficient solution that improves library quality without sacrificing chemical space. Crucially, PDS enables the construction of structurally tailored 2nd Generation DELs needed to provide the high-resolution data required for productive ML-driven active learning cycles, establishing a critical operational link for modern drug development.

papers.title: AERIS: an Autonomous Extensional Rheology Imaging-based System for rapid, high throughput characterization of soft materials
papers.abstract: Rheological characterization provides key performance metrics for hydrogel formulations and pre-formulations. However, it remains a bottleneck in formulation optimization due to the long measurement times and limited throughput of conventional rheometers. When combined with a large formulation design space, identifying compositions with targeted rheological properties becomes laborious and time-intensive, thereby substantially increasing time to market. Here, we present AERIS, an Autonomous Extensional Rheology Imaging System designed to accelerate formulation screening through high-throughput, automated rheological characterization. AERIS is built on an Opentrons OT-2 liquid-handling platform integrated with a high-speed camera, enabling fully automated sample handling, data acquisition, and analysis using capillary breakup extensional rheometry (CaBER) methodologies. We demonstrate the development of AERIS and its application to both Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluids, as well as viscoelastic Mg(II)–hyaluronic acid (HA) hydrogels, illustrating its ability to capture extensional rheological behavior across a range of material classes. This platform achieves a throughput of up to ten samples per hour autonomously, representing a substantial improvement over conventional approaches. Overall, AERIS enables rapid, reproducible, and scalable rheological screening, providing a powerful tool for accelerating formulation development and enabling data-driven optimization of complex soft materials.

papers.title: Expediting chemoenzymatic access to bacterial ‘sialic acid-like’ sugars via mapping of wild type sialic acid aldolase enzyme substrate tolerance and promiscuity
papers.abstract: Bacterial ‘sialic-acid-like’ sugars, including legionaminic acid and pseudaminic acids, are critical for the virulence and immune evasion of numerous human pathogens, including pandrug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii and global gut pathogens Campylobacter jejuni and Helicobacter pylori. Despite this importance, a detailed understanding of the role these sugars play in pathogenesis is hampered by the challenging synthesis of their 9-deoxy nonulosonic acid backbones. Herein we expedite access to these complex glyco-architectures through exploration of the biocatalytic potential of sialic acid aldolase enzymes (also known as N-acetyl neuraminate lyases). By mapping the substrate tolerance and promiscuity of a library of wildtype aldolases, we identified the enzyme from Corynebacterium glutamicum (Cg) as a highly effective biocatalyst for the synthesis of 9-deoxy ‘sialic acid-like’ sugars, particularly Leg5Ac7Ac. Notably, the Cg aldolase synthetically outperformed established orthologs and highlighting its utility for preparative scale syntheses. Furthermore, we demonstrate that stereochemical limitations in these transformations can be bypassed through the use of N-acetyl to azide substitution, enabling chemoenzymatic access to pseudaminic acid architectures with potential for late stage N-diversification. In summary establishing a powerful, regioselective tool for the efficient production of complex bacterial carbohydrates and deeper exploration into their glycobiology.

papers.title: Stacked-Ring Aromaticity Rewires Quantum Interference and Through-Space Transport
papers.abstract: Stacking antiaromatic rings does more than switch aromaticity: it rewires how electrons interfere and flow through space. Here, we show that stacked-ring aromaticity (SRA), generated by cofacial coupling of 4nπ antiaromatic molecules, transforms their quantumtransport landscape. Vertical compression converts paratropic monomers into cylindrically delocalized aromatic dimers with continuous interlayer current-density flux and strong through-space electronic coupling. Remarkably, this antiaromatic-to-SRA transition systematically inverts the preferred electrode connectivity: the anchoring topology that favors transport in the monomer becomes the less efficient interlayer pathway in the dimeric configuration, while the alternative connectivity becomes dominant. This behavior arises from the reorganization of destructive quantum-interference features through interlayer orbital coupling. The effect is maximized near d = 2.70 Å, where magnetic reversal, energetic stabilization, and high interlayer transmission converge. Interestingly, the odd-layered stacking remains globally antiaromatic yet preserves efficient transport across the full three-layer stack, showing that the stacking-induced transport network survives the even-odd magnetic reversal. SRA therefore provides a mechanically accessible strategy for reshaping quantum interference and through-space conductance in molecular junctions.

papers.title: Beyond the Magic Methyl Effect: Activity Cliff Asymmetry of Functional Group Substitution in Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Activity cliffs occur in drug discovery programmes when a small structural change leads to a very large change in biological activity. We have used a matched molecular pair approach for common functional groups to establish examples of activity cliffs. We then measure how positive and negative activity cliffs are over-represented relative to a normal distribution. The ‘Magic Methyl Effect’ highlighted examples of where methylation led to significant activity increases, yet our data suggests that negative activity cliffs are more common than positive ones for methyl, and that significant increases are less common than most other functional groups. We show that both scaffold and substitution position effects play an important role in the occurrence of activity cliffs.

papers.title: Valorization of Waste Biomass for Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) Production: A Comprehensive Review of Feedstocks, Microbial Biosynthesis Pathways, Recovery Strategies, and Integrated Biorefinery Approaches
papers.abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are microbially synthesized, fully biodegradable polyesters and are among the few commercial bioplastics certified for biodegradation in marine, freshwater, and soil environments without industrial composting infrastructure, positioning them as a credible structural alternative to petroleum-derived plastics. Despite this favorable materials profile, PHA commercialization remains constrained primarily by production economics, with substrate cost and energy-intensive downstream processing (DSP) together accounting for the majority of production expense. This review provides a critical, quantitatively grounded synthesis of the literature on waste-biomass valorization for PHA biosynthesis, integrating four interconnected layers of the production chain. First, it evaluates four waste feedstock categories — food-waste-derived volatile fatty acids (VFAs), agricultural and lignocellulosic residues, wastewater- and microalgae-derived streams, and industrial by-products (cheese whey, crude glycerol, palm oil mill effluent) — with reported PHA titers and cell dry weight (CDW) contents compared across systems. Second, it details the molecular and enzymatic basis of PHA biosynthesis via the phaCAB and phaC1ZC2 operons and synthesizes recent metabolic and protein-engineering strategies in Cupriavidus necator and Pseudomonas putida that expand the substrate range and enable rational control of copolymer composition. Third, it compares pure- and mixed-culture production strategies, lignocellulosic pretreatment technologies, and downstream recovery methods — including green-solvent, surfactant-assisted, hydrodynamic cavitation, aqueous two-phase, and supercritical CO2 extraction routes — on a comparative basis of recovery yield, purity, and molecular weight retention. Fourth, it examines integrated multi-product biorefinery configurations that co-generate biohydrogen, biomethane, and biochar alongside PHA, and situates these within current techno-economic assessment (TEA) findings and the 2024–2026 commercial and regulatory landscape. The review closes by identifying the field's principal technical, economic, and regulatory barriers — substrate heterogeneity, DSP cost dominance, scale-up risk, genetic instability of engineered strains, and fragmented biodegradability certification — and proposes a prioritized research agenda centered on integrated biorefinery design, green DSP intensification, and standardized techno-economic benchmarking.

papers.title: Machine learning and carbon break-even assessment of CO₂-assisted thermochemical conversion of plastic waste
papers.abstract: CO₂-assisted thermochemical conversion offers a promising opportunity to couple plastic-waste valorisation with CO₂ utilisation in the context of low-carbon and net-zero development. Here, publication-grouped machine learning was applied to a harmonised literature dataset to evaluate transferable product-yield patterns and the predictive contribution of CO₂ concentration across independent studies. CO₂ provided detectable but context-dependent predictive information, while reaction temperature remained the most consistently influential descriptor. A screening-level carbon break-even analysis was further used to assess whether reported CO₂ consumption could offset the additional heating emissions associated with the higher temperatures used for CO₂-assisted conversion relative to conventional inert-atmosphere pyrolysis. Across the selected thermal and energy-supply scenarios, most condition–parameter combinations met the break-even criterion, while an increasing fraction failed to offset the additional heating emissions as energy carbon intensity increased. The framework integrates literature-derived machine learning with carbon assessment to evaluate both the predictive and carbon relevance of CO₂-assisted plastic conversion.

papers.title: Feature-disentangled prior transfer for small-sample chirality prediction in carbon nanotube synthesis
papers.abstract: Achieving chirality-selective synthesis of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) remains a central challenge for carbon-based electronics because chirality-labelled datasets are scarce and highly imbalanced, limiting both statistical inference and data-driven optimization. Here we show that transferable growth physics can be extracted from heterogeneous carbon nanotube synthesis systems and leveraged to predict chirality under extreme data scarcity. We construct a physics-guided transfer-learning framework that aligns large-scale growth datasets with a 35-sample chirality dataset through cross-system feature disentanglement and knowledge-guided regularization. The learned representation substantially reduces distributional discrepancies between synthesis systems and enables accurate chirality prediction, achieving 88.6% accuracy under strict leave-one-out cross-validation. Feature-attribution analyses further reveal a hierarchical Base–Advanced descriptor framework. Base descriptors, including H/C ratio, temperature and carbon supply, define the global growth window, whereas Advanced descriptors associated with catalyst and support properties govern chirality-selection boundaries. These results suggest that diverse carbon nanotube synthesis routes share an underlying growth manifold and demonstrate how transferable physical representations can bridge small-data prediction and mechanistic understanding. More broadly, this framework provides a strategy for interpretable materials discovery in data-limited systems.

papers.title: Polyethylene conversion to mevalonate via catalyst-free autoxidation and bioconversion
papers.abstract: Hybrid chemical and biological processes are promising strategies to valorize recalcitrant plastic waste streams by generating soluble oxygenates that can be biologically converted into a single product. Here, we show that acetic acid-mediated autoxidation in the absence of metal catalysts can deconstruct high-density polyethylene (HDPE) to soluble oxygenates at 80 C-mol% carbon yield. These yields are a major improvement over metal-catalyzed autoxidation, and the chemistry readily translates to post-consumer substrates. Multiple analytical approaches enabled identification of major product classes, including dicarboxylic acids (DCAs), 2-oxocarboxylic acids (ketoacids), and -lactone acids. An industrially relevant bacterium, Pseudomonas putida, was engineered to efficiently utilize ketoacids via a unique β-oxidation pathway discovered via barcoded transposon insertion libraries and transcriptomics. P. putida was then engineered to convert HDPE-derived DCAs and ketoacids into mevalonate, an exemplary high-value chemical. Overall, this study demonstrates a carbon-efficient, catalyst-free process for solubilizing HDPE to mixed oxygenates and highlights the need to improve the bioavailability of polyolefin-derived intermediates from oxidation.

papers.title: Towards Reactive Electrochemical Transport Using the Lattice Boltzmann Method. Part I: Electrostatics, Hydrodynamics, Species Transport, and Electrokinetic Benchmarking
papers.abstract: This work presents the first stage in the development of a lattice Boltzmann framework for reactive electrochemical transport. The present study focuses on the verification and validation of electrostatics, hydrodynamics, ionic species transport, and coupled electrokinetic phenomena using analytical benchmark solutions. A modular lattice Boltzmann framework is developed in Fortran, in which independent distribution functions are employed to solve the Poisson equation, Navier–Stokes equations, and Nernst–Planck equations within a unified computational framework. The numerical solutions are systematically compared with the corresponding analytical solutions, demonstrating excellent agreement for the electrostatic potential, electro-osmotic velocity, ionic concentration profiles, and the fully coupled electrokinetic system. The benchmark presented in this work establishes a robust and extensible numerical foundation for future developments toward reactive electrochemical transport and multiscale electrocatalytic simulations.

papers.title: Continuous Scalar Kernels for Quotients of Variable-Cell Periodic Structures: Compactness, Acquisition, and Target Boundaries
papers.abstract: Active learning for machine-learned interatomic potentials requires deciding which periodic structure should be labeled next. A common strategy is to select the structure that is least represented by the current data using a kernel similarity. For periodic systems, however, one physical structure can have many equivalent coordinate descriptions. If the novelty score changes under a shift of origin, atom relabeling, lattice-basis change, or rigid rotation, it measures the chosen representation rather than the physical structure. We remove this ambiguity by defining the design problem on physical equivalence classes and constructing a scalar kernel that is invariant to these rewritings. For this notion of novelty to remain meaningful as structures are explored, the kernel must also vary continuously when atomic positions and the simulation cell change. We establish this continuity by showing that the finite neighbor-distance features entering the kernel depend only on a uniformly bounded set of periodic images. On a compact physically admissible domain, the resulting construction makes maximum-novelty selection well posed and yields the standard kernel interpolation bound for compatible scalar targets. The scope of this guarantee is set by the information retained by the kernel and by the symmetry of the target. Although Cartesian force and deviatoric-stress components require an equivariant extension, hydrostatic pressure remains accessible through isotropic dilation under additional differentiable-extension and common-potential hypotheses. The framework therefore provides a physically well-defined notion of kernel novelty for variable-cell periodic structures together with a precise boundary on the guarantees that follow from it.

papers.title: Universal Structure Generator: A Simple Plugin Agent For Computational Chemistry and Agentic Frameworks.
papers.abstract: Initial structure generation is the universal first step in computational chemistry but remains a bottleneck as each class of structures requires a different structure preparation workflow. We present an open-source UniversalStructure Generator(USG) based on artificial intelligence (AI) that converts natural-language prompts into molecular structures for both molecular and matter simulations, enabling rapid workflow development and seamless agentic AI integration. Computational and theoretical chemistry have recently transitioned into essential parts of modern chemical research. They serve multiple purposes such as supporting experimentally observed behaviour, enabling high-throughput screening before selecting top candidates for synthesis, and revealing underlying mechanisms. Regardless of the research direction or the problem being addressed, the first step in any simulation always remains the same: constructing the initial structure of the system.

papers.title: AI-ASSISTED MULTIPLEXING OF KINASE ACTIVITY IN CELLULO
papers.abstract: All Dysregulated protein kinase signaling is central to cellular pathogenesis, yet simultaneously tracking multiple kinase activities in live cells with high spatial resolution remains a major analytical challenge. Here, we present an AI-assisted multiplexed imaging platform that combines peptide-based biosensors with multiparametric fluorescence microscopy to simultaneously profile Src and Akt1 activity in cellulo. We employed a combination of long-fluorescence-lifetime triangulenium dyes to take advantage of fluorescence lifetime imaging approaches. For multiplexing experiments, we established a multi-color excitation (485/560 nm) and three-channel detection scheme and developed a machine learning framework featuring a hybrid ensemble architecture—coupling Random Forest and Multi-Layer Perceptron neural networks via a soft-vote mechanism—for automated, user-independent unmixing. Analyzing over 4 million pixels across 23 extracted features, the algorithm achieves rapid, pixel-wise classification into nine biochemical states with high accuracy (90.2%) and an AUC-ROC of 0.9904. The platform reconstructs color-coded spatial kinase activity maps, spatial confidence images, and quantitative population histograms, revealing distinct subcellular activity microdomains in HeLa cells. This integrated chemical-computational methodology provides an accessible, robust blueprint for multiplexed kinome profiling and biomarker detection.

papers.title: Induced Structural Disorder Enables High Ionic Conductivity and Capacity in Li2Fe1−xMnxCl4 Cathodes
papers.abstract: The development of high energy density solid-state batteries requires the discovery of ionically conductive cathode active materials which enable the production of electrode composites with high cathode active material loadings. Here, we show the ionic conductivity of Li 2 FeCl 4 can be more than doubled by increasing the structural disorder via a facile mechanochemical and low temperature annealing procedure. We find that the metastable Fd- 3 m Li 2 FeCl 4 phase produced by mechanochemical synthesis undergoes a room temperature structural re-ordering to a Cmmm phase on the scale of months, which lowers the ionic conductivity, and raises concerns for the shelf-life of metastable materials. We demonstrate that the structural disorder can be “locked-in” by introducing Mn 2+ into the system without significantly impacting the ionic conductivity. We further elucidate the origin of the phase transitions and the role of entropic stabilisation on ionic conductivity though density functional theory modelling and machine-learning force field molecular dynamics calculations. These reveal a 3-dimensional Li + conduction pathway in the disordered structure, which is not present when the material is ordered. By engineering high conductivity disordered, Fd-3m , phases of Li 2 FeCl 4 and Li 2 Fe 0.75 Mn 0.25 Cl 4 , solid-state batteries containing zero catholyte are demonstrated with high voltage plateaus of 3.7 V and capacities of 115 mAh/g CAM and 90 mAh/g CAM , respectively. Considering the high cathode loadings, we demonstrate that the materials Li 2 FeCl 4 and Li 2 Fe 0.75 Mn 0.25 Cl 4 can be used to produce solid state battery cathodes with higher energy densities than that of the commercial material LiFePO 4 , with similar cost effectiveness.

papers.title: Pnictogen-bond-directed self-assembly of Sb and As cages enables partitioning of organic reaction media
papers.abstract: Pnictogen bonding directs self-assembly of antimony- and arsenic-based thiolate cages in organic media, with the Sb system forming persistent reversed-bilayer vesicles capable of chemical compartmentalization. This is demonstrated using chemoswitchable fluorescent probes that selectively quench extravesicular species. In contrast, As analogues form dynamic, transient assemblies with diminished compartmentalization. Density functional theory calculations reveal reduced electrostatic potential and cooperativity in the As systems, consistent with weaker pnictogen bonding interactions. These results establish pnictogen identity as a key factor governing vesicle stability and demonstrate a potentially general strategy for probing compartmentalization in nonaqueous systems.

papers.title: Coupling Digital Twins with Human Expertise to Scale-Up Electrochemical Energy Devices: Present & Future
papers.abstract: Currently, there is considerable excitement surrounding the potential of Digital Twins (DTs) for electrochemical energy devices; however, there is also significant ambiguity regarding the DT term itself. Often, it is confused with a standard mathematical model, which is simply a digital representation of a physical system. In this Perspective article, we first aim to provide a unified definition of a DT. We clarify that a true DT requires real-time, automated, and bidirectional interaction between the physical system and its digital counterpart. Furthermore, we discuss why DTs are complementary to human scientists and engineers and not their replacement. We then delve into the concept of Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) where DTs are overseen and controlled by human operators and/or where DTs are used as a copilot of human scientific intelligence. We also explore these concepts focusing specifically on the battery field, with examples in the context of research and design of battery management systems, self-driving laboratories for battery material synthesis, and battery manufacturing. Finally, we discuss the emerging opportunities in regards of the implementation of advanced artificial intelligence techniques in DTs and HITL approaches for the accelerated design and optimization of electrochemical energy devices, but also we warn about the associated challenges..

papers.title: A Room Full of Experts, None of Them Human: Multi-Agent AI as Virtual Research Teams
papers.abstract: Scientific progress has historically depended on collaboration. For the first time, some collaborators may be non-human. Multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) systems operate as teams of specialised digital scientists addressing shared challenges. Instead of relying on a single model, these systems integrate multiple AI agents, each assigned distinct roles, perspectives, or reasoning strategies. Agents generate proposals, critique one another’s suggestions, and iteratively refine solutions through both collaboration and competition. Advancement arises from the interaction of diverse viewpoints and the exchange of ideas, rather than from a single insight.

papers.title: Engaging medical students with chemistry through enhancing relevance and diversifying assessment
papers.abstract: An inorganic chemistry module for undergraduate medicine students was redesigned based on student feedback, using Universal Design for Learning principles to improve student experiences. The main aim was to boost engagement by maximising chemistry's relevance to medicine, while minimising distractions and accessibility-barriers. Structural supports built into large modules reduce need for once-off accommodations. Redesign choices included pre-scheduled communications, accessible learning materials, videos, varying assessment (including peer-assessment), and linking learning to student-generated examples of medicinal applications. Redesign ensured most prior critiques did not recur in post-implementation feedback. Focus group comments and a general uplift of grades largely supported positive impact of interventions.

papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors
RACI-LEAN: A MACHINE-CHECKED FORMALIZATION OF RESTRICTED ACCESS TO CONICAL INTERSECTIONS AS A MECHANISTIC BASIS OF AGGREGATION-INDUCED EMISSION
papers.abstract: Aggregation-induced emission (AIE) is usually rationalised by the phenomenological RIM/RIR picture, in which intramolecular motions are restricted in the aggregate. Here we develop RACI- Lean, a machine-checked formal theory in Lean 4 that states the mechanism more sharply: AIE follows when restricted geometry removes access to the S1/S0 conical intersection. We prove, within the Jablonski competition model, an exact criterion: emission enhancement occurs if and only if knr,agg × kr,sol < knr,sol × kr,agg, i.e. the nonradiative channel is suppressed more strongly than the radiative channel. The geometric part of the theory is formalised without proof gaps, including the codimension-two local structure of the CI seam and the Longuet-Higgins sign change around the intersection. As a first molecular instance, we combine ORCA SF-TDDFT calculations of tetraphenylethylene with crystallographic constraints to instantiate the criterion. No new experiments are introduced; all empirical inputs are literature values or quantum-chemical data.

papers.title: Potential Dependent Modulation of Surface Enhanced Electronic and Vibrational Raman Scattering Intensity at Roughened Gold Surfaces
papers.abstract: Electrochemical surface enhanced Raman scattering (EC-SERS) spectroscopy combines the sensitivity and molecular specificity of SERS with electroanalysis. This combination enables real time monitoring of reactions at the electrode surface as the electrode potential is swept. The surface plasmon resonance (SPR) of gold nanostructures deposited on electrodes are sensitive to electrode potential. A similar dependence of the SPR of hot-spots on roughened gold electrodes could result in the vibrational SERS intensities of the adsorbed molecules, changing with electrode potential. However, isolating and identifying this effect is challenging since several other factors can cause potential dependent changes in the intensity of the vibrational SERS spectra during voltammetry. These include reorientation of molecules with respect to the surface, AuO formation, local changes in pH, and changes in the oxidation state of the analytes. Here we combine high speed Raman spectroscopy together with SERS probes that are essentially insensitive to changes in pH, or reorientation effects etc., to minimize these interfering effects. We demonstrate that the background in the Raman spectra due to electronic Raman inelastic scattering can be used to detect electrode potential generated shifts in the SPR spectrum of the hot-spots that are responsible for the SERS enhancement. We therefore show that the observed changes in the EC-SERS spectra from physisorbed sub-monolayers of the complexes [M(II)(bpy)3]

papers.title: Achieving High Active Material Loading for Co- and Ni-free cathodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries Through Conductive Network Integration
papers.abstract: Disordered rocksalt (DRX) cathodes could enable high-capacity, cobalt- and nickel-free lithium-ion batteries, but their poor electronic conductivity has required high carbon contents and intensive mechanical processing, sacrificing electrode-level energy density. Here we report a solution-based electrostatic self-assembly approach that uniformly decorates polyethylenimine-modified Li1.05Mn0.85Ti0.10O2 particles with multiwalled carbon nanotubes (CNTs). The high-aspect-ratio CNT network provides electrode-level electronic percolation at < 3 wt% total carbon. Electrodes with < 3 wt% CNT match conventional electrodes containing 20 wt% carbon black while increasing the active-material mass fraction up to > 95%. This low-inactive-content architecture delivers ~500 Wh kg−1 electrode-level specific energy, compared with ~370 Wh kg−1 for carbon-rich electrodes, and remains effective at active-material loadings up to ~56 mg cm−2 and areal capacities of ~8.5 mAh cm−2. The high active-material electrode architecture also delivers a high electrode-level energy density of ~2098.8 Wh L-1, which is comparable to the conventional layered oxides. These results establish conductive-network engineering as a practical route to high-loading DRX cathodes.

papers.title: Hydration Shell Structure and Water-Mediated Binding of closo-Dodecaborates Probed by Raman Hydration-Shell Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The binding of closo-dodecaborates, B12X122- (where X = H, Cl, Br, I), to solutes and interfaces has widely been attributed to a water-mediated (super-)chaotropic effect. The role of water, however, has so far been inferred only indirectly from thermodynamic measurements. Herein, we employ Raman hydration-shell spectroscopy in the OH stretch region to investigate B12X122- in aqueous solution. Specifically, we elucidate i) the water structure in the hydration shell, ii) its temperature dependence, and iii) the water release upon superchaotropic binding. The hydration-shell spectra reveal that all dodecaborates give rise to a sharp Raman band close to 3600 cm-1. This feature is strongly blue-shifted compared to bulk water and represents weakly H-bonded, “almost dangling” OH-groups in the hydration shell. Heating is found to blue-shift the hydration water resonance less than the bulk water resonance. Hydration and bulk water resonances thus become more similar at high temperature. This trend reflects a progressively reduced difference in hydrogen-bonding energy upon heating between hydration and bulk water, and is opposite to that of hydrophobic hydration. Furthermore, hydration difference spectra in the presence of the non-ionic polymer hydroxypropylcellulose (HPC) reveal that weakly H-bonded hydration water is released from B12X122- upon superchaotropic binding, together with more strongly H-bonded hydration water from the hydration shells of both B 12 X 12 2- and HPC. These findings identify weakly bound hydration water, its weak temperature dependence, and its spontaneous release upon binding as molecular hallmarks of the superchaotropic behavior of B 12 X 12 2- .

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn by the authors because a contributor should not have been listed. An updated version is available at 10.26434/chemrxiv.15007800/v3

papers.title: Cross-mixture-size graph neural network for CO2 solubility prediction in multicomponent amine solvents
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of equilibrium CO 2 loading in aqueous amine blends is essential for the design and screening of next-generation carbon capture solvents. However, existing machine learning models are generally developed for a fixed number of mixture components, limiting their applicability to increasingly complex solvent formulations. In this work, we introduced a mixture-size-invariant graph neural network (MSI-GNN) that enables prediction of CO 2 loading across different amine blend complexities within a single architecture. The model represents each amine-water-CO 2 system as a disjoint-union of graph, generates component-level representations using shared message-passing neural network, and combines solvent contributions through a learnable mole-fraction-weighted mixing rule. The resulting mixture context is integrated with CO 2 modulator and temperature descriptors to predict CO 2 equilibrium loading. Trained on 6,835 experimental data points spanning 121 solvent combinations, MSI-GNN achieves an R 2 of 0.987 ± 0.001 on the held-out test set and gives an R 2 of 0.913 ± 0.006 on the held-out test set aggregated from single-, dual-, and triple-amines. This demonstrates generalization beyond both the chemical systems and mixture complexities represented during model development. Benchmarking against a baseline GNN and its physics-informed variant demonstrates competitive accuracy on single-amine systems, while MSI-GNN uniquely extends prediction to binary and ternary blends without architectural modification. The mixture-size invariance provides a scalable approach for predicting previously unexplored multicomponent solvents and establishes a computational framework for accelerating high-throughput screening and discovery of next-generation amine-based CO 2 capture solvents.

papers.title: Ontology-guided deep reinforcement learning for site-specific construction of lead compounds representing coal macromolecular active sites
papers.abstract: Quantum-chemical studies of coal reactivity rely on small model compounds that represent local structures within the coal macromolecule, yet these surrogates are still chosen by analogy and investigators’ experience. The resulting mismatch is rarely quantified: a model may share a functional group and an approximate two-dimensional topology with its target site while reproducing a substantially different local electronic environment. This work reformulates that selection step as a constrained generative search. Liuqiao (LQ) coking coal was characterized by proximate and ultimate analysis, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and solid-state 13C nuclear magnetic resonance, and an experimentally constrained statistical-average macromolecular model of formula C209H134O15N2 was assembled under those constraints; its simulated 13C spectrum reproduces the measured spectrum to within a 2.14% local dispersion deviation. The macromolecule was then formalized as a knowledge ontology that decomposes it into computable semantic units under two top-level classes, nuclei and dispersoids, carrying object properties and quantitative data properties. Instantiation against PubChem under LQ-derived screening rules yielded 560 structural primitives, in which aromatic carbon rose from 60.23% to 72.56%, and carbonyl carbon fell to 0.385%. On this library, EF-GRL — an actor–critic agent that assembles molecules by single-bit flips over a hierarchical binary encoding under site locking and hard-constraint gating — was rewarded by a weighted combination of two-dimensional structural similarity and three-dimensional electrostatic-potential similarity (SESP). For the –OH, –CH3, –O– and –C(=O)H sites, the constructed leads reached SESP values of 0.8332, 0.7368, 0.8127 and 0.8463, exceeding the best conventional homolog at every site.

papers.title: A new twist on Hayashi–Miyaura arylation: Overcoming the Fürst–Plattner torsional barrier
papers.abstract: 2Skaggs Graduate School of Chemical and Biological Sciences ABSTRACT: The Rh-catalyzed Hayashi–Miyaura conjugate addition is frequently limited by the instability of heteroaryl boronic acids under aqueous conditions and the intrinsic stereoelectronic biases of cyclic enones. Here, we report a robust, non-aqueous protocol using commercial bisphosphine ligands and cesium salts that enables the efficient coupling of highly labile heterocyclic and heteroaryl boronic acids, including challenging furanyl, pyrrolyl, pyridyl, and pyrimidyl derivatives. Using a conformationally locked decalenone, we provide experimental validation of the Fürst–Plattner torsional strain model in carborhodation and demonstrate that this inherent bias can be overridden to achieve ligand-controlled, anti-Fürst–Plattner additions. This protocol allows modular access to cis-3,5-disubstituted cyclohexanones that are difficult to reach by substrate-controlled addition and provides a unified approach to construct high-value medicinal chemistry scaffolds, as demonstrated by the formal syntheses of tolterodine analogs and the synthesis of C12-cyclohexenyl-O6C-salvinorin A.

papers.title: Semi-automated Synthesis and Interactive Visualization of Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework- Based Biocomposites
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT Zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) biocomposites are widely studied for their potential in biocatalysis and biomedicine. However, their preparation is highly sensitive to precursor composition, concentration, washing conditions, and operator-dependent handling procedures. Here, we combine a semi-automated syringe-pump system, high-throughput sample preparation, and digital data visualization to map synthesis-structure-property relationships in ZIF biocomposites. A programmable four-syringe pump platform was used to systematically prepare 360 distinct samples in triplicate, yielding 1080 samples. The investigated synthetic parameters were relative amounts of metal, ligand, protein, the total precursor concentration, and the washing protocol. Structural, chemical, and functional characterization yielded a dataset of ~2250 entries comprising crystalline-to-amorphous ratios, IR-based protein-to-framework ratios, encapsulation efficiency, and loading capacity. We note that exploring such a large dataset manually can be challenging and that current static visualizations can hide meaningful trends. With the aim of enabling a customized and interactive exploration of the data, we designed the ZIF Biocomposite Explorer App (ZIF-BEA), which supports user-defined navigation in the space of the variables, providing direct access to experimental data and material properties. We anticipate that integrating large experimental datasets with interactive digital platforms may expedite the design of MOFbased biocomposites, while providing a transferable tool for the exploration of other classes of functional materials.

papers.title: Direct Mechanochemical Aryl Amination of Polystyrene for Creep Resistant Imine Elastomers
papers.abstract: Imine-based covalent adaptable networks (CANs) hold promise for the development of recyclable thermoset materials, but due to low barriers for dynamic exchange, such networks typically suffer from significant material creep. Incorporating linear polymers into imine CANs can improve creep resistance by introducing physical crosslinks, while reactive variants further mitigate through chemical crosslinks. Herein, we directly aminate polystyrene (up to 1.1 mol%) using ball mill grinding mechanochemistry with liquid-assisted grinding for inclusion into dynamic materials. This post-polymerization modification technique allows us to avoid excess solvent while preserving high molar mass. Incorporating aminated PS (aPS) in representative polyimine elastomers enhances creep resistance relative to unmodified PS, while maintaining comparable mechanical properties. These findings establish waste PS grafted with low densities of reactive primary amines as an effective additive for improving deformation resistance in polyimines, thus offering a route to give post-consumer plastic waste renewed value.

papers.title: FERA-MS: formula-and collision-energy-aware tandem mass spectrum prediction for molecular identification
papers.abstract: Motivation: High-resolution in silico MS/MS prediction can expand spectral-library coverage and facilitate small-molecule identification. However, accurate prediction requires the joint modeling of chemically plausible fragment ions, collisionenergy-dependent fragmentation, and spectrum-level competition among candidate ions. Results: We propose FERA-MS, a formula-and collision-energy-aware framework for high-resolution MS/MS prediction. FERA-MS generates fragment-ion candidates from a depth-3 fragment directed acyclic graph with bounded hydrogen-transfer states and composition-valid neutral-loss channels, incorporates collision energy at multiple levels of fragment-ion scoring, and transforms candidate probabilities into spectra through local m/z rendering, chemical reranking, and spectrum-wise intensity allocation. Across 19 659 unmerged positive-ion QTOF/CID spectra from 2 274 molecules, FERA- MS consistently outperformed four collision-energy-conditioned baselines under both molecule-disjoint random and scaffold-disjoint evaluation, reaching mean micro CBIN/JSS values of 0.656/0.622 on the random test and 0.622/0.602 on the scaffold-disjoint test. In fixed mass-compatible candidate-structure pools containing the true structure and 49 fingerprint-similar non-target structures, FERA-MS achieved Top-1 accuracies of 28.89% and 28.51% on the random and scaffold-disjoint tests, respectively, demonstrating that improved spectral fidelity translates into more reliable structure ranking. Perturbation and ablation analyses further confirmed that FERA-MS benefits from multi-level collision-energy conditioning and mass-resolved fragment-ion rendering. Availability and implementation: Source code, preprocessing and split-construction scripts, locked configurations and evaluation scripts are available at https://github.com/lrq-one/FERA-MS. Contact: liweihua@ynu.edu.cn Supplementary information: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.title: Liquid-State Photoreactions of Ru-Containing Ionic Liquids with PF5CN Anions: Ligand-Dependent Coordination Modes and Reversibility
papers.abstract: Functional liquids that respond to external stimuli have recently attracted considerable attention. We have previously developed Ru-containing photoreactive ionic liquids bearing multidentate coordinating anions and achieved liquid-to-solid conversion based on photoinduced metal bridging. In this study, we synthesized two Ru-containing ionic liquids, [Ru(C5H5)(N-methyl-N-hexylaniline)]PF5CN ([1]PF5CN) and [Ru(C5H5)(octylbenzene)]PF5CN ([2]PF5CN), containing the monodentate anion PF5CN−, and investigated their photoreactivity. Upon UV irradiation, these ionic liquids generated anionic Ru complexes in which the arene ligand was photodissociated and replaced by two PF5CN− anions together with the dissociated arene ligand; the extent of photodissociation was approximately 70%. [1]PF5CN afforded a product in which the arene ligand was N-coordinated, and this product thermally reverted to the original ionic liquid, resulting in reversible photo/thermal changes in ionic conductivity. In contrast, [2]PF5CN gave a product in which the arene ligand was η2-coordinated, and this transformation was irreversible. These results show that the use of a monodentate coordinating anion allows the photoreaction to proceed while retaining the ionic-liquid state, and that the reversibility can be controlled by the choice of arene ligand.

papers.title: Accessing block copolymers with independently modulated tacticities using sequential cationic-anionic polymerization of vinyl ethers and thiiranes
papers.abstract: Tacticity can have profound effects on the physical properties of polymers, such as self-assembly of block copolymers (BCPs). Despite its promise, previous reports on changing tacticity of BCPs have primarily focused on changing a single block or comparing fully isotactic to fully atactic copolymers. Herein, we report a platform to easily access fully atactic, fully isotactic, and mixed tacticity poly(vinyl ether)-block-poly(thiirane) BCPs. Isotacticity was independently accessed via stereoselective polymerization of vinyl ethers and by using enantiopure thiirane monomers, respectively. Thermal analyses of these materials were performed and semi-crystallinity was observed in aryl-containing isotactic blocks. For BCPs with alkyl side chains or atactic aryl side chains, fractionation on the basis of composition was performed to accelerate self-assembly studies. These fractionated BCPs were characterized via small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), where we observed hexagonally-packed cylinder or lamellar morphologies for some fractions. The development of this framework of selective tacticity modulation opens up facile access to diverse BCPs with varying thermal, solution-state, and bulk properties.

papers.title: Tuning Structural Order in Photogenerated Metal-Complex Solids from Ruthenium-Containing Ionic Liquids
papers.abstract: We recently demonstrated photoinduced liquid-to-solid transformations of metal-containing ionic liquids into coordination-based solids; however, control over the solid-state structure of the resulting products has not been explored. In this study, we investigated the photoreaction of a Ru-containing ionic liquid bearing an asymmetric cyanoborate anion, [Ru(C5H5)(PhNMeHex)][B(C2H4CN)(CN)3] (1a), and found that the structural order of the photogenerated solids could be tuned by adding the nonphotoreactive ionic liquid [Ru(C5H5)(PhNMeHex)]Tf2N (1b). Photoirradiation of neat 1a afforded a predominantly amorphous solid with an estimated crystalline fraction of 13%, and subsequent heating regenerated the original ionic liquid. Addition of 1b at 25 and 50 mol% increased this fraction to 19% and 44%, respectively. The crystalline components were identified as the cubane-type tetranuclear Ru complex 3, whereas the amorphous components contained structurally less-defined polynuclear and extended coordination species together with composition-dependent amounts of 3. Thus, 1b influenced both the overall fraction of 3 in the photoproducts and its distribution between the amorphous and crystalline phases. These results demonstrate a photochemical strategy for generating metal-complex solids directly from ionic liquids while tuning their structural order through composition.

papers.title: Phase Behavior and Solid-State Photoreactivity of Organometallic Ionic Plastic Crystals with Cyanoborate Anions
papers.abstract: Ionic plastic crystals (IPCs) exhibit long-range translational order with orientational disorder and high molecular mobility, yet their chemical reactivity remains unexplored. Salts of the sandwich-type Ru complex cation [Ru(Cp)(C6H6)]+ ([1]+) often exhibit IPC phases, while cyanoborate salts of [1]+ undergo photochemical reactions to form polynuclear complexes in solution and in the ionic-liquid state. These properties prompted us to synthesize [1]BE(CN)3 (E = F, H, or Me) and [1]BE2(CN)2 (E = F or Et) and investigate their phase behavior and photoreactivity in IPC phases. All five salts exhibited IPC phases, with transition temperatures from the ordered crystalline phase to the IPC phase ranging from 277 to 378 K; three underwent the transition below 300 K. UV irradiation of these three salts in their IPC phases afforded cubane-type tetranuclear complexes from [1]BF(CN)3 and [1]BH(CN)3 in conversions of 50–77%. In contrast, irradiation of [1]BH(CN)3 and [1]BMe(CN)3 in their low-temperature crystalline phases gave conversions of only 18% and 11%, respectively. These results demonstrate that the high molecular mobility of IPCs enables solid-state photochemistry, with the salts acting as both reactants and reaction media.

papers.title: Base-Free Palladium-Catalyzed Synthesis of 2-Alkoxy-1,3-Dienes from Primary Propargyl Carbonates with Benzyl Alcohols
papers.abstract: Although several methods have been reported for the synthesis of 1,3-diene skeletons from propargyl esters, only a few are effective for the synthesis of 2-alkoxy-1,3-dienes. Herein, we report a convenient palladium-catalyzed synthesis of these compounds using primary propargyl carbonates and benzyl alcohols. Mono-substituted 1,3-dienes were synthesized in up to 80% yield using various benzyl alcohols. Furthermore, the robustness and versatility of this method were demonstrated through a gram-scale synthesis and a one-pot reaction.

papers.title: XGBoost Prediction of Ionizable Lipid Transfection Potency with Chemistry-Aware Validation
papers.abstract: Ionizable lipids play key determinant role for the mRNA delivery performance of lipid nanoparticles (LNP), yet structure-activity relationships (SAR) for this compound class remain difficult to generalize across chemically diverse head groups and tail architectures. We used the publicly available AGILE ionizable lipid library, 1200 lipids synthesized by three-component Ugi reaction chemistry and formulated into LNPs carrying firefly luciferase reporter mRNA, to build an interpretable quantitative structure-transfection model based on extended-connectivity fingerprints (ECFP4), four physiochemical descriptors, and gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost). Because random data splitting inflates apparent predictive performance for structurally similar compound libraries, we designed a distance-buffered leave-one-cluster-out (LOCO) validation protocol that excludes any training compound within a Tanimoto distance of 0.1 from a held-out cluster, verified to eliminate chemical neighbor leakage. Under random five-fold cross validation, the model explained 48.9% of transfection variance (pooled R2 = 0.489, RMSE = 2.31), while under the buffered LOCO protocol measuring extrapolation to structurally novel chemotypes, pooled R2 fell to 0.354 (RMSE = 2.64, n = 938 of 1200 compound covered). This gap is real but moderate, and narrower than a naive per-cluster averaging of the same predictions would suggest. SHAP analysis, aggregated across all 50 LOCO folds to assess both stability and direction identified a head-group-ring-dependent instead of amine-presence-dependent structure-activity relationship: a piperazine head group was the single most stable determinant of predicted transfection potency and was consistently associated with reduced potency, while a cis-alkene tail motif showed a direction dependent on its position along the acyl tail, confirmed at both the individual-fold and pooled-split level. Calculated logP showed a moderate, mostly consistent, positive association with predicted potency. Molecular weight contributed comparable magnitude but a directionally inconsistent, collinearity confounded signal. This substructure-level finding converges independently with the original AGILE study, which used a mechanistically unrelated approach (integrated gradients on a graph neural network fit to Mordred descriptors) and identified a tertiary-amine descriptor (SssNH) as similarly influential for the same HeLa cell endpoint. We also integrate a nearest-neighbor applicability domain check into the prediction workflow so that candidate lipids structurally distant from the training library are flagged. We discuss the scope limitations of the underlying dataset, in particular its dependence on a single reporter mRNA and a single cell line, and position chemistry-aware generalization testing as a validation practice that should accompany in vitro confirmation of computationally prioritized ionizable lipid.

papers.title: Regularized Alternatives to Conventional Density Fitting: Tikhonov Regularization with Discrete Picard Condition
papers.abstract: Density fitting (DF) reduces the computational cost of correlated electronic-structure methods but can become unstable when the fitting metric contains small eigenvalues or near-linear dependencies. We introduce a new set of protocols based on the Tikhonov regularization (TR) framework combined with the Discrete Picard Condition (DPC) to adaptively determine an effective truncation of the auxiliary space in DF-MP2. Truncation indices are selected using either a two-line L-curve fit or local sharp-corner protocols. Across the S22 benchmark set and an AlkB hydrogen-atom-transfer reaction, the three-point sharp-corner methods provide the highest overall accuracy, with the best-performing protocol showing consistent performance across basis sets and molecular structures. The two-line protocol is less accurate but more robust when the auxiliary basis is reduced or poorly matched to the orbital basis. These results show that TR–DPC provides a flexible strategy for stabilizing DF while maintaining accuracy across varied auxiliary-basis conditions.

papers.title: Temperature-induced Changes to the Nucleation Mechanism of MOF-5-inspired Crystals through the Lens of Multiscale Simulation
papers.abstract: A comprehensive map of metal-organic framework (MOF) formation mechanisms is crucial to facilitate the experimental realization and/or synthesis optimization of computer-generated MOFs. Experiments to gain this knowledge face challenges with the time and length scales of the crucial MOF nucleation stage and the interplay of a multitude of synthesis-relevant factors. In response to this challenge, this work uses molecular simulation to isolate the effect of temperature, one of the most common processing conditions used to optimize MOF solvothermal synthesis, on the nucleation mechanism of porous, cubic crystals representative of the prototypical material MOF-5. The simulation framework used herein is multiscale, culminating with coarse-grained (CG) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations enhanced with Hamiltonian replica exchange (HREX), enabling the construction of free energy surfaces (FESs) and minimum free energy pathway (MFEP) analysis. This analysis suggests that MOF-5 nucleation in DMF follows a non-classical, multistage nucleation pathway at the studied temperatures (i.e., 300 K, 413 K, and 500 K), where metastable amorphous nuclei form prominently before annealing into ordered cubic nuclei, following a multibarrier free energy pathway. Critically, consistent with the well-established solvothermal synthesis of MOF-5 in DMF at ~ 413 K, our analysis identifies this temperature as more kinetically favorable than 300 K and 500 K. Briefly, it exhibits the smoothest free energy landscape from dense liquid to nucleus formation, the highest equilibrium population of the cubic nucleus, and the fastest rate for nucleus formation. These factors collectively rationalize why this temperature range may be favored in practice. Similarities and differences in the sequence of events leading to formation of large, ordered nuclei across the studied temperatures are discussed as well.

papers.title: A Generalizable Framework for Quantifying Uncertainty and Bias in Curve Aggregation for High-Throughput Electrodeposition Data
papers.abstract: Experimental reproducibility in electrochemistry is fundamentally limited by process uncertainty. This challenge, especially pronounced in complex systems like Fe-based multi-metal electrodeposition, is a major bottleneck for high-throughput and autonomous materials discovery. To address this, we present a generalizable curve aggregation framework that combines Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) with Functional Data Analysis (FDA) to aggregate replicate measurements while preserving within-curve correlation structure. The method represents each transient as a continuous function and iteratively optimizes curve-wise weights to emphasize consistent signals and suppress outliers. We validate the framework using potentiostatic transients from near-equiatomic CoCuFeNi electrodeposition across seven deposition conditions. The framework successfully aggregated 226 transients, quantified experimental variance and transient shape, and showed performance comparable to a more computationally intensive but physically robust first-principle measurement model. We find that uncertainty, bias, and convergence difficulty evolve with dataset size resembling a Dunning–Kruger-like pattern, where small datasets appear deceptively certain, followed by a maximum convergence difficulty peak, then converge to a stable final aggregate. For this system, the variance stabilized at approximately 𝑁 ≈ 35–40 measurements, providing a practical criterion for data sufficiency. The GPR-FDA framework is broadly applicable to any experimental field involving replicate functional data that must be aggregated without losing correlation information.

papers.title: Electrochemical Robustness and Spin-Selective Transport in Self-Assembled MYG-0 Peptide Monolayers
papers.abstract: Chiral Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) in biomolecules offers a revolutionary pathway for the development of molecular spintronic devices. However, achieving both high spin-filtering efficiency and robust electrochemical stability under high electric fields remains a significant challenge for peptide monolayers. Here, we investigate the nanoscopic electrical and spin-transport properties of self-assembled MYG-0(Ac-HEHGH-GPGP-HGDAH-C-NH2) peptide monolayers on gold substrates. Conductive atomic 10 force microscopy (c-AFM) confirms the formation of a homogeneous and continuous peptide monolayer. Remarkably, the monolayer exhibits extraordinary electrochemical robustness, maintaining its structural and electrical integrity even under a wide biasing range from -5 to 5 V, while showing distinct current-voltage (I-V) hysteresis and rectification behavior. Crucially, magnetic c-AFM (mc-AFM) measurements reveal a pronounced spin-selective transport, where 15 the current is highly sensitive to the probe's magnetization direction (Mag Up vs. Mag Down). The corresponding graph unveil spin-dependent quantum resonance peaks, indicating strong spinorbit coupling within the chiral framework. At a bias of 4.5 V, the calculated spin polarization (SP%) reaches a maximum value of approximately 60%. These findings demonstrate that MYG-0 peptide monolayers possess both superior spin-filtering efficiency and exceptional durability

papers.title: Room-Temperature Tunable Dual Exciton Emission in Hybrid Lead Bromides with an Unreported Two-Dimensional Framework
papers.abstract: Low-dimensional hybrid lead halides offer a platform for tunable light emission, yet the relationship between structural topology and exciton dynamics in two-dimensional frameworks remains poorly understood. Here, we report two hybrid lead bromides, (IM)2(EA)Pb3Br9 (1, IM = imidazolium, EA = ethylammonium) and (PY)2(EA)Pb3Br9 (2, PY = pyrazolium), built around a 2D [Pb3Br9]3- framework of edge-sharing octahedral ribbons interconnected by bridging octahedra. This layer type is absent from known hybrid halide structures. Both compounds exhibit excitation- and temperature-dependent dual photoluminescence, arising from the coexistence of two distinct self-trapped exciton bands of different structural origin and a narrow free exciton band, enabling continuous color tuning from red-orange at 80 K to white or near-white emission at room temperature. DFT calculations reveal Pb–Br dominated valence bands and conduction band states showing site-selective localization on crystallographically inequivalent Pb sites, consistent with the dual STE emission. Flat band dispersion and large carrier effective masses support self-trapped exciton formation. These results demonstrate that framework topology strongly influences exciton behavior in hybrid halides, and that exploring structural motifs beyond conventional archetypes is a productive route toward materials with tunable, room-temperature emission for solid-state lighting and optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: GLPlot: GPU-accelerated interactive scientific visualization with a Matplotlib-like interface
papers.abstract: Interactive visualization is part of the scientific reasoning process: researchers use plots to inspect convergence, identify outliers, compare simulations, assess uncertainty, and decide which analyses or experiments to perform next. Furthermore, plots enable us to identify relationships that would otherwise be missed by visualizing abstract concepts alone; for these reasons, it is imperative that the scientific community have access to easy, fast tools to visualize their data. The complexity of these tasks rapidly escalates when a figure contains a large number of points, vertices, curves, or other geometric primitives. Conventional plotting workflows may incur substantial costs from CPU-side geometry construction, per-object draw calls, repeated rasterization, and transfer of expanded geometry to the graphics device. These speed bumps are not just a minor irritation, but an active hindrance to scientific discovery, as fewer potential lines of reasoning are pursued if one must wait hours to confirm one’s logic.

papers.title: Electrostatic Preorganisation Shapes a Hypercoordination Valley Along the Donor–Acceptor Bonding Continuum
papers.abstract: Understanding how ligands approach electron-deficient centres is a fundamental challenge, as the energetic landscape bridging weak encounter complexes and fully developed bonds remains poorly characterised. Here, we combine crystallographic and quantum-chemical studies to map the emergence of five-coordinate systems in trimethylaluminium complexes. By screening diverse library of ligands, we crystallographically captured distinct stages of ligand approach, from weak van der Waals complexes to fully hypercoordinate aluminium centres. Complementary calculations reveal that these structures populate a continuous interaction pathway. We define a remarkably shallow region on the potential energy surface – the hypercoordination valley – which seamlessly connects weak associations with stable hypercoordinate bonding, encompassing a transient stage of incipient orbital interaction. Local energy decomposition shows that this valley is primarily electrostatically preorganised, while short-range interactions stabilise the symmetric five-coordinate arrangement, analogous to a classical SN2 transition state. These findings suggest that hypercoordination valleys represent a general feature of main-group donor–acceptor chemistry.

papers.title: Electrostatic preactivation of dioxygen without metal redox activity
papers.abstract: Dioxygen is the terminal oxidant of aerobic life and one of the most widely used reagents in chemistry, yet it reacts slowly with closed-shell molecules. Its persistence is usually attributed to spin restrictions and to the cost of the first one-electron reduction. A third obstacle is rarely stated: at the equilibrium geometry of the neutral molecule the anion that is to receive the electron is not bound, so the acceptor does not yet exist at the geometry from which reaction must begin. Activation has instead been framed around the donor, and the electrostatic surroundings treated as scaffolding. Here we show that those surroundings act on dioxygen itself, in a stage we term preactivation . In dialkylzincs, where a redox-silent metal supplies the field and the Zn–R bond supplies the electron, a single ZnR2 unit lifts the degeneracy of the 𝝿* acceptor manifold of O2 and inverts the sign of its vertical attachment energy before any charge moves. A framework of bare point charges, incapable of orbital interaction of any kind, reproduces the response in full. Electron transfer then follows as a rate-determining crossing between two triplet states, and additional Lewis-acidic centres lower its energy further. Preparing dioxygen as an acceptor and delivering the electron to it are therefore separate functions, the first governed by the local electrostatic field alone – a quantity defined for any Lewis-acidic environment, from a metal alkyl to an enzyme active site.

papers.title: Efficient and reversible boron coordination in a fluorescent BODIPY rotaxane
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of a fluorescent rotaxane based on the threading of a BODIPY core through a macrocycle containing a biphenol unit. After stoppering, the macrocycle was efficiently released from the boron centre using BF 3 .OEt 2 , affording the corresponding rotaxane quantitatively within one minute. Conversely, the macrocycle was quantitatively recoordinated to the boron centre within one minute upon treatment with AlCl 3 . Remarkably, both states retain high fluorescence quantum yields (up to 91%), while the rotaxane exhibits enhanced two-photon absorption compared with its precursor. This rapid and reversible boron-centered coordination process provides a new approach to fluorescent mechanically interlocked architectures with tunable optical properties.

papers.title: Electrocatalytic Formic Acid Oxidation Behavior of Pt–N/C
papers.abstract: Pt–N/C was prepared by impregnation of a carbon support with a Pt precursor followed by urea-assisted thermal treatment at 950 °C under Ar. X-ray diffraction revealed the broad carbon diffraction feature together with weak reflections indexed to fcc Pt, while the N 1s XPS spectrum contained components assigned to pyridinic N, Pt–N-related coordination, graphitic N, and oxidized N. Compared with commercial Pt/C, Pt–N/C exhibited strongly attenuated hydrogen adsorption/desorption features and a smoother background cyclic-voltammetric profile, reflecting a distinct Pt surface environment. During formic acid oxidation, commercial Pt/C showed a prominent higher-potential oxidation response, whereas Pt–N/C displayed a dominant lower-potential oxidation feature. This redistribution indicates a greater relative contribution from the lower-potential oxidation pathway and a reduced contribution from the CO-associated higher-potential process. Overall, the results show that the N-containing carbon environment modifies Pt surface characteristics and leads to a distinct pathway distribution during formic acid electrooxidation.

papers.title: Topochemical Fluorination of the Ruddlesden−Popper In/Sb-Mixed Oxide Ba2In0.5Sb0.5O4; Staged Anion Insertion and Structural Evolution toward the Fluorine-Rich Oxyfluoride Ba2In0.5Sb0.5O2F4
papers.abstract: Layered Ruddlesden–Popper oxides provide a versatile platform for topochemical anion modification, enabling access to metastable mixed-anion phases with tuneable structural and electronic properties. In this work, we present a comprehensive investigation of how mixed B-site (indium and antimony) chemistry influences topochemical fluorination of Ba 2 In 0.5 Sb 0.5 O 4 using PVDF. Powder X-ray diffraction reveals anisotropic lattice expansion, dominated by elongation perpendicular to the perovskite layers, with minimal change in the in-plane lattice parameters. Fluorination proceeds through a composition-dependent multiphase regime in which several tetragonal ( I 4 /mmm ) RP components with progressively expanded c and slightly contracted a lattice parameters coexist, representing a distribution of fluorination states, followed by convergence to a single dominant fluorine-rich tetragonal phase at high fluorine content. Coupled X-ray/neutron Rietveld refinement establishes the end member as the anion-saturated oxyfluoride Ba 2 In 0.5 Sb 0.5 O 2 F 4 , and locates the three fully occupied anion sites of the tetragonal I 4 /mmm framework. The preferred O/F distribution, with oxide at the equatorial site and fluoride at the apical and interstitial sites, is supported by bond-valence-sums (BVSs) analysis of the refined interatomic distances and the corresponding global instability indices (GIIs), together with charge balance, since O and F cannot be reliably distinguished from their neutron scattering lengths alone. XPS confirms that In remains in the +3 oxidation state, while the Sb spectral changes are consistent with modifications of the local O/F coordination environment rather than changes in the formal oxidation state. X-ray absorption near-edge structure measurements further support the retention of the formal In 3+ and Sb 5+ oxidation states upon fluorination.

papers.title: A Thirty-Year Gap: Reviving All-Nitride Glasses as Processable, High-Performance Materials
papers.abstract: This study revisits oxygen-free, all-nitride glasses as a distinct class of highperformance materials, originally reported three decades ago by Grande, Holloway, McMillan, and Angell. A novel glass family at the time, such glass systems have remained unreplicated, largely due to the highly specialized experimental conditions required for their synthesis. With contemporary advances, such constraints are no longer prohibitive. Rather, in light of the persistent challenges in enhancing the performance of conventional glass systems, all-nitride glasses are reconsidered herein as a potentially viable class of processable materials that combine the formability of glasses with ceramic-level performance – without compromising optical transparency. Building upon progress in the modeling and computational evaluation of glass properties, a thermodynamic and semi-empirical framework is established to delineate the accessible chemical space and to estimate key properties, including liquidus temperature, density, elastic modulus, and refractive index. This approach enables assessment of the attainable property space, which is shown to far surpass that of oxide glasses, consistent with experimental trends observed in oxynitride systems. Prospective processing routes, functionalization strategies, and high-performance applications are discussed in light of overcoming supply chain risks associated with materials in current use.

papers.title: CsPbBr3 Enabled Skeletal Divergence of N-Arylglycine via Deoxygenative Spiroannulation
papers.abstract: Spirooxindoles are attractive three-dimensional molecular architectures that provide valuable structural complexity for the exploration of biologically relevant chemical space. Herein, we disclose a visible-light-driven, CsPbBr3-catalyzed deoxygenative spirocyclization of Isatins with N-arylglycines that provides rapid access to spiro-imidazolidine oxindoles. Notably, the transformation unlocks an alternative reaction manifold of N-arylglycines, diverting their established annulation reactivity toward a skeletally distinct spirocyclic architecture. This skeletal divergence enables the direct assembly of two privileged heterocyclic motifs, oxindole and imidazolidine, within a structurally compact three-dimensional framework. The reaction displays broad substrate compatibility and functional group tolerance and can be extended to structurally complex heterocycles and pharmaceutically relevant derivatives, highlighting its synthetic versatility. Carbonyl chemoselectivity experiments, Stern-Volmer quenching analysis, EPR spectroscopy, light ON-OFF-ON studies, and radical-trapping experiments collectively support a photoinduced radical pathway. Beyond providing an efficient route to spiro-imidazolidine oxindoles, this study highlights the ability of CsPbBr3 perovskite photocatalysis to redirect the reaction trajectory of N-arylglycine-derived intermediates toward otherwise distinct heterocyclic architectures.

papers.title: Oxidation of ether quantum defects sustains carbon nanotube emission
papers.abstract: Fluorescent quantum defects enable single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) to emit brightly in the short-wave infrared (SWIR), but how these sites evolve during oxidative degradation, and whether their emission survives, remains unclear. Here we show that hypochlorous acid (HOCl) drives defect-specific transformation in chirality-pure (6,5) SWCNTs under the conditions examined. In accessible surfactant environments, HOCl converts a parent ether defect (O-(6,5)) emitting at ~1124 nm into a distinct oxidized emissive state at ~1163 nm before further lattice damage, whereas aryl sp 3 defects (ArNO 2 -(6,5)) and pristine nanotubes (Pris-(6,5)) predominantly lose emission. Coating and pH control the formation of this intermediate by regulating oxidant access and reactive-chlorine speciation. Time-resolved photoluminescent spectroscopy and single-particle hyperspectral imaging resolve the distinct two emissive states, and density-functional-theory supports a vicinal diol-like sp 3 (OH) 2 -(6,5) motif as the most plausible oxidized structure among the candidates examined. Its D-band intensity per defect resembles that of conventional sp 3 defects, indicating a comparable nanotube defect geometry. Consequently, O-(6,5) oxidizes more rapidly than ArNO 2 -(6,5) yet retains a larger fraction of total defect emission. These findings establish oxidation-driven conversion between emissive quantum defects and identify defect configuration and surface coating as design parameters for degradable, oxidation-responsive SWIR probes with sustained fluorescence.

papers.title: Local-Loop Regenerative Zeolite Cooling (L-RZC): A Fixed-Bed, Non-Mobile Approach for Energy-Efficient AI Data Center Cooling Using Regional Zeolite and Local Waste Heat
papers.abstract: Artificial-intelligence (AI) data centers impose large, continuous cooling loads that are conventionally met by electricity-intensive vapor-compression chillers. Adsorption cooling driven by low-grade heat can reduce electrical demand, yet mobile zeolite thermal-battery concepts require continuous transport of large adsorbent inventories. This paper introduces Local-Loop Regenerative Zeolite Cooling (L-RZC), a fixed-bed architecture in which zeolite remains stationary at the data center while thermal energy is transferred through a short local heat loop (design focus: distance less than or equal to 15 km). Hybrid charging from industrial waste heat, residual server heat, and optional solar thermal input is supported. The study specifies zeolite selection (synthetic 13X and activated Indonesian clinoptilolite), preparation and activation steps, and particle form and size suitable for a packed vacuum reactor (beads or pellets approximately 1.5-3 mm). Mass-energy balances and a dynamic Linear Driving Force simulation size a 50 kW-class prototype and evaluate six scenarios over 48 h. Model coefficients of performance of approximately 0.62-0.68 and discharge-specific cooling powers near 190 W/kg meet predefined thresholds (COP greater than or equal to 0.50; SCP greater than or equal to 150 W/kg). A staged experimental validation protocol is specified. L-RZC targets co-located industrial and data-center sites with accessible waste heat and domestic zeolite resources.

papers.title: “Carbon dioxide expanded ionic liquid mixtures for changing reaction outcomes and efficient separation”
Electrostatic templating and the dynamics of physisorbed CO2 ordering in CALF-20
papers.abstract: Reducing CO2 emissions requires adsorbents combining high selectivity with large capacity, however the molecular origins leading to such properties remain poorly understood. Physisorbents are desirable for their low regeneration energy but they often lack the selectivity needed for efficient large-scale CO2 separation.
