papers.title: Synthesis of novel 2-(tetrafluoro(1,2,2-trifluorovinyl)- λ6-sulfaneyl)Aryls and their applications
papers.abstract: This study introduces a novel method for the synthesis of 2-(tetrafluoro(1,2,2-trifluorovinyl)- λ6-sulfaneyl)Aryls, followed by an exploration of their applications. Specifically, (tetrafluoro(1,2,2-trifluorovinyl)- λ6-sulfaneyl)Aryls were synthesized from Aryl-SF4Cl via radical addition to trifluoroethylene in presence of 2,2'-Azobis(2,4-dimethylvaleronitrile) (ADVN) catalyst, followed by the elimination of HCl. Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this novel compound is demonstrated.

papers.title: Structure sensitive enantioselectivity on surfaces: tartaric acid decomposition on all surfaces vicinal to Cu(100)
A Heterobimetallic MnIIIFeIII Complex Reproduces the Enhanced C-O Bond Formation Reactivity of Biological MnFe Cofactors Over FeFe Analogs
papers.abstract: R2-like ligand-binding oxidase (R2lox) is a class of protein that contains a manganese–iron (MnFe) dinuclear cofactor. This heterobimetallic cofactor promotes a two-electron C–O coupling reaction between a tyrosine and a valine residue within the protein scaffold. Previous studies have shown that the MnFe form of R2lox is approximately four times more effective for oxidative C–O coupling than the FeFe variant; however, the origin of this reactivity difference remains poorly understood. To address this question, we developed a synthetic model complex with an Mn(III)Fe(III) center that closely mimics the first coordination sphere of the biological heterobimetallic cofactor. The Mn(III)Fe(III) oxo and the analogous Fe(III)Fe(III) oxo species are generated at −80 °C by oxidizing the corresponding Mn(II)Fe(II) precursor with hydrogen peroxide and are characterized by EPR, UV–vis, 57Fe Mössbauer, and resonance Raman spectroscopy. Despite the well-known inertness of dinuclear iron(III) and manganese(III) oxo species toward oxidative reactions, both Mn(III)Fe(III) and Fe(III)Fe(III) oxo species synthesized here can abstract hydrogen atoms from O–H substrates and promote catalytic C–O coupling of two phenol molecules. Importantly, the Mn(III)Fe(III) oxo model complex is more efficient at promoting C–O coupling than the Fe(III)Fe(III) analog, achieving turnover numbers (TONs) up to 14 times higher than the FeFe complex. Kinetic studies of oxidation reactions with a range of phenols suggest that the superior catalytic performance of the Mn(III)Fe(III) complex could be attributed to the greater contribution of electron transfer (ET) to the transition state of proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) relative to the FeIIIFeIII analog. The preference of MnFe over FeFe centers for activation of electron-rich O-H sites is consistent with the known functions of MnFe cofactors.

papers.title: Ligand backbone engineering enables pincer catalysts for highly efficient hydrogenation reactions
papers.abstract: Here, we report a new class of pincer catalysts featuring a piperidine backbone that exhibits exceptional activity and longevity in the hydrogenation of esters, amides, and polyesters. The catalysts achieve turnover numbers of up to 1 million for ester hydrogenation, 50,000 for amide hydrogenation, and 490,000 for polyester hydrogenation, including the depolymerisation of post-consumer PET waste (up to 100,000), representing the highest values reported for these transformations. Mechanistic studies indicate that the rigid piperidine backbone enhances both catalyst stability and the concentration of catalytically active meridional dihydride species. These findings establish a platform for the development of highly efficient hydrogenation catalysts.

papers.title: Implications for dinucleotide cofactor complexation as a novel mechanism of uranium chemical toxicity.
papers.abstract: Heavy metal exposure poses a significant risk to human health and the environment. Here, we report that uranyl ions (UO 2 2+ ), the soluble uranium species present upon dissociation in aqueous buffer, directly modify nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+/H), a critical cofactor in cellular metabolism. At equimolar concentrations, uranyl nitrate and NADH form an orange precipitant in the presence of an aqueous solution. Using 31P and 1D 1 H/ 13 C nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy on this mixture, we show that uranyl binding induces a dramatic downfield shift of the NADH phosphate signal—from –11.78 ppm in free NADH to values near 0 ppm—and promotes the formation of multiple adduct species. Cell free studies show that uranium (U) does not modulate the chemical reduction of the hydride-accepting C4 of NADH via sustained reduction of resazurin, suggesting that U-adduction is limited to the phosphoryl moieties. These findings suggest a novel mechanism of uranium-induced metabolic disruption whereby uranyl adduction of NADH exacerbates broad cellular dysfunction. Our study provides evidence for a Molecular Initiating Event (MIE) characterized by direct interaction of uranyl and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotides that impairs energy metabolism and helps explain bioenergetic dampening effects observed in uranium-exposure studies.

papers.title: Li+ dynamics in LiTa2PO8 probed by μ+SR
papers.abstract: Lithium tantalum phosphate (LiTa 2 PO 8 ) is among the fastest oxide Li + conductors, yet the relationship between the disordered Li + substructure and ion transport remains unclear owing to the coexistence of competing structural models and the lack of local experimental probes of Li + dynamics. Here, we combine powder neutron diffraction (PND), bond valence site energy (BVSE) calculations and muon spin relaxation (μ + SR) spectroscopy to establish a microscopic picture for Li + diffusion. Rietveld refinement of the structure using the PND data indicates that the Li + substructure is best described with two partially occupied sites, while BVSE identifies low-energy 1D diffusion channels that become interconnected to form a 3D percolating network. μ + SR reveals two thermally activated dynamical regimes, corresponding to localized Li + hopping at low temperatures and long-range diffusion above 210 K, with an activation energy of 0.300(25) eV. Combining the refined crystal structure with the μ + SR hopping rates yields a Li + self-diffusion coefficient of 5.4 × 10 -10 cm 2 s -1 at 290 K, thereby providing a unified structural and dynamical description of Li + transport in LiTa 2 PO 8 .

papers.title: Charge Dominates, Configuration Modulates: Lanthanide FrontierOrbital Energetics
papers.abstract: The 4f orbitals of lanthanides are shielded by filled 5s 2 5p 6 subshells, so that lanthanide–ligand bonding is often dominated by electrostatic interactions. Random forest models built from 31 composition-based descriptors, without any three-dimensional coordinates, predict the HOMO energies of 17,269 lanthanide complexes (LnQM, ωB97M-V/def2-SVPD) with a 5-fold cross-validation MAE of 0.159 eV (R 2 = 0.991), and total charge dominates feature importance (∼95%) in leave-one-element-out validation. A controlled comparison on 41,374 3d complexes (tmQM) shows markedly weaker charge dependence, consistent with a larger role of covalent interactions in 3d systems. Standard equivariant graph neural networks, untuned for this task, perform far worse than the composition-based model. The spin-resolved HOMO-LUMO gap reaches a minimum at Gd 3+ (f 7 ), a configuration-based analog of the gadolinium break, while absolute orbital energies remain electrostatically dominated.

papers.title: Shake it off: Abl kinase regulatory domain dynamics explain conformational changes upon activation
papers.abstract: Abl kinase is a major molecular target for chronic myeloid leukemia therapy. Its activity is tightly controlled by a regulatory module composed of the SH3 and SH2 domains and the SH2–kinase linker. Although the assembled autoinhibited and extended active conformations have been structurally characterized, the molecular pathway connecting these states remains poorly understood. Simulations initiated from the endpoint structures failed to sample the complete transition, even when Gaussian accelerated molecular dynamics (GaMD) was employed to enhance conformational sampling. To overcome this limitation, we combined multiscale modeling with extensive molecular dynamics simulations and Markov state modeling to reconstruct the Abl disassembly pathway. The resulting kinetic landscape revealed two coupled conformational equilibria: a faster exchange between the canonical assembled state and an intermediate ensemble that captures the initial rotation of the regulatory module, and a slower transition toward the extended state, characterized by migration of the regulatory module atop the kinase domain N-lobe. The canonical assembled autoinhibited state is strongly favored, accounting for approximately 60% of the equilibrium population, while early disassembly disrupts the E98-K294 and SH3-inker interactions and promotes exposure of Y226 and Y70. By revealing how these phosphorylation-sensitive residues become accessible during the earliest stages of disassembly, our model provides a mechanistic framework for Abl activation and identifies regulatory interfaces as potential targets for allosteric stabilization of the autoinhibited state.

papers.title: Synthesis, physical, chemical and biological properties of a M(CO)3 (M = Cr, Mo, W, Mn, Re) matched quintet
papers.abstract: A matched quintet bis-quinoline tricarbonyl complex was synthesized across Group 6/7 transition metals (M = Cr, Mo, W, Mn, Re). The complexes display trends in structure and bonding, observed by X-ray crystallography, NMR, Infrared, UV-Vis and fluorescence. Biological testing reveals high activity for Group 7 complexes against Gram-positive bacteria. Post-synthetic functionalisation with Click chemistry was explored.

papers.title: A spectral reset law explains and predicts periodic recurrence in the elements
papers.abstract: The recurrence of chemical properties is the defining feature of the periodic system, yet it is conventionally explained only indirectly, through inferred electron configurations and heuristic filling rules rather than being directly derived from atomic observables. Building on an empirical spectral framework in which elements occupy a bounded spectral space defined by two measured frequencies, the K-edge frequency (𝜈 max ) and the first ionization frequency (𝜈 ion ), we show that recurrence arises from simple quantitative constraints operating directly on these observables. As 𝜈 max increases across the elemental sequence, 𝜈 ion rises toward the upper boundary of the spectral space. At this limiting condition, a spectral mode bifurcates and 𝜈 ion undergoes a sharp reset toward a nearly invariant baseline, cancelling the accumulated rise to within 1%. Repetition of this rise–split–reset structure partitions spectral space into successive bounded intervals that emerge as periods, with lower and upper edges corresponding to elements conventionally classified as Groups 1 and 18, respectively. The rise–split–reset structure yields the recurrence 𝜈 ion (𝑛 + 1) = 𝜈 ion (𝑛) + Δ𝜈 ion (rise) − Δ𝜈 ion (reset) , with |Δ𝜈 ion | = 𝐴𝜈 𝑚𝑎𝑥 𝑏 , so that successive period anchors recur at the same relative position in spectral space. Across the four experimental period boundaries, reset magnitude scales linearly with the spectral splitting amplitude (𝑅 2 = 0.962), empirically linking the recurrence to the mode differentiation that establishes the periods. Seeded with a single measured value (lithium), the recursion regenerates the experimental G1 and G18 period anchors with a median error of 1.4%, and extrapolates beyond the known table to hypothetical periods 8 and 9, including element 119 at 𝜈 ion = (1.12 ± 0.33) × 10 15 s −1 (4.6 ± 1.4 eV). These results establish periodic recurrence as a quantitative, generative spectral structure in measurement space and show that ionization frequencies are not independent quantities, but are determined sequentially from a single seed and a pair of spectral scaling power laws with only two measured observables.

papers.title: Stable Phosphonate Inhibitors of Elastase LasB Suppress Pseudomonas aeruginosa Virulence via Zinc-Targeting Pyrrolidone Scaffolds
Engineering Receptor-Mediated Cell-Surface Mobility with Phage-Inspired DNA Tetrapods
papers.abstract: Viruses have long inspired the development of multiligand display systems that engage cell surface receptors through strong multivalent interactions. However, considerably less attention has been devoted to recapitulating the early stages of infection, during which weak, reversible interactions promote receptor-mediated mobility across cell membranes. Bacteriophages provide a striking example of this behavior, using transient receptor interactions to move across bacterial surfaces in search of favorable binding sites. Inspired by this mechanism, we developed DNA tetrapods targeting bacterial receptors exploited by phages during adsorption and demonstrate that phage-like lateral mobility on living bacterial cells can be achieved by tuning ligand affinity, valency, and spacer length. Furthermore, this platform can be extended to mammalian systems, where the tetrapod architecture similarly governs lateral motion and cell association, enabling selective cancer-cell recognition and improved antisense oligonucleotide uptake. Together, these findings demonstrate receptor-mediated mobility as a promising design principle for enhancing cellular targeting and cargo delivery.

papers.title: Introducing Redox-Active Residues to Enhance P450 Peroxygenase Performance
papers.abstract: P450 peroxygenases depend on the high-valent Iron-Oxo intermediate Compound I (Cpd I) to activate C–H bonds. However, the non-productive oxidative damage caused by Cpd I compromises enzyme stability and limits catalytic efficiency. Here, we report a rational protein engineering strategy to address this bottleneck by constructing additional “hole traps” on the enzyme surface. Guided by structural analysis, we introduced redox-active tyrosine/tryptophan residues at spatially defined positions on the surface of the P450BM3 F87A mutant. The optimal double mutant, M8 (F87A/L215W/H408W) significantly enhances turnover numbers (TONs) across a range of peroxide-driven hydroxylation reactions of aliphatic and aromatic substrates. Steady-state kinetics, reductant supplementation assays, and half-life measurements consistently indicated that the introduced Trp residues play a crucial protective role, improving both catalytic output and enzyme robustness. The crystal structure of M8 revealed that the mutations facilitate an expanded local network of π π interactions, forming efficient surface hole traps. Electrostatic potential calculations further showed a reduced potential near the engineered sites, consistent with a more favorable electron transfer gradient. These findings establish the rational construction of auxiliary hole traps as a novel and effective strategy to enhance P450 peroxygenase performance, offering potentially applicable for other heme and even broad oxidizing enzymes.

papers.title: FRIE: Machine Learning Models for Interfragment Interaction Energies among Amino Acid Residues Based on Quantum Mechanical Data from FMODB
papers.abstract: In recent years, quantum mechanical-based methods have offered superior accuracy for drug discovery; however, their high computational costs have limited their application in the late stages of molecular optimization. To overcome this efficiency bottleneck and enable rapid, large-scale structural biology assessments, in this study, we developed Fragment Regression Model for Interaction Energy (FRIE), a machine learning framework designed to predict interfragment interaction energies calculated using the fragment molecular orbital (FMO) method. This model focuses exclusively on interactions between amino acid residues within protein structures and establishes a robust baseline for macromolecular evaluation. Using the comprehensive FMO database named FMODB (https://drugdesign.riken.jp/FMODB/), we compiled a dataset comprising over 11 million amino acid residue pairs derived from 6,329 unique Protein Data Bank entries. Heavy atom distance matrices and formal charges were extracted as molecular explanatory descriptors to train and compare multiple machine learning algorithms. Among them, the Extra Trees Regressor model exhibited the highest predictive precision, achieving an average R 2 of 0.914 and an RMSE of 1.953 kcal/mol across 210 amino acid residue pairs. Furthermore, pair interaction energy decomposition analysis demonstrated that FRIE performed exceptionally well in predicting electrostatic interactions but encountered relatively greater difficulty with aromatic systems. Finally, external validation on AlphaFold2-predicted protein structures yielded high accuracy (R 2 ≥ 0.958), proving the model’s robustness and its potential for rapid evaluation of model structures, effectively bridging quantum chemical accuracy and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Solid-electrolyte interphase reactivity with the bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide anion governs cycling instabilities of sodium metal anodes
papers.abstract: Highly reversible and long-cycling Na metal anodes would enable Na-based batteries to approach energy densities competitive with established Li-ion technologies while leveraging earth-abundant materials. While several Na electrolytes have demonstrated impressive cyclability with Coulombic efficiency (CE) exceeding 99%, the number of high-performance electrolytes is lower, and designs are more restrictive, than counterpart Li systems to date. Meanwhile, design principles for high-performance Na electrolytes and their derived Solid Electrolyte Interphases (SEI) are less well established. Here, we examine factors that differentiate Na cyclability across different salts (1 M NaPF 6 , NaOTf, NaClO 4 , and NaFSI) in an exemplar class of primarily diglyme (G2) electrolytes. We first examine the hypothesis, commonly encountered in literature, that elevated Na SEI solubility compared to Li is a strong driver of CE. Upon conducting solubility measurements of sodium and lithium fluoride, carbonate, oxide, and methoxide ( i.e. MF, M 2 CO 3 , M 2 O, and MOCH 3 , with M = Na or Li) phases in neat solvent, we find that while solubilities are indeed elevated for Na SEI compared to Li SEI ( e.g. Na 2 O and Li 2 O in neat G2: 2.3×10 -4 M and 2.3×10 -5 M, respectively), the absolute solubility is expected to be exceedingly small in 1 M electrolytes (<10 -9 M) due to the common ion effect. However, one notable exception is (Na, Li)OCH 3 , which exhibits ~2–100 fold higher solubility than ionic SEI phases in neat G2 and orders of magnitude higher solubility than ionic phases in 1 M electrolytes. Looking beyond simple solubility as the mechanism for capacity loss, we find that OCH 3- is particularly reactive with the FSI anion via a nucleophilic substitution reaction that occurs readily at room temperature without a catalyst, producing FSI decomposition products that are detected in the cycled electrolyte by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and NaF in the SEI. Supported by the elevated solubility of methoxide, this pathway provides a continuous driving force for sustained SEI methoxide dissolution, its consumption over cycling, and SEI evolution towards a highly resistive interphase. Upon examining capacity loss partitioning across electrolyte systems, electronically isolated ‘dead’ Na 0 and NaF correlate negatively with CE, implicating FSI decomposition and NaF formation in irreversible Na loss and low CE.

papers.title: Molecular Origins of CO2 Capture Behavior in Amine-Appended Nanoporous Frameworks
papers.abstract: Amine-appended porous frameworks are leading materials for direct air capture of CO 2 . Yet the molecular origins governing CO 2 uptake within their dynamic porous environments remain poorly understood, limiting the design of next-generation frameworks. We selected covalent organic framework-999 (COF-999) as exemplar for investigating CO 2 uptake behavior using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations enabled by machine-learned interatomic potentials and enhanced sampling methods. Mapping the complex free-energy surfaces reveals pocket-like amine constructs which foster CO 2 chemisorption because hydrogen bonding within such pockets lowers activation barriers. We found that the population of active amines doubles under humid conditions because water molecules expand the amine pockets and in turn increase the number of hydrogen-bonding sites. This explains the puzzling experimental observation of doubling uptake in the presence of water. Our findings allow us to propose design principles for next-generation carbon capture materials.

papers.title: A Novel QSPR Workflow for Predicting Molecular Critical Properties: Balancing Accuracy, Applicability, and Explainability
papers.abstract: The critical point is the endpoint of the vapor–liquid coexistence curve of a pure substance and plays a key role in thermophysical property calculations. However, due to the limited availability of high-precision experimental data, most thermophysical property datasets are typically small. Their modeling faces challenges in terms of accuracy, applicability, and explainability. To address these issues, this work proposes a workflow for QSPR modeling of thermophysical properties by considering multiple aspects. The workflow uses RDKit, Mordred, and PubChemFP to calculate molecular 2D descriptors, and uses Gaussian to optimize molecular conformations and calculate molecular 3D descriptors. Based on these descriptors, Boruta-based multi-round feature selection combined with the EM algorithm is used to estimate and identify important features related to the modeling target. Appropriate models can then be selected for prediction. For critical properties modeling, the proposed approach achieves impressive test-set prediction AARDs of 2.31% for T c and 5.98% for P c . From the perspective of extrapolation, its accuracy is better than that of existing state-of-the-art machine learning models. Because molecular descriptors are used as modeling features, the model has better applicability than GNN models. The workflow further proposes the use of Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection combined with SHAP to identify and interpret relevant features for molecules in specific clusters. In addition, from a physical perspective, it proposes a strategy for the targeted improvement of the model, providing new insights into explainability. In the future, this workflow is expected to be extended to a wider range of thermophysical property modeling tasks and to provide a general framework for thermodynamic property prediction based on small datasets.

papers.title: An Integrated Workflow for Exosome Capture, Recognition-Guided Proximity Labeling of Surface Proteins, and Release
papers.abstract: Chemical modification of extracellular-vesicle surfaces provides molecular handles for vesicle analysis and functionalization, but conventional covalent labeling offers limited spatial control, whereas established proximity-labeling approaches commonly require genetically encoded catalysts. Here, we report a non-genetic strategy that uses molecular recognition to organize exosome capture, surface-proximal covalent labeling, and release within an integrated chemical workflow. Horseradish peroxidase conjugated to an anti-CD63 antibody or to the phosphatidylserine-binding protein Tim4 converted recognition at the vesicle surface into localized oxidative activation of externally supplied labeling reagents, enabling recognition-dependent biotin labeling. The reversible, Ca²⁺-dependent Tim4–phosphatidylserine interaction was then used to connect affinity capture and Tim4-guided labeling with EDTA-induced release of the labeled particles. This work demonstrates how reversible biomolecular recognition can coordinate separation, localized catalysis, and product recovery, providing a design framework for the chemical modification of nanoscale biological assemblies.

papers.title: Polyester (PET) Degradation in Mild-Alkaline Solutions Assisted by Ultrasonication and UV-Activated Metal Oxides
papers.abstract: The exponential and continuous growth in the production and consumption of plastics, particularly polyethylene terephthalate (PET), due to their versatile applicability, has led to the accumulation of persistent plastic waste in the environment. This has created an urgent need to develop more sustainable and efficient recycling technologies. Although several recycling methods, such as mechanical and chemical recycling, have been implemented on an industrial scale, existing technologies still do not fully recover PET to its original quality or rely heavily on hazardous chemicals at elevated operating conditions. In this study, we explored a greener approach for PET depolymerization through hydrolysis under milder conditions, enhanced by mechanochemical degradation via ultrasonication, and integrated with UV-assisted treatment using five heterogeneous catalysts (ZnO, ZnFe₂O₄, Fe₂O₃, Y₂O₃, and SrO). The results of this study proved the significance of the mechanochemical effect of ultrasonication, which enhanced PET degradation by promoting chain scission, achieving up to 21.5% PET conversion and 19.0% terephthalic acid (TPA) yield in 1M NaOH hydrolysis. Among the catalysts tested under 0.1M NaOH hydrolysis, SrO exhibited the highest catalytic performance due to the formation of Sr(OH)2, which provides additional hydroxide ions for ester bond cleavage. However, excessive SrO loading led to SrSO₄ precipitation during acidification, requiring additional purification of the TPA product.

papers.title: Cucurbit[8]uril Couples Enzymatic and Supramolecular Reaction Networks for Peptide Isomerization and Recognition in Gain-of-Function Hydrogels
papers.abstract: Adaptive biological systems regulate molecular recognition through enzymatic transformations that convert inactive precursors into functional states. Emulating such enzyme mediated gain-of-function behavior in synthetic supramolecular systems remains challenging because productive activation often competes with undesired deactivation pathways. Here, we report an enzyme-responsive depsipeptide switch in which Cucurbit[8]uril functions as a supramolecular chaperone, transiently stabilizing a latent peptide precursor against competing deactivation pathways and facilitating the productive enzymatic activation. The branched depsipeptide initially forms a weak binary complex with CB[8], slowing down hydrolysis and undesired intramolecular cyclization, thereby increasing the probability of trypsin-mediated transformation. Following proteolytic cleavage and spontaneous O→N acyl rearrangement, the depsipeptide is converted into a linear peptide that undergoes high affinity homoternary complexation with CB[8], resulting in a transition from binary to ternary supramolecular assembly. Time-resolved LC-MS, NMR spectroscopy, and isothermal titration calorimetry elucidate the competing activation and deactivation pathways and identify a tyrosine-containing depsipeptide that optimally balances hydrolytic stability with enzymatic responsiveness. Translation of this mechanism to hyaluronic acid conjugates enables enzyme-mediated supramolecular hydrogel reconfiguration through CB[8]-mediated intermolecular crosslinking, yielding adaptive materials with superior viscoelasticity and shear-thinning behavior. This work establishes a dynamic chaperone-assisted strategy for coupling enzymatic regulation with supramolecular molecular recognition and adaptive materials formation.

papers.title: Transient polarity amplification enables Markovnikov hydroamination with free alkyl amines
papers.abstract: Classical Markovnikov addition provides an atom-efficient blueprint for alkene hydrofunctionalization, but its reliance on electrophilic activation excludes strongly basic nucleophiles. Here we overcome this constraint by transiently amplifying alkene polarity. 15 Sequential reduction, selective protonation, and oxidation switch the alkene framework from nucleophilic to electrophilic, enabling Markovnikov C–N bond formation without sustained electrophilic activation. The reaction engages diverse primary and secondary alkyl amines and is amenable to chromatography-free preparative synthesis and downstream bond editing. Mechanistic experiments and calculations support this alkene-centered polarity switch.

papers.title: Faster Bacterial detection in dark using cyanotype-based photochemical reaction
papers.abstract: Rapid detection of metabolically active bacteria is important for the early detection of bacterial infections. However, it is considered by slow culture methods and costly molecular assays which is time taking process. People have used Cyanotype chemistry, based on Ferric ammonium citrate and potassium hexacyanoferrate forming Prussian blue sensitized with light for single-cell like bacterial detection, but its behaviour in complete darkness is unclear. Here, the incubation is done with E. coli DH5α cultures (10-2–10-10) mixed with classical cyanotype chemicals (potassium ferricyanide) under strictly dark conditions and monitored by OD700, UV–Vis spectra and visual inspection. Higher cell-density samples showed a clear yellow-to-blue transition (detectable in naked eyes) after ~14 hours and strong 680–720 nm absorbance, while controls did not show this transition. This study demonstrates a simple, low-cost, colour-based bacterial detection without external light.

papers.title: A small molecule inhibitor of the Staphylococcus aureus agr quorum sensing system with low-nanomolar potency
papers.abstract: The accessory gene regulator ( agr ) quorum sensing system regulates virulence in certain common Gram-positive bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus . Small molecules have been reported that block agr , but most have modest potencies and warrant further mechanistic characterization. Herein, we report a structure-function study on CP-20, a compound recently shown to inhibit agr in S. aureus by targeting the histidine kinase AgrC. We designed a robust new synthetic route to the CP-20 scaffold, generated a collection of CP-20 analogs, and evaluated their activities in cell-based agr reporter and phenotypic assays. These investigations led to the discovery of a compound, CP-20t, which inhibits agr in S. aureus with low-nanomolar potency and acts on AgrC. CP-20t represents, to our knowledge, the most potent small molecule inhibitor of agr known — bridging the almost 1000-fold potency gap between peptide- and small molecule-based inhibitors — and is a powerful tool to study quorum sensing in S. aureus .

papers.title: Inferring water’s liquid–liquid phase transition from two-state-point simulations with exponential Thermodynamic Maps
papers.abstract: The liquid-liquid phase transition (LLPT) in supercooled water has been recently explored using a range of techniques including molecular dynamics (MD) simulations performed at a fine-grained grid of conditions. Given that the phase transition depends sensitively on the choice of force field parametrization, often even using relatively expensive machine learning force fields, it is desirable to develop approaches where the LLPT attributes can be obtained in a data-austere manner. Specifically, we are interested in the possibibility of characterizing the LLPT using a limited number of simulations at thermodynamic state points far from the phase transition. We demonstrate this capability using a statistical physics and generative AI integrated approach named “exponential Thermodynamic Maps (expTM)”, which was previously shown to accurately predict the phase behavior of the Ising model and CO2. We propose a framework that learns from simulations at only two thermodynamic conditions, but predicts properties far away from these. We test the performance on three setups containing training data generated (i) at a fixed temperature with varying pressures, (ii) at a fixed pressure with varying temperatures, and (iii) different pressures and temperatures. We use expTM to predict density and local molecular arrangements to identify phases and characterize local water structure. Generated data recovers the density distribution, enabling accurate identification of the binodal curve, and remains reliable at temperatures above and pressures below the liquid-liquid critical point. It also reproduces the probability distribution and correlation of selected order parameters, capturing local structural environments rather than merely distinguishing phases. Together, these findings suggest that the complex phase transition behavior of supercooled water can be inferred from limited MD data using a generative model, substantially reducing the need for expensive simulations, in particular those using machine learned force fields.

papers.title: MolScrub: an open-source tool to generate conformers and protonate drug-like molecules
papers.abstract: We introduce MolScrub, an open-source Python-based tool to prepare drug-like molecules for structure-based simulations. MolScrub takes common molecular input specifications like SMILES, predicts the protonation states, and generates 3D structures. It is a high-throughput tool, having an average runtime of 0.3 to 0.5 seconds per molecule per CPU core. MolScrub returns as few protomers and conformers as reasonable to avoid feeding high-energy states to downstream simulations. Protonation state assignment includes both pKa prediction for acid-base pairs and tautomer enumeration. During 3D-coordinate generation, MolScrub enumerates 6-membered ring conformations to ensure that the final structure is close to a global minimum. These improved input geometries benefit docking programs that do not change the internal state of small rings. MolScrub was primarily developed to generate high-quality ligand structures to support docking-based virtual screenings but its modules (pKa prediction, tautomer enumeration, and ring geometry corrections) can be used and configured independently to support other applications.

papers.title: Cobalt Catalyzed Divergent Construction of Non-Adjacent Multiple Chiral Elements
papers.abstract: An enduring challenge in asymmetric catalysis is the precise control of remote, nonadjacent stereoelements. Herein, we report a cobalt/Salox-catalyzed enantioselective desymmetrization of aryl hydrazones with maleimides, providing a powerful platform for the simultaneous construction of distal quaternary stereocenters and axial chiral elements, both achieved with exceptional enantioselectivity. This sustainable protocol delivers an array of multi-chiral frameworks with cleavable directing group under mild conditions using air as the sole oxidant. Experimental and density functional theory studies elucidate the pathway, revealing that the C–H activation is both reversible and enantiodetermining step. The synthetic utility and versatility of this strategy are highlighted by facile scale-up, diverse product derivatizations, and streamline directing-group removal to access quaternary amine. Furthermore, the strategic deployment of a cleavable 2-(1-methylhydrazinyl)pyridine directing group provides a chemodivergent entry to challenging 1,3-nonadjacent frameworks, establishing concurrent central and remote C–N/N–N axial chirality with excellent stereocontrol.

papers.title: Dual-Channel Range-Separated Local Hybrid Functionals beyond the Zero-sum Game
papers.abstract: A dual-channel framework for range-separated local hybrid functionals (RS2LH framework) has been developed. It uses two local mixing functions (LMFs) for the coordinate-space mixing of semi-local and exact exchange-energy densities, one for the short-range, one for the long-range contributions. It is shown that previous range-separated local hybrids with strong-correlation corrections (scRSLH) can also be understood within this framework. As an intermediate step towards training of explicit RS2LH functionals with neural-network LMFs (n-LMFs), we start from an existing scRSLH, retain the human-designed Padé-form strong-correlation contributions but replace the human-designed t-LMF by an n-LMF. This gives the ωLH26nP functional, which in contrast to previous scRSLH functionals does not require a so-called calibration function to deal with the gauge ambiguity of exchange-energy densities. We then proceed to the first explicit RS2LH construction, ωLH26n, where both short-range and long-range LMFs are explicitly trained as neural networks on weak-and strong-correlation as well as fractional-charge training data. ωLH26nP and ωLH26n are evaluated on a wide range of data, including GMTKN55 and W4-17RE main-group energetics, organometallic transition-metal test sets, spin-restricted covalent bond dissociation as measure for strong correlations, but also on diverse quasiparticle energies, i.e., Koopmans-based computations of ionization potentials, electron affinities, and band gaps. Both RS2LH functionals perform well for many main-group energy benchmarks but show limited transferability to transition-metal energetics. While ωLH26nP also performs excellently for molecular quasiparticle energies comparable to previous RSLH functionals, the explicit ωLH26n RS2LH shows larger deviations. It is shown that the available energy data used currently for LMF training are good for the short-range LMF but insufficient for a full and stable training of the long-range LMF required to recover the correct asymptotic potential. Here the composite approach of ωLH26nP benefits from the pre-designed strong-correlation features and gives a more stable long-range LMF suitable also for quasiparticle energies. The deep-neural-network DM21 functional exhibits even larger deviations for quasiparticle energies than ωLH26n. Analyses strongly suggest that fractionalcharge data alone are insufficient to enforce the correct asymptotic potential and that quasiparticle-energy data should be included in the training of highly flexible functionals for which the correct behavior is not built into their physical structure.

papers.title: Chirality-Aware Molecular Learning via Complex-Valued Representations Inspired by Circular Polarization
papers.abstract: Molecular chirality requires stereochemical representations for molecular graph learning. Inspired by the connection between circular polarization and molecular stereochemistry, we propose a complex-valued message passing neural network that encodes molecular features as magnitude–phase representations and captures stereochemical differences around chiral centres. The model improves molecular property prediction, particularly chirality-sensitive chromatography.

papers.title: Guest-guest interactions and their impact on molecular mobility: a simulation study of 5-fluorouracil adsorption and diffusion in hydrophobic zeolites
papers.abstract: Zeolites have been proposed as carrier materials for the storage and controlled release of the anticancer drug 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). Containing both hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor groups, 5-FU molecules can form relatively strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Prior work on zeolite beta has shown that guest-guest interaction between co-adsorbed 5-FU molecules reduce their diffusivity at high loadings. However, a systematic assessment of the influence of 5-FU oligomer size and zeolite pore topology is so far lacking. Aiming to fill this gap, the present study employs atomistic simulations at different levels of theory to elucidate the strength of 5-FU−5-FU interactions as well as their impact on diffusion in all-silica zeolites. In the first part, adsorption energies of 5-FU oligomers in four zeolites (FAU, BEA, MOR, MFI frameworks) are computed with dispersion-corrected density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In all four zeolites, 5-FU dimers are considerably more stable than individual 5-FU molecules due to attractive guest-guest interactions. However, an additional stabilisation of larger oligomers is prominent only for FAU, where the large supercages impose less constraints on molecular orientation compared to zeolites with channel-type pores. In the second part, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with classical force fields are used to investigate the diffusion of 5-FU in zeolites FAU and MOR. For single molecules, the computed self-diffusion coefficients are on the order of 1 to 2∙10 −9 m 2 /s for both frameworks. Dimers and larger oligomers diffuse more slowly. While 5-FU dimers and trimers remain mobile in MOR, trimers and especially tetramers in FAU become nearly immobile on the nanosecond timescale. These findings highlight that the diffusion of molecules that can form strong hydrogen bonds can be significantly impeded by attractive guest-guest interactions, even at very low loadings. Besides, the low mobility of larger 5-FU oligomers could indicate that kinetic effects are responsible for the large discrepancy between experimentally reported 5-FU uptakes in FAU-type zeolites and theoretical predictions.

papers.title: Accelerated screening of diamines for polyamide synthesis
papers.abstract: Biobased polyamides offer an attractive route to more sustainable plastics, but identifying monomer combinations that yield targeted polymer properties remains challenging. Here, we screened diamines to identify monomers that enhance the thermal stability of polyamides synthesized from dimethyl furan-2,5-dicarboxylate. We described 38 commercially available diamines using molecular descriptors and transformed them into a low-dimensional latent representation that captured dominant diversity in diamine structure, size, flexibility, hydrophobicity and cyclicity. We systematically selected a representative subset of nine diamines for polyamide synthesis and regressed measured polyamide properties against the latent embeddings. The resulting regression models predicted thermal degradation onset and 5% mass-loss temperatures with mean validation errors of 14-25 °C for independent polyamides. Model interpretation indicated that higher degradation onset temperatures were associated with larger, more flexible and more hydrocarbon-rich diamines with reduced cyclicity and hydrogen-bonding capacity. Guided by these predictions we prepared polyamide films and found that a dodecane-1,12-diamine-based polyamide with higher thermal stability formed a self-standing transparent film with low water wettability, whereas a 1,2-cyclohexane-based polyamide with one of the lowest predicted stabilities formed a yellowish, fragile film with near-complete wetting. These results demonstrate how latent molecular representations can guide diamine selection and the design of biobased polyamides with targeted thermal and film-forming properties. Our approach can be used in other polymer synthesis problems where molecular descriptors can be linked to target properties.

papers.title: Divinyl-s-tetrazine as a Minimal Linchpin for Peptide Stapling, Protein Disulfide Re-bridging and Click Functionalisation
papers.abstract: Site-selective bridging of cysteines and native disulfide bonds represents a powerful strategy for peptide and protein modification. However, most existing bis-electrophilic reagents rely on azide-alkyne cycloadditions for downstream modifications. In contrast, inverse-electron-demand Diels-Alder (IEDDA) reactions of s-tetrazines have emerged as a powerful tool in bioconjugation. Here, we report divinyl-s-tetrazine (DvTz) as a minimal linchpin in which the electron-deficient tetrazine core simultaneously activates the vinyl groups as electrophilic Michael acceptors for rapid cysteine conjugation, while also serving as a bioorthogonal handle for subsequent IEDDA ligation. DvTz enables rapid, high-yielding cysteine-selective stapling of unprotected peptides across all twenty canonical amino acids. A broad range of peptide lengths, sequence compositions and stapling distances were also demonstrated. A one-pot stapling and IEDDA sequence was also established without intermediate purification. This technology was further extended to antibody Fab fragments, achieving site-specific disulfide re-bridging and subsequent IEDDA ligation across three distinct Fab proteins, with exclusive formation of singly conjugated species and fully preserved antigen-binding activity. Collectively, this work establishes DvTz as an efficient and simple linchpin for peptide and protein modification and bioconjugation.

papers.title: Mn-Driven Ferromagnetism and Electronic Correlations in Multiferroic Bi5Ti3MnO15 from First Principles
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive first-principles study of the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of the multiferroic Aurivillius phase Bi5Ti3MnO15. Among ten symmetry-inequivalent configurations arising from distinct distributions of Mn3+ across the perovskite B sites, we find a clear energetic preference for inner-site occupancy, consistent with recent experimental observations in related Aurivillius systems. A detailed investigation of the magnetic ground states of these symmetrically inequivalent configurations shows strong ferromagnetic coupling between nearestneighbor Mn3+ cations, driven by superexchange interactions, while interactions between more distant neighbors are significantly weaker. Using Heisenberg exchange parameters extracted from Green’s function calculations, we estimate a Curie temperature for the energetically most stable structure of approximately 300 K within the mean-field approximation. We further demonstrate that the ferromagnetic ground state in these systems is governed by the splitting of Mn t2g and eg orbitals, which is modulated by the Jahn–Teller distortions of the MnO6 octahedra. Explicit inclusion of Hund’s coupling reveals its important role in determining orbital occupation within the Mn-3d orbital manifold, and influencing the competition between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions. These results establish a unified microscopic picture linking Mn site preference, octahedral distortion, and intraorbital exchange to room-temperature ferromagnetism in Aurivillius multiferroics Bi5Ti3MnO15.

papers.title: Regulation of the Enzymatic Activity of a Condensing Amidohydrolase by Organic Solvents
papers.abstract: Biocatalysis in non-aqueous environments offers great opportunities for industrial applications since organic solvents can enhance substrate solubility, tune enzymatic chemo-, regio-and enantioselectivity, exert thermodynamic control and facilitate product recovery. However, understanding enzyme behavior across solvents remains challenging. The amidohydrolase NatAM is part of a biosynthetic cascade producing benzoxazoles, which are important building blocks of pharmaceutical drugs. Therefore, finding non-aqueous media preserving or even improving the enzyme’s operability while facilitating product removal becomes increasingly important. Our experiments show that the enzymatic activity of NatAM is influenced by organic solvents and that this effect depends more on the physicochemical properties of the solvent than on its concentration in aqueous mixtures. The analysis of extensive, full atomistic biomolecular simulations delivers a mechanistic foundation of the differential effect of the organic solvents on the catalytic activity of NatAM, determined by active site volume and hydration. Our work thus paves the way for future liquid media engineering efforts using organic solvents with minimal water-content.

papers.title: Heteroaromatic Sulfonyl Chlorides and Fluorides Bearing Carbonyl/Carboxylate Moieties: Bifunctional Building Blocks for Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Heteroaromatic sulfonyl halides bearing a free carboxylic acid, ester, aldehyde, or methyl ketone group were prepared for a series of heterocycles (pyridine, pyrazine, imidazole, pyrazole, oxazole, and thiazole). The synthetic scheme involved elaboration of the carboxylate/carbonyl handle on a hetaryl thioether intermediate, obtained by S N Ar or Pd-catalyzed thiolation, and the sulfur was oxidized to the corresponding sulfonyl halide only at the final step. The title products were obtained on up to 40 g scale in a single run. The stability of sulfonyl chlorides depended on the position of the sulfonyl group relative to the ring nitrogen and on the electronic nature of the additional functional group, free carboxylic acids being more demanding than the corresponding esters and aldehydes than carboxylic acids. For the labile cases, sulfonyl fluorides were obtained by KHF 2 halogen exchange or by a one-pot sequence bypassing isolation of the chloride; in addition, a set of primary sulfonamide building blocks bearing a free COOH group was prepared. Both organosulfur and carbonyl-containing handles were addressed chemoselectively under conditions compatible with parallel chemistry, and a virtual library enumerated from these transformations showed good compliance with drug- and lead-likeness criteria.

papers.title: Peptide Amphiphile-based Organelles for Fueled Synthetic Cells
papers.abstract: The bottom-up synthesis of life aims to replicate the characteristics of natural living systems from basic abiotic building blocks. In this context, synthetic cells based on liquid-liquid phase separation, such as complex coacervate droplets, have gained attention because they form spontaneously and readily take up molecules from their environment. More recently, we introduced fuel-dependent synthetic cells—coacervates that require fuel to form and decay unless periodically fueled. These synthetic cells are therefore under selection pressure to survive until the next fueling cycle. However, whereas natural cells rely on internal sub-compartments, complex coacervates typically lack structural heterogeneity. Here, we show that peptide amphiphiles can be activated in situ to generate discrete, phase-separated structures within complex coacervates. A chemically orthogonal stimulus enables spatiotemporal control over peptide assembly without disrupting fuel-driven phase separation. We further identify a reciprocal relationship: peptide assemblies alter the physical properties of the coacervate matrix, while the host compartment directs peptide morphology and assembly kinetics. These hierarchical assemblies function as artificial organelles within fueled synthetic cells. Together, they provide a strategy for integrating orthogonal supramolecular assembly with chemically fueled synthetic cells, enabling internal sub-compartmentalization, enhanced kinetic stability, and programmable morphology.

papers.title: Conformational Control of Substrate Selectivity in Benzoxazole-Forming Amidohydrolases
papers.abstract: Benzoxazoles are key heteroaromatic motifs found in pharmaceuticals, bioactive natural products, and synthetic lead structures. However, complex benzoxazole derivatives, such as bis(benzoxazoles), are challenging to produce using conventional chemical synthesis. Alternatively, biosynthetic pathways represent a promising platform for the production of structurally complex heterocycles, frequently under mild and potentially more sustainable conditions. Furthermore, the substrate flexibility of these pathways allows generating derivatives beyond their native products. Yet, the enormous potential of biosynthetic pathways is often hindered by the insufficient understanding of the principles governing substrate selectivity. Here, we investigated AMP ligase–amidohydrolase cascades as biocatalytic platforms for benzoxazole formation. Furthermore, by combining biochemical experiments with extensive molecular dynamics simulations, we established molecular determinants of substrate flexibility. Specifically, reconstitution of the closoxazole pathway from Clostridium cavendishii established a biocatalytic route for the direct assembly of the structurally complex bis(benzoxazole) closoxazole G from 3-amino-4hydroxybenzoic acid, both in vitro and in vivo. Systematic substrate profiling of the AMP ligases and amidohydrolases from three different pathways further demonstrated substantial flexibility toward substituted aromatic carboxylic acids, including halogenated derivatives. The combination of experiments, which showed preferential conversion of reactive ester intermediates in vitro, and the analysis of the simulations identified three main factors that govern substrate conversion: population of catalytically competent conformations, water accessibility and active-site interaction networks. Together, our results provide a mechanistic foundation for engineering enzyme cascades toward non-native and synthetically challenging benzoxazole architectures.

papers.title: Overlooked impacts of ball milling on the structure of Li3PS4-Li2S cathode composite
papers.abstract: Ball milling is a generic and effective way of grinding powder into fine particles. It has been widely used in the preparation of cathode composites for all-solid-state batteries as it can enhance particle contacts within cathode composites and hence improve battery performance. However, the effects of ball milling on the structure of cathode composites are overlooked. In this paper, we report investigations on how ball milling affects the structure of Li3PS4-Li2S cathode composites using solid-state 31P NMR spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction. Two cathode composites are compared, i.e., glassy Li3PS4-Li2S and β-Li3PS4-Li2S mixtures. 31P NMR spectra show that ball milling does not influence the structure of glassy Li3PS4, while the structure of β-Li3PS4 has changed significantly due to ball milling. Quantitative analysis of 31P NMR spectra indicates that more than 50 at% of β-Li3PS4 is converted into glassy Li3PS4 after the ball milling process. Interestingly, no obvious difference is observed regarding Li ion exchange within the two composites. We demonstrate that glassy Li3PS4 appears to be more resistant than β-Li3PS4 against ball milling. These results suggest that parameters related to ball milling, such as milling time,

papers.title: Bio-inspired Manganese-catalyzed Aromatic C–H Hydroxylation leads to an Intramolecular C(sp2)–C(sp2) Coupling Reaction: A Product Inhibition Study in Aromatic Hydroxylation
papers.abstract: The C–H hydroxylation of aromatic substrates with hydrogen peroxide to form phenol products catalyzed by bio-inspired manganese complexes 1a and 1b in fluorinated solvents has been recently studied in our group. The incorporation of bulky TIPS groups into the amino-pyridine ligand was found to favor aromatic C–H hydroxylation and overall catalytic efficiency for 1b over 1a. It was proposed that non-bulky complex 1a suffers from product inhibition due to phenolate binding to the manganese center, while this effect is less prominent for bulky complex 1b. In this work, we have investigated the origin of product inhibition and explained the lower activity of 1a using various spectroscopies, including UV-Vis and highresolution MS (HRMS). HRMS analysis showed the formation of manganese phenolate complexes and other manganese complexes during catalysis for the non-bulky as well as bulky complexes. HRMS also revealed the formation of a manganese-(2,2’-bi(parapropylphenolate)) species in which manganese has a high-valent +4 oxidation state. Catalytic experiments using independently synthesized manganese(II)-(bis(phenolate)) complexes 2c and 2d, demonstrated that these are catalytically active, whereas manganese(II)(2,2’biphenolate) complex 2e is not. Additionally, its VisPD spectrum points out that the high-valent [manganese(IV)(tipsbpmcn)(2,2’-bi(para-propylphenolate))]2+ species is responsible for the deep greenish-purple observed during catalysis. Overall, this work presents new insights into the mechanism of product inhibition in aromatic hydroxylation by bio-inspired manganese complexes through an ortho-ortho coupling pathway, which will aid further catalyst development.

papers.title: Metabolic Competition Reshapes the Performance of Engineered Polyketide Synthases
papers.abstract: Directed evolution is widely used to enhance enzymatic performance and evolve new-to-nature reactivities, typically in vitro or in model microbial systems. However, variants selected in a model host may not retain their relative performance in the intended production organism. Here, we engineered a single 2-pyrone synthase (2PS) scaffold by directed evolution in Escherichia coli ( E. coli ) and evaluated the resulting variants in both E. coli and planta. In E. coli, engineered 2PS variants showed distinct chemoselectivities, giving access to precursors for kavalactones and raspberry ketone from one protein scaffold. The best variant achieved >98% conversion of p -coumaric acid to >200 µg/mL bisnoryangonin. In planta, however, variant performance was reordered: the top-performing microbial variant was outperformed 2.7-fold by one with lower activity in E. coli . We traced this host-dependent shift to competition for the shared p -coumaroyl-CoA pool and identified cinnamoyl-CoA reductase from Nicotiana benthamiana ( Nb CCR) as a key competing enzyme. Introducing Nb CCR into E. coli recapitulated the variant rank order observed in planta, demonstrating that metabolic competition can reshape the performance of engineered enzymes across hosts. These results also suggest that reconstructing key competing pathways of the target host in a tractable microbial system can provide a practical strategy for engineering enzymes for otherwise difficult-to-evolve production hosts. Finally, 2PS variants enabled the chemoenzymatic synthesis of natural and fluorinated kavalactones with up to 64% isolated yield over two steps.

papers.title: Human exposome toxicity is driven by key toxicants following a Pareto law
papers.abstract: Humans are exposed to complex mixtures of environmental chemicals, raising two questions: how many chemicals may elicit toxicity at realistic exposure levels, and whether toxicity is driven by the mixture effects of numerous chemicals. Here, we propose a probabilistic model addressing both questions using large-scale chemical–protein interaction data from affinity selection mass spectrometry. Across 3.51 million interactions from 407,271 compounds and 110 human proteins, we observe a log-log relationship between binding probability and binding affinity. This model predicts that human toxicity is dominated by a small number (~100) of potent chemicals and their analogues under a Pareto law, rather than by the cumulative contributions of numerous weak compounds. These findings challenge the long-standing emphasis on mixture effects and instead support a ‘key driver’ hypothesis.

papers.title: Discovery of Novel Bis-arylamidines with Potent Activity Against Clinically Important Molds and Yeasts
papers.abstract: Pathogenic fungi represent an expanding threat to public health, and yet resistance to current antifungals is surging due to the longstanding use of drugs with limited target diversity. T2307 is a promising bis-arylamidine (BARA) antifungal with novel target specificity, broad-spectrum activity, and low toxicity, but the clinical development of which was discontinued after Phase I trials. To further advance the therapeutic development of this promising class of compounds, we designed and synthesized BARA analogues and systematically evaluated their antifungal activity against clinically important and drug-resistant strains of two very different classes of fungi: Candida and Aspergillus . Many analogues showed potency comparable to or exceeding that of T2307 , and somewhat divergent structure–activity relationships (SARs) observed between Candida and Aspergillus provide useful insights into the molecular mechanisms for efficacy of the drugs . For example, compounds Z3, Z15, and Z17 were the most active against Candida spp. , whereas Z4 – Z6 and Z14 showed the best activity against Aspergillus strains. Spermine/spermidine competition experiments support that these compounds share a carrier-mediated uptake pathway with T2307 . The leading anti-yeast and anti-mold analogues exhibited a favorable safety profile and ADME properties and robust pharmacokinetic behavior, supporting the potential of BARAs as drug candidates suitable for further development of selective, broad-spectrum antifungal agents.

papers.title: Rebooting Cyclobutadienes – Regiodivergent Functionalizations of Cyclobutadiene-Iron Complexes
papers.abstract: De novo design of cyclobutadiene-iron (CBD-Fe) complexes has allowed for the synthesis of new libraries of fourmembered building blocks. The use of tetramethylpiperidinyllithium bases (TMP-Li) allows for smooth, yet highly selective metalation of those CBD-Fe complexes, providing efficient and unprecedented access to trisubstituted architectures. Perfect control of the regiochemical outcome was achieved by fine tuning of the nature of substituents, applying steric, coordinating and electronic effects during the metalation step.

papers.title: Li+ dynamics in LiTa2PO8 probed by μ+SR
papers.abstract: Lithium tantalum phosphate (LiTa 2 PO 8 ) is among the fastest oxide Li + conductors, yet the relationship between the disordered Li + substructure and ion transport remains unclear owing to the coexistence of competing structural models and the lack of local experimental probes of Li + dynamics. Here, we combine powder neutron diffraction (PND), bond valence site energy (BVSE) calculations and muon spin relaxation (μ + SR) spectroscopy to establish a microscopic picture for Li + diffusion. Rietveld refinement of the structure using the PND data indicates that the Li + substructure is best described with two partially occupied sites, while BVSE identifies low-energy 1D diffusion channels that become interconnected to form a 3D percolating network. μ + SR reveals two thermally activated dynamical regimes, corresponding to localized Li + hopping at low temperatures and long-range diffusion above 210 K, with an activation energy of 0.300(25) eV. Combining the refined crystal structure with the μ + SR hopping rates yields a Li + self-diffusion coefficient of 5.4 × 10 -10 cm 2 s -1 at 290 K, thereby providing a unified structural and dynamical description of Li + transport in LiTa 2 PO 8 .

papers.title: Stabilizing lattice oxygen in RuO2 with high-valent 5d Re dopants for durable acidic water electrolysis
papers.abstract: The limited durability of Ru-based electrocatalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a significant challenge for their application in water electrolyzers. This instability arises from a coupled failure mode in which lattice-oxygen participation promotes oxygen-vacancy formation, Ru over-oxidation, soluble ruthenate species, and structural collapse. Herein, we use high-valent 5d transition-metal dopants as a compact platform to tune Ru-O covalency and Ru redox stability, taking advantage of their spatially extended d orbitals, large ionic radii, and accessible high oxidation states. Comparative studies of Ta-, W-, Re-, and Os-doped RuO2 suggest that different 5d dopants emphasize different stabilization roles: Ta is associated with attenuated lattice-oxygen reactivity, W underscores suboptimal Ru−O covalency, Os highlights the importance of redox buffering, and Re provides the most balanced combination of lattice-oxygen stabilization and Ru-valence regulation in our material series. Operando differential electrochemical mass spectroscopy, X-ray spectroscopy, electrochemical analysis, and theoretical calculations show that Re expands the RuO2 lattice, weakens Ru-O covalency, suppresses latticeoxygen participation, and dynamically regulates Ru valence under OER conditions. Re-RuO2 consequently achieves an overpotential of 138 mV at 10 mA cm-2, stable operation for >700 h at 200 mA cm-2 with reduced Ru dissolution, and >300 h operation in a PEMWE device at 1 A cm-2 with a negligible degradation rate of 69 μV h-1. These results establish a 5d-dopant design principle for RuO2: durable acidic OER requires simultaneous control of lattice oxygen and Ru overoxidation.

papers.title: Understanding Reporting Variability in Fire Debris Data Interpretation through an Interlaboratory Study
papers.abstract: 2 Highlights • Fire debris analysis reporting variability captured through an interlaboratory study. • Responses received from 78 participants spanning 52 laboratories and 14 countries. • Lowest response variability observed for samples that did not contain a substrate. • Highest response variability observed for samples containing a low-volume IL. • Substrate and IL volume had the largest effects on variability and certainty. 3 Abstract Fire debris analysis remains one of the most commonly requested trace evidence analyses. To determine the presence of an ignitable liquid in a sample, an examiner must manually interpret complex chromatographic and mass spectrometric data, making determinations based on available reference data, comparison samples, and guidance provided in documentary standards (namely ASTM E1618-19) or laboratory-specific protocols. Due to the generally subjective nature of these analyses, an interlaboratory study was conducted to investigate the variability in interpretation and reporting of fire debris data. Through this study, a group of 78 practicing fire debris examiners were provided with sets of 10 datafiles of varying complexities for analysis. Participants were asked to determine whether an ignitable liquid was present and, if so, what type, or class, it was. Regardless of the complexity of the sample, or the class of ignitable liquid present, variability in the determination of the presence of an ignitable liquid and its associated class was observed. Participants were found to have the lowest variability when analyzing data from samples with no substrate interference and samples where the dominant profile was an n-alkane product. Variability in reporting increased for samples containing substrate signatures and samples where the ignitable liquid was not a petroleum distillate product, an n-alkane product, or gasoline. This study provides insight into the variability of reporting fire debris results and can serve as an important benchmark to compare against after the adoption of new fire debris interpretation standards (ASTM E1618-25 and E3407-25).

papers.title: Multilayer Multistate Reaction Coordinate Model for Nonadiabatic Dynamics in Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Simulating nonadiabatic quantum dynamics in complex condensed-phase systems is computationally challenging due to the high dimensionality of the nuclear environment. To address this, we introduce the multilayer multistate reaction coordinate (ML-MRC) model, a general hierarchical transformation of the multistate harmonic (MSH) Hamiltonian that maps the complex bath into a structured chain of collective modes. We demonstrate that the ML-MRC framework allows the MSH model to be reformulated into hierarchies of arbitrary depth, from single-layer reaction coordinates to full-chain representations, while maintaining rigorous mathematical equivalence. This flexibility is validated across diverse physical systems, including the spin-boson model, the Frenkel exciton model for the photosynthetic light-harvesting Fenna-Matthews-Olson complex, and a realistic photoinduced charge transfer model for a carotenoid-porphyrin-fullerene triad in tetrahydrofuran. Furthermore, this hierarchical structure enables a robust dimensionality reduction strategy, where truncating the chain yields low-dimensional effective Hamiltonians that accurately reproduce the nonadiabatic dynamics of the untruncated model at a reduced computational cost. Finally, the ML-MRC model reveals valuable mechanistic insights through reaction coordinate trajectories, which are shown to synchronize remarkably with electronic population dynamics across multiple systems.

papers.title: Mild Photochemical Conditions Accesses Diverse Fluoroalkyl Arenes
papers.abstract: Fluoroalkyl arenes, particularly trifluoromethyl-substituted arenes, are valuable motifs in pharmaceuticals and materials but are challenging to synthesize due to harsh conditions and limited substrate scope in existing methods. Here we report a deoxyfluoroalkylation-aromatization sequence employing photoexcited 3*[DDQ] under mild conditions (35 °C, visible light irradiation), enabling efficient conversion of cyclohexan(en)ones to highly substituted fluoroalkyl arenes. This photochemical approach significantly broadens functional group tolerance and improves yields compared to prior thermal methods requiring high temperatures (120–140 °C) and the use of stoichiometric acid. The methodology accommodates diverse substrates, including heterocycles and acid-sensitive groups, and is scalable to decagram quantities. These findings provide a versatile and milder synthetic route to access complex fluoroalkyl arenes, facilitating their incorporation into advanced molecular architectures.

papers.title: Vertical Excitation Energies in Solution via a Two-Time-Scale Solvation Model Coupled to Pair-Density Functional Theory
papers.abstract: Accurately describing electronically excited states in solution requires both a multiconfigurational treatment of the solute and an efficient account of solvent effects. Multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory (MC-PDFT) and its multi-state, linearized extension (L-PDFT) can recover correlation beyond state-averaged complete active space self-consistent field theory (SA-CASSCF) at a fraction of the cost of multireference perturbation theory (e.g. CASPT2) or multireference configuration interaction. Here we combine MC-PDFT and L-PDFT with a nonequilibrium-treatment of the electrostatic solvation effect using the solvation model based on density (SMD). The resulting models are called MC-NSCRF-PDFT and L-NSCRF-PDFT, where NSCRF denotes the key state-specific excited-state nonequilibrium self-consistent reaction field step. We apply the new models to the solvatochromic shifts of the lowest valence excitations of formaldehyde, acetone, acrolein, and methylenecyclopropene and to the aqueous shifts of the lowest π → π∗ and n → π∗ transitions of cytosine. For vertical excitation energies in solution, MC-NSCRF-PDFT and L-NSCRF-PDFT give results that are in agreement with the far-more-expensive NSCRF model based on multistate CASPT2. These results establish MC-NSCRF-PDFT and L-NSCRF-PDFT as accurate and computationally efficient tools for electronic excitation energies in the condensed phase.

papers.title: Inversion for Solid Electrolytes with Single-Relaxation Dynamics: A Physics-Informed, Robust, and Automated Framework
papers.abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is a core technique for revealing the internal kinetic mechanisms of advanced battery materials. However, traditional equivalent circuit fitting incurs high time costs and subjective bias, while existing automated algorithms—lacking rigorous physical constraints—often yield non-physical results under complex real-world scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a physics-informed, high-throughput automated EIS analysis framework. The framework achieves a fully automated workflow by integrating physics-constrained preprocessing, geometric prior-guided circuit model selection, and a progressive joint fitting algorithm that autonomously generates reliable initial values. We validated the framework using synthetic datasets with controlled noise/artifacts and temperature-resolved EIS datasets of a polymer solid electrolyte. Simulations demonstrate the framework’s stability under artifact-coupled polarization scenarios, achieving < 2% relative errors in key parameter extraction with closed-form initialization. In real wide-temperature sequences, the framework successfully extracted intrinsic responses from EIS, accommodating impedance variations spanning several orders of magnitude. Furthermore, it identified macroscopic phase transition boundaries and achieved accurate inversion of both thermodynamic and kinetic parameters. Ultimately, this study provides a standardized 2 batch-analysis solution for the impedance spectra of polymer and inorganic amorphous ionic conductors in blocking electrode systems. By mitigating subjective errors, it offers reliable algorithmic support for the high-throughput evaluation and automated discovery of novel solid-state energy storage materials.

papers.title: Wastewater Treatment Plants as Anchor Infrastructure for Geothermal Energy in Cold Regions
papers.abstract: Thermal constraints in cold regions suppress biological treatment, increase energy demand, and elevate greenhouse gas emissions of existing wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), and remain a major barrier to the deployment of adequate sanitation infrastructure in many cold-region communities. Where geothermal resources exist, low-enthalpy hydrothermal heat is well matched to this energy gap. Yet, WWTPs are underrecognized anchors for broader geothermal deployment. We reframe geothermal-WWTP integration as a system-level enabler that benefits both parts. Using three cascaded configurations for a full-scale WWTP, a rapid techno-economic analysis identifies three trends: energy and carbon savings/revenues alone are insufficient under realistic policy stacks, whereas crediting the upgrade-deferral value of geothermally enhanced treatment makes the project economically favourable across most policy scenarios. The opportunity is greatest in cold, remote, and underserved communities, where local geothermal resources, treatment intensification, and community-scale demand together carry a case that no single driver could sustain alone.

papers.title: Chemical Descriptors as Bases and Metrics across Interpolation and Unseen-Element Transfer
papers.abstract: Chemical descriptors determine both the effect functions a model can express and the chemical levels across which it shares information. On complete perovskite and protein grids, we separate these roles as the rank and geometry of a common kernel: free categorical effects with a descriptor metric remove basis error, while the ratio of observed compositions to identified parameters, n/p, predicts where regularisation is most valuable. Holding an element out entirely exposes a second information limit: semiparametric transfer succeeds for smooth formation-energy and volume fields, whereas magnetic error concentrates in context-dependent A × X state variation. Target-free electronic probes reduce error from 0.7095 to 0.6523, and their per-element gain tracks the increase in outer-training state support (ρ = 0.475). These results define a two-axis design rule: use n/p to choose regularisation for represented levels and context-conditioned state support to evaluate representations for unseen-level transfer.

papers.title: Structural Diversification of PRE-084-Derived 2-Morpholinoethyl-1-Arylcyclohexane-1-Carboxylates Reveals Distinct Mitochondrial Membrane Potential Phenotypes
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm) is a key indicator of mitochondrial function and cellular bioenergetic status. Although amphiphilic small molecules can influence ΔΨm, the extent to which structural modification within a defined chemical scaffold alters mitochondrial response remains incompletely understood. In the present study, a focused series of 2-morpholinoethyl-1-arylcyclohexane-1-carboxylate analogues was synthesized using the Sigma-1 receptor ligand PRE-084 as a reference scaffold and evaluated for their effects on ΔΨm in U87-MG glioblastoma cells. Mitochondrial membrane potential was assessed using JC-1 flow cytometry, and ΔΨm was expressed as the normalized red/green fluorescence ratio relative to vehicle-treated controls. Compounds were evaluated at 1, 10, and 100 µM to investigate concentration-dependent response profiles. Structural diversification of the scaffold generated distinct mitochondrial phenotypes, including depolarization-like, hyperpolarization-like, near-neutral, and biphasic responses. PRE-084and several analogues were associated with reduced ΔΨm relative to vehicle controls, indicating depolarization-like behavior. In contrast, PIR-129 and PIR-131 produced concentration-dependent increases in ΔΨm, exhibiting hyperpolarization-like profiles. PIR-086 displayed a biphasic response, characterized by increased ΔΨm at lower concentration and reduced ΔΨm at higher concentration. Additional analogues produced minimal deviations from control values and were classified as near-neutral. Parallel cytotoxicity studies demonstrated that modulation of ΔΨm generally occurred in the absence of substantial cytotoxicity under the conditions examined. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that structural diversification of this amphiphilic scaffold is associated with distinct mitochondrial membrane potential phenotypes, supporting a scaffold-dependent relationship between molecular structure and mitochondrial response. These results provide an initial framework for further investigation of structure-phenotype relationships and the development of small molecules that modulate mitochondrial function.

papers.title: Quantifying and Eliminating Self-Interaction Error in Density Functionals: A Recipe for Traditional and Machine-Learning DFT
papers.abstract: Self-interaction and charge-delocalization errors remain important limitations of approximate density functional theory (DFT), affecting reaction barriers, self-consistent densities, and charged-fragment dissociation limits. Constrained DFT (CDFT) can stabilize complementary charge-localized determinants, which can subsequently be combined by nonorthogonal configuration interaction (CDFT-CI). We apply this construction to conventional functionals and to the machine-learning Skala functional for charged molecular dissociations and SN2 barriers. CDFT-CI substantially changes the energetics when the unconstrained solution is artificially stabilized by fractional charge transfer, but it does not make the underlying exchange-correlation functional self-interaction free. The benefit depends on the fragment partition, the selected constrained root, the determinant overlap, and numerical convergence; these diagnostics are therefore reported explicitly. The results show that learned nonlocality can reduce, but does not in general eliminate, charge-delocalization error.

papers.title: Phenonium-Ion-Mediated Skeletal Editing of Paracyclophanes
papers.abstract: Phenonium ions have played a central role in physical-organic chemistry, yet their use as strategic intermediates in synthesis remains underexplored. Here, we report a phenonium-ion-mediated strategy for the skeletal editing of paracyclophanes. Installation of a one-carbon handle at the aliphatic bridge, followed by direct alcohol activation with BF 3 ·OEt 2 under solvolysis-avoiding conditions, generates a paracyclophane-derived phenonium ion that undergoes regioselective ring opening by external nucleophiles. This strategy provides modular access to functionalised higher paracyclophane homologues and tolerates S-, N-, C-, selenium-, and halide-based nucleophiles under operationally simple, gram-scalable conditions. The sequence can be applied iteratively and extended to double bridge expansion, while reductive desulfurization furnishes the corresponding parent hydrocarbons.
