papers.title: Multiple-Kernel Ridge Regression for Learning the Structure-Electronic Property Relationships of Pyranoazacoronene COFs
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are highly ordered, porous organic materials whose reticular construction from tailored nodes and linkers enables atomic-level control over structure and function. The design space of COFs is vast with virtually unlimited combinations of nodes, linkers, and functional groups. Interpretable machine learning (ML) offers a pathway to navigate this complexity by identifying the structural features that govern materials performance, yet interpretability often comes at the cost of predictive accuracy. In this work, we introduce a novel multiple-kernel learning framework that achieves both accuracy and mechanistic insight. A multiple-kernel ridge regression (MKRR) model was trained on band gaps predicted from GFN1-xTB level theory for a dataset of 232 theoretical pyranoazacoronene (PAC) COFs produced from eight different conjugated linkers and 29 functional groups. Modifying these building units alone produced a range of band gaps between 0.4-2 eV. Manual analysis of the theoretical band gaps versus the linker indicates that breaking the conjugation pathway by altering the bond angle or by introducing a σ-bond increases the band gap while increasing the length of the linker decreases the band gap. All functional groups appear to reduce the band gap with three specific electron withdrawing groups reducing the band gap near 0.4 eV. For the ML, the building units were represented with three independent kernels that encoded the local environments of each node, linker, and functional group calculated from the Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP). After decomposing each kernel’s contribution to the model’s global predictions, we found that the MKRR model successfully captures the underlying structure–property relationships that influence the band gap. These results demonstrate that MKRR is an effective and interpretable framework for understanding and designing functional COFs.

papers.title: Cannabinoid and terpene analysis in Cannabis sativa L.: extraction workflows, chromatographic methods, and a weighted selection framework for quality control
papers.abstract: The analytical characterization of Cannabis sativa L. remains methodologically heterogeneous, limiting interlaboratory comparability, regulatory compliance, and product traceability across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic applications. This review systematically evaluates current extraction workflows and chromatographic methods for the routine quantification of cannabinoids and terpenes, with emphasis on analytical robustness, accessibility, and reproducibility under standard laboratory conditions. Extraction strategies, including conventional solvent-based extraction (ethanol maceration, n-hexane maceration, Soxhlet), ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE), microwave-assisted extraction (MAE), and supercritical fluid extraction (SFE), are comparatively assessed against eight analytically and operationally relevant criteria using a weighted scoring matrix. Ethanol-based UAE achieves the most favorable balance across selectivity, cost, reproducibility, and green analytical chemistry criteria. For cannabinoid quantification, HPLC-DAD is recommended as the most robust and cost-effective routine platform, enabling simultaneous analysis of acidic and neutral forms without thermal conversion or derivatization. GC-FID is recommended for terpene profiling, circumventing the dependency on costly deuterated standards inherent to MS-based detection. A consensus workflow integrating these components is proposed for laboratories operating with standard instrumentation and without routine access to LC-MS/MS or supercritical fluid systems. The adoption of such evidence-based, purpose-driven workflows is expected to substantially advance method standardization across sectors that increasingly rely on Cannabis sativa L. as a source of regulated active compounds.

papers.title: Expanding the Reactivity of Bifunctional Reagents: Photoinduced Metal-Free Access to Imino Carbonyl Compounds and Tetrahydrofurans
papers.abstract: Alkoxy radicals are versatile intermediates capable of engaging in diverse reaction pathways, yet the selective exploitation of their reactivity under mild conditions remains a significant challenge. Herein, we expand the synthetic utility of N-oxime-derived bifunctional radical reagents by exploiting two complementary alkoxy radical pathways, β-scission and intramolecular alkene cyclization, in combination with metal-free radical 1,2-carboimination of activated alkenes. Under visible-light irradiation using 5CzBN as an organic photocatalyst, the bifunctional precursors generate alkoxy radicals that undergo substrate-controlled β-scission or cyclization to produce carbon-centered radicals, which are regioselectively trapped by activated alkenes and subsequently coupled with iminyl radicals. This modular strategy provides direct access to remotely iminofunctionalized carbonyl compounds and tetrahydrofurans with broad substrate scope and excellent chemoselectivity, including the latestage functionalization of complex biomolecules and pharmaceuticals. Mechanistic studies support an energy-transfer-initiated radical-chain mechanism

papers.title: Nanoscale Confinement Enables Homogeneous Growth of Sub-4 nm Bi2Te3 Nanowires
papers.abstract: Homogeneous growth within ordered mesoporous templates remains difficult because strong nanoscale confinement is both poorly understood and challenging to characterise. Here, we report sub-4 nm Bi2Te3 nanostructures grown by electrodeposition within mesoporous silica thin films. Vertically aligned nanowire arrays with diameters of 3.7 nm and lengths of ~230 nm were grown in P6mm templates, while interconnected three-dimensional nanowire networks were formed in Fmmm templates with diameters of approximately 8 nm. Electron microscopy confirms homogeneous filling of both structures. Operando grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GISAXS) shows that homogeneous growth proceeds through the transient coexistence of electrolyte-filled and Bi2Te3-filled mesophases. This produces characteristic Bragg peak splitting, which provides a direct structural signature of homogeneous growth within the buried pore network. The growth mechanism is independent of pore geometry and size. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for confined electrodeposition across pore architectures.

papers.title: Kinetic behaviour of non-uniform sites of ZSM-5 catalysts
papers.abstract: NH3-TPD studies are used to characterise zeolite acidity. Site behaviour (number of site ensembles, and energetics) differs between vacuum- and atmospheric-NH3-TPD profiles. Accurate site behaviour is relevant to the construction of transient microkinetic models, pseudo steady-state kinetic models, and heterogeneity-based descriptions. Non-uniform sites have been observed over ZSM-5 catalysts. Four transient microkinetic models of non-uniform sites give activation energies of NH3 desorption between 87 – 137 kJ mol -1 for vacuum and atmospheric studies. The pseudo steady-state kinetic model with re-adsorption gives heat of adsorption of 132 kJ mol -1 , and a standard entropy change of 140 J mol-1 K -1 for atmospheric studies. Although energy distribution varies, the heterogeneity model can predict the behaviour of non-uniform sites by unifying the number of site ensembles across models. The implications for methanol-to-olefin conversion are discussed.

papers.title: Homoleptic Tri-coordinated Ga Alkoxide as Molecular Models for Low Coordinated Surface Sites
papers.abstract: Gallium-containing metal oxides have been used as the industrially relevant catalysts. In order to understand the speciation and roles of the surface Ga sites associated with the Lewis acidity and redox properties, syntheses of molecular model for the surface Ga sites combined with spectroscopic approaches, e.g. X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, has been shown as a powerful methodology to determine the structures and coordination environments of supported Ga sites. Among the various Ga(III) coordination environments, a tri-coordinated [3]Ga(III) complex in an oxygen environment can be an ideal model for the supported Ga sites on metal oxides, typically consisting of oxygen atoms as neighbors. Here, we synthesize a [3]Ga(III) alkoxide bearing bulky alkoxide, ‒OCMetBu2, which shows characteristic XAS signatures, as also observed in [3]Ga(III) complexes in nitrogen and carbon environments. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that such unique XAS features are derived from the difference of bonding manner, σ- vs. π-bonding, between Ga and neighboring atoms. This Ga model complex is further investigated to study the possible probe molecule, isocyanides, whose infrared spectroscopy (IR) signatures can highlight the presence of Lewis acidic sites. Respective spectroscopic signatures, i.e. XAS and IR, of the synthesized Ga(III) model complexes, complemented by DFT calculations, indicate the presence of [3]Ga(III) sites on Si-doped alumina in pseudo-trigonal planar geometry, corresponding to the Lewis acidity of the surface Ga sites.

papers.title: Ion Mobility-Mass Spectrometry and Collision Induced Unfolding Distinguish Tryptophan and Methionine Oxidation in Intact Monoclonal Antibodies with Correlated Solution Stability Shifts
papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibody (mAb)-based therapeutics are susceptible to numerous degradation pathways that may alter their native structure, stability and immunogenicity. Thus, biophysical tools that can rapidly assess subtle changes in higher order structure (HOS) are crucial for ensuring product safety and efficacy. Ion mobility-mass spectrometry (IM-MS) and collision-induced unfolding (CIU) assays have emerged as valuable methods to analyze mAb dynamics, structure and stability. IM-MS and CIU measurements have proven to be sensitive to HOS shifts resulting from accelerated stability studies and can differentiate conformational changes produced by pH-stress from thermal stress. Nonetheless, previous studies have used forced degradation conditions that can induce multiple degradation pathways, simultaneously modifying various amino acids at different levels. Therefore, questions regarding the ability of IM-MS/CIU to assess the degradation of specific amino acids, their sensitivity to the degree of modification and how these gas-phase measurements compare to solution-based assays remain under-explored. Here, we describe how IM-MS and CIU workflows can be used to probe HOS changes produced by oxidative modifications. Specifically, we examined three methionine residues, conducting CIU assessments at six distinct oxidation levels. We also analyzed CIU data recorded for mAb samples where a single tryptophan residue within the sequence was oxidized, comparing samples containing only singly oxidized products to those with a mixture of singly and doubly oxidized forms. Our data reveals that the oxidation of different mAb residues can result in significant and unique shifts in TWΩN2 and CIU transitions, with the latter data enabling the assignment of destabilized domains within the intact mAb. In addition, our results indicate a quantitative correlation between the extent of IM-MS and CIU shifts, and the extent of oxidation undergone by the mAb. Finally, our CIU stability shifts are consistent with standard thermal-shift assays carried out in solution. We conclude by discussing how IM-MS and CIU can be leveraged to rapidly elucidate detailed mAb degradation pathways.

papers.title: Improved Native Top-Down Characterization of Protein Complexes Afforded by Cyclic Ion Mobility-Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: Proteins originating from a single gene can exist as numerous distinct proteoforms, each defined by unique modifications and amino acid sequences. Because these proteoforms and their macromolecular complexes often display markedly different functions and abundance levels, their thorough characterization is essential for a comprehensive molecular understanding of living systems. Native top-down mass spectrometry presents a promising approach to analyzing native proteoform complexes, yet achieving high sequence coverage for large protein complex precursor ions remains a major challenge that limits their complete characterization and identification. In this study, we implement native top-down workflows on a cyclic ion mobility-mass spectrometer, utilizing multi-pass separations and tandem ion mobility operation modes to enable deeper sequence analysis of native protein complexes. We demonstrate that native topdown and complex-down workflows yield unique, sequence-informative fragments, and that ion mobility separation increases sequence coverage by at least 20% for all three of the protein complexes examined. Moreover, multi-pass ion mobility separations further enhance sequence coverage for avidin tetramers by 15%, while pseudo-MSn/IMSn experiments using tandem ion mobility result in a 10% improvement for alcohol dehydrogenase tetramers and permit unambiguous localization and identification of a sequence variant. Taken together, our findings indicate that that next-generation ion mobility instrumentation can result in a 2-fold improvement in the sequencing and characterization of the complexes commonly encountered in native proteomics.

papers.title: Using energy decomposition analysis from correlated wavefunction theory to characterize a range of hydrogen, halogen, and tetrel bonds: The relative importance of electrostatics, charge-transfer and polarization.
papers.abstract: Second-order Møller-Plesset theory (MP2) is the simplest wavefunction-based treatment of electron correlation and is a good compromise between accuracy and efficiency for evaluating the strength of many non-covalent intermolecular interactions. It has also been improved in accuracy and robustness by regularized methods, such as the size-consistent second order Brillouin-Wigner perturbation theory (BWs2) and κ-MP2. This work presents a non-technical summary of the recently developed second-generation absolutely localized molecular orbital (ALMO) energy decomposition analysis (EDA) method at the post-SCF level of MP2 and regularized MP2. The so-called frozen term is redefined to ensure that long range correlation contributions to electrostatics are correctly captured. The resulting EDA provides useful basis set limits to the correlation corrections for all physical contributions: donor-acceptor charge transfer, electrical polarization, dispersion, and Pauli repulsions and electrostatic interactions associated with frozen monomer orbitals. EDA calculations using MP2 are reported on several classes of systems: model systems to assess correlation effects on permanent and induced electrostatics, hydrogen bonds between water and model carbohydrate molecules, tetrel bonds ranging from 15 to 90 kJ/mol in strength, two halogen bonds-one of which is known to be solvent resistant, and a pair of “anti-electrostatic” halogen bonds. Several general conclusions emerge. First, to obtain physically reasonable conclusions, it is essential that the correlation contribution is not identified with dispersion alone: large corrections to the frozen term corresponding to changes in electrostatics are observed due to correlation. Second, the fingerprint of intermolecular interactions provided by the EDA reveals a range of interesting trends in the character of intermolecular interactions as a function of their type and strength. For example, the solvent-stable halogen bond is confirmed to be dominated by charge-transfer stabilization. On the other hand, the strongest tetrel bonds studied here are dominated by contributions from polarization, while more conventional hydrogen bonds between water and model carbohydrates represent a synergy between electrostatics, dispersion, and charge transfer. The metastability (or stability) of nominally antielectrostatic interactions depends strongly on the differing distance dependence of attractive and repulsive terms, and we demonstrated tuning based on changes in permanent electrostatics by increasing charge-separation through use of phenyl linkers.

papers.title: Fluorescence Detection of Fe(II) Senses Pitting Corrosion Differences Between 3D-printed and Wrought Steel
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing of stainless steel allows for automated, on-demand fabrication of complex metal materials. Yet, compared to wrought steel, additively manufactured metals have different physical properties including corrosion resistance. Differences in microscale chemistry of molybdenum in subgrain boundaries of additively manufactured stainless steel 316 (SS316) led to stronger corrosion pit growth. SS304 is another broadly applied stainless steel which contains no molybdenum. The corrosion properties of SS304 have had limited study in an additively manufactured form. Here, we use a combination of product-specific fluorescence sensing of Fe(II) with spatially-, temporally-, and reaction product-averaged electrochemical corrosion methods and ex situ imaging to reveal the mechanistic differences between the corrosion of additive manufactured and wrought SS304. We determine that the passive film on additively manufactured SS304 is resistant to breakdown but pits grow quickly with an acidic, Fe(II)-rich local environment, while the passive film formed on wrought SS304 is easier to breakdown but repassivates quickly at local metastable pits. Overall, fluorescence allows in situ detection of Fe(II) at the onset of pit formation to completement conventional corrosion technologies to reveal mechanistic differences in the chemistry of the corrosion of additively manufactured metals.

papers.title: Third-order size-consistent Brillouin-Wigner perturbation theory
papers.abstract: Low order Rayleigh-Schrödinger (RS) perturbation theory with Møller-Plesset partitioning is size-consistent but not regular, and for this reason, the third order variant, MP3, is not commonly used in computational quantum chemistry. Recently, it has become clear how to modify Brillouin-Wigner perturbation theory at second order to be both size-consistent and regular, by using a non-Møller-Plesset partitioning to define BWs2. In this work, a solution is presented for the problem of defining an iterative third-order generalization, iBWs3, that is size-consistent, regular, and exact for the electron correlation of 2 electrons in 2 orbitals. iBWs3 is closely related to coupled cluster theory with doubles, with the same compute scaling. An implementation and a series of tests on restricted orbital dissociations and relative energies are reported.

papers.title: Reductive Sulfinyl Smiles–Truce Rearrangement of α-Bromoamides to α-Aryl Quaternary Centers
papers.abstract: Radical sulfinyl Smiles–Truce rearrangements provide powerful approaches to aryl migration, but have predominantly been coupled to alkene addition or hydrogen-atom-transfer initiation. Here, visible-light reduction of α-bromo N-acyl sulfinamides generates α-carbonyl radicals that undergo intramolecular aryl migration to form α-aryl amides, predominantly bearing quaternary carbon centers. The reaction uses an organic photocatalyst under operationally simple conditions and accommodates cyclic and acyclic α-substitution, electronically diverse (hetero)arenes, and varied amide N-substituents. The transformation was performed on gram scale, and the products were converted into indolinone, oxazoline, and imidazoline scaffolds. Chiral sulfur(IV) substrates revealed strongly substrate-dependent, stereoconvergent sulfur-to-carbon chirality transfer, reaching 99:1 er in a favorable case. Electrochemical, luminescence-quenching, crossover, and quantum-yield experiments support reductive quenching, photocatalyst-mediated C–Br reduction, and intramolecular migration. This alkyl-halide initiation mode expands sulfur(IV)-mediated radical aryl transfer and provides modular access to congested α-aryl amides.

papers.title: Amplification of circularly polarised luminescence through the self-assembly of chiral tri-europium(III) clusters in a polar crystal
π-Armor Strategy: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
papers.abstract: Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes: reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained a challenge. Herein, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D 3 -symmetric π-conjugated cage in which two curved hexa- cata -hexabenzocoronene panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. The cage reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, with binding affinities governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size can be entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, the cage behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.

papers.title: “Like Dissolves Like” in Doped Organic Room-Temperature Phosphorescence
papers.abstract: Host-guest doping has emerged as a facile and efficient strategy for the fabrication of organic room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials. Nonetheless, how the chemical structures of dopants and matrices systematically influence the triplet exciton dynamics of solid-state materials remains elusive. While investigations have been focusing on electronic structures and energy levels, here we show that doped phenothiazine model systems largely follow the well-known principle of “like dissolves like” and exhibit phase-separation-controlled photophysical state switching between RTP and triplet-triplet annihilation delayed fluorescence (TTA-DF), evidenced by scanning electron microscopy, confocal microscopy, and micro-region spectrometry. In the structurally similar host-guest combination, the miscible solid solution exhibits strong guest RTP emission; in the thermodynamically favored microphase-separated state, the RTP is severely outcompeted by TTA-DF of the guest aggregate, which has significantly faster decay kinetics. Microscopy results show that simple mechanical force by gentle grinding is sufficient to partially amorphize the nanophase-separated crystalline sample and promote intense host-sensitized guest RTP. This work demonstrates that, in addition to quantum mechanical considerations, thermodynamic rules provide the crucial missing link to predictably govern structural morphology and macroscopic luminescence in doped organic crystals, laying a more complete foundation for the design of dynamically tunable, stimuli-responsive RTP materials.

papers.title: Tetracarboxyphenyl Iron Porphyrin as a Robust Aqueous Catalyst for the Reduction of N-oxide and Endoperoxide
papers.abstract: Small-molecule catalysts are pursued as they are widely used in fundamental and applied chemistry. Herein, we report that tetracarboxyphenyl iron porphyrin (FeTCPP) is a superior water-soluble catalyst for the reduction of N‑oxides and endoperoxides. Through screening tetraphenyl iron porphyrin (FeTPP) derivatives, we found FeTCPP performed best and only 0.4% FeTCPP could efficiently reduce the N‑oxide to tertiary amine. Impressively, FeTCPP catalytically reduced the endoperoxide of artemisinin to generate a main product while the known activator, heme, led to multiple products. The inactivity of the main product against tumor cells and malaria parasites will help in understanding the antimalarial and anticancer activities of artemisinin. Finally, we successfully applied FeTCPP in the reduction of transitionally-formed endoperoxide during direct chemiluminescence by isoluminol. Whether isoluminol is free or labelled with proteins, FeTCPP generated stronger chemiluminescence than hemin and increased the detection sensitivity by 20-fold. An undeniable advantage of FeTCPP is that it prefers to the low concentration of H 2 O 2 used in direct chemiluminescence detection. FeTCPP thereby could save 95% hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) compared to the traditional hemin catalyst. As isoluminol-based direct chemiluminescence detection is a routine test in clinics and hospitals, the wide application of FeTCPP will produce tremendous economic and environmental value.

papers.title: Towards an Unbiased Dataset of Cocrystals and Solvates by Crystal Structure Prediction
papers.abstract: The identification of coformers that can form a stable multicomponent crystal with molecules of special interest is an ongoing challenge in crystal engineering. The field is currently hampered by the available data in that contemporary experimental databases of multicomponent crystals lack negative data and suffer from chemical bias, limiting their applications to machine learning in particular. We have performed high-throughput crystal structure prediction on all unique 276 1:1 combinations of a set of 24 small rigid molecules. The resulting dataset of predicted cocrystal structures eliminates much of the bias observed in experimental datasets, and includes both negative and positive predictions. We present this as validation of an approach to generating large-scale data relating to the energetics of cocrystal formation. Most of the positive predictions are attributed to one of a small set of “super” coformers, rather than crystallographically favourable combinations of molecular features.

papers.title: Molecular Insights into Water Solubility in Fluid Carbon Dioxide for CCS Applications
papers.abstract: We estimate the solubility of water as an impurity in fluid CO2 by calculating the chemical potential from intermolecular interactions. The evaluation is conducted over a wide range of temperature and pressure relevant to CO2 transport and storage. The formation of hydrate from impurity of water reduces the solubility relative to the value expected for fluid CO2 coexisting with the metastable aqueous solution without hydrate formation. The solubility of water obtained shows good agreement with experimental measurements and model calculations. Compression leads to a lower solubility in a range of the gaseous state when the solubility is expressed in the conventionally used mole fraction. We show that this is merely an apparently strange behavior and disappears by changing the unit to molarity. The molarity-based solubility is beneficial not only for the present study to understand temperature and pressure dependence of solubility in terms of intermolecular interactions but also for correlating it with the driving force for water-induced corrosion. These fundamental insights into the phase equilibria of fluid CO2 and water are valuable for technological development to prevent pipeline blockages caused by hydrate formation and to mitigate water-induced corrosion in CO2 transport and storage.

papers.title: Uncovering Nonadiabatic Dynamics of Plasmonic Metal–Molecular Switch Hybrids with Surface Hopping
papers.abstract: Despite considerable interest in plasmonic nanoparticles for light-driven green chemistry under mild conditions, the mechanisms underlying their catalytic activity remain controversial. To resolve these mechanistic uncertainties, surface hopping has recently emerged as a powerful computational approach for atomistic descriptions of charge and energy flow at metal–molecule interfaces. Thus far, however, the method has been applied primarily to systems involving relatively small molecules such as H 2 and CO, owing to the high computational cost of quantum-chemical calculations for metallic nanostructures. In the present work, we use surface hopping simulations to explore the nonadiabatic dynamics of an azobenzene molecule covalently bound to a gold nanocluster following either molecular or plasmon excitation. In accord with recent experimental observations, we find that the optically excited molecule gets rapidly quenched by the metal continuum via competing energy and charge transfer decay channels at short azobenzene–gold distances. On the other hand, the plasmon-excited gold nanocluster is nearly unaffected by the photoswitch and primarily relaxes via electron-phonon interactions due to an efficient electronic decoupling of the metal-and molecule-centered orbitals at the interface. In summary, our results provide direct atomistic insight into how undesired metal–molecule couplings can suppress the reactivity of functional molecules at plasmonic gold nanostructures, thereby facilitating the rational design of novel plasmonic systems.

papers.title: From Eutectics to Ionic Cocrystals: Thermodynamics of N-Alkylquinolinium Bromide + α,ω-Diol Systems
papers.abstract: Solid–liquid equilibria of N-alkylquinolinium bromides ([Quin-Cn][Br], n = 4–12) with α,ω-alkanediols were investigated to elucidate the molecular mechanisms governing eutectic behaviour and cocrystal formation. Phase diagrams were established using differential scanning calorimetry and dynamic methods and subsequently correlated with the NRTL model to obtain excess thermodynamic functions and enthalpies of intermolecular compound formation. In parallel, a COSMO-RS-based molecular analysis was employed to derive surface descriptors and compatibility metrics from σ-profiles. The combined results demonstrate that, while strong charge-assisted hydrogen bonding dominates liquid-phase non-ideality, the decisive factor controlling solid-state organization and cocrystal formation is the geometric and amphiphilic compatibility between the alkyl chain of the quinolinium cation and the diol spacer. The study provides a concise molecular framework for rationalizing and screening eutectic mixtures and stable intermolecular compounds in ionic-liquid-based systems

papers.title: Pollutant induced cardiotoxicity: systematic review and evidence map of 400 toxicological studies
papers.abstract: Environmental pollutants are increasingly associated with adverse cardiovascular effects, posing serious public health concerns. We conducted a systematic mapping review to identify, organize, and make accessible the existing toxicological evidence on pollutant induced cardiotoxicity (PICT). An interactive systematic evidence map was developed to support research prioritization, risk assessment, and policy development. Following our previously published protocol, peer-reviewed studies were included if they reported cardiovascular outcomes resulting from pollutant exposure in animal or in vitro models. Data were extracted on study design, exposure-outcome relationships, and risk of bias (RoB) was assessed for all included studies. Out of 9,317 screened studies, 400 were included. Findings show substantial evidence of cardiotoxic effects from exposure to heavy metals, air pollutants, insecticides, PFAS, and related substances. Animal studies dominate the literature, commonly reporting cardiomyopathy, hypertrophy, fibrosis, and conduction abnormalities at environmentally relevant exposures. In vitro models primarily offer shared mechanistic insights, especially related to oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. RoB varied across studies, with common limitations in exposure characterization and endpoint validation, while in vivo and in vitro results showed good correlation. To improve data accessibility and reusability, we created an open-access interactive evidence map ( https://cardiotoxdb.org/ ), allowing users to filter by pollutant class, study type, species or cell type and cardiac outcome. This review and the systematic evidence map offer a structured and transparent overview of toxicological data on PICT, enabling stakeholders to explore the evidence base, identify gaps, and prioritize pollutants for further evaluation.

papers.title: A Flexible Framework for Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experiences in Advanced Chemistry Laboratory Courses
papers.abstract: Course-based undergraduate research experiences (CUREs) broaden access to the high-impact practice of undergraduate research, but even faculty experienced in mentoring undergraduate researchers may lack a clear roadmap for translating that research into a course format, creating a barrier to adoption of the CURE pedagogy. To address this barrier, we present a flexible framework (Flexi-Framework) for integrating faculty research into upper-level laboratory coursework using a series of activities that guide students through four phases of scientific research: (I) Obtaining, Evaluating, and Organizing Information, (II) Asking Questions and Planning Investigations; (III) Investigation, Data Analysis, and Iteration; and (IV) Justification and Communication through a written report and/or oral presentation. The framework consists of assessable, workshop-style activities that can be adapted to different research topics while maintaining the CURE-defining elements of collaboration, discovery and relevance, and iteration. Over the past decade, the Flexi-Framework has been implemented in multiple upper-division chemistry CUREs across three institutions and several subdisciplines of chemistry. Assessment using the Classroom Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE) survey and the Laboratory Course Assessment Survey (LCAS) demonstrates student-reported gains and course elements consistent with national CURE benchmarks. The CURE Flexi-Framework thus provides a model for integrating faculty research into coursework, with the goal of lowering barriers to CURE development and adoption across institutional and disciplinary contexts.

papers.title: Mechanism-Informed Molecular Fingerprints for Interpretable Skin Sensitization Prediction
papers.abstract: Skin sensitization begins with chemical-protein reactivity but culminates in a multistep immune response, making it a useful test of molecular representations that encode mechanism rather than topology alone. We developed MechanismFP v2, a prespecified 53-feature fingerprint comprising physicochemical descriptors, SMARTS-based reaction alerts, and reaction-domain indicators for Michael addition, Schiff-base formation, acyl transfer, SN2 chemistry, ring opening, redox/prohapten behavior, and an SNAr proxy. We benchmarked MechanismFP v2 against ECFP4 and MACCS using repeated scaffold-held-out evaluation across SkinSensDB-derived endpoints. MechanismFP v2 achieved ROC-AUC 0.803 for DPRA-derived peptide reactivity and 0.772 for LLNA; removal of all reaction-alert features reduced DPRA ROC-AUC by 0.101. The representation was then evaluated without modification on 1,183 connectivity-disjoint human-labeled chemicals, yielding ROC-AUC 0.705 and PR-AUC 0.462 compared with 0.625 and 0.294 for ECFP4. The paired ROC-AUC advantage over ECFP4 was 0.0795 (95% bootstrap CI 0.0357-0.1223). Integrating downstream AOP assay evidence further improved internal human-label prediction. These results show that mechanistic feature engineering can provide transferable and interpretable signal, especially for endpoints proximal to covalent protein reactivity, while downstream human outcomes require additional biological context.

papers.title: Bismuth-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks from a Dodecatopic Carboxylic Acid Linker as Catalysts for Aerobic Thiol Oxidation
papers.abstract: Herein, we report two bismuth-based metal–organic frameworks (Bi-MOFs), namely UU-207 and UU-208, constructed from a newly designed dodecatopic triptycene-based three-dimensional (3D) linker, called H12dpet, bearing twelve carboxylic acid (–COOH) groups. The rigid triptycene core and its multiple carboxylic acid groups enable the formation of highly connected architectures with welldefined microporosity and excellent connectivity. Under finely tuned synthetic conditions, hexagonal UU-207 with a rare ceq-net topology or monoclinic UU-208 with a three-nodal 9,5,4-c net can be selectively formed. These MOFs catalyze the aerobic oxidation of thiols to disulfides under mild 2 conditions (room temperature, atmospheric air, short reaction times), with excellent yields and a broad substrate scope. The differences in building units, stability, and Lewis acid concentration result in different catalytic performance between UU-207 and UU-208. The catalyst can be reused at least three times with no appreciable loss of catalytic performance or crystallinity. This work demonstrates the potential of triptycene-based multicarboxylate linkers for constructing highly connected Bi-MOFs and provides a new strategy for designing functional porous materials for catalytic applications.

papers.title: Tracking Lithium Intercalation and Deintercalation Behavior of Graphite Composite Electrode in All-Solid-State Batteries by Operando Raman spectroscopy and Optical Image Observation
papers.abstract: Graphite is widely used as a promising anode material for various battery systems because of its low cost, high capacity, and low operation potential. During Li intercalation and deintercalation, graphite undergoes a series of stage transitions, the behavior of which depends on the electrolyte system. However, the Li intercalation/deintercalation behavior of graphite in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) is not fully understood because previous Raman spectroscopy studies on ASSBs have reported inconsistent stage transition behaviors. Herein, we investigate the Li intercalation/deintercalation behavior of graphite in ASSBs using operando Raman spectroscopy while simultaneously tracking the spatial reaction distribution within the electrode by optical imaging. During the intercalation process, graphite exhibits the same stage transition behavior as in conventional lithium-ion batteries, whereas Li deintercalation follows an apparently irreversible stage transition pathway. This apparent irreversibility originates from an inhomogeneous reaction distribution across the thickness of the graphite electrode rather than the intrinsic staging behavior of graphite. These findings resolve the inconsistencies reported in previous Raman spectroscopy studies and demonstrate that spatial information on the reaction distribution within electrodes is essential for accurately interpreting the stage transition mechanism of graphite in ASSBs.

papers.title: Data-efficient fine-tuning for reaction modelling in explicit solvent
papers.abstract: Accurate modelling of chemical reactions is key to optimising synthetic procedures and molecular discovery. Yet doing so represents one of the grand challenges in computational chemistry, especially when considering solvent and non-statistical dynamic effects. Pre-trained machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional quantum chemistry approaches, offering stable out-of-the-box performance across chemical domains. Recent studies have shown that fine-tuning these MLIPs on task-specific datasets can substantially improve their accuracy. Nonetheless, it remains unclear how the composition and size of fine-tuning datasets influence model performance in reaction modelling, and to what extent fine-tuning compensates for limitations in pre-training datasets. In this work, we address these questions, focusing on organic reactions in solution, using three Diels–Alder reactions of increasing complexity as benchmark systems. We evaluate three pre-trained MACE models, each covering a different domain: a bespoke model for graphene-oxide (GO-MACE-23) and two `foundation' models for organic molecules (MACE-OFF-23) and materials (MACE-MP0), alongside the recently released and substantially larger MACE-OMOL model. We demonstrate that models can be fine-tuned using 50 or fewer samples representing vacuum and solvated clusters to accurately reproduce potential energy barriers, transition state geometries, and reaction dynamics in solution. We also identify key factors in model pre-training data that affect fine-tuning performance, including differences in levels of theory and limited coverage of non-equilibrium structures. While MACE-OMOL delivers competitive out-of-the-box performance, its improvement upon fine-tuning is less substantial, and its size and memory requirements currently limit its use in long molecular dynamics simulations required for free energy sampling. Overall, this study presents a systematic analysis of MLIP fine-tuning for modelling organic reactions in solution, offering practical guidelines that facilitate their use and move these approaches closer to routine applications.

papers.title: MolSanity: A Reliability Audit for Feature Attributions on Molecular Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Feature attributions are routinely used to justify molecular graph neural network (GNN) predictions to chemists, yet they are almost never audited for reliability: existing frameworks ask whether an explanation is faithful to the model, not whether it identifies the chemistry that determines the property, nor where it stops being trustworthy under scaffold shift. MolSanity is a reliability-audit framework that wraps canonical implementations (Captum, PyTorch Geometric, RDKit) rather than proposing a new attributor, scoring every (dataset × backbone × attributor × split) cell on six axes: motif-native coherence, occlusion–attribution faithfulness, ground-truth localisation where node labels exist, cross-checkpoint stability, calibration linkage, and confidence/correctness regime stratification. Our central finding is that faithfulness is not correctness, and that the two carry no dependable relationship in either regime. Across 30 selection tests — 5 molecular ground-truth arms × two splits × 3 ranking metrics — a faithfulness-only ranking picks an attributor other than the ground-truth-best one in 26, and this is no less true in distribution (14 of 15) than under scaffold shift (12 of 15); on MUTAG under shift it prefers an attributor anti-aligned with the nitro motif (GT AUROC 0.013) over one at 0.826. Pooled over 47 cells the faithfulness–correctness rank correlation is +0.222 in distribution (p = 0.134) and −0.124 under shift (p = 0.405), neither distinguishable from zero, while per arm under shift it runs from −0.564 to +0.786: reliability is a property of the individual (dataset, backbone, attributor, split) cell rather than of the attributor. Restricted to the 3 arms of an earlier analysis it gives −0.356 (p = 0.042); two externally authored rationale benchmarks remove the effect, and we report the 5-arm result. Faithfulness itself does not fall under shift — it rises, from 0.049 to 0.132, while ground-truth localisation does not move — so the metric gives no warning either way. Over 31,785 per-molecule records, localisation degrades on confidently-wrong predictions (0.769 to 0.681) while their measured faithfulness improves, and the calibration–reliability link attenuates from a per-cell median of 0.144 to 0.074 when cells are pooled. Every number, figure and table regenerates from the committed artifacts.

papers.title: Electronic states of diarylethene switch–gold nanocluster hybrids
Convergent Fragmentation: A Small, Shared Ion Vocabulary Underlies the Limits of Structure–Spectrum Fidelity
papers.abstract: Tandem mass spectral similarity is widely used to infer whether molecules are structurally related, yet the fragmentation processes underlying this assumption remain incompletely understood. Structure–Spectrum Fidelity (SSF) measures the strength of this correspondence. Across structurally stratified compound pairs from the METLIN reference library, structural and spectral similarity were only moderately related (R2 = 0.28): closely related molecules could produce dissimilar spectra, while structurally different molecules could produce similar spectra. We investigated two fragmentation processes that could contribute to these opposing outcomes. First, differences in net hydrogen redistribution were associated with reduced spectral similarity between compound pairs. At corpus scale, hydrogen redistribution accounted for approximately 25–30% of model-explained fragment-ion intensity, equivalent to approximately 6.7% of total fragment-ion intensity. Second, chemically diverse precursors frequently converged onto the same recurrent product ions. Sharing an individual recurrent aromatic/allylic cation was uninformative, but elevated spectral similarity was concentrated among the relatively small subset of compound pairs sharing the greatest numbers of these ions. This was an upper-tail effect rather than a general increase with recurrent-ion sharing. Across 958,450 deduplicated METLIN compounds, we identified 56 recurrent product-ion formulas spanning five chemical families and both ionization modes; every family became more prevalent with increasing collision energy. Together, these findings identify complementary routes to limited SSF: compound-specific fragmentation can separate the spectra of related molecules, whereas extensive convergent fragmentation can make a subset of unrelated molecules appear spectrally similar. More broadly, across nearly one million molecules, fragmentation repeatedly converged on a shared vocabulary of only 56 product-ion formulas.

papers.title: Learning when to use physical relationships in scientific machine learning
papers.abstract: Multiple properties of materials and energy devices are linked by known physical relationships, yet machine-learning models commonly predict each property independently from descriptors, here termed Direct prediction. This study tests whether these relationships remain useful when their inputs are themselves model predictions. Across 16 target–route endpoints spanning solid-state ionic conductors, thermoelectric materials, liquid metal batteries and photovoltaic devices, reconstruction through predicted auxiliary quantities and known physical relationships, termed Physics-only, was less accurate than Direct for 13 endpoints, showing that predicted inputs can turn physically valid relationships into error-amplifying transformations. A residual model correcting the Physics-only estimate, termed Residual-only, recovered much of this systematic distortion but was not consistently superior to Direct and often exhibited similar sample-wise errors. PhysicsGate therefore retains Direct as an anchor and learns a bounded, sample-specific interpolation towards Residual-only using training-side out-of-fold reliability signals. PhysicsGate ranked first for 15 endpoints and within the top two for all 16, with positive mean paired gain for every endpoint. Its endpoint-macro mean paired gain was 0.105, equivalent to a 7.0% reduction in root-mean-square error relative to Direct. Gains reached 7–10% for thermoelectric targets but remained below 1% for most photovoltaic targets. Repeated-split analyses showed that sample adaptation outperformed training-selected fixed blending for thermoelectric, but not photovoltaic, targets. Performance differences were associated with auxiliary-error propagation, residual correctability, branch-error redundancy and learnable variation in branch utility. Physical relationships improved prediction when their reliability under predicted inputs was both recoverable and identifiable.

papers.title: A Spectral Theory of an Electronic Hilbert–Pólya Operator: Reaction-Intermediate Lifetimes, Catalytic Eigenphases, and the Riemann Zeros
papers.abstract: (Dated: August 2, 2026) We develop the spectral theory of a catalytic mechanism compiled as a quantum circuit: a propagator at each geometry, a transition operator advancing the stoichiometric register, a non-adiabatic block at each crossing. Its generator is self-adjoint by construction, the principal logarithm of a unitary being anti-Hermitian. On a crossing-free segment at fixed electron number that generator is the molecular propagator’s, so its eigenphases are active-space eigenvalues, not proxies. Stoichiometry then constrains the spectrum: the clock Zm has a unique non-trivial inversion fixed point, and a stable intermediate there has a real eigenphase, located by group structure and not by energetics. The crossings fix the fluctuations: Stückelberg phases break time reversal, putting the eigenphases in the unitary class with sine-kernel correlations, arithmetic-free. For one class of mechanisms, distinguished by a requirement on the register, not the chemistry, and forced rather than fitted, the spectrum proves arithmetic: five exact correspondences to the Riemann zeta function; eigenphases simple unconditionally by Baker–Wüstholz independence of {log p}, where simplicity of the zeros is classically open; and, in the limit, the ordinates of the zeros, whence the Riemann Hypothesis—no zero off the critical line—within the class. The Hilbert–Pólya programme thereby gains an operator exhibited, not sought, and quantum chemistry a compiled mechanism whose spectrum is known in advance—free, not correlated, but exact, where no exact target existed. Limits are stated: the class is narrow, its home a discretised field theory not a metalloenzyme, its ladder a property of the register, not of orbital energies.

papers.title: Solvent-Dependent Self-Assembly of Fatty Acid Diphenylalanine Amphiphiles into 2D-Sheets
papers.abstract: Diphenylalanine amphiphiles can self-assemble into diverse morphologies. While structural modifications thereof are well studied, little is known on solvent effects that govern the assembly process. Here, diphenylalanine amphiphiles containing Nterminal fatty acids are systematically studied in acetonitrile/water mixtures. These show morphologies ranging from 0D micelles to extended 2D nanosheets.

papers.title: Triarylhydrazone Photoswitches with >360 nm Absorption Maxima, Highly Enriched Photostationary States, and Modular Scaffold Engineering
papers.abstract: Hydrazone-based molecular photoswitches have emerged as one of the most promising classes of light-responsive systems, particularly owing to their straightforward synthesis and broad structural tunability. However, only a limited number of hydrazone motifs combine efficient and stable photoswitching with absorption beyond 360 nm, a prerequisite for many emerging optical technologies and biological applications. Furthermore, the photochromic properties of hydrazones are often highly sensitive to structural modifications, making rational tuning challenging. Herein, we report a family of quinoline-containing triarylhydrazone (triaryl-HZ) photoswitches that exhibit absorption in the UV region above 365 nm. The prepared photoswitches display well-separated absorption bands (approximately 60 nm), minimizing spectral overlap between the switching states and enabling high photoconversions. Designed triaryl-HZs allow versatile structural modifications on both phenyl rings, with only a minor influence on their photochromic behavior. These results identify quinoline-based triaryl-HZs as a versatile platform for the development of robust and spectrally addressable molecular photoswitches.

papers.title: The Modular Quantum Emulator: Chemically Accurate, Polynomial-Cost Simulation of Multi-Step Metalloenzyme Catalysis in a Dissipative Protein Environment
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms for molecular dynamics propagate a wavepacket through configuration space, while quantum electronic-structure methods return a ground-state energy at one fixed geometry. Neither addresses the object a chemist means by a catalytic mechanism: a closed sequence of identified intermediates linked by proton-coupled electron transfers, non-adiabatic crossings, and a stoichiometric budget that must balance over the turnover. Here we introduce the Modular Quantum Emulator (MQE), a qudit architecture that takes that \emph{ mechanism } as the object of computation. Two registers are carried: a logical register assigning one four-level qudit per spatial orbital, whose states are that orbital's four occupancies, and a single auxiliary register counting cofactor turnover around the cycle. Stoichiometric bookkeeping makes the auxiliary register mandatory, and our central result is that it simultaneously performs four further roles---it is the clock for quantum phase estimation, so energies are extracted with no additional qubits; it shelters idle population from dephasing; it confines environmental coupling, leaving the electronic reduced state exactly unitary under open-system dynamics; and its winding number classifies the mechanism, predicting that a centred two-electron elimination requires a turnover electron count divisible by four, satisfied throughout the nitrogenase family and violated by two- and six-electron cycles. Electron number, phase closure, trace and spin sector are enforced as circuit-level invariants and verified at every step. Because the auxiliary sector is algebraically independent of the electronic Hamiltonian, nuclear quantum effects, relativistic and spin--orbit coupling, open-system dissipation and periodic boundary conditions are absorbed without altering the asymptotic cost. Every gate introduced compiles to the native GPI/GPI2/ZZ pulse set of trapped-ion hardware, the basis changes attaining the KAK lower bound of two entangling operations. Validation of these circuits across seventeen catalytic mechanisms, on chemically relevant active spaces small enough to admit exact reference energies, recovers every stoichiometric invariant and returns twenty-five phase-estimation measurements within 1.6~mHa of the exact result.

papers.title: The Tetrahedron Speaks: A Holistic Benchmark for DFT in Tetrahedral Framework
papers.abstract: For nearly three decades, benchmarking density functional theory (DFT) functionals for zeolites and other tetrahedral frameworks has commonly relied on average Si-O bond lengths as the primary metric for assessing structural accuracy, often supplemented by lattice parameters and T-O-T angles. This practice assumes that accurate reproduction of bond lengths implies correct overall framework geometry. In this work, we demonstrate that this assumption can be systematically misleading due to error cancellation: local overestimations and underestimations may cancel when averaged, producing apparently accurate mean values while the framework remains globally distorted. We introduce a new benchmarking paradigm based on two framework‑independent metrics: the tetrahedron‑normalized volume (Vᴛᴏ₄) and the tetrahedron‑normalized surface area (Sᴛᴏ₄), calculated directly from each TO₄ tetrahedron using the Cayley-Menger determinant for volume and Heron's formula for surface area. Twenty‑six DFT functionals-spanning LDA, GGA, and meta‑GGA approximations with and without dispersion corrections-were benchmarked against high‑precision experimental data for α‑quartz at 13 K. The results reveal a striking pattern of ranking inversion: the meta‑GGA functional M06‑L ranks first in absolute bond‑length error (-0.75%, rank #1) but twenty‑third in tetrahedron volume (-3.43%, rank #23) and twentieth in tetrahedron surface area (-1.96%, rank #20)-a dramatic demonstration of error cancellation. LDA functionals show excellent bond‑length errors (0.50-0.68%) but large cell‑volume underestimations (11-13%) and density overestimations (12-15%); in contrast, their tetrahedron‑normalized volume errors (ΔVᴛᴏ₄ = 0.85-1.32%) remain small, indicating that overbinding manifests primarily as reduced framework porosity rather than tetrahedral compression. The Pearson correlation between bond‑length error and tetrahedron‑volume error is remarkably weak (r = 0.31, R² = 0.10), indicating that 90% of the variance in volumetric accuracy is not explained by bond‑length benchmarks. A self‑consistency check using ||ΔV - ΔS|| successfully differentiates isotropic errors (LDA: |ΔV-ΔS| < 0.15%) from anisotropic errors (M06‑L: |ΔV-ΔS| = 1.47%). GGA-HCTH emerges as one of the most balanced functionals, combining moderate errors in tetrahedron volume and surface area (ΔVᴛᴏ₄ = +4.46%, ΔSᴛᴏ₄ = +3.05%) with a relatively small self-consistency discrepancy (|ΔV-ΔS| = 1.41%) and the lowest error in the Si-O-Si angle (-2.86%). Notably, Vᴛᴏ₄ and Sᴛᴏ₄ capture distortions that bond‑length averages inherently miss and are transferable to any tetrahedral material, including zeolites, metal-organic frameworks, germanates, and phosphates. We therefore propose that tetrahedron‑normalized volume and surface area be adopted as complementary metrics to traditional bond‑length and angle analyses in future DFT benchmarking studies of tetrahedral frameworks.

papers.title: Revisiting Deep Learning DTA Methods from the Dataset Viewpoint
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a study revisiting deep learning drug-target affinity models, which are otherwise used as benchmark methods in the literature to compare more complex and heavy-weighted architectures. We focus on training and testing these models using pKd values from BindingDB, a dataset that presents binding affinity information of a high variety of ligans and proteins. These activity data need a proper pre-treatment and curation prior to actually using them for production tasks, a factor that is often overlooked in the literature. We show that a combination of a thorough curation of the dataset and a proper hyperparameter tuning of slight modifications of the revisited models (e.g, by using pretrained protein embeddings to describe the proteins) provides beyond state of the art performances at a much lower computational cost, with respect to more demanding deep learning models. We study the distributions of the protein and ligand learned (or eventually, pre-trained) embeddings, to observe how they classify the proteins depending on the (super)families they belong to (for the former), and how they distribute in the embedding space depending on the values of their binding affinities, with respect to a given protein (for the latter). We take advantage of the graph representations of the ligands to further approach explainability at an atom-wise level, by computing the directional derivative of the model with respect to each of the atoms of a ligand. This method, unlike other derivative-based approaches such as Grad-CAM and variants, turns out to be extremely useful for regression tasks of binding affinities, as this provides direct means of assessing which atoms contribute to an increase/decrease of the binding affinity, depending on both the sign of the directional derivative, and on its absolute value-an indication of how steep the function is with respect to each atom.

papers.title: VizChemoton: Visualization of Quantum Chemical Reaction Networks and Their Cheminformatics Features
papers.abstract: Automated explorations of chemical reaction networks (CRNs) guided by quantum chemistry (QC) calculations are undergoing rapid development that enables numerous applications. However, CRNs are accessible primarily through specialized quantum chemistry software without interface for cheminformatic exploitation of the generated data. Here, we present VizChemoton, an open-source module within the reaction exploration framework Software for Chemical Interaction Networks. VizChemoton enables visualization of CRNs and serves as an interface for cheminformatics applications based on conversion of molecular structures that accounts for radicals, zwitterions, and molecular complexes into string-based representations via RDKit mol objects. The conversion performance exceeded 90% of QC-generated compounds based on the evaluation of four CRNs constructed with density functional theory and extended tight-binding methods. We find that compounds absent from public structural databases correspond primarily to molecular complexes and unstable reaction intermediates. All essential QC and associated cheminformatics data are distributed in interoperable CSV and JSON formats to support downstream machine learning applications whereas reaction networks are readily visualized through a browser-based standalone HTML interface.

papers.title: Molecular Origins of CO2 Capture Behavior in Amine-Appended Nanoporous Frameworks
papers.abstract: Amine-appended porous frameworks are leading materials for direct air capture of CO 2 . Yet the molecular origins governing CO 2 uptake within their dynamic porous environments remain poorly understood, limiting the design of next-generation frameworks. We selected covalent organic framework-999 (COF-999) as exemplar for investigating CO 2 uptake behavior using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations enabled by machine-learned interatomic potentials and enhanced sampling methods. Mapping the complex free-energy surfaces reveals pocket-like amine constructs which foster CO 2 chemisorption because hydrogen bonding within such pockets lowers activation barriers. We found that the population of active amines doubles under humid conditions because water molecules expand the amine pockets and in turn increase the number of hydrogen-bonding sites. This explains the puzzling experimental observation of doubling uptake in the presence of water. Our findings allow us to propose design principles for next-generation carbon capture materials.

papers.title: Automated and reproducible detection of the glass transition temperature with unsupervised machine learning and neural network partial charges
papers.abstract: Accurate computational modeling of the glass transition is a longstanding challenge in polymer chemistry. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations offer a powerful approach to observe the changes in viscoelasticity, density and chain mobility associated with the glass transition, yet they often overestimate the glass transition temperature (T g ) and have limited sensitivity to number average molecular weight and dispersity. These deficiencies are largely attributed to high levels of noise in simulation data masking the T g , inaccurate polymer representations, and limited force field transferability. In this study, we build a robust and automated workflow to calculate T g using unsupervised machine learning, and apply it to a range of polymer models and dispersities. We show that our workflow provides improved T g estimates when compared to other established, 'bulk' measurements (e.g., monitoring changes in RMSD or density). We also benchmark different neural network charge models, which streamline polymer force field parameterization, and assess their influence on the T g .

papers.title: Beyond Exactness: Approximation Strategies to the Many-Body Schrödinger Equation for Modern Quantum Chemistry Applications
papers.abstract: The many-body Schrödinger equation is a fundamental framework for describing the behaviors of electrons in molecular systems based on quantum mechanics. It largely forms the basis for quantum-chemistry-based energy calculation and has become the core concept of modern electronic structure theory. 1 However, its complexity increases exponentially with the number of interacting particles, and its exact solution remains intractable in most cases. To bridge this gap, various approximation strategies have been developed, forming the basis of modern quantum chemistry. 1 Accurate approximation methods for the many-body Schrödinger equation enable the solution of complex, otherwise intractable problems with enhanced accuracy and balanced computational costs. This review focuses on the conceptual foundations of these approximation approaches, ranging from mean-field theories, such as Hartree–Fock, through post–Hartree–Fock correlation methods, including configuration interaction, perturbation theory, and coupled-cluster techniques, to the widely adopted density functional theory and semi-empirical models; newly emerging methods such as quantum Monte Carlo, machine learning-augmented strategies, hybrid between classical and quantum computational methods, and the theoretical frontier of holographic principle which applies Ads/CFT correspondence to approximate quantum many body system inspired by higher energy physics would also be addressed. 2-8 The accuracy and efficiency will also be briefly mentioned for those approximation methods, highlighting the trade-offs between theoretical rigor and computational feasibility. These approximation strategies for the many-body Schrödinger equation continue to be central to quantum chemistry, enabling increasingly reliable predictions of molecular structure, energetics, and dynamics with reduced computational costs.

papers.title: SFRIS: A Systematic Fragmentation-Recombination Approach for Isomer Search
papers.abstract: Constitutional isomer enumeration is a fundamental task in cheminformatics, yet systematic automated approaches remain limited for flexible molecular systems. Here, SFRIS (Systematic Fragmentation and Recombination Isomer Search) is presented as an algorithm for constitutional isomer generation via systematic bond cleavage of an input structure, placement and recombination of fragments guided by Fibonacci sphere sampling, and subsequent refinement using a two-stage optimization workflow. The algorithm was validated on 17 benchmark systems (7–17 atoms; C, H, O, N, and S) at the B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVP level of theory, successfully reproducing known low-energy isomers while identifying previously unreported stable structures. Robustness analysis based on five independent runs per molecule shows that the most thermodynamically relevant isomers are consistently generated, with near-complete reproducibility for the lowest-energy structures. The combinatorial scanning stage contributes negligibly to the total computational cost, with the dominant expense arising from the high-level optimization. The SFRIS workflow provides adjustable parameters to control the search space and is available as an open-source tool for integration into cheminformatics pipelines. Scientific contribution SFRIS introduces a topology-driven strategy for isomer generation that operates directly on arbitrary input geometries, without requiring predefined reaction coordinates or pathway exploration. By systematically enumerating candidate structures through fragmentation and recombination, the SFRIS algorithm circumvents exhaustive potential energy surface exploration, thereby providing a complementary approach to existing isomer search techniques in computational chemistry.

papers.title: β-Turn Peptide Assemblies as a New Paradigm for Highly Efficient Piezoelectric, Ferroelectric, and Nonlinear Optical Biomaterials
papers.abstract: Biocompatible and biodegradable piezoelectric and ferroelectric materials are scarce as sustainable alternatives to conventional inorganic systems, despite their significant potential for advancing eco-friendly electromechanical technologies. Here, we establish, for the first time, that supramolecular assemblies based on the fundamental secondary structures of peptides, such as β-turns, constitute a previously unexplored platform for producing exceptionally high piezoelectric voltage and current output. These findings expand the design principles of peptide-based electromechanical materials beyond the extended β-sheet and helical supramolecular architectures reported to date. Using a minimalist capped dipeptide, Boc- D Pro-Leu-NHBn-OMe ( D PL), we demonstrate that a type II’ β-turn combined with non-centrosymmetric crystal packing ( P 1) generates a peak-to-peak open-circuit voltage of 8.4 V and a short-circuit current of 4.6 μA, representing the highest energy-harvesting performance reported to date for any biomaterial, and directly powers light-emitting diodes. Moreover, D PL exhibits exceptional multifunctional properties, including an effective piezoelectric coefficient (d 33 ) of 28.34 pm V -1 , robust ferroelectric switching, second-harmonic generation (SHG), and pronounced SHG circular dichroism (g SHG-CD = 0.48), establishing its extraordinarily polar, switchable, and asymmetric nature. Mechanistically, β-turn-directed dipole organization translates peptide conformation into macroscopic polarization and enhanced electromechanical functionality. These findings establish β-turn peptide assemblies as a new paradigm for sustainable, biocompatible, and structurally programmable piezoelectric, ferroelectric, and nonlinear optical materials.

papers.title: The Statue Problem: 2D Topology Outperforms Static 3D Representations in Large-Scale Solubility Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting thermodynamic solubility requires modeling the complex interplay between a molecular solute and a bulk liquid solvent. We propose an Asymmetric Dual-Branch Architecture that is motivated by the physical distinction between the molecular solute and the bulk solvent environment. Using this framework, we investigate a critical cheminformatics debate: does representing a solute with 3D spatial coordinates inherently outperform 2D covalent topology? Evaluating on the BigSolDB v2.1 dataset (105,373 triplets) under a rigorous Bemis-Murcko scaffold split, we demonstrate that a 2D Graph Convolutional Network (R2 = 0.5007) significantly outperforms advanced 3D models, including an Equivariant Graph Neural Network (R2 = 0.4440), the Uni-Mol 3D Foundation Model (R2 = 0.4116), and a state-of-the-art SphereNet (R2 = 0.2107). We attribute this failure of 3D representations to the "statue problem": vacuum-generated 3D coordinates fail to capture dynamic solvation states, injecting spatial noise that amplifies with higher-order geometric encoding. We conclude that until solvent-aware 3D conformers become tractable, explicitly modeling solvation with 2D topology provides a significantly more robust framework for macroscopic property prediction.

papers.title: Development of d2-benzylating reagents based on pyridinium salt
papers.abstract: Deuterium-incorporated compounds play important roles across organic chemistry, deuterated drugs (drug metabolism research), and materials science, and switching deuterium from hydrogen at metabolically labile C-H bonds—particularly the α-position of heteroatoms and benzylic positions—is a valuable strategy for improving the pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles of pharmaceuticals. While d3-methylation reagents are well established, practical reagents for introducing dn-alkyl groups other than d3-methyl, especially benzylic d2-groups, remain scarce. Herein, we report the development of d2-benzylating reagents based on N-benzyl-2,4,6-triphenylpyridinium (Katritzky) salts. Treatment of N-benzyl Katritzky salts with D2O under basic condition achieves highly efficient H/D exchange (deuteration) at the benzylic position (α-pyridinium C-H bonds), affording d2-benzyl Katritzky salts with deuterium contents exceeding 99%, and this deuteration proved compatible with a range of aromatic substituents, including halogens and electron-withdrawing groups, on various benzyl moieties. The resulting d2benzyl Katritzky salts serve as versatile electrophilic d2-benzylation reagents via their iodination. Thereby, the present d2-benzylation of diverse nucleophiles, including thiols, phenols, nitrogen heterocycles, and carboxylic acids, afforded d2-benzylated products in high yield and with excellent deuterium retention. Under photochemical conditions, the same salts also function as precursors to form d2-benzyl radicals, enabling direct addition to Nheterocycles, electron-deficient olefins, and alkynes. Furthermore, the deaminative reduction of benzyl/d2-benzyl Katritzky salts with/without D2O selectively access to form d1-, d2-, and d3-methyl aromatics. This work reveals Katritzky salts as a practical and versatile platform for site-selective benzylic deuteration, applicable to both electrophilic and radical-mediated d2-benzylation, with potential utility in the synthesis of deuterated drugs and functional molecules.

papers.title: Twin Ag10 Clusters Assembled into a Discrete Complex via Direction-Tuned Cooperative Coordination
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of multiple atomically precise metal nanoclusters has emerged as a promising strategy to amplify and diversify their properties and to create functional supramolecular materials based on these materials. Here, we report the construction of a discrete complex encapsulating dimerized Ag10 clusters, whose structure in the crystalline state was observed by X-ray diffraction experiments. Such a self-assembly is achieved by modifying cooperative coordination approach that integrates acetylide protection and metal–pyridyl coordination, as confirmed through the stepwise X-ray observation of the related acetylide-protected monomeric Ag8 clsuter and its partial transformation via Ag–pyridyl capping. Photophysical measurements and quantum-chemical calculations demonstrated that the Ag10 dimer showed cluster-based photoluminescence mediated by electronic coupling between the silver cluster core and the carbazole moieties in the ligand framework, with quantum yields of 0.04 in CH2Cl2 solution and 0.10 in the solid state. This work thus suggests that the combination of discrete coordination self-assembly and acetylide-based cluster formation may indeed represent a new way to the oligomerization of large metal clusters to generate structurally precise assemblies.

papers.title: Mode-Dependent Vibrational Energy Flow in Hydrogen-Bonded Dimers: A Unified Mechanism for Intramolecular Vibrational Energy Redistribution and Vibrational Predissociation
papers.abstract: Hydrogen-bonded complexes exhibit distinct relaxation pathways depending on the initially excited local vibrational mode. Using phenol and water dimers as prototypical systems, we show that donor O-H stretching excitation leads to faster intramolecular vibrational redistribution (IVR) but slower predissociation, whereas acceptor O-H excitation preferentially transfers energy into intermolecular hydrogen-bond modes, accelerating dissociation, which aligns well with the experimental findings on the phenol dimer. We attribute this asymmetry to geometric constraints on the donor over acceptor O-H groups. Consistent with this interpretation, the structurally constrained acceptor in the sulforaphane-cysteine complex exhibits the opposite coupling pattern. A reduced Hamiltonian including donor O-H, acceptor O-H, and hydrogen-bond coordinates with harmonic and anharmonic couplings, generated from the molecular geometries, successfully reproduces the IVR and predissociation dynamics observed in the simulations. This identifies the key coupling terms governing the competing relaxation pathways, and suggests that donor-acceptor coupling asymmetry is a general feature of hydrogen-bonded systems.

papers.title: Asymmetric Immobilized Chiral Phosphoric Acid-Catalyzed Transfer Hydrogenation of Imines via Reductant Fine-tuning in Continuous Flow
papers.abstract: This article describes asymmetric transfer hydrogenation of imines with benzothiazolines using a chiral phosphoric acid (CPA) catalyst immobilized on a polystyrene support. We demonstrate that the reduction of imines with immobilized Ad-TRIP CPA using 2-napthyl-substituted benzothiazoline proceeds with excellent enantioselectivities to provide 15 chiral benzylic amines in 77-99% ee. By carrying the benzothiazoline reductant optimization in continuous flow, we were able to streamline the optimization process and identify a new superior benzothiazoline reducing agent featuring 3,5-di-tert-butylphenyl substituent that facilitated the reductions with significantly higher levels of enantiocontrol (up to 99% ee). To demonstrate the scalability of this process, a 1.1 gram-scale reduction with 3,5-di-tert-butylphenyl substituted benzothiazoline was achieved in continuous flow in 99% ee and 92% yield. In addition, a computational study using the double-ended growing-string method (GSM) and DFT established a stereochemical model for this reduction. Analysis of the hydride-transfer transition states leading to the major and minor enantiomers reveals that the selectivity arises from the interplay between a stabilizing π–π interaction with the catalyst that favors the major pathway and steric repulsions with the catalyst's 3,3′-substituents that disfavor the minor one.

papers.title: Ir-Catalyzed Enantioselective Intramolecular Allylic Dearomatization of Naphthols for the Construction of Fused Carbocyclic Ring Systems: 10-Step Total Synthesis of (+)-Daphenylline
papers.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: Intramolecular asymmetric dearomatization of naphthols offers a powerful strategy for the direct construction of architecturally complex polycyclic ring systems. We report the first iridium-catalyzed intramolecular enantioselective allylic dearomatization of naphthols that enables rapid access to fused carbocyclic frameworks bearing all-carbon quaternary stereocenters. Using allylic alcohol-tethered naphthol precursors and Carreira’s chiral iridium catalyst, the reaction exhibits broad functional-group tolerance and proceeds with excellent chemo-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivity, delivering a broad range of fused benzocyclohexanone products in up to >19:1 dr and 99% ee. The synthetic utility of this dearomatization is demonstrated in a concise 10-step total synthesis of unnatural (+)-daphenylline, Other notable features of the synthesis include a manganese-catalyzed ketone-directed regioselective ortho-C(sp2)–H allylation and five simple one-pot operations.

papers.title: Synergistic Transdermal Drug Delivery via Piezoelectric P(VDF-TrFE)/Chitosan/Gold Nanohybrid Electrospun Membranes Combined with Targeted Ultrasonic Sonoporation
papers.abstract: Transdermal administration of therapeutic ointments for cutaneous malignancies and severe localized bacterial infections is fundamentally constrained by the stratum corneum (SC) barrier. Here, we report a multi-modal transdermal drug delivery system comprising an electrospun piezoelectric Poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene)/Chitosan/Gold nanoparticle (P(VDF-TrFE)/CS/AuNP) membrane coupled with a custom-designed, multifrequency ultrasonic excitation platform (1.0–3.0 MHz). The synthesized nanohybrid membrane exhibited superior biocompatibility, enhanced mechanical flexibility, and intrinsic acoustic impedance matching with human skin. FTIR and XRD analyses confirmed high 𝛽-phase crystallinity (82.4 ± 1.8%) in the electrospun fibers, crucial for efficient electromechanical transduction. A custom dual-layer Printed Circuit Board (PCB) integrating an ATmega328P microcontroller and an AD9833 Direct Digital Synthesis (DDS) IC was fabricated to drive a PZT-5H ceramic transducer via an LC Butterworth impedance matching network. In vitro permeation tests using Franz diffusion cells demonstrated a 5.20 ± 0.28-fold increase (𝑝 < 0.001, 𝑛 = 6) in the flux of a model oncology drug (5-Fluorouracil) across porcine skin under 2.4 MHz ultrasonic stimulation (1.2 W/cm2) compared to passive diffusion. Cytotoxicity assays (MTT) using L929 fibroblasts confirmed zero allergic response and 96.8 ± 1.4% cell viability for the composite substrate. This integrative platform provides a non-invasive, highly controllable strategy for rapid local drug bio-absorption without systemic toxicity.

papers.title: SELECTIVE MECHANOPORATION OF CANCER MEMBRANES VIA ACOUSTIC RESONANCE AND LDH NANOPARTICLES: A CALIBRATED MULTISCALE IN SILICO STUDY
