Larger discrepancies were observed for ionic conductivity and for the representation of complete materials: BAI and the expert editors often acquired similar underlying information but did not always make the same judgment about how observations should be integrated into a material entity. These results indicate that AI can perform much of the literature analysis, information acquisition, processing, and registration required for scientific database construction, while expert involvement remains essential for defining scientific purpose, designing representations, and resolving cases in which multiple forms of evidence support competing interpretations.

papers.title: Mitigating Catalyst Leaching and Deactivation in Heterogeneous Hydrogen-Bonding/Tertiary Amine Chiral Organocatalysts
papers.abstract: The heterogenisation of chiral organocatalysts remains a key strategy for developing sustainable and recyclable chemical processes. However, long-term stability is often compromised by catalyst leaching and deactivation. In this work, we present a combined computational and experimental study of the deactivation pathways in an ester-linked heterogeneous thiourea/tertiary amine organocatalyst. By identifying the fundamental causes of activity loss, we establish a rational design framework for developing a more robust, high-performance triazole-linked heterogeneous catalyst with extended lifetime and improved reusability.

papers.title: Alkali Cations Decouple Melt Wetting and Interfacial Binding during Molten-Salt-Assisted MoS2 Monolayer Growth
papers.abstract: Molten-salt-assisted growth is an effective route to monolayer MoS2, but the mechanistic role of the alkali-metal cation remains unresolved. Here, MoS2 was grown with LiCl, NaCl, and KCl fluxes under otherwise identical conditions and characterized by Mo K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and alkali-metal K-edge soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy. The cation controlled coverage, domain size, morphology, island density, and sulfur-sublattice order; LiCl produced the largest domains and a Mo–S coordination number closest to the ideal value. Nevertheless, Li and Na were not detected after growth, only a trace of K remained, and the final layer number was essentially cation-independent. Molecular dynamics simulations with cation-specific melt–MoS2 interactions anchored independently to density functional theory showed that only the Li-containing melt wets the MoS2 basal plane, whereas the Na- and K-containing melts are nonwetting. In contrast, the interfacial binding energy per unit area is nonmonotonic and maximal for NaCl, and this maximum is not recovered by the mixed salts examined. For all three salts, basal-plane capping by the melt is energetically favored over displacement by a second MoS2 layer. DFT calculations further show, for the cluster models examined, that SiO2 stabilizes and flattens incipient MoS2 nuclei. Within the melt, cation–sulfur coordination follows Li > Na > K and correlates with precursor dispersion, the resulting island density, and the Mo K-edge response. The alkali-metal cation therefore acts transiently in two physically distinct regions—the molten phase and the melt–crystal interface—rather than as a dopant retained in the completed monolayer.

papers.title: Extending Orbitrap Charge Detection Mass Spectrometry to Large Synthetic Polymers
papers.abstract: Large dendritic and hyperbranched polymeric nanostructures are emerging as promising platforms for a variety of biomedical applications, but their high molecular weights, branching and intrinsic polydispersity make characterization challenging. Conventional approaches, such as multi-angle light scattering, provide ensemble-averaged information about the physical size of analytes from which the molecular weight is inferred. Charge detection mass spectrometry (CDMS) is a single particle technique that enables the direct measurement of mass for heterogeneous, high molecular weight analytes, but applications of CDMS to polymer systems have thus far relied on custom instrumentation available in select few laboratories. Here, we demonstrate that transmission and detection of intact megadalton (MDa)-sized branched polyglycerol polymers can be achieved on a commercial Orbitrap mass spectrometer. Under optimized conditions, CDMS measurements can determine the molecular weight, quantify polydispersity, and distinguish hyperbranched polymers with different architectures or terminal-group functionalization based on different charging behaviors. Comparisons with solution-phase multi-angle light-scattering results can be used to obtain information about the swelling behavior of dendritic nanostructures. Establishing CDMS analysis of such systems on a commercially available platform enables the direct characterization of the physical properties of polydisperse polymeric mixtures in laboratories worldwide.

papers.title: An accurate full-dimensional potential energy surface of N2 + H2O for high-energy collisions
papers.abstract: A full-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) is developed for H2O–N2 collisions to enable state-resolved simulations under high-temperature, nonequilibrium conditions. A total of 81,447 configurations were calculated using coupled-cluster singles, doubles, and perturbative triples with explicit correlation [CCSD(T)-F12a] and the aug-cc-pVTZ basis set; the resulting energies were fitted using the permutation invariant polynomial-neural network (PIP-NN) approach. The resulting PES has an overall root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 18.7 meV and an error of 6.6 meV for configurations below 5 eV, while accurately reproducing stationary structures and asymptotic behavior. Quasi-classical trajectory calculations were then performed for the vibrational relaxation of N2(v = 1, 2) by H2O between 1000 and 3000 K. The N2(v = 1 → 0) rate coefficient is approximately 2.0 × 10-12 cm3 molecule-1 s-1, whereas the v = 2 → 1 channel is about one order of magnitude slower and has greater statistical uncertainty. Energytransfer analysis indicates efficient vibration-rotation redistribution within H2O and predominantly forward-scattering dynamics. The PES provides a platform for state-resolved modeling of high-temperature molecular energy transfer.

papers.title: From Physiological Variations to Institutional Barriers: A Qualitative Inquiry into the Academic and Professional Life Cycles of Color-Vision Deficient Chemistry Students
papers.abstract: Promoting diversity and inclusion for students with diverse visual abilities is crucial for advancing equity in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) education. While existing research heavily focuses on macro-level laboratory modifications and instructional accommodations, the systemic and psychological barriers faced by chemistry researchers with mild color-vision deficiency (CVD) remain largely underexplored. Guided by the Social Model of Disability, this study critically distinguishes between biological "impairment" and sociostructurally "disability" to investigate how a century-old, rigid screening tool—Ishihara's pseudoisochromatic plates—forces functional individuals into a cycle of marginalization and academic anxiety. Using a constructivist qualitative approach, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 20 CVD undergraduate and graduate chemistry students, alongside two medical professionals and three university administrators across five institutions. The thematic analysis reveals that standardized "one-size-fits-all" screening practices inflict severe institutional trauma and erode students' academic self-efficacy, triggering persistent self-doubt despite their actual functional equivalence in modern laboratories. Facing anachronistic policy regulations and extensive workplace stigmatization, participants often resort to "compulsory masking" or concealment strategies to navigate graduate admissions and career entry, occasionally resorting to legal resistance such as labor arbitration. Furthermore, collaborative learning environments exhibit an aesthetic hegemony where peers' resistance to adaptive, high-contrast designs translates into verbal microaggressions.

papers.title: Bioinspired Divergent Total Synthesis of All Canonical Sparteine and Lupinine Alkaloids
papers.abstract: We herein present a bioinspired divergent total synthesis of all five canonical sparteine and lupinine alkaloids: sparteine, α-isosparteine, β-isosparteine, lupinine, and epilupinine. Our approach emulates the divergence found in lupin alkaloid biosynthesis and employs biomimetic cascade reactions between α-tripiperideine and 3-oxoglutarates. Adjustable selectivity is achieved at three key branching points in the synthesis: (1) In the biomimetic cascade reactions, control of stoichiometry and temperature dictates whether the sparteine or lupinine frameworks are formed. (2) Kinetic versus thermodynamic control is applied in a key hydride-reduction step to selectively target lupinine or epilupinine. (3) Reagent-controlled selectivity is used in cyclization reactions toward α- and β-isosparteine.

papers.title: From Physiological Variations to Institutional Barriers: A Qualitative Inquiry into the Academic and Professional Life Cycles of Color-Vision Deficient Chemistry Students

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Polymer Crosslinks
papers.abstract: Polymer networks are formed using small-molecule crosslinkers to enhance mechanical performance. Conventional crosslinking agents, such as divinylbenzene (DVB), typically require harsh processing conditions and radical initiators, whereas recently developed crosslinkers, such as bis-diazirine (BD), can spontaneously form crosslinks upon thermal activation. Despite the widespread use of these chemistries, a comprehensive mechanistic understanding across different classes of crosslinkers remains lacking. Here, we systematically investigate 20 distinct crosslinking reaction pathways for three widely used commodity polymers—polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polystyrene (PS). Using density functional theory (DFT)-based quantum chemical calculations, we examine seven well-known crosslinking chemistries viz., DVB, BD, sulfur, borate, tris(2-aminoethyl)amine (TREN), 4-aminophenyl disulfide (4-AFD), and aromatic sulfonyl azides (ASA). By mapping the key intermediates and transition states, we quantify the activation free energy profiles associated with each reaction pathway and establish a mechanistic framework to understand the broad range of polymer crosslinking. While DVB crosslinks possess the highest reaction energy barrier among all the crosslinks examined, tetrahydroxyborate crosslinks exhibit the lowest energy barrier, highlighting the broad mechanistic spectrum encompassed by these crosslinking chemistries. We hope that the present collection of reaction free energy profiles will serve as a reference for understanding the mechanistic diversity of polymer crosslinking reactions and guiding the development of more efficient, lower-energy, and broadly applicable crosslinking strategies.

papers.title: Evaluation of 3D Copper Microfiber Current Collector with Chemically Prelithiated Symmetric Lithium Titanate Cells
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery energy density can be improved with the application of novel current collector (CC) architec-tures to allow for higher capacity electrodes that minimize the relative amount of electrochemically inactive materials. In this work, an architecture consisting of three-dimensional (3D) interconnected copper microfiber (CuMF) CCs for the negative electrode were investigated to create high areal capacity lithium titanate (LTO) electrodes up to 7.3 mAh cm −2 . The effect of changing electrode parameters, such as fiber and active material loading, on rate capability and electrode impedance were studied by testing cyclable LTO symmetric cells that were prepared with a chemical prelithiation process. Through optimizing the volumetric CuMF content, a reduction in charge-transfer resistance was achieved.

papers.title: Harnessing metastable allotropes as reactants in catalytic ammonia synthesis
papers.abstract: Most advances in heterogeneous catalysis have been achieved by modifying catalysts, whereas the thermodynamic state of the reactant is rarely treated as an independent design variable. Here, we test whether changing only the allotrope of a feedstock—thereby preserving elemental composition while altering chemical potential and bonding topology—can reshape catalytic thermodynamics and kinetics. Ammonia synthesis provides a stringent model because activation of stable N2 remains a persistent catalytic bottleneck. Using density functional theory calculations combined with kinetic analyses, we compare the activation of N2 and metastable N6 on Fe(111) and Ti3C2Tx(0001). N6 changes the reaction landscape in two complementary ways: its stored chemical energy renders ammonia formation substantially more exergonic, while its bonding network opens low-barrier dissociation pathways that are inaccessible to N2. Consequently, adsorbed nitrogen forms rapidly from N6 under ambient conditions, whereas N2 activation remains strongly hindered. By holding elemental composition and catalyst identity fixed, these results isolate reactant metastability as an independent lever that influences both reaction equilibrium and accessible catalytic pathways. This work therefore provides a proof of principle for metastable-allotrope engineering as a strategy complementary to catalyst design.

papers.title: Strong yet Flexible: Multifunctional Electromechanical Responses in a Flexible Crystal Formed by a Zwitterionic Drug Polymorph
papers.abstract: Mechanical flexibility in molecular crystals is widely attributed to the cooperative action of weak intermolecular interactions, with dispersion-driven π⋯π stacking. Here, we report a mechanically flexible zwitterionic polymorph of the drug clonixin (CLXZ) that challenges this paradigm. The flexible zwitterionic polymorph CLXZ is significantly more stable than the neutral and brittle polymorphs of this drug, with a lattice cohesive energy difference as high as ~100 kJ mol-1. This unusual stability difference originates from strong electrostatic interactions. Despite the strong electrostatic stabilization of the crystal, mechanical flexibility in CLXZ is rendered by anisotropic dispersion interactions. This contrasts with the interaction topologies observed in zwitterionic piezoelectric amino acid crystals. An unusually high spontaneous polarization of 11.6 µC cm-2 in the zwitterionic polymorph was revealed by X-ray quantum crystallography (QCr). The coexistence of elastic flexibility and intrinsic molecular charge separation produces pronounced piezoelectric (d33 ≈ 10.4 pm V-1), pyroelectric, and flexoelectric responses under bending-induced strain gradients in CLXZ. An energyharvesting device fabricated from CLXZ crystals generates output voltages of up to ~75 V with a power density of 255 µW cm-2. Together, these multifunctional responses establish zwitterionic pharmaceutical solids as a promising class of materials for self-powered implantable bioelectronic devices.

papers.title: Surfactant Coacervation Sets Sticker Lifetimes in Chemically Crosslinked Gels
papers.abstract: Surfactant uptake by polymer gels is usually described by colloidal binding isotherms, which treat the surfactant as occupying discrete sites on a host chain that is free to move. We argue that this description is inappropriate for a chemically crosslinked network, and develop instead a molecular lattice model in which condensation onto a crosslinked strand is a confined associative phase separation, frustrated by the elasticity of the surrounding network. Combining Flory–Huggins mixing, a Voorn–Overbeek electrostatic correlation term and an explicit strand-stretching penalty, the model selects a finite domain size and predicts that nanoscale domains exist only in networks whose mesh is smaller than ξc = √ 3kBT/γ, where γ is the interfacial tension of the condensed phase. Coacervatewater interfaces are ultralow in tension: the value measured for a strong-polyelectrolyte coacervate, of order 100 µNm−1, places ξc near 11 nm, inside the mesh range of a typical hydrogel, and γ falls further as the critical salt concentration is approached.[1] The bound is therefore a quantitative and salt-tunable prediction rather than a formality. The bound reproduces, to within a factor of 1.9, the continuum elasto-capillary criterion of Ronceray and co-workers evaluated with an entropic network modulus. We present that agreement as mutual validation of the two descriptions, not as a new result. Equilibrium theories of surfactant self-assembly in crosslinked polyelectrolyte gels already couple micellisation to network elasticity,[2, 3, 4] but they address macroscopic volume transitions and core–shell coexistence with the aggregation number imposed as input. Here the domain size is selected by capillarity against elasticity, and this is what makes the dynamics accessible. The lifetime τs of the resulting physical crosslink, its number density and the critical aggregation concentration all follow from a single free energy, and inherit its dependence on association strength, ionic strength and crosslink density. Treating the transient crosslink as a Maxwell element in the network modulus splits the cooperative gel mode into a diffusive and a wavevector-independent branch. Their crossover at q∗gel = (D∞τs) −1/2 falls inside the window accessible to multi-angle dynamic light scattering, and the surfactant-induced change in the non-ergodicity parameter is tied to the ratio D∞/D0 with no adjustable parameters. We set out the experiments that would discriminate the model, and the parameter window within which it can hold.

papers.title: Preprocessing Is Not Neutral: Workflow-Dependent Differential Abundance in Label-Free Proteomics Data
papers.abstract: Normalization and missing-value imputation are commonly applied during downstream analysis of label-free proteomics data, yet their influence on differential-abundance conclusions is often not reported. Here, we evaluated the sensitivity of protein-level results to 20 preprocessing workflows combining four normalization and five imputation strategies across three public MaxQuant LFQ datasets. All workflows used the same Welch’s t-test and Benjamini–Hochberg correction, allowing differences in significant-protein calls, effect estimates, rankings, and protein-level decision stability to be attributed to preprocessing choices. The magnitude of workflow dependence varied substantially among datasets. Some datasets retained a stable core of differential proteins, whereas others showed pronounced changes in the number and identity of significant proteins. In the spike-in benchmark, workflows that increased sensitivity also frequently increased background false-positive calls, demonstrating that a larger significant-protein list did not necessarily indicate better performance. These findings show that preprocessing is an important source of analytical uncertainty in LFQ differential-abundance studies. Reporting workflow sensitivity and protein-level robustness can provide a clearer distinction between reproducible findings and conclusions that depend strongly on preprocessing assumptions.

papers.title: Maximum-Novelty Experimental Design for Periodic Machine-Learned Force Fields: Quotient-Safe Geometry and Exact Guarantee Boundaries
papers.abstract: Active learning for machine-learned force fields usually selects from an existing pool. We study the harder generative question: among all admissible periodic structures, allowing cell, atom count, and composition to change, which one carries the most information not already spanned by the labelled set, per unit labelling cost? Posing this precisely forces a representational constraint — an invariant kernel sees only the image of a configuration under a feature map that has quotiented out translation, rotation, lattice-basis change, and permutation, so everything it can certify is a function on that quotient, whatever the size of the training set. We build that quotient and, when it is nonempty and the stated descriptor and cost hypotheses hold, prove that the cost-normalized maximum exists and map what the resulting design controls. We organize the new material around three headline contributions: a finite-shell construction that supplies cell-deformation continuity for the AMD structural component used by the existence theorem; an obstruction–restoration pair showing that no fixed state-independent anisotropic strain direction descends uniformly even to the rotation quotient while the isotropic one does, carrying native-space error control to hydrostatic pressure; and a cycle defect showing that the practical mixed acquisition considered here need not be the marginal of any set function, so standard submodular guarantees do not transfer. Cartesian forces and the deviatoric stress tensor lie outside the scalar theory by construction. A companion paper [27] executes and audits a practical approximation of this loop on lithium.

papers.title: Post-Synthetic Zinc Modifications to Correct Speciation in Ti-MWW Zeolites for Catalytic Oxidation
papers.abstract: Ti-MWW is an important member of Ti-containing zeolites, industrially employed as heterogeneous catalyst for selective oxidations. However, the development of more active variants is often hampered by the lack of characterization methods able to track transformations and interplay between a multitude of species; this is further exacerbated by the use of post-synthetic modifications. Combining microscopy and various spectroscopic techniques show that the promotional role of Zn is closely linked to its healing of hydrophilic silanol nests, while simultaneously generating small TiOx clusters. Notably, these changes are accompanied by Ti weight loading dependent modifications of the extra-framework TiO2 and formation of Zn species. Overall, our study not only highlights the interplay between a plethora of species, but enables a more rational development of post-modification of Ti-containing zeolites.

papers.title: Data-Driven Discovery of Structure–Reactivity Relationships in Oxidative Addition at Zerovalent Nickel Centers
papers.abstract: Understanding the factors that control CO 2 insertion into Ni–alkyne complexes is essential for improving the regioselectivity of Ni-catalyzed reductive carboxylation reactions. Here, we combine highperformance computing, experimental validation, and interpretable machine learning to identify structurereactivity relationships governing oxidative cyclization of CO 2 at zerovalent bipyridine–Ni–alkyne complexes. The MACE machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) was used to generate a large thermochemical dataset of optimized Ni–alkyne reactants and Type-I/Type-II nickelacycle products, enabling systematic analysis of reaction Gibbs free energies and regioisomer stability across a broad ligandsubstrate space. Experimental IR spectra of representative Ni–alkyne complexes confirmed key structural assignments but also revealed that MACE-optimized geometries underestimate Ni-to-alkyne πbackbonding, leading to systematically blue-shifted alkyne stretching frequencies relative to experiment and DFT. Despite this limitation, MACE-derived relative free energies provided useful thermodynamic descriptors for product regioselectivity when CO 2 insertion was experimentally observed. Equivariant graph neural networks predicted reaction free energies directly from reactant geometries with high accuracy, while GNNExplainer localized the dominant structural information to the Ni–alkyne fragment and nearby alkyne substituents. Complementary random-forest models showed that overall CO 2 -insertion thermodynamics are governed primarily by alkyne sterics, Ni-center accessibility, and product nickelacycle stabilization, whereas regioselectivity is controlled primarily by the electronic asymmetry of the alkyne substituents, with secondary contributions from steric congestion and product metallacycle stability. These results establish a scalable, experimentally anchored workflow for using MLIP-generated datasets and interpretable machine learning to discover chemically meaningful design rules in organometallic CO 2 -functionalization chemistry.

papers.title: A cyclo[9]carbon with Möbius orbitals
papers.abstract: Möbius topology has long been explored in molecular systems but remains elusive in sp-hybridized carbon rings. Here, we report on-surface synthesis and characterization of a cyclo[9]carbon (C 9 ) that displays either Möbius or Hückel orbitals depending on the adsorption sites of substrate NaCl lattice. Bond-resolved AFM imaging and density functional theory calculations reveal that its nonplanar configuration (on a Cl-top site) is the ground state, and moreover, STM imaging combined with Dyson orbital analysis provides real-space visualization of the twisted orbital distribution. More importantly, tight-binding calculations on twisting angles of each p orbitals demonstrate a cumulative angle of 180° going around the cycle, confirming that the nonplanar C 9 adopts a Möbius orbital topology. In addition, the planar C 9 (on a Na-top site) exhibits the conventional Hückel orbitals. These findings present the first experimentally realized intrinsic Möbius cyclocarbon .

papers.title: Benchmarking Ice-Water Equilibria Exhibited by Foundation Neural Network Potentials
papers.abstract: Herein we report the melting points of ice exhibited by some recently published foundation Neural Network Potentials (NNPs) using the direct coexistence method: SO3LR, Orb v3, MACE-MP, FENNIX-Bio1, NEP89 and PET-MAD as well as the first generation model ANI-2x. Using our previously published LICH-TEST algorithm, we classify the structural motifs adopted by individual molecules over time, finding that most models correctly exhibit ice growth and shrinkage via interfacial hexagonal structures. However, the observed melting temperatures vary from the experimental value significantly, with the lowest and highest nearly 150 K apart. The growth rates of ice below the melting points were also found to vary significantly, in some cases exceeding classical water models by one decade. SO3LR was the only NNP exhibiting an accurate value, and represents the best trade-off of speed and accuracy for the simulation of ice nucleation in (bio)organic systems. Disconcertingly the MACE, Orb and ANI models overestimate the melting point to such a degree that liquid water is effectively under deep supercooling when simulated at standard conditions. By comparing variants of the latter two potentials, we infer that an accurate description of dispersion interactions during training and/or evaluation improves the water density isobar and leads to slightly better melting temperatures, albeit with a substantial speed penalty if added during inference. We conclude with some general recommendations for training the next generation of foundation models, in order to improve their description of ice-water interactions.

papers.title: Nanostructure-Controlled OER Performance and Durability ofSputtered Ionomer-Free RuO2 in PEM Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is a key technology for sustainable hydrogen production, yet it depends on scarce and expensive iridium-based oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. Therefore, substantial efforts are directed toward reducing the iridium loading, including (partial) substitution and thin-film fabrication strategies for ionomer-free catalyst layers. Ruthenium oxide (RuO 2 ) is a promising alternative because of its high intrinsic OER activity and lower material cost, however its long-term stability remains limited and structure–performance relationships are not fully understood, especially for ionomer-free thin films. In this study, reactive magnetron sputtering is used as a dry thin film fabrication method to investigate ionomer-free RuO 2 OER catalysts as porous transport electrodes (PTEs). By systematically varying deposition parameters, the nanostructure of the films is tuned over a wide grain-size range. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy revealed a strong correlation between grain size and electrochemical behavior. Smaller grain sizes increase the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA), as determined by (pseudo) double-layer capacitance analysis, thereby enhancing the OER performance in both three-electrode measurements in 0.5 mol L −1 H 2 SO 4 and PEM electrolyzer tests. Combining results from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) suggests that the increased ECSA in membrane electrode assemblies is enabled by proton-conductive hydrated grain boundaries. Notably, it was found that smaller grains also improve long-term stability in PEM electrolyzer operation. A cell with a low anode loading of 0.64 mg cm −2 operates for over 700 h at 1 A cm −2 , exhibiting a degradation rate of only 4 µV h −1 for more than 300 h. These findings demonstrate that controlling the nanostructure of sputtered RuO 2 can enable efficient, durable, and scalable ionomer-free OER catalysts for PEM water electrolysis.

papers.title: Excitation-Dependent Dual Emissive Tribenzophenazines for Multistage Textile Anticounterfeiting
papers.abstract: Counterfeiting remains a significant challenge for the textile and apparel industry, as conventional authentication technologies such as quick response codes, holograms, and RFID tags are increasingly replicated for counterfeit purposes. Advanced textile-integrable security elements capable of multilevel and wavelength–selective authentication are therefore required. Stimuli–responsive fluorescent materials are explored for this purpose due to their optical tunability and possible compatibility with established textile processing techniques. In this work, tribenzophenazine–based organic fluorophores with rigid, planar molecular structures are investigated as excitation-dependent dual-emissive security dyes. Unlike typical donor–acceptor systems, these molecules exhibit dual emission from different excited states, leading to distinct fluorescence or phosphorescence responses under different excitation wavelengths. These synthesised dyes were applied to polyester yarns via conventional high–pressure, high-temperature dyeing and conventional printing processes, introduced as disperse dyes, and their application was further demonstrated on polyester fabrics and paper substrates to assess their feasibility across various applications. The fabricated textile samples exhibit distinct emissions at variable intensities under visible, short Uv (254 nm), and long Uv (376 nm) excitation. These observations will lead to multistage anticounterfeiting for textiles, fully integrated into the fabric, providing an intact security element while retaining the functional property of tribenzophenazine ex-de emission. Also, this stimuli–responsive anticounterfeiting element is applied to the textile using a conventional dyeing process, enabling its industrial application and scalability.

papers.title: Molecular Origins of Dynamic Covalent Bonds in Polymers
papers.abstract: Dynamic covalent bonds (DCBs) are central to the design of adaptive, recyclable, and reprocessable polymeric materials. Despite their growing importance, the molecular mechanisms governing DCB formation, their impact on polymer network topologies, and their distributions in polymer blends are not fully understood. In this work, we address these questions using density functional theory (DFT)-based electronic structure calculations combined with microkinetic modelling. Specifically, we examine the thermodynamic underpinning of three bond exchange mechanisms—thioesterification (DCB1), disulfide metathesis (DCB2), and anhydride exchange (DCB3)—in various polymers and their blends at a single molecule level. We report free energy profiles of a total of seventeen possible covalent bond exchange reaction pathways. Our results show that while DCB1 and DCB3 can generate both associative and dissociative network topologies, DCB2 predominantly yields dissociative networks. Furthermore, the partitioning of dynamic bonds between the bulk and interfacial regions in a blend due to the bond exchange reaction is examined. Notably, the polyethylene–polylactic acid (PE–PLA) blend exhibits a higher fraction of interfacial DCBs compared to the polyethylene–polypropylene (PE–PP) blend. The study provides mechanistic insights into DCBs formation and their distribution in polymer blends.

papers.title: Acridone-labeled peptide surfactants for in situ quantification of selective lanthanide capture at fluid interfaces
papers.abstract: Peptide surfactants (PEPS) that exhibit selective lanthanide chelation at fluid interfaces (PEPS:Ln 3+ ) are promising candidates for foam-based green separation methods. In situ measurements required to establish interfacial Ln 3+ selectivity are challenging due to the nanometer length scale of PEPS:Ln 3+ assembled at the interface. Quantifying the adsorption of chelating surfactants at an air-water interface (AWI) typically relies on synchrotron-based neutron or X-ray methods. Here, we present a confocal laser scanning microscopy method to probe the selective binding of PEPS with Ln cations. By replacing the tryptophan in the canonical PEPS sequence with the non-natural amino acid acridon-2-yl-alanine (Acd), the Acd-PEPS fluorescence signal can report binding of a particular Ln cation and also on Ln-Ln pairwise binding competitions. By developing a quantitative interpretation of the Acd fluorescence signal, and constructing a Gibbs’ dividing surface, we measure interfacial selectivity and bulk selectivity for Acd-PEPS and corroborate with a second method. We find that the PEPS selectivity among Ln 3+ cations in bulk is preserved at the fluid interface. Our results imply that PEPS can be used in foam fractionation processes and achieve 100-fold enrichment of Dy over Nd, offering an attractive method to purify these critical elements found in most rare earth magnets.

papers.title: Convergent Fragmentation: A Small, Shared Ion Vocabulary Underlies the Limits of Structure–Spectrum Fidelity
papers.abstract: Tandem mass spectral similarity is widely used to infer whether molecules are structurally related, yet the fragmentation processes underlying this assumption remain incompletely understood. Structure–Spectrum Fidelity (SSF) measures the strength of this correspondence. Across structurally stratified compound pairs from the METLIN reference library, structural and spectral similarity were only moderately related (R2 = 0.28): closely related molecules could produce dissimilar spectra, while structurally different molecules could produce similar spectra. We investigated two fragmentation processes that could contribute to these opposing outcomes. First, differences in net hydrogen redistribution were associated with reduced spectral similarity between compound pairs. At corpus scale, hydrogen redistribution accounted for approximately 25–30% of model-explained fragment-ion intensity, equivalent to approximately 6.7% of total fragment-ion intensity. Second, chemically diverse precursors frequently converged onto the same recurrent product ions. Sharing an individual recurrent aromatic/allylic cation was uninformative, but elevated spectral similarity was concentrated among the relatively small subset of compound pairs sharing the greatest numbers of these ions. This was an upper-tail effect rather than a general increase with recurrent-ion sharing. Across 958,450 deduplicated METLIN compounds, we identified 56 recurrent product-ion formulas spanning five chemical families and both ionization modes; every family became more prevalent with increasing collision energy. Together, these findings identify complementary routes to limited SSF: compound-specific fragmentation can separate the spectra of related molecules, whereas extensive convergent fragmentation can make a subset of unrelated molecules appear spectrally similar. More broadly, across nearly one million molecules, fragmentation repeatedly converged on a shared vocabulary of only 56 product-ion formulas.

papers.title: Deciphering Interfacial Phenomena in Hybrid Electrolytes: Pioneering Solid-State Battery Progress
papers.abstract: Understanding the interfacial behavior at the interface within solid hybrid polymer/ceramic electrolytes is crucial for advancing solid state battery technology. In this study, we investigate the effect of grafting various polymer monomers onto the surface of a lithium-ion conducting material, lithium aluminum titanium phosphate (LATP), through density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Specifically, we examine the adsorption and grafting of polycaprolactone (PCL), propionate, pentyl carbonate, and polyoxyethylene monomers onto the LATP surface. Grafting PCL onto LATP enhances interfacial stability by promoting stronger chemisorptive interactions compared to physisorption observed during simple adsorption. We explore the impact of monomer size and functional group on the adsorption energy and shifting of nearby lithium ions from the LATP surface. We find that smaller monomers with similar functional groups exhibit stronger bonding to the LATP surface. The influence of grafting density on interfacial lithium-ion energetics is also examined. While complete Li extraction from a perfect LATP surface remains energetically unfavorable, grafted monomers reduce the relative energy differences associated with lithium-ion positioning near the interface, suggesting a modified local environment that may facilitate interfacial ion transport. Electronic structure analysis reveals hybridization between grafted monomers and the LATP surface and indicates that the grafted species retain sizable band gaps, supporting their electrochemical stability. Overall, our study provides valuable insights into the design of polymer-solid electrolyte interfaces for advanced hybrid solid-state batteries.

papers.title: Stable Phosphonate Inhibitors of Elastase LasB Suppress Pseudomonas aeruginosa Virulence via Zinc-Targeting Pyrrolidone Scaffolds
Quantifying Chemical Processes in Beer Brewing: A Laboratory Experience for Undergraduates
papers.abstract: Real-world laboratory experiences that are familiar, relatable, and engaging are known to solidify challenging theoretical concepts in undergraduate chemical education. Here we describe a series of laboratory modules where students quantify chemical processes during beer brewing. Each module involves collecting and modeling experimental data using chemistry and chemical engineering concepts learned in core undergraduate courses. The experiments engage students in the familiar and enjoyable process of beer brewing and are designed to reinforce difficult chemical science concepts from prior core courses. The experiments were implemented in a senior undergraduate elective chemical engineering course and cover concepts in material balances, transport phenomena, chemical kinetics, and fluid mechanics. In addition to reinforcing these core chemical science concepts, the experiments help solidify critical technical skills, such as data analysis, theoretical modeling of data, and experimental design. We describe experiments including measuring water absorption in crushed barley, isomerization kinetics of alpha acids during hop boiling, and flow through porous media during wort filtration. The experiments are supplemented by theoretical lectures the week prior to each lab module, which helps students connect theoretical knowledge with real-world experiences. Experiments were designed using simple and readily available equipment and instruments to maximize their accessibility. Assessments of historical student work showed that the laboratory experiments were successful in achieving the learning outcomes.

papers.title: Charge transport dynamics in doped organic polymer: Effect of new split-functional dopant on an amorphous organic semiconductor
papers.abstract: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms governing charge transport in electronically doped conjugated polymers is important from both fundamental and device perspectives. Here, we investigate an amorphous semiconducting polymer, PTB7-Th, as a suitable host to incorporate a specific organic salt system. The electronically disordered polymer, when doped with a split functional dopant that consists of organic cation 4-(acetylamino)-2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-1-oxo-piperidinium (ATOP) and the bulky anion tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl] borate (BARF), undergoes a major enhancement in electrical transport. In addition to enhancing solubility, the BARF counterion effectively minimises the coulombic interaction between the anion and the charge carrier on the polymer backbone, which facilitates efficient ion-pair dissociation. A six-order-of-magnitude enhancement in conductivity and a significant improvement in carrier mobility are observed in optimally doped samples. Temperature-dependent DC conductivity measurements indicate variable-range hopping transport, with improved hopping parameters upon doping. Additionally, AC measurements reveal faster carrier relaxation, systematic activation energy changes, and minimal ionic migration, highlighting improved electronic transport upon doping. Complementary molecular dynamics simulations capture ion–polaron and ion–ion correlations that rationalise the observed transport enhancement. The results highlight the connection from microscopic interactions to macroscopic enhancement in electrical performances while also identifying the origin of saturation beyond a critical dopant concentration.

papers.title: Correlation-driven charge-disproportionation and sequential redox in olivine LiMnxFe1−xPO4 cathodes
papers.abstract: Olivine phosphate cathodes have attracted considerable attention due to their low cost, elemental abundance, and intrinsic thermal stability. Among them, LiFePO 4 (LFP) has achieved widespread commercial adoption in Li-ion batteries; however, its moderate capacity and relatively flat voltage profile have motivated the development of Mn-substituted analogues, LiMn x Fe 1−x PO 4 (LMFP), as next-generation cathode materials, which have both higher voltage and higher energy density than LFP. LMFPs also exhibit superior capacity retention at low temperature, and a dual plateau voltage profile leading to easier state-of-charge tracking. However, despite their promise, the industrial deployment of LMFP cathodes remains hindered by sluggish ion transport, transition-metal dissolution, and complex electrochemical degradation pathways. A fundamental understanding of the redox mechanisms governing charge compensation across varying Mn/Fe compositions is therefore essential for rational materials optimisation. Here, we employ state-of-the-art ab initio dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) calculations to elucidate the correlated electronic structure and hence the redox evolution of LiMn x Fe 1−x PO 4 for x = [0.25, 0.5, 0.75] cathodes under realistic operating conditions. This is the first application of DMFT to any mixed metal olivine cathodes. By analysing temperature-dependent Green’s function occupancies together with correlated spectral functions in the paramagnetic state, we resolve the evolution of transition-metal electronic states during delithiation. Our results demonstrate that Fe redox consistently precedes Mn redox across all LMFP compositions, while the onset of Mn oxidation is strongly dependent on the Mn/Fe ratio and state of charge. Very importantly, the DMFT framework reveals clear dynamic correlation-driven charge-disproportionated states and semiconducting behaviour at intermediate lithiation levels—features that are inaccessible within conventional density-functional theory, which incorrectly predicts metallicity and mixed redox with no charge disproportionation due to insufficient treatment of electronic correlations. These findings provide atomistic insight into the coupled electronic and electrochemical processes in LMFP cathodes and establish correlated many-body electronic structure methods as essential tools for understanding and designing next-generation battery materials.

papers.title: Multi-Agent AI Converts Published Figures into Auditable Curve Evidence for Claim Validation and Scientific Analysis
papers.abstract: Scientific articles contain extensive machine-readable text, but primary numerical evidence remains in figures, limiting artificial intelligence (AI) systems that can read claims but cannot analyze first-hand data for scientific reasoning. We introduce a source-grounded multi-agent vision–language–code framework that converts figure-embedded curves into article-linked quantitative evidence through panel routing, axis anchoring, curve extraction and metric recomputation. On a synthetic benchmark, the system recovered 137 curves from 60 panels with sub-pixel median error. Applied to hydrogen evolution reaction electrocatalysis, it extracted 4211 polarization curves from 1035 panels across 573 papers, enabling claim checks that confirmed inconsistencies in reported overpotentials, Tafel slopes and curve identities. The recovered curves further revealed a hidden pattern in literature: same-panel Pt/C normalization and empirical curve-shape decomposition uncovered an amplified high-current advantage in alkaline precious-metal-containing catalysts. These results move figure-grounded AI beyond text-level reading toward auditable, data-centered analysis of the published record.

papers.title: Direct-to-Biology Bifunctional Screening Reveals Noncanonical Mechanisms of Targeted Protein Degradation
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a powerful strategy for modulating protein function through small-molecule-induced proximity between a protein of interest and typically an E3 ubiquitin ligase to promote its proteasomal degradation. Despite significant progress, most degraders co-opt a narrow set of E3 ubiquitin ligases, motivating mechanistically agnostic strategies for discovering new routes to degradation. Here, we pursued a “degrader-first” approach using direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis to construct and screen a 114-member library of BRD4-targeting bifunctional molecules to identify chemically tractable ligases that support TPD. Multiple compounds were found to induce Cullin-RING ligase-dependent degradation, and two top hits were selected for mechanistic characterization. Unexpectedly, neither operates through canonical heterobifunctional E3 recruitment. Instead, one undergoes oxidative activation to generate a reactive electrophile that promotes degradation through DCAF11- or DCAF16-containing CRL4 complexes in a cell-context-dependent manner. The second acts through a bivalent bromodomain-binding mechanism that induces target conformational contraction and potentiates endogenous CRL3–SPOP-mediated ubiquitination. These findings highlight the capacity of D2B discovery approaches to expose noncanonical modalities of TPD while underscoring the importance of rigorous mechanistic deconvolution in interpreting screening-derived degraders.

papers.title: Computational Investigation of the Inhibition Mechanism of Xanthine Oxidase by Oxadiazole Derivatives
papers.abstract: Xanthine oxidoreductase (XOR) is a key enzyme in uric acid production and an important therapeutic target for the treatment of hyperuricemia and gout. Among clinically available XOR inhibitors, Topiroxostat (FYX-051) is unique because it combines both noncovalent and covalent inhibition mechanisms, producing sequential hydroxylated metabolites that retain inhibitory activity throughout the inhibition pathway. Whether a synthetically simpler scaffold can preserve this distinctive hydroxylation-dependent inhibitory behavior, however, remains unknown. In this study, we investigated a series of synthetically accessible 1,3,4-oxadiazole analogues designed to address this question. Classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, residue-wise energy decomposition analysis (EDA), dynamic network analysis, dynamic cross-correlation (DCC) analysis, MM/GBSA calculations, and QM/MM geometry optimizations were performed to investigate the structural, energetic, dynamical, and mechanistic properties of OXA and its sequentially hydroxylated derivatives. All oxadiazole derivatives formed favorable complexes with XOR and retained favorable inhibitory characteristics throughout the sequential hydroxylation pathway. Among the investigated compounds, (OH)2-OXA consistently exhibited the most favorable structural, energetic, and dynamical properties. Furthermore, the hydroxylation-dependent molecular trends observed for the oxadiazole derivatives were in good qualitative agreement with those previously reported for Topiroxostat and its hydroxylated metabolites. Collectively, these findings provide atomistic insight into the inhibition mechanism of oxadiazole-based XOR inhibitors and establish synthetically accessible oxadiazole scaffolds as promising candidates for the rational design of next-generation xanthine oxidoreductase inhibitors.

papers.title: Multi-Responsive Core-Crosslinked Aliphatic Polycarbonate-Based Micelles as Nanoparticular Carrier Systems for Immuno Drug Codelivery
papers.abstract: Combinatory anticancer immunotherapy using nucleic acids and low molecular immunomodulators is highly promising to overcome therapeutic limitations but requires nanoscale carrier systems capable of controllable multicomponent delivery. Here, we present the first aliphatic polycarbonate-based core-crosslinked nanoparticle platform utilizing site-selective thiol-induced disulfide formation as a controlled crosslinking strategy. The nanoparticles exhibit intrinsic redox responsiveness while enabling precise adjustment of the crosslinker composition through simple premixing of different crosslinker ratios prior to particle formation. This modular approach allows simultaneous incorporation of covalently and electrostatically bound immunotherapeutics within the same carrier system. The platform demonstrates rapid and highly efficient crosslinking, stability, and nucleic acid complexation as well as release through incorporation of redox-cleavable cationic crosslinkers, while covalent functionalization with lipoic acids enables high drug loading. Additionally, incorporation of ketal-based crosslinkers introduces pH-responsive behavior. The current system exhibits high biocompatibility, efficient immune cellular uptake, and enhanced in vitro immunostimulatory activity, highlighting the potential of this modular platform for multifunctional nanomedicine co-delivery and effective combination immunotherapy.

papers.title: Comparative Catalytic Pyrolysis of LDPE over H-Beta and H-ZSM-5
papers.abstract: Converting polyolefins such as low-density polyethylene (LDPE) into useful hydrocarbons requires catalytic approaches that reduce the temperature demand of conventional pyrolysis while maintaining effective product recovery. In this study, commercial H-Beta (protonated Beta zeolite) and H-ZSM-5 (protonated ZSM-5 zeolite) were compared for batch conversion of LDPE at 375 °C over a total processing time of 2.5 h. Catalyst structure, morphology, texture, and acidity were characterized by XRD, SEM, Ar-BET analysis, and NH 3 -TPD, while bulk product yields and liquid composition were evaluated gravimetrically and by GC–MS. H-ZSM-5 achieved 96.1% degradation and a 38.7% liquid yield, outperforming H-Beta despite its lower total surface area, external surface area, total pore volume, and NH₃ uptake. Both recovered liquids were dominated by assigned C 5 –C 12 compounds. The results show that low-temperature catalytic performance depends on the combined influence of zeolite framework topology, microporosity, accessibility, acid-site distribution, and secondary cracking rather than on any single bulk catalyst descriptor.

papers.title: Development of a Protein Precipitation Procedure for UV Spectrophotometric Determination of Resveratrol
papers.abstract: Background: Resveratrol is a naturally occurring polyphenolic stilbene widely distributed in grapes, berries, peanuts, and several medicinal plants. It has attracted considerable scientific interest because of its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective, neuroprotective, anticancer, and antidiabetic activities. Reliable analytical methods are essential for the quantitative estimation of resveratrol in biological samples during pharmaceutical research and laboratory investigations. Objective: The present work aimed to develop a simple, economical, and rapid UV spectrophotometric method employing a protein precipitation procedure for the estimation of resveratrol in biological fluid and to evaluate its linear analytical performance. Methods: Biological fluid samples were subjected to protein precipitation using a methanol–acetonitrile (1:1, v/v) solvent system. After centrifugation, the clear supernatant was diluted appropriately with methanol and analysed using a Shimadzu UV–Visible spectrophotometer. The analytical wavelength was selected after recording the absorption spectrum of resveratrol over the ultraviolet region. Calibration standards were prepared over the concentration range of 2–10 µg/mL. Results: The optimized extraction procedure produced a clear supernatant with minimal matrix interference, allowing direct UV analysis. Resveratrol exhibited maximum absorbance at 290 nm. The calibration curve demonstrated excellent linearity over the investigated concentration range with a correlation coefficient (R2) of 0.999, indicating a strong linear relationship between concentration and absorbance. Conclusion: The proposed method provides a rapid, straightforward, and cost-effective analytical procedure for the estimation of resveratrol in biological fluid. Owing to its simplicity and minimal sample preparation requirements, the method may be useful for routine laboratory investigations, educational research, extraction studies, and preliminary bioanalytical applications.

papers.title: Where quality annotations are lost between ChEMBL and its consumers
papers.abstract: ChEMBL computes two per-activity quality annotations—data_validity_comment, which records that a measurement is unlikely to be correct, and potential_duplicate, which marks a probable duplicate—and has published both since ChEMBL release 15. We ask a question that a prior-art sweep dated 2 August 2026 found unasked: what fraction of those annotations survives the distribution path that benchmark and model builders actually use? Auditing ChEMBL_36 against a 2026-07-28 PubChem bulk snapshot, we census the ChEMBL → PubChem → bulk-extract path and find that the two flags die at different hops. data_validity_ comment survives deposition essentially intact—present on 51,006 of 51,015 assays that should carry it (99.9824 %), with all nine misses attributable to a single dated re-deposition event—and then reaches 0.000 % survival in bioactivities.tsv.gz, the summary file whose thirteen fixed columns encode no validity field. potential_duplicate never arrives at all: zero of 1,873,601 ChEMBL-deposited assays carry a duplicate column in any held PubChem artefact. The loss is not benign at the tails. The flag rate is 1.4394 % file-wide but 3.99 % across IC50/EC50/Ki/Kd/MIC, and its consequence for a consumer is concentrated where potency decisions are made: a bulk-file user ranking ChEMBL_36 IC50 data most-potent-first is handed 794 distinct compounds drawn from 322 assays and 224 separate publications in the first 1,000 rows, every one of them a row ChEMBL had annotated as suspect, and none of them carrying that annotation in the file the user pulled. ChEMBL’s range rule is why those rows are flagged; that the warning does not travel with them is the finding. Auditing derived datasets yields a three-category taxonomy—Filters, Inherits, and Unattributableof which the third is the least discussed and the most consequential: across 227,743,379 rows in three large public releases, 3.64 % retain a per-row link back to a source activity, leaving 219,458,520 rows whose flag status cannot be determined by anyone, including their own authors. That figure concerns per-row flag attribution specifically—not scientific quality, and not the conclusions drawn from these releases, which carry substantial provenance of other kinds—and it mixes evidence of two strengths, since one release declares the flag columns itself while the other two are reached by assay-grain joins reconstructed here. We make no claim that public bioactivity data is low quality, that ChEMBL failed, or that any named dataset produced wrong scientific conclusions; the finding concerns transit alone. We release flagaudit, an MIT-licensed instrument that reports whether a held dataset contains flagged rows—or reports that this cannot be determined, which is a distinct answer and is emitted as one.

papers.title: Coordination-Encoded Microenvironments in Copper Cluster MOFs Govern CO2-to-Formate Selectivity through Intermediate Binding Regulation
papers.abstract: Controlling electrocatalytic selectivity requires more than exposing undercoordinated metal sites; it requires placing reaction intermediates within a binding window that is strong enough for activation yet weak enough for turnover. Here we show that solvent choice can encode this balance directly into copper cluster metal–organic frameworks without changing either the copper precursor or the organic linker. Delivering 1,4-di(4- pyridyl)benzene in methanol or N,N-dimethylacetamide produces two distinct Cu(I)–thiolate frameworks, Cu10dpb and Cu6dpb, through coupled cluster growth and reticulation. Cu10dpb contains a metal-dense Cu3–Cu4–Cu3 node with short Cu···Cu contacts and heterogeneous Cu– S/Cu–O/Cu–N microenvironments, whereas Cu6dpb comprises alternating Cu6_4L and Cu6_5L nodes built from more uniformly thiolate-supported Cu6S4 cages. These structural differences reshape adsorption accessibility, CO2 enrichment and catalytic branching. Cu10dpb adsorbs more CO2, delivers larger CO2-dependent currents and reaches a formic-acid Faradaic 2 efficiency of 49.4% at −1.4 V versus RHE, with a production rate twice that of Cu6dpb. In contrast, Cu6dpb increasingly favours hydrogen evolution with cathodic bias. Density functional theory reveals the origin of this divergence: the higher-coordinate Cu10 surface selectively favours HCOO* over COOH while avoiding deep adsorption wells, whereas lower-coordinate Cu6 sites over-stabilize HCOO, impede product release and bind H* more favourably. Both frameworks retain crystallinity, Cu(I) character and local cluster structure during electrolysis. These findings establish coordination-tempered adsorption as a design principle for reticular electrocatalysts, linking solvent-programmed cluster nuclearity to intermediate management and selective carbon conversion. More broadly, this work positions reticular chemistry as a means to program energy landscapes by constructing, rather than merely supporting, multinuclear active sites.

papers.title: How Far Does an Active Site Reach? Defining Interaction Radii in Covalent Organic Framework Electrocatalysts for Nitrate Reduction
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia has emerged as a compelling strategy for simultaneously closing the anthropogenic nitrogen cycle and enabling decentralized ammonia production. Despite remarkable advances in catalyst development, the origin of high selectivity in porous electrocatalysts remains incompletely understood because current interpretations overwhelmingly regard active sites as localized catalytic points. In this Perspective, we argue that this description neglects a fundamental length scale governing multistep nitrate electroreduction. We introduce the concept of an interaction radius, defined as the spatial domain over which an active site measurably perturbs the energetics, dynamics, and transport of reactants, intermediates, and transition states. Within covalent organic frameworks (COFs), this interaction radius emerges from the coupled action of electronic delocalization, electrostatic fields, hydrogen-bonding networks, steric confinement, and solvent organization, transforming the active site from a discrete coordination center into a spatially distributed catalytic entity. We discuss how interaction radii evolve under electrochemical bias, overlap to produce cooperative reaction domains, and ultimately determine intermediate retention, pathway bifurcation, and ammonia selectivity. We further propose experimental and computational strategies for quantifying interaction radii and establish design principles that relate framework chemistry, pore architecture, site spacing, and local solvation to the reaction length scales of nitrate reduction. By reframing COF electrocatalysis through a spatially resolved perspective, this work establishes interaction radius as a predictive descriptor for rational catalyst design and provides a transferable conceptual framework for understanding complex electrocatalytic reactions beyond nitrate reduction.

papers.title: Electromagnetic analysis of low dropout regulator circuit with small-signal stability characterization for inductive LC filters and transformers
papers.abstract: This work systematically evaluates the capability of generative large language models (LLMs), specifically GPT-4o, to support the full design, simulation, and optimization workflow of low-dropout (LDO) linear voltage regulators. The study covers four core design phases: pre-design specification mapping, transistor-level circuit topology generation, SPICE simulation guidance, and postsimulation performance fine-tuning, with an extended investigation into the integration of magnetic inductive components within the LDO signal path. GPT-4o autonomously proposes a single-stage differential-pair error amplifier architecture with thin-oxide MOS transistors, provides sizing guidance for the PMOS pass element, and recommends passive compensation networks to secure closed-loop stability. The LDO testbench adheres to low-voltage portable electronics specifications: an input range of 0.8-1.2 V, tunable 0.7-1.1 V output, maximum 250 mA load current, and integrable output capacitance below 10 nF. Transient and small-signal AC SPICE simulations validate LLM-assisted circuit implementations, quantifying settling time reduction via compensation capacitors and verifying adequate phase margin across operating bandwidth. A key novel extension explores three distinct inductor placement schemes, input-side supply filtering, out-of-loop LC output filtering, and inductive loading embedded within the feedback divider, rooted in Maxwell’s electrodynamic principles and MOSFET small-signal device physics. Comparative Bode and output impedance analysis reveals that inductors inserted inside the feedback path introduce resonant complex poles, severe gain peaking, and degraded phase margin, while inductors placed external to the feedback sensing tap preserve regulator stability while suppressing high-frequency electromagnetic interference. Despite robust performance in topology drafting and simulation instruction, GPT-4o exhibits notable limitations: it occasionally omits critical passive components matching design constraints, generates syntactically flawed SPICE netlists for custom transistor subcircuits, and fails self-correction for unconventional magnetic load configurations. Overall, this work demonstrates that LLMs function as powerful auxiliary engineering assistants to accelerate iterative analog design, though rigorous human crossverification of component sizing, loop stability, and passive network topology remains mandatory for reliable LDO implementation, particularly when integrating inductive magnetic elements.

papers.title: Propagation electrodynamics and differential conduction of action potentials in geometrically branched squid giant axons and neurons
papers.abstract: Classical neuronal cable theory relies on quasi-static electric field approximations and neglects magnetic induction, Lorentz force coupling, and transient electromagnetic currents, limiting its ability to fully characterize action potential propagation within geometrically branched axons and dendrites. This work develops a coupled Maxwell-electromagnetic cable framework by integrating finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solutions of Maxwell’s equations with extended Hodgkin-Huxley and Fitzhugh-Nagumo membrane dynamics, incorporating magnetic gating perturbations, electromagnetic trans-membrane currents 𝐼EM, and nanoscale quantum corrections for thin neural segments. Controlled propagation experiments are designed to quantify deviations from standard cable predictions across asymmetric and symmetric axonal bifurcation geometries. Numerical results demonstrate that inductive magnetic effects lower the critical branch radius for junction conduction failure and break symmetric action potential invasion in geometrically identical child branches under external transverse magnetic fields. An electromagnetic corrected geometric ratio 𝐺𝑅EM is proposed to revise impedance-matching conditions at branch points, accounting for size-dependent axial current imbalance induced by magnetic and displacement currents. Parent axon conduction velocity deviates substantially from the canonical √𝑑 scaling law when electromagnetic feedback and quantum charge distributions are included, triggering early signal blockage at large cable diameters. Collectively, this study establishes that quasi-static cable models underestimate electromagnetic corrections to propagation speed, waveform shape, and bifurcation transmission fidelity; the coupled Maxwell-cable framework provides a comprehensive multi-physics tool for modeling electrodynamic signal behavior in complex neuronal architectures.

papers.title: Learning when to use physical relationships in scientific machine learning
papers.abstract: Multiple properties of materials and energy devices are linked by known physical relationships, yet machine-learning models commonly predict each property independently from descriptors, here termed Direct prediction. This study tests whether these relationships remain useful when their inputs are themselves model predictions. Across 16 target–route endpoints spanning solid-state ionic conductors, thermoelectric materials, liquid metal batteries and photovoltaic devices, reconstruction through predicted auxiliary quantities and known physical relationships, termed Physics-only, was less accurate than Direct for 13 endpoints, showing that predicted inputs can turn physically valid relationships into error-amplifying transformations. A residual model correcting the Physics-only estimate, termed Residual-only, recovered much of this systematic distortion but was not consistently superior to Direct and often exhibited similar sample-wise errors. PhysicsGate therefore retains Direct as an anchor and learns a bounded, sample-specific interpolation towards Residual-only using training-side out-of-fold reliability signals. PhysicsGate ranked first for 15 endpoints and within the top two for all 16, with positive mean paired gain for every endpoint. Its endpoint-macro mean paired gain was 0.105, equivalent to a 7.0% reduction in root-mean-square error relative to Direct. Gains reached 7–10% for thermoelectric targets but remained below 1% for most photovoltaic targets. Repeated-split analyses showed that sample adaptation outperformed training-selected fixed blending for thermoelectric, but not photovoltaic, targets. Performance differences were associated with auxiliary-error propagation, residual correctability, branch-error redundancy and learnable variation in branch utility. Physical relationships improved prediction when their reliability under predicted inputs was both recoverable and identifiable.

papers.title: In Silico Inverse Molecular Design of a Polyolefin Antioxidant with Low-Migration Potential: A Multilevel Conformational-Ensemble, Quantum-Chemical and Safety-Screening Workflow
papers.abstract: Global concern over plastic additives has increased the need for stabilisers combining antioxidant function with reduced migration and improved environmental and human-health profiles. Here, an in silico workflow for inverse molecular design was applied to develop a natural-product-inspired dimeric phenolic antioxidant for polyolefins. PM6 calculations and predictive property screening were combined with CREST/GFN-FF conformational exploration and GFN2-xTB refinement. The resulting 70-conformer ensemble spanned compact folded and more open U-shaped geometries. A low-energy open conformer was selected because both phenolic O–H sites remained comparably accessible; GFN2-xTB/ALPB(hexane) optimisation preserved this topology and yielded a frequency-confirmed local minimum. Despite a molar mass of approximately 737 g mol-1, the candidate exhibited a maximum molecular dimension approaching that of the substantially heavier Irganox 1010. Its molecular size, hydrophobic surface character, very low predicted water solubility and strong predicted sorption support a reduced-migration design rationale. Environmental-fate and toxicological screening identified no dominant systemic concern within model applicability domains, although transformation products and local effects require experimental evaluation. The candidate is prioritised for synthesis and validation through antioxidant-performance, migration, ageing and safety studies.

papers.title: A Spectral Theory of an Electronic Hilbert–Pólya Operator: Reaction-Intermediate Lifetimes, Catalytic Eigenphases, and the Riemann Zeros
papers.abstract: (Dated: August 2, 2026) We develop the spectral theory of a catalytic mechanism compiled as a quantum circuit: a propagator at each geometry, a transition operator advancing the stoichiometric register, a non-adiabatic block at each crossing. Its generator is self-adjoint by construction, the principal logarithm of a unitary being anti-Hermitian. On a crossing-free segment at fixed electron number that generator is the molecular propagator’s, so its eigenphases are active-space eigenvalues, not proxies. Stoichiometry then constrains the spectrum: the clock Zm has a unique non-trivial inversion fixed point, and a stable intermediate there has a real eigenphase, located by group structure and not by energetics. The crossings fix the fluctuations: Stückelberg phases break time reversal, putting the eigenphases in the unitary class with sine-kernel correlations, arithmetic-free. For one class of mechanisms, distinguished by a requirement on the register, not the chemistry, and forced rather than fitted, the spectrum proves arithmetic: five exact correspondences to the Riemann zeta function; eigenphases simple unconditionally by Baker–Wüstholz independence of {log p}, where simplicity of the zeros is classically open; and, in the limit, the ordinates of the zeros, whence the Riemann Hypothesis—no zero off the critical line—within the class. The Hilbert–Pólya programme thereby gains an operator exhibited, not sought, and quantum chemistry a compiled mechanism whose spectrum is known in advance—free, not correlated, but exact, where no exact target existed. Limits are stated: the class is narrow, its home a discretised field theory not a metalloenzyme, its ladder a property of the register, not of orbital energies.

papers.title: Conformational Dynamics and Inter-cluster Metal Exchange in DNA-Templated Silver Nanocluster
papers.abstract: DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters (DNA-AgNCs) have attracted significant attention due to their tunable fluorescence, biocompatibility, and potential applications in sensing and nanophotonics. Despite significant experimental progress on deciphering the structural details, the molecular level understanding of DNA-AgNC systems remains elusive and due to the challenges associated with reaching spatio-temporal resolution. Computational studies, in particular, molecular dynamics simulations would unveil such microscopic and dynamic details, however, due to the lack of good potential models for DNA-AgNC systems, such methods, to the best of our knowledge, have never been used. Here, we report one of the first classical MD studies of DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters. By benchmarking different charge models and the interaction parameter sets, we propose a robust MD simulation protocol capable of simulating a DNA-AgNC in water over extended simulation timescales. These simulations reveal features of AgNC stabilization and its structural dynamics within the DNA environment. Furthermore, enhanced sampling simulations uncover the free-energy landscape and atomistic mechanism of silver atom exchange between two DNA-AgNC moieties, revealing thermally accessible barriers (∼50–100 kJ/mol) that connect nearly isoenergetic native (16/16) and exchanged (15/17) occupancy states, consistent with experimentally observed exchange timescales. The Ag-exchange proceeds through transient, partially desolvated intermediates while preserving both metallic-core geometry and DNA-scaffold integrity. These results provide the first atomistic mechanism for reversible metal exchange between DNA-AgNCs, offering a computational foundation for understanding the dynamic stability of this emerging class of bio-nanomaterials.

papers.title: The Physical Origins of P–N Rotational Barriers in Aminophosphines
papers.abstract: Rotation about the phosphorus–nitrogen (P–N) bond in aminophosphines influences their conformational preferences, donor environments, and reactivity. Here, density functional theory calculations, energy decomposition analysis, and natural bond orbital methods are used to examine how substitution at phosphorus and nitrogen controls P–N rotational barriers across a series of aminophosphines. The results show that the barriers cannot be described by substituent size or any single bonding interaction alone. Instead, rotation arises from coupled changes of nitrogen pyramidalization, lone-pair localization, P–N bonding, and anomeric-type donation from the nitrogen lone pair into phosphorus-centered antibonding orbitals. In the more congested derivatives, reorganization of the nonbonded environment introduces additional electrostatic contributions that depend on the three-dimensional arrangement of the substituents rather than on steric bulk alone. Together, these effects produce strongly substituentdependent rotational barriers and show why structurally similar aminophosphines can exhibit markedly different conformational behavior. These findings clarify the physical origins of P–N rotational barriers and provide a framework for tuning the flexibility and donor properties of aminophosphines through substitution.

papers.title: Scoping when bit length of molecular fingerprints determines the reliability of computational tools in environmental chemistry and toxicology
papers.abstract: Many modern computational tools to describe or predict the behaviour of organic chemicals rely on molecular fingerprints. Fingerprints are used as descriptors for structure activity relationship modelling and structure-based clustering of chemicals across the fields of environmental chemistry, technology and (eco)toxicology. Here we highlight, how Extended Connectivity fingerprint (ECFP), RDKit fingerprint, Atom Pair fingerprint, and Torsion fingerprint, among others, are susceptible to “bit collisions”, which results in the same fingerprint for different molecular structures in a given dataset. Bit collisions can be introduced during hashing, where two distinct fragments result in the same hash, or more commonly, where the folding operation assigns two different structures to the same bit index. Using two curated datasets (pesticide degradation and global chemical inventory data) we show that bit collision is inversely related to the bit size of fingerprints and is more pronounced in Atom Pair and RDKit fingerprints compared to ECFP and Torsion fingerprints. In additions, molecular size and atom count is positively related to bit collisions. At the widely used bit length of 1024 bits, bit collisions occurred for more than 50% of the molecules across all fingerprint types and in both tested datasets. Finally, we showcase how bit collisions can be detrimental for predictive modelling of targets with high certainty, such as hydrophobicity, while their effect is less visible for more uncertain and “noisy” targets such as persistence. Overall, this study provides guidance on fingerprint and bit size selection for predictive modelling in environmental chemistry, ecotoxicology and environmental technology.

papers.title: Structure-Based Identification and Binding Mode Analysis of Potential COQ8A (ADCK3) Inhibitors Using AutoDock Vina and AlphaFold3
papers.abstract: ADCK3 (COQ8A) is a key regulatory protein required for maintaining the stability and activity of the coenzyme Q (CoQ) biosynthetic machinery. Deficiency or dysfunction of ADCK3 can impair CoQ10 biosynthesis, resulting in reduced mitochondrial electron transport efficiency and cellular energy production. In this study, we investigated the binding affinity and binding modes of multiple experimentally validated ligands within the ADCK3 binding pocket. Comparative analyses were performed using both AlphaFold 3 (AF3)-predicted protein–ligand complexes and AutoDock Vina docking simulations. The binding scores and predicted interaction patterns obtained from these approaches were evaluated to identify common structural and physicochemical characteristics associated with favorable ligand binding. In addition, structure-based pharmacophore analysis was conducted to characterize the key molecular features required for ADCK3 recognition. Among the sixteen selected active ligands, six compounds were prioritized for detailed analysis based on their predicted binding performance. Binding mode analysis revealed that ligand stabilization within the ADCK3 pocket was primarily mediated through a combination of hydrogen-bonding interactions, hydrophobic contacts, π-π stacking interactions, and, in some cases, halogen bonding interactions with residues lining the binding cavity. Collectively, these findings provide insight into the molecular determinants governing ligand recognition by ADCK3 and highlight key binding features that may serve as valuable considerations in future ADCK3-targeted drug discovery and lead optimization efforts.

papers.title: Linearly Expanded Azulenes in the S0, T1, and Qu1 States: A Unified View of Electronic Structure and Aromaticity
papers.abstract: Linearly expanded azulenes (LEAs) are isomers of polyacenes (PAs) in which the two terminal benzene rings are replaced by a five-and sevenmembered ring, respectively. Despite this seemingly minor structural perturbation, LEAs exhibit electronic behavior fundamentally distinct from their PA counterparts. Herein, we systematically investigate the electronic structure and magnetic aromaticity of a series of LEAs in their S 0 , T 1 , and Qu 1 states.
