In this work, we derive, for the first time, lattice dynamics expressions that allow for a fully atomistic treatment of molecular flexibility with a commonly used force field in CSP, relying on distributed multipole moments for the description of electrostatic interactions. We implement these expressions in the CrystalDynamics algorithm to calculate dispersion curves, phonon density of states and vibrational free energies and we demonstrate its application to molecular crystals of three compounds of increasing size and molecular flexibility. The analytical derivations underlying our proposed methodology result in an efficient and robust evaluation of the free energy of molecular crystals. Our work facilitates the study of relative stability as a function of temperature, enabling the evaluation of enantiotropic transitions between crystal forms. Thanks to its low computational cost our suggested method can be integrated into CSP protocols to bridge the gap between static lattice energies computed at 0 K and temperature-dependent free energies.

papers.title: A Recursive Algorithm for Finding Multi-Step Reaction Mechanisms
papers.abstract: Building reaction networks for kinetic modeling hinges on locating transition states (TSs) in order to compute reaction rates. In many cases, the reactions of interest involve complex, multi-step mechanisms with intermediates. Double-ended methods such as the nudged elastic band (NEB) are built for elementary steps, where a single TS separates reactant and product, and they struggle (or even fail) when given endpoints that straddle several saddle points, corresponding to multi-step mechanisms. We present an autosplitting NEB (ASNEB) algorithm that detects nascent intermediates during path optimization, splits the reaction at those minima, and recurses on the resulting segments until every step is elementary. Network completions then probe alternative connections among the discovered reactant, intermediates, and product, exposing competing mechanisms. Running discovery at a semiempirical level (GFN2-xTB) and refining intermediates and TSs with DFT keeps the cost dominated by the same ab initio refinement already required by conventional modeling, while improving TS guess quality and lowering the computational cost. We demonstrate the utility of ASNEB with the Oxy-Cope, Wittig, and Dakin reactions, where ASNEB recovers the established mechanisms and uncovers competing pathways with no prior specification of intermediates.

papers.title: Multiscale Modeling of Radical Polymers and the Design Properties Affecting Conductivity
papers.abstract: Radical polymers are an emerging class of organic electronic materials that offer electronic properties, making them attractive for transparent, biosensing, and energy storage applications. Charge transport in these materials occurs through redox-active side chains rather than a conjugated backbone. However, their practical use is limited by relatively low charge mobility compared to conjugated polymers, in which charge is transported along a continuous conjugated backbone. In addition, most designs have focused on TEMPO-based systems and small molecules, leaving the broader design space of radical chemistries and backbone structures insufficiently explored. Here, a multiscale modeling framework is used to systematically investigate the influence of radical side-chain chemistry and polymer backbone structure on charge transport in radical polymers. The approach integrates system-specific coarse-grained parametrization derived from machine-learned interatomic potentials with molecular dynamics simulations of equilibrated morphologies and kinetic Monte Carlo charge transport calculations. The effects of radical side-chain chemistry, polymer backbone structure, and active radical-site fraction were systematically investigated across polymers containing TEMPO, verdazyl, and galvinoxyl side chains with PEO and PMMA backbones. The results show that radical side-chain chemistry strongly influences both morphology and charge transport, with galvinoxyl exhibiting the highest charge mobility, followed by verdazyl, while TEMPO systems exhibit comparatively lower mobility. Galvinoxyl achieves high mobility through large intersite hopping rates and the formation of extensive connected charge-transport networks, whereas verdazyl balances intermediate hopping rates with high site connectivity. In contrast, TEMPO-based systems exhibit limited transport because unfavorable intermolecular hopping kinetics dominate despite their higher site connectivity relative to galvinoxyl. The coarse-grained representation of PEO and PMMA backbones produces similar averaged mobilities, suggesting that backbone-dependent transport differences observed experimentally may originate from atomistic effects not captured by the CG model. Computational annealing does not produce significant changes in radical packing or charge transport, likely because equilibrated CG morphologies are already partially relaxed due to the initial equilibration procedure. Finally, reducing the fraction of active radical sites to mimic synthesis imperfections, such as protonation and missing side chains, decreases charge displacement and mobility, while the resulting changes in transport-network formation depend on the underlying hopping kinetics and network topology. These findings establish structure--property relationships governing charge transport in radical polymers and provide design guidelines for improving their conductivity. More broadly, the workflow establishes a general framework for probing mesoscale structure--transport relationships using system-specific force fields and is readily extensible to a broader molecular design space.

papers.title: In Situ Potentially Prebiotic (Re)activation of 3′-Amino-2′,3′dideoxynucleotides for Sustainable Chemical Copying Chemistry
papers.abstract: Nonenzymatic primer extension is thought to have enabled genetic replication prior to the emergence of enzymatic replicases. Chemically modified nucleic acids have proven effective in overcoming key limitations of nonenzymatic RNA replication, including low reaction rates and poor fidelity. Specifically, activated 3′-amino-2′,3′-dideoxynucleotides polymerize substantially faster than their RNA counterparts, but undergo intramolecular cyclization over time. Here we show that these cyclic phosphoramidates are not dead-end products, but dynamic intermediates connecting nucleotide activation, phosphorus recycling, and template-directed polymerization. Chemoselective triphosphorylation, pH-modulated phosphorus transfer, and imidazole-catalyzed ring opening enable reversible phosphoroimidazolide formation; resulting in monomers that can directly participate in in situ nonenzymatic chemical copying. These results establish a sustainable chemical network linking nucleosides to template-directed synthesis of N3′→P5′ phosphoramidate DNA, offering new insights into sustainable prebiotic (re)activation chemistry.

papers.title: A Framework for Data-Driven Design and Discovery of PEGDA Hydrogel through Insights from Structure, Processing, and Mechanical Tunability
papers.abstract: Poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) is a widely used hydrogel across applications from biomedical to soft electronics due to its biocompatibility and tunable mechanical properties. However, this tunability also makes PEGDA highly sensitive to formulation, processing, handling, and testing, all of which lead to large scatter in reported mechanical properties. This work identifies factors governing these heterogeneities through a comprehensive structure-process-property analysis, with the aim of establishing a standardized reporting framework to support data-driven design strategies. The theoretical basis for heterogeneity was highlighted as arising from its chemistry and reaction kinetics, as reflected in its bottlebrush architecture, distinct from that of standard point-junction hydrogels. Manufacturing methods (bulk casting, additive manufacturing, and two-photon laser printing) were evaluated to identify critical process parameters influencing network formation. These included commonly understood factors such as PEGDA chemistry and choice of photoinitiator, and less-reported parameters such as oxygen exposure, choice of mold, and post-curing processes, that can significantly impact the outcome. Mechanical variability across the testing scale arises from these inherent heterogeneities, with additional factors, such as the testing scale (macroscale tension and compression to nano- and microscale indentation) and sample state, further influencing the outcome. Based on the above, the work proposed a unifying framework organized under five categories required for reporting and analyzing PEGDA outcomes: formulation and composition, initiator information, curing parameters, post-cure handling, and testing conditions. Such standardization, reported in a suitable database format, is demonstrated, including its application in workflows that use large language models (LLMs) for querying. Future work can incorporate the framework in training more advanced machine learning (ML) models for a data-driven design. Overall, the study establishes a data-driven strategy for PEGDA and other hydrogels for advancing research across different applications.

papers.title: The Modular Quantum Emulator: Chemically Accurate, Polynomial-Cost Simulation of Multi-Step Metalloenzyme Catalysis in a Dissipative Protein Environment
papers.abstract: (Dated: July 19, 2026) Quantum algorithms for molecular dynamics propagate a wavepacket through configuration space, while quantum electronic-structure methods return a ground-state energy at one fixed geometry. Neither addresses the object a chemist means by a catalytic mechanism: a closed sequence of identified intermediates linked by proton-coupled electron transfers, non-adiabatic crossings, and a stoichiometric budget that must balance over the turnover. Here we introduce the Modular Quantum Emulator (MQE), a qudit architecture that takes that \emph{ mechanism } as the object of computation. Two registers are carried: a logical register assigning one four-level qudit per spatial orbital, whose states are that orbital's four occupancies, and a single auxiliary register counting cofactor turnover around the cycle. Stoichiometric bookkeeping makes the auxiliary register mandatory, and our central result is that it simultaneously performs four further roles---it is the clock for quantum phase estimation, so energies are extracted with no additional qubits; it shelters idle population from dephasing; it confines environmental coupling, leaving the electronic reduced state exactly unitary under open-system dynamics; and its winding number classifies the mechanism, predicting that a centred two-electron elimination requires a turnover electron count divisible by four, satisfied throughout the nitrogenase family and violated by two- and six-electron cycles. Electron number, phase closure, trace and spin sector are enforced as circuit-level invariants and verified at every step. Because the auxiliary sector is algebraically independent of the electronic Hamiltonian, nuclear quantum effects, relativistic and spin--orbit coupling, open-system dissipation and periodic boundary conditions are absorbed without altering the asymptotic cost. Every gate introduced compiles to the native GPI/GPI2/ZZ pulse set of trapped-ion hardware, the basis changes attaining the KAK lower bound of two entangling operations. Validation of these circuits across seventeen catalytic mechanisms, on chemically relevant active spaces small enough to admit exact reference energies, recovers every stoichiometric invariant and returns twenty-five phase-estimation measurements within 1.6~mHa of the exact result.

papers.title: Integrating ToxCast/ToxRefDB Data with Quantitative Adverse Outcome Pathway for Risk Assessment of Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) pose complex, multi-mechanistic health risks that are difficult to evaluate using conventional in vitro or in vivo approaches alone. Here, we developed a quantitative adverse outcome pathway (qAOP) model integrating ToxCast and ToxRefDB data to enable mechanism-based, high-throughput risk assessment of EDCs. Molecular initiating events (MIEs) for 40 representative EDCs were prioritized from ToxCast bioassay data and mapped onto the AOP wiki database, yielding six integrated AOP networks comprising 22 MIEs, 167 key events, and 40 adverse outcomes (AOs) spanning organ- and gender-specific endpoints. Chemical–MIE potencies were quantified using Toxicological Priority Index (ToxPi) scores derived from ToxCast AC50 values, while MIE–AO probabilistic relationships were weighted using the PageRank algorithm applied to AOP network topology. Matrix multiplication of these two probabilistic layers generated integrated toxicity scores predicting EDC–AO associations. Model performance was validated against in vivo ToxRefDB data using machine learning-based receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, achieving AUC values of 0.86 and 0.73 for hepatotoxicity and reproductive toxicity, respectively. This data-driven qAOP framework provides a mechanistically transparent alternative to black-box QSAR models, bridges in vitro and in vivo toxicological evidence, and offers a scalable, animal-free strategy for prioritizing and screening emerging EDCs and structural analogues within Integrated Approaches to Testing and Assessment (IATA) frameworks.

papers.title: Cheméo Relay, a D-MPNN-based chemical property prediction model family
papers.abstract: A message-passing neural network is a learned group-contribution method only if its readout carries molecular size, which the framework-default mean readout discards. We train directed message passing neural networks (D-MPNN, Chemprop v2) on experimental thermophysical data from the Cheméo database, one model per property, as a general-purpose graph-based alternative to the Joback group-contribution method [14], strongest in the regime where Joback degrades: Joback was fitted on small molecules and, as we show here head-to-head, degrades steadily as molecules grow; those larger molecules are a minority of the corpus (a quarter to a third of a typical set has eleven or more heavy atoms, though the spread is wide, from 11% for the small Gibbs-energy set to 56% for melting point), but they are exactly the regime where a group-contribution method has no good alternative. The contribution is not that sum pooling beats mean pooling, a fact already established in the graph-learning literature [18,19]; it is a property-by-property diagnosis on experimental thermophysical data of how the default silently fails, a reusable release discipline, and a family of released models measured against Joback, a simple descriptor baseline, and external data. The mean readout is size-invariant: it returns the average per-atom contribution, so a molecule and its dimer map to nearly the same vector, and every property that tracks molecular size collapsed toward the training mean; six properties, among them the critical constants and the Gibbs energy of formation, landed at test R2 near zero, and a gradient-boosted tree on plain RDKit descriptors beat the graph network on all six. Replacing the mean with a sum-aware pooling (sum and max concatenated) makes the molecule embedding scale with atom count, and the message passing then learns the higher-order structural corrections that Marrero and Gani add to a classical scheme by hand as second-and third-order groups [15]. The distinction we keep is between a graph-extensive readout (a property of the network) and a thermodynamically extensive target: the sum is needed outright for extensive targets such as critical volume and the formation enthalpies, while intensive targets that rise along homologous series, such as the boiling and critical temperatures, benefit because molecular size is a strong predictor of them, not because they are extensive. Nine of sixteen properties are released under a two-part criterion: a statistical bar (mean out-of-sample R2 above 0.70 with a train-test gap of at most 0.20 under repeated scaffold cross-validation, or state-of-the-art accuracy on a shared external benchmark) and a veto, that the incumbent Joback must not significantly out-predict the model in its tested domain; we lead with mean absolute error, since a small scaffold test set makes R2 noisy: normal boiling point (MAE 13.5 K, RMSE 30 K, 3.5% average relative error), melting point (MAE 30.8 K), critical volume and critical temperature, enthalpies of formation and vaporisation, ionisation energy, aqueous solubility and the acentric factor, each reported against Joback, the published state of the art, and the experimental reproducibility floor of the property. Against Joback on identical held-out folds the graph model significantly wins on five of the nine comparable properties (boiling-point MAE 13.5 vs 26.3 K, formation enthalpy 35.5 vs 70.9 kJ/mol), ties two, and its error grows far more slowly with molecular size than Joback’s, which grows several-fold; it also covers the compounds Joback cannot fragment at all, a few percent of a typical set and up to about 12% for some properties, at undiminished accuracy on the ordinary organics among them; the two properties Joback still out-predicts, Gibbs energy of formation and critical pressure, are exactly the two the veto holds back as beta, with Joback served in their place. We release them as the Cheméo Relay family, one model per property.

papers.title: Collision Induced Unfolding Predicts the Aggregation of Glycoengineered Monoclonal Antibodies
papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapeutics exhibit substantial structural heterogeneity, requiring analytical methods capable of rapidly assessing critical quality attributes (CQAs) that influence stability and developability. Non-native aggregation is a key CQA, given its propensity to decrease mAb efficacy and increase immunogenicity. However, current analytical tools commonly used to screen mAbs during drug development provide limited structural insight into aggregation prone monomeric structures. Orthogonal tools such as ion mobility-mass spectrometry (IM-MS), collision-induced unfolding (CIU), and IM-selected CIU (IM-CIU) enable rapid gas-phase structural characterization of proteins, offering the ability to enhance the resolution of complex structural mixtures, bridging the gap left by conventional aggregation analyses. In this study, we establish CIU as a prompt predictor of mAb aggregation propensity. Analysis of IgG1 CIU fingerprints revealed a high-energy bimodal structural population, quantified here as the ‘A/B ratio’, that correlates with pH-induced aggregation observed in our forced degradation studies. IM-CIU and CIU-electron capture dissociation (ECD) further characterized these structural populations, allowing us to localize the A/B ratio diagnostically to the hinge region of the mAb. We conclude by demonstrating that A/B ratio data, collected for glycoengineered mono-disperse mAb glycoforms can be used to test and predict the ability of specific glycans to protect mAbs from aggregation. Together, these results establish CIU-derived structural metrics as rapid predictors of mAb aggregation propensity, enabling higher-throughput structural assessment of biotherapeutic stability and glycoform-dependent effects.

papers.title: Measuring the Membrane Protein-Bound Lipidome
papers.abstract: Lipids play diverse physiological roles in energy storage, signaling, and cell structure. Another less appreciated role is as allosteric modulators of membrane proteins. However, it is challenging to determine the identify and affinity of lipids interacting with a given membrane protein target. In this review, we discuss analytical advances in using lipidomics to profile lipids bound to specific membrane proteins, which we will refer to as protein-lipid interactomics. We will consider the challenges of solubilizing and isolating the membrane protein while retaining relevant lipid interactions, focusing on detergents and lipid nanoparticles made with polymer, peptide, and protein scaffolds. We will also discuss aspects of overall experiment design, including basic identification, quantitative experiments, progressive delipidation, and lipid exchange to probe the strength of lipid interactions. Finally, we conclude with key questions, current analytical challenges, and proposed future directions for this emerging field.

papers.title: Foundation interatomic potentials learn the practical chemistry they were never taught
papers.abstract: Chemists understand molecular reactivity through simplified concepts such as substituent effects, acidity, and aromaticity, which are compact descriptors of the potential energy surface and of the electronic structure that shapes it. Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are transforming applied computational chemistry by learning the same surface from atomic structures, energies, and forces, making atomistic simulations of complex systems practical. Like chemists, MLIPs build compact internal representations of that surface, yet these are usually treated as a means to faster, larger-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Here we show that they also contain directly recoverable chemical information: simple models applied to the invariant per-atom embeddings of pretrained universal MLIPs recover Hammett substituent constants, Brønsted and Lewis acidity, and ring aromaticity with Spearman ρ = 0.8–0.99. The same representations predict the yield of a four-component palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling at ρ = 0.96, matching models built from curated descriptors, while pinpointing the aryl halide as the reaction’s key substrate and ranking isoxazole additives by catalyst-poisoning strength. Universal MLIPs are therefore not only fast engines for energies and forces but also chemically meaningful representations of molecular reactivity, opening a route to extracting chemical insights directly from the learned potentials themselves.

papers.title: MLIP-Enhanced Thermochemistry Predictions across Organic Chemical Space
papers.abstract: This work presents thermoMLIP, a machine-learning-interatomic-potential-based workflow for efficient conformer optimization and thermochemistry prediction across organic chemical space. By combining MLIP-driven geometry optimization with robust thermochemical corrections, thermoMLIP achieves near-DFT accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. We further show that MLIP-based conformer searches systematically identify lower-energy structures than conventional approaches, improving thermochemical predictions across diverse datasets. Although thermoMLIP substantially accelerates thermochemistry calculations, its computational cost remains prohibitive for exhaustive screening of very large chemical spaces. We therefore employ an uncertainty-aware active-learning strategy based on evidential graph neural networks to efficiently generate a large, uniform thermodynamic dataset, which is subsequently used to train thermoGNN, a surrogate capable of near-instantaneous prediction of molecular thermodynamic properties. Together, thermoMLIP and thermoGNN establish a hierarchical framework that bridges accurate MLIP-based thermochemistry and ultra-large-scale molecular screening, enabling applications such as reaction-network exploration and high-throughput reaction discovery.

papers.title: A Stereochemistry-Aware Circular Algorithm and Fingerprint for Resonance-Invariant Molecular Representation
papers.abstract: Algorithmic molecular fingerprints remain attractive for high-throughput chemoinformatics because they are fast, discrete, and easy to integrate into screening, similarity search, and machine-learning workflows. However, widely used circular fingerprints such as ECFP rely on conventional molecular graph representations that capture stereochemistry incompletely and may distinguish chemically equivalent resonance forms through localized atom charges and bond-order-dependent encodings. Here, we introduce the Stereochemistry-Aware Circular Algorithm (SACA) and the derived Stereochemistry-Aware Circular Fingerprint (SACFP), a stereo chemically informed, resonance-invariant extension of circular graph refinement built on the StereoMolGraph representation.[Papusha and Leonhard, J. Chem. Inf. Model, 2026, 66, 7, 3830] In this framework, stereo chemistry is encoded through local stereodescriptors grounded in group theory, allowing atom-centered and bond-centered stereochemical information to be incorporated directly while avoiding artificial distinctions be tween resonance structures. We show that SACA yields locally consistent atom invariants for stereoisomers, preserves equivalence across resonance forms, and discriminates challenging stereochemical cases, including delocalized radicals and metal complexes. Compared with ECFP on stereoisomer datasets, SACFP produces less over-discriminating atom identifiers and a more reliable mapping between subgraphs and fingerprints. Evaluation on 1.4 million ChEMBL small molecules shows a low color-refinement-hash collision rate of 0.1%, with remaining ambiguities resolvable by exact StereoMolGraph isomorphism. We showcase how its mathe matical properties make it suitable for substructure search on large-scale datasets.

papers.title: VirtualLab_CC: An LLM-Augmented Virtual Laboratory for Automated Computational Chemistry Research
On the Role of Hydroxide Ions as the Mediators of Cathodic Cu Corrosion
papers.abstract: Understanding changes and degradation of the copper cathode during the electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR) is a fundamental challenge. Advances in operando experimental methods and computational tools have shed light on the degradation mechanisms. However, the role of the hydroxide ions formed from the alkaline Volmer reaction remains under-studied. Here we report a computational investigation of *Cu(OH) n adatom complexes that can form on a roughened surface as possible intermediates that can lead to cathodic copper corrosion. Constant-potential density functional theory calculations are utilized to compute the voltage-dependent free energy surfaces of Cu(OH) n electrodissolution from adatom defects on a Cu(100) surface under cathodic conditions. The results show that the dissolution of a Cu(OH) adatom complex is endergonic by ∼ 1 eV at an electrode bias of −1.59 V vs. the Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) and thus quite unfavorable. In contrast, the dissolution of *Cu(OH) 2 at the same bias only requires ~ 0.2 eV. The Cu oxidation states of both complexes are +1 regardless of the applied potential. The atomic partial charges and their change show that two hydroxides of surface-bound *Cu(OH) 2 induce an image quadrupole which allows facile dissociation. Pathways to form these two complexes are analyzed using transition state calculations evaluated at constant potential. The presence of oxygen adatoms, for example from subsurface oxygen, is identified to facilitate the formation of *Cu(OH) n via dissociative chemisorption of water. The disproportionation of surface *OH to form new *O is also found to be favorable under strongly reducing conditions. Including both pathways to form Cu(OH) n as well as *OH disproportionation,, the stochastic simulation model predicts approximately 6 monolayers per hour of Cu loss through Cu(OH) n formation. The model also highlights how *OH disproportionation sustains active Cu sites and generates *O, a key intermediate facilitating dissolution to [Cu(OH) 2 ] - (aq). These results show that hydroxide-ion mediated cathodic Cu dissolution without external species is viable. Remaining questions and further work that could validate the proposed mechanism are discussed.

papers.title: Guest Protonation Gates Hydrogen-Bond-Driven Selectivity in Native Cyclodextrin Molecular Recognition
papers.abstract: Cyclodextrin inclusion is often described primarily in terms of hydrophobic displacement of cavity-bound water, a framework that explains volume-dependent affinity but does not account for why closely related guests exhibit distinct stabilization within the same host cavity. Hydrogen bonding is increasingly recognized as an additional recognition element in macrocyclic hosts, but whether this principle operates within an unmodified, native cyclodextrin cavity—and whether it can be switched reversibly—has not been established. Here, we show that guest protonation supports switchable encapsulation behavior, using albendazole and fenbendazole as structurally matched benzimidazole drugs that allow hydrogen-bond donor–acceptor character to be tuned independently of the hydrophobic scaffold. Solubility measurements across native α-, β-, and γ-cyclodextrin show that protonation enhances association in all three hosts, while NMR spectroscopy, variable-temperature thermodynamic analysis, and semiempirical molecular dynamics simulations focused on β-cyclodextrin reveal that this enhancement reflects two mechanistically distinct outcomes. Although both protonated guests form 1:1 complexes with comparable hydrophobic cavity occupancy, albendazole achieves deeper cavity insertion that positions its protonated benzimidazole to engage a broader network of hydrogen bonds at the host rim, yielding a larger enthalpic gain offset by greater entropic compensation. Comparison with simplified benzimidazole fragments lacking the hydrophobic anchor shows that hydrogen bonding alone cannot sustain stable association in water, establishing that hydrophobic anchoring is a prerequisite for productive protonation-dependent recognition. These results identify protonation as a general, structurally contingent switch for redistributing enthalpic and entropic contributions to host–guest stabilization in native cyclodextrin systems.

papers.title: Animal Intelligence Helps Seek Air Particulate Matter Exposure Limits
papers.abstract: Air particulate matter (PM) standards rely heavily on epidemiological and toxicological endpoints, in addition to failing to consider regional differences and population sensitivity. Using rat's natural intelligence, this work has pioneered a PM exposure threshold measurement protocol by quantifying the amount of PM-spiked water consumed and then extrapolating them to human exposure at the time of rats' avoidance. Using the method, the no-observed health effect limits of ambient PM for representative cities: Beijing, Hohhot, Guangzhou, Xi'an, and Taiyuan were sought as 8.54 (7.57, 9.50) μg/m 3 , 3.88 (3.45, 4.31) μg/m 3 , 3.39 (3.15, 3.63) μg/m 3 , 1.46 (1.27, 1.66) μg/m 3 , and 0.70 (0.46, 0.94) μg/m 3 , respectively. PM standards as determined by rats for some cities here are close to 5 μg/m 3 as recommended by World Health Organization. Interestingly, these exposure thresholds appear before rats develop pathological damages, and such limits for hypertensive rats groups were observed further lower. The PM water avoidance by rats was also accompanied by changes measured here in their breath-borne volatile organic compounds (VOCs), gut microbiota, metabolic enzymes, inflammation, oxidative stress, and pathologies for different cities. This work has pioneered the use of animal intelligence (AI) in developing sensitive PM standard for different cities, and using rats' intelligence, different city PM standards can be readily developed for maximizing air pollution control cost-effectiveness.

papers.title: Iron / Oxide Cycling Behavior Probed via in situ Mössbauer Spectroscopy, X-ray Diffraction and X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Iron is a promising energy carrier for sustainable energy storage via hydrogen-based reduction of iron oxides and energy release through oxidation with air. While it is well known that the cycling of iron powders affect their morphology and reactivity, the associated structural changes and the reaction mechanism remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the solid-state cycling of iron oxide powder using complementary in situ techniques: synchrotron based Mössbauer spectroscopy, quick scanning X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and time-resolved synchrotron X-ray diffraction. With a time resolution better than 1 min, compositional changes during three consecutive oxidation–reduction cycles were monitored both with respect to changes in the oxidation state of iron and the transformation of the corresponding crystalline phases. During isothermal cycling at 560 °C, the rate of iron oxidation increased with each cycle number, whereas the corresponding reduction rates to metallic iron decreased. The oxidation proceeded initially via Fe → Fe3O4 → Fe2O3 and then involving wustite as reaction intermediate Fe → FeO → Fe3O4 → Fe2O3. Reduction occurred exclusively through Fe2O3 → Fe3O4 → FeO → Fe, though the observed reaction behavior changed in each cycle between initial and advanced reduction phase.

papers.title: Predicted metabolites of the methylmethcathinone positional isomers (2-, 3- and 4-MMC) as candidate analytical targets, with in silico hERG-block screening
papers.abstract: 2-Methylmethcathinone (2-MMC) has emerged across Europe as a successor to the scheduled ring- substituted cathinone 3-methylmethcathinone (3-MMC), is frequently sold under or missold as the 3-MMC name, and has recently been implicated in clinical and forensic casework, including a case series of 13 intoxications with 5 fatalities. Despite this, its human metabolism and cardiac liability remain uncharacterized, and no certified reference materials are available to support confirmatory analysis. We report a validation-gated, in silico characterization of the 2-, 3- and 4-MMC positional isomers. Each method was first benchmarked against measured reference data before being applied to 2-MMC: a metabolism ensemble (rule-based enumeration and a random-forest site-of-metabolism model, the latter reproducing its published performance and the measured isomer metabolite maps); an in silico hERG-block screen (a machine-learning classifier validated against CiPA reference drugs, with an O’Hara–Rudy ventricular actionpotential model used to bound the electrophysiological consequence of block); and molecular docking against a 5-HT2B agonist-bound structure. We predict N-demethylation to nor-2-MMC as the major Phase I route — a candidate urinary marker by read-across to the transporter-active metabolite nor-mephedrone — and report a predicted benzylic-oxidation gradient consistent with the measured suppression of ortho-isomer metabolism. The isomers are classified as weak hERG blockers, clustering with low-torsadogenic reference drugs; the block classification is not calibrated to a fractional channel block, so the action-potential model is used only to bound what such weak block would imply, not to compute a compound-specific proarrhythmia metric. Rigidreceptor docking failed its own validation gate for 5-HT2B efficacy and is noted, briefly, as a methodological negative. All predictions are framed as leads for experimental confirmation and to guide targeted analytical method development in the absence of reference standards.

papers.title: Hydrophobic monomer incorporation tunes the pH responsivity of polycationic brushes
papers.abstract: We tune the pH-responsive swelling response of polycationic brushes via incorporation of hydrophobic repeat units. We observed that careful compositional tuning can realize apparent brush p K a values, which we term p K a * , between 5.0 and 5.7. Further we observed monotonic decreases in p K a * with increasing hydrophobic monomer incorporation. Although brush p K a * was readily tuned with composition, the cooperativity of deprotonation was only influenced by polycation identity and not hydrophobic monomer incorporation. Interestingly, hydrophobicity-driven p K a * decreases were observed exclusively for brushes, and not untethered, compositionally matched polymers, suggesting that confining polymers in the form of nanoparticle-tethered brushes might grant more fine-tuned control over pH responsivity than what can be obtained with free polymers alone. We readily reproduced p K a * trends from planar substrates to nanoparticle-tethered brushes, potentiating applications in intracellular pH sensing and nucleic acid delivery where precise pKa tuning is essential. In future work, we will apply p K a * -tuned brush-grafted nanoparticles to overcome intracellular delivery barriers that have hindered free polymers.

papers.title: Design and Simulation of a Cryogenic Air Separation Unit for a Biogas-to-Ammonia Process
papers.abstract: This paper presents the process design, steady-state simulation, and mechanical sizing of a cryogenic air separation unit (ASU) developed as part of a sustainable ammonia production flowsheet from biogas. The unit uses Linde double-column cryogenic distillation to separate atmospheric air (modeled as a ternary O2/N2/Ar mixture) into a high-purity nitrogen stream for ammonia synthesis and an oxygen stream for autothermal reforming of biogas-derived methane. The process was simulated in Aspen HYSYS at a feed rate of 1300 kmol/h, achieving a nitrogen product purity of 99.883% and an oxygen product purity of 95.04%. Detailed plate hydraulic design (Souders-Brown flooding, weeping, entrainment, and downcomer back-up checks) and AIChE tray-efficiency calculations were carried out for both the high-pressure column (HPC) and low-pressure column (LPC), followed by mechanical design of the pressure vessels and an equipment cost estimate. The low-pressure column required 30 theoretical trays (41 actual stages) at a diameter of 1.746 m, with an estimated 2024-indexed cost of $380,368. A reflux-ratio/number-of-stages optimization was performed for the high-pressure column to identify the trade-off between operating and fixed costs. The results demonstrate a technically sound and economically quantified ASU design suitable for integration into a green ammonia production route.

papers.title: AtomFormer: A Simple Model for Any Mixture Odor Prediction and Beyond
papers.abstract: *Corresponding author: yangxiao_ztri@foxmail.com Abstract. Odor prediction has relied on two implicit assumptions: that a closed set of expert-defined labels is necessary for training, and that individual molecules must serve as the encoding unit—forcing mixtures to be decomposed into constituents, predicted separately, then aggregated through ad hoc fusion. Here we show that both assumptions can be eliminated simultaneously. We introduce AtomFormer, which uses GIN layers as a molecular tokenizer and Transformer self-attention to enable atoms from different molecules to interact directly in a single forward pass, eliminating the need for separate mixture aggregation. On a rigorously decontaminated test set of 6,260 binary mixtures, AtomFormer achieves macro-AUROC = 0.9347 with 16.9M parameters. Beyond odor perception, we validate this architecture on predicting excess enthalpy of mixtures, where it achieves Pearson R = 0.937 with 1.18M parameters. Across these two distinct tasks, AtomFormer achieves strong performance with zero pretraining and end-to-end prediction, demonstrating the generality of the framework across diverse mixture prediction domains.

papers.title: Runtime-steered ultrashort molecular dynamics enables million-pose protein–ligand screening
papers.abstract: Large-scale prioritization of protein–ligand interactions requires dynamic information at screening scale. We present a docking-to-dynamics workflow that evaluates poses by ensembles of ultrashort molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories (0.1–5 ns) and an online ligand-RMSD stability metric, MDscore. In a conditional six-target retrospective benchmark of 88 active and 702 inactive compounds, MD-score achieved pose-aware ROC-AUC of 0.868 at top ten poses, while sampling analyses indicated that broad pose and velocity sampling was more useful than extending a small number of trajectories. Runtime steering, which terminates unstable poses and redistributes unfinished tasks, scaled the workflow to 1,234,620 docked poses from 124,245 generated compounds on Fugaku supercomputer while reducing simulated time to 24% of exhaustive evaluation. In a Marburg virus nucleoprotein screen, the workflow prioritized compounds that yielded three initial minigenome-active hits among 76 tested compounds. These results position ultrashort MD as a practical dynamic filtering layer between docking, data-driven prediction and higher-cost validation methods.

papers.title: Transformer Architectures for Molecular Property Prediction: A Study of Featurization, Attention, and Self-Supervised Pretraining
papers.abstract: Predicting physicochemical and biological properties of small molecules directly from structure is a central problem in computational drug discovery, materials design, and chemical safety assessment. In recent years, Transformer architectures, originally developed for natural language processing, have been adapted to molecular graphs and string representations with considerable success, complementing message-passing graph neural networks (GNNs) and classical descriptor-based models. This paper presents a comprehensive study of Transformer-based molecular property prediction. We (i) survey the landscape of molecular featurization strategies, including SMILES tokenization, graph-based atom/bond features, learned fingerprints, and three-dimensional conformer descriptors; (ii) introduce a unified Transformer architecture, which we refer to as MolFormer-X, that accepts either sequence-based or graph-structured inputs through a shared self-attention backbone with relative and structural positional encodings; (iii) describe a two-stage training regime combining self-supervised pretraining on unlabeled molecular corpora with supervised fine-tuning on downstream property-prediction tasks; and (iv) provide an extensive empirical analysis across regression and classification benchmarks drawn from the MoleculeNet suite, including solubility (ESOL), solvation free energy (FreeSolv), lipophilicity, bloodbrain barrier penetration (BBBP), and toxicity (Tox21). We further conduct ablation studies isolating the contributions of tokenization scheme, positional encoding, pretraining objective, and model depth, and we analyze learned attention patterns for chemical interpretability. We conclude with a discussion of current limitations of Transformer-based molecular models, including data efficiency, extrapolation to novel scaffolds, and computational cost, and outline directions for future work at the intersection of chemistry and sequence modeling.

papers.title: Predicting CYP450 Induction and PXR Activation with Machine Learning Approaches: Challenges and Opportunities
papers.abstract: Many drugs increase the activity of cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes, an effect known as induction, which is a major cause of harmful drug-drug interactions (DDIs). Predicting induction from chemical structure would help identify DDI risks early in compound development. Yet, unlike many other drug properties, CYP450 induction is rarely modeled, because the data needed to train models is scarce and expensive to produce. Using an industry-scale dataset covering induction of three CYP450 enzymes (CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP1A2) and PXR activation, we benchmark four machine learning models across six molecular representations and compare performance against models trained on a curated public dataset. On the internal data, the best models separate inducers from non-inducers moderately well (MCC ~0.5) but cannot predict the magnitude of induction, and no model or representation does meaningfully better, pointing to the data rather than the method as the limit. The same pattern holds in public data, where a large public PXR set reaches this range, while a small, heterogeneous public CYP3A4 set fails where the data is scarcer and noisier. We then show that the shared biology of these endpoints carries a usable signal. A model trained on one endpoint partly predicts the others, and this transfer follows the known regulatory relationships between PXR and the CYP450 enzymes, so these biological links can serve as useful inductive biases for future models. Finally, we found that the models we trained are already reasonably well calibrated, which, combined with their classification performance, makes them useful for prioritizing compounds today.

papers.title: Swelling in the Eye of Secondary Interactions
papers.abstract: Swelling is expected to be an inherent property of nanoplastics, defining their interactions with their environment. First, we created models for polyurethane (PUR) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) nanoplastics, which, based on structural descriptors, including density, these particles were found to exhibit realistic geometries. Using these models, we identified the sequence of steps that result in the swelling of these nanoplastics in water, trifluoroacetic acid, and dimethylformamide. For PET, bearing weaker polymer-polymer interactions, swelling was found to be a continuous process. In the case of PUR, in which hydrogen bonding forms a dominant type of intermolecular interactions within the polymer, these hydrogen bonds first have to be broken by the solvent, thereafter, solvent molecules penetrating the particle can cleave off individual chains in separate steps, resulting in a more complex swelling mechanism. The resulting mechanistic picture is consistent with earlier models of polymer swelling deduced from second order kinetics.

papers.title: ChemRAG-Mol: A Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Framework for Molecular Property Prediction and Reaction Reasoning
papers.abstract: Computational chemistry has been reshaped by deep learning, yet molecular property prediction, reaction product inference, and spectral–structure alignment remain bottlenecked by scarce labeled data, the absence of an explicit interface to external chemical knowledge bases, and a persistent modality gap between high-dimensional molecular representations and symbolic chemical knowledge. We propose ChemRAG-Mol, a unified retrieval-augmented multimodal framework that integrates four synergistic modules: a Parallel Graph-Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning module that dispatches multiple reasoning chains over molecular property, reaction template, and spectroscopy–structure graphs; a Chemistry Chain-of-Specificity module that enforces valence, stereochemistry, and stoichiometric constraints via step-wise refinement; a Spectral Enhancement Frontend that combines filtered feature recycling, dual local/non-local attention, and explainable hyperspectral reconstruction to denoise IR/Raman spectra; and a Secure 3D Molecular Field module that embeds tamper-resistant intellectual property messages into 3D Gaussian Splatting molecular fields. We evaluate ChemRAG-Mol on four datasets spanning the four core chemistry tasks: QM9 for property prediction, USPTO-50K for reaction inference, PubChem-Spec for spectral–structure retrieval, and Molecule3D-GS for secure 3D molecular representation. ChemRAG-Mol reduces HOMO mean absolute error by 13.9 percent relative to the strongest baseline on QM9, improves Top-1 accuracy by 3.5 percentage points on USPTO-50K, raises Recall@1 from 0.452 to 0.601 on PubChem-Spec, and achieves a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio of 31.02 decibels with 99.84 percent message extraction accuracy on Molecule3D-GS, establishing a new state of the art across all four tasks.

papers.title: High temperature and pressure sorption of ammonia using zeolites and supported metal halides: experimental investigations and sorption modeling
papers.abstract: Sorption‑enhanced ammonia synthesis (SEAS) requires solid sorbents with high capacity, fast kinetics, and reliable models at elevated temperature and pressure. Here, zeolites and supported metal halides are compared systematically for high‑temperature NH3 sorption for SEAS process design. Commercial zeolites (3A, 4A, 13X, LiLSX) were screened by quasi‑continuous pulse chemisorption (ambient pressure, 50–350 °C), combining capacity determination with TPD‑based site analysis. The most promising candidate LiLSX, still adsorbing NH3 at more than 300 °C, was then benchmarked against supported MnCl2‑based sorbents in a high‑pressure magnetic suspension balance (200–400 °C, up to 12 bar ammonia partial pressure). Morphology and salt distribution were characterized by SEM/EDX. Equilibria were modeled with Langmuir, Toth, Sips and dual‑site Langmuir (DSL) isotherms. NH3 adsorption kinetics on LiLSX were fitted using driving force, stretched exponential (SE) and double SE (DSE) rate expressions. Only LiLSX showed appreciable NH3 uptake above 200 °C in pulse chemisorption and remains active at 300 °C and 0.1 bar ammonia partial pressure. TPD signal and isotherm modeling confirm adsorption on two site types. At SEAS‑relevant conditions, LiLSX attained on average ~40 % higher NH3 capacity than MnCl2(30 wt.%)/AC. LiLSX sustained a quasi‑stable working capacity over 90 adsorption–desorption cycles at 300–350 °C without detectable structural damage. Among all kinetic models tested, the DSE approach best captures LiLSX NH3 uptake behavior and reflects two characteristic time scales aligned with the dual‑site equilibrium description. The presented methodology and model parameters directly support the design and simulation of SEAS reactors.

papers.title: A Nonclassical Mechanism for Dicopper(I)-Catalyzed Ketone Hydrosilylation Enabled by Synergistic Metal–Metal and Metal–Ligand Cooperativity
papers.abstract: The mechanism of ketone hydrosilylation catalyzed by a dicopper(I) monohydride PNNP complex was investigated through a combined computational and experimental study. Systematic evaluation of various catalytic pathways excluded a conventional hydride insertion pathway, as well as alternative options involving bimetallic oxidative addition and hypervalent silicon intermediates, converging instead on a single mechanism consistent with all experimental observations. This pathway commences with a stepwise metal–ligand cooperative activation of HSiPh3, followed by metal–metal cooperative preorganized coupling of the stabilized silyl nucleophile with the activated ketone. A bimetallic silyl migration and ligand-assisted protonation releases the hydrosilylation product. Notably, the hydride ligand acts as a spectator that stabilizes the dicopper core rather than participating directly in substrate transformation. These findings establish a nonclassical hydrosilylation mechanism in which metal–metal and stepwise metal–ligand cooperativity operate synergistically, illustrating how cooperative bimetallic architectures can access reaction pathways unavailable to mononuclear catalysts.

papers.title: A feedstock-conditioned process design framework for sustainable carbon resource valorisation: coal-to-GO/rGO manufacturing as a demonstration case
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous carbonaceous resources offer scalable pathways to advanced carbon materials, but their conversion is constrained by variations in composition, mineral matter, structural order, reactivity, and feedstock-preparation burden. Coal-derived graphene oxide (GO) and reduced graphene oxide (rGO) provide a representative case where feedstock selection, beneficiation, oxidation chemistry, product validation, and sustainability assessment are often treated as disconnected steps. Here, coal-to-GO/rGO conversion is used to demonstrate a feedstock-conditioned process design framework for sustainable carbon resource valorisation. The proposed seven-layer framework integrates coal-rank routing, ash and mineralogical triggers, composition- and texture-based process selection, rank-specific pretreatment severity windows, GO/rGO pathway selection, closed-loop product validation, and early-stage sustainability screening. A literature-informed sensitivity matrix and heat map identify variables governing material quality, yield, reagent demand, water use, energy intensity, and environmental performance. The framework is demonstrated through a lignite-to-GO case study incorporating mass and energy balances, reagent inventories, and cradle-to-gate sustainability indicators. The process yielded 0.138 kg GO kg-1 raw lignite, with a cumulative energy demand of 15.5 GJ kg-1 GO, a greenhouse-gas footprint of 2.00 × 103 kg CO2-eq kg-1 GO, and a water footprint of 6412 L kg-1 GO. We further introduce the Feedstock Conditioning Penalty (FCP) as the additional material, energy, chemical, and environmental burden required to convert a heterogeneous carbon resource into a synthesis-ready precursor. In the case study, feedstock conditioning contributed approximately 72% of greenhouse-gas emissions and 89% of electricity demand, identifying upstream upgrading as the dominant sustainability hotspot.

papers.title: Concentration and Temperature Dependence of the Helical Pitch in Cholesteric Xanthan Gum Solutions
papers.abstract: Solutions of partially depolymerized xanthan gum which form cholesteric lyotropic liquid crystal (LLC) phases, can be used to produce structurally colored, non-brittle photonic films. A key factor which determines the photonic properties of the dried xanthan films is the helical pitch p in the solid cholesteric structure retained from the liquid crystal phase, which enables the films to selectively reflect visible light. However, detailed experiments and a sophisticated theoretical model for unraveling the evolution of helical pitch over a broad concentration range in LLC systems containing semiflexible building blocks have remained elusive. In this work, we systematically study the temperature and concentration dependence of the helical pitch in aqueous solutions of ultrasonically treated xanthan gum over an extended concentration range up to 30 wt%. This investigation reveals that while the inverse pitch, i.e. the helical twist, increases linearly with temperature, it grows much more dramatically with concentration. Current theories cannot explain such strong non-linear concentration dependence of the inverse pitch at high concentration. Therefore, we propose a new molecular statistical model based on the so called Generalised Van der Waals Theory (GVWT) of the nematic phase, taking into account the concentration dependent steric intermolecular correlations as well as the effective attraction interaction. This model successfully interprets the divergence of the inverse pitch at high concentrations and estimates reasonable minimum achievable pitch values in the dried films as observed for the xanthan samples. These findings reinforce our understanding of chiral interaction in semiflexible LLCs, more deeply bridging the cholesteric ordering and structural coloration in solid films.

papers.title: Exploring the Coordination of π-Acids and Redox-Active Diatomics to a High-Spin and Highly Fluorinated Ferrous Compound
papers.abstract: A new trigonally symmetric ligand scaffold is reported from the reaction of tris(2-aminoethyl)amine (TREN) and methyl trifluoroacetate. Deprotonation and metallation with iron(II) yields a trigonal monopyramidal ferrate that bears an open coordination site surrounded by C–F motifs. The weak-field ligand environment promoted by the fluorinated amidate donors leads to distinctive behaviors that are apparent in reactions with π-acids such as CO and tert-butylisocyanide. As shown by structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies, the trifluoromethyl substituents lead to an attenuation of π-backbonding capabilities, while also labilizing the Fe–Namidate bonds. While no tractable reactivity with O2 occurs, the ferrate irreversibly coordinates NO to yield a high-spin {FeNO}7 complex.

papers.title: Supramolecular behavior of heterochiral dipeptides with Ile
papers.abstract: This study describes the supramolecular behavior and gelation of heterochiral, aliphatic dipeptides D-Ile-L-Xaa (Xaa = Ala, Val, Leu, Ile) in various solvents, and buffered water at neutral pH. In the case of metastable gels, the consequent rapid transition towards crystals enabled X-ray diffraction analysis to unveil the dipeptides’ packing modes in amphipathic layers.

papers.title: Electronic Coupling, Not Dopant Identity, Governs Charge Dynamics in BiVO4 Photoanodes
authors: Víctor A. de la Peña O’Shea
papers.abstract: Transition-metal incorporation is widely employed to enhance the photoelectrochemical (PEC) performance of BiVO 4 photoanodes, yet how the local incorporation environment governs charge-carrier dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a direct structure-function relationship between the local environments of Fe, Co, and Ni and the resulting charge-dynamics in BiVO 4 . Combining synchrotron-based X-ray spectroscopies with femtosecond-to-microsecond photophysical measurements, we show that all transition metals improve water oxidation activity relative to pristine BiVO 4 , following the trend (Ni > Fe > Co) incorporated > BiVO 4 . Fe and Co adopt heterogeneous, weakly coupled oxide-like environments that generate disordered electronic states and only moderate improvements in charge separation. In contrast, Ni forms highly oxidized, locally octahedrally coordinated Ni–O units that remain electronically coupled to the BiVO 4 lattice, modifying the V–O electronic structure, suppressing charge localisation and recombination, and extending carrier lifetimes from femtoseconds to microseconds. Operando X-ray absorption further reveals that lattice-incorporated Ni remains electronically responsive under working conditions, directly linking local electronic structure to photogenerated charge accumulation. These findings demonstrate that the photoelectrochemical behaviour of transition-metal-modified BiVO 4 is governed by the nature of metal–lattice electronic coupling rather than by the identity of the incorporated species, providing a general design principle for oxide photoanodes.

papers.title: Engineering Conductive Polymer Brushes for Bioelectronics and Biomedical applications
papers.abstract: Conductive polymer brushes, among the most promising advanced materials in bioelectronics and medical applications, have drawn broad attention because they uniquely integrate electrical conductivity, biocompatibility, surface functionalization, and the ability to achieve accurate structural design. Through their brush-like morphology, these platforms—while enhancing electrical charge transfer—also enable control over protein adsorption, mitigate surface contamination (biofouling), modulate cell–material interactions, and allow selective immobilization of biological molecules. In this review, the scientific basis of brush-like conductive polymers, their structural characteristics, and the governing concepts of electrical conductivity are reviewed first. Next, the key materials employed, including polypyrrole, polyaniline, PEDOT, and their derivatives, are presented and compared, together with biocompatible polymers and hybrid systems. Then, engineering approaches such as tuning grafting density, adjusting chain length, tailoring polymer architecture, using surface-initiated polymerization techniques, performing surface modification, designing stimuli-responsive platforms, and pursuing composite engineering are examined. Finally, the most significant challenges, current constraints, and future prospects for developing a new generation of brush-like conducting polymers are assessed.

papers.title: Turning Nd-Fe-B Swarf into High-value Bulk Feedstocks via Sustainable Hydrogen Plasma: From Rare-earth Oxides to Metals and Hydrides
papers.abstract: Rare-earth permanent magnets (REPMs) are crucial for electric vehicles, wind turbines and other high-efficiency electric motor systems. However, their production is energy intensive, and global recycling rates are below 0.2%. Machining swarf is the main industrial waste from REPMs production. Despite its high rare-earth elements (REEs) content (~20 wt.%), it has received limited attention for sustainable recycling. We introduce hydrogen plasma reduction (HPR) as a new environmentally-friendly method to recover REEs from REPM swarf. By tuning the hydrogen content and treatment time, we obtain phase‑separated metallic Fe and high-purity rare-earth oxides that are usable as direct feedstock in REPM production. The process also enables direct rare-earth hydride formation, confirming the in-operando metallization of rare-earth oxides in melted state. This procedure turns REPM swarf into separated, high-value, high-purity feedstock in a single, acid-free step. Our approach reduces the huge 70 kg CO 2 /kg average footprint of finished magnet by about 90% and decreases the dependence on critical REE supply chains.

papers.title: Kinetic Programming of Dynamic Covalent Networks via Isomer-pure Diels-Alder Kinetics
papers.abstract: The precise control of material properties through molecular-level architecture remains an enormous challenge in materials science. Here, we present a platform for the kinetic programming of covalently crosslinked networks by translating selective cycloreversion kinetics of isomer-pure endo- and exo-Diels-Alder (DA) diastereomers into controlled material responses. By combining experimental kinetic studies with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we identify a selectivity window at 70 °C that enables sequential, temperature-selective cycloreversion. We demonstrate that these thermolabile motifs retain their molecular-level kinetic selectivity when incorporated into bulk macromolecular networks, as confirmed by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and high-resolution magic-angle spinning (HR-MAS) NMR spectroscopy. To demonstrate such precise kinetic control, we fabricate via multi-photon printing mono- and multi-material microstructures that can be degraded in a stepwise and temperature-selective manner. We herein thus establish a robust design paradigm for responsive materials whose macroscopic functional changes are programmed at the stereochemical level of a single molecular motif.

papers.title: Terazosin analog 7d shows low predicted α1-adrenergic binder-likelihood across subtypes and high predicted PGK1 binder-likelihood in a Parkinson's disease repurposing analysis
papers.abstract: Terazosin binds and activates phosphoglycerate kinase 1 (PGK1), a mechanism associated with neuroprotection in preclinical Parkinson's disease models, but its established α1-antagonist pharmacology creates an unwanted orthostatic liability in the PGK1-repurposing context.1,2 Published terazosin analogs have been optimised against PGK1 activation; Wang et al. did not report α1-subtype profiling of them.3 Ten ligands were evaluated with the Boltz-2 co-folding model against PGK1 and all three human α1 subtypes, with five seed-labelled predictions per target–ligand cell (200 predictions). The ring-opened analog 7d received uniformly low predicted binder-likelihoods at α1A, α1B and α1D (0.108, 0.121 and 0.120), roughly a third of terazosin's under the same five-seed protocol (0.306, 0.399 and 0.319). It simultaneously received the panel's highest PGK1 value (0.693 ± 0.011); no other compound combined comparably low α1 means with a PGK1 mean that high. The α1 result was consistent across subtypes and reproduced the expected control behaviour, with the established α1 antagonist tamsulosin scoring highly at all three α1 subtypes and substantially lower at PGK1. The PGK1 axis was less settled: the model did not reproduce the published activation rank, and an orthogonal docking cross-check reversed the 7d-overterazosin ordering. 7d's experimental case does not rest on that contested ordering, as it is already synthesised and independently increased relative PGK1 activity in a published assay. These are binding predictions: they do not establish functional α1 antagonism, reduced orthostatic liability, activation potency, or safety. 7d is nominated for direct α1-subtype binding and functional antagonism assays, alongside a PGK1 activation assay.

papers.title: Tracing chemical water pollution through global supply chains: A framework integrating PRTR data, grey water footprint, and MRIO analysis
papers.abstract: Chemical pollution has emerged as a major threat to freshwater sustainability; however, its impacts and associated responsibilities across global supply chains remain insufficiently understood. This study developed an assessment framework to trace water pollution from chemical emissions embodied in global supply chains driven by final consumption. Pollutant Release and Transfer Register (PRTR) data, grey water footprint assessment, and a multi-regional input-output (MRIO) model were integrated. Annual emissions of 17 chemicals reported in PRTR systems from 39 countries were harmonized and linked to the GLORIA database. Freshwater emissions were estimated using substance-specific transfer fractions from the USEtox model, converted into assimilation water volumes using the grey water concept as a proxy for water pollution. Consumption-based water pollution was quantified using MRIO analysis. Although a limited number of chemicals dominated emissions, priority chemicals changed after accounting for environmental fate and substance-specific water quality thresholds. More than half of the impacts in some countries were induced by foreign final consumption, highlighting the importance of consumption-based responsibility. By identifying priority chemicals, sectors, and consuming countries, this framework provides a basis for understanding the responsibility for water pollution across global supply chains and supports supply chain-oriented chemical management strategies to mitigate chemical water pollution.

papers.title: Air-Stable Nickel Oxide Nanosheets as a Model Platform for Decoupling Structure-Activity Relation in Oxygen Evolving Electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: Nickel oxides are among the most active electrocatalysts for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a key process in green hydrogen production. However, the fundamental reaction mechanism remains unclear, limiting the rational design of electrocatalysts capable of reducing the cost of sustainable hydrogen generation. Here, we develop an air-stable model electrocatalyst system of sub-monolayer nickel oxide (NiO) nanosheets with controlled coverages and morphologies on atomically flat Au(111), enabling atomic-scale investigation of structure–activity relationships under ambient conditions. Atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM) in ultra-high vacuum (UHV), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electrochemical measurements were combined to correlate nanosheet structure and composition with electrocatalytic performance. We reveal OER activity scales with nanosheet edge density, identifying edge sites as the dominant active sites of the reaction. XPS measurements demonstrate the formation of nickel hydroxide on the nanosheet surfaces and edges following OER testing, consistent with the generation of a catalytically active nickel oxyhydroxide phase during operation. These findings provide insight into the structure–activity relationships governing NiO electrocatalysts and demonstrate a strategy for resolving atomic scale structure–activity relationships without the need to maintain samples under UHV. We propose that future NiO-based OER electrocatalysts are designed to maximize the number density of accessible edge sites hence, maximizing the electrocatalytic activity.

papers.title: PAMOS: Encoding Chemical Environment Response in a Minimal Basis Set Molecular Orbital Method. I. One-Electron Diatomic Ions
papers.abstract: We present PAMOS (Parameterized Approximate Molecular Orbital method with Slater orbitals), a semiempirical electronic structure method that keeps a minimal Slater-type basis set yet captures the response of atomic orbitals to their molecular environment. Rather than fit many coupled parameters to a training set, we build the model from the most elementary molecular species and introduce each parameter to emulate one feature of ab initio theory that a minimal basis cannot reach. Two devices distinguish the method. Different classes of integrals receive different effective Slater exponents, ζ e N for electron–nuclear attraction and ζ S for overlap, so a single basis function emulates the radial contraction and polarization that would otherwise require an extended basis. The off-diagonal Hamiltonian matrix elements satisfy a conservation-of-charge constraint that cancels the interatomic electrostatic interactions at large internuclear separation. Together with a bonding parameter λ and a heteronuclear weighting exponent p, these devices reproduce benchmark potential energy curves for ten one-electron diatomic ions, from H2++ to BeLi 6+ , to within ∼1 kcal/mol ( Z 2 -scaled). A core-correction strategy extends the model to one-valence-electron ions from Li2+ to BC 6+ . We close with a preview of a two-electron treatment of static correlation and a route to dynamic correlation.

papers.title: General Applicability of Optical Crystallography to Time-Resolved Serial Xray Crystallography
papers.abstract: Femtosecond laser excitation of molecular crystals results in heterogeneous populations under all conditions of laser power, laser polarization, and crystal symmetry. Crystal optics determine the photoselection and heterogeneous distributions in time-resolved crystallography; their analysis allows the separation of pure species from the photochemical ensemble. Laser fluence dependence of timeresolved crystallography can therefore not be rigorously analyzed without accounting for the ensemble contributions. Since the separation of heterogeneous populations under a single fluence already provides an interaction dependence at the level of pure species, the additional measurement of the fluence dependence is not strictly necessary under most conditions. Optical crystallography can be applied generally to all 230 three-dimensional space groups and for all combinations of linear and circular optical polarization and linear and circular absorber types, including the photoselection treatment applicable to cubic systems. Specific guidance for all these combinations is presented, with the specific consideration of X-ray crystallographic data for serial crystallography, which includes the treatment of pseudo-merohedral twinning.

papers.title: The Brewing Process and Hop Chemistry
papers.abstract: Beer production is often represented as a sequence of unit operations, whereas product quality emerges from a coupled network of extraction, enzymatic conversion, thermal reaction, phase separation, microbial metabolism, and interfacial phenomena. Hops add a second layer of complexity because their bitter acids, volatile terpenoids, sulfur compounds, and polyphenols respond differently to temperature, time, pH, oxygen, solids, and yeast. This Review connects the brewing process to hop chemistry from malting and mashing through boiling, whirlpool treatment, fermentation, maturation, and packaging. It emphasizes four recurring control variables: molecular polarity and phase behavior; reaction and extraction kinetics; the history of oxygen and heat exposure; and the distinction between an analytical marker and sensory response. Particular attention is given to the whirlpool, which should be regarded not only as a separator but also as a declining-temperature reactor in which α-acid isomerization, trub formation, adsorption, volatile loss, and late-hop extraction continue simultaneously. A previously disclosed 3000-L pilot case is used descriptively to illustrate these trade-offs: extension of whirlpool residence from 20 to 120 min was accompanied by higher final-beer bitterness, a marked increase in myrcene, modest changes in oxygenated monoterpenes, and stronger overall hop aroma; no further sensory gain was observed at 180 min. Because this case lacks replicated process runs, it is interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than causal proof. The Review also examines yeast-mediated aroma conversion, oxidative aging, foam stability, the operational nature of the International Bitterness Unit, lightstruck flavor, and hop-derived antimicrobial activity. An integrated process-design framework is proposed in which targets for fermentability, bitterness, aroma, foam, colloidal stability, and shelf life are optimized together rather than one operation at a time.

papers.title: Phytochemical analysis and screening of biological activities of Anthemis lorestanica Iranshahr
papers.abstract: This is the first report of studying phytochemicals and biological activity of the essential oil and different extracts of Anthemis lorestanica Iranshahr. Flower essential oil was analyzed using GC-MS. Total phenolic, flavonoid and tannin contents were evaluated and HPLC analysis of the richest extract was performed to quantify some flavonoids and phenolic acids. Antioxidant, antimicrobial and cytotoxic activity of the extracts was also investigated. Germacrene-D was identified as the main component in the flower essential oil. HPLC analysis of methanol extract from the stems and leaves resulted in existing high amount of chlorogenic acid. This extract shows also high antioxidant activity in DPPH and beta-carotene assays; on the other hand, essential oil and non-polar extracts showed higher antimicrobial activity against tested bacteria strains. Regarding the results from anticancer activity, hydro-alcoholic extract shows high activity on Hela cell line via MTT test.

papers.title: LIFE: Line-Shape Integrity and Fidelity Enhancement for Reconstructing Non-Uniformly Sampled Protein NMR Spectra
papers.abstract: Non-uniform sampling (NUS) accelerates multidimensional NMR spectroscopy, but strong undersampling can introduce missing peaks, artifacts, and line-shape distortion. Here, we present LIFE, a self-supervised deep-learning framework for reconstructing two-dimensional and three-dimensional NUS NMR spectra. LIFE combines paired observations generated from experimental FIDs, neighborhood-based contextual inputs, and a five-stage cascaded U-Net with data-consistency enforcement. Across four retrospectively undersampled protein NMR datasets, LIFE yielded lower reconstruction errors than hmsIST, SMILE, and JTF-Net under matched exponentially weighted sampling conditions. Peak-level analyses of representative 2D and 3D datasets further showed improved peak recovery, fewer false peaks, and smaller peak-intensity and peak-position errors. These findings support LIFE as a reconstruction approach that preserves spectral features under the evaluated experimental conditions.

papers.title: Discrimination and Classification of Coke Variants via Hybrid E-tongue
papers.abstract: Soft drinks contain different proportions of sugars, salts and other compounds, giving them a signature taste. We explore whether hybrid e-tongue (HET), utilized previously to discriminate pure tastes, can discern the tastes of Original (OC), Diet (DC) and Zero Coke (ZC). We further enquire how (dis)similar their taste is to pure tastes. Principal component analysis (PCA) of open circuit potential, pH, charge-transfer resistance, and double-layer capacitance data generated by HET distinguishes OC, DC, and ZC, with a silhouette coefficient of 0.7, accounting for 92.75% of the total variance. HET captures compositional variation and places Coke variants away from pure tastes, and components’ ionic strength and binding ability at the Ni electrode facilitate hierarchical clustering in dendrograms. This encourages further study using HET with modifications to yield a detailed taste map of Coke variants, thereby adding objectivity to formulation optimization in soft drink sectors for consumer satiety. Keywords: Carbonated soft drinks, e-tongue, taste mapping, multivariate data analysis.

papers.title: Strategies Toward Pharmaceutical Self-reliance in Nepal for Strengthening the Health Care System.
papers.abstract: Under the federal system of governance in Nepal, health facilities are supervised by the local and provincial governments. However, people have faced challenges in accessing quality, affordable medicines over the years. Lack of innovation and technology, the absence of active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing facilities, and weak pharmaceutical policies have contributed to the shortage of medicines in the country. Thus, there is an urgent need to move toward self-sufficiency in the pharmaceutical industry. This paper presents a literature review to investigate approaches to pharmaceutical growth and to expand its potential in production, testing, and innovation. The study proposes evidence-based strategies, including the effective implementation of pluralistic environments, fostering university-industry collaboration for innovation, and introducing strong policies for the growth of the pharmaceutical industry. Ultimately, the combined actions from academia, industry, and government can support the health care system of the country by strengthening domestic pharmaceutical capacity.

papers.title: Synthordle: A web-based game for retrosynthetic training
papers.abstract: Organic chemistry courses often suffer from high attrition and may benefit from instructional approaches beyond passive recall. Retrosynthetic analysis, a core skill for organic chemists, requires iterative practice and flexible reasoning rather than rote memorization, making it well-suited to a game-based format. Inspired by the popular game Wordle, we developed Synthordle, a free, browser-based game that challenges players to design multi-step syntheses through color-coded feedback on their guesses. Supporting both synthetic and retrosynthetic modes across multiple difficulty levels, Synthordle is open-source, requires no installation, and can be adapted to a range of courses. Recently adopted in a graduate-level synthesis course at Scripps Research, Synthordle offers an accessible, game-based complement to traditional problem sets for building retrosynthetic reasoning skills.

papers.title: Sustainable Ammonia Production from Biogas: A Review
papers.abstract: Green hydrogen produced from biogas reforming offers a low-carbon feedstock route to sustainable ammonia synthesis, coupling waste valorization with decarbonized fertilizer and chemical production. This review examines the technical foundations of this pathway: the composition and purification of biogas; the principal reforming routes to hydrogen — steam reforming, dry reforming, partial oxidation, and autothermal reforming — together with the catalysts that enable them; the cryogenic air separation required to supply oxygen and nitrogen to the process; and the reactor configurations and catalysts used for ammonia synthesis. The economic evaluation methodology commonly used to assess hydrogen production cost is outlined, alongside a SWOT analysis of green hydrogen production in Egypt, a country with substantial biogas feedstock potential and a strategic export position. Ammonia's principal industrial applications are also summarized. Taken together, this review provides a technical basis for evaluating biogas-derived green hydrogen as a route to sustainable ammonia production, particularly in regions with abundant organic waste streams and growing renewable energy ambitions.
