Furthermore, we demonstrate that the direct use of a solution of pre-formed iminophosphorane eliminates end-user azide handling altogether. The utility of the reaction was demonstrated through reaction scale-up and late-stage functionalisation of pharmaceutically-relevant compounds.

papers.title: Pauli Charges Improve the Training of Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Despite the utility of machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), they can be difficult to train and use due to a lack of well-defined methods to assess their accuracy. This problem can be mitigated by combining traditional MLIPs with pair potentials that have machine learned coefficients. The use of pair potentials with strictly defined limiting behavior can help create a more reliable MLIP by restricting a general atomic neural network (ANN) to regions of the training set with lower variance in interatomic distances and total energies. This approach is demonstrated by simultaneously training both a short-range ANN as well as an ANN to fit charges for a Pauli repulsion potential. We show that this combination of ANNs significantly improves both the accuracy and stability of MLIPs across a wide range of materials, temperatures, and pressures. In particular, the addition of Pauli repulsion greatly improves the accuracy of potentials for use at high temperatures and high pressures, while also leading to a modest improvement in accuracy at ambient temperature and pressure conditions.

papers.title: Sources of the Most Prevalent Persistent Organic Pollutant in the Global Atmosphere
papers.abstract: Global atmospheric contamination with hexachlorobuta-1,3-diene (HCBD) has been rising rapidly for the past decade, despite its listing as a persistent organic pollutant (POP) under the Stockholm Convention. The unintentional nature of its production makes it challenging to identify emission sources. A multi-pronged investigation integrating monitoring evidence, emission estimation, and environmental transport modeling reveals that Chinese emissions, likely from chlorinated solvent manufacturing, are necessary and sufficient to explain the temporal and spatial trends in HCBD contamination recorded in East Asia and across the globe. A multiple-fold increase of emissions after the time of listing underscores significant shortcomings in the provisions of Article 5 of the Convention in reducing, let alone eliminating, the environmental releases of unintentionally produced POPs.

papers.title: Complex Fragment Coupling via O-Mesyl Hydroxylamines: Direct Conversion of Primary Amines to Electrophilic Aminating Agents
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-containing molecules are ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals, natural products, ligands, and functional materials, sustaining continued interest in efficient C–N bond-forming strategies. Although electrophilic amination has emerged as a powerful complement to classical nucleophilic substitution and cross-coupling methods, the transfer of structurally complex NH-alkyl groups remains limited by the lack of general access to suitably reactive electrophilic aminating reagents. Herein, we report the direct single-step oxidation of primary amines to N -alkyl- O -mesyl hydroxylamines using dimesyl peroxide (MPO). This transformation achieves an umpolung of otherwise nucleophilic amines and provides rapid access to synthetically versatile electrophilic nitrogen building blocks under mild conditions. A broad substrate scope enables the preparation of structurally complex and chiral N -alkyl- O -mesyl hydroxylamines, including derivatives of amino acids, natural products, and pharmaceuticals. These reagents were directly deployed in established electrophilic amination manifolds, including arene C–H amination, olefin aziridination, and aza-Rubottom oxidation, enabling the transfer of structurally complex and chiral amine fragments. Collectively, this work establishes a general strategy for converting readily available primary amines into electrophilic nitrogen fragments for efficient C–N bond formation and N-electrophilic fragment coupling.

papers.title: Assembly-by-Elimination of 3D Nanoarchitectures with Designed Interstitials and Interweaves
papers.abstract: The realization of metamaterials with tailored functional responses requires three-dimensional (3D) architectures that combine low packing fractions with complex topology. Such metastructures can enhance strength-to-weight ratios, accommodate large deformations, manipulate light and enable efficient transport and actuation under 3D confinement. However, extending topology-driven design from the macroscale to the nanoscale remains challenging due to limitations in 3D nanofabrication. Although self-assembly offers a path to realizing 3D organizations, it typically favors densely packed, high-symmetry structures, making it difficult to achieve intricate, low-density architectures with complex connectivity. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Assembly-By-Elimination (ABEL), a strategy for designing periodic topologically complex low-packing-fraction 3D nanoscale metastructures. ABEL begins by assembling a fully interconnected, high-packing-fraction template lattice, followed by programmable removal of selected structural elements, yielding a targeted metastructure. We experimentally demonstrate the ABEL strategy using, as a 3D template, a body-centered-cubic DNA lattice composed of DNA cubic frames with a sequence-specific set of bonds. After assembly, addressable elimination of bonds sculpts the template into an open metastructure by disconnecting prescribed individual frames or sublattices, thus realizing low-density nanoscale organizations and interpenetrating networks. We then investigate the Young’s modulus of created metastructures, and show that it scales approximately linearly with bond density, directly linking nanoscale architecture to mechanical response. By combining designed 3D lattice templates with addressable elimination of bonds and structural elements, ABEL provides a route to realizing complex architectures with prescribed nanoscale topology.

papers.title: Programming Rotational Register to Prescribe Crystal Polymorphism
papers.abstract: Crystal polymorphism underlies many of the distinct properties of condensed matter, yet for atoms and molecules, polymorphs are typically selected by thermodynamics and kinetics rather than by design. Programming crystal polymorphism is particularly challenging for structures that share identical bond connectivity but differ only in the relative orientation of neighboring building blocks. Although programmable self-assembly can prescribe which building blocks bind, it does not directly encode how they are oriented once bonded. Here, we introduce the rotational register, the relative torsional orientation between bonded building blocks, as an independent bond descriptor that complements programmable valence and connectivity. Progressive symmetry breaking of the sequence-programmed DNA pattern at the vertices of DNA tetrahedra provides increasingly precise control over the rotational register, enabling the selective assembly of tetrahedrally coordinated crystal polymorphs: type-II clathrate, cubic diamond, and hexagonal diamond. Cubic and hexagonal diamond differ only in the rotational register encoded at a single vertex type, yet this local rule controls polymorphism while preserving identical bond connectivity. The programmed polymorphs are validated by small-angle X-ray scattering, electron tomography, 2 and both Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations. Furthermore, reprogramming the rotational register enables reversible transformation between cubic and hexagonal diamond. These results establish rotational register as a programmable bond descriptor, complementing programmable connectivity with explicit control over the orientation of bonded building blocks.

papers.title: Foldamers with Two Distinct Helical Motifs Controlled by Solvent
papers.abstract: Abiotic foldamers that switch between distinct, well-defined geometries are rare. Here, we report a structurally simple series of oligomers with alternating or tho-p henylene and 2,3-pyrazinylene repeat units. Deconvolution of variable-temperature ¹H NMR spectra, with the help of ab initio chemical shift predictions, shows that the oligomers favor a compact, arene-stacked helix in chloroform but a structurally distinct extended helix in acetone. The longest oligomer investigated, a heptamer, exhibits nearly perfect solvent-switching behavior at low temperature, effectively doubling its length in acetone compared to chloroform. X-ray crystallography confirms that the hybrid backbone is capable of both folding motifs. While arene–arene stacking drives folding in chloroform, non-classical intramolecular C-H···N hydrogen bonds appear to be more important in acetone. Both geometries are enthalpically favored in their respective solvents, highlighting how a balance of weak, competing interactions can be harnessed to achieve large-scale geometry changes in synthetic foldamers.

papers.title: Tailoring carbon nitride nanoarchitecture and cellular interactions through hydrothermal alkaline etching
papers.abstract: Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ) is a versatile material for biomedical, energy, and environmental applications. Bulk g-C 3 N 4 is commonly used as a precursor for nanoscale objects, yet systematic links between synthesis conditions, nanostructure morphology, surface chemistry, and biological response remain limited. Here, we have fabricated a palette of carbon nitride nanostructures via hydrothermal alkaline etching. By varying the hydroxide (LiOH, NaOH, or KOH) and reaction conditions, etching yields carbon nitride quantum dots, carbon nitride nanowires and their networks, as well as larger flakes and sponge-like objects. Automated transmission electron microscopy image analysis supported this comparison by converting heterogeneous micrographs into object-level morphology and particle-size statistics. The hydroxide type also controls surface chemistry: LiOH and KOH promote stronger oxidative functionalization, whereas NaOH leads to a more hydrated and passivated surface. In immortalized human cervical cancer cells, the samples show little effect on metabolic activity after 24 h at 200 µg mL −1 , while cellular accumulation varies markedly with preparation conditions. Notably, smaller nanostructures do not guarantee higher cellular accumulation, suggesting that nanowire networks with entangled quantum dots may dominate membrane adhesion. Overall, this work provides a practical route to tune carbon nitride nanostructures for bioimaging applications.

papers.title: Unraveling the Temperature-Dependent Redox Cycle of Chromium Species in Molten Chloride Salt via In-Situ X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Molten chloride salt is a widely studied high-temperature electrolyte, with established use in pyrochemical reprocessing and electrorefining, and frequent use as a model system for concentrated solar power and molten salt reactor applications. Chromium (Cr) is a key element in high-temperature structural alloys. However, the temperature-dependent evolution and stability of Cr species in this environment remain insufficiently understood. Cr-redox chemistry in molten chloride salts governs the dissolution, oxidation and transformation of Cr-containing species, with direct implications for corrosion and dealloying of structural alloys as well as broader molten-salt processing applications. In the present study, the chemical stability of CrCl2, CrCl3, and Cr2O3 in LiCl-KCl eutectic molten salt at elevated temperatures was systematically investigated using in-situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy. The results revealed that CrCl3 and Cr2O3 remained chemically stable under the tested conditions, whereas CrCl2 underwent oxidation by impurities to form Cr2O3 at 500 °C, but partially converted back to Cr2+ species upon cooling to room temperature. Additionally, the interaction between chromium and NiCl2 in molten salt was examined, indicating that chromium likely reduced Ni2+ to metallic Ni0, while being oxidized to Cr2+, which subsequently underwent a similar chemical evolution as CrCl2 in the molten salt. These findings unravel a temperature-dependent, impurity-mediated redox cycle of Cr species in molten chloride salt, providing a foundation for understanding and controlling Cr the dissolution, oxidation and transformation, and for developing effective corrosion-mitigation strategies to enhance the stability of high-temperature structural alloys in molten-salt systems.

papers.title: From Molecular Intent to Auditable Computation: Black-Box Evaluation of a Text-to-Experiment Platform
papers.abstract: Natural-language interfaces can simplify computational chemistry workflows, but a plausible model response does not establish that an experiment is executable, traceable, or scientifically correct. We evaluate a proprietary text-to-experiment platform that separates intent interpretation from scientific calculation and exposes an observable path from request to validated plan, controlled execution, linked output, and auditable result package. A frozen offline suite contained nine benchmark families and 14 runs spanning planning, molecular computation, dataset controls, baseline modeling, and complete reruns; all passed their declared software gates. The 30-case deterministic intent corpus matched every expected plan and safety label, including seven required blocks. Because it used mocked provider envelopes, this is a compiler regression result rather than live-model performance. Across two generations of seeds, validity and constraint-pass rates were 1.0, uniqueness was 0.870 and 0.769; and mean pairwise Tanimoto distance was 0.754 and 0.696. Two complete reruns agreed on all 12 semantic and integrity checks spanning molecular identities, descriptors, conformers, artifacts, manifests, hashes, and provenance. A caffeine case links calculated properties and 2D structures to ETKDGv3/UFF conformer approximations. These results support controlled repeatability and auditability within the evaluated environment, not independent reproducibility or chemical efficacy. Benchmarks were internally constructed, panels were small, and no wet-lab validation was performed. The contribution is an evidence-linked black-box framework for observable text-to-experiment behavior under a proprietary boundary.

papers.title: Sulfonylative Pauson-Khand Reaction
papers.abstract: The Pauson-Khand reaction is a landmark transformation in organic synthesis, enabling the rapid assembly of cyclopentenone frameworks through a (2+2+1) cycloaddition of alkenes, alkynes, and carbon monoxide. Despite its long-standing impact, the conceptual framework of Pauson-Khand chemistry has remained largely restricted to carbon monoxide incorporation. Here we report a fundamentally distinct sulfonylative Pauson-Khand-type protocol enabled by interception of a photoinduced energy-transfer-mediated (2+2) cycloaddition pathway. The reaction proceeds under mild, energy-efficient conditions, exhibits broad substrate scope across diverse 1,6-enynes, and delivers products in good to excellent yields. A complementary photocatalyst-free variant relying on direct triplet excitation of alkynyl cyclohexadienones is also disclosed. Mechanistic studies, supported by Density Functional Theory calculations reveal the origin of reactivity and selectivity and establish this process as a mechanistically orthogonal alternative to classical Pauson–Khand chemistry.

papers.title: Iterative Constructing and Screening of DNA-Encoded Libraries Enable the Discovery and Structure Optimization of Macrocyclic Hit Compounds
papers.abstract: Macrocyclic peptides occupy a privileged "middle space" in drug discovery, offering the specificity of biologics combined with the synthetic tractability of small molecules. However, the rapid identification and structural optimization of macrocyclic leads for challenging targets remain formidable tasks. Here, we report a robust DNA-encoded library technology (DELT) platform designed for the synthesis, screening, and iterative optimization of novel dimeric macrocyclic peptides. Initially, a pooled library of approximately 1.2 billion unique members, cyclized via diverse thioether linkages or disulfide formation, was constructed and screened against the oncogenic target MDM2. This first-generation selection yielded compound Comp_1, which incorporates a highly enriched pharmacophoric fragment, F_1, and displays a 𝐾i value of 1.5 𝜇M. Leveraging the synthetic modularity of our platform, we established an iterative optimization campaign by incorporating F_1 into a second-generation asymmetric dimeric library (DEL_2) synthesized with enriched building blocks. A subsequent selection campaign against DEL_2 led to the discovery of highly potent macrocyclic candidates, exemplified by compound Comp_2 with a 𝐾i value of 18 nM—representing an approximate 100-fold affinity enhancement over the first-generation hit. This work not only highlights MDM2-targeting macrocyclic binders but also establishes a highly efficient, generalizable DELT-based iterative workflow for the rapid evolution of peptidic leads.

papers.title: pH-Dependent Free Energies of Insulin Fibril Assembly from Protonation Ensemble Statistics
papers.abstract: Protonation equilibria govern the pH-dependent stability of protein aggregates, yet their thermodynamic implications remain difficult to quantify. Here, we establish a direct connection between site-unresolved protonation statistics and pH-dependent free energy differences within a semi-grand canonical framework. Using constant-pH simulations of insulin fibril assemblies from monomers to octamers, we show that the differential protonation response relative to the isolated monomer is directly related to the pH dependence of the assembly free energy. Integration of this response reveals a non-monotonic free energy landscape with a crossover near pH ≈ 5.5–6 separating distinct electrostatic regimes. While the position of the crossover is largely insensitive to aggregate size, the stabilization increases systematically with it, demonstrating cooperative proton-coupled interactions arising from charge regulation within the fibrillar assembly. These results show that pH-dependent stability is encoded in site-unresolved titration curves, while site-resolved analysis provides mechanistic interpretation. The present work demonstrates that protonation statistics sampled by constant-pH simulations provide direct access to the pH-dependent thermodynamics of biomolecular self-association.

papers.title: Conformational Flexibility and Size of Large trans-Vinylene-Bridged Thiaporphyrinoids Influences Boron Coordination Modes
papers.abstract: Two π-extended core-modified porphyrinoids were synthetized and structurally characterized to probe boron-induced geometry switching and modulation of electron delocalization. Trans -vinylene-bridged hexathia-dodecaphyrin forms the largest, fully characterized, porphyrinoid BODIPY-type complex while retaining parent, open-form geometry, whereas octathia-hexadecaphyrin does not support boron coordination. Notably, a smaller, figure-of-eight tetrathia-octaphyrin analogue exhibits unusual, direct C–B bond formation, highlighting pronounced structural sensitivity of expanded porphyrinoids and their utility in accessing unconventional bonding and coordination modes.

papers.title: Iron-digermanium cluster: synthesis, Lewis-base-induced isomerization, dihydrogen activation, and alkene cycloaddition
papers.abstract: Heterometallic complexes containing multiple heavier tetrylidyne ligands (RE; E = Si, Ge, Sn, Pb) are promising for cooperative bond activation but are rare because RE units tend to oligomerize. We present the synthesis, electronic structure, and reactivity of an irondigermanium complex, [Fe(GeAr’)2] (1, Ar’ = 2,6-Dipp2-C6H3, Dipp = 2,6-iPr2-C6H3), featuring adjacent Ar’Ge units bonded to Fe through double and single Fe–Ge bonds, respectively. Complex 1 reacts readily with tBuNC, H2, and styrene via coordination, bond activation, and cycloaddition pathways, producing diverse structural outcomes. Coordination of tBuNC to Fe induces a formal reductive elimination of the two Ar’Ge units, forming an iron-digermyne complex (2) with a rare σ,σ-type double-bonding mode. Under mild conditions, H2 is activated, forming a germyl(IV)-iron-germylidyne complex (3). The reaction with styrene involves a [3+2] cycloaddition, yielding a bis(germylene)-iron complex (4). Notably, the reaction with 2,3-dimethyl-1,3-butadiene (DMB) proceeds via an unusual kinetic [3+4] cycloaddition pathway to produce a bis(germylene)-iron species (5), which then irreversibly rearranges into the thermodynamically favored [1+4] product (6). In contrast, the heavier iron-tin analog exhibits distinct reactivity towards these substrates, highlighting fundamental differences between Fe–Ge and Fe–Sn bonding and reactivity.

papers.title: Explainable Machine Learning for Low-Emission Methane Tri-Reforming: Carbon Formation, Hydrogen Production, and Operating-Window Optimization
papers.abstract: Tri-reforming of methane (TRM) is a promising route for producing hydrogen-rich syngas while partially utilizing CO2, but its deployment is limited by trade-offs among methane conversion, syngas composition, reactor duty, and carbon deposition. In this study, a Gibbsequilibrium model in Aspen Plus was used to generate a database of 46,464 operating points spanning temperature, pressure, and inlet H2O/CH4, CO2/CH4, and O2/CH4 ratios. Decision tree, random forest, XGBoost, and artificial neural network models were trained and compared, followed by SHAP and permutation-importance analysis and multi-objective genetic-algorithm optimization. The neural network showed the best predictive performance. Explainability analysis identified temperature as the dominant factor governing carbon formation, followed by steam, carbon dioxide, and oxygen feed ratios. Optimization revealed multiple distinct operating windows, confirming that no single universal optimum exists and demonstrating a rapid, interpretable framework for low-emission TRM screening and design.

papers.title: Bright Red Solid-State Circularly Polarized Luminescence from Crystalline H-Aggregated Perylene Bisimide
papers.abstract: Achieving deep-red circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) in the solid state from purely organic molecules remains challenging because molecular transitions are magnetic dipole-forbidden and nonradiative decay is enhanced by the energy-gap law. We present a pair of chiral perylene bisimide (PBI) dyes that show intense deep-red CPL with high color purity in thin films. Using a crystal-engineering strategy, we achieved significant mixing of Coulombic and charge-transfer (CT) coupling between π−stacked PBIs, resulting in an exceptionally large exciton splitting (2J). The resulting twisted H-aggregated PBI crystals exhibits pronounced violet-orange pleochroism. Polarization-dependent absorption spectroscopy of single crystals reveals one of the largest 2J values (∼165 meV) reported for H-aggregated PBIs. This large splitting stabilizes the lowest Frenkel exciton, suppresses excimer formation, and enables bright, long-lived excitonic PL with high spectral purity. Increased CT character further enhances the magnetic transition dipole moment, which is reflected in large PL dissymmetry factor (glum ∼ 3-8×10−3). Combined with a high PL quantum yield (ϕPL) of 8%, these materials rank among the brightest known deep-red solid state CPL emitters based on purely organic molecules. At 100 K, a 23-fold enhancement in emission intensity with marked spectral narrowing highlights their potential for cryogenic CPL applications.

papers.title: Which Metrics Best Capture Protein Structural Change in Molecular Dynamics Simulations? Evaluating Score Combinations and Force Field Effects
papers.abstract: The scores RMSD, TM-score, GDT, lDDT, SphereGrinder, CAD, QCS, FlexE, and MolProbity provide an automated, comprehensive assessment of conformational changes and structural quality of proteins and thus represent a promising tool for routine use in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, particularly in high-throughput settings. However, it remains unclear to what extent these scores provide redundant information and which scores are most informative for capturing conformational changes. Based on MD simulations of 268 diverse proteins, we demonstrate that the investigated scores are highly correlated and that one global score (or QCS), one local score, and FlexE capture almost 90% of the variance across all scores. Since MD randomness partially explains FlexE’s variability, we argue that a combination of one global and one local score is sufficient for most practical applications. We also investigate the influence of simulation setups and find that the choice of the force field can significantly affect scoring results. In particular, the setup using the Amber ff19sb force field yields systematically different scores than all CHARMM36m-based setups, emphasizing the importance of methodological choices when designing MD experiments and interpreting their results.

papers.title: Predictive Modelling Enables Exploration of the Anticancer Potential of Ruthenium(II) Polypyridyl Complexes
BeamStop: A software for analysing chemical imaging and tomography data
papers.abstract: Chemical imaging datasets, particularly those from techniques like X-ray powder diffraction imaging and tomography (XRD-CT), are challenging to analyse due to their high dimensionality, complexity, and spatial heterogeneity. BeamStop is a specialised software developed to address these challenges through an integrated, tab-based environment tailored to chemical imaging workflows. Created at Finden Ltd to meet the needs we routinely face in synchrotron-based experiments, BeamStop brings together our extensive experience in XRD-CT data processing and analysis. At its core is a powerful hyperspectral imaging explorer, enabling users to visually inspect chemical imaging data and interactively examine spatially-resolved spectra or diffraction patterns. The software also supports workflows such as unsupervised clustering, peak fitting, and mask creation. Importantly, BeamStop introduces a highly optimised GPU Rietveld engine for full profile analysis which delivers results an order of magnitude faster compared to conventional approaches. This GPU capability is complemented by a native CPU solver, the PQ-Net deep learning model, and integration with the TOPAS software. This paper presents an overview of BeamStop's architecture and capabilities, illustrating how it facilitates reproducible, high-throughput interpretation of complex chemical imaging data.

papers.title: A Foundation Model for Accurate Atomistic Simulations in Drug Design
papers.abstract: While artificial intelligence has revolutionized the prediction of static protein structures, characterizing their dynamics and interactions with drug candidates remains a computational bottleneck. Here, we introduce FeNNix-Bio1, a foundation machine learning model designed to power accurate, reactive atomistic simulations of biological systems at an unprecedented speed and scalability. Trained exclusively on high-accuracy computational chemistry data, FeNNix-Bio1 accurately captures complex condensed-phase phenomena such as ion solvation and subtle liquid water properties for which it outperforms state-of-the-art specialized force fields. We demonstrate its versatility across a full spectrum of drug design applications, including the calculation of hydration free energies (HFEs), the structure and dynamics of proteins, the simulation of protein-ligand absolute binding free energies (ABFEs), lipid bilayer properties and chemical reactions. Notably, FeNNix-Bio1 provides excellent agreement with experiments for both the HFEs of the more than 600 molecules of the Freesolv dataset (MAE of 0.7 kcal/mol) and for the ABFEs of 30 representative protein-ligand complexes covering three protein targets (MAE of 1.05 kcal/mol). By enabling scalable, quantum-accurate molecular dynamics without the need for manual parametrization, FeNNix-Bio1 bridges the gap between static structure prediction and dynamic biological reality, unlocking next-generation drug design with physics-driven AI.

papers.title: Association-gated multiphoton activation of inert haloarenes via sequential electron donor–acceptor assembly
papers.abstract: The functionalization of recalcitrant chemical bonds that require extreme reduction potentials is often thwarted by the absence of a defined reaction field to control potent intermediates. Conventional multiphoton photocatalysis generates super-reductants, whose immense energy dissipates through chaotic, diffusion-controlled pathways. Herein, an "association-gated" strategy is introduced that constructs sequential electron donor–acceptor complexes as programmable reaction microenvironments. This system initially captures a single photon through its sulfide/naphthalene monoimide complex. The resulting naphthalene monoimide radical anion serves as a scaffold to pre-organize the haloarene substrate into a second, distinct electron donor–acceptor complex, creating a reaction pocket for the final, energy-storing excitation. Such supramolecular confinement generates an extreme reducing potential at the carbon–halogen bond, suppressing both diffusive side-reactions and parasitic hydrogen atom transfer from amine donors. This unlocks a broad scope of transformations under air-tolerant conditions, providing a versatile tool for late-stage diversification.

papers.title: Development of ionically crosslinked network in metal oxide based carboxylated acrylonitrile butadiene copolymer with self-healing characteristics
papers.abstract: Ionic clusters produced during the crosslinking of elastomers with zinc oxide influence the overall mechanical performance of ionic elastomers such as carboxylated nitrile rubber (XNBR). The composition of these ionic aggregates is investigated for the first time in this work by maintaining time as variable and other factors constant. Lower temperature healing properties by formation of ionic crosslink has been observed. Detailed analysis by Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy revealed that interaction between Zn2+ and COO1- actually affects the bonding structures and Universal Testing Machine proved that ionic crosslink shows better healing efficiency than a combination of covalent and ionic crosslink due to sulphur and zinc oxide, for the first time. The inability to heal the rubber compound at all due to the presence of Carbon Black filler was also observed for the first time.

papers.title: Adapting Pressurized Sample Infusion ESI-MS for Real-time Monitoring of Heterogeneous Photoelectrocatalytic Reactions
papers.abstract: Pressurized sample infusion (PSI) enables real-time electrospray ionization mass spectrometric (ESI-MS) monitoring of reactions through continuous delivery of solution from a pressurized vessel. Existing PSI configurations, however, are not well suited to systems involving heterogeneous catalysts with strict geometric demands, such as TiO2 nanotube plates. Here, we describe a modified PSI configuration in which a standard media bottle fitted with a silicone septum replaces a traditional multi-neck Schlenk flask. This design accommodates plate-based catalysts that cannot be easily used in conventional PSI reactors, specifically TiO2 nanotube arrays, enables controlled pressurization via needle-based gas injection, and permits insertion of capillary tubing for continuous sample infusion to the mass spectrometer. Rhodamine B is used as a model compound to monitor photocatalytic (PC) and photoelectrocatalytic (PEC) degradation under different reaction conditions. The approach enables real-time mass spectrometric monitoring of PEC and PC systems employing plate-based catalysts.

papers.title: The Effects of Substituent Position and Stereochemistry on Sulfide/Sulfoxide-Containing Monomers on Metathesis
papers.abstract: While the Ru-based Grubbs metathesis catalysts have shown incredible tolerance for a range of functionalities, sulfur-containing functional groups have been one notable exception, with a range of reactivities observed depending on sulfur oxidation and placement relative to the olefin. While sulfone-substituted norbornenes were shown to engage in living ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP), the reactivity of sulfoxides depended heavily upon norbornene stereochemistry. We sought to synthesize a range of 3-, 4-, and 5-sulfide- and sulfoxide-substituted cyclooctenes in order to investigate the effect of position and stereochemistry on ROMP. Although all three sulfide monomers were polymerizable, yielding polymer with moderate dispersities, their reaction rates varied widely, with the 5-substituted cyclooctene polymerizing the fastest and the 3-substituted cyclooctene polymerizing the slowest. Following oxidation of the sulfides to sulfoxides, the stereochemistry at the sulfur was found to heavily impact the reactivity of the 3-substituted monomers. While the threo 3-sulfoxide polymerized very slowly, with less than 50% catalyst initiation after 48 h, the erythro 3-sulfoxide polymerized readily with dispersities <1.1, being the only known example to our knowledge of a cis-cyclooctene that has been polymerized in a living manner. Density functional theory was employed to study the mechanism of ROMP to assist in explaining the effects on these small molecular modifications on the varied rates of polymerization.

papers.title: Fast parameter identification for elementary-step surface mechanisms using kinetically parameterized neural networks
papers.abstract: Microkinetic models provide physically grounded descriptions of catalytic systems. However, quantitative prediction of catalyst performance requires refinement of elementary-step parameters against reactor-level measurement data. This calibration is computationally demanding because it involves repeated reactor simulations with computationally expensive microkinetic models. Surrogates that approximate the kinetic model reduce evaluation cost, but are currently tied to fixed kinetic parameters and therefore cannot be used for mechanism calibration. To address this limitation, we introduce kinetically parameterized Global Reaction Neural Network (pGRNN) surrogates that map both operating conditions and elementary-step kinetic parameters of a detailed microkinetic mechanism to species source terms. By embedding stoichiometry, thermodynamic consistency, and elementary-step structure, the surrogate replaces expensive kinetics evaluations while retaining a mechanism-consistent representation. Using the preferential CO oxidation on platinum, we show that the pGRNN predicts source terms across a broad range of operating conditions and kinetic parameters with a relative error of 1.2 %. Reactor model evaluation is accelerated by a factor of 3100. The pGRNN is used in place of the kinetic model during mechanism calibration, reducing calibration time by factors of approximately 2400 for a synthetic single light-off curve and a synthetic multi-experiment campaign. Finally, we demonstrate the workflow by efficiently calibrating the mechanism against measured reactor-performance data from two experimental setups. A differentiable implementation of kinetic and reactor model further enables efficient gradient-based calibration. The proposed workflow provides an accelerated route for adapting detailed microkinetic models to catalyst-specific performance data.

papers.title: Interfacial Charge Redistribution Controls Reducibility and Oxygenate Selectivity in Silica-Supported Mo MXenes
papers.abstract: The selective hydrogenation of CO to oxygenates over unpromoted Mo carbide-based catalysts under Fischer-Tropsch (FT) conditions remains challenging due to the dominance of competing hydrocarbon-forming pathways. Here, we show that SiO2-supported two-dimensional (2D) MXenes Mo2CTx and Mo4/3CTx (Tx = O, OH, F) yield oxygenates under FT conditions, i.e., methanol and dimethyl ether (DME), with ca. 15%–25% selectivity. In contrast, unsupported Mo2CTx and Mo4/3CTx yield mostly kerosene-range alkanes (C5+) and methane, respectively, with only small or no quantities of methanol or DME under comparable conditions. This selectivity difference correlates with distinct reducibility profiles: e.g., while Mo2CTx can be fully reductively defunctionalized via H2 treatment, a similar treatment of Mo2CTx/SiO2 retains a stable Tx coverage of approximately 0.3 monolayer. Density functional theory calculations reveal that on the unsupported Mo2COx model, the progressive removal of O* leads to in-plane lattice expansion, lowering the Mo d-band center and weakening Mo–O* bonds, thereby facilitating the complete defunctionalization by H2. In contrast, a Mo2COx/SiO2 model with a partially defunctionalized MXene exhibits an interfacial MXene–support interaction that constrains lattice expansion and induces a redistribution of the electron density at the reactant-exposed surface. Together, these two effects stabilize residual O* groups on Mo2COx/SiO2, which, in turn, destabilize intermediates of the FT pathway and hinder the diffusion of CHx * species through repulsive O*-CHx * interactions, thereby suppressing C–C coupling and favoring pathways to methanol, DME, and methane. Overall, interfacial polarization, hindered defunctionalization, and surface diffusion are at the origin of the SiO2 support effect, controlling adsorption energies and reaction barriers in Mo-based MXenes, thereby providing guidelines for tuning the selectivity of Mo carbide-based MXene catalysts.

papers.title: Diastereo- and Enantioselective Photobiocatalytic α-Alkylation of α-Heteroaryl Amines Enabled by Unconventional Pyridoxal Photochemistry
papers.abstract: We report a photobiocatalytic system for the enantio- and diastereoselective α-alkylation of α-heteroaryl amines, a largely underexplored class of synthetically valuable non-native amine donors. Evaluation and directed evolution of thermophilic threonine aldolases, enabled by high-throughput photobiocatalysis, furnished pyridoxal 5’-phosphate (PLP)dependent enzymes capable of mediating radical C–C bond formation with high levels of stereocontrol. The resulting system enabled the synthesis of diverse chiral aliphatic amines bearing valuable nitrogen heterocycles, including pyridines, pyrimidines, pyrazines, thiazoles, imidazoles, benzothiazoles, and benzimidazoles. Notably, challenging stereochemical elements, such as α-tetrasubstituted stereogenic centers, contiguous trisubstituted stereocenters, and contiguous tri- and tetrasubstituted stereocenters, were readily accessible with our evolved radical C–C coupling enzyme, with excellent diastereo- and enantiocontrol. UV–visible spectroscopy revealed that directed evolution promoted the rapid formation and stabilization of a catalytically essential quinonoid intermediate from non-native amine donors, while mechanistic studies supported an unconventional PLP-enabled photochemical pathway for radical generation from Katritzky salts. Collectively, these results establish pyridoxal radical catalysis as a strategy for expanding chemical space beyond α-amino acids, highlighting its potential to access structurally complex chiral amines with excellent stereocontrol.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Polarity-Reversed Corey–Chaykovsky Cyclopropanation
papers.abstract: Cyclopropanes are ubiquitous structural motifs in biologically active molecules and functional materials, yet their synthesis remains largely either dependent on carbene-based approaches or limited to activated electron deficient π-systems. Herein, we report a photocatalytic polarity-reversed Corey–Chaykovsky cyclopropanation that exploits the single electron oxidative activation of sulfoxonium ylides to generate electrophilic carbon-centered radicals to access cyclopropanes from electron rich alkenes following a radical-polar crossover process. This strategy enables the efficient, mild and selective synthesis of functionalized cyclopropanes from non-activated alkenes, while avoiding the use of hazardous diazo reagents. Beyond expanding the synthetic utility of sulfoxonium ylides in cyclopropane synthesis, this work establishes photocatalytic oxidative activation of sulfur ylides as a powerful platform for polarity-reversed C-C bond construction.

papers.title: PEG Architecture as a Predictor of Anti-PEG Antibody Cross-Reactivity and Sequential Dosing Risk Across PEGylated Nanomedicines
papers.abstract: The conjugation of polyethylene glycol (PEG) to nanomedicines has transformed drug delivery, yet PEG's immunogenicity now threatens the safe and effective use of these platforms. Pre-existing and induced anti-PEG antibodies can accelerate clearance, reduce efficacy, and provoke hypersensitivity reactions on repeated dosing. While there are established frameworks to understand PEG immunogenicity and a comprehensive catalog of mitigation strategies, to date, there is no shared framework that correlates quantitative measurements of cross-reactivity outcomes across different classes of nanomedicine with specific architectural variables. This review analyses published data on anti-PEG antibody binding across PEGylated liposomes, lipid nanoparticles, and polymer-protein conjugates, relating those data to PEG chain length, surface density, polymer architecture, terminal chemistry, and immobilisation state. The analysis shows that PEG immunogenicity is not a single, uniform phenomenon but a class-dependent outcome shaped by the interaction between architectural variables and the immunological context of the carrier. From this comparison, we derive and mathematically formalise a Cross-Reactivity Score that combines weighted architectural variables with class-specific multipliers. We then apply the score to 12 approved or clinically advanced PEGylated nanomedicines, achieving concordance with observed immunogenicity in 82 percent of cases and correctly distinguishing the clinically critical divergence between Doxil and Onivyde, as well as the divergence between Pegasys and PegIntron. We convert the score into a class-stratified sequential dosing schema that provides clinical guidance on patient screening, dosing interval selection and PEG versus alternativepolymer dosing approach. The score is quantitative, cross-class, and benchmarked against marketed products, and can be used to make rational formulation design decisions, to aid clinical decisions, and to standardise risk assessment in the growing number of PEGylated nanomedicines.

papers.title: DATML: A Digital Analytical Twin Markup Language for Specimen-Centred Multimodal Surface Imaging and Analysis
papers.abstract: Multimodal analytical workflows increasingly combine microscopy, spectroscopy, chemical imaging, surface analysis and automated experimental planning. However, the information produced by such workflows is still commonly organised around instrument-specific files: one file for an image, another for a spectrum, another for a map, and often a further proprietary project file for the software package that produced or processed the data. These files may contain rich analytical signals, but they often fail to provide a durable, specimen-centred account of where those signals were obtained, how they relate to one another spatially, and how the accumulated record should be reused by later human or autonomous experiments. This paper proposes DATML, the Digital Analytical Twin Markup Language, as an open, XML-based format for representing specimen-centred spatial analytical records. The initial DATML Core 0.1 specification describes one or more Digital Analytical Twins (DATs), each containing metadata, a specimen-centred Cartesian coordinate system, modality-specific layers, spatial points or regions, material descriptions, references to external data files and provenance information. XML namespace extension points allow later or domain-specific vocabularies to add registration transforms, uncertainty and predictive state models without changing the meaning of the core. DATML is intended to complement, not replace, existing analytical formats such as ISO 14976/VAMAS, OME-TIFF, HDF5/NeXus and proprietary instrument files. Its function is to supply the missing spatial context layer: where on the specimen an analytical signal belongs, how that location relates to other measurements, and what specimen-centred record remains after the instrument session has ended. The paper develops the rationale for DATML by analogy with the earlier development of spectral interchange formats in surface chemical analysis. Just as VAMAS-style formats allowed spectra and related analytical signals to move beyond individual instrument vendors’ software ecosystems, specimen-centred spatial context will increasingly need to move beyond stage coordinates, proprietary project files and single-vendor correlative microscopy environments. This need is likely to become more urgent as shared facilities, regulated laboratories, materials databases and self-driving analytical laboratories require machine-readable, auditable and interoperable representations of physical specimens. We describe the DATML design principles, the normative scope of Core 0.1, validated XML examples, relationships to existing standards, a public reference repository and a roadmap toward Predictive Digital Analytical Twins (PDATs), in which spatial analytical records also carry probabilistic state estimates and predicted observations.

papers.title: Spin-Polarization-Driven Modulation of Oxygen Reduction Pathway Selectivity in Chiral Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) enables spin-polarized charge transport in molecular and framework systems, introducing electron spin as a potential control parameter in catalysis (Naaman Waldeck, 2015; Naaman et al., 2019). Here, I pro- pose a mechanistically grounded framework for in- vestigating whether spin polarization can direct oxy- gen reduction reaction (ORR) pathway selectivity in chiral covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Enan- tiopure R- and S-COFs, alongside racemic analogues with identical topology and porosity, are identified as model systems to isolate chirality—and thus spin polarization—as the primary independent variable. I hypothesize that CISS-induced spin polarization bi- ases the stabilization of oxygen reduction intermedi- ates, particularly the *OOH species, thereby favor- ing the two-electron pathway toward hydrogen per- oxide (HO) formation over the four-electron reduc- tion to water. A systematic experimental strategy is outlined combining magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy for spin characterization with rotat- ing ring–disk electrode measurements for quantita- tive evaluation of ORR selectivity. If spin polarization influences ORR branching, enantiopure frameworks would be expected to exhibit lower apparaent elec- tron transfer numbers, hence, demonstrating higher hydrogen peroxide yields relative to racemic con- trol. Demonstrating a monotonic relationship be- tween spin polarization magnitude and hydrogen peroxide selectivity would provide evidence support- ing a spin-dependent contribution to ORR pathway selectivity.

papers.title: Accurate Thermodynamics of Phenol Aggregates across Concentration and Temperature
papers.abstract: Phenol aggregate populations in carbon tetrachloride are governed by an enthalpyentropy balance that varies with concentration and temperature. This redistribution is reflected in the infrared O H stretching band, whose position and shape provide a sensitive test for population models. Here, monomer-to-tetramer populations are determined over a concentration–temperature grid using two strategies that share the same graphbased aggregate classification: a cluster-based approach relying on partition functions from conformational-search structures, and a trajectory-derived approach extracting populations from molecular dynamics simulations. The latter reproduces the experimental attenuation and displacement of the aggregate-associated bands, especially in concentrated solutions, whereas the cluster-based model predicts an overly sharp thermal depletion of larger aggregates. Temperature-dependent data further enable van’t Hoff estimates of aggregation enthalpies and entropies. Comparison with experiment shows that the trajectory-derived strategy captures aggregation thermodynamics across the aggregate series by better sampling configurational space.

papers.title: Ball-Milling-Enabled Pd-Catalyzed One-Pot Cross-Coupling of Aryl Sulfonium Salts with In Situ Generated Reformatsky Enolates
papers.abstract: Mechanochemistry enables an efficient Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling of aryl thianthrenium salts with in situ generated Reformatsky-type enolates. Ball milling plays a dual role by promoting both the activation of zinc for the formation of Reformatsky-type organozinc enolates from α-halo esters and amides and their subsequent cross-coupling with solid aryl thianthrenium salts. This one-pot protocol provides access to a broad range of α-arylated products in high yields within short reaction times. The mechanochemical process is performed under ambient conditions without the need for an inert atmosphere, highlighting its operational simplicity and practicality. Furthermore, the methodology is readily applicable to the late-stage functionalization of structurally complex bioactive molecules.

papers.title: Solvent-Controlled Formation of Arrested Polyelectrolyte–Surfactant Interfacial Assemblies and Their Impact on Emulsion Stability
papers.abstract: Arrested interfaces formed through confined polyelectrolyte–surfactant association offer a promising route for designing emulsion systems with tailored properties. However, the impact of organic solvents on the formation, organization, and functionality of polyelectrolyte-surfactant assemblies at oil/water interfaces remains unexplored. In this study, we examine the structure and functionality of arrested interfacial assemblies of the oil-soluble surfactant hexadecylamine and the water-soluble polyelectrolyte sodium polystyrene sulfonate. To elucidate the role of the organic phase, undecanol/water and toluene/water systems were systematically compared. Structural evolution and organization of the interfacial assemblies were examined using interfacial tension measurements, infrared spectroscopy, small- and wideangle X-ray scattering (SAXS/WAXS), freeze-fracture transmission electron microscopy, and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Undecanol molecules act as a cosurfactant at the undecanol/water interface, promoting the formation of multilamellar polyanion/mixed surfactant films with long-range order. Timeresolved SAXS reveals the gradual development of ordered structures, and temperature-dependent SAXS, WAXS, and DSC demonstrate a thermotropic transition from a gel-like lamellar phase to a fluid lamellar phase. In contrast, the toluene/water interface produces disordered polyelectrolyte-surfactant assemblies with finite curvature that lack lamellar ordering and detectable thermotropic transitions. These structural differences directly govern emulsion behavior. Multilamellar films formed at the undecanol/water interface stabilize oil-in-water emulsions and enable nonspherical droplet morphologies to persist. Conversely, assemblies formed at the toluene/water interface induce composition-dependent phase inversion and stabilize spherical droplets. These findings demonstrate that organic solvents play a decisive role in determining the structure of arrested interfaces and their macroscopic functionality, offering new insights into the design of structured liquid systems.

papers.title: Fluorescence-based post-mortem interval estimation using cell lysate from DNA/RNA co-extraction of human soft tissue
papers.abstract: Post-mortem interval (PMI) estimation is an important element in medico-legal death investigations, as reliable estimates can establish timelines and generate investigative leads. Various analytical techniques are used to monitor biomolecular degradation throughout decomposition, with promising results obtained from fluorescence spectroscopy. In this work, we analyzed the fluorescent profile of cell lysates from 96 biopsy punches collected from 14 human cadavers at a human taphonomic facility in Québec, Canada, with PMIs ranging from 2 to 1098 days. Excitation-emission matrices (EEMs) were acquired for each lysate and deconvoluted using parallel factor analysis for fluorophore identification. We analyzed both composite and tissue-specific (muscle, adipose, and skin) samples. Overall, tryptophan fluorescence decreased with increasing PMI, whereas fluorescence between 400-500 nm, attributed to fluorescent oxidation products, increased. Fluorescence in skin and muscle was dominated by tryptophan at early PMIs, whereas adipose exhibited minimal signal. As PMI increased, EEM fluorescence became progressively more homogeneous across tissue types, indicating that tissue-specific contributions decrease as decomposition advances. Six machine learning models were built from the composite samples to predict PMI, and XGBoost performed best, with an R 2 of 0.88 and RMSE of 127.2 days, corresponding to an error of 11.6% relative to the maximum PMI. Our findings demonstrate that fluorescence analysis of cell lysates is practical and yields accurate PMI estimates, provides important insight into decomposition-related biomolecular degradation, and can also be readily integrated into DNA/RNA co-extractions.

papers.title: Phase equilibrium engineering in biorefinery reactive systems: chemical equilibrium prediction in acetylation of n‐alkanols
papers.abstract: In this work we perform simultaneous phase and chemical equilibrium calculation using the Group Contribution with Association equation of state (GCA-EOS), aiming to assess reactive systems in the framework of biorefinery development. The lack of equilibrium data in reactive systems is quite common; therefore, group contribution methods allow knowing the phase behavior of the system as the reaction proceeds. The GCA-EOS is applied to the prediction of n-alkanol esterification with acetic acid, from ethanol to 1-hexanol. Most of the model interaction parameters have been taken from the literature, while in this work we also correlate a few missing interactions from non-reactive phase equilibria data only. In order to solve the simultaneous chemical and phase equilibria we apply a non-stoicheiometric approach, together with the stability test criteria. We perform all the calculations of the chemical equilibria in a predictive manner, using literature values of the formations properties of all the compounds. We show that the GCA-EOS is a reliable model to predict the chemical and phase equilibria in acetylation reactions.

papers.title: Methyl substitution driven preferential hydrogen bonding over chalcogen bonding by heavy chalcogens
papers.abstract: Spectroscopic investigation of tellurium-centered hydrogen bonds is relatively scarce. Here, 1:1 complex of dimethyl ditelluride (Me2Te2) and H2S was investigated using matrix isolation infrared spectroscopy and quantum chemical calculations. Only S-H···Te hydrogen-bond (HB) were identified in argon matrix, evident from pronounced 𝜈spectral shifts. Quantum chemical calculations predicted the S-H···Te HB to be significantly stronger than S···Te chalcogen-bond (ChB), in spite of very low electronegativity of Te (2.10, Pauling scale). In fact, S-H···Te HB in Me2Te2-H2S was found to be as strong as O-H···O HB in water dimer. When compared against H2Te-H2S, the smallest binary complex capable of forming an intermolecular S-H···Te HB and S···Te ChB, the absolute as well as relative strengths of the two noncovalent interactions were found to be systematically increased by two factors (i) methyl substitution in the acceptor moiety and (ii) incorporation of a dichalcogenide bridge. The same two modifications were found to have similar effects for S and Se, too. Increasing methyl substitution was found to increase the proton affinity of the acceptor moiety resulting in shorter HB and larger 𝜈spectral shifts, indicating stronger HB.

papers.title: Engineering Cooperative Multi-Domain DNA Probes for Programmable Nucleic Acid Detection
papers.abstract: Nucleic acids are powerful recognition elements because base pairing enables straightforward probe design, yet selective target recognition under physiological conditions remains challenging when specificity cannot rely on melting-based discrimination. Here we introduce a programmable multi-domain DNA probe that converts target binding into a cooperative self-assembly process. The recognition sequence is split into two short domains carried on separate strands, each coupled to a programmable stem domain through a flexible linker. Target hybridization increases the effective local concentration of the stems and drives their cooperative assembly into a stable three-way junction. This architecture enables independent control over probe performance: stem length tunes thermodynamic stability and apparent affinity, linker length regulates signal transduction without significantly affecting recognition, and cooperative assembly introduces an activation threshold that sharpens discrimination against mismatched and truncated targets. We demonstrate high sequence specificity with model DNA targets, extend the approach to disease-relevant miRNAs, and show that distinct probes operate orthogonally in a multiplexed format. Finally, we translate the same mechanism to a signal-ON electrochemical platform that supports point-of-care formats and operates directly in whole blood. Multi-domain probe design thus provides a modular, amplification-free strategy for programmable, high-specificity nucleic acid detection.

papers.title: Fatty Acid Composition in Ocean-Derived Triglyceride Oils and its Influence on Rheology and Chemical Conversion
papers.abstract: Valorization of aquaculture waste into biofuels and biomaterials is crucial to advancing a low-carbon bioeconomy. However, the inherent variability in the fatty acid composition introduces uncertainties in conversion efficiencies during transesterification and poses challenges in chemical processing. Through integration of gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), rheology, transesterification studies, and kinetic parameters associated with the activated flow state (and Eyring analysis), this work investigates the variability in fatty acid composition of ocean biomass-derived oils (fish and microalgae) and its influence on the viscosity of the oil. The findings reveal that salmon ( Salmo salar ) oil is high in monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFA), 53.26 ± 7.08%, which correlates to a high viscosity of 39.61 ± 0.01 cP hindering its conversion to fatty acid methyl esters (FAMEs). However, ω-3 fish oil ( Engraulis encrasicolus and Sardina pilchardus ) is high in polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) 38.59 ± 2.80%, increasing its conversion to FAME. These 2 findings demonstrate that transport phenomena governed by molecular composition can outweigh intrinsic energetic barriers in determining reaction performance. By directly linking fatty acid composition to rheology and chemical conversion, this work establishes viscosity as a predictive descriptor of feedstock processability, which could lead to increased energy efficiency and rational selection of ocean biomass-derived oils for sustainable chemical manufacturing.

papers.title: Cross-species principles of silk protein assembly from metastable feedstocks to hierarchical materials
papers.abstract: Silk is one of nature’s most versatile structural biomaterials, produced independently by a vast diversity of species across insects, spiders, marine invertebrates, crustaceans, and even select vertebrates. Despite their evolutionary distance and ecological differences, these organisms share a common overarching strategy for silk biomaterial production: the synthesis of a protein-rich feedstock, its stabilization and storage in a highly concentrated yet metastable form, and its controlled conversion into a solid fiber or adhesive during spinning. These steps are essential for living systems to achieve remarkable tunability in silk material properties through the integration of molecular design, biochemical environment, and glandular architecture. While the Bombyx mori silkworm silk and major ampullate spider silk have served as classical models, expanding the comparative lens reveals a much wider range of solutions to the challenges of protein solubility, controlled assembly, and functional adaptation. Caddisflies larvae spin β-sheet-rich fibers underwater; bees produce coiled-coil protein silks for cocoon formation; marine mussels and polychaetes secrete silk-like underwater adhesives; and crustaceans such as amphipods and tanaids have independently evolved silks with distinct repetitive motifs and assembly mechanisms. Together, these taxa exemplify the breadth of molecular architectures, accessory proteins, ionic environments, and extrusion pathways that collectively modulate silk material performance. This review summarizes the cross-species insights to highlight general multifaceted framework of mechanisms governing protein assembly during silk spinning, from sequence-encoded disorder-order transitions and liquid-phase stabilization to fibrillation and hierarchical structural organization. By uncovering shared principles and organism-specific innovations, natural silk spinning provides a powerful model for guiding the design of next-generation biomimetic materials with programmable architectures and sustainable processing strategies.

papers.title: Symmetry Numbers: A Flexible Approach for Molecules and Transition States
papers.abstract: Symmetry numbers are essential corrections in thermochemistry and chemical kinetics, but their reliable assignment remains difficult in automated workflows, especially for stereochemical, fluxional, cyclic, and transition-state structures. We present a stereochemistry-aware automorphism (SAA) approach for computing symmetry numbers using the StereoMolGraph (SMG) framework. In this representation, local stereodescriptors encode rigid local geometries directly in the molecular graph, so the symmetry number is obtained as the order of the automorphism group that preserves both connectivity and encoded stereochemistry. This avoids the need for a post hoc “label stereocenter” correction and provides a direct graph-theoretical analogue of permutation-based symmetry number definitions. Model dependence is handled explicitly by choosing which molecular features are treated as fixed or fluxional, enabling consistent treatment of rigidity, free rotation, umbrella inversion, and pseudorotation assumptions. Beyond overall molecular and transition-state symmetry numbers, the same framework yields external and internal symmetry numbers for hindered-rotor treatments, including an effective external symmetry number for cases where the overall symmetry number is non-separable. Benchmark calculations reproduce the expected symmetry numbers for all supported benchmark molecules and resolve cases where existing rule-based or corrected-connectivity approaches fail, including stereochemically distinct structures with identical connectivity. The SAA approach is highly robust, making it suitable for automated thermochemical and kinetic modeling of molecules and reactions.

papers.title: Photoredox/Cobalt Dual Catalysis Enables C(sp3)C(sp2)/C(sp) Bond Construction via a Biomimetic Approach
papers.abstract: We developed a photoredox–cobalt synergistic biomimetic reaction, constructing an unsaturated molecular library. Remarkably, we demonstrate the synthesis of a series of polysubstituted cinnamaldehydes. Furthermore, reported an unprecedented property of α‑fluoroalkyl compounds, defluorination was absent in the presence of a cobaloxime catalyst or vitamin B12, but pronounced without cobalt catalyst.
