papers.title: Structural flexibility of styrylpyrene chromophore in reproducing solvent-induced spectral shifts
papers.abstract: Solvatochromic shifts in UV-vis absorption of photoreactive chromophores and microenvironment effects in their light-induced [2+2] cycloaddition reactions are presently not fully understood. Spectral shifts observed experimentally could not be yet resolved in silico. The understanding of the reactivity of chromophores is not possible without the foundational reasoning of their solvatochromism. Here, using quantum mechanical (QM) calculations coupled to a multiscale computational scheme with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we demonstrate the role of structural flexibility of the styrylpyrene chromophore, its solvent-induced conformational, electrostatic and vibronic effects in adequate capturing of absorption spectral shifts. The methodological insights suggest computational schemes relevant to the design of advanced photoprogrammed systems and the capture of their photoreactivity.

papers.title: Application of photocatalytic degradation of Rhodamine B (A Review) (2021-2025)
papers.abstract: One particularly harmful dye known as Rhodamine B, or RhB, is widely utilized, yet it can linger in aquatic environments for extended periods and poses risks. Traditional methods for purifying water, such as employing chemicals or allowing tiny organisms to consume the material, are not always effective and sometimes lead to additional issues. This article discusses a solar-powered refining technique, the materials participating, and the factors that enhance its effectiveness, including the significance of light and color in water. Furthermore, it presents innovative approaches, such as employing magnets to acquire the cleaning materials or utilizing artificial information to optimize the process. Various industries and brands incorporate different dyes to produce items such as clothing, cosmetics, and food packaging. At times, these dyes wash away with polluted water, which further contaminates rivers and lakes, complicating access to clean water for both wildlife and humans. While this technology offers numerous benefits, there are lasting challenges to address, particularly with regard to treating very large volumes of water. Researchers aim to discover new eco-friendly materials and smarter methods to enhance water purification practices in the future. This knowledge aids scientists, environmentalists, and policymakers in developing improved strategies for maintaining clean and safe water resources. Scientists are currently investigating a novel method called “photocatalysis,” which utilise sunlight and specific materials to decompose the dye into harmless substances such as water and carbon dioxide. This method is advantageous as it is more environmentally friendly, affordable, and beneficial for the ecosystem. Keywords Rhodamine B, photocatalysis, wastewater treatment, TiO2, color removal

papers.title: A Geometric Pre-Screening and Target-Range Ranking Dataset of 12,597 Lattice-Verified Metal–Organic Frameworks for Prioritized Adsorption Simulation Screening
papers.abstract: High-throughput computational screening of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for gas storage and separation applications routinely begins from structural repositories containing tens of thousands of candidates, only a small fraction of which are geometrically suitable for further simulation. We report a geometry-based pre-screening dataset of 12,597 lattice-verified MOF structures, filtered from an initial pool of approximately 71,500 candidates drawn from four public repositories (pore-limiting diameter ≥ 3.3 Å, crystal density ≥ 0.1 g cm-3, and related structural criteria). Rather than ranking structures by simple maximization of pore size or minimization of density– an approach that disproportionately favors extreme, often mechanically unstable frameworks – each structure is scored against a trapezoidal target-range function that rewards geometric properties falling within ranges considered reasonable for stable, practically usable MOFs. The dataset, its scoring methodology, and an independent reproducibility check (a standalone script that recomputes all scores from raw geometric columns and matches the published values to floating-point precision) are made available to support downstream grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) adsorption screening campaigns. Two methodological limitations identified during quality control – a large tied-score plateau affecting 42.6% of structures, and duplicate entries arising from alternate relaxation protocols – are documented and addressed with a deduplicated shortlist.

papers.title: Sensitive Derivatization-Free HPLC-MS Method For Quantification of Cyclohexylamine as a Process-Related Impurity in Rosuvastatin calcium salt
papers.abstract: Cyclohexylamine is an alicyclic amine that may be introduced as a process-related impurity during the manufacture of rosuvastatin calcium. Due to its potential toxicological relevance, sensitive and selective analytical methods are required to monitor cyclohexylamine at trace levels in pharmaceutical active ingredients. In this study, a derivatization-free reverse-phase highperformance liquid chromatography method coupled with single quadrupole mass spectrometric detection (HPLC–MS) was developed and validated for the quantification of cyclohexylamine in rosuvastatin calcium. Chromatographic separation was achieved using a pentafluorophenyl (PFP) column with an acidic mobile phase composed of formic acid, water, and acetonitrile, providing adequate retention and selective detection of cyclohexylamine. Quantification was performed in positive electrospray ionization mode using single-ion monitoring. The method demonstrated good linearity over the concentration range of 0.01–0.15 µg/mL with a correlation coefficient of 0.999. The limit of quantification was established at 0.01 µg/mL, and the method performance characteristics, including accuracy, precision, and robustness, were evaluated and found to comply with the requirements of ICH Q2(R1)1. The proposed method is suitable for routine quality control analysis of cyclohexylamine as a process-related impurity in rosuvastatin calcium.

papers.title: Online Liquid-Phase Adsorption (online LPA) equipment. A step forward on liquid phase adsorption characterisation techniques for porous materials
papers.abstract: Liquid-phase adsorption (LPA) measurements are less frequently applied for the characterisation of porous materials than gas adsorption, although, for a variety of applications, such as (water) purification or heterogeneous catalysis, the liquid phase characteristics are critical. This is due to the lack of standardized commercially available instrumentation enabling rapid LPA experiments. In general, LPA experiments are done manually following tedious and time-consuming on-bench procedures. In this work, we describe new equipment for performing automatised LPA measurements. The equipment consists of four independent modules interconnected by multi-port valves enabling measurements of adsorption isotherms under controlled temperature, release measurements, and adsorption/desorption kinetics studies. We describe the components and the equipment operation to perform the different measurements. As proof of concept, the adsorption capacity in the liquid phase for bisphenol A, naphthalene, and toluene was evaluated for three different materials, including the metal-organic framework (MOF) HKUST-1, the carbon NoritRox0.8, and the MOF-based commercially available composite BasoliteA100 (MIL-53). The developed method shows good linearity (R2 > 0.9995) in a working range from 20 to 340 mg L-1, limits of detection up to 0.32 mg L-1, and relative standard deviations lower than 5.6%. Besides, the collected experimental data could be successfully fitted by established models.

papers.title: Native Mass Spectrometry Based Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) Informs Structural Improvement of Artificial Photocyclase Enzymes
papers.abstract: Directed evolution is a powerful strategy for enzyme engineering, and has successfully enabled unique stereoselective biosynthesis of high-value organic molecules. Enantiomeric excess (ee) remains the gold standard to assess the enzyme performance, but only reflects the final reaction outcome and provides limited mechanistic insights, leaving design efforts effectively a "black box", especially for multimeric proteins and heterogenous systems. Here, we introduce a Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) that links protein point mutations and catalytic enantioselectivity via structural features measured by native mass spectrometry (native MS). Using eleven artificial photocyclase mutants, we demonstrate that single point mutations can have profound impact on protein structure, resulting in highly convoluted effect on protein function not easily explainable by a single variable. We derived a multivariate linear regression model from the proteoform-explicit native MS data based on the enzyme’s oligomeric state, photosensitizer labelling efficiency, susceptibility to oxidation, and photodegradation half-life. PrEMS showed significantly higher correlation (adjusted R2 increase from 0.051 to 0.881) to enzyme’s enantioselectivity than the conventional physiochemical descriptors of the mutated amino acids. PrEMS serves as a quantitative framework to fill the knowledge gap in structural descriptors between sequence mutation and enzyme’s function, rationalizing enzyme improvement strategies. For example, our analysis indicated that photodamage can be suppressed by incorporating aromatic residues near the active site. Our study outlines a tangible path with quantifiable metrics for integrating native MS data into enzyme design workflows.

papers.title: Quantum defect density controls carbon nanotube sensor sensitivity via photophysical cooperativity
papers.abstract: Single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) fluoresce in the near-infrared (NIR), which overlaps with the biological transparency window. Therefore, SWCNTs are used as versatile materials for (bio)photonics. Controlled covalent functionalization of SWCNTs with quantum defects (QDs) creates color center carbon nanotubes (CCNTs) with red-shifted additional emission features and increased overall emission. QDs are a new chemical dimension for sensing but is unclear how the number of QDs affect sensor properties such as sensitivity or dynamic range. Here, we develop a NIR fluorescent ratiometric pH sensor based on benzoic acid QDs. We vary the amount of QDs in (6,5)-chirality enriched CCNTs and demonstrate that the amount of pH-sensitive QDs does not affect the dynamic range of the nanosensor (pH = 6.0-8.5), but influences the sensitivity (ratiometric response E 11 */E 11 ) by more than 100 %. We attribute this impact of defect density on sensing to photophysical positive cooperativity between QDs, while the dissociation constant of the (pKa-value) of the quantum defect determines the dynamic range of the sensor. These pH sensitive CCNTs can be incorporated into agarhydrogels for ratiometric (1130 nm / 990 nm) pH imaging. Overall, we show that the number of QDs is an efficient tool to tune properties of fluorescent sensors.

papers.title: Nile Red–phosphate binding macrocycle conjugate for phosphatidylserine sensing
papers.abstract: Detection of phosphatidylserine (PS) in biomembranes is important because externalized PS serves as a functional signal for key biological processes. Towards developing new probes for PS, the phosphate-binding macrocycle was conjugated with polarity-sensitive Nile Red and used to probe the molecular recognition of phospholipids. The new probe demonstrated high selectivity in binding and detection of phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylserine in experiments with large unilamellar vesicles. Live-cell imaging experiments demonstrated high sensitivity in detecting necrotic cells.

papers.title: Selenenic vs. Sulfenic Acids: Enthalpies of Formation, Bond Dissociation Energies, and Thermochemical Properties from Composite Methods
papers.abstract: Selenenic acids (RSeOH) are reactive intermediates of atmospheric, biological, and environmental importance, but their thermochemistry has been experimentally inaccessible and computationally under-characterized. We report the first systematic thermochemistry of five selenenic acids (HSeOH, CH3SeOH, C2H3SeOH, C2HSeOH, C6H5SeOH) using three independent composite methods, G4, mChS (a modified jun-ChS scheme, applied here for the first time to selenium), and DLPNO-CCSD(T)/CBS, by way of isodesmic S/Se exchange reactions anchored to the sulfenic acid values of Ventura et al. (J. Phys. Chem. A 2022, 126, 6091); atomization energies were employed for the purpose of diagnostic comparisons rather than as a primary method. Recommended enthalpies of formation (kcal mol-1, 298.15 K) are HSeOH = −20.6 ± 0.8, CH3SeOH = −28.7 ± 0.8, C2H3SeOH = −3.1 ± 1.0, C2HSeOH = +40.1 ± 0.9, and C6H5SeOH = +4.4 ± 1.1. Across all five substituents the Se/S shift is nearly constant at +(7–8) kcal mol-1, giving a simple scaling rule (selenenic acids are ~7.2 kcal mol-1 less stable than their sulfenic analogs). Eleven X–H and X–OH bond dissociation energies are reported using the three methods (the sample standard deviations across the available methods average 1.7 kcal mol-1 and range from 0.1 to 2.4 kcal mol-1), including CH3SeO–H = 80.9 ± 1.1 and both phenyl bonds at the three-method consensus (C6H5Se–OH = 67.4 ± 1.4, C6H5SeO–H = 80.2 ± 2.2). The pipeline is supported by external bond dissociation energy (BDE) checks: CH3S–H within experimental uncertainty and HSO–H within ~2 kcal mol-1 of the high-level sulfenic benchmark (with CH3SO–H as a qualitative third comparison), while CASSCF/NEVPT2 analyses confirm single-reference character for the CH3SeO• radical but reveal pronounced multireference character for the parent HSeO• radical, whose O–H BDE is therefore reported from SC-NEVPT2 corroborating G4 (84.6 ± 1.1 kcal mol-1). These results provide the first systematic isodesmic thermochemical dataset for the selenenic acid family and the first composite-method BDE table beyond the sulfenic benchmark.

papers.title: Cyclization-Mediated Nonradiative Decay in Carbo[n]helicenes (n = 5–12): Reaction Path Analysis of Molecular Size Effects
papers.abstract: Carbo[ n ]helicenes are helically fused polycyclic hydrocarbons that exhibit low fluorescence quantum yields and predominantly undergo triplet-mediated relaxation. However, their nonradiative decay paths remain unclear. To elucidate the relaxation process, we systematically explored and optimized the T 1 /S 0 seams of crossing (T 1 /S 0-SX ) and the S 1 /S 0 conical intersections (S 1 /S 0-CI ). The barriers leading to them were then compared to identify the plausible decay paths on a structural basis. For [5]- and [6]helicenes, we considered two decay paths: the intersystem crossing (ISC) path back to S 0 through the triplet manifold via T 1 /S 0-SX , and the internal conversion (IC) path via S 1 /S 0-CI . Although cyclization provides the most favorable crossings for both ISC and IC paths, the favored ring size depends on the helicene length. That is, the 6-membered-ring type is the most favorable in [5]- and [7]–[12]helicenes, whereas the 7-membered-ring type is favored for [6]helicene. We also identified outer-type crossings whose barrier decreases with helicene length, making them kinetically competitive in longer helicenes.

papers.title: AI-driven design of a cost-effective synthetic route to malaria drug Ganaplacide
papers.abstract: Malaria is a deadly infectious disease that disproportionately affects third-world countries. Ganaplacide is a drug candidate that is highly effective against malaria, but no affordable way to produce it exists yet. Here we show how we used a combination of AI-driven design and expert chemistry knowledge to develop a novel synthetic route to ganaplacide. The AI retrosynthesis algorithm suggested a non-evident two-steps synthesis of the imidazolopiperazine core of the molecule from benzyl-protected dimethylpiperazinone through a strategic thioimidate intermediate. We also present the Synthetic Confidence Score, which assesses the level of risk associated with a given retrosynthetic disconnection and allows balancing creativity and reliability. The synergy between AI creativity, metrics such as the Synthetic Confidence Score and expert chemist knowledge has the potential to unlock non-evident efficient routes for important molecules, when expert chemists alone have explored mainstream chemistry unsuccessfully.

papers.title: Active site density distribution controls the reaction efficiency of methanol conversion
papers.abstract: The transient evolution of fresh catalysts to working catalysts involves an induction period, transition region, and steady-state. There is, however, limited information on how to increase the reaction efficiency. Reaction-diffusion-dynamic coupling is revealed using a dynamic hybrid multiscale model that integrates active site dynamics into catalyst surface models, and fluid dynamics for transient kinetic studies of methanol conversion. Using the dynamic hybrid multiscale model, the influence of bed porosity on the dynamic site-interconversion mechanism over three active site-ensembles in improving the reaction efficiency is quantified. With only the methoxymethyl mechanism, dynamic site-interconversion mechanism, and the influence of bed porosity, the transient evolution of fresh catalysts to working catalysts can be accurately described without inclusion of the hydrocarbon pool mechanism. Six models that describe the change in the distribution of active site density explain the variation in desorption profiles with catalyst composition. Periodic step response cycles over working catalysts show non-linear dynamics, that is asymmetric cyclic orbits in stark contrast to the first step response cycle over fresh catalysts. The dynamic hybrid multiscale model predicts higher propylene formation at longer reaction times with active site density distribution as the molecular descriptor that controls the reaction efficiency of methanol-to-olefin conversion.

papers.title: Deciphering the Chiral Inducer in Micelle-Templated Growth of Chiral Gold Nanorods
papers.abstract: Micelle template-directed growth has emerged as a powerful strategy for the synthesis of chiral gold nanorods (AuNRs), enabling precise modulation of their chiroptical response across the UV-Vis-NIR spectral range. In this approach, hexadecyltrimethylammonium chloride (CTAC) and 1,1′-binaphthyl-2,2′-diamine (BINAMINE) assemble into chiral micelles that direct the chiral growth of AuNRs. Herein, a distinct color change observed upon incubation of Au(III) with BINAMINE and CTAC motivated a detailed analysis of the underlying chemical processes, providing insight into the still poorly understood mechanism of chiral NR formation. The results show that Au(III) induces BINAMINE oxidation, leading to the formation of oligomeric species that play a key role in chiral induction. Suppressing this oxidation leads to a pronounced reduction in the anisotropy (g) factor. Moreover, notable morphological differences are observed, with AuNRs displaying a higher density and inclination of surface wrinkles when oxidation occurs. These findings highlight the crucial role of BINAMINE oxidation in directing chiral growth and contribute to a deeper understanding of chirality emergence of these systems.

papers.title: A Modular Quantum Emulator for Multi-Step Fermionic Catalysis: Eliminating the Jordan-Wigner Bottleneck via Qudit Encoding
papers.abstract: (Dated: July 14, 2026) Simulating the dynamical trajectories of complex metalloenzymes, such as the nitrogenase FeMo-cofactor, remains classically intractable due to real-time entanglement growth and non-adiabatic surface crossings. Here, we introduce the Modular Quantum Emulator (MQE), a polynomialcomplexity quantum architecture designed for the chemically accurate emulation of multi-step fermionic catalysis. The MQE employs a universal four-dimensional qudit encoding that natively absorbs fermionic exchange signs. This entirely eliminates the Jordan-Wigner parity string bottleneck, reducing the entangling gate count from quartic to quadratic scaling. To track multi-step stoichiometry, the emulator utilizes a dual-manifold design: a logical register for electronic structure and a virtual register for coherent cofactor phase accumulation. We prove a structural isomorphism wherein this virtual register natively functions as the phase clock for Quantum Phase Estimation, enabling exact energy extraction with zero ancilla overhead. Finally, we establish strict polynomial resource bounds for complete catalytic trajectories and demonstrate that the architecture seamlessly accommodates eight systematic physical extensions—including open-system dissipation and relativistic kinematics—without altering its asymptotic complexity class. Validated across seventeen biochemical mechanisms, this framework fundamentally shifts the computational paradigm from static variational minimization to exact, polynomially-bounded dynamical emulation.

papers.title: Reaction-Depth Learning Enables Apparent Yield Extrapolation in Catalyst Informatics
papers.abstract: Extrapolative prediction of high-yield catalyst performance remains challenging because conventional direct-yield machine-learning models do not explicitly represent the target, side, and competing reactions that determine the final yield. Here, we propose a reaction-depth learning framework for interpretable extrapolative prediction of catalytic performance. Instead of directly predicting product yield, the model predicts latent reaction-depth variables associated with a predefined stoichiometric reaction network from catalyst and reaction condition inputs. Outlet flows are reconstructed through the stoichiometric matrix, expressing predictions as pathway-specific reaction progress. Applied to an oxidative coupling of methane dataset, this representation transformed apparent extrapolation in C2-yield space into interpolation or near-interpolation in reaction-depth space. The reaction-depth model achieved a Spearman rank correlation of 0.51 in the extrapolation region, whereas conventional direct-yield models showed near-zero correlations. Reaction networks inconsistent with the feed environment frequently produced negative reconstructed outlet flows, indicating that such violations can diagnose reaction-network validity.

papers.title: A Geometric Interpretation of Slater’s Shielding Constants: Radial Overlap as P (rinner < router)
papers.abstract: In 1930, J. C. Slater introduced a set of empirical shielding constants—0.35, 0.85, and 1.00—that remain widely used for estimating effective nuclear charge. Despite ninety-five years of use, a geometric interpretation of these specific values has remained absent. We identify a dominant geometric quantity that explains a major component of the three empirical shielding scales. For different-subshell pairs, the probability P (rinner < router) that one electron’s radial position lies inside another’s yields 0.359, 0.862, and 0.979 (vs. Slater’s 0.35, 0.85, 1.00)—deviations under 3%. For the same-subshell case, radial symmetry gives σ = 0.5000, which is reconciled with 0.35 through an angular-overlap decomposition. The core quantity is P (rinner < router), computed from hydrogenic wavefunctions. A complete periodic-table feature set (Z = 1–118) using these geometrically obtained constants achieves a median ionization energy error of 13.3% against NIST data (Kramida et al., 2024). A formation-energy benchmark on 92 compounds demonstrates that these geometrically derived features achieve statistically equivalent accuracy (MAE = 0.351 ± 0.069 eV/atom) to standard empirically-tabulated features (MAE = 0.322 ± 0.037 eV/atom). We note that the raw hydrogenic ionization energy formula has a mean error of 95.2% and should not be used directly; the primary value lies in the Zeff features themselves. All code, data, and reproduction scripts are provided as supplementary material.

papers.title: NJmatWeb: An AI-Driven Web Platform Automating Machine Learning and Genetic Algorithm for Materials Science
papers.abstract: Data-driven methodologies are now widely employed for predicting materials properties; however, most existing tools fail to integrate automated feature selection, interpretable modeling, and an accessible user interface into a unified pipeline. To bridge this gap, we introduce NJmatWeb, a web-based platform that automates machine learning (ML), genetic algorithm (GA) and SHAP analysis for materials science applications. Designed to perform robustly on the small datasets commonly encountered in this field, NJmatWeb incorporates a GA module that yields interpretable symbolic expressions, thereby enhancing model transparency. NJmatWeb incorporates an automatic featurizer that handles both inorganic and organic materials. The platform further provides automated feature selection, feature ranking, SHAP analysis, dataset visualization, and heat map comparisons of the feature space before and after selection. Prediction accuracies of available models are reported, with results from both widely adopted materials benchmarks and diverse case studies. This study demonstrates a useful AI tool aligned with the Materials Genome Engineering, accelerating materials design by combining predictive power with interpretability in an accessible web platform.

Dissecting Dual Ir/Lewis base Mechanophotoredox Catalysis by Ex Situ Kinetic and Thermographic Profiling for Solvent-free Air-tolerant Giese-type Addition of Boronic esters onto Electron-Deficient Olefins
papers.abstract: We describe a dual Lewis base mechanophotocatalytic protocol for Giese-type additions that unites an iridium photocatalyst with Lewis bases under solvent-minimized or solvent-free conditions. The combination of mechanical agitation and visible-light excitation enables a fast and efficient coupling between boronate esters and electron-deficient olefins, delivering near-quantitative NMR yields within 40 minutes when using a liquid-assisted grinding (LAG) agent. Reactions carried out in the absence of LAG agent proceeded more slowly but still gave significant amounts of the desired product. Among the Lewis bases examined, 4-dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP) provided the highest conversions, regardless of whether a LAG agent was used or not. Thermal imaging and solvent-screening experiments revealed that methanol was the optical LAG agent, providing a micro-solvated environment that assists Lewis-base turnover. Together, these results and insights valorise dual Ir/LB mechanophotocatalysis as an efficient, rapid, and solvent-minimized methodology for this class of C sp3 -C sp2 cross-coupling reactions.

papers.title: On Contemporary Tafel Analysis
papers.abstract: Tafel slope analysis has been the cornerstone of mechanistic interpretation in multi-step electrochemical reactions for nearly a century, underpinning our understanding of reactions from hydrogen evolution to carbon dioxide reduction. Here we demonstrate that the contemporary framework, universally adopted for relating Tafel slopes to rate-determining step identity and position, is mathematically incomplete, a consequence of omitting the chain rule in its original derivation.Instead, it is only valid in the low coverage limit where the electrode remains dominated by empty sites, or when the number of electrons transferred before the rate-determining step is only counted from the step consuming the most abundant surface species. We resolve this inconsistency by introducing a corrected analytical framework for both bound and unbound adsorption models, the latter expressed in closed matrix form for arbitrary reaction networks. Applied to the hydrogen evolution and oxidation reactions, the corrected framework reveals that small Tafel slopes are indicative of a reversible Volmer step with low surface coverage, irrespective of reaction path and adsorption type, while mechanistic discrimination only emerges at high Tafel slopes. Experimentally, we observe Tafel slopes of 140-190 mV/dec on polycrystalline Pt in alkaline media, values not captured by the classical framework but naturally described by the corrected one. Furthermore, by providing a continuous analytical solution that spans from these interaction-dominated asymptotes down to the rigorous 0 mV/dec reversible limit, our framework eliminates the need to heuristically define Tafel regions.

papers.title: Cooperative Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic Oxidations
papers.abstract: We show that cooperation of heterogeneous metal and homogeneous Brønsted-acid catalysts enables direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 + O 2 → H 2 O 2 ) in aprotic solvents. By studying different molecular acids, we discover that the selectivity of H 2 O 2 vs H 2 O formation is controlled by the steric profile of the acid, which we hypothesize orchestrates the formation of transition states for proton-coupled reduction of metal-bound O 2 . This mechanistic understanding informs our selection of unhindered Brønsted-acid catalysts that tune H 2 O 2 selectivity by ~20× in aprotic solvents and improve H 2 O 2 selectivity by ~60× compared to protic solvents. We show the synthetic value of H 2 O 2 formation in organic solvents by addition of a third catalytic function via Lewis-acidic TS-1 zeolite that activates H 2 O 2 to oxidize thioanisole into the corresponding sulfoxide and sulfone with quantitative selectivity. This work thus establishes strategies for tunable heterogeneous–homogeneous catalytic cooperativity and synthetic protocols for peroxide-mediated oxidation applicable to a broad expanse of organic substrates.

papers.title: Phase-Aware Adaptation for Functional Group Recognition fromCondensed-Phase Infrared Spectra
papers.abstract: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy is widely used for functional group identification, but machine-learning models often struggle when spectra are transferred across physical phases. Here we establish a phase-separated 16-label benchmark for functional group recognition across gas, liquid, and solid IR spectra and show that direct gas-to-condensed transfer is unreliable, especially for solid spectra. Simply increasing model capacity or replacing the backbone provides only limited improvement. In contrast, the main two-stage gas-pretrained adaptation protocol substantially improves condensed-phase recognition over target-only training, raising solid Macro-F1 from 0.6902 to 0.7351 and liquid Macro-F1 from 0.7198 to 0.7792. The improvement is class-dependent, with strong recovery for labels such as nitrile, while alkene remains difficult because of weak and overlapping spectral evidence. Additional analyses show that the adaptation benefit is not explained by longer target-only training or class weighting, and that it transfers across multiple model families. To make the adapted model more suitable for resource-limited use, we applied segment max pooling under the two-stage gas-pretrained adaptation pipeline, reducing the model to 9.23% of the original Dual Head parameter count while retaining 99.04% of its Macro-F1 performance. Together, this work establishes a phase-aware adaptation framework for condensed-phase IR functional group recognition, showing that gas-phase spectra can be converted from an unreliable direct predictor into useful prior training data for solid and liquid spectra.

papers.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Electrolyte Structural Transport Mechanism: Attempt Frequencies and Activation Free Energies
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion transport through an electrolyte, in addition to standard diffusion (vehicular), a second Li+ transport mechanism, called structural diffusion, is important. Very recently the molecular-level process, partial desolvation (a solvent molecule leaving the Li+/solvent cluster), that is responsible for structural diffusion was delineated. Here, we deepen our understanding of structural diffusion. The concentration dependence of Li+ structural diffusion in liquids with three different anions was studied using ultrafast two dimensional infrared experiments. The time dependencies of the fundamental physical fluctuations that underlie partial desolvation were determined. These fluctuations correspond to the attempt frequencies in transition-state theory. Attempt frequencies in the context of molecular transtition state theory have not previously been measured. Knowing the partial desolvation rates and the attempt frequencies enabled the determination of the activation free energies for partial desolvation, which range from ~7 to ~9 kJ/mol. The quantitative results provide the path from molecular-level fluctuations to diffusion constants.

papers.title: Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer Dynamics with Neural Network Potentials and Nuclear Quantum Effects
papers.abstract: Excited-state intramolecular proton transfer is a prototypical ultrafast process that forms the foundation for many chemical and biological phenomena and is highly sensitive to changes in the underlying potential energy landscape. Here, we develop neural network potentials for 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline that describe ground- and excited-state dynamics with near ab initio accuracy. These neural network potentials enable efficient sampling of the proton transfer coordinate and incorporation of nuclear quantum effects through path-integral molecular dynamics. The free energy profiles show that excited-state intramolecular proton transfer proceeds on a largely barrierless excited-state surface, with nuclear quantum effects reducing and smoothing the residual barrier. Non-equilibrium simulations yield an average proton transfer time of ~11.4 fs for quantum hydrogen, consistent with experiment, and reveal a clear isotope effect, with slower dynamics for deuterium and classical nuclei. Mechanistic analysis identifies transient proton donor–acceptor contraction as the key enabling coordinate, while the proton crosses the midpoint prior to reaching the minimum of this coordinate, indicating a dynamically driven transfer. Subtle changes in the conjugated backbone precede proton transfer, reflecting early electronic reorganization and coherent coupling between proton motion and backbone vibrations. Bond-length alternation and vibrational coherence analysis reveal isotope-dependent coherence loss, with deuteration producing stronger damping and more localized proton/backbone dynamics relative to hydrogen. These results establish neural network potential-based approaches as an effective framework for simulating excited-state proton transfer with explicit nuclear quantum effects.

papers.title: One-pot systhesis of a long-chain metal-backboned polymer
papers.abstract: Metal-backboned polymers, featuring backbones composed exclusively of metal atoms interconnected by consecutive metal–metal bonds, have been proposed as a new class of materials for promising applications in optics, electronics, and magnetics; however, they remain unavailable for synthesis. Taking advantage of the long-range aurophilic attraction of gold, we report a straightforward one-pot synthesis method to fabricate metal-backboned polymers. This strategy achieves a degree of polymerization exceeding 50 and stable chain integrity in solution, providing a concise and efficient route for their production. Systematic structural characterizations revealed a one-dimensional Au backbone with continuous Au–Au bonds stabilized by quasi-covalent bonding in synergy with ligand protection. The resulting gold-backboned polymer (GBP) exhibits typical polymer behaviors, including the glass transition temperature and film-forming ability. In addition, GBP exhibits effective electron delocalization, semiconducting properties, and long-wavelength phosphorescence, with a preliminary electroluminescent fiber device demonstrating its potential in flexible optoelectronics. This study establishes a general and efficient route for the synthesis of metal-backboned polymers.

papers.title: The Quantum-Volume and Bragg-Williams Equations of State
papers.abstract: The quantum-volume (qv) and Bragg-Williams equations of state, as derived from a lattice gas model, are exploited. The qv equation of state includes a temperaturedependent excluded volume related to the thermal wavelength included in the translational contribution to the molecular partition function, but apart from this contribution intermolecular interactions are not included. The qv equation of state has the correct limiting behaviour both in the limit of an ideal gas and in the packing-density limit. It also includes a non-classical contribution to the internal energy and thereby a manyparticle contribution to the kinetic energy, and it supports the view that it is both the position as well as the momentum of a system of particles that are distributed over the volume to maximize the multiplicity of the system. The qv equation of state is extended with intermolecular interactions through the Bragg-Williams mean-field approach, including also a hard-core contribution. For a one-component lattice gas, analytical expressions are presented for the pressure and the critical point as well as for the internal energy, the isochoric heat capacity, and the chemical potential, and results are presented for some simple systems. Given its relative simplicity, essentially on a textbook level, the model shows promising results, in particular for the temperature dependence of the isochoric heat capacity that shows a maximum close to the critical temperature. The presented model is supposed to serve as a foundation for further model extensions as well as for the development of interpretable analytical models in molecular thermodynamics for more complex systems and processes.

papers.title: From Photon Spiral Motion to Superheavy Elements: A Unified Analytical Atomic-Molecular Energy Theory Based on Quantum Phase Vortices and Relativistic Corrections
papers.abstract: Within the constructive theoretical framework, this work establishes the Ether-Vortex Atomic and Molecular Model (EVAM), a fully analytical energy scheme covering the entire periodic table with atomic numbers from to . Three foundational constructive physical pictures, namely photon spiral propagation, etheric structural medium, and electron quantum phase vortex, are introduced with methodological status analogous to imaginary numbers in mathematics. They do not claim ontological physical reality, but merely serve as instrumental structures for unifying theoretical formalism, simplifying analytical derivation, and sustaining self-consistent and stable computation. EVAM adopts exponential wave packets to characterize electronic spatial distributions, realizing strictly analytical integration of all Coulomb interactions while completely eliminating basis sets, numerical integration, and self-consistent field iterations. The computational complexity is reduced to . A constructive relativistic wave packet width formula is constructed to achieve automatic wave packet saturation, which fundamentally eliminates computational divergence for heavy and superheavy elements, enabling uniform, stable, and high-precision descriptions across light, heavy, and superheavy nuclides. Resting on only 10 globally fixed parameters, EVAM achieves chemical accuracy for light atoms and small molecules. For heavy elements, deviations from Dirac–Fock reference data remain below , while superheavy element results are provided exclusively for theoretical benchmarking. All calculations are completed within milliseconds to seconds on a conventional single personal computer. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations attain approximately 115-fold speedup relative to parallel DFT-AIMD computations. Within the constructive paradigm, the model uniformly interprets electron correlation, chemical bonding, and relativistic effects. It can be employed as an independent computational tool for material simulation, catalytic mechanism research, and theoretical investigations of superheavy elements.

papers.title: Distribution of Relaxation Times through the Lens of Distribution Theory
papers.abstract: The distribution of relaxation times (DRT) model is widely used to deconvolve electrochemical impedance spectra into timescale distributions. However, standard DRT formulations assume integrable impedance. This condition is violated by electrochemical systems with blocking boundaries where diffusion or charge accumulation causes the low-frequency response to diverge. We formulate DRT inversion in the space of tempered distributions and derive a distributional Fuoss–Kirkwood boundary-value relation in S ′(R), under explicit analyticity, growth, and boundary-value assumptions on the strip continuation of the impedance. In this setting, the DRT is determined by the strip boundary values of the impedance, with Dirac atoms from simple poles, derivatives of Dirac masses from higher-order poles, and power-law tails from non-integrable low-frequency behavior. This formulation clarifies reported discrepancies for capacitive and diffusive systems by making the boundary-value convention explicit and separating distributional identities from pointwise evaluations. We derive closed-form distributional DRTs for generalized resistor-capacitor (RC) circuits, constant-phase elements, and finite-length diffusion transmission-line models in multiple geometries, and establish relationships between the DRT and the distributions of diffusion and capacitive times.

papers.title: Cholesterol-Dependent Membrane Fluidity in Sindbis Virus Governs Viral Particle Stability and Infectivity
papers.abstract: Cholesterol is a key biomolecule that regulates the fluidity of lipid bilayers, with cholesterol-rich domains in host cells and virions being critical for virion entry and egress. Herein, using the Alphavirus Sindbis virus (SINV) as a model, we combine new experimental methodologies and single-particle biological characterization to revisit how envelope cholesterol affects particle stability and the biological consequences for infectivity. To this end, we generated two SINV populations exhibiting a 3-fold difference in cholesterol levels in the viral envelope (SINV HC and SINV LC ) to understand how cholesterol levels affect SINV stability and infectivity. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and dynamic light scattering (DLS) showed minimal differences in morphology and size, indicating that cholesterol minimally alters virion structure. Electrochemical and microfluidic measurements between SINV HC and SINV LC particles revealed similar Zeta Potentials (ζ-potential ~ -31 mV), which implies that the surface distribution of the E1-E2 glycoprotein heterotrimers within the envelope is cholesterol-independent. Titer measurements showed that SINV HC retains nearly an order of magnitude higher infectious particles than SINV LC when pre-exposed to 30 minutes of thermal stress. Single-particle fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy analysis using the fluidity-sensitive dye DI-8-ANEPPS revealed a statistically significant increase (≥ 0.2 ns; p < 0.0001) of photon arrival times in the SINV HC population, indicating that elevated cholesterol enhances membrane rigidity. Because virion size and ζ-potential remained unchanged while fluorescence lifetimes increased with cholesterol level, these findings indicate that membrane fluidity is the primary parameter governing viral stability and subsequent infectivity.

papers.title: Dibenzothiophenium Carborane: A Carbon-Centered Carboranyl Radical Transfer Reagent under Photoredox Catalysis
papers.abstract: Icosahedral carboranes are a unique class of three-dimensional aromatic boron clusters whose functionalized derivatives have found broad applications in materials science, ligand design, organic synthesis, and medicinal chemistry. Despite significant advances in radical-based transformations, methods for generating C-centered carboranyl radicals remain scarce because of the relatively high C–H bond dissociation energy and the limited availability of suitable radical precursors. To address this issue, we designed and synthesized a dibenzothiophenium carborane reagent as a practical precursor for C-centered radicals. Although dibenzothiophenium salts have emerged as efficient radical progenitors, their application in carborane chemistry has not been explored. Herein, we demonstrate that this reagent undergoes single-electron reduction by a photoredox catalyst under visible-light irradiation to generate C-centered carboranyl radicals, enabling efficient alkene difunctionalization. This approach provides versatile access to otherwise challenging C-functionalized carborane derivatives and expands the synthetic toolbox for boron-cluster radical chemistry.

papers.title: Charge-neutral organic photocatalysts with exceptional excited-state reducing power
papers.abstract: Organic photocatalysts with exceptionally strong reducing power have emerged as powerful tools for enabling transformations that are inaccessible to conventional photoredox systems. However, developing robust, charge-neutral organic photocatalysts that combine extreme excited-state reducing ability with practical stability under visible-light irradiation remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report the rational design of carbazole-based organic photocatalysts featuring multiple sterically compact amino substituents installed at positions with large HOMO coefficients. Among the substituents evaluated, azetidinyl groups act as particularly effective electron donors, outperforming the commonly used dimethylamino group. This enhancement arises from their compact steric profile, which minimizes congestion around the nitrogen atom and promotes a more coplanar orientation of the amino substituent relative to the carbazole core, thereby enhancing conjugation between the nitrogen lone pair and the carbazole p-system. As a result, these charge-neutral photocatalysts exhibit extraordinarily deep negative excited-state oxidation potentials, exceeding those of elemental sodium and lithium, while maintaining sufficient air stability and photostability. Leveraging this exceptional reducing power, visible-light-driven C–H carboxylation of a broad range of (hetero)arenes with CO 2 proceeds smoothly under mild conditions, highlighting an advantage of charge-neutral photocatalysts over anionic systems, which can revert to their neutral forms under the acidic CO 2 atmosphere. In addition, the same photocatalyst platform enables challenging reductive hydrodefluorination of aryl fluorides. Collectively, this work defines molecular design principles for achieving extreme reducing power in charge-neutral organic photocatalysts and expands the range of photoreductive transformations accessible under visible light.

papers.title: Electrosynthesis of free-standing asymmetric chitosan films at polarised soft interfaces
B, F Doped Graphitic Carbon Nitride (g-C3N4) as Efficient Volatile Organic Compound Sensing 2D Material: A DFT Study
papers.abstract: 2D graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) are achieving immense research interest due to their unique electrical, optical, and mechanical properties. In recent past, 2D nano materials have manifested their excellency for identifying disease-related volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Herein, the potential sensor applicability of B,F g-C3N4 towards aniline, acetone, ethanol and benzene biomarkers is studied using density functional theory (DFT). The results attributed that simultaneous doping in g-C3N4 with non-metal B and F atoms, modulates the surface chemistry and switch the adsorption of biomarker gas molecules from strongly bound covalent to weakly bound non-covalent state. Substantial band gap narrowing, significant charge transfer interaction, work function calculations, enhanced conductivity, and sensitivity upon adsorption, implied B,F g-C3N4 as a potential and high performance sensor selectively for aniline. The Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) and Reduced Density Gradient (RDG) analyses decisively established that adsorption of VOCs on B,F g-C3N4 are dominated by pure non-covalent van der Waals (vdW) interaction. Finally, the recovery time of 212.78 ms calculated for aniline begin a new avenue by proposing non metal doped B,F g-C3N4 for medical diagnosis.

papers.title: N-Insertions on 2H-Azetines: A 4-to-5 Skeletal Editing Strategy towards Imidazoles
papers.abstract: A nitrogen insertion ring-expansion strategy employing nitrene precursors has been developed for the conver-sion of 2H-azetines into the corresponding imidazoles. The transformation proceeds via transient nitrene spieces and involves C–C bond cleavage of an aziridine intermediate, a mechanism supported by DFT calculations. The resulting functionalized scaffolds also provide access to structurally unique 1,3,5-triazines and halogenated pyrimidines, highlighting the synthetic versatility of this approach.

papers.title: MOONLIT: A Trackable Antisense strategy targeting the miR-675-5p/HIF-1α axis in Glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma remains one of the most aggressive and treatment-resistant brain tumours. Here, we demonstrate the therapeutic efficacy of a novel family of antisense oligonucleotides (MOONLITs) targeting the miR-675-5p/HIF-1α oncogenic axis. MOONLITs significantly suppress cell viability in both temozolomide-sensitive and temozolomide-resistant glioblastoma cell lines via downregulation of miR-675-5p and HIF-1α expression and nuclear localization. Therapeutic efficacy was preserved in 3D spheroids, where MOONLITs inhibited tumour growth under physiologically relevant conditions. Systemic administration of fluorescently labelled MOONLITs in an orthotopic luciferase-expressing (Temozolomide-resistant) glioblastoma mouse model achieved efficient tumour biodistribution and retention, resulting in inhibition of tumour progression in vivo. Ex vivo analyses confirmed selective downregulation of miR-675-5p and suppression of HIF-1α signalling exclusively in treated animals. Molecular Dynamics simulations and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance-informed analyses revealed that, although full sequence complementarity enhances duplex stability, it is not required for biological efficacy. Collectively, our findings establish MOONLIT-mediated targeting of the miR-675-5p/HIF-1α axis as a powerful and translationally relevant therapeutic strategy for glioblastoma.

papers.title: High Chirality Induced Spin Selectivity in the Multilayered Moiré Superlattices of n-type as well as p-type 2D Crystalline Silicene Based on Resonant Quantum Tunneling
papers.abstract: The recent efforts to fabricate spintronic devices based on layered two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) materials through twisted stacking offers a promising avenue in electronics (especially spintronics) by taking advantage of quantum phenomena such as resonant quantum tunneling for superior performance outcomes. Herein, we report resonant tunneling diode (RTD) characteristics observed at room-temperature in moiré superlattices of n-type multilayered silicene (phosphorous doped) and p-type multilayered silicene (boron doped) homostructures that were synthesized using a scalable method of heat-assisted sonication in liquid medium. The twisted interface served as a quantum well, while the 2D nanosheets functioned as the tunneling barrier, eliminating the need to rely on any different resistive material typically used as physical tunneling barriers in 2D heterostructure RTDs, and as a result, could allow increased tunneling current. The NDR peak position can be tuned where the direction of the magnetic field could determine its occurrence either for an applied positive or negative bias. Further, the moiré superlattices were chiral in nature and displayed chirality dependent spin selection where maximum spin polarizability of 97.20±1.81% was observed at -0.2 V for 0.45 T for p-type multilayered silicene moiré superlattice and 98.33±2.30% at -0.6 V for n-type multilayered silicene moiré superlattice for 0.45 T. Here we also provided a method to synthesize precisely twist-stacked moiré superlattices of n-type or/and p-type multilayered silicene through reaction of precursor 2D nanosheets with ZnCl2. The experimental 2 observations reported herein indicate the possibility of fabricating portable quantum devices based on resonance tunneling.

papers.title: Determination of Asbestos Fibre Release Potential from Contaminated Craft Sand and Sand-Based Toys
papers.abstract: Over the last century, human exposure pathways for asbestos have changed from those associated with direct interaction with the minerals (e.g. mining) to secondary exposure from a variety of asbestoscontaining materials, including those linked to para-occupational, domestic and environmental pathways. In 2025, the discovery of asbestos in children’s toy sand products caused panic, stress and fear amongst the community. Although there is no safe level of asbestos exposure, these products were deemed to be low risk by some due to uncertainty around whether fibres could become airborne during play. In this experimental study, contaminated sand samples were “played with” inside a Class A asbestos enclosure by an asbestos technician wearing protective equipment. Air samples collected were analysed using a combination of light and electron microscopy undertaken by two independent laboratories. 90% of tested craft sands released asbestos fibres into the air during play activities. Some fibres met the criteria for respirability. Air samples taken during experiments using moulding sand samples did not show any airborne asbestos fibres; however, analytical detection limits for this study were high. This demonstrates that the potential risk from asbestos in the product can create a real risk from fibres in the air; however, the magnitude of this risk has yet to be determined by further research. Nevertheless, no amount of risk of asbestos exposure through toys is acceptable so the most practical way to eliminate this risk would be to avoid the use of artificial sand products in toys or similar consumer products.

papers.title: Directional Electric Fields Reveal Nonadditive Polarization–Geometry Coupling in Cyclo[13]carbon Dichloride
papers.abstract: Electronic polarization and nuclear relaxation can cooperate under oriented electric fields, but their nonadditivity is rarely resolved for deformable carbon rings. We computed the gas-phase, static, adiabatically relaxed response of singlet C13Cl2 in a 33-point scan of signed in-plane and ring-normal fields at the ωB97X-D/def2-TZVP level; harmonic analysis verified a minimum at every point. The in-plane response was initially near-linear but developed a pronounced structural reorganization between |F | = 0.015 and 0.020 atomic units, where the helical coordinate, bond-length alternation, anchor charges, and C–Cl bond indices changed cooperatively. At |Fx| = 0.020 atomic units, the total energy response partitioned into a −52.0 kcal mol−1 fixed-geometry electronic term and a −15.1 kcal mol−1 field-conditioned relaxation term, while the separate four-state cross difference reached −45.3 kcal mol−1. Charge-displacement profiles and force projections connected polarization to field-induced internal forces and geometry feedback. The ring-normal response remained smooth over the same range. These results identify a directionselective mixed electronic–nuclear response without invoking a discrete topological switch or extrapolating to scanning-probe dynamics.

papers.title: A Stretchable Interactive Photonic Electronic Hydrogel with Intrinsic Luminescent Timing Function for Strain Rate Recording
papers.abstract: Stretchable electronics hold promising applications in diverse fields such as wearable healthcare devices and human-machine interfaces. However, current devices suffer from insufficient interactivity and reliance on external clock/timing modules. The luminescence as a user-friendly visual mode possesses native multi-dimensional attributes including intensity, wavelength (color), and lifetime, which provide possibilities to acquire interactive high-dimensional information. In particular, the unique temporal attribute of lifetime has not been fully exploited in function constructing of stretchable materials. Herein, time-resolved photoluminescence signals as the source of intrinsic timing function are introduced into elastic conductive hydrogels to develop stretchable photonic electronics which can realize photonically spatio-temporal strain rate recording and multi-dimensional interaction including photonic-electronic dual-modal and human-material-smartphone multi-entity interactions independent of additional timing modules. The light-mapped-time paradigm provides a fresh strategy for functional material design, and the afforded hydrogel delivers a promising candidate for flexible interactive sensory devices construction.

papers.title: Hybrid Expert-Fuzzy Control for Dissolved Oxygen and Biomass Regulation in Extended-Aeration Activated Sludge Systems
papers.abstract: Extended-aeration activated sludge systems are nonlinear and highly coupled biological processes whose performance depends on the coordinated regulation of dissolved oxygen, reactor biomass, returned biomass, sludge wasting, return sludge flow, and aeration. Conventional PI/PID control remains widely used in wastewater treatment plants, but its performance may deteriorate under hydraulic, organic-load, and thermal disturbances due to nonlinear dynamics and multivariable interactions. This study develops and evaluates a hybrid expert-fuzzy control strategy for dissolved oxygen and biomass regulation in an extended-aeration activated sludge system. A control-oriented nonlinear reactor–clarifier model was formulated to represent biodegradable substrate, reactor biomass, returned biomass, and dissolved oxygen dynamics. The model incorporated an airflow- and temperature-dependent oxygen transfer coefficient, and the local linearized model was used for stability analysis, MIMO interaction assessment, and partial dynamic decoupling of the biomass subsystem. Three strategies were compared through nonlinear simulation: a conventional PI/PID baseline, a hybrid base strategy with incremental fuzzy dissolved oxygen control and decoupled biomass PI control, and a hybrid expert-fuzzy strategy with supervisory modules for sludge wasting and return-sludge-ratio adjustment. The strategies were evaluated under set-point tracking, individual hydraulic and organic-load disturbances, and combined hydraulic, organic, and thermal disturbances. The hybrid base strategy achieved the best set-point tracking score, whereas the hybrid expert-fuzzy strategy achieved the best disturbance-rejection performance. Under the combined disturbance scenario, the normalized score decreased from 1.000 for the PI/PID baseline to 0.695 for the hybrid expert-fuzzy strategy. The accumulated dissolved oxygen error was reduced by approximately 89.5%, and the reactor biomass error decreased by approximately 72.6%. The hybrid expert-fuzzy strategy also maintained the manipulated variables within feasible operating ranges and reduced actuator variability. These results suggest that the proposed architecture provides a reproducible and interpretable framework for improving robustness in extended-aeration activated sludge control under variable operating conditions.

papers.title: Fragment-based discovery of mycobacterial thioredoxin reductase inhibitors guided by virtual chemical space exploration
papers.abstract: The rising number of people dying from tuberculosis and the increase of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) strains lead to an urgent need for new antituberculosis drugs. The mycobacterial thioredoxin reductase (Mtb-TrxR) is a novel and promising target with already demonstrated druggability. Based on a crystallographic fragment screening, two promising but inactive fragments binding in the NADPH-binding pocket of M-TrxR were selected for optimisation using two different fragment-based drug design methods. One fragment was developed using a SAR-by-catalogue approach, while the other was optimised via a socialisation-andgrowth strategy supported by computer-assisted synthesis planning, which informed subsequent reaction condition optimisation. After only one cycle of optimisation and testing, a new scaffold of micromolar Mtb-TrxR inhibitors was developed, with a hit compound exhibiting double-digit micromolar activity (pIC 50 = 4.41 ± 0.02) after synthesising only five fragment expansions.

papers.title: Beyond Global Drug-Likeness: The FamDLike Framework as a Target Family-specific Druglikeness Score
papers.abstract: Drug-likeness is a central metric which is used to evaluate the physicochemical profile of small molecules either as a filter for virtual screening or, more recently, as a reward function in generative design tasks. Established scores such as QED are widely adopted for these purposes, although the ligands of different therapeutic target families occupy different regions of physicochemical space. Applying a single global drug-likeness criterion can therefore systematically reward some target classes while penalising others, narrowing the chemical space considered druglike in a way that may not reflect the actual requirements for a given project. In this work, we propose a target family specific drug-likeness approach, the FamDLike framework, designed to distinguish target families more accurately than existing metrics and to explore family specific druglike regions of chemical space. This framework combines three complementary modelling paradigms: desirability functions, generalized additive models and tree-based machine learning models that span the interpretability–flexibility spectrum. The three components can also be used independently, depending on whether interpretability or predictive flexibility is prioritized. The abilities of the proposed method have been tested on real-world use cases in computational medicinal chemistry: an independent set from DrugBank, library screening of Enamine and KLIFS compounds, and de novo molecule generation via REINVENT4. The proposed approach therefore provides a more discriminative, interpretable and target-aware complement to existing drug-likeness scores, suitable for ranking in early discovery pipelines and as a reward function for generative chemistry. Furthermore, a user-friendly web portal ( https://huggingface.co/spaces/kochgroup/FamDLike ) is available to obtain drug-likeness profiles of molecules.

papers.title: Heptacoordinated Antimony(V) Cations
papers.abstract: Heptacoordinated pnictogen cations are quite rare, although cationic Sb(V) species are formally isoelectronic with neutral Sn(IV) compounds, for which several heptacoordinated structures are known. Here, we report on the synthesis, isolation, and structural characterization of two heptacoordinated Sb(V) cations, i.e., [(ppy) 3 Sb–X] + (X = F; [ 1–F ] + , X = CH 3 ; [ 1–CH 3 ] + , ppy = 2-(2-pyridyl)phenyl), which represent [14–Sb–7] + -type chemical species. Fluorination of neutral (ppy) 3 Sb ( 1 ) followed by fluoride abstraction afforded fluorostibonium cation [ 1–F ] + , while methylation of 1 furnished methylstibonium cation [ 1–CH 3 ] + . In the solid state, [ 1–F ] + adopts a pentagonal-bipyramidal (PBP) coordination geometry, whereas [ 1–CH 3 ] + adopts a tricappedtetrahedral (TCT) one. Density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations for [ 1–F ] + , [ 1–CH 3 ] + , and related [(ppy) 3 Sb–X] + cations (X = Cl, Br, CF 3 , H) revealed that the preferred coordination geometry depends on the acceptor character at the site trans to the Sb–X bond. Strongly electron-withdrawing substituents (X = F, Cl, Br) increase the acceptor character at this position and lead to PBP structures, whereas weaker electron-withdrawing substituents (X = CH 3 , CF 3 , H) reduce the acceptor character and favor TCT structures.

papers.title: Semicrystalline Chain-growth Photopolymer Networks Synthesized by Orthogonal Neat Polymerization Reactions
papers.abstract: A sequential and orthogonal polymerization reaction strategy was developed to synthesize semicrystalline polymer networks. Acrylate-terminated oligomers were first prepared by thiol-Michael oligomerization between difunctional aliphatic acrylate and thiol monomers, giving oligomers with molecular weight ranges of 3.1-7.4 kDa. These crystalline oligomers were then photopolymerized in their molten state at 70 °C. The longer oligomers yielded semicrystalline networks, confirmed by thermal, mechanical, optical, and X-ray diffraction characterizations, whereas shorter-chain analogs were weakly crystalline or amorphous. Mechanical testing suggested strain-induced crystallization behavior, in which samples crystallized under tension reached 680% elongation-at-break and 15 MPa ultimate tensile strength.

papers.title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of O6C-Salvinorin Alkyne Probes
papers.abstract: The salvinorins represent a unique class of polyoxygenated, non-nitrogenous diterpenes that potently and selectively modulate the kappa-opioid receptor (KOR). We recently disclosed a de novo asymmetric synthesis of this scaffold that enabled the discovery of highly potent, biased analogs, including C11-alkynes designed for the CATCH (Clearing-Assisted Tissue Click Chemistry) assay. Here, we report an optimized, scalable synthetic route that substitutes a problematic 1,4-conjugate addition of a Grignard reagent with a robust organozinc protocol in DMA, and improves a samarium-mediated Reformatsky reaction via the addition of LiBr. These methodological improvements facilitated the scalable synthesis of two highly active positive-control probes and three tailored negativecontrol probes, including functionally silent and cross-linking deficient analogs. A screen of >300 GPCRs confirmed the exceptional KOR selectivity of the novel alkyne probe, establishing it as a critical tool to validate target-specific engagement in situ.

papers.title: Openclatura–an Open-Source Nomenclature Framework for Rule-Based Molecule Naming
papers.abstract: Naming molecules systematically remains an open challenge in cheminformatics. The reverse task—converting names to structure—has been largely solved for over a decade by OPSIN, yet no open-source tool performs the forward direction. Here we introduce Openclatura, which generates IUPAC names from molecular structures. The rule set was constructed by an agentic system that exhaustively enumerates naming rules, with each candidate name checked for structural round-trip consistency against OPSIN. Across three challenging benchmarks (QM9, PubChem, and ZINC22), Openclatura produces valid names for 98% of molecules, compared to 95% for the deep-learning baseline STOUT, while running on a single CPU core (40 times faster). We further present Robomoleculographer, an extension that generates natural-language descriptions of molecular graphs, bringing to chemistry what robocrystallographer offers to materials. Openclatura is fully deterministic and exposes an inspectable decision trace for every generated name.

papers.title: Effect of washing on the surface chemistry of silica nanoparticles
papers.abstract: The surface chemistry of silica nanoparticles is central to their use in applications such as catalysis, CO2 adsorption, environmental remediation, or drug delivery, yet the role of post synthesis washing remains poorly understood. The surface of silica nanoparticles produced by the conventional Stöber process, in which tetraethoxysilane reacts with water in the presence of ammonia, is covered with silanol groups and residual species from the synthesis, such as ethoxy groups and ammonia. Here, we systematically investigate how washing with ethanol, water, or water/hydrochloric acid affects the concentration of silanols, ethoxy groups, and ammonia on the surface of silica nanoparticles. Using 29Si, 1H, and 13C solid state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, complemented by infrared spectroscopy and elemental analysis, we demonstrate that washing with ethanol effectively removes adsorbed ammonia, but has little effect on the distribution of silanol groups or on the amount of ethoxy groups on the silica surface. In contrast, water and water/HCl effectively hydrolyze surface species, increasing the density of single silanols and removing residual surface-bound ethoxy groups and ammonia. Subsequent surface functionalization with 3-(aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES) showed that all particles retain a sufficient number of silanol groups to achieve maximum APTES grafting, suggesting that surface silanization processes are largely insensitive to variations in the washing history. At the same time, the washing protocol offers a means of modulating residual ethoxy groups and, to some extent, the binding mode of the grafted APTES. In particular, water-washed particles exhibit the least residual ethoxy groups after APTES grafting. These results show that careful washing can be used to control the surface chemistry of silica nanoparticles without compromising maximal APTES grafting, underscoring the robustness of the silica system for further functionalization.

papers.title: Force Fields and Simulation Engines: Lessons Learned from Porting Amber ff14SB and ff19SB to GROMACS
papers.abstract: The GROMACS molecular dynamics simulation package has historically supported a number of molecular mechanics force fields, including Amber. Force fields have evolved over time and continue to do so through refinement of existing interactions and the definition of additional ones to more faithfully match real-world experiments and higher-level quantum chemistry calculations. Although users have provided a number of conversions of newer Amber force fields over the years, the two most recent Amber protein force fields, ff14SB and ff19SB, had not previously been officially ported to GROMACS. A technical challenge is that ff19SB introduces residue-specific backbone dihedral energy correction maps (CMAPs), which required new support in GROMACS for residue-aware force-field preprocessing and topology generation. Unlike older force fields such as CHARMM27, in which CMAPs are parameterized using only atom types, ff19SB extends this scheme with additional amino-acid typing. Here, we describe how we ported and validated the Amber ff14SB and ff19SB force fields for use with GROMACS as AMBER14SB and AMBER19SB, respectively. The ported force fields reproduce the Amber reference topologies exactly, with per-interaction energies matching to within the single-precision floating-point limit (< 10 −7 kJ/mol). To achieve this level of consistency between Amber and GROMACS, we resolved discrepancies in their handling of fundamental constants, parameter precision, and improper-dihedral atom ordering logic. In long unrestrained ubiquitin simulations, the converted ff19SB reproduces the conformational free-energy profile obtained with the native Amber implementation. This work provides the first official port of an Amber force field to GROMACS in more than a decade, improving feature parity between the two simulation packages. We provide a reproducible porting and validation procedure that can be used for modified variants and future versions of Amber force fields.

papers.title: Electrocatalytic Hydrodeoxygenation of Aldehydes Enabled by Pd@CNTstabilized Pickering Emulsions
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrodeoxygenation (ECHDO) has the potential to produce high-value chemicals from aromatic aldehydes using water as a hydrogen source. However, the efficiency of this approach is limited by the low solubility of aromatic aldehydes in aqueous electrolytes, by electrical losses in organic electrolytes, and by generally low Faradaic efficiency and complex product separation. In addition, recent reports have revealed that aldehyde electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) predominantly yields alcohols, while their subsequent electrocatalytic hydrodeoxygenation remains a major challenge, limiting overall C–O bond cleavage. Here, we report the ECHDO of aromatic aldehydes using a Pd@CNTs catalyst located at the interface of a Pickering emulsion system. Our approach leverages the triphasic nature of the Pickering emulsion to create an effective environment for complex catalytic processes, enabling selective ECHDO of various aromatic aldehydes to valuable tolyl derivatives with up to >99% yield and ~62% Faradaic efficiency (FE). Mechanistic investigations confirm that the reaction is of electrocatalytic nature, and that the sequential ECH-ECHDO pathway proceeds through transient alcohol intermediates in our system. This strategy may thus provide alternative solutions to the ECHDO of biomass-derived aromatic aldehydes including lignin-derived aromatic aldehydes encountered in biorefineries and fine chemical synthesis.

papers.title: An Autonomous Passive MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
papers.abstract: Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ 2 -OH)[( E )-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kg MOF −1 day −1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating uniquely fully autonomous multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RH avg = 12.4 %, T avg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (I avg = 496 W m −2 ) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day −1 (185 mL kg MOF −1 day −1 ). These results demonstrate the highest reported specific productivity for a passively heated water harvester under very low humidity (RH avg < 20%) desert operation and represent the most severe reported field deployment conditions for any water harvester.

papers.title: Metal-and Additive-Free Transfer Hydrogenation of Nitrones to Hydroxylamine Derivatives with PhSiH3
papers.abstract: Hydroxylamine derivatives are essential structural motifs in numerous pharmaceuticals, bioactive compounds, and synthetic intermediates. Despite significant advances, the reduction of nitrones remains challenging owing to their inherent 1,3-dipolar character and limited efficient metal-free protocols. Therefore, this study reports a practical metal-and additive-free transfer hydrogenation of nitrones, employing a readily available PhSiH3 serving as the hydrogen donor. The findings demonstrated the effective conversion of a wide range of ketone-and aldehyde-derived nitrones into their corresponding hydroxylamine derivatives in good to excellent yields with remarkable chemoselectivity under mild conditions. The reaction is readily scalable and demonstrates broad functional group tolerance, accommodating bromo, chloro, fluoro, trifluoromethyl, thioether, thiophene, and furan substituents. Hence, the proposed operationally simple protocol provides a practical and sustainable strategy, facilitating the synthesis of structurally diverse

papers.title: Rapid, energy-lean sonochemical synthesis of metal-free polybenzoxazine bifunctional photocatalyst for H2O2 production and furfuryl alcohol oxidation
papers.abstract: The development of scalable, selective, and durable photocatalysts remains a major challenge in artificial photosynthesis. Herein, we introduce a new class of metal-free polybenzoxazine frameworks synthesized through an unconventional template- and surfactant-free emulsion sonochemical strategy, enabling systematic elucidation of the structure–property relationships governing photocatalytic activity. This green, energy-efficient process affords gram-scale quantities within an hour, circumventing the substantial energetic demands typically associated with the synthesis of architecturally complex porous photocatalysts. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the benzoxazine-rich framework selectively drives the visible-light-mediated twoelectron oxygen reduction reaction (2e- ORR), facilitating efficient H2O2 production from water and molecular oxygen under ambient conditions. Among this series, P-mtt exhibits the highest activity, achieving an H2O2 evolution rate of 1250 μmol g-1 h-1 and accumulating 6.4 mM H2O2 after 24 h of continuous irradiation while retaining excellent structural and photochemical stability. P-mtt further demonstrates efficient photon utilization, delivering an apparent quantum yield of 12% at 420 nm and a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.48%. Notably, its performance translates to practical conditions, enabling efficient H2O2 production directly from unpurified seawater. Combined ultrafast spectroscopic measurements and theoretical simulations indicate that sub-nanosecond localization of photogenerated electrons from both free-carrier and excitonic states at catalytic reaction centers facilitates efficient charge utilization and selective 2e- ORR. Beyond H2O2 photosynthesis, P-mtt exhibits remarkable bifunctionality by simultaneously driving the Achmatowicz oxidation of furfuryl alcohol to a value-added pyranone intermediate through a decoupled energy-transfer pathway, while continuously producing H2O2. By integrating scalable low-energy synthesis, high photocatalytic efficiency, and dual-function catalytic selectivity, P-mtt represents a promising polymeric platform for decentralized H2O2 production and sustainable solar-driven chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Breaking Enantiopurity Paradigm: A Chiral Catalyst That Requires Enantioimpurity for Enantioselectivity
papers.abstract: Asymmetric catalysis traditionally relies on enantiopure ligands to achieve high enantioselectivity. However, nonlinear effects (NLEs) can enable scalemic catalysts to match or even surpass their enantiopure counterparts. Here, we report an unprecedented phenomenon in zinc-catalyzed alkylation of benzaldehyde using 3,3'-diiodo-BINOL ligand: the enantiopure ligand yields a racemic product, while scalemic versions generate significant enantioselectivity (up to 60% ee). This challenges the paradigm that enantiopure ligands are inherently superior. Mechanistic studies reveal multiple active catalytic species in equilibrium, with distinct enantioselectivities dependent on ligand enantiopurity, catalyst loading, and temperature. Kinetic analyses and VTNA studies confirm non-constant catalyst orders, suggesting higher-order aggregates (e.g., trimers) alongside dimers. This work demonstrates how scalemic ligands can outperform enantiopure ones, offering a new perspective on chiral amplification and practical advantages in catalytic design.

papers.title: Linking wind-power fluctuation to degradation of PEM water electrolyzer
papers.abstract: Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is highly attractive for renewable-powered hydrogen production, yet its degradation under realistic wind-power fluctuations remains insufficiently understood.
