Although both disk and nanotip electrode geometries have been incorporated into ultrafast ACh biosensors, it remains unclear whether sensor geometry influences quantal measurements and the observed distribution of exocytotic spike shapes. Amperometric recordings were obtained from single cholinergic cells and analyzed using a spike-shape classification system consisting of eight distinct event categories, including low sharp, high sharp, increasing, decreasing, plateau, high spike, overlap, and funky events. Although disk and nanotip biosensors produced comparable estimates of vesicular release content and global spike kinetics, detailed spikeshape classification revealed a geometry-dependent redistribution of the detected exocytotic event populations. Nanotip biosensors detected a significantly higher proportion of high sharp events and lower proportions of morphologically more complex full-release events and overlap events than disk biosensors. The reduction in complex full-release events was not driven by a single subtype but instead reflected distributed changes across multiple event categories. These findings demonstrate that electrode geometry can influence the apparent composition of the detected exocytotic spike populations without substantially altering estimates of vesicular release content or global spike kinetics. The results provide new insights into how nanoscale sensor geometry shapes electrochemical observations of neurotransmitter release and highlights the importance of considering biosensor geometry when interpreting single-cell exocytosis measurements.

papers.title: Photorelease of Anandamide at the Cell Plasma Membrane with Optically-Cleavable Targeted Ligands
papers.abstract: Anandamide (AEA) was the first endocannabinoid discovered to act on CB1 cannabinoid receptors, which are the primary target of the psychoactive compounds found in marijuana. AEA and cannabinoid signaling are ubiquitous throughout the body and are implicated in numerous physiological functions. However, AEA's precise effects on cell physiology and disease have been difficult to deconvolute due to its rapid metabolism, ability to activate multiple receptors on the cell surface and inside the cell, as well as its hydrophobicity, which makes AEA application slow and difficult to control. To overcome these limitations, Optically-Cleavable Targeted (OCT) ligands combine photopharmacology with protein tag bioconjugation. This approach enriches photocaged (inactive) ligands on the cell membrane expressing protein tags, and then releases the unmodified ligand with a flash of light. Here, we present hOCT-AEA for membrane-targeted AEA uncaging, which consists of a UV-A activated photocage masking an AEA ligand, attached to a chloroalkane moiety for covalent tethering to HaloTags. Using UV-Vis spectroscopy, we demonstrate that hOCT-AEA uncages with UV-A light but not longer wavelengths, making it compatible with fluorescence imaging applications. In cells, we found that hOCT-AEA released AEA on the plasma membrane and was capable of activating a CB1 receptor-derived fluorescent biosensor. Cannabinoid activation was dependent on UV-A stimulation and HaloTag tethering. This work represents the first membrane-targeted, optically controlled delivery of AEA to the plasma membrane and expands the OCT-ligand platform to encompass CB1 receptors, presenting a novel chemical biology tool to dissect cannabinoid signaling and physiology with enhanced spatiotemporal precision.

papers.title: Hydronium-Driven Concerted Ring-Opening: Deciphering the Structural Collapse of 2,2,6,6-Tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPO) in Aqueous Flow Batteries
Promoting N−N Bond Formation of Ammonia Oxidation by a Dangling Carboxylate Proton Relay
papers.abstract: Inspired by enzymatic proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) control, introducing proton relays into catalysts' second coordination sphere accelerates proton-transfer reactions, yet this strategy remains underexplored for N–H bond cleavage in ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR). Here, we report ammonia oxidation catalyzed by [Ru(pdc-κ-N 1 O 1 )(tpy)(NH 3 )] ( Ru(pdc-t)(NH 3 ) ; H 2 pdc = 2, 6-pyridinedicarboxylic acid; tpy = terpyridine), featuring a pendant carboxylate group, and its structural analog [Ru(pic)(tpy)(NH 3 )](PF 6 ) ( Ru(pic-t)(NH 3 ) ; Hpic = picolinic acid). Such a structural design creates a dangling carboxylate group as a proton relay, assisting the proton transfer during N− bond formation. Ru(pdc-t)(NH 3 ) exhibits superior AOR performance relative to Ru(pic-t)(NH 3 ) and previously reported [Ru(pdc-κ-N 1 O 2 )(bpy)(NH 3 )] ( Ru(pdc-b)(NH 3 ); bpy = bipyridine), with a catalytic rate of 209.7±12.2 s −1 (11.1-fold increase) and a turnover number (TON) of 319 for N 2 (4.2-fold increase). The calculated barrier for N−N bond formation for Ru(pdc-t)(NH 3 ) is +0.8 kcal/mol, which is significantly lower than the +7.8 kcal/mol barrier for Ru(pic-t)(NH 3 ) . This work demonstrates the promotional effect of a proton relay on the catalytic oxidation of ammonia to N 2 .

papers.title: Breaking Kinetic Symmetry: How Wet–Dry Cycling Ratchets Prebiotic Chemistry Far from Equilibrium
papers.abstract: Wet-dry cycling drives formation of biological oligomers from unactivated monomers, but the mechanism of directional accumulation has remained unclear. Low water activity and high monomer concentrations favor condensation; high water activity and low monomer concentrations favor hydrolysis. In the absence of directional bias, oscillations average to zero — systems orbit equilibrium and do not escape it. Using kinetic modeling of coupled condensation, hydrolysis, and exchange reactions among mercapto acids, hydroxy acids, and amino acids, we identify a chemical ratchet in which kinetic asymmetry between dry-phase condensation and exchange and wet-phase hydrolysis drives directional compositional change. In the dry phase, second-order exchange reactions are fast; in the wet phase, dilution suppresses them. This asymmetry gates flux directionally: thioesters and esters convert to amides, but not the reverse. The ratchet harvests free energy from environmental cycling to drive accumulation of condensation products. Chemical evolution on the ancient Earth must have been inherently directional — ratcheting small molecules into complex, functional biopolymers — before biological evolution could begin. We propose that chemical ratcheting is a prerequisite for the onset of biological evolution, serving as the bridge between stochastic chemistry and historical biology.

papers.title: Beyond the Spectral Shift: First-Principles Colorimetric Screening of Donor-Acceptor Copolymers as pH-Responsive Chromatic Indicators
papers.abstract: Color change upon change of pH is a key indicator for smart packaging that signals food spoilage. Donor-acceptor (D–A) conjugated copolymers are attractive candidates for such indicators, as their charge-transfer transitions are sensitive to protonation. A large spectral shift, however, does not necessarily translate translate into a perceived color change, and this relation remains relatively unexplored. In this study, we use DFT and TDDFT to screen 16 D–A copolymers from a 4×4 pairing of four donors and four acceptors, in their neutral, intermediate and fully protonated states using the oligomer approach. For each system we compute the protonation-induced abosrption shift and convert the spectra into perceived color through the CIE-1931/CIEDE2000 formula. For six representative systems spanning the full range of functional-sensitivity, we additionally perform a hole-electron analysis of the excited states to quantify the change in charge-transfer character upon protonation and to benchmark the performance of B3LYP against CAM-B3LYP. The peak shift depends almost entirely on the acceptor, but is by itself a poor predictor of the color change a human observer registers, as the largest shifts often fall in the near-infrared. B3LYP functional yields optical gaps closer to experiment than CAM-B3LYP, and DPP-based copolymers prove robust to functional choice, whereas the standing of the TPD- and BT/isoindigo-based systems is functional-sensitive. Hole-electron analysis reveals that B3LYP inflates excited-state charge separation in protonated IDT--BT and Carbazole--Isoindigo, while CAM-B3LYP is more conservative. Carbazole--BT emerges as the most promising candidate, showing a strong, easily perceptible color change with both functionals.

papers.title: QuantumPioneer: Scalable generation of quantum chemical data for solution-phase hydrogen transfer reactions
papers.abstract: High-fidelity quantum chemical (QM) datasets that jointly resolve reaction thermochemistry, kinetics, and solvation at scale remain scarce, especially for radical chemistry. We introduce QuantumPioneer, an open-access reaction-centered QM database and workflow for small organic molecules, focused on peroxyl-mediated hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and the corresponding homolytic bond dissociation reactions. QuantumPioneer contains 348,258 species (2–21 heavy atoms), 167,237 validated HAT transition states (TS) with corresponding reaction energies and homolytic bond dissociation energies (BDEs), and over 100 million COSMO-RS solvation free energies (∆Go_solv) and enthalpies (∆Ho_solv) across 295 solvents. The workflow uses ωB97X-D/def2-SVP geometries, DLPNO-CCSD(T)-F12d/def2-TZVP single-point energies, empirical thermochemical corrections, transition-state theory, and COSMORS BP-TZVPD-FINE solvation in a single high-throughput pipeline. Our benchmarks show reliable accuracy, with mean absolute errors compared to experimental data of 0.82 kcal/mol for gas-phase enthalpies of formation, 1.60 kcal/mol for C–H BDEs, 1.45 kcal/mol for HAT barriers, and 0.57 kcal/mol for ∆Go_solv values. We demonstrate two predictive applications. First, we show that a combined BDE and HAT-barrier model identifies experimentally observed oxidative degradation sites in drug-like molecules with a 91% top-5 hit rate and 80% site-level recall. Second, a QM-parameterized Abraham model enables rapid solvation energy estimates at near-COSMO-RS accuracy within its training domain, reproducing ∆Go_solv and ∆Ho_solv values with MAEs of 0.16 kcal/mol and 0.18 kcal/mol, respectively, though performance on experimental ΔGo_solv values for unseen solutes was worse, with MAEs of 1.32 kcal/mol, providing a scalable template for other reaction families, unifying equilibrium species, validated TS, thermochemistry, kinetics, and solvation into one workflow.

papers.title: Understanding the insertion/folding mechanism of penetratin forspecific lipid compositions by replica-exchange simulations
Scalable and Generalizable Analog Design via Learning Medicinal Chemistry Intuition from Matched Molecular Pair Transformations
papers.abstract: Chemical analog design in the hit-to-lead and lead optimization stages of drug discovery relies on systematic structural modifications often guided by medicinal chemistry intuition. Although a matched molecular pair (MMP) provides an interpretable framework to capture the intuition, models trained on individual MMP instances face significant limitations, such as bias toward frequent transformations in historical data. This work introduces a novel approach to transform the concept of ”how to design chemical analogs like a medicinal chemist” into a primary training objective for generative models by focusing on matched molecular pair transformations (MMPTs) as the fundamental unit of chemical modifications. This allows for a more generalizable and context-independent representation of medicinal chemistry intuition, enabling the application of the same transformation priors across different projects, regardless of the target or indication. Using a consistently curated ChEMBL-derived dataset, we compared a transformationcentric foundation model (MMPT-FM) with multiple MMP-based generative formulations trained on the same underlying data. Furthermore, performance is assessed through challenging within-patent and cross-patent real-world test cases derived from drug discovery patents. The MMPT-FM model achieves comparable or improved recall and novel metrics across all test cases, demonstrating particularly strong performance for low-frequency and previously unseen transformations This work not only shifts the paradigm of learning and utilizes medicinal chemistry intuition in an efficient and scalable manner in the AI for drug discovery era, but also establishes a significant competitive advantage by enabling the drug discover industry to encode decades of collective medicinal chemistry knowledge—both public and proprietary—into a scalable foundation generative model that could help researchers design chemical analogs.

papers.title: Scalable Low-Energy Molecular Conformer Generation with Quantum Mechanical Accuracy
papers.abstract: Understanding molecular geometry is crucial for biological activity and chemical reactivity; however, computational methods for generating 3D structures are limited by the vast scale of conformational space and the complexities of stereochemistry. We approach this problem with a method that combines a dataset of molecular conformers with generative diffusion models. We introduce ChEMBL3D, containing 280 million molecular geometries for 1.8 million drug-like compounds, optimized using AIMNet2 neural network potentials to a near-quantum mechanical accuracy with implicit solvent effects. This dataset captures organic molecules in various protonation states and stereochemical configurations. We then developed LoQI, a stereochemistry-aware diffusion model trained on ChEMBL3D. Through graph augmentation, LoQI generates molecular structures with targeted stereochemistry, an advance over prior generative methods. The model outperforms traditional approaches, achieving up to tenfold improvements in energy accuracy and effective recovery of optimal conformations. Benchmark tests on macrocycles, flexible molecules, and crystal structures confirm efficient low-energy conformer search.

papers.title: Dual cancer-selective lysosomally-targeted antibody–drug conjugates expand the ADC-druggable proteome
papers.abstract: Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) are standard-of-care therapies for many types of cancer, with an expanding representation in clinical development pipelines. 1 A key determinant of efficacy for most ADCs is their ability to internalize into the target cell and traffic to the lysosome, where the ADC payload is released. However, this internalization process is target- and antibody-dependent, limiting therapeutic results and ADC target scope. Here we extend the lysosome-targeting chimera (LYTAC) 2,3 concept to ADCs. We conjugated a lysosome-targeting polyspecific integrin-binding peptide (PIP) 4,5 to ADCs, generating lysosomally targeted ADCs (LytADCs). Across three targets (HER2, EGFR, CA9), two cancer cell lines (SKOV‑3, U-87 MG), and three payloads (MMAE, MMAF, Dxd), LytADCs were significantly more potent than the corresponding ADC in cell culture, 3D spheroid culture and in a murine xenograft model. Notably, the LytADC strategy converted an anti-CA9 ADC, a poor internalizer with no detectable cytotoxicity in 2D cell culture despite target expression, into a potent therapeutic in vitro and in vivo . LytADCs therefore expand the ADC-druggable target space to include cell surface antigens with poor intrinsic internalization properties.

papers.title: Mo(CO)₃(cht) as an air-stable precatalyst for highly Z-selective one-bond isomerization of terminal alkenes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT: The selective transposition of terminal alkenes to Z -2-alkenes remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report that the air-stable molybdenum(0) complex 2 (Mo(CO) 3 (cht)) serves as a highly efficient precatalyst when combined in a 1:1:1 ratio with tricyclohexylphosphine (PCy₃) and diphenyl phosphate (dpp). Under mild conditions (room temperature, 0.2 mol % catalyst) the system delivers >95 % conversion of 1-octene within five minutes and Z : E ratios exceeding 20:1, outperforming our previously reported Mo(CO)₄(pip)(PCy₃) system. Systematic variation of the phosphine ligand reveals that symmetrical, bulky monodentate phosphines (PCy₃, P( p -tolyl)₃) afford the optimal balance of activity and stereocontrol, whereas biaryl phosphines and the less sterically demanding P(Bn) 3 give diminished selectivity. Bidentate ligands (Xantphos, dppf) offer moderate conversion but do not match the 2 /PCy₃ benchmark. The catalyst exhibits high turnover numbers (TON >4500) and retains Z selectivity across a broad substrate scope, including functionalized alkenes, epoxides, and heteroatom-substituted olefins with reduced efficiency for strongly coordinating substrates. Kinetic investigations indicate a zero-order dependence on alkene concentration and a second-order dependence on total catalyst concentration. Collectively, these findings establish 2 /PCy₃/dpp as a general platform for the rapid, highly Z -selective isomerization of terminal alkenes.

papers.title: A Standard Machine-Learning Virtual Screening Pipeline Produces Candidates Indistinguishable From Random Drug-Like Compounds: A Quantitative Audit Using COX-2 As Case Study
papers.abstract: Motivation: Machine-learning (ML) virtual screening pipelines report strong retrospective benchmark performance (Pearson R > 0.8) and convert it into prioritized candidate lists. Whether those candidates dock better than random drug-like compounds against the actual target is rarely tested. We test it. Methods: Random Forest regressors were trained on COX-2 (CHEMBL230, n = 4,445; Pearson R = 0.756, RMSE = 0.81 pIC50) and COX-1 (CHEMBL221, n = 1,652; R = 0.682, RMSE = 0.72 pIC50) and applied to 249,455 ZINC250k compounds. Potency, Lipinski, solubility-window (−1 ≤ logP ≤ 3), and PAINS filters returned 42 candidates, each annotated with predicted COX-1 selectivity, Murcko scaffold, max-Tanimoto applicability-domain coverage, synthetic accessibility (SA), and BRENK alerts. All 42 candidates and a 100-compound random ZINC250k control (sampled before any ML scoring) were docked into the chain-A binding pocket of human COX-2 (PDB 1CX2) with AutoDock Vina. Celecoxib was redocked as positive control; pose recovery was scored by heavy-atom RMSD to the crystal ligand. Results: Celecoxib redocked at −11.23 kcal/mol with 0.63 Å RMSD to the crystal ligandprotocol valid. All 42 candidates docked successfully (Vina best −11.06, median −7.58, worst −3.63 kcal/mol; 11 reached ≤ −8.0); none beat celecoxib. 39 of 42 candidates (93%) lay outside the applicability domain (T ≥ 0.40; mean max-Tanimoto = 0.243). The candidate Vina distribution was statistically indistinguishable from the random baseline (Mann-Whitney p = 0.89; Welch p = 0.68; Cohen’s d = −0.08; Hodges–Lehmann shift −0.02 kcal/mol, 95% CI [−0.42,+0.34]). ML pIC50 and Vina rankings were uncorrelated (Spearman ρ = −0.086, 95% CI [−0.35,+0.20]). The top-20 ML-prioritized candidates engaged celecoxib’s pocket residues at parity with random ZINC (Val523: 16/20 vs. 16/20; mean contact recovery 0.73 vs. 0.66). A Vina-on-training validation showed that Vina at our settings did separate genuine ChEMBL COX-2 actives from random ZINC (actives median −8.40 vs. random −7.53 kcal/mol, p = 0.006)—yet the ML candidates docked at the random level (−7.58), not the actives level. Candidates were synthesizable (SA ≤ 5 for all 42, mean 3.01); 19/42 carried BRENK alerts. Conclusions: A standard Random Forest screen at R = 0.756 produces no candidate enrichment over random ZINC by any objective measure: no docking gain, no positive ML–Vina rank correlation, 93% out-of-domain prediction. Critically, the same docking oracle does separate genuine COX-2 actives from random ZINC—so the failure is a property of the ML candidate list, not of the evaluation. The benchmark R does not predict prospective hit-finding on cross-library screens. Applicability-domain coverage and a same-library random-baseline comparison should be mandatory reporting elements in ML virtual screening papers.

papers.title: Exploring Functional Patterns in Mass Spectrometry Imaging Data with Spatial Pathway and Chemical Class Analysis (SPCCA)
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) has enabled unprecedented advances in spatial mapping of metabolites and lipids within tissues. However, interpretation remains challenging when following common practice of visualizing one ion image at a time. To address this, we present a novel workflow for Spatial Pathway and Chemical Class Analysis (SPCCA), which applies single-sample pathway and chemical class scoring to MSI data. By integrating biological pathways from the Reactome database and chemical classes from the ChEBI resource, our Python-based framework transforms annotated MSI data into spatial maps based on biological function and chemical taxonomy. We illustrate the approach using MALDESI bladder cancer and DESI colorectal cancer datasets. Spatial Pathway Analysis (SPA) highlights known pathway connections despite sparse annotation coverage (~10%), while Spatial Chemical Class Analysis (SCCA) utilizes over 90% of filtered features, providing superior spatial congruence with H&E-defined histopathology. Our results demonstrate that SPCCA effectively recapitulates known cancer metabolic shifts and captures histological features in the original dataset, offering a robust and biologically grounded alternative to single-ion interpretation. This work highlights the potential of integrating biological and chemical knowledge into spatial metabolomics to enhance the depth and interpretability of MSI studies.

papers.title: Assembly of Membranized Coacervates through Transmembrane Peptides
An element-resolved coupled cluster atomization energy data set ranging across the periodic table
papers.abstract: We introduce the total atomization energy periodic table compass (TAE-PTComp), a collection of 67 atomization energy data sets, each specifically designed to probe various chemical environments of a characteristic element of the periodic table. In total, this set comprises 2,097 carefully curated closed-shell, single-reference molecules containing up to 50 atoms, with an average of 31 structures per element-specific subset. The chemical space covered ranges from conventional covalent and coordination compounds to noncovalently bound clusters, extracted fragments of periodic crystalline structures, and artificial "mindless" molecules. Additionally, we include a balanced amount of charged species with charges of ±1. For each molecule, as well as its constituent atoms (and ions), we provide high-level coupled cluster reference energies. We therefore envision this benchmark as a resource for parameter fitting, validation, and testing of approximate density functional theory methods, semi-empirical models, and machine-learning interatomic potentials. An initial assessment of TAE-PTComp for a representative set of density functional approximations, together with the semi-empirical g-xTB method and the machine-learned Universal Model for Atoms (UMA), shows that this benchmark can efficiently differentiate between broadly robust methods, such as the range-separated hybrid ωB97M-V, and approaches that exhibit localized, element-specific failures, such as the hybrid M06-2X functional.

papers.title: High-resolution MALDI imaging mass spectrometry of wholebody adult zebrafish
papers.abstract: We developed an optimized sample preparation workflow tailored for high-spatial resolution matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization imaging mass spectrometry (MALDI IMS) of adult zebrafish tissue. Zebrafish (Danio rerio) are an important model organism that would benefit from the development of molecular imaging approaches that allow comprehensive, spatially resolved analysis of multiple molecular species in a single experiment. However, imaging zebrafish tissue has been limited by challenges in preserving tissue morphology during sample preparation, particularly because swim bladders are prone to tearing. To address this, we established a MALDI IMS workflow suitable for both whole-body and organ-specific imaging using a single embedding strategy. We demonstrate the utility of this workflow by mapping lipid distributions along the zebrafish body-axis and within discrete brain regions. Whole-body imaging at 10 µm pixel size identified organ-specific lipid signatures, including PC(22:6_32:6) in the retina, 5a-cyprinol sulfate in gastrointestinal tissue, and sulfatide and plasmalogen species specific to nervous tissue. High-spatial resolution IMS of the brain (5 µm pixel size) followed by histological staining showed that sulfatide and plasmalogen species co-localize throughout the brain and are present in a small, specialized region corresponding to intertectal neurons. These findings establish a robust embedding strategy suitable for high-spatial resolution MALDI IMS in adult zebrafish, followed by additional staining of the same tissue section for multimodal imaging.

papers.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies structurally novel, parasite-selective inhibitors of Plasmodium falciparum dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
papers.abstract: Background. Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) is a clinically validated antimalarial target: Plasmodium falciparum depends on de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis and, unlike the human host, cannot salvage pyrimidines. The leading inhibitor chemotype — the triazolopyrimidine DSM series — has advanced to clinical development, but documented resistance motivates the discovery of structurally distinct chemical matter. Methods. We assembled a structure-based virtual screening pipeline against P. falciparum DHODH (Pf DHODH; PDB 7L01) that couples molecular docking (smina, Vinardo scoring) with a native-pharmacophore interaction-fingerprint filter, an enforced structural-novelty constraint, a parasite-versus-human selectivity comparison (human DHODH, PDB 6CJF), and a resistance-liability annotation. The pipeline was benchmarked against 205 known potent actives and 200 property-matched, topologically distinct decoys before screening a library of 1,200 drug-like compounds. Results. Native-ligand redocking reproduced the crystallographic pose to 1.28 Å RMSD, confirming a geometrically correct setup. Docking score alone enriched actives only weakly (Vina ROC-AUC 0.60; Vinardo 0.64), but requiring a contact to the native pharmacophore anchors Arg265 or His185 raised enrichment to ROC-AUC 0.70. Applying this benchmarked protocol to the screening library returned 134 structurally novel, drug-like hits spanning 125 Murcko scaffolds (all Tanimoto < 0.4 to any known active). Among the top 25 hits, all were predicted to bind Pf DHODH more tightly than the human ortholog (selectivity Δ −0.3 to −2.4 kcal/mol), and five contacted none of six literature-associated resistance positions. The highest-ranked candidate, CHEMBL3794605, combined strong predicted Pf affinity (−11.5 kcal/mol), the largest selectivity margin (−2.4 kcal/mol), pharmacophore engagement, resistance-residue avoidance, and structural novelty. Conclusions. The pipeline nominates a diverse, parasite-selective, resistance-aware set of novel candidate Pf DHODH inhibitors and is offered as a reproducible lead-generation workflow. All results are computational predictions and require experimental validation.

papers.title: OPTIMIZATION OF WASTE ENGINE OIL REGENERATION USING ACID-ACTIVATED BENTONITE
papers.abstract: The conditions for deep acid activation of natural bentonite have been substantiated, and its effectiveness in the process of regenerating waste engine oil has been investigated. It has been established that the modification leads to a radical restructuring of the mineral structure due to partial destruction of the octahedral layer and complete ion exchange. According to chemical analysis, the content of the framework-forming SiO2 increased from 56.23 % to 70.15 %, while the concentration of aluminum and iron oxides decreased by half. Alkali and alkaline earth components (CaO, Na2O) were completely removed, which caused a shift in the suspension pH to 3.1, an increase in specific surface area to 252 m2/g, and pore volume to 0.48 cm 3 /g. The high adsorption capacity of the obtained sorbent in the purification of waste engine oil with an acid number of 2.5 mg KOH/g and a transparency of 52 % has been proven. Using mathematical modeling, the optimal regeneration parameters were determined: sorbent dose 6–8 g/100 ml, time 35–45 min, and temperature 55-60 ° C. Under these conditions, a reduction in acidity to 0.23 mg KOH/g and an increase in transparency to 92 % are achieved. The chemisorption selectivity of the sorbent for thermo-oxidation products while fully preserving the base hydrocarbon matrix of the petroleum product was confirmed by IR spectroscopy.

papers.title: Straightforward structure determination of beam-sensitive low-symmetry compounds at room temperature by precession SerialED
papers.abstract: SerialED is acknowledged as an easily automatable alternative to 3DED, especially promising for the structure elucidation of very beam sensitive samples, like pharmaceuticals, porous framework materials for catalysis and macromolecules. Yet, SerialED in TEM, as an alternative to synchrotron SerialXRD, has been successfully applied to sub-micrometric crystals only for structures with high symmetry, generally cubic or tetragonal. Several authors have proposed combining SerialED with sample rotation, for increasing data redundancy and facilitating indexation routines. However, this approach undermines the very principle of serial crystallography, which implies the acquisition of a single diffraction snapshot per crystal, to avoid any beam damage effect. Here, we show that collecting proper SerialED data with a precessing electron beam drastically improves the quality of reflection intensities, allowing straightforward structure determination and refinement of inorganic and organic materials with symmetry as low as monoclinic. For beam-sensitive materials, data collected at room temperature guarantee accuracy far superior to the accuracy attainable by 3DED, even without the application of algorithms for reflection clustering and rescaling.

papers.title: Practical One-pot Synthesis of Cyclic Conjugated Amides from Ketones
papers.abstract: Conjugated amides are valuable building blocks in organic synthesis; however, general access to cyclic conjugated amides remains limited, restricting their broader use in method development and complex molecule synthesis. Herein, we report a practical one-pot synthesis of cyclic conjugated amides directly from readily available ketones. The transformation employs bromoform, an amine nucleophile, and 1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU), and is proposed to proceed through carbene-mediated homologation followed by in situ trapping of an acyl halide intermediate. A range of cyclic ketones and amines is converted into the corresponding conjugated amides in moderate to very good yields, including substrates bearing protected heterocycles, ether functionality, and alkyl or aryl substituents. The method also provides access to selected linear conjugated amides from acyclic ketones, including 1,1-disubstituted derivatives.

papers.title: Biophysical Descriptors of Single Protein Domains
papers.abstract: Quantitative relationships among geometric and surface-chemical descriptors of single-domain proteins remain insufficiently characterized, despite their relevance for interpreting structural datasets and modeling biomolecular interactions. Using a curated, non-redundant set of 614 single-domain proteins, we analyze the hydrophobic fraction of the solvent-accessible surface area ( SASA H ), charged surface fractions ( SASA + and SASA − ), size measures, secondary-structure content, and shape descriptors derived from high-resolution meshes. SASA H exhibits a narrow, reproducible range (0.45–0.65), whereas SASA + and SASA − follow similar Gaussian-like distributions but centered near 0.1, indicating conserved patterns of hydrophobic exposure and surface charge. Correlation analysis reveals strong interdependence among size descriptors and an inverse relationship between sphericity and surface roughness. A minimal, near-orthogonal set—mass, sphericity, SASA H , net charge, and helical content—captures the dataset’s essential variation with minimal redundancy. This framework provides geometry-aware descriptors for analyzing large collections of predicted structures, including those generated by AlphaFold, and offers physically interpretable parameters for protein comparison, coarse-grained modeling, and the design of domains with tailored surface properties.

papers.title: Deciphering the anion dynamics in the fully deuterated pyridinium-based ionic liquid [C5Py][NTf2] via 19F fast field cycling NMR relaxometry and MD simulation
papers.abstract: Fast Field Cycling (FFC) NMR relaxometry allows the investigation of molecular dynamics over a broad frequency range from 10 kHz up to 100 MHz. However, quantitative data interpretation is often limited by system-specific motional models and simplified assumptions for the analytical form of the relevant time correlation functions. Here, we propose a different “quasi first principles” based approach utilizing atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to predict frequency dependent relaxation rates based on the time evolution of the dipolar spin-spin interactions. The combination of MD simulations with the analytical Hwang-Freed (HF) theory allows us to accurately describe the low-frequency behavior of the intermolecular relaxation. We show that the theory asymptotically converges with the MD data at long times, providing a physically consistent description of intermolecular relaxation over many orders of magnitude in frequency. As a proof of concept for a complex ionic liquid (IL), we investigate the temperature-dependent 19 F NMR relaxation of a fully deuterated IL 1-(n-pentyl)-pyridinium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide [C 5 Py-d 16 ][NTf 2 ]. Deuteration suppresses heteronuclear 1 H- 19 F relaxation pathways, restricting the system to a single NMR-active nucleus. Using this framework, we determine both the intermolecular and intramolecular 19 F relaxation rates and additionally disentangle internal CF 3 rotations from overall anion tumbling motions. Our simulations highlight the importance of so-called “eccentricity” effects for the intermolecular relaxation rate caused by mutual reorientations of adjacent ions. Despite the limitations of molecular models, the predicted frequencydependent relaxation rates are in reasonable agreement with the experimentally measured FFC NMR data.

papers.title: Genetically-targeted and red-emitting fluorescent indicators for subcellular zinc imaging
papers.abstract: The concentration of biologically relevant metal cations can be monitored with subcellular precision thanks to chemogenetic fluorescent indicators that combine a small molecular probe with a recombinant protein tag but, despite a few reported examples emitting in the blue/green range, genetically-encoded indicators for Zn 2+ remain underexplored. Using a combination of rational and theoretical design, we report a series of hybrid fluorescent zinc indicators based on a hemicyanine scaffold with red fluorescence emission. The photoinduced electron transfer (PeT) underlying the sensing mechanism was studied by TD-DFT calculations to guide the probe design, leading to the development of two zinc indicators HemiZin-2 and HemiZin-3 , that were successfully used to detect exogenously applied zinc in live cells by confocal microscopy with subcellular resolution. This study evidences the complementarity between the rational design and the theoretical calculations to fast-track the probe design. It also emphasizes the importance of the interaction with HaloTag that strongly improves the brightness of the viscosity-sensitive hemicyanine and can also be used to fine-tune the affinity of the resulting complex, opening new possibilities for the design of genetically-encoded PeT-based metal cation sensors.

papers.title: Why a Single Mutation Dims the Light: Local Chromophore Organization Modulates Fluorescence in smURFP
papers.abstract: Predicting mutation-induced photophysical changes in bilin-binding fluorescent proteins remains challenging. Here, we investigate the origin of fluorescence modulation in smURFP and its lowfluorescent-quantum-yield Y56R variant using classical MD simulations and QM/MM calculations. Comparison of multiple chromophore binding states supports a wild-type configuration involving A-ring attachment and chromophore reduction, whereas Y56R adopts the opposite orientation, revealing substantial plasticity of the chromophore pocket in response to a single mutation. The experimentally observed differences in fluorescence efficiency and absorption energy arise not from simple global rigidification, but from redistribution of local steric confinement and electrostatic polarization across the biliverdin scaffold. Overall, our results highlight how spatially-resolved steric and electrostatic descriptors extracted from classical MD simulations can provide mechanistic insight into biliprotein photophysics

papers.title: Correlating the distribution of site energies, activation energies and saddle point energies in the energy landscape of a lithium borate glass
papers.abstract: Long range transport of ions in a solid electrolyte is subject to the potential energy landscape in which local hopping of ions occurs. Local hopping occurs between neighboring sites (energy minima). It involves passing a local saddle point implying the concept of local activation energy. Here, we elaborate a direct comparison of the populated part of a site energy distribution (PSED) derived from CAIT with a distribution of activation energies g(Ea) derived from NMR. This provides information on the relevant distribution of saddle points (SPD).

papers.title: Designer Pseudopeptide for In Situ Liquid Crystal Gelation toward Smart Window Applications
papers.abstract: Supramolecular self-assembly serves as a fundamental backbone for designing multifunctional gel materials. A simpler diphenylalanine (Phe-Phe) sequence has been strategically modified with distinct terminal functional groups, namely, tert-butoxycarbonyl (Boc) and trifluoromethyl (CF 3 ), to investigate their role in the gelation of liquid crystal (LC) media. Notably, CF 3 -functionalized Phe-Phe exhibits efficient gelation characteristics in nematic and cholesteric LCs. This is due to enhanced molecular packing and efficient fibrous self-assembly, aided by the pronounced hydrophobic character of the CF 3 group. In contrast, Boc-protected Phe-Phe remains non-gelating under identical conditions due to the bulky Boc group causing steric hindrance and impeding LC-based gel-assembly. Polarizing optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, rheology, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy well characterize the prepared LC gels. The electrically switching ability of LC molecules is harnessed for controlling the transmittance in the LC-gel media and utilized for developing smart window devices. The contrast ratio, threshold voltage, operating voltage, rise and fall time, and haze of the smart windows are optimized by varying the concentration of pseudopeptide-based gelator in LCs. The cholesteric LC gel, even at a lower gelator concentration than in nematic gels, achieved a ~3.4-fold higher contrast ratio and enhanced haze while operating at comparable voltage, though at the cost of slightly slower switching times.

papers.title: GraPAS: Gradient-Matched Probabilistic Analytical Spectroscopy Denoiser for Self-Supervised Photoacoustic Signal Recovery in Analytical Chemistry
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) is a powerful analytical chemistry technique that combines optical absorption selectivity with acoustic detection sensitivity, enabling non-destructive characterization of chemical species in complex matrices. However, the acquired PAS signals are inevitably contaminated by thermal noise, electronic noise, mechanical vibration, and sample heterogeneity, while existing denoising methods either rely on hand-crafted basis functions that generalize poorly or require paired clean references that are almost impossible to obtain in real chemical scenarios. In this work, we propose GraPAS, a self-supervised deep learning framework that unifies four complementary modules for PAS denoising and quantitative analysis: an Analytical Prior Constraint (APC) module that encodes frequency-and wavelet-domain structural priors as differentiable constraints, a Probabilistic Noise Modeling (PNM) module that leverages Gumbel-prior reparameterization to fit non-Gaussian chemical noise, a Gradient-matching Selfsupervision (GMS) module that distills knowledge between teacher and student denoisers via gradient alignment without clean labels, and a Multimodal Attention (MMA) module that fuses PAS signals with synchronously captured spectral images. We construct ChemPAS-2K, a dataset of 2,000 noisy photoacoustic signals spanning five representative chemical scenarios including lithium-sulfur battery polysulphide diffusion, beta-FeOOH photo-Fenton catalysis, desalination conductivity monitoring, trace gas detection, and biological tissue characterization. Experiments on ChemPAS-2K and the public SPADE-Bench show that GraPAS consistently outperforms classical and supervised deep learning baselines across five noise levels, achieving 19.86 dB SNR with only 3.6 ms inference latency, while requiring no paired clean labels and retaining 96.7 percent of full-data performance with only 25 percent of the training data.

papers.title: Autonomous Multi-Agent Reconstruction of Prebiotic Reaction Networks Reveals Organizational Features of Amino Acid Synthesis
papers.abstract: Decades of origin-of-life research have uncovered hundreds of prebiotically plausible reactions across hydrothermal, surface, and biochemical environments, yet this knowledge remains fragmented across chemistry, geochemistry, and astrobiology. Here we present ASTRA, a multi-agent AI system that reconstructs prebiotic reaction networks for biomolecular targets by integrating autonomous literature synthesis, reaction network construction, and iterative mechanistic evaluation. Applied to the twenty canonical amino acids, ASTRA reconstructed 286 reaction networks encompassing 2,850 plausible pathways and 4,513 reactions, more than 92% of which are not represented in existing curated databases of prebiotic reaction pathways. Across these networks, ASTRA identifies recurrent organizational features of prebiotic amino acid synthesis, including shared network hubs, shared intermediate building blocks, and environment-dependent molecular properties. For literature-sparse targets such as histidine and tryptophan, ASTRA reconstructs pathways grounded in published experiments, identifies missing mechanistic links, and generates explicit, testable bridging hypotheses. These results reveal system-level organization in prebiotic amino acid synthesis and demonstrate how autonomous scientific agents can accelerate the reconstruction and exploration of chemical evolution.

papers.title: One-Step Access to Ultra-Bright Macrocyclic Oligo-BODIPYs Featuring Long-Lived Cyclic Excitons
papers.abstract: The controlled organization of chromophores into defined assemblies with collective photophysical properties is a key concept for natural and artificial photonic systems. A template-free, one-step synthesis affords a series of methylene-bridged macrocyclic oligo-BODIPYs from readily available BODIPY precursors. Brønsted acid catalysis with paraformaldehyde as a C1 synthon links multiple BODIPY cores into β-connected linear oligomers and macrocycles comprising up to twelve non-conjugated chromophores. Optical spectroscopy and quantum chemical calculations provide first insights into the photophysical mechanisms: steady-state and timeresolved spectroscopy reveal pronounced excitonic coupling across the chromophore arrays, which is confirmed by quantum chemical investigations at the simplified time-dependent density functional theory level. The linear oligomers display typical J-type characteristics, while the macrocyclic systems exhibit distinct multiband emission and unusual size-dependent photophysical properties. Distinct excitonic regimes coexist in the macrocyclic oligomers. Intense absorption bands seem to originate from localized J-coupled chromophore segments within the ring, while fluorescence can occur from J-coupled segments and a lower-lying cyclic exciton state with strongly reduced oscillator strength. In summary, our work establishes cyclic oligo-BODIPYs as a versatile platform for investigating topology-dependent excitonic phenomena, and also for developing functional superchromophores with tunable photophysical properties.

papers.title: WHERE TO CUT, HOW DEEP: BPE AND UNIGRAM-LM ON CHEMISTRY SMILES
papers.abstract: Every chemical language model reading SMILES begins with a tokenizer, yet the field has inherited byte-pair encoding (BPE) from natural language with little scrutiny. In natural language, BPE’s principal alternative, Unigram-LM, is known to build structurally different vocabularies. Whether that contrast survives in chemistry was open: the complete glyph base already covers every conformant molecule, so the learned pieces add compression rather than coverage, and a tiny alphabet under hard valence constraints could drive two frequency-based algorithms to converge. We report a controlled comparison of BPE and Unigram-LM over a fixed 165-token chemistry base, at the small vocabulary sizes where token embeddings are learnable, across three corpus typologies (diverse, drug-like, natural-products) and both pre-tokenization boundary policies. The two do not converge. In all 22 matched conditions they build near-disjoint subword vocabularies: cross-algorithm Jaccard overlap on the learned pieces above the shared base never exceeds 0.161, and at most 0.05 once weighted toward the high-frequency pieces a model updates most. Unigram-LM also segments held-out molecules into 29–41% more tokens; the arms largely agree on where to cut but not how deeply, so BPE’s segmentation is a strict coarsening of Unigram-LM’s on 80–99% of molecules. The separation holds across corpus, boundary, and vocabulary size, persisting even at eight times that scale, past where embeddings remain learnable; only token-frequency imbalance attenuates in magnitude, shrinking with vocabulary size and most on the natural-products corpus, without closing.

papers.title: Chalcogen-Controlled Triplet Harvesting in Benzophenone-Derived Chromophores: A Theoretical Investigation of Excited-State Relaxation Pathways
papers.abstract: Efficient triplet-state harvesting in organic chromophores is governed by a delicate interplay between excited-state energetics, orbital character, spin–orbit coupling, and vibronic relaxation pathways. Here, we present a systematic theoretical investigation of chalcogen substitution in benzophenone-derived chromophores, in which the carbonyl oxygen is progressively replaced by sulfur and selenium. Three molecular families were examined: benzophenone, Michler’s ketone, and 4,4′-dinitrobenzophenone, together with their thio-and seleno-analogues. Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) calculations were employed to characterize excited-state energetics, natural transition orbital (NTO) characters, spin–orbit coupling matrix elements, vibronic reorganization parameters, and the rate constants associated with fluorescence, phosphorescence, internal conversion, and intersystem crossing. Chalcogen substitution is found to systematically stabilize the low-lying excited states, producing pro- nounced red shifts in the lowest absorption bands and substantially reducing singlet–triplet energy separations. Simultaneously, the heavier chalcogen atoms markedly enhance spin–orbit coupling, leading to dramatic increases in intersystem crossing rates. In the parent ben- zophenone series, the calculated rate increases by more than five orders of magnitude from benzophenone to its selenium analogue. While the oxygen-containing Michler’s ketone and 4,4′-dinitrobenzophenone derivatives exhibit excited-state decay dominated by internal conversion, sulfur and selenium substitution switches the dominant relaxation pathway to ISC, resulting in near-quantitative triplet-state population. NTO analysis reveals that the lowest singlet excited states are predominantly of (𝑛𝜋∗) character, whereas the triplet states involved in the dominant ISC pathways generally possess substantial (𝜋𝜋∗) character, creating favorable El-Sayed-allowed spin-conversion channels. The results demonstrate that chalcogen substitu- tion simultaneously tunes excited-state energetics, orbital character, and spin–orbit coupling, providing an effective molecular design strategy for enhancing triplet harvesting in metal-free organic chromophores.

papers.title: Photocatalytic and Copper-Catalyzed 1,3-Aminoarylation of Aryl Cyclopropanes: Complementary Mechanistic Strategies for Synthesizing 3,3‑Diarylpropylamines
papers.abstract: A regioselective 1,3-aminoarylation of aryl cyclopropanes is reported through two complementary catalytic strategies based on distinct reactivity. First, photoactivation of N-chloro-N-(phenylsulfonyl)benzenesulfonamide (NCBSI) enables a rapid and efficient 1,3-aminochlorination of aryl cyclopropanes. This transformation could be combined with a Friedel–Crafts arylation in a two-step, one-pot sequence, affording the corresponding arylated products bearing electron-rich arenes. Second, a copper-catalyzed protocol was developed, allowing direct 1,3-aminoarylation using electron-deficient aryl boronic acids as coupling partners. Mechanistic studies provide insight into the distinct reaction pathways underlying these complementary approaches. Together, these methodologies display broad functional group tolerance and provide access to 3,3-diarylpropylamines, valuable medicinally relevant motifs, in a one-pot process involving both C–N and C–C bond formation.

papers.title: Three-color Photopharmacology: Chromatically Orthogonal Visible-Light Photocages for Optical Control of Adrenergic Receptors
papers.abstract: Photopharmacology enables precise optical control of biological function through lightresponsive ligands, yet multiplexed photocontrol has been constrained by limited wavelength selectivity and reliance on UV-activated photocages. Here we report a three-color photopharmacological platform based exclusively on visible-light-responsive photocages that enables sequence-independent photorelease of multiple ligands. By combining the diethylaminocoumarin (DEAC) photocage with the xanthenium photocages RX540 and CX640, we establish a chromatically orthogonal uncaging system addressable with standard 405, 488, and 638 nm light sources. The three photocages exhibit minimal spectral overlap, high dark stability, watersolubility, rapid photolysis, and >90% chromatic selectivity (i.e., chromatic orthogonality) in multicomponent mixtures, enabling independent payload release irrespective of irradiation order. We apply this strategy to photocaged agonists and antagonists of the α1A-adrenergic receptor and demonstrate wavelength-selective receptor activation and inhibition in mammalian cells through calcium imaging. Dual-color combinations permit programmable agonist/antagonist sequencing, while three-component systems retain wavelength selectivity in cellular environments. This work establishes the first ternary visible-light photocage combination for sequence-independent photorelease in living cells and provides a general strategy for multiplexed optical control of endogenous GPCR signaling using standard confocal microscopy. The combination of visible- 3 light activation, chromatic orthogonality, and compatibility with native receptors might offer new opportunities for studying complex signaling networks with high spatiotemporal precision.

papers.title: Arginine tuning of coiled-coil peptides yields single-domain nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Programming three-dimensional order in peptide-based materials requires lateral interactions that are precise enough to propagate over hundreds of nanometres, yet robust enough to operate in water. Here, we show that a rationally designed coiled-coil peptide meets both demands by assembling into a hierarchical suprahelix that promotes spontaneous crystallisation under physiological buffer conditions. Coiled-coil dimers wind around one another to generate the higher-order suprahelix. Subtle lysine-to-arginine substitutions tune lateral cohesion, revealing a non-monotonic dependence on arginine density: 46-residue peptides with three or six arginine residues form ellipsoidal nanocrystals, whereas arginine-free or arginine-rich variants form amorphous aggregates. Time-resolved spectroscopy and cryogenic electron microscopy show that crystallisation proceeds by a non-classical pathway, in which condensed protofibrils align before consolidating into an ordered lattice. Cryo-electron tomography supports the single-domain nature of the resulting nanocrystals, and three-dimensional electron diffraction shows that both crystalline variants adopt the same near hexagonal unit-cell metrics. These findings translate a principle from protein crystallography, that arginine favours crystal contacts relative to lysine, into a sequence-level design parameter for coiled-coil nanocrystallization, providing a route to programmable three-dimensional order in soft molecular materials.

papers.title: Where do proteomics people come from?
papers.abstract: The field of proteomics is one of the fastest growing scientific disciplines in the world today. Beginning in 2020, ambitious market predictions anticipated proteomics to more than double in market size in 4-6 years, and to even surpass the well-established genomic sciences industry in 8-12 years. While the market is still growing, it has not come close to matching these initial projections. To better understand the root cause of this I have collected field surveys and direct interviews of over 200 scientists actively involved in proteomics research today. While ultimately incomplete, it is worth noting that over 68% of respondents received their technical training in proteomics during either doctoral or postdoctoral training. In stark contrast, only 4.3% obtained training during their undergraduate education. Given the 5.7-to-9.4-year average cycle for traditional doctoral and post-doctoral training in the life sciences, it appears the limiting factor in growing the proteomics field may be linked directly to current practices in training a qualified workforce.

papers.title: SEA WASTE GOLD: NOVEL HYDROPHOBIC TO HYDROPHILIC SWITCHABLE DEEP EUTECTIC SOLVENTS FOR THE SELECTIVE EXTRACTION AND RECOVER OF ASTAXANTHIN FROM BLUE CRAB SHELL
papers.abstract: Callinectes sapidus crab, commonly known as blue crab, is an invasive species known for its easy adaptability, high reproduction rate and aggressive behaviour. Its meat is edible and widely used in food industry, so its use is directly linked to a high production of waste due to its abundant shell. This work aims to selectively recover astaxanthin from blue crab shells with the use of novel hydrophobic to hydrophilic Switchable Deep Eutectic Solvents (SDESs). Astaxanthin is a relevant carotenoid known for its biological beneficial properties such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardiovascular protection activities. The novel SDESs are based on phenylacetic acid, a natural occurring edible molecule, mixed with a set of different edible molecules giving DESs liquids. The selectivity and efficacy of the optimized extraction procedure, the switchable property of the liquids and the edibility of the SDESs components render this procedure a promising green alternative for astaxanthin production from waste.

papers.title: Chemometric exploration of multispectral fluorescence landscapes for dried fruit extracts profiling
papers.abstract: The food industry requires rapid, reliable, and cost-effective analytical methods for quality and production process control. Fluorescence spectroscopy, combined with chemometric methods, offers a promising alternative to more complex analytical approaches due to its simplicity, accessibility, and low operational costs. This study investigates the applicability of excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectroscopy (multispectral fluorescence) coupled with chemometric analysis for the characterization and classification of dried apple and orange extracts obtained through different dehydration methods. Dried apple and orange extracts were prepared using three osmotic solutions: sucrose solution (SU), rosehip juice concentrate (RH), and cherry juice concentrate with xylitol (CH). Osmotic dehydration was assisted by pulsed electric field (PEF) and ultrasound (US) treatments. Fluorescence EEMs were acquired and then analyzed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Parallel Factor Analysis (PARAFAC), and Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA). The results showed that both the type of osmotic solution and the assisted dehydration method influenced the fluorescence characteristics of the samples. PCA and PARAFAC revealed similarities and differences among the dried apple and orange extracts and enabled the identification of major fluorescent components and their relative contributions. Furthermore, classification models based on PARAFAC-PLS-DA and unfolded PLS-DA achieved satisfactory accuracy and low classification errors, allowing reliable discrimination of fruit extracts according to the applied processing conditions. These findings highlight the potential of multispectral fluorescence spectroscopy, combined with chemometric methods, as a rapid and effective tool for assessing the quality of dried fruit extracts and classifying processed fruit products.

papers.title: Proteomics as an Emerging Tool for Understanding Biotransformation and Toxicological Impacts of Contaminants
papers.abstract: Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics is rapidly advancing, becoming fast, affordable, and increasingly accessible to environmental scientists. This perspective outlines how proteomics can illuminate biotransformation processes and sublethal organism-level effects, and highlights future opportunities enabled by emerging technologies. Our goal is to give a concise overview on realistic expectations of current capabilities while inspiring scientists to adapt and develop novel proteomic approaches addressing fundamental questions in contaminant science.

papers.title: RESEARCH ARTICLE Fast Isotopic [18F]Fluoride Exchange in Iminosulfur Oxydifluorides and Triflimidoyl Fluorides: A novel approach for [18F]tagging of primary amine-derived precursors
papers.abstract: Direct incorporation of fluorine-18 into primary amine- derived molecules remains a major challenge in radiochemistry. Current strategies largely rely on multistep conjugation of electrophilic prosthetic groups, limiting automation and generating significant waste. Herein, we report a general and ultrafast 19 F- 18 F isotopic exchange on iminosulfur oxydifluorides and triflimidoyl fluorides, two Sulfur-Fluorine exchange (SuFEx) derived motifs readily accessible from primary amines. The reaction proceeds within seconds and tolerates a broad range of functionalities. Additionally, the method was successfully automated on commercial modules, and radiolabelled molecules were isolated through simple cartridge purification, with high molar activity, further highlighting the potential of this methodology for streamlined and more sustainable radiotracer production. Finally, we carried out chemical and biological stability studies showing that [ 18 F]iminosulfur oxydifluorides resist in vivo metabolism and can be employed as radiolabelled synthons for PET imaging.

papers.title: CACHE Challenge #4: Targeting the TKB Domain of the E3 ligase CBLB, an Immuno-Oncology Target
papers.abstract: The Critical Assessments of Computational Hit-finding Experiments (CACHE) are prospective benchmarking exercises where small molecule ligands predicted for a nominated protein of interest are procured and tested experimentally. In CACHE #4, 23 participating teams each selected up to 100 compounds designed to bind the E3 ligase CBLB, an immuno-oncology target. The organizers released the first public structure of CBLB in complex with a known ligand at the outset of the challenge to enable the discovery of chemically novel molecules. Out of the 1,688 compounds collectively predicted, ten compounds from nine participants showed some sign of activity (primary hits), but only two were convincingly confirmed (validated hits) across multiple biophysical binding assays and in subsequent analogs, and only one of them was chemically novel. The apparent difficulty of finding novel CBLB ligands, previously reflected by the chemical similarity of inhibitors from the patent literature, suggests that potent CBLB hit molecules were either rare in the screened commercial libraries, or that computational methods may have struggled to retrieve presumably present but weak ligands, or that the conformational dynamics of the binding site was not sufficiently accounted for. The successful method was strikingly atypical. Selection from a chemical binding similarity classifier followed by a Random Forest binding affinity predictor trained on inhibitors from the patent literature were refined using a diffusion-model binding pose predictor. The road to an ML-driven breakthrough in computational hit-finding can take unexpected turns. Which of these turns reveal novel horizons and which are mere distractions will best be investigated and answered collectively. The discovery in CACHE #4 of a novel series of CBLB ligands is not a trivial achievement and may inform medicinal chemistry efforts towards clinical candidates that complement immune checkpoint inhibition to elicit antitumor immune response in cancer patients.

papers.title: Systematic Expansion of Chemical Reaction Space from Graph-Based Model Reactions
papers.abstract: Computational kinetic modeling relies on accurate transition-state geometries and activation barriers. While machine learning models trained on ab initio data have shown promise for transition-state search and barrier prediction, they often struggle to generalize to out-of-domain reactions due to biases and uneven coverage of reaction space in existing datasets. To address this challenge, we introduce a dataset of 12,030 actual reactions (ARs) derived from 452 model reactions (MRs), which are sampled from an extensive, heuristic-free, graph-based reaction template database. The dataset includes DFT-optimized transition-state geometries and thermochemistries and is designed to improve model transferability by systematically expanding chemically relevant reaction space around shared reactive cores. We also provide an automated workflow to generate this dataset, enabling broader use and extension by the community. Finally, we benchmark MR activation barriers as surrogates for AR barriers and present a case study demonstrating that AR augmentation improves machine-learning performance, highlighting the value of structured reaction-space expansion for kinetic modeling.

papers.title: A Nickel-Olefin Pincer Complex as Catalyst for Aldehyde Hydrogenation under Mild Conditions via a Cooperative Mechanism
papers.abstract: The use of a Ni(0)-olefin pincer complex for the base-free catalytic hydrogenation of aldehydes under mild conditions is reported. Insights from DFT calculations complemented by isotope labeling experiments support an unusual H2 activation mechanism involving metal-ligand cooperation via ligand-to-ligand hydrogen transfer (LLHT) to the olefin moiety. In the case of the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl substrate cinnamaldehyde, the C=C bond is hydrogenated preferentially over the C=O bond, which can be assigned to a slower product-release step for C=O hydrogenation.

papers.title: Magnetic Fields Affect Hydroxyl Structure at the Interface of Water and Dysprosium-Treated Alumina
papers.abstract: Resolving magnetic field effects on surface and solution structure at the molecular scale is important to a range of applications, including synthesis, separations, and catalysis. We present direct evidence that paramagnetic rare earth element (REE) ions adsorbed onto alumina surfaces respond to magnetic fields by reorganizing interfacial water and hydroxyl structure. Vibrational sum-frequency generation (vSFG) spectroscopy showed that REE adsorption suppresses free aluminol intensity and increases hydrogen- bonded hydroxyls. Mapping the REE ion distribution revealed surface-bound domains correlated with the underlying alumina lattice. When a 1 T magnetic field was applied, dysprosium-treated alumina interfaces experienced pronounced hydroxyl restructuring, including suppression of free hydroxyls, reorganization of weakly hydrogen-bonded species, and increased ordering and adsorption of strongly hydrogen-bonded hydroxyls. Magnetic-field effects were absent for lanthanum-treated alumina and other non-magnetic controls. Density functional theory simulations showed that Dy 3+ is likely to dynamically occupy inner- and outer-sphere adsorption states that induce long-range spin polarization in water and hydroxyls, substantially quenching its magnetic moment while perturbing hydrogen-bond networks across multiple solvation layers; a result validated by magnetometry measurements. This unexpected magnetic field effect on hydroxyl structure presents opportunities for controlling interfacial phenomena and energy landscapes at the molecular scale, beyond simply using magnets to affect mass transport.

papers.title: Ion Transport Enhancement in Charge-Regulating Hydrogels
papers.abstract: Weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels are emerging as a versatile platform for ion transport and separation, desalination, and energy applications. However, a predictive understanding how charge regulation influences ionic mobility in these polymer networks remains elusive. Here, using large-scale molecular simulations, we dissect the coupled mechanisms governing small-ion transport in weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels, and reveal how charge density, competitive binding, and dynamic charge regulation jointly control ion mobility. By systematically isolating these effects, we uncover a pronounced non-monotonic dependence of ion self-diffusion on hydrogel pKa and salt concentration for multivalent ions. Strikingly, allowing the hydrogel backbone to dynamically regulate its charge eliminates this non-monotonicity and leads to dramatic enhancements in ion mobility, with diffusion coefficients increasing by up to an order of magnitude for trivalent ions. We attribute this effect to a protonation-assisted hopping mechanism, which provides an additional pathway for ion unbinding beyond translational escape and accelerates ion-pair kinetics without affecting the fraction of free ions. Our results demonstrate that charge regulation can decouple ion mobility from equilibrium binding strength, offering a powerful design lever unavailable in fixed-charge materials. Building upon these insights, we propose simple molecular design principles for next-generation ionconducting hydrogels and suggest new strategies for membranes, energy materials, and biologically inspired charge-adaptive soft matter.

papers.title: Joint analysis of transfer coefficient and proton reaction order exposes kinetic relevance of elementary steps in electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Mechanistic analysis in heterogeneous electrocatalysis is currently rooted in one of two predominant approaches. Either (i) measured Tafel slopes near cardinal values (30, 40, 60, or 120 mV dec −1 ) are interpreted to reflect a single rate-determining step or (ii) non-cardinal Tafel slopes and reaction orders are fit by multi-step microkinetic models. While the cardinal approach is simple and intuitive, it is valid only in limiting regimes and neglects complexities such as multiple rate-determining steps and non-ideal surface isotherms. By contrast, microkinetic modeling can capture these complexities, but requires extensive parameterization and incurs significant computational cost. Here we bridge the two using the degree of rate control and elementary-step reversibility. We show that two routinely measured observables—the transfer coefficient and proton reaction order—are individually ambiguous but, together, exactly specify the rate control of chemical and electrochemical steps. We apply these developments to analysis of literature data for H 2 evolution, O 2 evolution, and CO electroreduction and demonstrate the facile identification of rate-determining step(s) and quantification of elementary-step symmetry factors at near-zero computational expense. In doing so, the developed framework transforms non-cardinal kinetic observables from aberrations to invaluable mechanistic descriptors that elicit otherwise elusive molecular-level information.

papers.title: Sisyphus: A Topology-Compiled Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Platform with Structure-Only Input and Bayesian Parameter Refinement
papers.abstract: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) platforms have achieved regulatory acceptance for drug–drug interaction and pediatric dose optimization, yet regulatory-grade use of the dominant implementations typically relies on experimentally measured or expert-curated absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) parameters, limiting their utility in early drug discovery when only molecular structure is available. Machine learning approaches that predict pharmacokinetic endpoints directly from structure address this constraint but lack mechanistic interpretability and cannot extrapolate to untested scenarios such as drug–drug interactions or alternative dosing regimens. Sisyphus, an open-source PBPK platform that represents the human body as a typed directed multigraph, automatically compiles ordinary differential equation (ODE) systems from graph topology, and accepts a simplified molecular-input line-entry system (SMILES) string as the sole molecular input, is presented here. Five quantitative structure–activity relationship models predict ADME parameters from molecular structure; these are propagated through a whole-body PBPK model with native Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification, and a four-track meta-learner combines mechanistic-engine, direct machine-learning, clearance-regression, and volume-of-distribution-based predictions using compound-class-adaptive weights with conditional volume-of-distribution activation. On a 107-drug retrospective benchmark (healthy volunteers, single oral dose, immediate-release, fasted state), the platform achieved a population-level geometric mean absolute fold error (AAFE) of 2.743 for maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), with 44.9% of predictions within 2-fold of observed values (bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI] [2.37, 3.20]; in-domain subset AAFE 2.791, N = 81, excluding applicability-domain-flagged compounds). This figure reflects the physics corrections and data-hygiene fixes described below—a corrected hepatic and gut clearance flux that restores the canonical first-pass extraction limit, an added paracellular (tight-junction) absorption pathway for small hydrophilic compounds, a leak-free clearance-training regeneration, and a single-path glucuronidation fix—each improving mechanistic or data fidelity, with externally anchored constants and none fitted to the benchmark. All reported benchmarks were generated from a fresh clone of the public repository with no proprietary or environment-specific data artifacts loaded, so the reported accuracy is structure-only and independently reproducible. Forty-eight enumerated optimization attempts—spanning alternative molecular representations, training-data expansion, in vitro–in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) chain bypass, bond-dissociation-energy reactivity features, residual-correction models, post-hoc meta-learners, and orthogonal prediction sources—failed to improve downstream accuracy, while two strategies improved it and are retained in the pipeline. These results indicate that the accuracy ceiling originates from intrinsic clearance prediction quality (coefficient of determination R² ≈ 0.24 on the Therapeutics Data Commons Hepatocyte_AZ dataset under scaffold-split cross-validation) rather than from model architecture or data scale. Substituting experimentally measured ADME parameters for predicted values in a 10-compound subset produced a mixed improvement in engine AAFE (2.85 to 2.37; 6 of 10 compounds improved), indicating that ADME input quality is one contributor to prediction error rather than establishing that the engine is fully input-limited. The platform additionally supports multi-dose regimen simulation, Bayesian posterior parameter refinement that reduced prediction uncertainty by an average of 86% from a single observation across five compounds, model-informed precision dosing that repositions the engine as a mechanistic prior updated by sparse measured data, drug–drug interaction prediction, and pharmacodynamic modeling. Prospective validation on 28 small-molecule new molecular entities (NMEs) approved in 2024–2025, re-scored on the current corrected engine, yielded AAFE 3.29 (N = 28; in-domain 3.32, N = 16), modestly worse than the retrospective benchmark; the gap was localized to systematic under-prediction of oral bioavailability for novel chemotypes rather than to clearance, and the first-pass correction did not reduce it (it deepened the out-of-distribution bioavailability deficit rather than removing it). Sisyphus addresses a capability not met by existing tools: a single platform spanning structure-only screening through observation-informed parameter refinement, in which mechanistic parameters retain physical meaning throughout the pipeline.

papers.title: Mucus Anchoring Protein (MAP) – Antibody Conjugates: A Strategy to Enhance Antiviral Efficacy
papers.abstract: Respiratory viruses initiate infections at the airway mucosa, where improved localization and retention of neutralizing antibodies at the infection interface may enhance antiviral activity under mucus-containing conditions. To enhance antibody interactions with mucus and therefore improve antiviral performance we introduce antibody mucus anchoring protein (mAb-MAP) conjugates, generated by late-stage chemical conjugation of antibodies with the mucus-binding protein Trefoil Factor 3 (TFF3). This strategy converts existing antibodies into mucus-interacting bioconjugates without genetic modification, and enhances their mucosal localization. Using the SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody Imdevimab, mAb-MAP conjugates displayed up to a five-order-of-magnitude increase in antiviral activity under mucus-containing conditions. Biophysical studies using fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) and single virus tracking (SVT) revealed increased antibody retention within mucin environments and a pronounced reduction in viral mobility. Collectively, the mAb-MAP concept provides a versatile and broadly applicable strategy to improve locally administered antibody therapeutics against respiratory infections.

papers.title: Data-Efficient and Fast Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics through Integrated Active Learning and Knowledge Distillation
papers.abstract: We develop data-efficient machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for fast molecular dynamics simulations, combining DeePMD and MACE models within an active learning and knowledge distillation framework. Using liquid water as a case study, we first independently train DeePMD and MACE models from scratch through active learning. We find that MACE requires around 3 times less training data than DeePMD, but its inference speed is 10 times lower. We also show that starting from a pretrained foundation model based on the MACE architecture further reduces the training data by a factor of 7, resulting in a fine-tuned foundation model with a 25 times data reduction compared to DeePMD. To overcome the limitation associated with the lower inference speed of MACE potentials, we next develop a knowledge distillation scheme to train a DeePMD potential from the fine-tuned foundation model through an inexpensive active learning workflow. The distilled model is generated with ~10 times less computer time than the DeePMD model trained from scratch, while showing the same fast inference speed. Comparison with ab initio calculations shows that all the models reach the same level of accuracy in reproducing structural, vibrational, and diffusive properties of liquid water. Our approach enables practical, data-efficient training of customized MLIPs with high speed and accuracy.

papers.title: Shear viscosity of liquid Sb and Bi from pseudopotential theory: the temperature-insensitive soft-tail component
papers.abstract: A static, pairwise pipeline, a Bretonnet–Silbert (BS) pseudopotential with Rice–Allnatt transport theory, reproduces the magnitude of liquid-metal shear viscosity, while its temperature gradient marks where the static description reaches its boundary. We compute the shear viscosity η(T) of liquid Sb and Bi from each melting point to at least 500 K above it, using five local-field corrections and the Zahid pseudopotential parameters, and resolve the temperature gradient |dη/dT| into kinetic, hard-core, and soft-tail components. The soft-tail component η_s accounts for 54–59% of the total viscosity but barely changes with temperature, so the calculated gradient is systematically too weak: η is underestimated at the melting point (−16% for Sb, −32% for Bi) and overestimated at high temperature, crossing the reference data near 1025 K (Sb) and 850 K (Bi). Because η_s is an integral over the pair structure g(r), replacing the hard-sphere form g^HS(r) with a modified hypernetted-chain (MHNC) one raises η_s by 7–21% but does not recover the gradient; across the hard-sphere and MHNC closures tested here, improving the static pair structure alone leaves the slope deficit largely unchanged, pointing to the Rice–Allnatt decomposition rather than these g(r) models. The local-field correction changes η by only 3–4%, an order of magnitude less than the spread induced by the non-unique BS parameters; the sparse ab initio molecular-dynamics data do not contradict this weaker-than-experiment gradient. These results delimit the static, pairwise framework for Sb and Bi and provide a component-resolved benchmark for dynamic, many-body, or screening extensions of liquid-metal transport theory.

papers.title: Distribution and Function of Pyrimidine Nucleoside 2'-Hydroxylases across the Tree of Life
papers.abstract: Pyrimidine nucleoside metabolism is classically divided into phosphorolytic and hydrolytic pathways mediated by nucleoside phosphorylases and nucleoside hydrolases (NSHs), respectively. While ribonucleoside turnover is well characterized, it remains unclear how 2'-deoxynucleosides such as thymidine are integrated into these pathways in non-metazoans.
