In plants, thymidine catabolism has been linked to NSH activity in vivo, yet inconsistencies across species and structural considerations raise the question as to whether thymidine is a direct substrate. Here, we show that Arabidopsis thaliana NSH1 hydrolyses uridine and 5-methyluridine, but not thymidine, implying the existence of an upstream activation step. We identify pyrimidine nucleoside 2'-hydroxylases (PDN2'Hs) as this missing activity and demonstrate that they are conserved across fungi, plants, and selected bacterial and SAR lineages, where they convert thymidine to 5-methyluridine. These findings reveal an evolutionarily ancient metabolic strategy linking DNA-derived nucleosides to canonical ribonucleoside turnover across diverse branches of life.

papers.title: Estimating the make-up of a blend in terms of its parent mixtures (e.g., reverse-engineering a wine blend) based on chemical fingerprints
papers.abstract: In the chemical, food & beverage, agricultural, and pharmaceutical industries, non-reacting complex mixtures are often blended to tune the properties of a finished product. Herein, we tackle the inverse problem of reconstructing the unknown make-up of a blend in terms of its parent mixtures based on chemical fingerprints. As an experimental case study, we estimate the volume percentages of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, and Cabernet Franc composing a Bordeaux red wine blend. For chemical fingerprinting, we measure the ethanol, sugar, and acid concentrations in the blend and each pure-varietal wine. A mass balance on each constituent over mixing (neglecting chemical reactions, evaporation, and excess volume) gives a system of linear equations, subject to a sum-to-one constraint, governing the make-up of the blend. To find the best approximate solution to this overdetermined system, we solve a constrained, scaled total least squares optimization problem, thereby explicitly accounting for measurement errors in all of the chemical fingerprints. We predicted the Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, and Cabernet Franc content in four different blends with an average error of <5 vol. %. Monte Carlo sampling and propagation of measurement errors provided uncertainty quantification. Such “computational unmixing” of a blend is useful for authenticity verification, fraud detection, forensics, quality control, and routing of blends across many different industries.

papers.title: Programmable Porosity in Polymers via Microfluidic Templating and 3D Printing
papers.abstract: Polymeric functionally graded porous materials (pFGPMs) enable spatial control over transport and mechanical response in a continuous solid in which porosity is strategically placed rather than uniformly distributed. Early research on the production of pFGPMs has demonstrated that graded architectures can be induced, typically as indirect outcomes of time-evolving temperature, pressure, or concentration fields. Because these gradients emerge from process-driven kinetics rather than desired architectural arrangements, reproducibility and spatiotemporal control remain limited. Fluid (foam or emulsion) templating offers a more direct route: the transient structure of polymerizable and crosslinkable foams or high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) can be transferred into a solid matrix while controlling compartment size, packing, and film stability during solidification. Microfluidics enhance fluid management by confining interfacial breakup to produce monodisperse bubbles or droplets whose size, volume fraction, and interconnectivity can be tuned independently, transforming liquid templates into programmable solid architectures. This review follows the evolution of microfluidic templating towards its integration with additive manufacturing, with an emphasis on platforms that embed in-line bubble or droplet generation at the printhead. We conclude with an outlook on the opportunity to expand the palette of available materials and discuss the emerging role of data-driven approaches in managing the coupled dynamics of formulation, breakup, and solidification, enabling truly programmable polymeric FGPMs.

papers.title: Membrane Deformation Enables Conduction in a Non-Membrane-Spanning Artificial Ion Channel
papers.abstract: Artificial ion channels (AICs) are emerging as synthetic therapeutics and biophysical models for membrane transport, yet their design has largely assumed that functional channels must fully span the lipid bilayer. The (Fe 2+ )6 Star of David [2]Catenane (SoD) forms highly conductive chloride channels despite a substantial mismatch with bilayer thickness. Atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support SoD insertion via pre-existing or transient membrane defects and subsequent stabilisation within lipidlined toroidal pores, producing pronounced local membrane thinning and an hourglass-shaped conductive pathway. Under an applied external field corresponding to +100 mV, SoD adopts ensembles of conductive states between 0.4-2.1 nS. Conductance is modulated by embedding depth and tilt angle, consistent with dynamic lipid gating. These findings challenge the idea that AICs must span the membrane and present membrane deformation as a viable design principle, increasing design flexibility and expanding the scope of accessible AIC architecture space.

papers.title: Exploring MIL-88B-Derived Mesoporous Carbon as a Platinum Catalyst Support for Polymer Electrolyte Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Polymer electrolyte fuel cells (PEFCs) are promising for clean energy conversion; however, their performance is limited by sluggish oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) kinetics and mass-transport losses in the cathodic catalyst layer. This study investigates mesoporous carbons derived from the metal-organic framework MIL-88B as support for platinum nanoparticles. Controlled pyrolysis at 700-1100 °C produces carbon materials with high surface areas (~700 m2 g-1) and well-developed mesoporosity. Platinum nanoparticles were deposited via polyol reduction, and ORR activity and fuel cell performance were evaluated using rotating disk electrode and membrane electrode assembly measurements. The carbonization temperature influences electronic properties, and wettability. An intermediate temperature of 900 °C provides a balance between conductivity and hydrophilicity, improving performance at low ionomer-to-carbon ratios despite the large support particle size, which can hinder oxygen transport. The Pt/MIL material exhibits a high electrochemically active surface area (~55 m2 g-1) and competitive ORR performance (up to 1 A cm-2 at 0.7 V), compared to 0.25 A cm-2 and ~15 m2 g-1 for Vulcan XC-72R at low ionomer content (I/C=0.25) in a single-cell fuel cell. These findings show that MOF-derived mesoporous carbons enable lower ionomer loadings without sacrificing kinetic activity in PEFCs.

papers.title: Ketal versus Ester Linker Hydrolysis in Ionizable Lipids: Mechanistic Implications for Endosomal Escape in mRNA-LNP Therapeutics
papers.abstract: A poorly understood mechanistic issue in the therapeutic translation of mRNA lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology beyond prophylactic vaccination is the lack of exploration of the relationship between linker biodegradation and endosomal escape. This review presents a kinetic alignment framework that directly translates the linker hydrolysis mechanism onto the pH-defined time scale of time-resolved LNP trafficking and assesses the role of linker chemistry in the temporal efficiency of endosomal escape. The productive endosomal escape window is a constrained pH range of 5.5 to 6.5 and a time window of 1-30 minutes after internalization, during which endosomal maturation renders mRNA cargo therapeutically inactive upon lysosomal fusion. In this context, we show that hydrolysis of ester and ketal linkers is not a single biodegradation strategy; they are two distinct mechanisms that do not overlap and have different relationships to the escape event. Ester hydrolysis is carboxylesterase-mediated and lysosomal and happens outside the escape window. Ketal hydrolysis is acid-catalyzed and happens at pH 6.5 when the early endosome starts to acidify; thus, it is not separated from the activation of the ionizable lipids, but rather temporally integrated. The framework made two new predictions that could be immediately tested: 1) structurally similar pairs of ionizable lipids with different linker chemistry, but the same tail structure (ketal vs. ester, for example), should be measurably different in their endosomal escape kinetics when tested under controlled pH conditions using single-particle imaging; 2) the position of the ionizable amine relative to the ketal vs. ester should be a dual variable for both pKa and onset of the hydrolysis reaction, i.e., optimizing one parameter in isolation should result in sub-optimal performance under the second. An examination of the currently available ketal lipid library (DLin-KC1-DK2-DMA; KEL12) with regard to these predictions shows that no published study has yet maintained the tail architecture while changing the linker chemistry. We specify the minimum experimental design required to test it. Finally, we argue that this mechanistic gap has direct regulatory and clinical consequences for repeat-dose mRNA therapeutics currently in clinical development, where linker chemistry selection is proceeding on empirical rather than predictive grounds.

papers.title: Biomimetic Total Synthesis of (±)-Haloxine
papers.abstract: Haloxine, a naturally racemic β-ketoamide alkaloid, has eluded chemists for nearly 60 years. It has a unique tricyclic core which links it to quinolizidine alkaloid family. Herein we report a plausible biosynthesis and based on that the first total synthesis of this elusive alkaloid. The synthesis relies on a bioinspired Mannich–Mannich–Enamine domino reaction between tetrahydroanabasine and β-ketoesters to generate an enamine-ester core followed by a hydrolysis–acylation domino reaction to rearrange it into the β-ketoamide core of haloxine. The synthesis allowed the first comprehensive NMR characterization of the alkaloid.

papers.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Enantioselective Radical C(sp3)–C(sp3) Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: Enantioselective radical–radical cross-coupling represents a powerful yet largely unsolved strategy for constructing stereogenic C(sp 3 ) centers, because simultaneously controlling cross-selectivity and absolute stereochemistry between two distinct, transient alkyl radicals is exceptionally challenging. Here, we report a nickel-catalyzed C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) cross-coupling that overcomes this limitation by using alkylzirconocenes, readily generated in situ from unactivated alkenes, and α‑halo amides. The reaction proceeds under mild, blue‑light‑driven conditions and provides direct access to chiral α‑aliphatic amides with outstanding efficiency (up to 98% yield) and enantioselectivity (up to 99:1 e.r.). The method exhibits remarkably broad substrate scope: a wide range of functional groups are tolerated on both coupling partners, and the protocol is successfully applied to the late‑stage diversification of complex natural products, including derivatives of cholesterol, estrone, and vitamin E. Furthermore, the reaction is extended to the highly enantioselective construction of quaternary carbon stereocenters, underscoring its practical synthetic value. Critical to this success was the development of a new pyridine–imidazoline (Pyim) ligand through over 140 iterative experimental cycles and deep learning framework for ligand optimization. This systematic screening campaign not only delivered a superior ligand, but also generated a rich, high‑quality dataset that precisely maps ligand structure to catalytic performance.

papers.title: Analysis of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons and Heavy Metals in the Lake Champlain Basin
papers.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are a family of neutral hydrophobic organic compounds containing a number of fused aromatic rings. Some sources of PAHs include gasoline and diesel engine combustion, wood burning, and pavement sealants. Anthropogenic activity is therefore a direct cause of increasing PAH concentration in the environment. A significant number of PAHs have been determined to be carcinogenic if inhaled or ingested. Another product of anthropogenic activity has been increased heavy metal leaching into the environment. Heavy metals, including mercury, cadmium, and lead, can be found in products such as batteries, industrial waste, cigarettes, and paint. At or above certain concentrations, heavy metals can be carcinogenic or toxic to organisms through direct exposure or by ingesting food products that concentrate these metals. Therefore, the aim of this study was to obtain longitudinal data to determine if infrastructure development and anthropogenic activity, which has increased in the Lake Champlain Basin Area in recent years, has affected the health of the lake via contamination of PAHs and heavy metals. We report, herein, data obtained from 2018 - 2023 on the presence or absence of PAHs in sediment from sites across the Lake Champlain Basin, as well as the concentration of heavy metals in the lake water at those sites. We also discuss several different methods employed for the extraction of PAHs from lake sediment. Qualitative results presented herein indicate that PAHs have been detected at various sites across the lake in 2018 and again in 2022 - 2023. Quantitative results from 2023 show two sites with Cd concentrations and one site with Pb concentration over the maximum contaminant level goal (MLPG) of the United States Environmental Protection Agency, and a number of sites with Tl concentrations above the MLPG.

papers.title: Programming electrophotochemical selectivity through feedback-controlled synchronization
papers.abstract: Controlling complex chemical reactivity by digital orchestration requires systems that can synchronize stimuli, sense reaction state in real time, and adapt decisions during the experiment. Electrophotochemistry (EPC) accesses reactive intermediates under mild conditions, but remains difficult to reproduce because light, current, atmosphere, temperature, and analysis are usually optimized and executed separately. Addressing this problem requires a digital framework for coordinating physical stimuli in which photon flux, current waveform, atmosphere control, sampling, and analysis are specified as one executable reaction program. Here, we report the ElectroPhotoChemputer, a fly-by-wire approach for automated batch EPC that integrates programmable light–current synchronization with inline analytical feedback. Chemical programs (XDL) encode this multiparameter space as a coordinated set of executable operations. System validation showed linear programmable irradiation across LED channels (R2 ≥ 0.98), temperature control at 24–34 °C under continuous irradiation, deoxygenation to <1 ppm O2 and reproducible eight-vial actinometric photon delivery of 3.60 ± 0.37 µmol s-1 per vial. This digitization opens a reaction window, enabling the previously unreported EPC C3-formylation of indoles with glyoxylic acid, in which synchronized 457 nm irradiation and 100 ms rapid alternatingpolarity (rAP) electrolysis favour radical coupling over competing thermal dimerization. Real-time UV–Vis/CV feedback enabled algorithmic termination, giving the target product in 78.7 ± 2.1% isolated yield, a 45–81% substrate scope, and preparative synthesis from a 9 g substrate charge. These results show that electrophotochemical selectivity can be programmed through feedback-controlled synchronization of physical stimuli and analytical stop rules.

papers.title: Fabrication of graphitic carbon nitride nanostructures with tunable morphology for bioimaging
papers.abstract: Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ) is a versatile material for biomedical, energy, and environmental applications. Bulk g-C 3 N 4 is commonly used as a precursor for nanoscale objects, yet systematic links between synthesis conditions, nanostructure morphology, surface chemistry, and biological response remain limited. Here, we have fabricated a palette of carbon nitride nanostructures via hydrothermal alkaline etching. By varying the hydroxide (LiOH, NaOH, or KOH) and reaction conditions, etching yields carbon nitride quantum dots, carbon nitride nanowires and their networks, as well as larger flakes and sponge-like objects. Automated transmission electron microscopy image analysis supported this comparison by converting heterogeneous micrographs into object-level morphology and particle-size statistics. The hydroxide type also controls surface chemistry: LiOH and KOH promote stronger oxidative functionalization, whereas NaOH leads to a more hydrated and passivated surface. In immortalized human cervical cancer cells, the samples show little effect on metabolic activity after 24 h at 200 µg mL −1 , while cellular accumulation varies markedly with preparation conditions. Notably, smaller nanostructures do not guarantee higher cellular accumulation, suggesting that nanowire networks with entangled quantum dots may dominate membrane adhesion. Overall, this work provides a practical route to tune carbon nitride nanostructures for bioimaging applications.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Path Memory in Coarse-Grained Stochastic Molecular Systems
papers.abstract: Experiments on small nonequilibrium, chemical, and biophysical systems often record a coarse observable rather than the full mesoscopic state, making it unclear whether the measured present is sufficient to predict future response. We study this sufficiency through two preparation histories can be indistinguishable in the observed present but remain distinguishable by their later behavior. We call this effect probe-recoverable path memory in which the framework conditions on the observed state before asking whether history is still recoverable, separating endpoint imprinting from hidden storage as well as response-based readout. Within finite Markov systems, this memory arises when a preparation difference lies in the observation-null subspace but is carried into observable coordinates by subsequent dynamics. Lumpable probe dynamics eliminate the readout whereas non-lumpable dynamics can expose hidden preparation modes. Controlled Markov constructions provide explicit witnesses, including disappearance under observed-level closure and decay under hidden equilibration. Ground-truth smFRET benchmark trajectories validate the same decomposition at the trajectory level, that is noisy coarse observations retain conditional history dependence, while conditioning on the full hidden state removes it. Public molecular datasets are used as application-base analyses of latent structure and macrostate insufficiency. This framework gives a way to distinguish visible state matching from hidden path memory and potentially allow insights into when the observed present is not the whole thermodynamic state.

papers.title: Is One Molecular Representation Enough? A Comparative Study of Featurization Methods Across Diverse Datasets
papers.abstract: The predictive performance of molecular machine learning models depends on how molecules are featurized, yet fair comparisons across methods are rare because studies often vary architectures and hyperparameters. We benchmark five molecular featurization techniques i.e., Coulomb Matrix, Bag of Bonds, ACSF, SOAP, and Weighted Views across five benchmark datasets (ESOL, FreeSolv, BBBP, BACE, ClinTox). WhileWeighted Views employs a unique weighted aggregation architecture, we ensure a fair comparison by keeping the total number of trainable parameters identical across all methods through width adjustment, isolating the impact of the representation itself. Our results show that no single representation universally dominates. SOAP and Bag of Bonds performed well on regression tasks, capturing the 3D structural information. In contrast,Weighted Views achieves superior performance on biological classification benchmarks such as BBBP and ClinTox, where integrating multiple molecular perspectives through learnable aggregation proves advantageous. The Coulomb Matrix consistently underperforms across all tasks. These findings establish that the optimal featurization strategy is fundamentally task dependent, providing an evidence based roadmap for selecting molecular representations.

papers.title: Molecular Thermodynamics of Lower Critical Solution Temperature Ionic Liquid/Water Mixtures: Tetrabutylphosphonium Trifluoroacetate
papers.abstract: Lower critical solution temperature (LCST) ionic liquids (ILs) are thermoresponsive materials that undergo liquid–liquid demixing with water into water-rich (WR) and IL-rich (ILR) phases upon heating. Despite the vast combinatorial space of cation–anion pairings, LCST behavior is observed in only a handful of aqueous ILs. To uncover the enthalpic and entropic driving forces that govern this unique phase behavior among molecular liquids, we investigate an exemplary LCST IL, tetrabutylphosphonium trifluoroacetate ( [\mathrm{P_{4444}}][\mathrm{TFA}] ), by pairing equilibrium molecular dynamics and finite-concentration thermodynamic integration with chilled-mirror dew point water activity experimental measurements. Computationally predicted excess chemical potentials of water ( \mu^{\mathrm{E}}_{\mathrm{H_2O}} ) show excellent agreement with experimental measurements over IL weight fractions w_{\mathrm{IL}} = 85\text{–}95\% at T = 300\,\mathrm{K} and 323\,\mathrm{K} , with absolute deviations ranging from 0.04 to 1.2\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} , establishing accurate resolution of the non-ideal solvation contribution. \mu^{\mathrm{E}}_{\mathrm{H_2O}} is counterbalanced by a strongly favorable ideal entropy of mixing, governed by the large ( {\sim}19{:}1 ) IL/water molar volume ratio, and a uniformly unfavorable solvation free energy (relative to bulk water). The excess partial molar enthalpy of water ( h^{\mathrm{E}}_{\mathrm{H_2O}} ) is marked by strong temperature sensitivity, undergoing an exothermic to endothermic shift of {\sim}5\text{–}6\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} from 300\text{–}373\,\mathrm{K} . On the other hand, the non-ideal entropy of solvation ( s^{\mathrm{E,\,n.id.}}_{\mathrm{H_2O}} ) is uniformly unfavorable. Mechanistically, this enthalpy/entropy temperature dependence is traced to electrostatic screening probed by the charge-correlation structure factor S_{ZZ}(\mathbf{k})/k^{2} , the competing water–water and water–anion interactions, and the structural organization of water imposed by the hydrophobic \mathrm{P_{4444}^+} cation.

papers.title: Crystal Structure of a Ytterbium(III)–Pyrroloquinoline Quinone (PQQ) Complex
papers.abstract: Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) is a redox-active quinone-based cofactor best known for its role in bacterial alcohol dehydrogenases, including a subset of lanthanide-dependent enzymes discovered in recent years. To gain further structural insight into lanthanide-PQQ coordination chemistry, we report the crystal structure of [YbPQQ(H 2 O) 4 ]·4H 2 O. In the solid state, YbPQQ units assemble into one-dimensional coordination polymer chains, with PQQ present in its fully deprotonated form. The Yb 3+ center is coordinated within the biologically relevant ONO pocket, mirroring the binding mode observed in the active sites of lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenases. The structure is compared to the previously reported EuPQQ and Ca 3 PQQ 2 complexes.

papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Ionic Conductivity in Solid-State Electrolytes Using Compositional, Structural, and Neural Potential Features
papers.abstract: Identifying solid-state electrolyte (SSE) materials with high ionic conductivity is critical for next-generation lithium-ion batteries, yet experimental discovery remains slow and resource-intensive. Here we present a machine learning pipeline that combines compositional features from the Materials-Agnostic Platform for Informatics and Exploration (Magpie), structural descriptors from the OBELiX dataset, and energy features extracted from the Crystal Hamiltonian Graph Neural Network (CHGNet) to predict ionic conductivity of Li-based SSEs. Using gradient boosted ensemble methods (XGBoost and CatBoost), we achieve a test R2 of 0.775 and MAE of 0.954 log(S/cm) on 606 experimentally measured materials from the OBELiX benchmark dataset, surpassing the published random forest baseline of R2 ≈ 0.65. We further apply an inverse design pipeline to propose 16 novel candidate SSE compositions not present in existing databases, including promising Li-P-S-halide compositions consistent with the Argyrodite family. This work demonstrates that combining composition-based, structural, and neural potential features yields meaningful performance gains for data-scarce materials property prediction tasks.

papers.title: Systematic Errors Begone! Yb(III) Electronic Structure Demands Dynamic Electron Correlations
papers.abstract: Yb(III) complexes are promising targets for molecular spin qubits and near-IR luminescence agents but often struggle to achieve noteworthy single-molecule magnet performance. These properties are highly dependent on the electronic structure generated by the crystal field splitting of the ground J-multiplet. However, the commonly used complete active space self-consistent field calculation (CASSCF) consistently underpredicts the crystal field splitting of the ground J-multiplet. We have found that the incorporation of dynamic electron correlations using extended multistate second-order complete active space perturbation theory (XMS-CASPT2) produces close agreement with crystal field splitting energies visualised by luminescence spectroscopy and cross validated by inelastic neutron scattering and electron paramagnetic resonancespectroscopies. XMS-CASPT2, in addition to, CASSCF is therefore a critical correction to allow for accurate interpretation of the simulations or predictions of Yb(III) compounds.

papers.title: A Computational Study of Gemcitabine Encapsulation in CC3 Porous Organic Cage: Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, Binding Free Energy, and Structure-Activity Relationship Analysis
papers.abstract: Gemcitabine, a first-line nucleoside analogue chemotherapy drug, is rapidly inactivated in plasma by cytidine deaminase (CDA), severely limiting its therapeutic efficacy. Porous organic cages (POCs) have emerged as promising drug delivery vehicles due to their discrete, soluble architecture and tunable cavities. Here, we report a comprehensive computational structure-activity relationship (SAR) study of gemcitabine encapsulation across five CC3-based cage variants using molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and MM-PBSA binding free energy analysis. AutoDock Vina blind docking yielded exclusively endohedral binding (20/20 poses, best ΔG = −5.7 kcal/mol) for pristine CC3. Three independent 200 ns GROMACS MD simulations of pristine CC3 at 300 K reveal stochastic encapsulation-release dynamics consistent with μM-affinity binding (ΔGbind = −13.44 ± 0.41 kcal/mol). A systematic SAR campaign across four additional cage variants establishes critical design rules: N-methyl endofunctionalization (CC3-methyl) eliminates encapsulation by reducing cavity volume; aromatic fluorination (CC3-F12) provides marginal electrostatic improvement but insufficient kinetic stabilization; exo-phenyl functionalization (CC3-exo-phenyl) blocks drug entry entirely; while lowering simulation temperature to 280 K achieves complete, reproducible endohedral encapsulation across all three independent replicas (100% endohedral, mean 2.25 ± 0.25 Å, no exit events in 181–190 ns each). Probability distribution analysis confirms the transformation from a broad bimodal distribution at 300 K (mean 9.4 Å, 46% endohedral) to a sharp unimodal peak at 280 K (mean 2.25 Å, 100% endohedral). Framework breathing analysis reveals that CC3 is more rigid at 280 K (Rg std = 0.07–0.08 Å) than at 300 K (Rg std = 0.17 Å), consistent with thermally-stabilized encapsulation. These results establish a robust multi-scale computational framework to guide the rational design of porous organic cages for targeted drug delivery applications.

papers.title: Data Scarcity in Mutant-Specific Drug Design:
papers.abstract: Drug resistance remains a critical challenge in EGFR-targeted cancer therapy, with the T790M gatekeeper mutation accounting for approximately 60% of acquired resistance to firstand second-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). We present an end-to-end AIdriven pipeline for inverse molecular design targeting both wild-type EGFR and the clinically prevalent L858R/T790M resistance mutant. An AttentiveFP graph neural network (GNN) trained on 17,623 ChEMBL bioactivity records achieves a Pearson correlation of R = 0.736 (R2 = 0.534, RMSE = 0.890) on the wild-type EGFR binding affinity prediction task. Extension to the T790M mutant reveals a critical data scarcity problem: with only 1,552 mutantspecific training samples (9× fewer than wild-type), model performance degrades substantially (R = 0.400, R2 = 0.155). We demonstrate that a PI1M-style pseudo-labeling strategy—augmenting mutant training data with 12,348 wild-type compounds labeled by the mutant model at a down-weighted loss (w = 0.3)—recovers performance to R = 0.698 (R2 = 0.487, RMSE = 0.717), approaching wild-type model quality. A genetic algorithm (GA) inverse design pipeline generates 16 novel wild-type EGFR inhibitor candidates and 13 T790M-targeted candidates, all satisfying drug-likeness constraints (SA Score ≤ 4.0, QED ≥ 0.4, Lipinski Rule of Five). Notably, acrylamide warhead motifs (C=CC(=O)N-) emerge spontaneously in T790M candidates—consistent with the covalent binding mechanism of third-generation EGFR-TKIs such as osimertinib. Preliminary AutoDock Vina docking validation confirms that all candidates bind the EGFR kinase pocket with reasonable affinities (−7.6 to −8.3 kcal/mol). A full cross-docking analysis, however, reveals that T790M-targeted candidates do not show preferential binding to the mutant receptor under standard non-covalent scoring—a discrepancy we attribute to Vina’s inability to model the covalent mechanism of the acrylamide warhead these candidates spontaneously acquired, highlighting a validation gap relevant to AI-driven covalent inhibitor design. Our results establish a transferable inverse design methodology—previously validated on polymer property prediction (Polyinverse)—applied here to drug discovery, and highlight pseudo-labeling as an effective strategy for data-scarce mutant-specific drug design.

papers.title: Exploring the interactions in the ceramic-ceramic membrane, La0.9Sr0.1CoO3-Ce0.8La0.2O2, during the partial oxidation of methane via in situ diffraction
papers.abstract: Combining a robust catalytically active oxygen transport membrane with ceria-based oxides with high oxygen storage capacity has been used to improve catalytic properties, such as the partial oxidation of methane, with the goal of efficient hydrogen generation. This work focuses atomic- and macrostructural changes of the combined ceramic composite formed between La0.9Sr0.1CoO3 and Ce0.8La0.2O2 using SEM-EDS and in situ neutron diffraction. The structural changes are correlated with the partial oxidation of methane. In situ neutron diffraction data show that Ce0.8La0.2O2 neither significantly changes the overall phase transitions of La0.9Sr0.1CoO3 during the partial oxidation of methane nor the reoxidation. In situ diffraction and SEM-EDS show no cation migration between the ceramic components, but macrostructural changes are seen in Ce0.8La0.2O2 in the form of dendrite formation. Ce0.8La0.2O2 enhances the catalytic properties of La0.9Sr0.1CoO3 by increasing the H2 yield relative to CO during syngas production and improving catalytic stability over multiple cycles.

papers.title: Support-induced charge redistribution governs restructuring trajectories in bimetallic Pt oxidation catalysts
papers.abstract: Supported Pt bimetallic catalysts often exhibit enhanced performance compared to their monometallic counterparts, but their widespread implementation remains challenging due to reaction-driven surface restructuring and phase segregation under reaction conditions, which often deteriorate performance. Here, we demonstrate that the electronic character of an oxide support dictates the restructuring trajectory of Pt/Cu bimetallic catalysts under reaction conditions by driving charge redistribution across both metal components. In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy and diffuse-reflectance infrared spectroscopy of highly uniform Pt/Cu nanocrystals supported on nonreducible Al2O3 and reducible Mn2O3, corroborated by first-principles calculations, demonstrated that charge equilibration across all metals at the metal–support interface can stabilize a transient bimetallic oxide configuration that is highly active for the structure-sensitive oxidation of propene. This support-induced charge redistribution alters the initial redox state of supported Pt/Cu nanoparticles and redirects their restructuring trajectory, leading to a more active catalyst with substantially attenuated deactivation.

papers.title: Advancing Host Cell Protein Characterisation in Monoclonal Antibody Therapeutics: A Nanoparticle-Enriched and High-Sensitive Mass Spectrometry Approach
papers.abstract: The substantial concentration gap between low-abundance host cell proteins (HCPs) and high-abundance monoclonal antibody drug products presents a significant analytical challenge for HCP analysis using conventional proteomics workflow. Advances in sample preparation, chromatography and mass spectrometry techniques have aimed at either reducing this concentration imbalance or the peptide co-elution effects during chromatography. Despite this, comprehensive characterisation of HCPs remains difficult, particularly at below ppm levels, often requiring complex and low-throughput methodologies. In this study we report a rapid, sensitive and high-throughput approach for HCP characterisation using a workflow that integrates the Seer Proteograph XT nanoparticle-enrichment platform, the Evosep ONE liquid chromatography (LC) system, and the timsUltra AIP mass spectrometer (MS). This workflow enables efficient sample preparation (accommodating 40 samples within 6 hours) and LC-MS analysis supporting up to 40 samples per day. Using a dynamic protein standard set, the method achieved a reproducible LOD as low as 0.2 ppm, outperforming native digestion approaches, which were limited to approximately 1 ppm. Compared with previously reported methods, this workflow provided deeper HCP coverage in NISTmAb 8671, identifying over 350 HCPs, including those present at sub-ppm levels, with high confidence and reproducibility. Furthermore, application to three commercial products resulted in the identification of 80–200 additional HCPs undetected by native digestion. Overall, our results highlight the potential of automated nanoparticle-based enrichment combined with advanced mass spectrometry to enable high-throughput, sensitive characterisation of low-level HCPs in biopharmaceutical products enabling prompt risk assessment during manufacturing and next generation purification workflow development.

papers.title: Waste and Peroxide-free Aerobic Oxidative Coupling of Aldehydes and Amines to Amides
papers.abstract: The economic and environmental costs associated with conventional acid–amine coupling continue to limit the sustainability of amide bond formation. Oxidative coupling of aldehydes and amines offers an attractive alternative, but most existing methods rely on transition metals and stoichiometric oxidants or generate peroxides, thereby restricting functional group compatibility. Moreover, amide bond formation remains highly sensitive to steric hindrance, rendering the synthesis of tertiary amides particularly challenging. Herein, we report a base mediated aerobic oxidative coupling of aldehydes and amines to amides via an α-aminophosphonate intermediate. The transformation is performed using a minimal amount of green solvent and without chromatographic purification, substantially improving the environmental metrics of the process. It operates under redox neutral conditions, without peroxide formation, and generates only water and water-soluble amine bases as byproducts, together with recyclable phosphites. In addition, a phosphite-catalyzed aerobic oxidative amidation of cyclic iminium intermediates derived from the corresponding aldehydes and amines has also been developed. Our methods are largely unaffected by steric demand and exhibit excellent tolerance toward unprotected and sensitive functional groups. Additionally, this strategy provides direct access to metastable amides that can undergo in situ activation and derivatization into structurally diverse non-amide products.

papers.title: Enhancing Substrate Transformation: By Nano-Bioelectrocatalysis with Engineered
papers.abstract: The development of efficient bioelectronic interface for redox enzyme is essential for advancing biosensing and electrocatalytic applications. In this study, we report a gold nanoparticle (Au NPs) modified electrode platform for immobilization and electrocatalysis of engineered CYP175A1 variants. Citrate-capped Au NPs were attached on cysteamine-functionalized gold electrode to construct a favourable nanoengineered interface that enhances enzyme loading and facilitates direct electron transfer between the heme active site and electrode surface. Electrochemical investigations under both anaerobic and aerobic conditions demonstrated significantly improved electron transfer kinetics compared to unmodified electrodes. Electrochemical based engineered variants, CYP175A1_F329H_Q333C exhibited a formal redox potential of approximately -350 mV versus Ag/AgCl under anaerobic condition, whereas under aerobic condition a pronounced cathodic reduction current was observed indicating oxygen influenced electrochemical behavior of the heme center. The developed bioelectrode enables the electrocatalytic conversion of 1-Methoxynaphthalene to Russig’s blue dye, which was confirmed by UV-Visible spectroscopy and Electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS). Kinetics analysis using the Michaelis-Menten model yielded with K M of 334 μM, indicative effective substrate interaction in the immobilized state. Overall, this work demonstrates strategy for integrating engineered CYP175A1 enzyme offering strong potential for biosensing and bioelectronic applications.

papers.title: MIM-Flow: An Integrated Forward-Inverse Framework for Navigating Sparse Pareto-Optimal Regions in Functional Conjugated Molecules
papers.abstract: Functional molecules that simultaneously satisfy multiple, often competing, objectives are critical for improving device performance, yet discovering such candidates under multi-objective constraints remains a fundamental challenge. To address this, we introduce MIM-Flow (Moiety-in-Molecule FlowNet), an integrated framework supporting both accurate forward characterization and moiety-assembly-based inverse generation. MIM-Flow integrate moiety types, site types, and assembly-pattern selections into a unified MIM action space, and utilize a dual-tower architecture to predict the representations of intermediate 1 states and local sites. The dual-tower model is pretrained on 10-million-scale conformations and single-step assembly trajectories, achieving global awareness of 3D space and site distribution. Using narrowband MR-TADF emitters as validation cases, we optimize the probability flow of the assembly process within the Sub-Trajectory Balance (SubTB) GFlowNet architecture. For de novo generation, MIM-Flow predicts emission spectra with high accuracy (Rš = 0.837 against quantum-mechanical (QM) calculations). The top-3 generated molecules satisfy all multi-objective constraints and fall within the top 5% of reported MRTADF molecules. For local generation, we incorporate a synthetic-accessibility prior by restricting MIMs to reported patented scaffolds, and successfully synthesize the top-1 candidate—an unprecedented molecule whose experimental emission spectrum closely matches the QM prediction and whose CIE coordinates fall within the top 50% of reported MR-TADF molecules. Therefore, MIM-Flow can effectively explores the sparse, distributed Pareto-optimal regions that jointly satisfy property and synthesizability criteria, drastically reducing the trial-anderror space for experimental synthesis. This generalizable framework can also be transferred to the multi-objective design of other complex functional materials.

papers.title: Monoamidoamino Carbene Copper(I)-Hydride Mediated Catalytic CO2 Hydrogenation and Hydrofunctionalization
papers.abstract: N-Heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) are well known for their strong, tunable electronic properties and their ability to stabilize reactive copper(I) species, thereby enhancing catalytic performance. Herein, we report a well-defined, room-temperature-stable monoamidoamino carbene (MAC)-supported Cu(I) hydride, [MACCu-H]2 (III), which was further utilized for CO2 hydrogenation via a frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) pathway. The utilization of earth-abundant first-row transition metals for CO2 hydrogenation to formate remains underexplored, with noble metals currently dominating this transformation. The newly synthesized [MACCu-H]2 (III) exhibits remarkable activity and selectivity in conjunction with a Lewis pair, affording formic acid from the reduction of CO2 with dihydrogen with a high turnover number (TON). Key intermediates, including copper formate (IV), copper formate-B(C6F5)3 adduct (VIII), and copper-BH4 complex (IX), are also isolated and studied to propose a mechanistic cycle, aided by DFT calculations. The theoretical calculation highlights the crucial role of the MAC ligand in stabilizing the copper(I) hydride (III) with high hydricity, thereby facilitating the insertion of CO2 and promoting the formation of copper formate. Moreover, [MACCu-H]2 (III) also facilitates the efficient hydrofunctionalization of ketones and terminal alkynes, demonstrating its broader synthetic utility for important organic transformations.

papers.title: Dual-Function Cosubstrates Enable Threonine Dehydrogenase-Driven Chemoenzymatic Pyrrole Synthesis
papers.abstract: Preparative biocatalytic synthesis of substituted pyrroles remains challenging despite recent advances in enzymatic αaminoketone generation. Herein, we report a concurrent chemoenzymatic cascade to disubstituted pyrroles based on threonine dehydrogenase (ThrDH)-catalyzed generation of aminoacetone from L-threonine that is intercepted in situ by Knorr pyrrole condensation with β-dicarbonyl compounds. To overcome cofactor limitations at high substrate concentrations, Escherichia coli ThrDH was coupled to an alcohol dehydrogenase from Rhodococcus ruber DSM 44541 (ADH-A), enabling dual-function of the β-dicarbonyl cosubstrate as both a hydride acceptor and pyrrole building-block. The whole-cell catalyst tolerated up to 8% (v/v) β-dicarbonyl and afforded pyrrole products in up to 90% yield and space-time yields of 4.5 g L−1 h−1. Preparative synthesis on a 100 mL scale furnished 4.3 g of pyrrole (279 mM, 93% isolated yield). Among the products obtained, the cascade provides direct access to a reported sunitinib intermediate, illustrating its potential utility for pharmaceutical synthesis. This work establishes ThrDHs as outstanding biocatalysts for heterocycle synthesis and demonstrates that amino acid feedstocks can be efficiently converted into substituted pyrroles through a scalable chemoenzymatic cascade.

papers.title: Real-Time, Label-Free Monitoring of Microbial Pectin Degradation and Carbon Assimilation Using Raman Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Pectin is one of the major polysaccharides produced in plants, and a valuable source of renewable carbon. In this study, we have established a Raman spectroscopy-based framework to study the degradation of pectin by Bacillus subtilis BGN4 and directly trace the metabolic fate of the released carbon. The ensemble of extracellular Raman spectroscopy, ATR–FTIR spectroscopy, dinitrosalicylic acid (DNS) assay and single cell Raman spectroscopy offered a full picture of microbial pectin degradation at various biological levels. Raman spectroscopy directly identified progressive structural changes related to pectin depolymerization; the results obtained by ATR–FTIR spectroscopy independently confirmed the molecular changes; and the gold standard DNS assay revealed the release of reducing sugars during enzymatic hydrolysis. In addition, a direct link between the degradation of extracellular pectin to the assimilation of carbon into newly synthesized cellular biomass was established by reverse stable isotope probing. Overall, these complementary methods have shown the capability of Raman spectroscopy to serve as a tool to connect the extracellular enzymatic activity and the intracellular metabolic response to create a versatile platform for microbial carbon utilization studies. This analytical approach can be applied to study the degradation of other complex biopolymers by microbes and has applications in microbial ecology, valorisation of biomass and the development of sustainable bioprocesses.

papers.title: NEW APPROACH FOR INDIRECT CHEMICAL SHIFT DETERMINATION AND ITS APPLICATION TO HIGH-FIELD PROTEIN NMR SPECTROSCOPY
papers.abstract: Multidimensional nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) experiments are valuable source of information on molecules, playing a pivotal role in chemistry and biochemistry. Sensitivity and resolution of such spectra depend on transverse relaxation rates of nuclei of interest. Therefore, this approach can become unfeasible when transverse relaxation rate is high, leading to loss of signal intensity. We propose a new way of indirect chemical shift determination which omits the problem of transverse relaxation of selected nuclei. The approach involves perturbation of the signal intensity via selective irradiation of nuclei of interest. In addition, we increased the experimental time efficiency of this method by co-incrementing the irradiation frequency with the evolution time in one of the indirectly-detected dimensions, following the principles of accordion spectroscopy. We called this approach FREESIA (FREquency Encoding via Selective Irradiation with Accordion spectroscopy). We designed a new experiment HNCA(COirr) which enables the indirect measurement of carbonyl 13C chemical shifts (insensitive to 13C transverse relaxation) in proteins. The experiment was validated on 41 kDa maltose-binding protein and allowed us to determine chemical shifts of carbonyl 13C nuclei for 90.54 % of residues. We anticipate the FREESIA approach will become particularly useful for ultra-high field NMR measurements of nuclei which suffer from fast relaxation.

papers.title: The Snow Hypothesis of the Origin of Life, version 2.0: a quantitative thermal-gradient conveyor with a cryoprotectant
papers.abstract: The Snow Hypothesis proposes that prebiotic chemistry concentrated and organized at the boundary between snow and a warm mineral surface. Version 2.0 develops this into a quantitative “thermal-gradient conveyor” model and revises one key point: the reactor’s cold zone is not pure water at 0 °C but a non-freezing cryoprotectant solution (glycerol and salts) that remains liquid and chemically active down to about −40…−46 °C. On a warm mineral plate in a cold environment a spatial gradient forms spontaneously; the thermal gradient itself, with no external pump, drives thermocapillary (Marangoni) convection (Ma ~ 106) that shuttles material between zones. Explicit formulas, parameters and order-of-magnitude calculations are given for the whole chain: reactor regimes, cryoconcentration, chirality amplification, the dual role of cold, the full reachability mathematics and the Eigen error threshold. The conclusion is symmetric: the physics of the environment is favourable and is not the bottleneck — short functional RNA motifs (~40–52 nt) are reachable given chirality amplification; the unresolved part reduces to two measurable quantities — the rarity of function F(L) and whether “crude correctors” of fidelity actually operate. The claim is the reachability and preservation of short motifs, not the spontaneous emergence of a self-copying replicase.

papers.title: Nature-Positive Insights into PHBH Biodegradation: Linking Carbon Transformation, Microbial Responses, and Nitrogen-Related Dynamics
papers.abstract: Materials designed for a circular bioeconomy are increasingly expected to support useful performance while remaining compatible with natural ecosystem processes. In this context, biodegradable polymers provide a useful entry point for studying the links between polymer degradation, microbial activity, and aquatic carbon–nitrogen processes. Here, we investigated the aquatic biodegradation of poly(3hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyhexanoate) (PHBH) in a 13C-labeled estuarine microcosm, focusing on the relationships among molecular-scale carbon transformation, microbial community responses, and nitrogen-related water-quality changes. The approach combined time-resolved 1H–13C heteronuclear single quantum coherence (HSQC) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), region-of-interest (ROI)-based spectral descriptors, maximum entropy method (MEM)-derived bondomer-like features, microbiome profiling, functional prediction, and symbolic regression. Estuarine water was pre-labeled with 13C-glucose to generate an isotopeenriched organic carbon background, after which unlabeled PHBH was introduced to follow degradation-associated molecular signal changes. The initial spectra showed distinct 13C–13C coupling-related peak splitting, whereas PHBH addition led to regiondependent weakening, simplification, or reorganization of these patterns, indicating changes in local carbon connectivity and molecular environments during microbial carbon processing. ROI intensity, entropy-related descriptors, and bondomer-like features captured these isotope-resolved molecular changes, while microbial community structure and predicted nitrogen-cycling functional potential varied with degradation stage. Symbolic regression identified interpretable associations among PHBH degradation, nitrogen-related responses, 13C-HSQC molecular descriptors, microbial taxa, and predicted functional features. By linking isotope-resolved molecular signals with microbial and nitrogen-related responses, this study provides a multiscale approach for evaluating biodegradable polymer degradation in aquatic ecosystems.

papers.title: Luminescence Behavior of Di(pyridine-2-yl)methyl-substituted Phosphine Oxides
papers.abstract: Two new di(pyridine-2-yl)methyl-substituted phosphine oxides, (dpym) 2 PhPO and (dpym) 2 PyPO , were synthesized, both exhibiting blue luminescence in the solid state. Suitable single crystals for X-ray diffraction experiments could be obtained to investigate the solid-state structure. Based on the geometry in the crystalline state, TD-DFT and GW/BSE calculations were performed to gain better insight into the photophysical properties. Time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal that the emission is dominated by phosphorescence, with lifetimes of 116 µs upon 251 nm excitation and biexponential microsecond-scale decays upon lower-energy excitation. In solution, luminescence is observed only at high concentrations (22 mm), indicating aggregation-mediated excitation. Excitation–emission spectroscopy of the powders shows two emission bands: one near 390 nm upon excitation at 250 nm and a second band at 500–540 nm upon excitation above 300 nm, the latter also appearing in concentrated solution. The theoretical and spectroscopic data point toward a complex photoluminescence mechanism in which direct triplet excitation, aggregation-mediated low-energy states, and efficient intersystem crossing all contribute to the observed emission.

papers.title: In silico interface stability scoring identifies improved ferredoxin partners for class I P450 biocatalysis
Influence of Inorganic-Organic Hybrid Nanoparticle -Containing Composite Materials on Lanthanide-dependent Growth of Methylobacterium extorquens PA1
papers.abstract: Lanthanide (Ln)-using bacteria inhabit diverse ecological niches and the study of Ln-dependent carbon metabolism has seen immense interest in the past decade. This is also owed to the technological importance of the elements and the potential for Ln-dependent proteins and biomolecules being used in Ln-recycling and separation. One central question is how the bacteria take up lanthanides from their environment, which most often presents them with poorly soluble species rather than well-available, soluble Ln-species. Addressing this question requires model systems in which Ln-availability, rather than total Lncontent, can be tuned in a reproducible and quantifiable manner. To design well-defined growth conditions and provoke bacteria to upregulate their metal-ion acquisition machinery, we synthesized La-containing inorganic-organic hybrid nanoparticles (IOH-NP) with the pH-sensitive dye Alizarin Red S (ARS) and embedded them in 3D-printed polymer disks of different sizes and with different IOH-NP concentrations. The [La(OH)2]+[ARS]- IOH-NP-containing composite-material disks of identical dimensions (1.2 × 0.2 cm) were compared at two La concentrations in the medium: 100 nM and 1 µM. While cultures supplied with 1 µM [La(OH)2]+[ARS]- IOH-NP disks showed reduced but significant growth compared to cultures where 1 µM LaCl3 had been added, 100 nM [La(OH)2]+[ARS]- disks did not support growth beyond the negative controls. [Yb(OH)2]+[ARS]- IOH-NP disks were also fabricated and added alongside 1 µM LaCl3 to some cultures, and these did not show any impairment of growth, ruling out material toxicity. The effect of surface area was assessed by comparing small (0.8 × 0.35 cm, 1.9 cm2) and large (1.2 × 0.2 cm, 4.5 cm2) disks, both at nominal equal 1 µM La concentrations in the disks. The larger surface area supported better growth, indicating that increased contact between the composite material and the medium enhances La release and consequently bacterial growth. Our study establishes [La(OH)2]+[ARS]- IOH-NP composite materials as a chemically defined, reproducible, and geometrically tuneable model platform for imposing Ln-limitation and probing Ln-accessibility in bacterial cultivations. We believe such materials are of high promise in the rapidly developing field of lanthanide-dependent bacterial metabolism and in general for the reproducibility of bacterial growth studies.

papers.title: Electrolyte Dynamics in High-Ni NMC Observed via Operando Neutron Imaging
papers.abstract: Understanding electrolyte dynamics within lithium-ion batteries is critical for improving performance and longevity, yet remains experimentally challenging due to the difficulty of probing liquid phases inside opaque cells. Here, we employ in situ neutron computed tomography (NCT) and operando neutron radiography to non-destructively visualise liquid electrolyte mobility in commercial Li-ion pouch cells with single-crystal (SC) and polycrystalline (PC) cathodes. The neutron-based techniques enable three-dimensional and time-resolved (4D) tracking of electrolyte distribution, leveraging their strong sensitivity to hydrogen in carbonate-based electrolytes. We find that SC cells exhibit a more homogeneous electrolyte distribution after wetting and the first charge, whereas PC cells retain pronounced heterogeneities and higher overall electrolyte mobility, which could have further implications for cell performance and lifetime. Varying the charge rate reveals that slower rates promote more extensive electrolyte movement, facilitating homogeneous electrolyte wetting throughout the electrode stack. Despite limited spatial resolution, the combination of NCT and radiography provides unprecedented full-cell insight into electrolyte redistribution and electrode motion during formation and cycling. This work highlights the capability of neutron imaging to probe electrolyte behaviour in operando, establishing it as a powerful diagnostic tool for next-generation battery design and optimisation.

papers.title: Bidirectional Photocurrents in Layered Hybrid Perovskites Triggered by Switchable Ferrocene Spacers
papers.abstract: As our technology advances, the need for more functional semiconductor materials grows. Multistate logic systems are one way to achieve that and could be realized by a combination of negative and positive photocurrent (NPC, PPC). However, NPC mechanisms are not yet well understood and still unknown in layered hybrid perovskites. Here, we show the NPC in layered Dion-Jacobson-like hybrid perovskites triggered by the switchable ferrocene spacer. The reversibility of the ferrocene switching in the perovskite was shown by cyclic voltammetry. Photoexcitation as well as charge transfer between ferrocene and perovskite were followed via transient absorption spectroscopy. The p- and n-doping character of the ferrocene spacer frontier orbitals leads to the injection of charge carriers into the semiconductor upon excitation of the ferrocene. Under an external electric field, the induced charge carriers are rearranged into space charge zones, which quenches the conductivity. The NPC was shown for bromide and iodide ferrocene hybrid perovskites. However, for Ruddlesden-Popper phases a PPC was observed, as its van der Waals gap prohibits the arrangement of charge carriers. This work paves the way for the possible combination of NPC and PPC effects in one hybrid perovskite for, e.g., multistate photosensing logic gates.

papers.title: FAIRaman: making clinical Raman spectroscopy data FAIR through biobanking and NeXus standards
papers.abstract: Raman spectroscopy is increasingly applied to biomedical and diagnostic research, generating spectral datasets that could support the development of robust artificial-intelligence models for disease diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment guidance. However, most clinical Raman datasets remain difficult to reuse across laboratories because spectra are often stored separately from structured information on sample characteristics, provenance, donor context, pre-analytical processing, acquisition parameters, and data governance. This limits reproducibility, external validation, multicentre integration, and the development of transferable models. Here, we introduce FAIRaman, a FAIR-by-design framework and open-source software tool for the structured organisation of clinical Raman spectroscopy data. FAIRaman combines the hierarchical logic of the Investigation–Study–Assay model with biobanking-derived descriptors for sample, donor, and processing-event annotation, and NeXus/NXraman-inspired metadata for Raman acquisition parameters and spectral data. The resulting structure is implemented in open HDF5 files. The software, developed in Python, converts native Renishaw WDF files and vendor-neutral textbased spectral files into FAIRaman-compliant HDF5 files through a graphical interface, allowing users to combine batch-level metadata with sample-specific clinical associated data. We demonstrate the framework using a real Raman map of breast cancer tissue, and a spectrum from a sample of plasma-derived extracellular vesicles showing that spectral data, acquisition metadata, and clinical sample descriptors can be stored in a single structured file and that the information can be easily recovered using independent free software tools.

papers.title: Introducing Redox-Active Residues to Enhance P450 Peroxygenase Performance
papers.abstract: P450 peroxygenases depend on the high-valent Iron-Oxo intermediate Compound I (Cpd I) to activate C–H bonds. However, the non-productive oxidative damage caused by Cpd I compromises enzyme stability and limits catalytic efficiency. Here, we report a rational protein engineering strategy to address this bottleneck by constructing additional “hole traps” on the enzyme surface. Guided by structural analysis, we introduced redox-active tyrosine/tryptophan residues at spatially defined positions on the surface of the P450BM3 F87A mutant. The optimal double mutant, M8 (F87A/L215W/H408W) significantly enhances turnover numbers (TONs) across a range of peroxide-driven hydroxylation reactions of aliphatic and aromatic substrates. Steady-state kinetics, reductant supplementation assays, and half-life measurements consistently indicated that the introduced Trp residues play a crucial protective role, improving both catalytic output and enzyme robustness. The crystal structure of M8 revealed that the mutations facilitate an expanded local network of π π interactions, forming efficient surface hole traps. Electrostatic potential calculations further showed a reduced potential near the engineered sites, consistent with a more favorable electron transfer gradient. These findings establish the rational construction of auxiliary hole traps as a novel and effective strategy to enhance P450 peroxygenase performance, offering potentially applicable for other heme and even broad oxidizing enzymes.

papers.title: Controlling Interfacial and Bulk Charge Transport in Exsolution Catalysts for High-Activity Water Oxidation
papers.abstract: Metal exsolution is explored as a means of tuning catalytic activity in perovskite oxides for the oxygen evolution reaction in aqueous medium. Controlling nanoparticle size and distribution through external reaction parameters is inherently coupled to the simultaneous evolution of the functional properties of the exsolved nanoparticle population and the host oxide under reducing synthesis conditions. Our analysis reveals that insufficient control over electronic properties of both the exsolved nanoparticles and the oxide support can fundamentally decouple the performance of exsolution catalysts from morphological descriptors such as nanoparticle density. Building on these findings, we demonstrate that metal exsolution can be employed to achieve catalytic performance comparable to that of established high-performance perovskite oxide electrocatalysts which rank close to the top of the volcano plot, while reducing the required amount of critical transition metals by a factor of 20, as evaluated through activity and stability testing.

papers.title: Computational Screening of Molecular Descriptors in Functional Groups for Polypropylene Electret Modification
papers.abstract: Improving charge retention in polypropylene (PP) electrets through chemical modification has attracted considerable interest; however, the molecular descriptors governing charge stabilization remain poorly understood. Here, Density Functional Theory (B3LYP/def2-TZVP, CPCM) was used to computationally screen twelve energetic, electrostatic and structural descriptors across eleven different functionalized PP fragments and to correlate these descriptors with Hirshfeld-derived spin density localization as a proxy for charge accommodation and potential charge trapping behaviour. The results show that different descriptors produced different rankings of functional-group performance, indicating no single property fully explains charge stabilization. Correlation analysis reveals that LUMO energy (r= -0.899, p=0.0002) and electron affinity (r=0.8081, p=0.0005) exhibit the strongest correlations with anionic localization, indicating electron acceptance and orbital energetics as the primary contributors influencing electron stability. Electrostatic effects (dipole moment, charge separation) and charge redistribution (polarizability) also showed weak yet significant correlations with anionic localization. In contrast, none of the descriptors showed strong correlations with cationic localization, though some weak correlations with HOMO energy and ionization potential were identified. In addition, several functional groups showed marked asymmetry between electron and hole stabilization, and the different values of the asymmetry metric suggest that this selectivity can be tuned by molecular design. These results suggest that charge stabilization in functionalized polypropylene is a multifactorial phenomenon dependent on a combination of orbital, electrostatic and charge-redistribution effects and give an insight into molecular design strategies for better electrets.

papers.title: An Autonomous Agentic Query Framework with MCP Tools and Modernized NIST SRD-46 for Accelerating Aqueous Speciation Analysis
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) could automate reasoning over structured scientific databases in chemistry and materials science, but this requires purpose-built agentic architectures, not simply better models. We present an agentic workflow for systematically querying and extracting data from the NIST Standard Reference Database 46 (SRD-46) to perform autonomous speciation and thermodynamic analysis, with three contributions: (1) a hierarchical toolset, served by Model Context Protocol (MCP) framework, which converts natural-language scientific questions into validated SQL over a database enriched with canonical chemical identifiers, equilibrium-reaction maps, and fingerprint-similarity matrices; (2) an induction-deduction-validation reasoning loop with compactors that preserve key chemical context across multi-turn sessions under dynamic memory limits within the same session; and (3) a soft time/turn-budget hook that maintains coherent reasoning within resource constraints. The resulting framework is LLM-agnostic and spans queries from direct lookups to cross-species comparisons to open-ended tasks like estimating unknown Fe complexation constants and selecting ligands for acidic Fe electrodeposition. We benchmark four frontier models (Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, and GPT-5.4) on 49 prompts across four complexity levels, repeated five times (~1,000 answers), using automated claim-level validation and regex-based tool-result matching. All models retrieve reliably on direct-lookup tasks, confirming the architecture bridges natural-language reasoning and structured database access. Beyond lookups, behaviors of models diverge: GPT-5.4 converges rapidly with high per-claim verifiability but limited exploratory depth, whereas Opus 4.6 pursues broader, cross-examined reasoning at the cost of slower convergence and more unsupported claims. This reveals a fundamental tradeoff between convergent efficiency and exploratory breadth on fuzzy scientific queries that scalar benchmarks cannot resolve. It also suggests that fuzzy scientific queries require expert-stewarded reasoning, not faster convergence criteria or higher benchmark metrics alone. Our results demonstrate that domain-expert-designed agentic architectures and evaluation frameworks are essential infrastructure for AI-driven scientific discovery, and that mixed-model deployment strategies may be needed to balance efficiency and explanatory depth for different classes of scientific questions.

papers.title: Structure Prediction of Multi-Component Molecular Crystals with Genarris 4.0
papers.abstract: Multi-component molecular crystals are increasingly used in pharmaceuticals, organic electronics, and energetic materials because they can have unique, tunable properties that are not achievable in single-component crystals. Predicting the structure of multi-component crystals is more challenging, owing to the need to explore the larger space of multiple asymmetric unit configurations. We present a new version of the Genarris open-source molecular crystal structure generator, capable of treating multicomponent crystals. The main new feature of Genarris 4.0 is generation of asymmetric units (ASUs) from the input components and a workflow for selecting ASUs for crystal structure generation. For each ASU, crystal structures are generated in all space groups compatible with the requested number of ASUs per unit cell (Z). The Universal Model for Atoms (UMA) machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are used here for structure relaxation and energy evaluation within the workflow. Genarris 4.0 successfully predicts the structure of six targets: three co-crystals, two salts, and one crystal with Z ′ = 2. Because the UMA MLIPs were trained on single-component molecular crystals, we evaluate its performance for multi-component crystals by comparison to dispersion-inclusive density functional theory (DFT). We find that the results of relaxation and lattice energy ranking of putative structures obtained with UMA are in better agreement with DFT for co-crystals than for salts. Nevertheless, the UMA MLIPs perform well within the workflow, with all experimentally observed structures ranked first or second. Genarris 4.0 therefore provides an effective platform for multi-component crystal structure prediction and the generation of MLIPs training data.

papers.title: On Contemporary Tafel Analysis
papers.abstract: Tafel slope analysis has been the cornerstone of mechanistic interpretation in multi-step electrochemical reactions for nearly a century, underpinning our understanding of reactions from hydrogen evolution to carbon dioxide reduction. Here we demonstrate that the IUPAC-endorsed framework, universally adopted for relating Tafel slopes to rate-determining step identity and position, is mathematically erroneous, a consequence of omitting the chain rule in its original derivation. Instead, it is only valid in the low coverage limit where the electrode remains dominated by empty sites, or when the number of electrons transferred before the rate-determining step is only counted from the step consuming the most abundant surface species. We resolve this inconsistency by introducing a corrected analytical framework for both bound and unbound adsorption models, the latter expressed in closed matrix form amenable to machinelearning-assisted mechanism discovery. Applied to the hydrogen evolution and oxidation reactions, the corrected framework reveals that small Tafel slopes are indicative of a reversible Volmer step with low surface coverage, irrespective of reaction path and adsorption type, while mechanistic discrimination only emerges at high Tafel slopes. Experimentally, we observe Tafel slopes of 140mV dec−1-190mV dec−1 on polycrystalline Pt in alkaline media, values not captured by the classical framework but naturally described by the corrected one. Furthermore, by providing a continuous analytical solution that spans from these interaction-dominated asymptotes down to the rigorous 0mV dec−1 reversible limit, our framework eliminates the need to heuristically define Tafel regions.

papers.title: Reactive Atomistic Simulations of Doping-Driven Co-Aggregation in P3HT:F4TCNQ
papers.abstract: The performance of doped organic semiconductors (OSCs) is governed by a strong coupling between the doping equilibrium and the film morphology, yet capturing both simultaneously in a single atomistic model has remained difficult. Here we use the Reactive Monte Carlo Molecular Dynamics (RMCMD) method to study poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) doped with 2,3,5,6-tetrafluoro-7,7,8,8-tetracyanoquinodimethane (F4TCNQ), a prototypical OSC-dopant pair, and show that dopant aggregation and doping efficiency are mutually determined. We find that ionization converts a pre-aggregated dopant cluster into a mixed P3HT:F4TCNQ ”co-aggregate” whose extent is set by the reaction free energy; as dopants ionize, Coulomb repulsion drives them apart and pulls in ionized P3HT so that higher doping efficiency and greater OSC-dopant mixing are self-reinforcing. Introducing explicit solvent, we observe ionization-driven P3HT:F4TCNQ co-aggregation and displacement of solvent from the dopant coordination shell, consistent with experimentally reported poor solubility of ionized P3HT:F4TCNQ complexes. We also observe a higher doping efficiency in the more polar solvent acetonitrile than in chlorobenzene.

papers.title: Conversion-Resolved Kinetics of ABS Thermolysis Using Differential Coats-Redfern and Friedman Analysis
papers.abstract: Acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene (ABS) is an important engineering plastic in electrical, electronic, automotive, consumer-product, and additive-manufacturing applications. However, its pyrolytic recycling requires reliable kinetic interpretation beyond global thermogravimetric descriptors. In this study, non-isothermal thermolysis of ABS was investigated at 15, 20, and 25 °C·min-1 using differential Coats-Redfern and Friedman isoconversional analyzes with rate-parity and conversion-variant compensation checks. Because conversion-averaged Ea can mask local deviations for isoconversional mechanistic model selection, root mean square error (RMSE) of Ea was used as the primary metric for comparing d-CR and Friedman activation-energies. Under the combined criteria, the L2 random-scission model showed the smallest RMSE of Ea and acceptable rate-parity (R2parity = 0.98938) and compensation behavior (R2compensation = 0.99597), and was therefore selected as the most plausible approximate model. The conversion-averaged Friedman activation energy was 171.12 kJ·mol-1, and the mean pre-exponential factor reconstructed with L2 at 25 C·min-1 was 3.86 × 1020 s-1. These results demonstrate that the d-CR-Friedman framework provides a practical conversion-resolved strategy for interpreting ABS thermolysis beyond classical CR linearity and global kinetic-parameter extraction.

papers.title: Intrinsic Irreducible-Cartesian Tensor Carrier for Equivariant Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Equivariant interatomic potentials use compact angular irreps, while many observables and long-range sources are Cartesian tensors. We introduce the intrinsic irreducible-Cartesian tensor carrier (ICTC), which builds harmonic polynomial bases and intertwiners in Cartesian algebra while storing features directly in compact 2l+1 carriers. A degree-wise orthogonal bridge lets supported MACE checkpoints run in ICTC coordinates with 10000-step double-precision energy/force agreement, and fused ICTC tensor products remove the high-degree Cartesian-3j bottleneck. With matched MACE training protocols, ICTC trains faster on revised MD17, liquid water, and a Materials Project trajectory subset; learning-rate controls identify a finite-width update-scale effect inside the same irreducible function space. The carriers also define deployable Cartesian source coordinates for production molecular dynamics, covering electrostatic multipoles and an l=2 anisotropic polarizability for eigensolver-free many-body dispersion.

papers.title: Enhancing the robustness of rhodium single-atom catalysts for styrene hydroformylation through carbon nitride doping
papers.abstract: Rh single-atom catalysts (SACs) have recently attracted significant attention as highly active heterogeneous catalysts for the hydroformylation of olefins. Despite the potential of these systems to become an alternative to the commercial and highly efficient homogeneous Rh and Co catalysts, leaching, an important drawback of SACs, still needs to be addressed. In this study, we have developed a series of Rh SACs supported on heteroatom (P or/and B)-doped carbon nitride for the hydroformylation of styrene and investigated the effects of heteroatom-doping on the catalytic performance. The developed Rh SACs selectively promoted the reaction and exhibited superior durability against Rh leaching to a dopant-free counterpart catalyst.

papers.title: Cross-exposure transferability and failure boundaries of self-supervised DNN denoising for AR-HAXPES depth profiling
papers.abstract: Laboratory-source angle-resolved hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (AR-HAXPES) is photon-starved atthespatialresolution required formapping,wheretheframe averaging needed to recover a clean depth profile at every position drives total acquisition time into a prohibitive regime. Self-supervised neural denoising offers an alternative to acquisition-time scaling, and a recent companion study 1 has systematically benchmarked its performance against alternative strategies; however, its operational envelope across exposures, its cross-exposure transferability, and its failure modes in the photon-starved regime remain uncharacterised. Here we evaluate self-supervised denoising atthe smallestpossibletargetwindow across three exposures spanning a 25-fold range of per-frame photon flux on a model C / Al 2 O 3 / TiO 2 / Si multilayer. We identify an empirical directional rule for cross-exposure denoiser deployment — train S/N ≥ inference S/N —, characterise the failure boundary in the photon-starved regime where upstream denoiser collapse propagates into constraint-saturated inversion solutions, and locate the asymptotic reach of alltested denoising strategies (frame averaging, Self-DNN, Cross-DNN) relative to a methodological floor set by the reproducibility of the reference. Within the success region of this rule, cross-exposure transfer enables up to a 48-fold equivalent acquisition-time reduction on the depth-RMSE axis (14-fold on the Wasserstein-1 interface- localization axis) at the most photon-starved 4.8 s/frame condition. These results frame self- supervised AR-HAXPES denoising as a characterisable engineering operation with quantifiable failure boundaries and recovery routes, rather than as an empirical post-processing recipe.

papers.title: Asymmetric Pulse Electrodeposition of High-Index Faceted Gold Nanostructures for 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Oxidation
papers.abstract: This work reports the electrodeposition of high-index faceted gold particles resembling rhombic hexecontahedrons in choline chloride urea deep eutectic solvent through the application of asymmetric potential pulses. Potential pulses alternated between cathodic potentials ranging from -0.20 V to -0.25 V vs. Ag/AgCl and an anodic limit of 0.35 V vs. Ag/AgCl near the gold dissolution onset. While the cathodic pulse duration was fixed at 0.5 s, the anodic pulse duration varied from 0.5 s to 2.5 s to study its influence on crystal growth. Symmetric pulses produced poorly defined structures, whereas longer anodic pulses induced tetrahexahedral and truncated bipyramidal nanostructures. Further increasing the reduction overpotential induced a shape transition to rhombic hexecontahedral morphologies, attributed to the ligand effect of urea. Blank cyclic voltammograms in NaOH solution and Pb underpotential deposition measurements on pulse-deposited gold indicated the formation of structures enclosing [n(110) × (111)] facets. The electrocatalytic performance of the pulse deposited nanostructures towards 5-hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation was tested, showing strong activity for partial aldehyde oxidation and moderate activity for the oxidation of the alcohol moiety. This study demonstrates that asymmetric pulse electrodeposition offers a promising approach to tailoring surface geometries and highlights the role of deep eutectic solvents in shaping crystal structures.

papers.title: Immobilized Thiol Catalyst for Native Chemical Ligation in Flow
papers.abstract: Native chemical ligation (NCL) is a well-established research tool, used to access long and complex peptides that cannot be efficiently synthesized by other means such as linear solidphase peptide synthesis (SPPS).
